```html
    <article id="launcher-v1.3.0">
      <div class="bar"><h2>Launcher 1.3.0</h2><span class="cat">Launcher · 2026-11-18</span></div>
      <div class="body prose notes">
<p class="how">The launcher offers its own updates; with the portable zip, download the new zip and unpack it over your folder.</p>
<p>A launcher update: a second cheat, and Report a bug fixes. It comes with game 1.6.0.</p>
<h4>What's new</h4>
<ul><li>
<b>Unlimited coins (<a href="https://github.com/ILFforever/YW4Recomp/issues/17">#17</a>).</b> Settings → Cheats → <b>Manage</b> now lists <b>Unlimited coins</b>: cranking the Crank-a-kai never uses up a coin.
</li><li>
<b>Report a bug is easier to find.</b> Help now has <b>Report a bug</b> under Troubleshooting, and the page is shorter.
</li><li>
<b>Build errors in plain words.</b> When a build stops, the launcher says what to fix first, then the technical reason. A missing title key now says which file needs it and why its own ticket wasn't used.
</li></ul>
<h4>Fixes</h4>
<ul><li>
<b>Report saved: Open GitHub and Show the zip (Windows).</b> Both buttons could open your Documents folder instead. Open GitHub now opens the filled-in bug form, and Show the zip selects the report's zip.
</li></ul>
      </div>
    </article>

    <article id="v1.6.0">
      <div class="bar"><h2>Game 1.6.0</h2><span class="cat">Game · 2026-11-18</span></div>
      <div class="body prose notes">
<p class="how">The launcher gets it for you: <b>Update</b> on the Play screen rebuilds the game in a few minutes, and the version before stays playable if anything goes wrong.</p>
<h4>What's new</h4>
<ul><li>
<b>Running modes (<a href="https://github.com/ILFforever/YW4Recomp/issues/18">#18</a>).</b> Controls has a new <b>Running mode</b> row under the Nintendo icons: <b>Default</b> (the game's: hold B to run), <b>Always</b> (hold Run to walk), <b>Toggle</b> (press Run to start or stop running) and <b>Hold</b> (hold Run to run). The <b>Run</b> key is Left Shift on a keyboard, and the left stick press on a controller. Jump stays on its own button. Suggested by <a href="https://github.com/Zavichu">@Zavichu</a>.
</li><li>
<b>Close hints moved to Left Ctrl</b> on the keyboard, so Left Shift is free for Run. If yours was on Left Shift, it moves to Left Ctrl, unless you use Left Ctrl for something else.
</li><li>
<b>F2 pauses a battle.</b> In a battle, the F2 key sheet opens the Stopwatch and closing the sheet closes it again. On the field F2 doesn't pause by design.
</li><li>
<b>Clearer Controls help.</b> Removed AI jargon on control descriptions with clear commands.
</li><li>
<b>Battle keys hints fixed</b> on the F2 key sheet and the Controls page: <b>Tab</b> (left stick press) cycles through your allies, the <b>middle mouse button</b> (right stick press) locks on and off, and <b>Left / Right</b> (D-pad) cycle through every target, allies and enemies.
</li></ul>
<h4>Fixes</h4>
<ul><li>
<b>Videos play smoothly.</b> The title menu's background and the opening movie could stutter at 60 frames/s or VSYNC on a display whose refresh isn't a multiple of 60 (for example 165 Hz). Videos now play at 30 frames/s.
</li><li>
<b>Black bars in shadows on AMD graphics cards (<a href="https://github.com/ILFforever/YW4Recomp/issues/19">#19</a>, <a href="https://github.com/ILFforever/YW4Recomp/issues/8">#8</a>): likely fixed.</b> We couldn't test it on an AMD card yet, so this fix is an estimation. If you still see them, please tell us on the issue. Until then, Shadow mask → Game avoids them.
</li><li>
<b>Build errors in plain words.</b> When a build stops, the launcher says what to fix first, then the technical reason. A missing title key now says which file needs it and why its own ticket wasn't used.
</li></ul>
<h4>For testing</h4>
<ul><li>
<b><code>YW4_OCCLUSION=off</code> (<a href="https://github.com/ILFforever/YW4Recomp/issues/14">#14</a>).</b> Turns off the occlusion queries, to test a GPU hang on some Intel graphics on Linux.
</li></ul>
      </div>
    </article>

    <article id="v1.5.0">
      <div class="bar"><h2>Game 1.5.0</h2><span class="cat">Game · 2026-11-17</span></div>
      <div class="body prose notes">
<p class="how">The launcher gets it for you: <b>Update</b> on the Play screen rebuilds the game in a few minutes, and the version before stays playable if anything goes wrong.</p>
<h4>What's new</h4>
<ul><li>
<b>Five save slots in the Diary.</b> On the Switch the game has room for just one save, plus an autosave. Now <b>Continue</b> on the title shows five save slots and the Autosave under them, in the game's own Diary rows. Your existing save is slot 1. When you save in the game, Left and Right choose the slot.
</li><li>
<b>New Game asks where your game goes.</b> Right after New Game, choose a slot in a list that looks like the Diary. A slot with a save asks before it's used, and that save is only replaced when you save your new game over it. <b>Back to the title</b> leaves without starting one.
</li><li>
<b>Delete a slot.</b> On Continue, press X twice: the X key on a keyboard, Square on a PlayStation controller.
</li><li>
<b>Unlimited coins cheat (<a href="https://github.com/ILFforever/YW4Recomp/issues/17">#17</a>).</b> Cranking the Crank-a-kai never uses up a coin. Turn it on in the overlay's <b>Cheats</b> page or the launcher's <b>Manage cheats</b>.
</li><li>
<b>The mouse works in more menus:</b> Slimey Marks, Soulmates, Yo-kai Trophies and the treasure photos.
</li></ul>
<h4>Performance</h4>
<ul><li>
<b>Busy places run faster.</b> Where the CPU limits the frame rate, the graphics work takes less of it: about 9% more frames per second on our busiest test street.
</li><li>
<b>No more stutter in the overlay's popups.</b> Moving through a popup could freeze the game for a moment at 4K.
</li></ul>
<h4>Fixes</h4>
<ul><li>
<b>A crash after saving in some late-game areas.</b> Going back to the map after a Diary save could load more textures at once than the game could handle, and it stopped.
</li><li>
<b>Long sessions no longer use more and more memory.</b> The performance log kept every frame, a few hundred MB after three hours.
</li><li>
<b>Logs don't pile up.</b> The game keeps the newest 5 runs' logs (at most 1 GB) and only writes the large per-frame file when asked.
</li><li>
<b>Better bug reports (<a href="https://github.com/ILFforever/YW4Recomp/issues/14">#14</a>).</b> Every log now starts with your system: OS, CPU, memory and free disk space.
</li></ul>
      </div>
    </article>

    <article id="v1.4.0">
      <div class="bar"><h2>Game 1.4.0</h2><span class="cat">Game · 2026-11-16</span></div>
      <div class="body prose notes">
<p class="how">The launcher gets it for you: <b>Update</b> on the Play screen rebuilds the game in a few minutes, and the version before stays playable if anything goes wrong.</p>
<h4>What's new</h4>
<ul><li>
<b>The shortcut wheel.</b> While exploring, hold your key for <b>L</b> (<b>1</b> by default) and all eight field shortcuts appear in a wheel. Point at one with the mouse and let go of the key to use it. Let go in the middle to cancel. So now you can toggle game shortcuts without having to let go of the mouse. You can turn the wheel off on the overlay's <b>Controls</b> page (Mouse, Shortcut wheel).
</li><li>
<b>Image Sharpening.</b> A new <b>Sharpening</b> setting under <b>Anti-aliasing and upscaling</b> makes the world crisper. It's a slider with five levels: Off, Low, <b>Medium</b> (the default), High and Max. It works with every anti-aliasing mode. DLSS gets a stronger sharpen at each level, so it looks as crisp as FSR at the same level.
</li><li>
<b>Sharpen text and menus.</b> Right under Sharpening, an option to sharpen the game's menus, text and HUD too. Off by default; it helps most at low resolutions.
</li><li>
<b>The mouse works in Naviwoof Guide.</b> The wheel moves along the row of pins, left click starts guiding, right click goes back.
</li></ul>
<h4>Fixes</h4>
<ul><li>
<b>Lighter graphics on weak GPUs at first start (<a href="https://github.com/ILFforever/YW4Recomp/issues/14">#14</a>).</b> On first start the game picks lighter graphics for integrated or low-memory GPUs. This was skipped if you had changed "Full screen at start" or a cheat in the launcher before playing for the first time, so those PCs got the heaviest shadows and could crash in the first cutscene. It now runs in that case too.
</li><li>
<b>Better bug reports.</b> The game's log now lists your picture and shadow settings at start and on every change, and records more detail if the graphics card stops responding. Attach the log when you report a bug and we can find the cause faster.
</li></ul>
<h4>On Linux (experimental)</h4>
<ul><li>
<b>Building from source with GCC works (<a href="https://github.com/ILFforever/YW4Recomp/issues/12">#12</a>),</b> and FSR now builds correctly when the source is a git clone.
</li></ul>
      </div>
    </article>

    <article id="launcher-v1.2.0">
      <div class="bar"><h2>Launcher 1.2.0</h2><span class="cat">Launcher · 2026-11-15</span></div>
      <div class="body prose notes">
<p class="how">The launcher offers its own updates; with the portable zip, download the new zip and unpack it over your folder.</p>
<p>A launcher update: a Cheats card, and Linux fixes. The game itself is updated separately (game 1.3.0): press <b>Update</b> on the Play screen to get it.</p>
<h4>What's new</h4>
<ul><li>
<b>Cheats card.</b> Settings has a new <b>Cheats</b> card under Playing. Its switch shows or hides the game's Cheats page (in the overlay, Escape). <b>Manage</b> lists the cheats, for now <b>Unlimited Crank-a-kai</b>, and turns each one on or off. It's the same setting as the game's own Cheats page, so the last change wins. Close the game to change them here.
</li></ul>
<h4>On Linux (experimental)</h4>
<ul><li>
<b>The launcher runs on Linux</b> as an AppImage, attached to this release. It was checked in WSL only (no real Linux desktop yet); if it fails on your system, please <a href="https://github.com/ILFforever/YW4Recomp/issues">report a bug</a> with your log. You can still <a href="https://github.com/ILFforever/YW4Recomp#building-on-linux">build from source</a>.
</li><li>
<b>Upscaling and frame generation.</b> The launcher offers AMD FSR (upscaling and frame generation) and NVIDIA DLSS (upscaling only), as on Windows. Tried only on software rendering so far; we'd love reports from real Linux graphics cards.
</li><li>
<b>Build works from the AppImage (<a href="https://github.com/ILFforever/YW4Recomp/issues/13">#13</a>).</b> Build stopped at 0% with "No module named 'encodings'": the AppImage's own settings reached the programs it started. They now start with your normal settings.
</li><li>
<b>The icon and banner show (<a href="https://github.com/ILFforever/YW4Recomp/issues/13">#13</a>).</b> The game's icon, and the banner made from it, were missing on Linux. They appear after a rebuild.
</li><li>
<b>FSR builds inside your copy of the project (<a href="https://github.com/ILFforever/YW4Recomp/issues/12">#12</a>).</b> When the build folder was inside your project folder, AMD FSR failed to build and the game was built without it. It builds now, with GCC or Clang.
</li></ul>
      </div>
    </article>

    <article id="v1.3.0">
      <div class="bar"><h2>Game 1.3.0</h2><span class="cat">Game · 2026-11-15</span></div>
      <div class="body prose notes">
<p class="how">The launcher gets it for you: <b>Update</b> on the Play screen rebuilds the game in a few minutes, and the version before stays playable if anything goes wrong.</p>
<h4>What's new</h4>
<ul><li>
<b>Cheats: unlimited Crank-a-kai.</b> The overlay (Escape) has a new <b>Cheats</b> page. Turn on <b>Unlimited Crank-a-kai</b> and the day's cranks never run out, so you can crank as long as you have coins. Each crank still costs a coin. If you turn it on with no cranks left, you get one back.
</li><li>
<b>The mouse works in more places.</b>
<ul><li>
<b>Title screen and save list:</b> the wheel moves the selection, left click chooses, right click goes back.
</li><li>
<b>Conversations and shops</b> (and the Crank-a-kai): the wheel moves between choices, left click confirms, right click cancels.
</li><li>
<b>The map:</b> move the mouse to pan the map, use the wheel to zoom, right click to close it.
</li><li>
<b>The battle's Stopwatching menu</b> (and the Start Battle / Stopwatching choice): left click confirms, right click goes back.
</li><li>
<b>The overlay:</b> the wheel now moves the selection, like Up and Down.
</li></ul>
</li><li>
<b>"N/A" for buttons with nothing bound.</b> If you removed the key or pad button for an action, its hint now shows <b>N/A</b> instead of a Switch button name that nothing presses. It matches your hint style: keyboard, Xbox, PlayStation or Switch.
</li><li>
<b>A cleaner cursor on the Yo-kai Pad.</b> On the Yo-kai Pad and its pages, the mouse now shows the touchpad's round grey cursor instead of the Windows arrow. It is also bigger, so it is easier to see in a small window.
</li></ul>
<h4>Fixes</h4>
<ul><li>
<b>Blurred screens are no longer black with upscaling on (<a href="https://github.com/ILFforever/YW4Recomp/issues/10">#10</a>).</b> With FSR or DLSS upscaling, the blurred picture behind the pause menu, battle transitions, battle results and the capsule scene was black. It shows again.
</li><li>
<b>Stopwatching menu keys and hints.</b> With the default keys, <b>Switch ally</b> had no key. In that menu, the left stick press key (<b>Tab</b> by default) now switches ally too, and the hints show the keys that work: Tab for Switch ally, <b>F</b> for Switch enemy.
</li><li>
<b>A rare thread timing bug.</b> One way the game's threads wait for each other could fail in a rare timing window. It showed up in our tests, not in play, and is fixed.
</li><li>
<b>Less work for your graphics card.</b> Objects hidden behind others are now skipped on the graphics card, as the game asks. The picture is the same. One more kind of graphics effect also runs now instead of being skipped (it has not been seen in play yet).
</li></ul>
<h4>On Linux (experimental)</h4>
<ul><li>
<b>FSR and DLSS upscaling, and FSR frame generation.</b> DLSS hasn't been tried on an NVIDIA card under Linux yet.
</li><li>
<b>Clearer messages when adding DLC (<a href="https://github.com/ILFforever/YW4Recomp/issues/3">#3</a>).</b>
</li></ul>
      </div>
    </article>

    <article id="v1.2.3">
      <div class="bar"><h2>Game 1.2.3</h2><span class="cat">Game · 2026-11-14</span></div>
      <div class="body prose notes">
<p class="how">The launcher gets it for you: <b>Update</b> on the Play screen rebuilds the game in a few minutes, and the version before stays playable if anything goes wrong.</p>
<h4>What's new</h4>
<ul><li>
<b>Smoother first play after an update.</b> The game now keeps its shader cache when it's updated and rebuilds what changed in the background while it starts, instead of hitching the first time places and effects appear.
</li><li>
<b>Native FSR and DLSS are easier to find.</b> The first Upscaling choice now says <b>Off (native)</b>: set Anti-aliasing to FSR or DLSS and Upscaling to Off (native) to smooth edges at full resolution.
</li><li>
<b>Better graphics compatibility.</b> The game now follows the Vulkan rules more closely: its shaders stay within what every desktop graphics card supports, and NVIDIA DLSS and Reflex get everything they ask for. Nothing should look different; it may help on graphics cards and drivers that are less forgiving.
</li></ul>
      </div>
    </article>

    <article id="v1.2.2">
      <div class="bar"><h2>Game 1.2.2</h2><span class="cat">Game · 2026-11-14</span></div>
      <div class="body prose notes">
<p class="how">The launcher gets it for you: <b>Update</b> on the Play screen rebuilds the game in a few minutes, and the version before stays playable if anything goes wrong.</p>
<h4>What's new</h4>
<ul><li>
<b>Full jumps while running at high frame rates.</b> Above 60 frames/s a jump made while running was only a small hop. It now goes as high as on the Switch (<a href="https://github.com/ILFforever/YW4Recomp/issues/9">#9</a>).
</li><li>
<b>Shadows on AMD graphics cards.</b> A fix for shadows flickering on and off on AMD cards on Windows (<a href="https://github.com/ILFforever/YW4Recomp/issues/8">#8</a>). If you set <b>Shadow mask</b> to the game's to work around it, set it back and let us know if the flicker is gone.
</li><li>
<b>FSR on AMD graphics cards.</b> FSR anti-aliasing and FSR frame generation now get the scene's depth in a form that is valid on AMD cards.
</li></ul>
      </div>
    </article>

    <article id="launcher-v1.1.0">
      <div class="bar"><h2>Launcher 1.1.0</h2><span class="cat">Launcher · 2026-11-13</span></div>
      <div class="body prose notes">
<p class="how">The launcher offers its own updates; with the portable zip, download the new zip and unpack it over your folder.</p>
<h4>A launcher update for mods.</h4>
<ul><li>
<b>Clash warnings.</b> The Mods tab tells you when two mods can't work together, before you play. Mods that clash are shown in groups: the one the game uses is marked <b>Used</b>, and you switch off the ones you don't want right there.
</li><li>
<b>Readable mod names.</b> Mods show as "Crank-a-kai Overhaul" instead of their folder name.
</li><li>
<b>More mods found.</b> Mods without a <code>romfs</code> folder, or inside an extra folder of their own, show up in the list.
</li><li>
<b>Buy me a coffee.</b> If you enjoy YW4 Recomp, there's a small Support card in Settings.
</li><li>
<b>Portable zip fixes.</b> Update now points you to the new portable zip instead of running the installer, and the zip includes the themes.
</li><li>
<b>The installer carries game 1.2.0</b> with the YKW Mod Merger™, so a new install starts from the current game.
</li></ul>
<p><b>Using the portable zip from 1.0.1?</b> Don't press Update for this one: it runs the installer. Download YW4-Recomp-Launcher-1.1.0-portable.zip below and unpack it over your folder.</p>
      </div>
    </article>

    <article id="v1.2.0">
      <div class="bar"><h2>Game 1.2.0</h2><span class="cat">Game · 2026-11-13</span></div>
      <div class="body prose notes">
<p class="how">The launcher gets it for you: <b>Update</b> on the Play screen rebuilds the game in a few minutes, and the version before stays playable if anything goes wrong.</p>
<h4>What's new</h4>
<ul><li>
<b>YKW Mod Merger™.</b> Mods that change the same part of the game, such as items or shops, now work together. Gameplay mods such as Free Tag Battles or Unshackled Equipment work next to the English translation and next to each other, instead of only one mod working at a time.
</li><li>
<b>More mods load.</b> Mods that come without a <code>romfs</code> folder, or inside an extra folder of their own, are found now.
</li><li>
<b>Clash warnings.</b> The game now detects when mods clash and warns you through the launcher.
</li></ul>
      </div>
    </article>

    <article id="v1.1.0">
      <div class="bar"><h2>Game 1.1.0</h2><span class="cat">Game · 2026-11-13</span></div>
      <div class="body prose notes">
<p class="how">The launcher gets it for you: <b>Update</b> on the Play screen rebuilds the game in a few minutes, and the version before stays playable if anything goes wrong.</p>
<h4>What's new</h4>
<ul><li>
<b>Names typed in English look right.</b> Names you type with the English patch no longer come out spaced apart ("N a t e").
</li><li>
<b>PS touchpad support.</b> Use a DualSense or DualShock 4 touchpad to move a cursor in the game's menus and the overlay, and click to choose.
</li><li>
<b>More controller icons.</b> The middle buttons show the icons printed on your controller: CREATE, SHARE or SELECT on PlayStation pads, and the Back and Start icons on Xbox 360 pads.
</li><li>
<b>Mouse hints in battles.</b> With mouse and keyboard, battle hints show the mouse button first.
</li></ul>
      </div>
    </article>

    <article id="v1.0.2">
      <div class="bar"><h2>Game 1.0.2</h2><span class="cat">Game · 2026-11-13</span></div>
      <div class="body prose notes">
<p class="how">The launcher gets it for you: <b>Update</b> on the Play screen rebuilds the game in a few minutes, and the version before stays playable if anything goes wrong.</p>
<h4>What's new</h4>
<ul><li>
<b>Switch-style controllers.</b> Some Switch-style controllers show up on PC as an Xbox controller, so the button hints showed letters that don't match the ones printed on the controller. Turn on <b>Nintendo icons</b> on the overlay's Controls page, and the hints show the letters on your controller.
</li><li>
<b>Open the overlay with the shoulder buttons.</b> Hold L, R, ZL and ZR together (LB, RB, LT and RT on an Xbox controller). This helps on controllers where Minus + Plus also opens the Xbox Game Bar or Steam.
</li><li>
<b>Faster builds.</b> Building the game is about 20% faster.
</li></ul>
      </div>
    </article>

    <article id="launcher-v1.0.1">
      <div class="bar"><h2>Launcher 1.0.1</h2><span class="cat">Launcher · 2026-11-13</span></div>
      <div class="body prose notes">
<p class="how">The launcher offers its own updates; with the portable zip, download the new zip and unpack it over your folder.</p>
<h4>A small update to the launcher.</h4>
<ul><li>
<b>New installs build the newest game straight away.</b> Before the first build, the launcher now downloads any game update that came out after it. New players used to build the old version first, then get the update and build again.
</li><li>
<b>"What's new" shows the game update you have.</b> After a game update, the Play screen lists that update's changes instead of the launcher's own.
</li><li>
<b>The installer carries game 1.0.1</b>, so a new install starts from the current game.
</li></ul>
<p><b>Using the portable zip?</b> Its Update button runs the installer, which installs a second launcher instead of updating yours. Download the newest portable zip from the releases page and unpack it over your folder instead. Fixed in launcher 1.1.0.</p>
      </div>
    </article>

    <article id="v1.0.1">
      <div class="bar"><h2>Game 1.0.1</h2><span class="cat">Game · 2026-11-13</span></div>
      <div class="body prose notes">
<p class="how">The launcher gets it for you: <b>Update</b> on the Play screen rebuilds the game in a few minutes, and the version before stays playable if anything goes wrong.</p>
<h4>What's new</h4>
<ul><li>
<b>Better first-start settings.</b> New installs now start at 60 frames a second instead of 30. PCs with a dedicated graphics card start on a high-quality set: 1440p, 120 frames a second, sharper shadows, and DLSS where the card has it. Integrated graphics still get the lighter set. If you already play, your settings stay as they are: change them in the overlay (Esc) any time.
</li><li>
<b>Much faster on Linux.</b> The game was sending almost every texture to the graphics card again on every frame, and kept 3D models in system memory. Both are fixed, so towns no longer drop to 20-something frames a second.
</li></ul>
      </div>
    </article>

<script>
/* The download cards point at the newest launcher release when GitHub answers; the links above are the fallback. */
fetch("https://api.github.com/repos/ILFforever/YW4Recomp/releases/latest")
  .then(r => r.ok ? r.json() : Promise.reject(r.status))
  .then(rel => {
    if (!rel.tag_name || !rel.tag_name.startsWith("launcher-v")) return;
    const v = rel.tag_name.slice("launcher-v".length);
    document.querySelectorAll("[data-asset]").forEach(a => {
      const f = (rel.assets || []).find(x => x.name.endsWith(a.dataset.asset));
      if (f) a.href = f.browser_download_url;
    });
    document.querySelectorAll("[data-ver]").forEach(s => { s.textContent = v; });
  })
  .catch(() => {});
</script>
<script>
/* Releases: the newest SHOW_FIRST shown, SHOW_MORE more per click on "Show older releases" (or the list's "Older
 * releases"); the Releases list shows the same ones. A link to an older release (#v1.2.0) opens up to it. Without
 * this script every release shows. */
(() => {
  const SHOW_FIRST = 3, SHOW_MORE = 4;
  const main = document.querySelector('main');
  const rel = [...main.querySelectorAll(':scope > article')].filter(a => a.id !== 'download');
  const list = document.querySelector('.pad ol');
  const item = id => list.querySelector(`a[href="#${CSS.escape(id)}"]`)?.closest('li');
  let shown = SHOW_FIRST;
  const more = document.createElement('button');
  more.type = 'button'; more.className = 'older';
  main.append(more);
  const older = document.createElement('li');
  older.innerHTML = '<a href="#older"><span class="n">+</span>Older releases</a>';
  list.append(older);
  function render() {
    rel.forEach((a, i) => { a.hidden = i >= shown; const li = item(a.id); if (li) li.hidden = i >= shown; });
    const left = rel.length - shown;
    more.hidden = older.hidden = left <= 0;
    more.textContent = `Show older releases (${left})`;
  }
  function showMore() {
    const first = shown;
    shown = Math.min(rel.length, shown + SHOW_MORE);
    render();
    return rel[first];
  }
  more.addEventListener('click', showMore);
  older.querySelector('a').addEventListener('click', e => {
    e.preventDefault();
    const a = showMore();
    if (a) a.scrollIntoView();
  });
  function openTo(id) {
    const i = rel.findIndex(a => a.id === id);
    if (i < shown) return;
    shown = i + 1;
    render();
    rel[i].scrollIntoView();
  }
  render();
  if (location.hash) openTo(decodeURIComponent(location.hash.slice(1)));
  addEventListener('hashchange', () => openTo(decodeURIComponent(location.hash.slice(1))));
})();
</script>
<script>
/* the theme switch: the other theme than the one showing, kept for next time */
(() => {
  const btn = document.getElementById('theme'), root = document.documentElement;
  const dark = () => root.dataset.theme ? root.dataset.theme === 'dark' : matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches;
  const label = () => btn.setAttribute('aria-label', dark() ? 'Light mode' : 'Dark mode');
  label();
  const flip = () => {
    root.dataset.theme = dark() ? 'light' : 'dark';
    try { localStorage.setItem('yw4-theme', root.dataset.theme); } catch (e) {}
    label();
  };
  /* a slow cross-fade between the themes (site.css sets its length), where the browser can do one */
  btn.addEventListener('click', () => {
    if (document.startViewTransition && !matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches) document.startViewTransition(flip);
    else flip();
  });
})();
</script>
</body>
</html>
```

```html
  <main>
    <article id="resolution" data-cat="Graphics">
      <div class="bar"><span class="q">1</span><h2>Resolution: the Switch and 4K</h2><span class="cat">Graphics</span></div>
      <div class="body">
        <div class="top">
          <div class="prose"><p>The Switch draws the world at 1600×900; here it can go up to 3840×2160, 5.8 times the
            pixels. The menus and text are drawn at the same size on top. Same moment, only the resolution changed
            (anti-aliasing off in both); the 1600×900 shot is stretched to 4K the way a 4K screen would show it.</p></div>
          <div class="spec"><dl>
            <dt>Setting</dt><dd><kbd>F1</kbd> Display › Resolution</dd>
            <dt>Switch</dt><dd>1600×900</dd>
            <dt>Options</dt><dd>1080p, 1440p, 4K</dd>
            <dt>4K speed</dt><dd>90+ frames/s on an RTX 4070 laptop with the other features off; more with upscaling</dd>
            <dt>Record</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/ILFforever/YW4Recomp/blob/master/docs/decisions/0031-resolution-scaling.md">decision 0031</a></dd>
          </dl></div>
        </div>
        <div data-cmp="resolution"></div>
      </div>
    </article>

    <article id="ultrawide" data-cat="Graphics">
      <div class="bar"><span class="q">2</span><h2>Aspect ratio: ultrawide</h2><span class="cat">Graphics</span></div>
      <div class="body">
        <div class="top">
          <div class="prose"><p>The world goes on at the sides while the menus stay 16:9 in the middle, where they are
            on the Switch. Full-screen layers reach the edges; pictures made for 16:9 keep black bars. 21:9 at 4K
            height (5120×2160).</p></div>
          <div class="spec"><dl>
            <dt>Setting</dt><dd><kbd>F1</kbd> Display › Aspect ratio</dd>
            <dt>Options</dt><dd>16:9, 16:10, 21:9, 32:9</dd>
            <dt>Record</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/ILFforever/YW4Recomp/blob/master/docs/decisions/0033-widescreen.md">decision 0033</a></dd>
          </dl></div>
        </div>
        <div class="gallery" id="uw"></div>
      </div>
    </article>

    <article id="shadowmap" data-cat="Graphics">
      <div class="bar"><span class="q">3</span><h2>Shadow map size</h2><span class="cat">Graphics</span></div>
      <div class="body">
        <div class="top">
          <div class="prose"><p>A bigger shadow map gives sharper, more detailed shadow edges, most visibly far from the
            camera. The bamboo forest with soft shadows off, so only the map size changes.</p>
            <p><b>Meant to be used with soft shadows (PCSS):</b> a sharp 4096 map alone shows every leaf as a hard dot; soft shadows on top keep the detail and soften it with distance, as in the next section.</p></div>
          <div class="spec"><dl>
            <dt>Setting</dt><dd><kbd>F1</kbd> Shadows › Shadow map</dd>
            <dt>Switch</dt><dd>1024</dd>
            <dt>Recommended</dt><dd>4096 with soft shadows ×2</dd>
          </dl></div>
        </div>
        <div data-cmp="shadowmap"></div>
      </div>
    </article>

    <article id="pcss" data-cat="Graphics">
      <div class="bar"><span class="q">4</span><h2>Soft shadows (PCSS)</h2><span class="cat">Graphics</span></div>
      <div class="body">
        <div class="top">
          <div class="prose">
            <p>Percentage-closer soft shadows behave more like real ones. Shown with the shadow map at 4096.</p>
            <ul>
              <li><b>Sharp at the contact</b>: feet, poles, the base of a wall.</li>
              <li><b>Softer farther away</b>: tree canopies become dappled shade, not hard dots.</li>
              <li><b>Less shimmer</b> on distant shadows while the camera moves.</li>
            </ul>
          </div>
          <div class="spec"><dl>
            <dt>Setting</dt><dd><kbd>F1</kbd> Shadows › Soft shadows</dd>
            <dt>Shown with</dt><dd>Shadow map 4096</dd>
            <dt>Recommended</dt><dd>×2</dd>
            <dt>Record</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/ILFforever/YW4Recomp/blob/master/docs/decisions/0025-pcss-soft-shadows.md">decision 0025</a></dd>
          </dl></div>
        </div>
        <div data-cmp="pcss"></div>
      </div>
    </article>

    <article id="contact" data-cat="Graphics">
      <div class="bar"><span class="q">5</span><h2>Contact shadows</h2><span class="cat">Graphics</span></div>
      <div class="body">
        <div class="top">
          <div class="prose">
            <p>The shadow map can't see small, close detail. Contact shadows fill it in from the picture itself: a short
              ray from each point toward the sun finds what's in the way.</p>
            <ul>
              <li><b>Small objects cast their shadow</b>: the taps over the schoolyard sink.</li>
              <li><b>Depth in foliage</b>: hedge and flower-bed leaves shade each other.</li>
              <li><b>Thin lines under ledges</b>: balconies, a window's awning, a wall's cap.</li>
            </ul>
          </div>
          <div class="spec"><dl>
            <dt>Setting</dt><dd><kbd>F1</kbd> Shadows › Contact shadows</dd>
            <dt>Quick flip</dt><dd><kbd>F7</kbd></dd>
            <dt>Default</dt><dd>On</dd>
            <dt>GPU cost, 4K</dt><dd>+0.04 to 0.25 ms</dd>
            <dt>Limit</dt><dd>only what's on screen casts</dd>
            <dt>Record</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/ILFforever/YW4Recomp/blob/master/docs/decisions/0045-contact-shadows.md">decision 0045</a></dd>
          </dl></div>
        </div>
        <div data-cmp="contact"></div>
      </div>
    </article>

    <article id="aa" data-cat="Graphics">
      <div class="bar"><span class="q">6</span><h2>Anti-aliasing</h2><span class="cat">Graphics</span></div>
      <div class="body">
        <div class="top">
          <div class="prose"><p>Applied to the 3D scene before the menus are drawn, so text stays sharp. TAA also stops
            thin things (fences, nets, wires) from shimmering while the camera moves. Yo-kai World, zoomed in 3×.</p></div>
          <div class="spec"><dl>
            <dt>Setting</dt><dd><kbd>F1</kbd> Anti-aliasing</dd>
            <dt>Switch</dt><dd>None</dd>
            <dt>Options</dt><dd>FXAA, SMAA, TAA, FSR, DLSS</dd>
            <dt>Record</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/ILFforever/YW4Recomp/blob/master/docs/decisions/0032-taa.md">decision 0032</a></dd>
          </dl></div>
        </div>
        <figure class="whole"><img loading="lazy" src="img/aa-whole.jpg" alt="Yo-kai World street with TAA, the whole frame, the close-ups marked in red"><figcaption>The whole frame, TAA; the red boxes are the close-ups below.</figcaption></figure>
        <div data-cmp="aa"></div>
      </div>
    </article>

    <article id="filtering" data-cat="Graphics">
      <div class="bar"><span class="q">7</span><h2>Texture filtering</h2><span class="cat">Graphics</span></div>
      <div class="body">
        <div class="top">
          <div class="prose"><p>Without it the ground blurs a short way ahead. Anisotropic filtering keeps the road,
            pavement and walls sharp into the distance, even at a low angle. Yo-kai World, zoomed in 2×.</p></div>
          <div class="spec"><dl>
            <dt>Setting</dt><dd><kbd>F1</kbd> Detail › Texture filtering</dd>
            <dt>Switch</dt><dd>Off</dd>
            <dt>Recommended</dt><dd>×16, almost no cost</dd>
          </dl></div>
        </div>
        <figure class="whole"><img loading="lazy" src="img/filtering-whole.jpg" alt="Yo-kai World street with ×16 texture filtering, the whole frame, the close-ups marked in red"><figcaption>The whole frame, ×16; the red boxes are the close-ups below.</figcaption></figure>
        <div data-cmp="filtering"></div>
      </div>
    </article>

    <article id="upscaling" data-cat="Performance">
      <div class="bar"><span class="q">8</span><h2>Upscaling: DLSS and FSR</h2><span class="cat">Performance</span></div>
      <div class="body">
        <div class="top">
          <div class="prose"><p>The world is drawn smaller than the resolution and rebuilt at full size from the frames
            before; the menus are drawn afterwards at full size. <b>DLSS for the cleanest picture, FSR for the most
            frames.</b> Each image: the whole native frame on top, the 1:1 crops underneath.</p></div>
          <div class="spec"><dl>
            <dt>Setting</dt><dd><kbd>F1</kbd> Anti-aliasing › Upscaling</dd>
            <dt>DLSS</dt><dd>NVIDIA RTX, else FSR</dd>
            <dt>FSR</dt><dd>any GPU</dd>
          </dl></div>
        </div>
        <table>
          <thead><tr><th>Mode · 4K 21:9 · RTX 4070 laptop</th><th>World drawn at</th><th class="num">DLSS</th><th class="num">FSR</th></tr></thead>
          <tbody>
            <tr><td>Native, TAA</td><td>5120×2160</td><td class="num" colspan="2">~81 frames/s</td></tr>
            <tr><td>Quality</td><td>3413×1440</td><td class="num">~85</td><td class="num"><b>~94</b></td></tr>
            <tr><td>Balanced</td><td>3013×1271</td><td class="num">~92</td><td class="num"><b>~106</b></td></tr>
            <tr><td>Performance</td><td>2560×1080</td><td class="num">~82</td><td class="num"><b>~118</b></td></tr>
          </tbody>
        </table>
        <div class="gallery">
          <figure><img loading="lazy" src="../screenshots/63-fsr-dlss-quality-vs-native.jpg" alt="Bamboo forest in native, FSR quality and DLSS quality">
            <figcaption>Quality: DLSS keeps the bamboo and the lantern closest to native.</figcaption></figure>
          <figure><img loading="lazy" src="../screenshots/67-dlss-vs-fsr-performance-forest.jpg" alt="Bamboo forest in native, FSR performance and DLSS performance">
            <figcaption>Performance: DLSS keeps the bamboo and leaves crisper.</figcaption></figure>

// One comparison: both images fill the same box (its shape taken from the first image), the left one clipped at
// the line. The box takes pointer drags and the arrow keys.
function comparison(row, pixel, eager) {
  const fig = document.createElement('figure');
  const box = document.createElement('div'); box.className = 'cmp' + (pixel ? ' pixel' : '');
  box.tabIndex = 0; box.setAttribute('role', 'slider'); box.setAttribute('aria-valuemin', '0'); box.setAttribute('aria-valuemax', '100');
  const b = new Image(), a = new Image();
  if (!eager) b.loading = a.loading = 'lazy';
  b.decoding = a.decoding = 'async';
  b.addEventListener('load', () => { if (!b.naturalWidth) return;
    box.style.aspectRatio = `${b.naturalWidth} / ${b.naturalHeight}`; fig.style.setProperty('--ar', b.naturalWidth / b.naturalHeight); });
  const rule = document.createElement('div'); rule.className = 'rule';
  const knob = document.createElement('div'); knob.className = 'knob';
  const tl = document.createElement('span'); tl.className = 'tag l';
  const tr = document.createElement('span'); tr.className = 'tag r';
  box.append(b, a, rule, knob, tl, tr);
  if (fig.requestFullscreen) {
    const fs = document.createElement('button'); fs.type = 'button'; fs.className = 'fs';
    fs.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Full screen'); fs.title = 'Full screen (F)';
    fs.innerHTML = '<svg class="in" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2.4" stroke-linecap="round"><path d="M4 9V4h5M20 9V4h-5M4 15v5h5M20 15v5h-5"/></svg>' +
      '<svg class="out" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2.4" stroke-linecap="round"><path d="M9 4v5H4M15 4v5h5M9 20v-5H4M15 20v-5h5"/></svg>';
    fs.addEventListener('pointerdown', e => e.stopPropagation());
    const toggle = () => document.fullscreenElement === fig ? document.exitFullscreen() : fig.requestFullscreen();
    fs.addEventListener('click', toggle);
    box.addEventListener('keydown', e => { if (e.key === 'f' || e.key === 'F') { toggle(); e.preventDefault(); } });
    box.append(fs);
  }
  const place = p => { p = Math.min(100, Math.max(0, p)); box.dataset.p = p;
    a.style.clipPath = `inset(0 ${100 - p}% 0 0)`; rule.style.left = knob.style.left = p + '%'; box.setAttribute('aria-valuenow', Math.round(p)); };
  const at = e => { const r = box.getBoundingClientRect(); place((e.clientX - r.left) / r.width * 100); };
  box.addEventListener('pointerdown', e => { box.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId); at(e); });
  box.addEventListener('pointermove', e => { if (box.hasPointerCapture(e.pointerId)) at(e); });
  box.addEventListener('keydown', e => {
    const step = e.shiftKey ? 10 : 2, p = +box.dataset.p;
    if (e.key === 'ArrowLeft') place(p - step); else if (e.key === 'ArrowRight') place(p + step);
    else if (e.key === 'Home') place(0); else if (e.key === 'End') place(100); else return;
    e.preventDefault();
  });
  place(50);

  let ia = 0, ib = row.set.length - 1;
  const picks = document.createElement('div'); picks.className = 'picks';
  const show = () => {
    a.src = IMG + row.set[ia][1]; a.alt = row.set[ia][0]; b.src = IMG + row.set[ib][1]; b.alt = row.set[ib][0];
    tl.textContent = row.set[ia][0]; tr.textContent = row.set[ib][0];
    box.setAttribute('aria-label', `Comparison: ${row.set[ia][0]} on the left, ${row.set[ib][0]} on the right`);
    picks.querySelectorAll('.chip').forEach(c => c.setAttribute('aria-pressed', +c.dataset.k === (c.dataset.s === 'a' ? ia : ib)));
  };
  if (row.set.length > 2) {
    for (const [s, who] of [['a', 'Left'], ['b', 'Right']]) {
      const g = document.createElement('div'); g.className = 'side ' + s;
      const w = document.createElement('span'); w.className = 'who'; w.textContent = who; g.append(w);
      row.set.forEach(([name], k) => {
        const c = document.createElement('button'); c.type = 'button'; c.className = 'chip'; c.textContent = name;
        c.dataset.s = s; c.dataset.k = k; c.onclick = () => { if (s === 'a') ia = k; else ib = k; show(); };
        g.append(c);
      });
      picks.append(g);
    }
    fig.append(picks);
  }
  fig.append(box); show();
  return fig;
}

for (const el of document.querySelectorAll('[data-cmp]')) {
  const c = CMP[el.dataset.cmp];
  for (const row of c.rows) {
    if (row.name) { const h = document.createElement('h3'); h.className = 'row-name'; h.textContent = row.name; el.append(h); }
    el.append(comparison(row, row.pixel ?? c.pixel, false));
  }
}
// The header: one comparison and a button per scene; a scene's button swaps the comparison for that scene's.
const hero = document.querySelector('[data-hero]');
const heroRows = CMP[hero.dataset.hero].rows;
let heroFig = comparison(heroRows[0], false, true);
const scenes = document.createElement('div'); scenes.className = 'scenes'; scenes.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Scene');
heroRows.forEach((row, k) => {
  const c = document.createElement('button'); c.type = 'button'; c.className = 'chip'; c.textContent = row.name;
  c.setAttribute('aria-pressed', k === 0);
  c.onclick = () => {
    const f = comparison(row, false, true); heroFig.replaceWith(f); heroFig = f;
    scenes.querySelectorAll('.chip').forEach((b, j) => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', j === k));
  };
  scenes.append(c);
});
const hint = document.createElement('p'); hint.className = 'hint';
hint.textContent = 'Drag the line (or use the arrow keys); the corner button or F shows it full screen. The Switch on the left, 4K high on the right.';
hero.append(heroFig, scenes, hint);

const uw = document.getElementById('uw');
for (const [f, cap] of ULTRAWIDE) {
  const fig = document.createElement('figure');
  const img = new Image(); img.loading = 'lazy'; img.src = IMG + f; img.alt = '21:9: ' + cap;
  const fc = document.createElement('figcaption'); fc.textContent = cap;
  fig.append(img, fc); uw.append(fig);
}

// plain pictures (galleries, whole frames): wrapped so a click or the corner button shows them full screen
const FS_ICONS = '<svg class="in" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2.4" stroke-linecap="round"><path d="M4 9V4h5M20 9V4h-5M4 15v5h5M20 15v5h-5"/></svg>' +
  '<svg class="out" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2.4" stroke-linecap="round"><path d="M9 4v5H4M15 4v5h5M9 20v-5H4M15 20v-5h5"/></svg>';
if (document.documentElement.requestFullscreen) {
  for (const img of document.querySelectorAll('.gallery img, .whole img')) {
    const wrap = document.createElement('div'); wrap.className = 'zoom';
    img.replaceWith(wrap); wrap.append(img);
    const fs = document.createElement('button'); fs.type = 'button'; fs.className = 'fs';
    fs.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Full screen: ' + img.alt); fs.innerHTML = FS_ICONS;
    wrap.append(fs);
    const toggle = () => document.fullscreenElement === wrap ? document.exitFullscreen() : wrap.requestFullscreen();
    wrap.addEventListener('click', toggle);
  }
}

// contents: one entry per article, grouped by category, the one in view marked
const toc = document.getElementById('toc');
let group = '', n = 0;
const links = [];
for (const art of document.querySelectorAll('article')) {
  if (art.dataset.cat !== group) { group = art.dataset.cat; const g = document.createElement('li'); g.className = 'grp'; g.textContent = group; toc.append(g); }
  const li = document.createElement('li'), a = document.createElement('a'); a.href = '#' + art.id;
  const num = document.createElement('span'); num.className = 'n'; num.textContent = String(++n).padStart(2, '0');
  const t = document.createElement('span'); t.textContent = art.querySelector('h2').textContent;
  a.append(num, t); li.append(a); toc.append(li); links.push([art, a]);
}
const spy = new IntersectionObserver(es => { for (const e of es) if (e.isIntersecting) for (const [art, a] of links) a.classList.toggle('here', art === e.target); },
  { rootMargin: '-30% 0px -65% 0px' });
links.forEach(([art]) => spy.observe(art));
const rv = new IntersectionObserver(es => es.forEach(e => { if (e.isIntersecting) { e.target.classList.add('in'); rv.unobserve(e.target); } }),
  { rootMargin: '0px 0px -8% 0px' });
document.querySelectorAll('article').forEach(el => { el.classList.add('reveal'); rv.observe(el); });
</script>
<script>
/* the theme switch: the other theme than the one showing, kept for next time */
(() => {
  const btn = document.getElementById('theme'), root = document.documentElement;
  const dark = () => root.dataset.theme ? root.dataset.theme === 'dark' : matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches;
  const label = () => btn.setAttribute('aria-label', dark() ? 'Light mode' : 'Dark mode');
  label();
  const flip = () => {
    root.dataset.theme = dark() ? 'light' : 'dark';
    try { localStorage.setItem('yw4-theme', root.dataset.theme); } catch (e) {}
    label();
  };
  /* a slow cross-fade between the themes (site.css sets its length), where the browser can do one */
  btn.addEventListener('click', () => {
    if (document.startViewTransition && !matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches) document.startViewTransition(flip);
    else flip();
  });
})();
</script>
</body>
</html>
```

```html
<script>
/* the theme switch: the other theme than the one showing, kept for next time */
(() => {
  const btn = document.getElementById('theme'), root = document.documentElement;
  const dark = () => root.dataset.theme ? root.dataset.theme === 'dark' : matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches;
  const label = () => btn.setAttribute('aria-label', dark() ? 'Light mode' : 'Dark mode');
  label();
  const flip = () => {
    root.dataset.theme = dark() ? 'light' : 'dark';
    try { localStorage.setItem('yw4-theme', root.dataset.theme); } catch (e) {}
    label();
  };
  /* a slow cross-fade between the themes (site.css sets its length), where the browser can do one */
  btn.addEventListener('click', () => {
    if (document.startViewTransition && !matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches) document.startViewTransition(flip);
    else flip();
  });
})();
</script>
```

`docs/debugging.md`:

```md
# Run options and debugging

Environment variables and keys read by the runtime. The game runs fine with none of them set. Tools that run the
game with them and compare results: [tools/dev](../tools/dev/README.md).

Which build is running ([decision 0047](decisions/0047-versioning.md)): `yw4 --version` prints one line
(`YW4 Recomp 0.7.0 (a8b8184, built 2026-11-03)`) without starting the game; the log's first lines and the
window title say the same. The number is the repo's `VERSION` file; `+dirty` means uncommitted changes.

Where the game looks for its own files ([decision 0048](decisions/0048-home-folder-and-icon.md)): every `work/...`
path is relative to its home folder, which it changes to at start (the log's `yw4: home` line): `YW4_HOME=<folder>`
if set, else the folder above `work/` when `yw4.exe` is in `<home>/work/build/`. Relative paths in the variables
below are relative to it too. The three folders on the command line are made absolute first.

Started with no arguments (a double-click, a shortcut), the game reads `game.ini` next to `yw4.exe`
([decision 0050](decisions/0050-launcher-and-install-layout.md)): one `YW4_...=value` per line, any variable on
this page, plus `YW4_EXEFS`, `YW4_ROMFS` and `YW4_SAVE` for the three folders. Paths are relative to `game.ini`'s
folder; a variable already in the environment wins. Without it a message says to run the launcher.

The save folder is optional, on the command line and in `game.ini`: without one the saves go to
`$XDG_DATA_HOME/YW4Recomp/save` (`~/.local/share/YW4Recomp/save`) on Linux, `%APPDATA%/YW4 Recomp/save` on Windows.
The log's `yw4: saves in` line names the folder used.

For reports from other PCs, the log's `window:` lines near the start name the GPU, the driver and its version
(`driver radv, Mesa 25.1.4`), the window system (`windows`, `wayland`, `x11`) and every screen format the driver
offers as `format/colour space` numbers (Vulkan's `VkFormat` / `VkColorSpaceKHR`: 44 = B8G8R8A8_UNORM,
37 = R8G8B8A8_UNORM, 50 = B8G8R8A8_SRGB; colour space 0 = sRGB, others are HDR, extended or linear ones). The
game uses an 8-bit UNORM format in colour space 0; any other choice makes the colours look wrong (pale), and the
line then says WARNING.

## Everyday options

| Variable | What it does |
|---|---|
| `YW4_SETTINGS_FILE=<file>` (`none`) | Where the settings panel's choices are kept (default `settings.ini` next to `yw4.exe`): read at start, written on every change in the panel, one `YW4_...=value` line per setting. A variable set in the environment wins over its line. `tools.dev.run` sets `none`, so test runs neither read nor change the owner's file |
| `YW4_FIRST_RUN_LEVEL=low` (`high`) | Tests: a new install's first start (no settings file yet: point `YW4_SETTINGS_FILE` at a file that doesn't exist) as on that kind of GPU. Without it the GPU decides: integrated, or under 4 GB of video memory, is low (shadow map 1024, soft and contact shadows off, effects half); else the high defaults stay. The file is then written, so it runs once, and a notice fades in at the top for about 6 s (screenshots include it). [Decision 0062](decisions/0062-first-start-graphics.md) |
| `YW4_SCREENSHOTS=600,2500` | Save a screenshot at these frame numbers (also F12 at any time) |
| `YW4_SCREENSHOT_DIR=path` | Where screenshots go (default `<work_dir>/screenshots/`) |
| `YW4_THEME=id` | The overlay's and the HUD's theme (Settings > Look > Theme, saved in settings.ini): `recomp` (built in) or a file's name in the themes folder, e.g. `jibanyan` ([decision 0055](decisions/0055-overlay-themes.md)) |
| `YW4_THEMES_DIR=path` | The themes folder (the launcher's `.css` files); else `themes` next to yw4.exe, else the repo's `launcher/ui/themes`. The log says which: `yw4: themes: 11 (...)` |
| `YW4_FLASH=1` | **Flash detector** (`runtime/src/window.c`): every presented frame also goes into a 320-wide thumbnail, read back one frame later without stalling. A frame where many thumbnail texels are brighter than in both the frame before and after is logged (`yw4: flash: frame N ...` with the area) and the three thumbnails are saved to the screenshot folder (`flash_<frame>_a_before/b_flash/c_after.bmp`, first 40). `YW4_FLASH_THRESHOLD` (brighter by, of 255, default 40) and `YW4_FLASH_MIN` (texels per mille, default 3) tune it. Sees the game's frames, not DLSS-G's generated ones |
| `YW4_MINIMAP_WATCH=1` `YW4_MINIMAP_DIR=path` | **Minimap watch** (`runtime/src/gpu_watch.c`; run it with `python -m tools.dev.minimap`, which also prints the report): every frame, for each of the minimap's own images (340x304, 516x460): the draws into it, its clears, the draws that put it on screen, texture slots with nothing behind them, textures uploaded in that frame, and the image itself read back two frames later (texels lit and opaque, per mille). Rows in `minimap_draws.csv` and `minimap_pixels.csv` in that folder (default `work/minimap`); when a count or the picture drops: an event (`minimap`), the pictures before / blank / after (`minimap_<frame>_<size>_*.bmp`, first 40) and the draws of the frames around it with their textures, vertices and constant buffers (`minimap_<frame>_draws.txt`) |
| `YW4_PERF=0` / `YW4_PERF=1` | `0` turns off the performance log; `1` adds the per-frame `work/perf/perf_<time>.csv` (the dev tools set it: 17-30 MB an hour of play, so players don't get it; a player asked for one adds the line `YW4_PERF=1` to their `settings.ini`, which the game keeps when it saves). On by default without the CSV: a `.txt` summary (the whole run counted as it goes, in 0.1 ms steps, so memory stays the same however long it runs) and `.jsonl` events: frame interval, game work, GPU busy/span from timestamp queries, time in command-list translation and GPU waits, CPU, memory; every 600 frames stderr also lists each busy guest thread's share of a core; `YW4_PERF_DIR` moves it) |
| `YW4_EXIT_AT=<frame>` | Tests: the game exits cleanly once that frame has been presented (`tools.dev.scene` sets it to the last scheduled frame). At a clean exit the log lists what was scheduled for a frame the run never got to (`yw4: never reached: YW4_SCREENSHOTS frame 900`): screenshots, `YW4_SET_AT`, image dumps, A/B frames |
| `YW4_TEST_GPU_CRASH_AT=<frame>` | Tests: at that frame the game ends as if the GPU were lost (exit code 3), to check the `yw4: gpu crash:` lines a real GPU error writes: the picture and shadow settings, video memory and its peak, and the last frames' GPU times. The picture settings are also logged as `yw4: picture:` at the first frame and on every change, and head each perf summary |
| (the events file) | Next to each `perf_<time>.csv`, `perf_<time>.jsonl`: one JSON line per thing that happened (screenshot, setting change, stall with its cause, same-frame A/B count, fatal stop, end), written as it happens (`runtime/src/events.h`). The test tools read it instead of the log's text |
| `YW4_PROFILE=1` | Sample where the presenting (main) thread is every millisecond (Windows; `YW4_PROFILE=submit`: the threads that submit GPU work), from frame `YW4_PROFILE_FROM` if set; `work/perf/profile_<time>.txt`, named with `python -m tools.yw4.profile` |
| `YW4_PROFILE_THREAD=<n>` | With `YW4_PROFILE=submit`: sample only guest thread n (the number in the performance report's thread lines; the busiest render thread is usually 20) |
| `YW4_PROFILE=hitch` | Sample every guest thread but keep only the samples of frames longer than `YW4_PROFILE_HITCH_MS` (default 100): what the game did in a freeze. Each kept frame is logged (`yw4: profile: frame N took M ms`) |
| `YW4_PACE=refresh` (`tick`) | How FRAME RATE 30 and 60 are held: by a deadline whose period is a whole number of the display's refreshes (from Quandiy's fork), or by the emulated 60 Hz vsync tick. Unset: refresh at 30, the tick at 60 (measured, decision 0064); `refresh` or `tick` uses that way at both. For comparing the two ([decision 0064](decisions/0064-pacing-tick-or-refresh.md)): the log says which at the first frame (`yw4: pacing: tick ...` / `yw4: pacing: refresh, period 16.667 ms at 120.00 Hz ...`), and each performance summary has a line `pacing <way> at <cap> frames/s: N frames over 25 ms = x%, standard deviation y ms` (over 50 ms at 30) |
| `YW4_STALL_MS=<n>` | Hitches: a `yw4: stall:` line when a frame's work on the GPU thread (its command lists and present) takes over n ms (default 50; 0 = never), with where it went: waiting for the GPU lock, waiting for the GPU, pipelines built, shaders loaded, images made (with their uploads), texture uploads, and what that leaves. Found on 2026-11-02: images freed in bulk every 300 frames (now a few a frame) and an area's few hundred new textures at once. Outside that timing, also a `stall:` line when the window's present plus Reflex's sleep take over 30 ms, a `window: slow present:` line splitting the present, and every swapchain rebuild logs its frame and time |
| `YW4_GPU_DETILE=0` | Textures out of the game's block-linear layout on the CPU (`tegra.c`) only. By default the GPU does it (`runtime/shaders/detile.comp`): it reads a level straight from the game's pool into a 64 MiB ring in video memory, copied into the image after; levels whose rows aren't whole 16-byte pieces, 12-byte texels, and textures that find the ring busy stay on the CPU. An area's 380 new textures: 168-185 ms in one frame before, 105 ms after |
| `YW4_IMAGE_BLOCKS=0` | Every image its own video-memory allocation. By default images up to 16 MiB take slices of shared 64 MiB blocks (`gpu.c` `image_memory`): an allocation each cost ~40 ms of an area's 380 new textures. Every 600 frames a `yw4: vram:` line (with `VK_EXT_memory_budget`) gives the video memory in use, its peak since the last line, the driver's budget, the blocks and the de-tiling ring |
| `YW4_DETILE_CHECK=1` | Every texture the GPU de-tiles is also de-tiled on the CPU and the two compared byte for byte once the GPU is done (`yw4: detile check:` lines every 500 textures and at any difference). Slower |
| `YW4_TEGRA_CHECK=1` | Every texture read out of the game's block-linear layout (`runtime/src/tegra.c`) is done again the general way and compared; `yw4: tegra check:` lines every 2000 reads and at any difference |
| `YW4_WAITPROF=1` | With the performance summary every 600 frames: where the main thread blocked in the kernel (SleepThread, WaitSynchronization, ArbitrateLock, WaitProcessWideKeyAtomic, WaitForAddress), ms per frame and calls per frame per guest call stack, with the address waited on; and the SignalToAddress calls per signalling thread, address and call stack (who wakes those waits) |
| `YW4_SHORT_SLEEP=0` | Sleeps under 0.2 ms use Windows' timer again (~0.5 ms at least). By default they yield and check the clock: the game's main thread polls its jobs with `nn::os::SleepThread(1 us)`, and each poll used to oversleep (busy late-game spot, DLSS P, unlimited: 61 -> 77 frames/s) |

| `YW4_AB_AT=<GPU frame>[,...]` or `<from>-<to>` `YW4_AB_PASS=gbuffer\|material\|shadow` | **Same-frame A/B** (`runtime/src/gpu_ab.c`), with our pass on (`YW4_GBUFFER=native`): in those frames the pass's commands run twice from the same images, with our draws and with the game's, and every target is compared texel by texel (`yw4: ab:` lines; 0 = identical). Saved screenshots get the same sRGB decode as the window, so their colours match what is on screen.

## Capture keys

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| F12 | Screenshot of the next frame, as the window shows it: the HUD, the in-game overlay (also F2's quick look) and the corner notice included. `YW4_SHOT_MENU=0`: the game's picture and HUD only |
| F11 | Full screen or a window (the settings panel's WINDOW MODE row, saved; `YW4_WINDOW`) |
| Shift+F11 | Describe the draws of the next frame in the log (F11 until 2026-11-03; still `F11` in recordings): targets, shaders, textures, the vertex stage's matrices (`YW4_GPU_TRACE=<n>` with `YW4_GPU_TRACE_AT=<frame>` does the same from a start frame) |
| F10 | Dump multi-layer depth images (shadow maps) to `work/dump/*.pgm` |
| F1 | Settings panel, the only place for the graphics settings (the other keys here are debugging tools): the graphics settings in groups (display, anti-aliasing and upscaling, frame generation and latency, detail, shadows), every option shown, the current one on a chip, and a box explaining the chosen setting and option; scaled up with the window by whole steps; Up/Down choose, Left/Right change, F1 or Escape close. The last row, DEVELOPER OPTIONS (Enter or Right), opens a page with the switches players don't need: who draws each pass (shadow pass, G-buffer, bloom, distance blur pass: the game or ours) and BATTLE BLUR; Escape or B goes back. Replays that reach a setting by counting rows (`UP`/`DOWN`) follow this order. On a gamepad the panel opens from the in-game overlay (Escape row); in it L/R or the triggers switch pages; the D-pad or left stick choose and change; B closes. While it is open neither the keyboard nor the gamepad reaches the game, and after it closes they stay held back until everything is let go (so the B or Escape that closed it doesn't reach the game too). F2 opens the CONTROLS page instead (F1 and F2 switch between the pages, the same key again closes; on a gamepad L/R switch) (`runtime/src/bindings.c`): per Switch button and stick direction two keys and one gamepad input (a button, or a stick or trigger direction; sticks stay analog); Enter (A) waits five seconds for the new key or input, Delete/Backspace (X) clears, the last row resets all; a key or input that presses two Switch inputs shows orange. The panel's own keys stay fixed. Choices and controls are saved (`YW4_SETTINGS_FILE`). In replays: `k <tick> F1`, then `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `ENTER`, `DELETE`, `F2`, `PAGE` (a binding itself can't be captured from a replay) (`runtime/src/settings.c`) |
| F2 | While playing (LEGACY MENUS off): a quick look at the keys, the game not paused, but the keyboard, mouse and controller kept from it while the card shows (and after, until everything is let go), so a key pressed to see it light up does nothing in the game (the cursor stays free to point at keys: Alt doesn't hand the mouse to the camera then, and moving it never turns the camera): the keyboard and the mouse with the bound keys lit and what each does, centred over the blurred picture, opening in the game's current mode (a battle's keys during one, else exploring's), which its Exploring / Battle / Cutscene switch changes (a click; on a pad a short press of View / Create / Minus goes round the pages and holding it half a second hides the card; no keys; replays `KV_NEXT`); a key or click shows the keyboard's view, a pad button or stick the controller's; F2 again hides it, Esc opens the overlay. In the overlay, F2 opens the Controls page: the Bindings table, and a Keyboard view button (P, Y / Triangle) showing the same keyboard with an Exploring / Battle / Cutscene switch (Q / E, LB / RB) and, under the mouse, what a key does. The names are the owner's (`kv_action` in `runtime/src/gamemenu.c`); a key whose input has no name isn't lit |
| `YW4_TITLE_KEYS=Down,A,Left,A` | The overlay's **Return to title** (above Exit game; greyed out, and passed over by the keys and the mouse, where the game has no pause screen: the title screen, cutscenes, or while its pause still opens): after its popup ("Last saved ... ago": the game's last save Commit, else its save's newest file, `savefs.c`) the game's own pause screen, still open behind the kept picture, is answered with these buttons, 0.25 s apart, 0.6 s after an A (a window may open: default Down to Return to Title, A, Left to Yes in the game's Yes / No window, where No is chosen first, A). The kept picture stays up until half a second after the last button, about 1.75 s in all: the game's menu state doesn't end on its way to the title, so nothing else says it is done (`window.c`, `pause.c` PAUSE_TITLE). The log: `yw4: pause: return to title, button N of 4`, `yw4: fs: the game saved (Commit)` |
| Escape | The in-game overlay ([decision 0053](decisions/0053-in-game-overlay.md); `runtime/src/gamemenu.c`, drawn by `ui.c` as its design on the overlay's design canvas): a side panel over the paused game (the F4 pause) with Resume, Settings (its page: the player's settings by section, as the F1 panel's), Controls (the bindings as a table: Enter waits for the new key or input, Delete clears), Overlay (the performance HUD's form, corner and parts, with a live preview), Report a bug (not built yet: a note says so; F12 takes screenshots) and Exit game (with Keep playing / Quit game). Escape and Backspace go back one step (a page's rows to its sections, a page to the side panel, the side panel to the game); Resume also closes it. Keys: W/S or the arrows choose, A/D or Left/Right change (D or Right also opens a page), Enter or Space select (on a setting: its next option), Q/E jump between sections; Settings opens on its section list (Enter or Right into the rows). Held direction keys, the D-pad and the stick repeat; lists stop at their ends. The mouse: hovering chooses, a click selects (the value arrows, the hint bar, sliders by click or drag), the right button goes back, the wheel scrolls the Controls table (one row a notch; nothing elsewhere); hovering never scrolls it. The hints follow the device used last. Settings has **Preview** (P, Y / Triangle, or its button; not for Advanced): the game runs again with the player held still and a bar at the bottom with the chosen graphics section's rows, its description and the frame rate, so each change shows live; W/S choose, A/D change, Q/E the graphics sections, H (Y / Triangle) hides the bar, Escape or B pauses again and goes back to Settings (`gamemenu.c` draw_preview; window.c shows only `gamemenu_preview_rect`'s part over the live picture). In replays: `k <tick> PAUSE` ([`runtime/src/pause.c`](../runtime/src/pause.c), `runtime/src/window.c`) |
| F5 | Per-pass GPU timing on or off (`YW4_GPU_PASSES`): where the GPU's time goes, in the log every 300 frames |

## Recording and replaying input

| Variable | What it does |
|---|---|
| `YW4_RECORD=0` | Every input change and capture key is recorded in `work/inputs/rec_<time>.txt` (on by default); this turns it off |
| `YW4_PLAYER_NAME=<name>` | The game's name entry (a new game asks the boy's and the girl's names) answers this at once instead of showing the name popup. In replays the popup isn't shown either (their clock counts frames, which stop while the game waits): they answer "Nate", then "Katie". `YW4_NAME_PROMPT=1` shows the popup in replays too (`runtime/src/swkbd.c`). Its on-screen keyboard shows while a controller is in use; `YW4_OSK=1` shows it with any device (tests: its keys can be clicked) |
| `YW4_REPORT_DIR=<folder>` | Where the overlay's Report a bug saves its zips (default `reports` in the home folder; `runtime/src/bugreport.c`). `YW4_REPORT_OPEN=0`: Send and Show the zip only write the link in the log instead of opening the browser or Explorer (test runs) |
| `YW4_REPLAY=<file>` | Feed a recording back, so a route can be run without a person. While it plays, the game's main loop runs on a clock of exactly 1/60 s per frame and the recording's ticks are taken as frames, so a route ends in the same place every run (`runtime/src/kernel.c` `yw4_replay_frame_clock`); the game's time then follows its frames, not the wall. When the replay ends, real time again, and the keyboard and gamepad work again, so a short recording can just load the save. Text typed into the overlay's fields is recorded as `t <tick> <text>` lines and its editing keys as `T_LEFT`, `T_RIGHT`, `T_HOME`, `T_END`, `T_BACK`, `T_DEL`, `T_DONE` (`runtime/src/textin.h`). Videos play on real time, so during a replay they blink and stutter against the game's frame time (only then) |
| `YW4_REPLAY_CLOCK=real` | The replay on the wall clock instead (before 2026-10-31): routes drift with loading and shader-build times |
| `YW4_REPLAY_HZ=<rate>` with `YW4_REPLAY_HZ_AT=<frame>` | During a frame-clock replay, from that presented frame on each frame moves the game's clock 1/rate s instead of 1/60, so a route loads at 60 and then plays as at another frame rate (`runtime/src/kernel.c`; [decision 0069](decisions/0069-motion-least-time.md)). `YW4_DT_LOG=1` shows the step the game got |
| `YW4_MOUSE=0` | The game never takes the mouse: no capture, camera, clicks or wheel (`tools.dev.run` sets it, so the PC can be used during test runs) |
| `YW4_RUMBLE=0` | Turn off controller vibration/rumble (default 1, on; [decision 0058](decisions/0058-controller-rumble.md)) |
| `YW4_RUMBLE_GAIN=<float>` | Scale vibration intensity on the host gamepad (default 1.0; e.g. 0.5 for half strength, 1.5 for stronger rumble) |
| `YW4_RUMBLE_SHAPE=0` | The game's vibration as sent (linear), instead of shaped for PC pads' motors: faint texture dropped, a kick at each swell's start, cut while it fades ([decision 0058](decisions/0058-controller-rumble.md), 2026-11-10) |
| `YW4_RUMBLE_TRIGGERS=0` | Xbox One / Series pads: no trigger-motor kicks for the high band (default on) |
| `YW4_NINTENDO_LAYOUT=1` | A controller that reports as an Xbox pad gets the Switch's button icons and names, so hints match the letters printed on a Switch-style pad; the buttons keep their places (the bottom one confirms). For Switch-style pads that show up as an Xbox 360 controller on PC (vendor 045e, product 028e). The Controls page's CONTROLLER NINTENDO ICONS row; `python -m tools.dev.padtest` shows what a pad reports |
| `YW4_RUMBLE_LOG=1` | A log line per change: what the game asked (both bands' amplitude and frequency) and the motor and trigger speeds sent |
| `YW4_INPUT=2400:1:10` | Scripted presses, `tick:buttons(hex):length`, comma separated; `1` is A |

## Looking inside a frame

| Variable | What it does |
|---|---|
| `YW4_DUMP_IMAGE=<hex addr>[,<hex addr>...]` `YW4_DUMP_IMAGE_AT=<frame>[,<frame>...]` | Read back the images at those guest addresses at that frame (several frames: the file names get `_f<frame>`) (depth, RGBA8, RGBA16F, R11G11B10F): per-layer min/max/cleared share, `work/dump/image_*.pgm`, and raw floats in `image_*.rgbaf` (colour) or `image_*.depthf` (depth). This is the image's last use in the frame |
| `YW4_CAPTURE_FS=<fs key prefix>[,...]` with `YW4_DUMP_IMAGE_AT=<frame>[,...]` | Copy the colour targets right after each draw with that fragment shader in those frames (up to 64), to `work/dump/cap_<n>_<fs>_f<frame>_t<target>.raw`; shows a pass's output before later passes reuse the target. `python -m tools.yw4.capview` makes a contact sheet |
| `YW4_COMPUTE_TRACE=<n>` | Every n frames, the inputs and results of the last dispatch of each compute shader |

Image addresses and shader keys come from the Shift+F11 log. Shaders are named by the FNV-1a hash of their assembly:
`work/shaders/asm/<key>.<stage>.asm` is the original, `work/shaders/glsl/<key>.<stage>` the translation (one GLSL
statement per instruction, with the source as a comment).

## Tracing and probes

`YW4_TRACE_*`, `YW4_PROBE*`, `YW4_WATCH*` (guest write watch with a call stack; one per process) and
`YW4_GPU_TRACE*` are described where they are read in `runtime/src/`. `YW4_PROBE` lines show x0 to x3, s0 to s2 and the presented frame; `YW4_PROBE_X0=<hex>` keeps
only the calls on that object; `YW4_PROBE_DUMP=<bytes>` prints that many bytes at x0, or at the pointer chain
`YW4_PROBE_DUMP_PTR=<off>[,<off>]`, as floats on each call (diff two runs to find a field;
[decision 0069](decisions/0069-motion-least-time.md)). To name a guest address in a log, pipe it
through `python -m tools.yw4.where -`.

Two of them map the engine's frame ([frame.md](frame.md)):

| Variable | What it does |
|---|---|
| `YW4_TRACE_LAYERS=<frame>` | Every layer the model renderer (`f_a45890`) draws while frames `<frame>` to `<frame>+2` are presented: thread, layer kind, key range, mask and submeshes drawn. Maps layer kinds to passes ([frame.md](frame.md)) |
| `YW4_TRACE_RENDER_JOBS=<frame>` | Every job the render threads run while frames `<frame>` to `<frame>+2` are presented: function, its two arguments, the thread. Slows the game a little (a check at every function entry) |
| `YW4_COUNTER_LOG=<from>-<to>` | The game's occlusion queries in those GPU frames (`runtime/src/gpu_query.c`): one line per pair of `ReportCounter(SAMPLES_PASSED)` calls (address, draws between them, target) and per `SetRenderEnableConditional` (the first 40 of a frame), then a line per frame: pairs, conditions, draws under a condition and how many of those the count in memory would skip. A count shown is what the game's memory holds at that moment; the GPU writes it later, so it is an earlier frame's (the game rotates through 4 sets of addresses). Evening town street: 270 pairs, 920 conditions, 878 draws, 498 skipped |
| `YW4_TRACE_DRAW_CALLERS=1` | Each different call stack that records a draw, once per render-target size and program, with the shaders; `python -m tools.yw4.mainview <log>` groups such a log (with `YW4_GPU_TRACE`) into passes with the drawing functions |
| `YW4_TRACE_DRAWLIST=<frame>` | From that frame, the model renderer's draws (`YW4_TRACE_DRAWLIST_MAX`, default 24): what was bound, the submesh record, and where in the draw object, geometry and submesh records the bound addresses and uniform-buffer contents are found (pointer search two levels deep), the engine's texture slots, the model record's texture table and a texture view's words. `YW4_TRACE_DRAWLIST_COLOURS=3` keeps only draws into 3 colour targets (the G-buffer). Slow while it prints |
```
