`docs/decisions/0076-sharpening.md`:

```md
# 0076 — SHARPENING: one setting after every anti-aliasing

<!-- decision
state: accepted
date: 2026-11-15
replaces: none
code: runtime/src/gpu_aa.c, runtime/shaders/sharpen.glsl, runtime/shaders/taa_output.frag, runtime/shaders/ui_sharpen.frag, runtime/src/gpu.c, runtime/src/settings.c, runtime/src/gpu_draw.c, runtime/src/gpu_post.c
-->

Status: accepted (owner, 2026-11-15, through the relay session). Measured in the game on every anti-aliasing
(below); not yet seen by the owner on screen.

## Context

GitHub issue #11: a player found the game a little soft even with DLSS at native resolution (DLAA), and compared it
with an emulator using FSR's sharpening. What the port did before this:

- **TAA**: a fixed sharpen in its last pass (`taa_output.frag`, 0.5, only `YW4_TAA_SHARPEN` changed it).
- **FSR**: FSR's own sharpener (RCAS) at 0.5, only `YW4_FSR_SHARPNESS` changed it.
- **DLSS**: none. NVIDIA took the sharpening out of DLSS (2.5.1 and later), and our pass after it ran with 0. So the
  best-looking mode was the softest one.
- **OFF / FXAA / SMAA**: none.

## Decision

A **SHARPENING** row in the settings (ANTI-ALIASING AND UPSCALING, under UPSCALING): **OFF / LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH /
MAX** = 0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 1.0, default **MEDIUM**. It is a list of options rather than a slider (the owner's
choice: five steps are easy to tell apart and to talk about). It is never greyed out: the same choice applies to every
anti-aliasing, OFF included. Saved as `YW4_SHARPEN=0..4`.

Where it happens:

| Anti-aliasing | Sharpening |
|---|---|
| TAA | its last pass (`taa_output.frag`), as before, now with the setting's amount |
| DLSS | the same pass, which already copied DLSS's output back: nothing extra to run |
| FSR | FSR's own RCAS, with its own table of amounts (below; 0 turns it off). Not our pass too: sharpening twice brings rings and grain |
| OFF | the scene encoded (as for the others) and our pass: two full-screen passes |
| FXAA / SMAA | their result encoded again and our pass |

With OFF, the two places that start the anti-aliasing (`gpu_draw.c`, `gpu_post.c`) used to skip it. They now always
call `gpu_aa_apply`, which returns at once when nothing (anti-aliasing, upscaling, sharpening) is on.

The sharpen (`sharpen.glsl`, used by `taa_output.frag`) became **contrast-adaptive**, after the method AMD published as FidelityFX CAS (our
code, from the idea). The old one pushed every pixel away from its four neighbours' average by the same amount. The
new one scales that push by `sqrt(darkest / brightest)` of the 3x3 neighbourhood, in the perceptual curve (`aa.glsl`,
values 0..1). Soft, flat detail (textures) gets the full push, and edges with strong contrast get little, so they
don't ring. As before, the result is clamped to the four neighbours' range, so it adds no bright or dark rims. The
push is 2 x the amount where the area is flat (MEDIUM 1.0, MAX 2.0), so MEDIUM sharpens textures about as much as
the old fixed 0.5 did, and edges less.

Why the clamp and not CAS's own way of limiting: CAS limits its weight so the result can't leave 0..1. Our curve
already keeps it in range, and the clamp is what kept TAA free of rims before. It costs nothing extra (the min and
max are already there).

### FSR's own table

FSR's RCAS grows much faster with its amount than our pass: its amount is in stops of 2x, and nothing holds the result
to the neighbours' range. With the plain 0.25 a step, FSR's MAX (1.0) added 142% detail where DLSS's added 50-64%, and
looked crunchy. FSR now gets **LOW 0.25 / MEDIUM 0.5 / HIGH 0.6 / MAX 0.7**: measured to add about as much at each step
as DLSS and TAA (table below). `YW4_FSR_SHARPEN_MAP=<low>,<medium>,<high>,<max>` replaces it, for measuring.

### SHARPEN TEXT AND MENUS

Where things are drawn: the game draws the 3D into its scene image, our anti-aliasing (and with it every sharpening
above, FSR's RCAS included) runs on that image right after the bloom composite, then the game draws its UI (HUD,
menus, text) into the same image and copies the whole into the window image that is presented. So until this record,
**nothing of the UI was sharpened**, in any mode. Our own overlay (settings, controls, F3 HUD) is drawn later still,
onto the window (`window.c`).

Some players at low resolutions want the text sharpened too. A row **SHARPEN TEXT AND MENUS < OFF / ON >**, right
under SHARPENING, default **OFF**, saved as `YW4_SHARPEN_UI=0/1`, greyed out while SHARPENING is OFF. With ON:

- At the anti-aliasing point, the 3D as it is there (already sharpened) is copied into an image like the window image,
  where the window shows it: the same copy frame generation makes as its HUD-less image (`gpu_fg.c`).
- At the present (`gpu_present`, before the captures, screenshots and frame generation), `ui_sharpen.frag` sharpens the
  window image with the same filter and amount, in its own values, **only where it differs from that copy** (by more
  than 1.5/255): the pixels the UI drew. The 3D is left as it was, so it isn't sharpened twice, and frame generation's
  HUD-less image still matches the 3D of the picture it gets.
- A frame with no 3D (the title, full-screen menus, videos) has no copy: it is sharpened whole.

Why not one pass over the finished picture instead of two places: the 3D would then be sharpened by our filter after
the UI, FSR's RCAS would have to step aside, and the HUD-less image frame generation compares with would differ from
the picture everywhere (FSR's frame generation reads such differences as UI). Why not the 3D again with the UI: twice
sharpened is grainy.

`YW4_TAA_SHARPEN` (our pass: TAA, DLSS, OFF, FXAA, SMAA, text and menus) and `YW4_FSR_SHARPNESS` (FSR) still override
the amount with any value, for testing.

## Alternatives

- **A slider** (0..1 in steps of 0.05): the first plan. The owner chose five fixed steps.
- **Only for TAA / FSR / DLSS, greyed out otherwise**: also in the first plan. The owner wanted it everywhere: OFF and
  FXAA are soft too (FXAA blurs textures a little), and a greyed-out row needs explaining.
- **NVIDIA's sharpening**: DLSS no longer has one, and NVIDIA's NIS is another library for the same job as a few
  lines of shader.
- **Our pass after FSR as well**: FSR already has a sharpener made for its output. Running both would sharpen twice.
- **Default 0 for DLSS** (no change for DLSS players): the owner picked MEDIUM for all. DLSS was the softest mode.

## Measurements

The school scene (`tools.dev.scene school`, the schoolyard by day), 3840x2160, one run per anti-aliasing. In each run
the setting changes at fixed frames (`YW4_SET_AT`), so MEDIUM, OFF and MAX are pictures of the same place a few
seconds apart. "Detail" is the mean absolute Laplacian of the brightness over a brick wall (higher = crisper; the
character and the camera move a little between the shots, the wall doesn't change).

| Anti-aliasing | Detail OFF | MEDIUM | MAX | GPU time of the sharpening at 4K |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OFF | 5.47 | 7.68 (+40%) | 8.95 (+64%) | 0.65-0.7 ms (encode + our pass) |
| FXAA | 5.28 | 7.39 (+40%) | 8.60 (+63%) | ~0.65 ms (encoded again + our pass) |
| SMAA | 5.37 | 7.59 (+41%) | 8.79 (+64%) | ~0.6 ms |
| TAA | 3.75 | 5.16 (+38%) | 6.15 (+64%) | inside TAA's last pass, as before |
| FSR | 4.74 | 6.24 (+32%) | 11.47 (+142%) | inside FSR (its RCAS), as before |
| DLSS (DLAA) | 3.80 | 4.94 (+30%) | 5.71 (+50%) | the write-back pass 0.16 -> 0.30 ms |
| DLSS Quality | 3.60 | 5.02 (+39%) | 5.82 (+62%) | 0.30 ms |

- That first table had FSR at 0.25 a step. MEDIUM added about the same everywhere (+30-40%), but FSR's MAX added 142%
  and looked crunchy (dark specks along shadow edges): hence FSR's own table.
- The cost is a fraction of a millisecond at 4K: about a quarter of that at 1080p.
- What also makes the background soft is the game's own DISTANCE BLUR (on, at HALF, by default). Sharpening doesn't
  undo it; DISTANCE BLUR set to OFF does. Worth telling a player who finds the picture soft.
- The full test suite passes (`pytest tests`: 66 tests), with a test for the row (`tests/test_settings_texts.py`).

### Every level, FSR on its own table (second round)

Same scene and method, the setting stepped OFF, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, MAX every 40 frames in one run; detail gained
over OFF, averaged over three areas (a brick wall, the ground, a house):

| | LOW | MEDIUM | HIGH | MAX |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DLSS (DLAA) | +17% | +29% | +39% | +49% |
| TAA | +20% | +36% | +50% | +61% |
| FSR, 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.6 / 0.7 (chosen) | +21% | +35% | +43% | +58% |
| FSR, 0.35 / 0.55 / 0.65 / 0.8 (tried) | +24% | +39% | +46% | +73% |

The chosen table falls between DLSS and TAA at every step; FSR at MAX no longer looks crunchy.

### SHARPEN TEXT AND MENUS, OFF against ON (MEDIUM, TAA)

| 3D view | 3D (brick wall) | Minimap | Objective text | GPU time of the pass |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1600x900 | 7.42 -> 7.34 (same) | +18% | +18% | not timed |
| 1920x1080 | 7.19 -> 7.15 (same) | +13% | +18% | 0.31-0.34 ms |
| 3840x2160 | 5.19 -> 5.20 (same) | +25% | +20% | 0.80 ms |

The 3D measures the same with ON (not sharpened twice); the UI is crisper. The copy at the anti-aliasing point adds a
blit of the 3D (counted in the anti-aliasing's own line). A 720p window was not run: 900 lines is the smallest picture
the game draws, and a smaller window only shows it scaled down after the sharpening, so it should look like the
900-line row made smaller. Seen at 4x zoom: the filter works per colour channel (as
CAS does), so hard UI edges can get a faint coloured edge; at normal size it doesn't show.

## Follow-up 2026-11-16: DLSS's own steps, and FSR's method for our pass

The player on #11 found FSR sharper after this record but DLSS "kinda the same". Measured at 1080p (school scene,
upscaling off, same method; wall / boy / ground / house): DLSS on MAX (10.0 / 11.2 / 4.7 / 6.5) was about FSR on
MEDIUM (10.3 / 10.1 / 5.7 / 7.0). Both add about the same share of detail per step; DLSS's picture simply starts
15-30% softer than FSR's (OFF: 6.6 / 7.5 / 3.2 / 4.4 against 7.8 / 8.0 / 4.2 / 5.4), so matching steps by the share
gained left DLSS a step behind everywhere.

- **Our pass now uses RCAS's method** (`sharpen.glsl`: FSR's own sharpener, AMD FidelityFX, MIT): one weight for the
  three colours, as large as keeps the result in 0..1, at most 0.1875, scaled by FSR's sharpness in stops. The clamped
  push from above measured about the same at a given step, but pushed further it went blocky (tree trunks at 2.5x MAX)
  and still stayed under FSR on soft ground; RCAS reaches FSR's look cleanly. Every mode now takes FSR's amounts:
  **LOW 0.25 / MEDIUM 0.5 / HIGH 0.6 / MAX 0.7** (`YW4_SHARPEN_MAP`).
- **DLSS gets its own steps: 0.6 / 0.75 / 0.8 / 0.85** (`YW4_DLSS_SHARPEN_MAP`), measured so each looks about as sharp
  as FSR at the same step. 0.85 is still clean; 1.0 puts bright rims on edges.

| 1080p | wall | boy | ground | house |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DLSS OFF | 6.64 | 7.49 | 3.18 | 4.40 |
| DLSS LOW (0.6) | 9.43 | 10.73 | 4.54 | 6.13 |
| DLSS MEDIUM (0.75) | 10.93 | 12.47 | 5.28 | 7.06 |
| DLSS HIGH (0.8) | 11.62 | 13.31 | 5.67 | 7.55 |
| DLSS MAX (0.85) | 12.62 | 14.47 | 6.15 | 8.13 |
| FSR LOW | 9.28 | 9.42 | 5.00 | 6.35 |
| FSR MEDIUM | 10.26 | 10.21 | 5.69 | 7.05 |
| FSR MAX | 11.92 | 11.43 | 6.63 | 8.15 |

TAA stays on the common steps (MEDIUM 7.95 / 8.91 / 4.28 / 5.66): softer than FSR and DLSS, as TAA is; nobody asked.
SHARPEN TEXT AND MENUS with RCAS: objective text +8% at MEDIUM over OFF (1080p), no rims seen at 3x zoom. Tests: 71 pass.

## Follow-up 2026-11-16: a slider at the five levels

The same player asked for a slider. The owner, who had picked five steps over a slider for this record, agreed, and
picked style B of a mockup (`work/mockups/sharpen_slider`): a track with the five levels marked on it. A first build
moved in 5% steps and showed the percent with the nearest level's name; the owner then wanted "only level": the
slider **stops only at OFF / LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH / MAX and shows the level's name, no number**.

- Kept in percent inside (0 / 25 / 50 / 75 / 100), MEDIUM the default, with exactly the amounts above (DLSS on its
  own). `sharpen_amount` still blends between two levels, unused while the slider snaps, should finer steps return.
- **Saved as `YW4_SHARPEN=0.50`** (the slider's fraction, as the HUD's sliders are saved). A file from before the
  slider (`YW4_SHARPEN=0..4`) is read as its level: HIGH comes back as HIGH. Any value snaps to the nearest level
  (a 5%-step build's 0.65 reads as HIGH). `YW4_SET_AT` takes either form.
- **The overlay** draws the slider where a row's arrows and value are (settings page and the preview's bar); Left /
  Right (and A / Enter) move it one level, a click or a drag on the track sets the nearest level. A slider with named
  points shows the name as its value (`slider_text`), so the old F1 panel's slider row says MEDIUM too.
- Checked in the game (school scene, DLSS, 1080p, a replay through the overlay): `3` started at HIGH, `0.65` at HIGH,
  each Left / Right one level with the picture following; screenshots of the settings page and the preview bar. The
  owner tried the mouse on the test window during the run. 71 tests pass.

```

```md
# 0077 — Discord Rich Presence: "Playing Yo-kai Watch 4", where and the Watch Rank, off unless turned on

<!-- decision
state: accepted
date: 2026-11-15
replaces: none
code: runtime/src/discord.c, runtime/src/discord.h, runtime/src/discord_game.c, runtime/src/discord_game.h, runtime/src/run.c, runtime/src/discord_ipc.c, runtime/src/discord_ipc.h, runtime/src/settings.c, runtime/src/main.c, tests/test_discord.py
-->

Status: accepted (owner, 2026-11-15, through the relay session). Tested against a stand-in Discord on Windows and
Linux, and on 2026-11-16 against the real Discord app on Windows with the owner's application ID: "discord:
connected", the owner saw "Playing Yo-kai Watch 4" on their profile ("works"), clean exit after a ~3 h run.

## Context

The owner wanted the player's Discord profile to show that they are playing the port. The first ask had the current
area and the player's level too; the owner then cut it to the basics: the game's name and the time played.

## Decision

- **What shows:** the Discord application's name (the owner names it "Yo-kai Watch 4"), its art uploaded as `icon`,
  and "elapsed" from when the game started; since 2026-11-18 also where the player is and the Watch Rank (below).
- **Off unless turned on:** DISCORD STATUS (Settings, ADVANCED), OFF / ON, saved as `YW4_DISCORD=0/1`, default OFF.
  Turning it off clears the activity at once.
- **The application ID** is `YW4_DISCORD_APP_ID` in `runtime/src/discord.h`: the owner's application
  `1571532450742665347` (created 2026-11-15; public, it goes in every build). An environment variable of the same
  name overrides it. Empty: no thread at all, and the row is greyed out ("NOT SET UP IN THIS BUILD").
- **No library.** Discord's local IPC is small: frames of an 8-byte header (op, length) and JSON. `discord_ipc.c`
  has the transport and the three messages (handshake, SET_ACTIVITY, clearing it) in about 250 lines. Windows: the
  named pipe `\\.\pipe\discord-ipc-0` to `-9`. Linux: the socket `discord-ipc-N` in `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `$TMPDIR`,
  `$TMP`, `$TEMP` or `/tmp`, and their `app/com.discordapp.Discord/` (Flatpak) and `snap.discord/` (Snap) folders.
  Discord's own SDK (a large DLL, its own licence) and discord-rpc (archived) were not needed for this.
- **Quiet:** a thread of its own wakes once a second. While on, it tries to connect every 15 s; no Discord means no
  error, no window and one log line at most ("connected", "status cleared"). It sets the activity once per connection
  and reads what Discord sends back (answers, pings) so the pipe never fills. Handshake replies other than READY (a
  wrong ID gets a CLOSE) end that attempt.

## Where the player is (added 2026-11-18, owner's ask)

**The card** (an emoji in front of each line; `discord_presence_text` in `discord.c`):

- Title's menus (`scene_on_title`): "🏠 In the main menu".
- Field: one of 20 wordings with the place, "🗺️ Exploring Meeting Bridge", "❓ Lost in …", "🤪 Mucking about in
  …" (the owner added those two) and so on; a new one, never the same twice, each time the place changes.
- Battle (`battle_active`): one of 6, "⚔️ Battling in …", "⚡ Unleashing a Soultimate in …", a new one each battle;
  the field's wording stays as it was when the battle ends in the same place.
- Second line "⌚ Watch Rank B". The icon's hover: the area ("Springdale City"). A button "Get YW4 Recomp" to the
  project site (Discord hides a player's own buttons from them).
- The place is the zone when it has a name ("Meeting Bridge"), else the area. At most one update per 5 s (Discord
  takes 5 per 20 s), the newest text. The random pick is the thread's own xorshift, not `rand()`.

**The area** is read live, not from the last save: the game data object at `*(*(main+0x1548fd8) + 0x5778)` is what
the save summary copies when the game saves (`f_32ec30`): +0x17 the Watch Rank (0 E .. 5 S), +0x30 the map ID. The
name is the game's own text, looked up as the Diary does: map ID -> text ID with `f_70ff90` (a pointer to the ID) or
else `f_70fdc0`, then `f_9b10d0(table, text, 0)` in the text tables at `*(G+8)` then `*(G+0)`. Map ID 0 (a save
still loading) is skipped: its text is an unrelated string ("Yo-kai Soulmates").

**The zone** ("Meeting Bridge") is what the expanded minimap shows under it; the game works it out only then
(`f_758430`, found by logging every text lookup, `YW4_PROBE=main+9b10d0`, while the owner opened it). The same steps
here: the zone slot at the data object's +0x301, its handle at FM + slot*0x14 + 0x44 (FM = `*(main+0x154b190)`, the
field manager; low 16 bits an index below 0x200, checked against FM + index*0xa60 + 0x148), whose record +0x15c is a
block at FM + block*0x100 (+0x18dab0: -1 for none, +0x18db90 the zone's number); the map's internal name from
`f_4d8e60(*(G+0x230), FM's map ID)`; `sprintf(main+0x12524ff, name, number)` ("block_name_t201_07"); its CRC-32
with the game's table (main+0x12bd348) is the text ID. No such text ("block_name_t201_00"): the area. On the way to
another area the field's map (and zone) turns over a moment before the data's map ID; the zone waits until both name
the same map (they are the same IDs: 0x6c6eefe0 in town).

All of these are the game's functions, so `discord_game.c` runs them on the game's thread, in the field player
controller hook (`run.c`), only when the map or zone changed and only while DISCORD STATUS is on.

Seen (2026-11-18): test runs, the late-game save `Mystic Grove`, rank 3 (B), as its save summary; the town walk
`Uptown Springdale` then the zone `Springdale Elementary`. The owner on the real Discord app (Windows): Mystic Grove,
then Springdale City and South Stream on walking there ("works"); zones Spring Breeze Blvd., Springdale Elementary,
Wildwood Way. Rank badges (art `rank_e` .. `rank_s` as the small picture) were drawn and dropped (owner, 2026-11-18).

## Not done

- **Player level.** (The area and zone are shown since 2026-11-18, above.) Looked into before the owner cut them: the save header (`HEADERSAVE/data.bin`, 1118
  bytes, not encrypted, fixed layout) holds 12 (character ID hash, level) pairs, the party, at 0x34-0x1A0 (the town
  save's first two, levels 2 and 2, match the Yo-kai Pad's "N Lv 2" and "Jibanyan Lv 2"), and a pair at 0x1E0/0x1EC
  that changes with the location (the same in saves at the same place). Both are rewritten when the game saves (an
  autosave changed the header's second block), so they would show the last save, not the moment. Still open: which
  party slot is "the player", and area IDs to names (the player's RomFS text). A live value would need the game's
  memory found and hooked.
- No invite / cover image on the Discord application (owner skipped it, 2026-11-16).
- Linux against the real Discord app: not run yet (stand-in only).

## Tests

`tests/test_discord.py`: the frame bytes, the handshake and activity JSON byte for byte (escaping, clearing, a buffer
too small), a connect with nobody listening (fails quietly), and the presence thread against a stand-in Discord that
checks the handshake, answers READY and checks the activity (its lines, hover and button, with a faked game
state); every wording names the place. Passes on Windows (llvm-mingw clang, named pipe) and
Linux (WSL: Clang 19 and GCC 13, Unix socket).
```

`docs/decisions/0078-diary-save-slots.md`:

```md
# 0078 — Five Diary save slots, stacked, and one Autosave

<!-- decision
state: accepted
date: 2026-11-17
replaces: none
code: runtime/src/savefs.c, runtime/src/savefs.h, runtime/src/diaryrows.c, runtime/src/diaryrows.h, runtime/src/romfs.c, runtime/src/svc_hid.c, runtime/src/kernel.h, runtime/src/gamemenu.c, runtime/src/gamemenu.h, runtime/src/bindings.c, runtime/src/swkbd.c, runtime/src/pause.c, recomp/overrides.toml
-->

Status: accepted (2026-11-17). First written as 0077 by an earlier session (Gemini, 2026-11-16); renumbered because
0077 is the Discord Rich Presence record on the `discord-presence` branch. Reviewed and corrected 2026-11-17 (see
"Changes after review"), then the title's Diary changed from one paged row to five stacked rows and the Autosave became
one shared file (see "Stacked rows"). The research behind it, with the formats and every game function used:
`docs/research/diary-save-slots.md`.

## Context

On the Switch, Yo-kai Watch 4++ gives a user one manual save (`USERDATA00/data.bin`), one autosave
(`AUTOSAVE/data.bin`), a two-row summary (`HEADERSAVE/data.bin`: row 0 the manual save, row 1 the autosave) and
shared system data (`SYSTEM/data.bin`). The Diary menu (class at `main+0x14d87f8`, `work/recomp/main_128.c`) has two
fixed `0x288`-byte rows of data at `menu + 0x210` and `menu + 0x498`, filled by `f_761aa0` from the two `0xa0`-byte
records of `headersave_obj` (`*(u64 *)(*(u64 *)(main + 0x1548fd8) + 0x57f8)`). New Game clears the save structs in
memory only; the old files are overwritten at the new game's first save (research, Round 4).

The Diary's look is data: its menu setting (`save_load_menu_setting.cfg.bin`) gives the row layer `diary_load_slot`
2 copies, and its locator object puts them on two bones of the anchor model `save00_06.g4pkm` (research, "Stacked
rows").

## Decision

**5 slots and one Autosave** (the owner, 2026-11-17: "5-10 save slots and then under all those 1 autosave slot which
saves your latest game save"; "autosave is autosave"). On by default; `YW4_DIARY_SLOTS=0` gives the game's single slot
back.

1. **Folders.** Slot 1 is the user's save folder as before, so an existing save is slot 1 with no migration. Slot
   *n* (2..5) is the folder `SLOTnn` in it (`SLOT02`..`SLOT05`): `host_path` sends `/USERDATA*` and `/HEADERSAVE*`
   there while that slot is active. `AUTOSAVE` and `SYSTEM` stay in the main folder, shared. A slot's folder doesn't
   exist before its first save, so for paths in a slot folder only, a missing parent folder, a folder opened, or a file
   opened for writing is made on demand. Anywhere else a missing path is still "not found".
2. **One Autosave.** Each slot's summary row 1 is the autosave its game last made; the newest of them is the one on
   disk (`newest_auto_slot_locked`). Loading it continues that slot's game, whose saves then go to that slot. Deleting
   a slot leaves the Autosave (and the slot's summary while it holds the Autosave's row). A slot counts as used when it
   has its save or its game made the Autosave.
3. **Summary cache.** `parse_slot_from_disk_locked` reads each slot's `HEADERSAVE` (Level-5 TLV, magic `0x10f2ffee`)
   into `slot_cache` at start, at each Commit and when the Diary opens. Row 0 counts only if its valid flag is set and
   its `USERDATA00` exists; row 1 if the shared `AUTOSAVE` exists.
4. **Title > Continue: five stacked rows, then the Autosave row** (owner: "the save slots stack, not Left / Right").
   At start the runtime changes three of the owner's game files in memory (`diaryrows.c`, `romfs.c`, after the mods;
   all three or none, and freed from their archives in the list): six row copies, six new row bones (saves 100 apart
   from y -250, the Autosave 128 below), a locator line for each. `YW4_DIARY_ROWS=0` keeps the game's two rows.
   The game's own row code draws every row: its setup is skipped for copies 1+ and our paint pass sends its copy
   lookup (`f_9f3e90`) to the row being drawn. The focus grid is made 6 rows; the cursor's attach line is moved over
   all six; Up from the top wraps to the Autosave; the first focus is the newest row, as the game does. The labels
   have no `"<n>/5"` (the rows show which slot it is). Rows are drawn 15..20 from the top, so a row's "Latest!" badge
   stands over the row above (their texts stay at 20). The game's "has row N a save?" and "load row N" Lua calls
   (`f_2672d0`, `f_266fc0`), which only know rows 0 and 1, are answered from the focused row. On an empty slot A is
   held back from the game (`savefs_filter_buttons`): no "load this diary?" box. The mouse wheel moves up and down
   the rows, and left and right on their Yes / No box.
5. **Save in the game: one card that pages.** Its menu has no row list, so Left / Right, L / R, the left stick and the
   mouse wheel change the slot, its name prefixed `"<n>/5 "`. It opens on the slot being played. Its hint reads
   "[Left][Right] Change Slot   [A] Save   [B] Back" (the English system text's line, changed in memory at start; the
   D-pad's two icons, which show the bound keys on a keyboard). Paging stops while the menu is opening, while its
   "Would you like to save all data to your diary?" box has the input (the menu's `+0x1a6` / `+0x1ac` are 0; that box
   isn't counted at `main+0x5511a84`) or while a save job runs.
6. **Clean HEADERSAVE.** The save writes both rows of `headersave_obj`, but only updates one (`f_32ec30`), so before
   it runs (`f_8a7b10` hook) the slot's own unprefixed rows are put back. No label and no other slot's row reaches
   the file.
7. **New Game asks for a slot** (owner: "choose on beginning which save slot to write to"). Just before the boy's name
   popup (swkbd.c), `savefs_new_game_naming` shows an overlay list of the 5 slots (`gamemenu_choice_begin`), the first
   empty one chosen; the game waits, as for the name entry. A new game is one that left the title without loading a
   save; once per new game. An occupied slot asks "Overwrite Diary n/5?" (No by default). Its old files stay until
   the new game's first save: until then the slot reads as empty (`fresh_slot`). Replays and
   `YW4_NEWGAME_SLOT=<1..5>` answer at once.
8. **Delete:** on the title's Continue, X on an occupied slot arms it for 5 s ("Press again to delete": no button
   named, it differs by device), X again deletes its save. Any other button or a slot change cancels; nothing on the
   Autosave row. Its hint shows it: "Delete" with the X button's icon before Select / Back (text `0xbdaf66c1`, the
   `diary_load` script's only, changed in memory where it is the English line). On a keyboard the icon is the X key,
   which deletes there too (it is the game's Minus, left out on that screen); Tab, the X button's key, still does. Not from the in-game Save (2026-11-17): it had refused only the slot being played ("In use: can't delete"),
   and the hint there has no room for it.
9. **Boot:** if slot 1 is empty but another slot has a save, the first used slot is made active.

## Why not other ways

- A list drawn by the overlay over the Diary: quicker, but not the game's look. The owner chose the game's own rows.
- Editing the game's files on disk, or shipping changed copies: they are derived from the game (rule 1 of
  `CLAUDE.md`); the runtime makes them from the owner's files at each start instead.
- A per-slot Autosave (the first version): the owner wants one ("the game tells you that the save is newest
  anyways"), and the game's own checks look for `AUTOSAVE` in the active slot's folder, which said "There is no save
  data available." after a save in another slot.
- A slot picker for New Game in the game's own UI would need a menu we don't have; the overlay already has a popup
  the game waits on (the name entry, decision 0053's overlay).

## Not verified

- The TLV reader in `parse_slot_from_disk_locked` was checked on the test saves only.
- Return to Title, then New Game, in one run.
- X delete on the stacked rows, and the mouse wheel there and on their boxes (the owner's hands).
- Other languages than the English patch: the in-game Save's hint is only changed where the line is the English one.

## Tested (2026-11-17)

- Stacked rows on the late-game test save and the owner's save (`dev_run_20261117_055132` .. `_073106`): six rows,
  the newest focused at open with its card; Up / Down through all six, wrapping both ways; A on an empty slot does
  nothing; A on a save asks and loads that slot's save; A on the Autosave asks and loads it; text and badges drawn
  right. Opening takes the same time with and without the stacked rows (832 ms, 26 frames; our drawing ~1 ms).
- In-game Save on the owner's save (`dev_run_20261117_065407`): opens on the slot loaded; Right in its box only moves
  the box's choice, after it the slot pages; the hint shows the arrow keys.
- New Game with `YW4_NEWGAME_SLOT=2`: chosen once at the boy's name, not again at the girl's; no save file changed
  through both names and into the intro (`dev_run_20261117_025213`).

## Still to do

- The game's "denied" sound for A on an empty slot (A does nothing now).
- The rows slide in as the game's two did (the new bones have no animation tracks).

## Changes after review (2026-11-17)

- New Game: the first version's hook (`f_32e540`) never ran in three runs, so a new game saved into the slot active at
  start, over its save. Now the picker before the boy's name, with an overwrite question.
- Folders `SLOT01..SLOT09` (one less than the slot shown) renamed `SLOT02..SLOT10`, then five slots `SLOT02..SLOT05`.
- On-demand file and folder creation was on for every path; now only in a slot's own folder.
- Deleting from the in-game Save is off (2026-11-17; before, only the slot being played was refused).
- `hid_current_buttons` declared in `kernel.h` beside `yw4_hid_update`, not in `savefs.h`.
- The title's Diary: one paged card became five stacked rows; the per-slot Autosave became one shared file; the
  "card shows the other row" problem of the paged card went with it.
```

`docs/decisions/0079-gpu-worker-cpu-trims.md`:

```md
# 0079 — GPU WORKER CPU: push descriptors and smaller per-draw costs

<!-- decision
state: accepted
date: 2026-11-17
replaces: none
code: runtime/src/gpu_draw.c, runtime/src/gpu.c, runtime/src/window.c, runtime/src/vk.h, runtime/src/gpu_queue.c, runtime/src/gpu.h, runtime/src/perf.c
-->

Status: accepted (owner, 2026-11-17: "I want the CPU to be cut down as much as possible"; "if it is better and it
doesn't prove to break things keep it in"). Step log: `work/tasks/cpu-optimization-log.md`, steps 57-85.

## Context

On the slow street (scene `lag`, 1440, DLSS performance, owner's settings) the game is CPU bound: the GPU is busy
about 6 ms of an ~11.5 ms frame. The busiest thread is not a game thread but ours: the GPU worker
(`gpu_queue.c`, decision 0029), which turns the game's command lists into Vulkan. It used a whole core, about 11 ms a
frame on its own, and the GPU and then the main thread waited for it (the main thread ~3 ms a frame in
`nvnSyncWait`). An earlier session had looked at the game's mutexes instead (lock spinning, `YW4_LOCK_SPIN`); they
cost about 1.2 ms a frame across all threads, mostly not on this path.

The per-thread CPU report did not list the worker (it is a host thread, not a guest one), so this was not visible.

## Decision

1. **The worker in the per-thread report**: `gpu worker (host): N% of a core, X ms/frame` every 600 frames.
2. **Push descriptors** (`VK_KHR_push_descriptor`, where the GPU has it): fragment and compute programs push their
   bindings into the command buffer instead of a descriptor set being allocated, written and bound for each draw.
   Vertex and geometry programs keep allocated sets: a pipeline layout may have only one push-descriptor set.
   `YW4_PUSH_DESC=0` turns it off. Measured: +9.4% fps (3 pairs, every pair), the worker -1.3 ms a frame.
3. **Geometry fingerprint 8 bytes a step** (`geo_print`, run for every small vertex/index range of every draw):
   +3.8% (3 pairs); the same rewrites are caught.
4. **Texture keys**: a texture that is neither screen-sized nor the shadow map's shape no longer asks the size
   settings (render height, upscaling, presented images); the widescreen check's second lookup only with widescreen
   on. Same keys by construction. +3.6% (3 pairs).
5. **Smaller trims, kept although their gain is within the machine's noise** (the laptop's speed swings ~15% between
   runs; less work helps slower CPUs more): only the dynamic states that changed are set again; image keys compared
   and hashed a word at a time; samplers found through a hash index and the upscale mip bias worked out once per
   mode; a small memo of recent geometry ranges in front of the 16 MB table.

Every change was checked with the Vulkan validation layer (only the two old messages: the swapchain image in
Streamline's draws, and its semaphore) and screenshots at the same replay frames.

## Tried and not kept

- **Lock spinning** (`YW4_LOCK_SPIN`, earlier session): +11% on the snow bridge only, nothing elsewhere; stays off.
- **Reusing identical descriptor sets** within a command buffer: only 7% could be reused (offsets differ per draw);
  3% slower. Push descriptors replaced the idea.
- **Flush rules instead of the page scan** (`YW4_UNTRACKED=1`): slower; the per-draw checks cost more than the scan.
- **The page scan split over helper threads**: the scan (~1.1 ms a frame, 1,092 MiB walked for ~1,900 written pages)
  took as long on 4 threads: GetWriteWatch calls don't overlap. A log line now reports its cost every 600 frames.
- **Scanning only the pages something reads** (2026-11-18): only textures we uploaded and geometry we copied read
  the write generations, so the scan was limited to those pages ("live" pages, tracking reset when a page joins, runs
  closer than 16 pages scanned as one call). Short runs: 0.26-0.64 ms a frame against 0.94-1.30. Dropped:
  - The saving fades: pages never leave the set, and after 9 minutes of play it held 600 MiB and cost 0.90 ms
    (whole pools: 0.97). Making pages leave again is more code for a background thread's fraction of a millisecond.
  - A content audit (a texture or copy the pages call unchanged, compared with its upload) over 8 scenes, live
    against whole pools: textures were all caught by the next scan, but geometry copies left stale for more than
    3 frames were 108 against 40, cause not found.
  - Windows itself was fine: GetWriteWatch and ResetWriteWatch on part of a region behave as documented (a standalone
    test). An early "missed write" was the test's own snapshot taken before the reset; resetting must come before
    anything reads the storage.
  - The whole-pool scan also leaves 40 geometry copies stale for more than 3 frames (ranges of 100 bytes to 5 KB)
    in those 8 scenes: not looked into yet.

## Consequences

- The first start after this rebuilds the driver's pipeline cache once (the fragment layouts changed).
- The worker is still the busiest thread (~11 ms). The remaining large step would be translating command lists on
  more than one thread, a large change to the renderer; not started.
- How to judge a change here: by fps or frame time in alternating pairs. The worker's CPU ms also falls when it only
  waits more (the split scan looked like -0.7 ms and gained nothing).

```

`docs/decisions/0080-running-modes.md`:

```md
# 0080 — Running modes: run without holding B (issue #18)

<!-- decision
state: accepted
date: 2026-11-18
replaces: none
code: runtime/src/run.c, runtime/src/run.h, recomp/overrides.toml, runtime/src/bindings.c, runtime/src/bindings.h, runtime/src/gamemenu.c, runtime/src/window.c
-->

Status: accepted (owner, 2026-11-17 and 18: the four modes, one Run key, the layout of the Controls page). Measured
with replays at 30 and 120 frames/s (Checks); the owner played it by hand.

## Context

Issue #18: running needs B held, which is uncomfortable while turning the camera; the reporter asked for a toggle.
On the Switch B does two things: a tap jumps, a hold runs. A run toggle has to leave the jump alone.

## How the game runs (traced 2026-11-17)

With `YW4_PROBE_DUMP` (walking against running in one replay), `YW4_WATCHW` write watches, and `llvm-nm` on
`yw4.exe` to name the recompiled function behind each host write address:

- Walking and running are the same action state (`action+0x8b5` = 7); running is a top speed, 6.55 against 9.0
  (`action+0xa4`, `+0xab0`), copied from `+0x6e0`, chosen in `main+0x1c2aa0` by `action+0x614 == 2`.
- That byte is a copy of `action+0x234`, set in `main+0x1bcd70` from the player's command object
  (`cmd = *(action+0x10f8)`): `+0x234 = cmd+0xa9 ? 2 : 1`.
- `cmd+0xa9` is set by the field's player controller, `main+0x1fe950` (one object, called once a frame), when its
  "run this frame" flag (`ctrl+0x5d`) is set. That happens when B's hold time (`ctrl+0x54`, + dt while B is down)
  is **greater than** a threshold from the game's config (`main+0x1531390`, 0.25 s), or, in the "moving" state only,
  while a carry-on timer (`ctrl+0x58`, - dt a frame) is above zero. `ctrl+0x5c` is "B was down last frame": when it
  is 0 the hold time starts again from 0. When B goes up, a long hold refills the carry-on timer (about 0.55 s); a
  short one is a tap, which jumps.
- B reaches the game as bit `0x4000` of the input object (`*(main+0x14d1008)`; held at `+0x8`), mapped from the
  Switch's bit 1 by the table at `main+0x12bdfb0`. The pad itself is read only in `main+0x964550`.

## Decision

1. **A hook before the player controller** (`yw4_hook_player_run`, `recomp/overrides.toml`): while running is
   wanted and the real B is up, it sets the controller up as if B had been held past the threshold: `ctrl+0x5c = 1`
   and `ctrl+0x54` a little over the threshold (the game's check is "greater than"). The controller runs by its own
   path, in any action state, and clears both values itself at the end of the frame.
2. **B stays the game's.** While the real B is down, and on the frame it goes up (when the game judges a tap by its
   hold time), the hook stays out, so a tap still jumps.
3. **Stopping is immediate:** when running is switched off, the carry-on timer the game set at the end of the last
   faked frame is cleared (else about 0.55 s more running). A real B hold still carries on as the game does.
4. **Four modes** (Controls page, RUNNING; `YW4_RUN_MODE`): DEFAULT (the game's; the Run key does nothing and is
   greyed out), ALWAYS (hold Run to walk), TOGGLE (Run switches running; off when a battle starts), HOLD (hold Run to
   run). Nothing changes in battles.
5. **One Run input of ours** (`INPUT_OURS`: read, never sent to the game): Left Shift; on a pad the left stick press,
   shared there with Close hints (no button is free), not marked as a clash. Close hints moved to Left Ctrl on the
   keyboard; a settings file from before (no `RUN` line) moves its Left Shift there when Left Ctrl is free.
6. **The Controls page:** RUNNING, then Run under it, below NINTENDO ICONS. Every row's help is now "what it is"
   above "how to change it" in a fixed-height area, so the table no longer resizes from row to row; a game input's
   "what it is" comes from the F2 sheet's action names (exploring, battles, cutscenes; the set shown first).

Why not the alternatives:

- **The carry-on timer alone** (tried first): the controller clears it outside the "moving" state, so a walk with
  turns fell back to walking; and it is cleared at the start of the frame unless the player ran the frame before.
- **Holding B for the player** (the input layer): the hold would also begin with a press, and a jump would need B
  let go and pressed again by us; the game's own run path is cleaner.
- **Patching the run speed**: running is more than a speed (animation, `cmd+0xa9` read elsewhere).

## Checks

Replay `work/inputs/run_modes.txt` on `save_base_walk` (schoolyard): three stretches of walking forward, the last with
a B tap. `YW4_RUN_KEY_TEST=<from>-<to>[,...]` holds the Run input (a replay feeds the Switch's buttons, not keys);
the player's speed from `YW4_PROBE_MEM` on `main+0x1bcd70`.

| Mode | Walk 1 | Walk 2 | Walk 3 + B tap |
|---|---|---|---|
| DEFAULT | 6.55 | 6.55 | 6.55, jump |
| ALWAYS, Run held in walk 2 | 9.0 | 6.55 | 9.0, jump |
| TOGGLE, pressed before walk 3 | 6.55 | 6.55 | 9.0, jump |
| HOLD, Run held in walk 3 | 6.55 | 6.55 | 9.0, jump |

- The same at 120 frames/s (`YW4_FPS=120`, `YW4_REPLAY_HZ=120`): every mode as above.
- TOGGLE on at frame 3905: running at 3906; off at 3960: walking at 3961 (was about 0.55 s).
- Left: while B is held for a tap (about 0.1 s) the player is at walking speed for those frames, then jumps and runs
  on. Covering it would mean faking B's hold during a real press, which is what broke the jump.

## Not done

- A pad button of its own for Run (none is free); the player can rebind it.
- An enemy-only target switch in battles (the game has allies only, Tab, and everyone, D-pad left / right): a
  separate feature, not started.

```

`docs/disk-usage.md`:

```md
# Disk space usage and build sizes

Measured disk usage for the launcher, the game installation, and intermediate build artifacts (measured 2026-11-10
during a clean build to drive `W:\YW4Clean` with `YW4 Recomp.exe` 0.6.0 on Windows 11, AMD Ryzen 9 7940HS).

## Summary

| Build stage / mode | Disk space | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Clean install (after build, folders mode)** | **11.28 GB** (11.35 GB drive delta) | Copied RomFS (8.46 GB), compiler (0.70 GB), dependencies (0.65 GB), generated C (0.49 GB), build output (0.43 GB), DLC (0.44 GB) |
| **Peak during build (folders mode)** | **11.35 GB** | Peak reached near the end of compiling and DLC extraction |
| **Peak during build (NSP/XCI mode)** | **~20.7 GB** | During extraction, `work/nca/` holds 9.40 GB of temporary NCAs until RomFS is fully extracted |
| **After "Free up space"** | **9.27 GB** (2.00 GB freed) | Deletes `toolchain`, `recomp/`, `build/obj/`, `deps/`, and `shaders/asm/` |
| **Building the launcher itself from source** | **~10.3 GB** | Cargo build in `launcher/src-tauri/target/` (10.24 GB) + `node_modules` (15 MB) |

## Breakdown of the game install folder (`<install>/`)

Measured after a complete clean build into `W:\YW4Clean` before "Free up space":

| Folder / file | Size | Kept after "Free up space"? | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data/romfs/` | 8.458 GB (9,081.5 MB) | Yes | The game's RomFS (update 2.2.0 applied) |
| `builder/toolchain/` | 0.699 GB (750.1 MB) | No (deleted) | Downloaded llvm-mingw compiler (`clang.exe`, libraries) |
| `work/deps/` | 0.654 GB (702.6 MB) | No (deleted) | Downloaded SDL3, FSR, DLSS, and Streamline SDK archives and unpacked headers/libs |
| `work/recomp/` | 0.489 GB (525.2 MB) | No (deleted) | Recompiled C source code generated from `main` and `sdk` |
| `work/build/` | 0.430 GB (461.7 MB) | Yes (except `obj/`) | `yw4.exe`, runtime DLLs, and `obj/` (153 MB of compiled object files) |
| `data/dlc/` | 0.219 GB (234.7 MB) | Yes | Copied add-on NSP files |
| `data/dlc-romfs/` | 0.216 GB (232.2 MB) | Yes | Extracted RomFS for the 4++ Upgrade Pack (index 100) |
| `work/shaders/` | 0.094 GB (101.2 MB) | Yes (except `asm/`) | Translated GLSL 4.60 shaders and compiled SPIR-V binaries |
| `data/exefs/` | 0.017 GB (17.9 MB) | Yes | Extracted ExeFS binaries (`main`, `sdk`, `rtld`) |
| `app/` (launcher app itself) | 0.039 GB (41.4 MB) | Yes | The launcher executable, embedded Python, and bundled tools |
| `work/pycache/` | < 1 MB | Yes | Python bytecode cache |
| **Total** | **11.276 GB** (12,107.5 MB) | **9.273 GB** after cleanup | Total installation size |

## Reclaimable disk space ("Free up space")

The Ready screen and Settings offer "Free up space" (`ready::free_space`), which deletes folders that only a full rebuild needs (`reclaim_dirs`):

* `builder/toolchain/`: 750.1 MB
* `work/deps/`: 702.6 MB
* `work/recomp/`: 525.2 MB
* `work/build/obj/`: 153.2 MB
* `work/shaders/asm/`: ~19 MB
* `work/nca/`: cleaned during extraction unless `--keep-nca` was used

**Total space reclaimed:** **2.003 GB** (`2,150.5 MB`).
The game remains fully playable from `<install>/work/build/yw4.exe`, taking **9.27 GB**. Future updates will re-download the compiler and dependencies as needed.

## Building from NSP vs Extracted Folders

The launcher supports two input modes:

1. **Folders mode (`mode: folders`)**:
   Copies already-extracted RomFS (8.46 GB) and ExeFS (16.6 MB).
   * Peak disk usage equals the final uncleaned build size: **11.35 GB**.
   * Build duration on a 16-thread Ryzen 9 7940HS: **~8.8 minutes**.

2. **Files mode (`mode: files`)**:
   Extracts `base_nsp` and `update_nsp` via `hactool.exe`.
   * Unpacks NCAs into `work/nca/`: the base program NCA (5.56 GB) and update NCA (3.84 GB), taking **9.40 GB**.
   * `hactool` extracts `data/romfs/` (8.46 GB) while both NCAs are still on disk.
   * **Peak disk space during extraction:** **~20.7 GB** (9.40 GB NCAs + 8.46 GB RomFS + ~2.8 GB toolchain/build/DLC).
   * Once extraction completes, `work/nca/` is deleted, dropping disk usage back to 11.28 GB.

## Developing and building the launcher from source

For developers working on `launcher/`:
* `launcher/src-tauri/target/`: **10.24 GB** (Rust debug and release builds, intermediate object files and dependencies).
* `launcher/node_modules/`: **15.4 MB** (Tauri CLI npm package).
* Output packages (`work/package/dist/`):
  * `YW4-Recomp-Launcher-0.6.0-setup.exe`: **14.5 MB**
  * `YW4-Recomp-Launcher-0.6.0-portable.zip`: **17.8 MB**

```

```html
<script>
/* the theme switch: the other theme than the one showing, kept for next time */
(() => {
  const btn = document.getElementById('theme'), root = document.documentElement;
  const dark = () => root.dataset.theme ? root.dataset.theme === 'dark' : matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches;
  const label = () => btn.setAttribute('aria-label', dark() ? 'Light mode' : 'Dark mode');
  label();
  const flip = () => {
    root.dataset.theme = dark() ? 'light' : 'dark';
    try { localStorage.setItem('yw4-theme', root.dataset.theme); } catch (e) {}
    label();
  };
  /* a slow cross-fade between the themes (site.css sets its length), where the browser can do one */
  btn.addEventListener('click', () => {
    if (document.startViewTransition && !matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches) document.startViewTransition(flip);
    else flip();
  });
})();
</script>
```

`docs/frame.md`:

```md
# The engine's frame

How the game builds a frame, from the engine's side: who decides what is drawn, and where our renderer can take
over ([decision 0023](decisions/0023-custom-renderer-plan.md)). Measured in the town street (the owner's save) with
`YW4_TRACE_RENDER_JOBS` and `YW4_TRACE_DRAW_CALLERS` ([debugging.md](debugging.md)); function names are offsets in
`main`.

## How work reaches the GPU

1. **The main thread schedules.** The engine runs named tasks each frame (registered through `f_96c470` with a
   name string: game logic such as `CSceneRpg080::Player` and the render stages below go through the same
   system). Render tasks don't draw: they append **jobs** to a per-frame list.
2. **A job is a callback:** a list node holds a function and two arguments (node `+8` function, `+0x10` a,
   `+0x18` b, `+0x30` next). `f_971ad0` is a job that runs a sub-list of the same kind.
3. **Three render threads run the lists** (`f_979790`: for each node, `fn(device, a, b)`), each with its own NVN
   command buffer, and submit. The NVN calls happen inside the jobs.

So the engine's passes are visible as jobs, and the place to hook a pass is its job function (render thread) or
the task that queues it (main thread).

## The three render threads

| Thread | Work | Queued by |
|---|---|---|
| A | **Shadow maps**: 3 cascades, 1024×1024 depth | `yw::CMainEndComponent` vtable slot 13 (`f_5dbe30`) → `f_7ed570` |
| B | Occlusion boxes for the camera (240×135), ambient cube map (128×128), **the G-buffer** (layer kind 2), the screen-space shadow mask | `yw::CMainComponent` slot 12 (`f_5d77f0`) |
| C | Main view: the named stages below, then UI, then present (`f_95b740`) | the stage tasks below |

## Shadow maps (thread A)

`f_7ed570` queues, per cascade (cascade index 0, 1, 2 passed to `f_7ee9a0`):

| Job | Arguments seen | Probably |
|---|---|---|
| `f_7ee4e0` | a = `0x71012982bc` / `c0` / `c4` (4 apart) | per-cascade value |
| `f_7ee510` | a, b = per-cascade structs (`0x71056ab3b0`, `…3f0`, `…430`: 0x40 apart) | set the cascade's target / matrices |
| `f_9abfc0` ×7, `f_9ab8c0` ×154 (in a sub-list) | a = `0x7105883790`, b = one object each | occlusion-query boxes (the 36-vertex boxes at 240×135, shader `b320bd…`) per caster |
| `f_7ed4d0`, `f_7ee830`, `f_7ee980` | | pass setup |
| `f_7ee9a0` | a = cascade index | select the cascade |
| `f_7ed100`, `f_7ecf00` | | render targets / state |
| `f_a45890` | b = layer item of **kind 1** | draw the shadow casters |
| `f_7ed350` | | end of cascade |

`f_7ed570` has six copies of this block; three ran in the street. The other three are not identified yet.

### Cascade data

Computed on the main thread every frame by `yw::CMainComponent` slot 11 (`f_5d4270`, the update; slot 12 queues
the render jobs) → `f_7e5570` → `f_a4e830(camera, out, near[], far[], third[], 3)`. `f_a4e830` inverts the camera
matrix, then calls `f_a4d100` once per cascade; `f_7e5570` copies the results into the **renderer object**
(`a` = `0x71056ab1b0` = `main+0x56ab1b0`, a static object, same address every run):

| Renderer offset | Per cascade i | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `+0x200 + i·0x40` | 4×4 floats, row-major | light view: same rotation for all cascades, own translation |
| `+0x140 + i·0x40` | 4×4 floats | projection, **perspective along light-space y** (last row `0 1 0 0`, so w = y): a perspective-warped shadow map (LiSPSM family), not the usual orthographic cascades |
| `+0x080 + i·0x40` | 4×4 floats | projection × view, multiplied in `f_7e5570` |
| `+0x2c0 + i·0x10` | 4 floats | per-cascade values (not decoded) |

The per-cascade settings (`main+0x56b07a0` = `[renderer+0x568] + 0x1cf0`, three arrays of three floats):

| Cascade | near | far | third (light depth range?) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.1 | 20 | 60 |
| 1 | 20 | 50 | 110 |
| 2 | 50 | 150 | 200 |

`f_7ee510` (the per-cascade job) copies the view matrix (a) and projection (b) into the render state
(`device+0x2c0`, `+0x280`) and takes the viewport from render target #0x14 (the shadow map).

**For the replacement:** read the finished matrices from the renderer object; the warped-projection math only
needs re-implementing for a better-shadows mod later.

### What the GPU gets

- One depth texture, **3 layers** (one per cascade), 1024×1024, format `0x34`.
- Culling per draw: none or back faces (polygon state `0,…` / `2,…`); depth test and write on.
- Five programs in the street (`YW4_TRACE_DRAWLIST`, 38 shadow draws):

| Vertex shader | Draws | Position |
|---|---|---|
| `b320bd…` | 16 | cbuf 2 bytes 128-191 (projection × view × world, per object, made on the CPU) × vertex |
| `a74842…`, `744205…` | 12 | cbuf 1 bytes 128-191 (projection × view of the cascade) × instance transform (cbuf 11, 3×4 per instance, `instance × 48` bytes; from `object+0x140 → +0x80`) × world (cbuf 2 bytes 0-63) × vertex: **instanced** props |
| `71faac…` | | **skinned**: up to 8 bones per vertex from cbuf 4 (3×4 each), then cbuf 2 bytes 128-191 like `b320bd` |
| `4cbb8e…` | | static (`b320bd`) plus texture coordinates (attribute 1) and the alpha threshold (cbuf 3 byte 12): **static cut-out** |
| `9904c2…` | | instanced (`a74842`), with the fade fragment shader `b7cd6e` |
| `fa9033…`, `61ebac…` | | wind-swayed plants: textures read in the vertex stage |

**Share of the shadow draws by program pair** (street, `YW4_SHADOWS=check`, about 300,000 draws): `b320bd`+`6ead6a`
(static) 38%; `744205`+`dceb89` (instanced cut-out) 20%; `a74842`+`6ead6a` (instanced) 13%; `fa9033`+`dceb89` 8%;
`71faac`+`b7cd6e` (skinned, fade) 6%; `4cbb8e`+`dceb89` (static cut-out) 6%; `9904c2`+`b7cd6e` (instanced, fade) 5%;
`e758a5`/`f8951f`+`d5f536` 3%; `61ebac`+`dceb89` 1%.

**Skinned draws, as bound** (`71faac`): the three vertex streams are one buffer, the submesh's vertices (stride 60):
position `0x22` at 0, weights `0x2f` at 28 (eight 16-bit weights in four 32-bit words; the shader scales the sum by
1/65535; bones 5-8 only if weight 5 is not 0), bone indices `0x2c` at 44 (eight bytes, ×48 into cbuf 4). cbuf 2
byte 128 equals our projection × view × world.

**Where the bone palette comes from:** cbuf 4 is a copy, made right before each skinned submesh's draw, of a palette
the game built earlier (one 3×4 matrix per bone of that submesh, e.g. 41, 51 or 6 bones). The copy is the engine's
generic constant-buffer upload `f_965eb0`: a state slot (`device + stage·0x150 + slot·0x18 + 13000`) holds a buffer
object B, the CPU data is at `[B+0x40] + [B+0x58]`, the size in the slot (`+0x32d0`), and when the slot is dirty
the data is copied into the frame's buffer (`f_977550`) and bound. The model renderer puts the submesh's palette
object in the slot: for submesh `i` of a geometry, B = `[[object+0x140] + 0xc8] + 0x140·i + 0x78` (a record of
0x140 bytes per submesh; the size at `+0x98`). Found by value: for each skinned draw, the bytes at that B's data
equal cbuf 4 (check mode, every draw tried).

| Fragment shader | Does |
|---|---|
| `6ead6a…` | nothing: depth only |
| `dceb89…` | alpha cut-out: drops texels of the material's texture (fs slot 0) below the threshold the vertex stage passes |
| `b7cd6e…` | **fade**: drops pixels by a 16×16 screen pattern (texture fs slot 18, `texelFetch` at the pixel position mod 16) where the object's fade (fs cbuf 3 byte 28 × attribute 3.w) is below the pattern's value; at full opacity nothing is dropped |

Checked by value: cbuf 1 bytes 128-191 in a shadow draw equal the renderer's projection × view of that cascade
(`+0x80 + i·0x40`, same row-major layout; the shader takes `dot(row, position)` per output component). Per-object
cbuf 2 starts with the object's world matrix (`object+0`, 38 of 38).

Vertex attribute layouts seen in the shadow draws (format / stream / byte offset, from `BindVertexAttribState`):

| Attributes | Draws | Likely |
|---|---|---|
| 0: `0x22` / 0 / 0 | 22 | position only |
| 0: `0x22` / 0 / 0, 1: `0x12` / 1 / 32 | 7 | position + texture coordinates (cut-out) |
| 0: `0x22` / 0 / 0, 1: `0x2f` / 1 / 28, 2: `0x2c` / 2 / 44 | 11 | position + bone weights and indices (skinned) |

**How textures are bound** (read from `f_974cd0`, the engine's "apply pending state" function, which also holds its
`BindTexture` and `GetTextureHandle` calls): the state block passed to it as its second argument has texture slots
at `+0x780 + slot·16` (texture object pointer, "set" byte at `+8`). A texture object keeps its NVN texture id at
`+8` and a small cache of finished handles per sampler from `+0xf8` (16-byte entries: handle, sampler id). The
slot's name hash is looked up in the bound program's binding table (`program+0xb8`, count at `+0xc0`: pairs of
name hash and binding index), the handle is made with `GetTextureHandle(texture id, sampler id)` and bound. Not
found yet: where the material keeps its texture objects (searching the draw object and the material set
`object+0x120` up to three pointers deep for the ids found nothing; next try is a write watch on a texture slot).

**What a replaced shadow pass needs per frame:** the three cascade matrices (renderer object); the shadow layer's
objects (draw list, layer kind 1, `object+0x1d1` set); per object its world matrix, geometry and submesh records
(vertex/index data, counts, stride), bones if skinned, instance transforms if instanced, and the cut-out texture
if alpha-tested. Still open: the vertex attribute layout per shader, and where the material's texture handle comes
from.

**The occlusion boxes** (measured 2026-11-14, `YW4_COUNTER_LOG`; `runtime/src/gpu_query.c`): before each cascade and
before the main view, `f_9ab8c0` draws one 36-vertex box per object into the 240×135 depth target, each between two
`ReportCounter(SAMPLES_PASSED)` calls whose results lie 16 bytes apart. The model renderer then wraps that object's
draws in `SetRenderEnableConditional(RENDER_IF_NOT_EQUAL, address)` (`a4a18c`; `SetRenderEnable(true)` at `a4a1ac`
for objects without a query, and at `a4c67c` after the list): the GPU compares the two counts and skips the draws
of an object whose box had no visible sample. The CPU does not need the counts. The bamboo forest: 37 pairs a frame,
nothing hidden. The evening town street: 270 pairs, 878 draws under a condition, 498 of them skipped.

## The model renderer `f_a45890`

Draws one **layer**: `f_a45890(device, draw list, layer item)`. Every layer gets the same draw list (nodes from
`[list + 0x20]`, linked at `+0x30`); the layer item picks which nodes it draws: kind byte at `+8` (0 = normal view,
1 = shadow, 2 = seen with the ambient cube), a key range at `+0xa`/`+0xc`, a mask at `+0x10`. For kind 1 it skips
objects whose byte `+0x1d1` is 0 ("casts no shadow"). `runtime/src/shadow.c` (`gather`) re-implements this selection; `YW4_SHADOWS=check` compares it with what the game draws (0 missed over 3,600 shadow layers). This list is the engine-level data a replaced pass
would read instead of NVN commands.

Read so far from the start of its loop (offsets; meanings partly guessed):

| Where | Field |
|---|---|
| node `+0x00` | draw object (if the object's `+0x108` is set, that object is used instead) |
| node `+0x10` | per-instance data; per-submesh records of 0xb8 bytes from `+0xb0` |
| node `+0x20` | layer mask byte (skip if it has the layer's bit) |
| node `+0x30` | next node |
| object `+0x101`, `+0x103` | signed bytes: priority / sort range |
| object `+0x120` | material set (its `[+0x18]+0x23` byte changes kind-0/kind-1 handling) |
| object `+0x128`, `+0x140` | model resource (`+0x140`: submesh count at `+0x200`) |
| object `+0x1b0`, `+0x1c8`, `+0x1cb`, `+0x1d1` | skip in shadow layers if `+0x1b0` ≠ 0; **number of geometries** (per geometry: `*(+0x128)[g]`, model `+0x140 + g·0x240`); layer bit; casts shadow |
| object `+0x80`, `+0x90` | bounding box min and max (local space) |
| model `+0x80` | instance transforms (instanced objects; their world matrix is the identity) |
| `[draw list + 0x18]` | submesh table, records of 0x50 bytes (bytes `+0x34`, `+0x3f`, `+0x43` tested) |

### How a draw item reaches the GPU

`f_a45890` works in two phases: it walks the nodes and fills an array of 0x48-byte draw items on its stack, then
sorts and draws them. Each mesh draw is `f_a75e90(device, geometry, primitive)` (call sites `a4bf90`, `a4c2cc`;
the object being drawn is in `f_a45890`'s stack slot `sp+0x390`, the geometry is `*(object+0x128)`); `f_a75e90`
sets the vertex range and draw call, then the engine's generic "flush state and draw" (`f_977e30` / `f_974630`)
issues the NVN calls. Measured with `YW4_TRACE_DRAWLIST` (150 draws in the street: 38 shadow, 112 main view):

| Data | Where | Found in |
|---|---|---|
| world matrix (4×4) | **object `+0x00`** (a copy at `+0x40`); it is the start of vertex constant buffer 2 | 143 of 150 draws |
| vertex data base | `[geometry+0x20] + 0x00` | all |
| index area base | `[[geometry+0x28]]`: the geometry's index buffer object, as `f_a75e90` reads it; usually the second object of the vertex buffer's record (`[geometry+0x20] + 0x68`), not always (one town object: 1.5% of draws there) | all |
| bones (vertex constant buffer 4) | `object+0x110 → +0x138` | skinned draws (59 of 112) |
| vertex constant buffer 6 (material values?) | `object+0x280 → +0x328 → +0x140` | all shadow, 62 of 112 |

The **primitive record** (one per submesh, 0x50 bytes):

| Offset | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `+0x00` | vertex offset from the vertex data base |
| `+0x04` | index offset from the index area base |
| `+0x08` | vertex count (× stride = the bound vertex buffer size) |
| `+0x0c` | index count (0: not indexed) |
| `+0x10`, `+0x20` | two float4 (w = 1, 0): probably bounding box min and max |
| `+0x38` | small number (submesh or material slot?) |
| `+0x3d` | primitive type (through a table) |
| `+0x3e` | vertex stride in bytes (0x24, 0x28 seen) |
| `+0x3f` | flags; bit 1 picks the index type |
| `+0x43` | byte the renderer uses as an index (bone palette or LOD?) |

Why decode it rather than keep `f_a45890`: in the street the render threads' busy time is about 3% `f_a45890`,
4% the engine's NVN wrapper layer (`f_965xxx`-`f_97xxxx`), 4.5% other game code and 7.5% our NVN → Vulkan
translation (`YW4_PROFILE=submit`, percent of all samples; the threads wait the other 84%). A pass drawn from the
list directly drops the wrapper layer and the translation, roughly 60% of that busy time.

wrappers (`f_9749c4`, `f_974bec`) in the call stack.

| # | Target | Draws | What | Drawn by |

says about draw items, objects, matrices, buffers and bones holds for them too.
```
