## Materials (measured 2026-10-25)

Read from `f_a45890`'s second phase (Ghidra merges `f_a4bf90` into it) and checked on G-buffer draws with
`YW4_TRACE_DRAWLIST` (`YW4_TRACE_DRAWLIST_COLOURS=3`: G-buffer draws only).

The second phase walks the sorted **draw items** (0x48 bytes): `+0` geometry, `+8` the **model record** of that
geometry (`object+0x140` + 0x240 × geometry index), `+0x10` the submesh records, `+0x18` the **material records**,
`+0x28` texture references, `+0x30` material constants. A submesh's byte `+0x43` picks its material record (the
same index the shadow selection uses for the sort key).

| Material record (16 bytes) | |
|---|---|
| `+2` (u16), `+0xa` (u8) | constants: start (in 16-byte units, from the draw item's `+0x30` array) and count; uploaded per draw with `f_977550` into a fresh uniform buffer. The model record's `+0x78` holds per-object overrides (0x80 bytes each) when `+0x219` bit 0 is set |
| `+4` (u16), `+0xb` (u8) | render state entries (2 bytes each, in the geometry header blob) |
| `+6` (u16), `+0xc` (u8) | textures: start in the draw item's `+0x28` table (6 bytes each; byte 0 = entry of the model's texture table) and count |
| `+8` (s8) | sort key |
| `+0xe` (u16) | UV transforms, 0x20 bytes per texture, from the model record's `+0x98` (`+0x90` when `+0x219` bit 1) |

**Textures:** the model record's texture table (`+0xf8`; `+0xf0` in one case) has 16-byte entries
`{texture resource, index}`. The resource's header (`+0x18`) holds a 0x18-byte descriptor per index
(`hdr + 4×u16(hdr+0xa) + 4×u16(hdr+0x3e) + index×0x18`). From those the engine makes **temporary texture views**
each draw (0x50 bytes: `+0` the NVN texture, `+8` the texture id that the shader handle carries, then format and
swizzle; ids rise through the frame and differ between runs) and puts them in the texture slots of a static state
at `main+0x58569f8 + 0x780 + slot×16`, which `f_977e30` commits when the submesh is drawn (`f_a75e90`).

So at our submesh-draw hook the engine has already resolved a draw's textures and constants: a first replaced
G-buffer or material pass can take them from the bound state (as the shadow pass does for cut-out textures) and only
a full takeover needs the descriptors decoded.

## What depends on the screen size (measured 2026-10-27)

For resolution scaling of the 3D view: what in a frame is sized from the game's 1600×900. Town walk, one frame
(`YW4_GPU_TRACE` with `YW4_GPU_TRACE_SCREEN=1`, which logs every constant that equals a screen-derived size or
0.25..4 over one; and a scan of the 565 translated fragment shaders in `work/shaders/asm`).

**Images.** Every image sized from the screen is a GPU-only render target:

| Size | Of 1600×900 | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| 1600×900 | 1 | G-buffer (3 colour + depth), lit material pass, lighting/fog/effects, and the UI (drawn into the same colour image) |
| 800×450 | 1/2 | depth copy, shadow mask, lamp lights, effects |
| 533×300 | 1/3 | effects |
| 400×225, 200×112, 120×67 | 1/4, 1/8, ~1/13 | bloom chain |

Not screen-sized and left alone: the window image (1920×1080; the last pass copies the 1600×900 image into it by
sampling), the occlusion boxes (240×135 depth, culling only), the ambient cube (128×128), the minimap (340×304,
516×460), the shadow maps (own setting).

**Shaders: resolution-independent, nearly.** They reach the screen three ways, none tied to the size:

- the pixel position (`fragment.position.xy`, 295 shaders): times 1/16 to tile a 16×16 dither texture (the
  screen-door fade of objects), or written out as depth. At a higher resolution the dither pattern gets finer.
- whole-pixel reads (`TXF`, 261 shaders): position × 16, truncated, into the same dither texture.
- size queries (`TXQ`, 74 shaders): they return the image's real size, so they follow it.

Screen images are read in 0..1 coordinates from interpolated positions, so the ratio between images (a half-size
image read at half the position) holds as long as all of them grow by the same factor.

**Constants.** One row: the camera block (`CBUSE_UB_CAMERA_IDX`, cbuf 8) row 32 = 1.5/1600, 1.5/900, 0.75/533,
0.75/300: tap offsets in 0..1 coordinates, read by 215 shaders (the lit pass's edge-aware upsample of the half-size
lighting: the position ± row 32, a few taps). Unscaled, the taps spread wider in new pixels (a little softer, not
wrong); scaled by 1/factor, the same look. Row 33 = 1920, 1080 (the window), read by no shader. Every other match
was a coincidence (fog and light distances of 300, 120, 200; 0.01 written in 397 shaders). Three shaders hold odd
small numbers worth a look before shipping: `4f5854cdab65c4b5` (0.005), `5ef1a937fe5a9908` (1/320, 1/160), the
compute shader `ff9fe0a375532914` (1/1920-like; not run in a town frame).

**Commands.** The frame copies no image by command (no copy, blit or resolve is recorded): the engine shrinks images
by drawing them into smaller ones. Pixel rectangles appear only as viewports and scissors (and clears through the
scissor), which the runtime already scales for the shadow maps (`gpu_dynamic_state`).

So resolution scaling is runtime work: make the screen-sized images bigger by one factor (fractional: 1440p is ×1.6,
and 533 does not divide evenly), scale viewports and scissors of draws into them, and scale camera row 32. Battles,
menus and cutscenes are still to be checked for other screen-sized images.

## Post-processing (measured 2026-10-28)

Bamboo forest, late-game save, one frame (`YW4_GPU_TRACE` + `YW4_TRACE_DRAW_CALLERS`, grouped by `tools.yw4.mainview`).
After the lit pass, the lighting and the effects, two engine functions do the post-processing, then the UI follows:

| Draws | Target | Programs (vs/fs) | What | Drawn by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 800×450 | `98c09b`/`2d68c8` | distance blur: the scene shrunk | `f_8007d0` (`f_80eb90`) |
| 2 | 800×450 | `29d827`/`b8856c` | distance blur: two blur passes | `f_7f3900` < `f_7f3620` < `f_8007d0` |
| 1 | 1600×900, blend | `93ff16`/`27b63a` | distance blur: blended over the scene by depth (decision 0031's half setting) | `f_8007d0` |
| 1 | 800×450 | `abf6e5`/`d794c4` | bloom: bright parts | `f_802e40` |
| 6 | 400×225, 200×112, 120×67 | `e1e948`/`158d33` | bloom: blur, across then down, per level | `f_802e40` |
| 1 | 1600×900, blend | `53e413`/`58b87f` | bloom: the three levels onto the scene | `f_802e40` |

### Bloom `f_802e40(device, renderer)`

`renderer` is the renderer object (`main+0x56ab1b0`). Its images are 0x28-byte records from `+0x2e28`: record `i` at
`+0x2e28 + 0x28*i` holds the engine texture object at `+0`, a descriptor at `+8` and two flags at `+0x22`/`+0x23`.
Render targets come from the target manager `[main+0x5865158]`, vtable slot `+0xd8`, by id; their size is
`u16 +0x3a` × `u16 +0x3c`.

1. **Bright parts** (`d794c4`, into the 800×450 target) from records 0 (slot 0) and 11 (slot 1). Constants (fragment
   cbuf 6, 0x30 bytes) = `renderer +0x800..+0x80f` (row 0, for slot 0), `+0x7f0..+0x7ff` (row 16, for slot 1) and
   `+0x7b0`; when `renderer +0x388d` is set, the
   `.w` of both rows is raised to at least 1.0. The shader: `d = in1 - in0`, `m = max|d|` over rgb,
   `a = max(in1 - 1.5 m, 0)`, out.rgb = `max(a * row16.rgb - row16.w, in0 * row0.rgb - row0.w)`,
   out.a = `max(in1.a, in0.a)`, all clamped at 0. Its output is record 9.
2. **Blur**, three levels, each across (into attachment 1 of target id 7, 8, 9) then down (into attachment 0):
   9 → 20 → 19 (400×225), 19 → 22 → 21 (200×112), 21 → 24 → 23 (120×67) (tables `main+0x1298380` ids, `+0x129838c`
   / `+0x12983a4` / `+0x1298398` records). Constants (cbuf 6, 0x40 bytes per pass): row 0 = (step, 0, 0, 0) across or
   (0, step, 0, 0) down with step = `renderer +0x7c0 + 4*level` / the target's width (or height), row 16 = 1.0 ×4,
   row 32 = the tap weights 0.150217, 0.138667, 0.118165, 0.092952, row 48 = 0. The shader adds 4 pairs of taps
   (8 taps) with those weights; the tap positions come from the vertex shader.
3. **Composite** (`58b87f`, into the 1600×900 scene image, blend on) from records 19, 21, 23 (slots 0, 1, 2).
   Constants (0x18 bytes, rows 0, 8, 16, two floats each) = (`+0x7d0`, `+0x7e0`), (`+0x7d4`, `+0x7e4`),
   (`+0x7d8`, `+0x7e8`): per level a brightness and a weight. The shader combines the three levels as a "screen"
   (1 - (1-a)(1-b)(1-c), each clamped) and its alpha from their brightest channels.

At 4K 21:9 the composite took 1.5-2.2 ms of GPU per frame (2026-10-28), the rest of bloom well under 1 ms.

All 8 draws use one sampler: min filter 3, mag 1, clamped (7), levels 0-15. The runtime's texture filtering
setting upgrades it (it allows mip levels), so a pass of ours must make its sampler the same way
(`gpu_sampler`), or about 20 texels per frame come out one bit different (decision 0037).
The full-screen quad in the engine's vertex buffer: corners (-1, 1), (-1, -1), (1, -1), (1, 1) with texture
coordinates (0, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1), (1, 0).

### Distance blur `f_8007d0(device, renderer)` (decoded 2026-10-28; ours: decision 0038)

Same renderer object and image records as bloom. Nothing is drawn when `renderer +0x868` (the number of blur
rounds) is 0.

1. **Shrink** into target id 5 (800×450), attachment 0 = record 9. Two variants:
   - `renderer +0x2c70` clear (the bamboo forest): a plain copy of record 0 (the scene), program by id
     `+0x38a8` (`98c09b`/`2d68c8`: colour × the vertex colour).
   - `+0x2c70` set: program `+0x38ea`, reading record 0, record 42 (`+0x34b8`, depth) and a texture from a G4TX
     container (`[+0x2e00]+0x18`, index `+0x2e1e`), with 0x20 bytes of constants (`+0x2c8c`, `(float)u32 +0x2c90 /
     +0x2c94`, `+0x2ca4`, `+0x2ca0`, `+0x2ca8`), and three sampler slots set to clamp. Not seen yet.
2. **Blur** `f_7f3620(radius +0x864, device, (+0x860, +0x860), rounds +0x868 (at most 32), target 5, 0, 1,
   record 9, record 10)`: per round, across from record 9 into attachment 1 (record 10), then down from record 10
   into attachment 0 (record 9), each by `f_7f3900` (`29d827`/`b8856c`, sampler slot 0 clamped on all axes). Weights:
   `w_k = expf(-k²/2r²) / s` for k = 0..7, `s = 2 Σ w` (the centre counted twice; the sdk's `expf` is musl's,
   runtime/src/hle_math.c). Constants (0x40 bytes): row 0 = (+0x860 / width, 0, 0, 0) across or (0, +0x860 / height,
   0, 0) down (the target's size), row 16 = 1.0 ×4 (the vertex colour's factor), rows 32 and 48 = the 8 weights.
   The blur's 16 taps are the centre twice and ±1..7 steps (the vertex program adds the step up as bloom's does).
3. **Composite** into target id 2 (the scene), program `+0x38c4` (`93ff16`/`27b63a`), from record 9 (slot 0) and
   record 42 (slot 1, depth): vertex constants (0x10) = `+0x86c` / record 42's width and height (from its
   descriptor `[+0x34c0]`, u16 +4 / +6); fragment constants (0x20) from the camera's near/far (`+0x5c0`, `+0x5c4`) and
   the focus settings `+0x850..+0x85c`; it also reads the camera block (cbuf 8, byte 48). The amount is the depth's
   distance past the focus (5 depth taps: the centre and 4 diagonal neighbours); pixels with almost none are
   discarded (`KIL`), the rest get the blurred colour with that amount as alpha. With `+0x2c70` set, a 0x70-byte
   variant with another G4TX texture (`+0x2e20`).

The runtime already changes this pass: the settings panel's DISTANCE BLUR halves the composite's amount (its
fragment constants row 0 `.w`) or skips the composite, and with full-size effects records 9 and 10 keep the
game's size ratio (`gpu_keep_game_ratio`, set when the game's draws of these programs are seen). The blur's quad has
three inputs (position, colour, texture coordinate), bloom's two.

## Model detail at a distance (checked 2026-10-27): not used

The engine has a level-of-detail class, `lives::gmdCObjModelLodInfo`, registered with its property system in
`main+0xa31a20`: `m_pLodDistance` at `+0x38` (a pointer to floats in the loaded model data), `m_lodDistanceNum` at
`+0x40` (a byte), set by `SetupLodDistance` (`main+0xa319e0`: info `x1`, floats `x2`, their size in bytes `x3`);
`lodChangeFadeTime` suggests models fade between levels. In the town walk, the late-game bamboo forest and the
Yo-kai World, a hook on `SetupLodDistance` was never called, every object had one geometry (object `+0x1c8`), and
the submeshes an object draws changed only by a few at a time as the camera turned (per-submesh culling by their
bounding boxes), never as a swap at a distance. So these maps don't use model LOD, and a "push detail further"
setting has nothing to act on there. What looked like distance drop-off was the distance blur and the texture
filtering (decision 0031 and the settings panel). Battles and other maps are not checked.

## Lighting stage (measured 2026-10-30)

Late-game save, bamboo forest, 4K 21:9 (5120×2160, so "half" = 2560×1080), one frame (`YW4_GPU_TRACE` +
`YW4_TRACE_DRAW_CALLERS`, `tools.yw4.mainview`) and per-pass GPU time over 300 frames (`YW4_GPU_PASSES=1`; 12.5 ms
of GPU time per frame in all). Between the G-buffer and the lit material pass:

| Pass | Size | Program (vs/fs) | GPU ms | What |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| depth copy | half | `98c09b`/`95ea1b` | ~0.3 | the G-buffer's colour and depth shrunk (`f_80d270`, `f_8050d0`) |
| | ⅓ | `98c09b`/`95ea1b`, `198f41`/`42759b` | ~0.4 | the same at a third (`main+0x80f988`, `f_8050d0`), then the lamp lights (`f_8050d0`) |
| **shadow mask** | half | `98c09b`/`06d03ad7` | **2.57** | `f_7f3e90`: the screen-space shadow, our PCSS inside (decision 0025): the most expensive pass of the frame |
| | half, 2 targets (0x29) | `98c09b`/`790774` | 0.16 | `f_7f4c90`: the lighting inputs (not the lamp lights, as first thought) |

The shadow mask is ~2.6 of the stage's ~3.5 ms, so it is the first piece of the stage to become ours: its program
is ours since 2026-10-30 ([decision 0044](decisions/0044-shadow-mask-pass.md), not bit-exact: a few texels differ by
one bit). Its shader
(`work/shaders/glsl/06d03ad703b4bee5.frag`, 725 lines with the PCSS helper) reads cb8 (camera: rows 20-23, 31),
cb12 (rows 0, 2, 3 and indexed rows: the cascades), `tex1` (sampled first: the half-size depth), `tex0` and the
shadow-map array (`tex15`), with up to six shadow lookups in cascade loops.

What the shadow mask computes, per half-size pixel (decoded from its NV assembly,
`work/shaders/asm/06d03ad703b4bee5.frag.asm`; cb rows are byte offsets / 16; `buf14` holds the texture handles):

1. **Position.** Depth from `buf14[8]` (the half-size depth) at the pixel; clip = (2u − 1, 1 − 2v, depth, 1); the
   view-space position is cb8 rows 20, 21, 22 dotted with clip, over row 23 (the inverse projection).
2. **Cascade.** For c = 0, 1, 2: the first whose cb12 row 7+c .x reaches −z (view depth) is used; for c < 2 a
   blend weight toward cascade c+1 from rows 7+c and 8+c. No cascade: the output is (0, 1, 0, 0).
3. **Normal.** The G-buffer normal from `buf14[0]` (rgb × 2 − 1, normalized); N·L with cb12 row 0 (the light
   direction). N·L ≤ 1e-4 (facing away) counts as in shadow: the mask is max(shadow, that flag) (the mask is how much is in shadow: 1 in shadow, 0 lit).
4. **Five lookups.** cb12 rows 10+4c..12+4c take the position and normal into the cascade's light view. Four
   taps sit ± an offset (cb8 row 31 .zw × cb12 row 4+c .xy) along the light's x and y, slid along the light
   depth so they stay on the receiving surface's plane; each tap and the centre are projected with rows 22+4c..25+4c.
   Bias: the centre's position in the 1024 texel grid (rows 34+4c..37+4c) gives a sub-texel distance; bias =
   min(row 2 .x + row 2 .y × saturate(distance / tan-like(N·L)), row 2 .z), subtracted from the depth compared.
   The five shadow compares are averaged (× 0.2). This is where our PCSS replaces each compare (decision 0025).
5. **Blend.** With a next cascade: one compare there (same bias), mixed in by the blend weight.
6. **Fade and output.** cb12 row 3 .xy (near, far) linearize the depth: lin = near / (far − depth × (far −
   near)); x = shadow × (1 − saturate(lin)²), y = z = lin, w = 0.

After the lit pass: a full-size
depth-only draw (`98c09b`/`6b4575`, 0.30 ms) and full-size draws `53e413`/`ace8e4`, `ff262a`/`4893be` (to identify).

### The screen passes (decoded 2026-11-02; ours: decision 0046)

The town save's frame (1600×900), in order, with what each program does (our readable version in
`runtime/shaders` in brackets). The renderer's image records (`renderer +0x2e28`, 0x28 bytes each) they use:
0 the lit scene, 4 the G-buffer colour read by the copy, 9-14 half-size images (14: the half G-buffer colour), 15-18
third size, 19-24 the bloom levels, 33-35 half-size (format 0x29), 42 the G-buffer depth, 43 a second full-size
depth, 44 half depth, 45 third depth, 49-51 1×1 textures. The half-size copy binds its images through a command
chunk the engine records once (the target description at `renderer +0x3720` points into it), not the records' first
words, and afterwards leaves record 44 bound to fragment texture 13 for later passes.

| Program | What |
|---|---|
| `95ea1b` | colour × the quad's colour and the depth texture as the depth, shrunk: the half-size copy before the shadow mask, the third-size one, and after the lit pass the lit scene into a half-size image (`depth_copy`) |
| `790774` | the lighting inputs: target 0 = (shadow, texture 1, texture 2, linear depth), target 1 = (normal × 2 − 1, linear depth); textures 1 and 2 are 1×1 in the town by day (`lighting_inputs`) |
| `42759b` | the lamp lights: point-light volumes (804 vertices in the town) at a third of the size, added: the position from the depth through the inverse projection (camera rows 20-23), falloff saturate((distance − radius) / −radius)² × the light's colour, × saturate(N·L) (`lamp_light`) |
| `627287` | sky and aerial perspective, at the far plane with the depth test: a camera ray from the field of view (pass constant x, as sin / cos), aspect and the camera's axes (rows 1, 2); a gradient by the ray's height (rows 34-38 below the horizon, 40-42 above, horizon row 47); a fog image (texture 14 .z) looked up edge-aware through a small depth (texture 13) like `3c94bd`; height fog exp2(−(height − row 45.x) × row 45.y × log2 e); Rayleigh (3 / 16π (1 + cos²) × 12) and Mie (Henyey-Greenstein-like, g = row 44.x, 3 / 8π) phases toward the sun (light row 2); extinction 1 − exp2(−distance × rows 43, 45, 46); desaturation by rows 39, 43.w, 46.y (`sky_fog`) |
| `6b4575` | depth only: texture 1 as the depth (the full-size depth copy after the lit pass) (`depth_only_copy`) |
| `22d015` | tone mapping: max(scene, 0), luminance with F16 weights, extended Reinhard L(1 + L / white²) / (1 + L) with L = luminance × exposure / adapted brightness (a storage buffer, eased toward a target), blended in by a strength that bit 0 of a G-buffer channel (texture 2 .z × 255) changes (`tonemap`) |
| `2571d0` | copy with negatives raised to 0 (`clamp_copy`) |
| `3c94bd` | edge-aware upsample: per axis, where the small depth's neighbours differ, the sample moves (2f − 1) texels toward the side whose depth is like the full-size depth's (`edge_upsample`) |
| `2d68c8` | copy × the quad's colour (`tinted_copy`) |
| `3f9fc9` | the game's own FXAA, the console FXAA 3: four corner lumas, blurs of 2 and 4 samples along the edge, the 4-sample one unless it leaves the lumas' range (`game_fxaa`) |
| `d2aaa3` | fill with the quad's colour (`vertex_colour`) |

`docs/ghidra.md`:

```md
# Ghidra setup

How we load `main` in Ghidra, both by hand (GUI) and from scripts (headless).

## Versions

| Tool | Version | Why this one |
|---|---|---|
| Ghidra | **12.1.2** | The Switch loader is built for exactly this version. Ghidra refuses extensions built for any other version, so don't upgrade Ghidra until the loader has a matching release. |
| [Ghidra-Switch-Loader](https://github.com/Adubbz/Ghidra-Switch-Loader) | 1.6.1-c600d05 (for Ghidra 12.1.2) | Loads NSO/NRO/KIP directly: decompresses segments, applies relocations, imports `.dynsym` names. |
| JDK | 21 | Ghidra 12 needs a full JDK 21, not just a JRE (`javac -version` must work). |

Both are user-installed tools (Apache 2.0 and ISC licenses). We only run them and never copy their code.

## Install

1. Unzip Ghidra 12.1.2 anywhere outside the repo.
2. Unzip the Switch loader release into `<ghidra>/Ghidra/Extensions/`, so you get `<ghidra>/Ghidra/Extensions/SwitchLoader/extension.properties`. Installing there (not through the GUI's per-user extension manager) makes it available to headless runs too.
3. Set `[tools] ghidra_dir` in `config.local.toml` to the Ghidra folder.

## Headless analysis (scripted)

```
python -m tools.yw4.ghidra            # import + full auto-analysis + export (first run is long)
python -m tools.yw4.ghidra --export   # only re-export from the existing project
```

- Refuses to run unless `main` matches `target.toml`.
- Project: `<work_dir>/ghidra/yw4.gpr`. Log: `<work_dir>/ghidra/analyze.log`.
- Heap defaults to 12 GB. Set `GHIDRA_HEADLESS_MAXMEM` to change it. Ghidra's own default of 2 GB is too small for a 17 MB `.text`.
- Output: `<work_dir>/ghidra/main.functions.json`, from `tools/ghidra/ExportFunctions.java`. One entry per function: `entry` and `size` as offsets from the image base (they match offsets in `work/exefs/main.bin`), `name`, `thunk`, and `ranges` when the body isn't contiguous.

**The project database contains the game's code.** It lives in `work/` (gitignored) and must never be committed or shared (CLAUDE.md rule 1). `.gitignore` also blocks `*.gpr` / `*.rep` anywhere.

## Opening it in the GUI

1. Run `<ghidra>/ghidraRun.bat`.
2. **File → Open Project →** `<work_dir>/ghidra/yw4.gpr`, then open `main`. Analysis is already done.

To start fresh instead: create a project, **File → Import File →** your ExeFS `main`. The format should show as "Nintendo Switch Binary". Accept the default analyzers.

## Seeding functions (do this after the first analysis)

```
python -m tools.yw4.ghidra --seed
```

Auto-analysis alone finds functions mainly through direct calls. On `main` it found 17,605 functions in 15 minutes, but only **2,645 of the 17,853** functions reached through vtables and pointer tables. `--seed` passes every `.eh_frame_hdr` start and address-taken target to `tools/ghidra/SeedFunctions.java`, which creates the missing functions and re-runs analysis on them.

Result (2026-10-20): 22,572 functions created, 6 failed. Ghidra now has **40,223 functions** in `.text`.

## Cross-checking Ghidra against our own parsers

```
python -m tools.yw4.compare_functions
```

| Source | Count | Missing from Ghidra |
|---|---|---|
| `.eh_frame_hdr` starts | 39,094 | 5 |
| address-taken targets | 17,853 | 4 |
| Ghidra-only (neither list) | 1,132 | – |

Missing addresses go to `work/ghidra/function_gaps.json`.

Takeaway for the recompiler: **the unwind table is the main source of function boundaries**, plus the address-taken set. Ghidra is for reading code and cross-references. The 1,132 Ghidra-only functions (thunks and small leaf functions without unwind info) are worth checking before Phase 2 decides whether to trust them.

# Graphics options in detail

The options in the [README](../README.md#graphics-options), with the comparisons and measurements behind them. Keys
work while playing; the environment variables set them at start ([debugging.md](debugging.md)).

## Native shadow pass (panel: SHADOW PASS)

Our own renderer draws the shadow casters the game would draw, from the game's data, instead of replaying the game's
draw calls one by one ([decision 0024](decisions/0024-shadow-pass.md)). It covers static, cut-out, skinned and
instanced casters, including props fading in and out and wind-swayed plants; the game still draws the rest (a second
kind of character, a few others).

The shadow pass is the first step, not the end point: the plan is to **replace the game's whole renderer with our
own**, one pass at a time ([the goals](../README.md#our-own-renderer)). Replaying the game's draw calls ties
every frame to the Switch's choices: its resolution, its 16:9 layout, its shadow map size and filters. A renderer of
our own draws the same scene from the game's data, so those choices become ours to change.

Same save and frame, the game's shadows against ours. The only differences are animation timing between the two
runs (Whisper's float, idle poses, leaves):

| The game's shadows | Our shadow pass |
|---|---|
| ![The game's shadows](screenshots/08-shadows-game.jpg) | ![Our shadow pass](screenshots/09-shadows-ours.jpg) |

<details><summary>Difference image (white: pixels that differ)</summary>

![Difference](screenshots/10-shadows-difference.jpg)

</details>

Cost per frame on a scripted walk through the town (average of 3 runs each, alternating, nothing else running;
RTX 4070 Laptop):

| Per frame | The game's shadows | Our shadow pass | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Game work, average | 10.9 ms | 10.3 ms | **−0.6 ms** |
| Game work, 95th percentile | 18.0 ms | 16.8 ms | **−1.2 ms** |
| GPU busy, average | 11.3 ms | 10.9 ms | −0.3 ms |
| Process CPU | 72.7% of a core | 71.3% of a core | −1.4 points |

## Shadow map size (panel: SHADOW MAP)

1024 (the game's), 2048 or 4096. Bigger maps give sharper edges, mostly in the far cascades. Recommended: 4096.

The bamboo forest with PCSS off at each size, and 2048 with PCSS ×1 added:

| 1024 (the game's) | 2048 |
|---|---|
| ![1024 shadow map](screenshots/12-shadow-map-1024.jpg) | ![2048 shadow map](screenshots/13-shadow-map-2048.jpg) |
| **4096** | **2048 + PCSS ×1** |
| ![4096 shadow map](screenshots/14-shadow-map-4096.jpg) | ![2048 shadow map with PCSS x1](screenshots/15-shadow-map-2048-pcss-x1.jpg) |

## PCSS, soft shadows (panel: SOFT SHADOWS)

Off, ×1, ×2, ×4. PCSS (percentage-closer soft shadows) makes shadows behave more like real ones:

- **Close shadows stay sharp.** Where a shadow touches the thing casting it (feet, poles, the base of a wall), the
  edge stays crisp.
- **Farther shadows get softer.** The farther the caster is from the surface the shadow falls on, the softer its
  edge, so tree canopies become soft dappled shade instead of a field of hard dots.
- **Less shimmering.** Hard shadow edges flicker and crawl as the camera moves, because each edge snaps to the
  shadow map's texels. Softer edges spread that over more pixels, so distant shadows shimmer much less.

It is added to the game's screen-space shadow mask shader only, so loading is as fast as before
([decision 0025](decisions/0025-pcss-soft-shadows.md)).

Another spot in the bamboo forest, 4096 map, PCSS off and its three strengths:

| PCSS off | PCSS ×1 |
|---|---|
| ![PCSS off: hard, speckled leaf shadows](screenshots/16-pcss-off.jpg) | ![PCSS x1](screenshots/17-pcss-x1.jpg) |
| **PCSS ×2 (recommended)** | **PCSS ×4** |
| ![PCSS x2](screenshots/18-pcss-x2.jpg) | ![PCSS x4](screenshots/19-pcss-x4.jpg) |

**Recommended: 4096 map with PCSS ×2** (also what the game starts with): sharp contact shadows and soft, clean canopy
shade. For the game's original shadows, start with `YW4_SHADOW_RES=1024 YW4_PCSS=0` (or set SHADOW MAP to 1024 and SOFT SHADOWS to OFF in the panel).

## Our G-buffer and material passes (panel: G-BUFFER)

The G-buffer and the lit material pass draw with our own draw calls and, for most surfaces, our own shaders
(`runtime/shaders/`), with `YW4_GBUFFER=native`; the panel's G-BUFFER switches back to the game's
([decision 0026](decisions/0026-gbuffer-pass.md)). They look exactly like the game's: compared pixel by pixel
within the same frame, 0 pixels differ. There is nothing to see yet; this is the base the resolution, aspect ratio
and lighting work builds on.

<section class="sec">
  <div class="wrap">
    <div class="about">
      <div>
        <div class="title"><h2>How it works</h2><p>Not an emulator: the game itself, rebuilt for the PC</p></div>
        <p>A static recompiler in the style of <a href="https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp">N64Recomp</a>: the game's ARM code
          is translated to C ahead of time and built into a Windows or Linux program, with the Switch's system services and
          its graphics API reimplemented on the PC (Vulkan).</p>
        <p>Unlike an emulator, which replays the game's GPU commands as they are, the port can replace the game's renderer
          piece by piece. That is how it gets higher resolutions, wider screens, better shadows and DLSS and FSR upscaling.</p>
      </div>
      <dl class="facts">
        <dt>Version</dt><dd>1.6.0 (beta)</dd>
        <dt>Platforms</dt><dd>Windows and Linux, x86-64</dd>
        <dt>Graphics</dt><dd>Vulkan</dd>
        <dt>Game version</dt><dd>2.2.0</dd>
        <dt>CPU, busy street</dt><dd>111% of a core (emulator: 210%)</dd>
        <dt>Memory</dt><dd>3.9 GB (emulator: about 7 GB)</dd>
        <dt>Licence</dt><dd>MIT</dd>
      </dl>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

/* the theme switch: the other theme than the one showing, kept for next time */
(() => {
  const btn = document.getElementById('theme'), root = document.documentElement;
  const dark = () => root.dataset.theme ? root.dataset.theme === 'dark' : matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches;
  const label = () => btn.setAttribute('aria-label', dark() ? 'Light mode' : 'Dark mode');
  label();
  const flip = () => {
    root.dataset.theme = dark() ? 'light' : 'dark';
    try { localStorage.setItem('yw4-theme', root.dataset.theme); } catch (e) {}
    label();
  };
  /* a slow cross-fade between the themes (site.css sets its length), where the browser can do one */
  btn.addEventListener('click', () => {
    if (document.startViewTransition && !matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches) document.startViewTransition(flip);
    else flip();
  });
})();
/* Auto-cycling (the hero's scenes, the Pad's tabs): the next one every CYCLE_MS, held while the mouse is over the
 * area or something in it has the keyboard focus, and never with reduced motion or a hidden tab. A pick by hand
 * starts the wait again. */
const CYCLE_MS = 5000;
function autoCycle(area, next) {
  if (matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches) return () => {};
  let over = false, timer = 0;
  area.addEventListener('pointerenter', e => { if (e.pointerType === 'mouse') over = true; });
  area.addEventListener('pointerleave', () => { over = false; });
  const restart = () => {
    clearInterval(timer);
    timer = setInterval(() => {
      if (!over && !document.hidden && !area.contains(document.activeElement)) next();
    }, CYCLE_MS);
  };
  restart();
  return restart;
}
/* the videos: YouTube's player put in on the first click, playing at once */
document.querySelectorAll('.video .play').forEach(b => {
  b.addEventListener('click', () => {
    const f = document.createElement('iframe');
    f.src = `https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/${b.dataset.yt}?autoplay=1`;
    f.title = b.dataset.title;
    f.allow = 'accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share';
    f.allowFullscreen = true;
    b.replaceWith(f);
  });
});
/* the before / after: the range input moves the line; the scene buttons swap the pair, and cycle on their own */
(() => {
  const ba = document.getElementById('ba'), range = ba.querySelector('input');
  const scenes = [...document.querySelectorAll('.scenes button')];
  const set = v => ba.style.setProperty('--pos', v + '%');
  range.addEventListener('input', () => set(range.value));
  let cur = 0;
  function pick(i) {
    const b = scenes[i], s = b.dataset.s;
    cur = i;
    ba.querySelector('.after').src = `compare/img/hero-${s}-4k.jpg`;
    ba.querySelector('.before').src = `compare/img/hero-${s}-switch.jpg`;
    for (const o of scenes) o.setAttribute('aria-pressed', o === b ? 'true' : 'false');
  }
  for (const s of document.querySelectorAll('.scenes button')) {  /* the next pictures, so a change shows at once */
    new Image().src = `compare/img/hero-${s.dataset.s}-4k.jpg`;
    new Image().src = `compare/img/hero-${s.dataset.s}-switch.jpg`;
  }
  const restart = autoCycle(ba.closest('.hero .wrap > div:last-child'), () => pick((cur + 1) % scenes.length));
  for (const [i, b] of scenes.entries()) b.addEventListener('click', () => { pick(i); restart(); });
  /* full screen: only where the browser can do it for an element (not iPhone Safari) */
  const fs = ba.querySelector('.fs');
  if (document.fullscreenEnabled) {
    fs.hidden = false;
    fs.addEventListener('click', () => {
      if (document.fullscreenElement) document.exitFullscreen();
      else ba.requestFullscreen().then(() => range.focus()).catch(() => {});
    });
    document.addEventListener('fullscreenchange', () =>
      fs.setAttribute('aria-label', document.fullscreenElement === ba ? 'Leave full screen' : 'Full screen'));
  }
})();
</script>

    ykview = document.getElementById('ykview'), tabs = document.getElementById('yktabs');
  let sel = 0, tapped = -1, lastPointer = 'mouse', curTab = 0;  /* tapped: the tile a touch already previewed */
  function view(a, k) {
    const v = a.views[k];
    curTab = k;
    for (const [j, c] of [...tabs.children].entries()) c.setAttribute('aria-pressed', j === k ? 'true' : 'false');
    document.getElementById('ykcap').textContent = v.cap;
    if (v.sw) {
      ykview.innerHTML = `<div class="ba"><img class="after" alt="YW4 Recomp" src="${v.pc}"><img class="before" alt="The Switch" src="${v.sw}">
        <span class="lab l">Switch</span><span class="lab r">YW4 Recomp</span><div class="line"></div>
        <input type="range" min="0" max="100" value="50" aria-label="Move the line between the Switch and YW4 Recomp"></div>`;
      const ba = ykview.firstElementChild, r = ba.querySelector('input');
      r.addEventListener('input', () => ba.style.setProperty('--pos', r.value + '%'));
    } else if (v.notes) {
      const esc = t => t.replace(/[&<>]/g, c => ({ '&': '&amp;', '<': '&lt;', '>': '&gt;' })[c]);

    } else ykview.innerHTML = `<img alt="${v.tab}" src="${v.img}">`;
  }
  function show(i) {
    const a = apps[i]; if (!a) return;
    sel = i;
    for (const [k, t] of [...grid.children].entries()) t.setAttribute('aria-selected', k === i ? 'true' : 'false');
    document.getElementById('ykdesc').textContent = a.d;
    document.getElementById('ykptitle').textContent = a.name;
    document.getElementById('ykopen').href = a.go;
    tabs.innerHTML = '';
    tabs.hidden = a.views.length < 2;
    for (const [k, v] of a.views.entries()) {
      const c = document.createElement('button');
      c.type = 'button'; c.textContent = v.tab;
      c.addEventListener('click', () => { view(a, k); restartTabs(); });
      tabs.appendChild(c);
    }
    view(a, 0);
  }
  for (const [i, a] of apps.entries()) {
    const b = document.createElement('button');
    b.title = 'Open: ' + a.name;
    b.type = 'button'; b.className = 'yk-tile'; b.setAttribute('role', 'option');
    const ic = document.createElement('span'); ic.className = 'yk-ico';
    ic.innerHTML = a.icon;  /* one icon style, as the game's tiles: no words or pictures on them */
    const lab = document.createElement('span'); lab.className = 'yk-lab'; lab.textContent = a.name;
    b.append(ic, lab);
    if (a.bang) { const g = document.createElement('span'); g.className = 'yk-bang'; g.textContent = '!'; b.appendChild(g); }
    /* the mouse: pointing previews, a click opens. The keyboard: moving previews, Enter opens. A touch screen has no
     * pointing, so as in the game with a pad: the first tap previews, a second tap on the same tile opens. */
    b.addEventListener('pointerdown', e => { lastPointer = e.pointerType; });
    b.addEventListener('pointerenter', e => { if (e.pointerType === 'mouse') show(i); });
    b.addEventListener('focus', () => { if (lastPointer === 'mouse') show(i); });
    b.addEventListener('click', e => {
      const touch = e.detail !== 0 && lastPointer !== 'mouse';
      if (!touch || (sel === i && tapped === i)) location.href = apps[i].go;
      else { show(i); tapped = i; }
    });
    grid.appendChild(b);
  }
  grid.addEventListener('keydown', e => {
    lastPointer = 'mouse';  /* keys again: moving previews */
    const n = apps.length, col = sel % 4;
    let to = null;
    if (e.key === 'ArrowRight') to = col === 3 || sel + 1 >= n ? null : sel + 1;
    if (e.key === 'ArrowLeft') to = col === 0 ? null : sel - 1;
    if (e.key === 'ArrowDown') to = sel + 4 < n ? sel + 4 : null;
    if (e.key === 'ArrowUp') to = sel - 4 >= 0 ? sel - 4 : null;
    if (to !== null) { grid.children[to].focus(); e.preventDefault(); }
  });
  /* the chosen app's tabs cycle on their own while the mouse is off the Pad */
  const restartTabs = autoCycle(pad, () => {
    const a = apps[sel];
    if (a.views.length > 1) view(a, (curTab + 1) % a.views.length);
  });
  show(0);
})();
</script>
</body>
</html>

```

`docs/known-issues.md`:

```md
# Known issues

What is known to be missing or wrong (checked 2026-11-13), roughly in the order it is likely to matter. Fixed items
move to [progress.md](progress.md).

## Graphics

- **The CPU caps busy scenes at about 70 frames/s** (measured 2026-10-29). With FRAME RATE unlimited, upscaling
  stops helping there: the GPU sits idle part of each frame. Busy late-game spot (`save_base_busy`, ~410 draws), DLSS
  Performance: game work 12.9 ms per frame, GPU 4.6 ms. The limit is the game's own code on the main thread and its
  two job threads (`main+0x97ad10` is the job queue). Next: profile both there (`YW4_PROFILE=1`, threads 6 and 7).
- **FSR frame generation with DLSS at 32:9 4K is slow for a few seconds after changing the aspect ratio** (~80
  frames of 200-660 ms "present"). The other upscaling and frame-generation choices recover at once (2026-11-10).
- **A short shadow flash after unpausing from the game's own pause menu** (the Plus button), only in the bamboo
  forest and not after closing our overlay (owner, 2026-11-06 and 2026-11-13). Minor; not looked into.
- **The first battle after loading a save stutters for its first few seconds**: about 25 frames of 70-80 ms
  ("window present" in the log) over ~4 s; the second battle in the same run had none (owner, 2026-11-13, late-game
  save, 4K 21:9, DLSS, DLSS frame generation). Cause not found. During the battles themselves frames were steady:
  ~38 game frames/s, GPU ~19-20 ms, no heavier than the bamboo forest around them.
- **PCSS (soft shadows) only reaches what the shadow mask covers.** Objects the game draws forward (6 other shadow
  shaders seen so far) keep the game's filter. Its strengths are tuned by eye in the town and the bamboo forest only.
- **Occlusion culling needs a GPU extension.** The game hides objects on the GPU from its occlusion queries
  (`runtime/src/gpu_query.c`). Without `VK_EXT_conditional_rendering` every such object is drawn, as before
  2026-11-14: the picture is the same, the GPU does more work. `SetRenderEnable(false)` is not done either (the
  game has not been seen to call it).
- **The one compute shader that writes an image has never been seen to run.** It is a plain texture copy
  (`2f3ceeb96f58c522`, the only one of the game's 5396 shaders with a storage image) and is supported since
  2026-11-14, but untested: no log so far (1278 of them) shows it. The log says `writes a storage image (first use`
  when it does.

## Linux

- **No launcher download yet**: the launcher builds as an AppImage ([decision 0071](decisions/0071-linux-launcher.md)),
  but it was checked only in WSL with software rendering, never on a real Linux desktop, and none is published.
  Until then the game is built from source ([Building on Linux](../README.md#building-on-linux)).
- **DLSS frame generation and Reflex are Windows only** (they come through Streamline). AMD FSR (upscaling and
  frame generation) and NVIDIA DLSS upscaling are now supported for Linux (Experimental)
  ([decision 0073](decisions/0073-dlss-fsr-on-linux.md)), but have not run on a real Linux GPU yet: FSR was checked on software Vulkan only, DLSS only builds.
- **A crash on exit** (segfault after "exit game") was seen once on 2026-11-12; later logs exit cleanly. Maybe gone,
  not confirmed by the tester.

## Game and system

- **C++ exceptions are not supported**: nothing in `main` throws
  ([decision 0012](decisions/0012-musl-startup-tls-exceptions-libc.md)).
- **The window stays blank for about 3.7 s at start**, while Vulkan, DLSS and the game's boot set up. Planned: a
  black screen with the game logo (`gamelogo.c`) until the first frame.

## Input and menus

- **A DualSense over Bluetooth adds about 2.5 s to the start** (first frame at 7.4-7.9 s, against 5.2-5.7 s on its
  USB cable). Two waits inside SDL while it reads the pad over the wireless link. A fix would open the pad off the
  window's thread; until then, use the USB cable.
- **Yo-kai Pad mouse support ([decision 0057](decisions/0057-mouse-menu-lists.md))**: open issues from real-mouse
  testing (owner, 2026-11-08; the rest of the Pad works):
  - **Watch skills**: characters cannot be clicked.
  - **Soulmate**: page is buggy.
  - **Slimey marks (Yo-kai Trophies)**: page not working.
  - **Treasure photos**: only up and down work.
  - **Organize Members → Switch moves**: not working.

## Tools

- The baseline benchmark against Eden ([baseline.md](baseline.md)) still lacks the opening scene's frame-time spread.

```

<script>
/* the theme switch: the other theme than the one showing, kept for next time */
(() => {
  const btn = document.getElementById('theme'), root = document.documentElement;
  const dark = () => root.dataset.theme ? root.dataset.theme === 'dark' : matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches;
  const label = () => btn.setAttribute('aria-label', dark() ? 'Light mode' : 'Dark mode');
  label();
  const flip = () => {
    root.dataset.theme = dark() ? 'light' : 'dark';
    try { localStorage.setItem('yw4-theme', root.dataset.theme); } catch (e) {}
    label();
  };
  /* a slow cross-fade between the themes (site.css sets its length), where the browser can do one */
  btn.addEventListener('click', () => {
    if (document.startViewTransition && !matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches) document.startViewTransition(flip);
    else flip();
  });
})();
</script>

        builds YW4Recomp on your PC once and starts it, with mods, DLC, saves and screenshots all in one place.</p>

    <article id="first-start">
      <div class="bar"><span class="q">1</span><h2>First start</h2><span class="cat">Setup</span></div>
      <div class="body">
        <div class="top">
          <div class="prose">
            <p>Follow the steps below to build your own copy of YW4Recomp:</p>
            <ol class="steps">
              <li><span><b>Point it at your game files.</b> NSP, XCI or extracted folders of version 2.2.0.</span></li>
              <li><span><b>It checks, extracts and builds the game.</b> locally, once: about 10 to 15 minutes.</span></li>
              <li><span><b>Play.</b> From the launcher, or from a shortcut.</span></li>
            </ol>
            <p>What you need before you start: the game and its 2.2.0 update, the keys
              for NSP and XCI files, a graphics card with Vulkan 1.3, and the free disk space. 
              The launcher checks your files before beginning the build process.</p>
          </div>
          <div class="spec"><dl>
            <dt>Needs</dt><dd>Windows (installer or portable zip) or Linux (AppImage), x86-64</dd>
            <dt>Graphics</dt><dd>Vulkan 1.3; NVIDIA RTX cards also get DLSS</dd>
            <dt>Your game</dt><dd>Yo-kai Watch 4++ with the 2.2.0 update</dd>
          </dl></div>
        </div>
        <figure class="whole">
          <img src="img/first-start.jpg" loading="lazy" alt="The launcher's first start: the welcome popup with three steps, the features and a 'don't show this again' box">
          <figcaption>The welcome popup, over the home screen</figcaption>
        </figure>
      </div>
    </article>

    <article id="game-files">
      <div class="bar"><span class="q">2</span><h2>Your game files</h2><span class="cat">Setup</span></div>
      <div class="body">
        <div class="top">
          <div class="prose">
            <p>Choose how your copy is stored: <b>NSP or XCI</b> files, or <b>extracted folders</b> (ExeFS and RomFS,
              the update applied). Then point it at the base game, the 2.2.0 update, the keys folder and, if you have
              them, the DLC.</p>
            <p><b>Nothing from the game comes with the launcher.</b> The YKW4 Recomp launcher does not ship with any game files nor assets and we do not condone piracy or unauthorized distribution of copyrighted materials.</p>
          </div>
          <div class="spec"><dl>
            <dt>Formats</dt><dd>NSP, XCI, or extracted folders</dd>
            <dt>Version</dt><dd>2.2.0 (Final version)</dd>
            <dt>Keys</dt><dd>prod.keys for NSP and XCI; an NSP also needs title.keys</dd>
            <dt>DLC</dt><dd>Optional (can be added later)</dd>
          </dl></div>
        </div>
        <figure class="whole">
          <img src="img/game-files.jpg" loading="lazy" alt="Where is your game?: NSP or XCI chosen, fields for the base game, the 2.2.0 update, the keys folder and the DLC folder">
          <figcaption>Step 1 of 5: where your game is (example paths)</figcaption>
        </figure>
      </div>
    </article>

    <article id="build">
      <div class="bar"><span class="q">3</span><h2>Check, options, build</h2><span class="cat">Setup</span></div>
      <div class="body">
        <div class="top">
          <div class="prose">
            <ul>
              <li><b>Check</b> launcher checks if the files are the right game and the right version,
                and the keys open them.</li>
              <li><b>Options</b>: where the build goes, whether saves and settings stay in the game's folder or in AppData, shortcuts, and your option to download AMD FSR or
                NVIDIA DLSS. It names your graphics card; DLSS is greyed out without an NVIDIA RTX card. The
                graphics settings themselves (resolution, shadows...) are in the game.</li>
              <li><b>Build</b>: the game's code is being translated and compiled into a Windows or Linux program on your PC, about
                10 to 15 minutes, once. You can follow along using the progress bar on screen.</li>
            </ul>
          </div>
          <div class="spec"><dl>
            <dt>Build time</dt><dd>About 10 to 15 minutes</dd>
            <dt>Saves</dt><dd>In the game folder or in AppData</dd>
            <dt>Downloads</dt><dd>AMD FSR, NVIDIA DLSS (optional)</dd>
            <dt>Record</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/ILFforever/YW4Recomp/blob/master/docs/decisions/0050-launcher-and-install-layout.md">decision 0050</a></dd>
          </dl></div>
        </div>
        <figure class="whole">
          <img src="img/check.jpg" loading="lazy" alt="The Check screen, all set: base game, update, keys, DLC and version each with a green tick, and Continue">
          <figcaption>Check: all set, with the files found</figcaption>
        </figure>
        <figure class="whole">
          <img src="img/options.jpg" loading="lazy" alt="The Options screen: your graphics card named, the install folder, saves in the game folder or AppData, AMD FSR, NVIDIA DLSS, free up space after building, shortcuts, and the download and disk size">
          <figcaption>Options: where the game goes, and what to download</figcaption>
        </figure>
        <figure class="whole">
          <img src="img/build.jpg" loading="lazy" alt="The Build screen: Building your game, 0% with a progress bar, Show details and Cancel">
          <figcaption>Build: the progress bar, initial build, about 10 to 15 minutes</figcaption>
        </figure>
      </div>
    </article>

    <article id="play">
      <div class="bar"><span class="q">4</span><h2>Play</h2><span class="cat">Every day</span></div>
      <div class="body">
        <div class="top">
          <div class="prose">
            <p>Once the game is built, the launcher opens on <b>Play</b>. With options:</p>
            <ul>
              <li><b>Overview</b>: what's new in this version, and your latest screenshots (<kbd>F12</kbd> in the game).</li>
              <li><b>Screenshots</b>, <b>Mods</b> (the English patch and other romfs mods; code patches in exefs don't work) and <b>DLC</b> tabs.
                Mods that change the same file are merged, and the Mods tab names the ones that really clash.</li>
              <li>Last played, play time, and shortcuts to the saves and the logs.</li>
              <li><b>Free up space</b>: you can remove the build files the game doesn't need to run.</li>
            </ul>
          </div>
          <div class="spec"><dl>
            <dt>Mods</dt><dd>romfs only, laid over your files at start</dd>
            <dt>Screenshots</dt><dd><kbd>F12</kbd> in the game</dd>
            <dt>Shortcut</dt><dd>Desktop and Start menu</dd>
          </dl></div>
        </div>
        <figure class="whole">
          <img src="img/play.jpg" loading="lazy" alt="The Play screen: the game's icon and Play on the left with mods, DLC, saves, logs and free up space; what's new and screenshots on the right">
          <figcaption>Play, with what's new in 0.7.0</figcaption>
        </figure>
      </div>
    </article>

    <article id="settings">
      <div class="bar"><span class="q">5</span><h2>Settings</h2><span class="cat">Every day</span></div>
      <div class="body">
        <div class="top">
          <div class="prose">
            <ul>
              <li><b>Playing</b>: the theme; what the launcher does when the game starts (hide and come back when it
                closes, minimise, stay open, or close); start in full screen; mods on or off.</li>
              <li><b>Cheats</b>: show or hide the game's Cheats page (off also turns every cheat off), and <b>Manage</b> to
                switch the cheats from here while the game isn't running.</li>
              <li><b>Where things are kept</b>: the game folder, and the saves and settings in it or in AppData.</li>
              <li><b>Shortcuts</b>: desktop and Start menu.</li>
              <li><b>Disk space</b>, <b>downloads</b> (changing them rebuilds the game) and <b>updates</b>.</li>
              <li><b>Rebuild</b> and <b>Uninstall</b> (it shows what is kept and how big it is).</li>
              <li><b>Support</b>: Buy me a coffee, if you'd like to. <b>Help</b> has <b>Report a bug</b> under
                Troubleshooting.</li>
            </ul>
          </div>
          <div class="spec"><dl>
            <dt>On Play</dt><dd>Hiding while running behaves like Ubisoft Connect</dd>
            <dt>Saves</dt><dd>choose Game folder or AppData</dd>
            <dt>Uninstall</dt><dd>with detailed selection</dd>
          </dl></div>
        </div>
        <figure class="whole">
          <img src="img/settings.jpg" loading="lazy" alt="The launcher's settings: playing, where things are kept, shortcuts, disk space, downloads, updates, Rebuild and Uninstall">
          <figcaption>Settings</figcaption>
        </figure>
      </div>
    </article>

    <article id="themes">
      <div class="bar"><span class="q">6</span><h2>Themes</h2><span class="cat">Look</span></div>
      <div class="body">
        <div class="top">
          <div class="prose">
            <p>Ten Yo-kai themes besides the built-in look: Damona, Happierre, Hidabat, Jibanyan, Komajiro, Komasan,
              Manjimutt, Shmoopie, Usapyon and Whisper.</p>
            <p><b>Synced with the game.</b> The game's in-game overlay and performance HUD use the same themes: the game
              opens in the launcher's theme, and a theme picked in the game (Settings › Look › Theme) is the
              launcher's too once the game closes.</p>
            <p>A theme is a small CSS file of colours in the launcher's <code>themes</code> folder, so a new one can be
              added without a rebuild; it shows up in both.</p>
          </div>
          <div class="spec"><dl>
            <dt>Themes</dt><dd>11, with the built-in one</dd>
            <dt>Where</dt><dd>Settings › Playing › Theme</dd>
            <dt>In the game</dt><dd>Settings › Look › Theme</dd>
            <dt>Record</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/ILFforever/YW4Recomp/blob/master/docs/decisions/0055-overlay-themes.md">decision 0055</a></dd>
          </dl></div>
        </div>
        <div class="pair">
          <figure class="whole">
            <img src="img/theme-jibanyan.jpg" loading="lazy" alt="The launcher's Play screen in the Jibanyan theme: red bars, yellow Play">
            <figcaption>Jibanyan</figcaption>
          </figure>
          <figure class="whole">
            <img src="img/theme-whisper.jpg" loading="lazy" alt="The launcher's Play screen in the Whisper theme: dark blue-grey bars, a blue Play">
            <figcaption>Whisper</figcaption>
          </figure>
        </div>
        <figure class="whole" style="margin-top: 14px">

<script>
/* the theme switch: the other theme than the one showing, kept for next time */
(() => {
  const btn = document.getElementById('theme'), root = document.documentElement;
  const dark = () => root.dataset.theme ? root.dataset.theme === 'dark' : matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches;
  const label = () => btn.setAttribute('aria-label', dark() ? 'Light mode' : 'Dark mode');
  label();
  const flip = () => {
    root.dataset.theme = dark() ? 'light' : 'dark';
    try { localStorage.setItem('yw4-theme', root.dataset.theme); } catch (e) {}
    label();
  };
  /* a slow cross-fade between the themes (site.css sets its length), where the browser can do one */
  btn.addEventListener('click', () => {
    if (document.startViewTransition && !matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches) document.startViewTransition(flip);
    else flip();
  });
})();
</script>
</body>
</html>

    <article id="installing">
      <div class="bar"><span class="q">1</span><h2>Installing a mod</h2><span class="cat">Mods</span></div>
      <div class="body">
        <div class="top">
          <div class="prose">
            <p>Put a mod in the layout a modded Switch uses, in <code>work/mods</code>: <code>contents/010086c00af7c000/&lt;mod&gt;/romfs/...</code>, or simply <code>&lt;mod&gt;/romfs/...</code>. At start its files replace the game's at the same paths and its new files are added; your dump is not changed. The launcher has an on / off switch for each mod.</p>
          </div>
          <div class="spec"><dl>
            <dt>Folder</dt><dd><code>work/mods</code></dd>
            <dt>Layout</dt><dd>A modded Switch's (Atmosphère)</dd>

    <article id="merger">
      <div class="bar"><span class="q">3</span><h2>YKW Mod Merger™</h2><span class="cat">Mods</span></div>
      <div class="body">
        <div class="top">
          <div class="prose">
            <p>Mods that change the same game file work together, which no Switch or emulator setup does. Six mods on at once below: the translation and five gameplay mods, three of which change the same item list. The launcher flags one pair only, the two Crank-a-kai mods, which change the same prizes; the rest are merged when the game starts.</p>
          </div>
          <div class="spec"><dl>
            <dt>Merges</dt><dd>Level-5 data lists (<code>.cfg.bin</code>), the archive list</dd>
            <dt>Records</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/ILFforever/YW4Recomp/blob/master/docs/decisions/0067-mods-merge-cpk-list.md">0067</a>, <a href="https://github.com/ILFforever/YW4Recomp/blob/master/docs/decisions/0068-mods-merge-data-files.md">0068</a></dd>
          </dl></div>
        </div>
        <figure class="whole">
          <img src="../screenshots/91-mod-merger.jpg" loading="lazy" alt="The launcher's Mods tab with six mods on: one pair flagged as clashing">
          <figcaption>The launcher's Mods tab: six mods on, one pair flagged</figcaption>
        </figure>
        <div class="tbl"><table>
          <tr><th></th><th>Modded Switch</th><th>Emulators</th><th>YW4 Recomp</th></tr>
          <tr><td>Several mods</td><td>One folder per game: you copy them all into it</td><td>A folder per mod, each on or off</td><td>A folder per mod, each on or off in the launcher</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Two mods ship the archive list</td><td>The last copied wins: the other mod's files come from the Japanese archives again</td><td>One copy wins</td><td>Merged: every file any mod takes out of the archives stays out</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Two mods change one data file</td><td>One copy wins, the other mod does nothing</td><td>One copy wins</td><td>Merged entry by entry: both work unless they change the same entries</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Clashes</td><td>Found while playing</td><td>Found while playing</td><td>The launcher names them before you play</td></tr>
        </table></div>
        <p class="note">Code patches (<code>exefs</code> <code>.ips</code> / <code>.pchtxt</code>) don't work: the game's code is
          recompiled for the PC, so its original bytes never run. Frame rate, widescreen and English names are built in.
          Only data lists are merged; textures, models, sound and whole archives can't be, and the later mod's copy is used.</p>
      </div>
    </article>

  </main>

<script>
/* the theme switch: the other theme than the one showing, kept for next time */
(() => {
  const btn = document.getElementById('theme'), root = document.documentElement;
  const dark = () => root.dataset.theme ? root.dataset.theme === 'dark' : matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches;
  const label = () => btn.setAttribute('aria-label', dark() ? 'Light mode' : 'Dark mode');
  label();
  const flip = () => {
    root.dataset.theme = dark() ? 'light' : 'dark';
    try { localStorage.setItem('yw4-theme', root.dataset.theme); } catch (e) {}
    label();
  };
  /* a slow cross-fade between the themes (site.css sets its length), where the browser can do one */
  btn.addEventListener('click', () => {
    if (document.startViewTransition && !matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches) document.startViewTransition(flip);
    else flip();
  });
})();
</script>
</body>
</html>

`docs/mouse-menu-map.md`:

# Yo-kai Pad mouse map

Map of every screen reached from the Yo-kai Pad (X menu), with its class vtable, control hash, layout and mouse
status. Positions are in the 1280 x 720 menu space. Work in progress (2026-11-16).

Method: `YW4_MOUSE_LOG=1` for the vtable and hash of each focus; `YW4_MOUSE_SCRIPT` for a scripted mouse;
F12 / script flag 256 for screenshots. Test saves are copies of `work/testsaves/save_base_lategame`.

## The Yo-kai Pad (yw::CMainMenu, vt main+0x14c0a88, grid hash 0x6098c54d)

How to open: X on the field (late-game save: clock popup first, A at about tick 4000, X at about 4300).
How to leave: B or a right click on the Pad closes it. The Pad opens on page 2 on this save.
Pages: a 4 x 3 grid, two pages. The first wheel notch goes to page 1; each later notch toggles (tested in a run).
Slot centres in 1280 x 720 space: x = 125 + 144 c, y = 215 + 143.5 r (screens[] "pad" row).
Mouse test set-up: replay `pad_live` (input ends at tick 4309, so the mouse is live). Important: while a replay still
runs, `window_input` (the mouse) is skipped, so a replay that runs on (e.g. to tick 9000) makes every mouse press
do nothing.

## Watch Skills: why its characters cannot be clicked (run G, 2026-11-16)

The character clicks at about (144, 420), (264, 420), (384, 420), (504, 420) fell through to the Pad under the page:
the log shows the Pad's grid focus stepping left and right and the Pad's Help, Settings, News and Play Record
opening. The Watch Skills page (vt 0x14c6b78) is not in screens[], so the mouse still thinks the Pad is in front.
So the fix is a screens[] row for vt 0x14c6b78, hash 0x5b8ae332, with the six character slots. Check the slot
positions on a screenshot before writing them (grid: `work/mouse_map_proof/runF_watch_grid.png` style, 80-unit lines).

## Fixes made (2026-11-16, after the map; runtime/src/mousemenu.c)

- `watch_skills`: vt 0x14bfa78 -> 0x14c6b78, hash 0x1405a5f7 -> 0x5b8ae332, x0 144, y0 420, dx 120, hw 60, hh 220.
  Tested (run L/M): Cole's character slot opens her skill tree with a click and returns with B. The hover step to the
  second character sends RIGHT but the focus does not move, so slots 2 to 6 still cannot be reached by mouse (open).
- `soulmates_tiles` (new row): vt 0x14c0838, hash 0x500ef853, 2 x 2, x0 440, y0 216, dx 400, dy 232, hw 164, hh 100.
  Tested (run N): the Soul List tile opens the Soulmates list (vt 0x14c0498, "Hot Pot Soul" list) by hover and click.
- `slimey_marks` (new row): vt 0x14c2348, hash 0x795f8b82, lv 0xff59842f, 1 x 8, x0 396, y0 162, dy 58.3, hw 332, hh 28.
  Tested (run N): the Slimey Mark icon opens the list. The row click is sent (not yet proven by a sub-page).
- `treasure`: now 5 x 3 (cols 5, rows 3, x0 176, y0 180, dx 229, dy 128, hw 108, hh 60), no wheel.
  Test: run O (see the status below).
- `trophies`: SCR_CLICK added (geometry not re-measured; it is the Yo-kai Trophies list on Pad page 2).
- Focus hook (`yw4_hook_menu_focus`): when the active screen's own hash takes the focus again while a page is open on
  the same menu, the page counts as closed (Watch Skills' skill tree left its layers unbalanced, so the screen stayed
  "covered" and the mouse ignored it: `front=0` in the log, run M).

## What is still unknown (end of mapping, 2026-11-16)

- Soulmates' Soul List page: needs the tile menu in screens[] first (then the click can get there).
- Switch Moves page: which list the rows belong to (the equipment or the moves list), and which control takes the focus.
- Trophies (page 2) rows: whether a click opens a detail page or only focuses the row.
- Watch Skills characters: the focus index for each character (not measured yet; the characters fell through to the Pad).
- Ark Scan and Ukiukipedia's inner lists: not reached (Ark Scan is a locked box most likely).
- Play Record: a stats page, no list.

## Notes from runs H to J

- Locked boxes: "The Ark Swap / Lambert Mail / Diary App isn't available right now." Each one takes all clicks until it
  is closed by A, and a right click does not close it. None of them is in screens[]. So after one of these, the rest of a
  run's clicks do nothing. Visit them last. A possible fix: a screens[] row for the box (vt 0x14bfa78, hash 0x31092732,
  one slot on its button, click = A).
- Members popup: the right click on the Pad closes the Pad (not the popup), so do not send an extra B on the Pad.
- The Watch Skills, Soulmates' tile menu and Treasure grid are all clicked wrongly today (see the rows above).

## Watch Skills: the character focus (2026-11-16, runs Q, R, S)

- Key-only replay runs Q and R (Pad -> Watch Skills, then RIGHT presses on the character select): the highlight moves
  Cole -> Summer -> Hammy -> Katie -> Bruno -> Dean (proof: work/mouse_map_proof/watch_skills_keys_right_steps.png).
  The game sends NO OnChangeFocus for hash 0x5b8ae332 on those moves: its control keeps focus index 0. So the
  screens[] focus cannot read the character.
- Fix in mousemenu.c: the mouse keeps its own character count (`wsk_index`): 0 when the screen opens from the Pad,
  +1 per RIGHT and -1 per LEFT the mouse sends. Built; pytest 71 passed.
- Not proven in a mouse run: run S (scripted mouse) failed before the screen opened. The Pad's A press on Watch Skills
  (slot 10) was lost: the log shows the focus reach slot 10 at the same time as the A press, and no Watch Skills
  focus followed. The same click worked in run M. Needs a retry (add a short wait after the last Pad step).

## Status of the five open issues (2026-11-16)

| Issue (decision 0057) | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Watch skills (characters cannot be clicked) | partly | Character 1 (Cole) opens with a click. Characters 2 to 6: the game's highlight moves with RIGHT/LEFT but is not reported through OnChangeFocus; a mouse count (`wsk_index`) now drives the steps. Built, not yet proven in a mouse run (run S lost the Pad click). |
| 2. Soulmate (page buggy) | partly | The tile menu now works (Soul List opens by hover and click). The Soul List's own rows are the old "soulmate" row (not re-tested). |
| 3. Slimey marks (Trophies) | partly | The Slimey Mark list opens from its icon and has a row (new `slimey_marks` row). The row click is sent; not yet shown to open a sub-page. Trophies (Pad page 2) got SCR_CLICK, not re-measured. |
| 4. Treasure photos (only Y works) | fixed (run P) | Was a 1 x 4 list; it is a 5 x 3 grid. Hover moves across columns and rows, a click opens the photo, B goes back. |
| 5. Organize Members -> Switch moves | partly | The click on Switch Moves works (run K). The moves/equipment page it opens is not in screens[] yet (its list hashes are in the map). |

Also found: locked boxes ("Diary / Lambert Mail / Ark Swap App isn't available") block all clicks until A is pressed,
and a right click does not close them. Not fixed; a possible row for the box is in the notes above.

    <article id="open">
      <div class="bar"><span class="q">1</span><h2>Opening it</h2><span class="cat">Basics</span></div>
      <div class="body">
        <div class="top">
          <div class="prose">
            <p>Press <kbd>Esc</kbd>, or on a controller the touchpad (PlayStation), Share (Xbox Series), Capture
              (Switch Pro) or Back and Start together. The game pauses behind it.</p>
            <p>The side panel: <b>Resume</b>, <b>Settings</b>, <b>Controls</b>, <b>Overlay</b> (the performance HUD),
              <b>Cheats</b>, <b>Report a bug</b>, <b>Return to title</b> and <b>Exit game</b>. <kbd>F1</kbd> opens Settings straight away.</p>
            <p>Keyboard, mouse and controller all work everywhere in it, and the key hints along the bottom follow
              whichever you used last.</p>
          </div>
          <div class="spec"><dl>
            <dt>Opens with</dt><dd><kbd>Esc</kbd>, touchpad, Share, Back + Start</dd>
            <dt>The game</dt><dd>Paused behind it</dd>
            <dt>Mouse</dt><dd>Hover chooses, click selects, right click goes back</dd>
            <dt>Record</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/ILFforever/YW4Recomp/blob/master/docs/decisions/0053-in-game-overlay.md">decision 0053</a></dd>
          </dl></div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </article>

    <article id="settings">
      <div class="bar"><span class="q">2</span><h2>Settings</h2><span class="cat">Graphics</span></div>
      <div class="body">
        <div class="top">
          <div class="prose">
            <p>Every graphics setting, in seven sections: Display, Anti-aliasing and upscaling, Frame generation and
              latency, Detail, Shadows, Look and Advanced. Each option shows what it does and what it costs in the box
              below, and the Switch's own choice is marked. <b>Sharpening</b> (off, low, medium, high, max) works with
              every anti-aliasing choice.</p>
          </div>
          <div class="spec"><dl>
            <dt>Sections</dt><dd>7</dd>
            <dt>Opens with</dt><dd><kbd>F1</kbd>, or Settings in the panel</dd>
            <dt>Saved</dt><dd>With the game's settings</dd>
          </dl></div>
        </div>
        <figure class="whole">
          <img src="../screenshots/97-overlay-settings.jpg" loading="lazy" alt="The overlay's Settings: the Display section with window mode, resolution, aspect ratio and frame rate">
          <figcaption>Settings: Display</figcaption>
        </figure>
      </div>
    </article>

    <article id="preview">
      <div class="bar"><span class="q">3</span><h2>Preview</h2><span class="cat">Graphics</span></div>
      <div class="body">
        <div class="top">
          <div class="prose">
            <p><b>See a change before you keep it.</b> Preview unpauses the game with your character held still and
              a bar at the bottom with the section's settings and the frame rate, so each change shows live.</p>
          </div>
          <div class="spec"><dl>
            <dt>Opens with</dt><dd><kbd>P</kbd>, Y / Triangle, or its button</dd>
            <dt>In the bar</dt><dd><kbd>W</kbd> <kbd>S</kbd> choose, <kbd>A</kbd> <kbd>D</kbd> change, <kbd>H</kbd> hides it</dd>
          </dl></div>
        </div>
        <figure class="whole">
          <img src="../screenshots/97-overlay-preview.jpg" loading="lazy" alt="Preview: the game running in the schoolyard under a bar with the shadow settings and the frame rate">
          <figcaption>Preview with the shadow settings</figcaption>
        </figure>
      </div>
    </article>

    <article id="controls">
      <div class="bar"><span class="q">4</span><h2>Controls</h2><span class="cat">Controls</span></div>
      <div class="body">
        <div class="top">
          <div class="prose">
            <p>Every Switch button with its two keys and its controller input, named as printed on your controller
              (× ○ □ △ on PlayStation, A B X Y on Xbox). Exploring and battles have their own sets, so a key can do one
              thing on the field and another in a battle.</p>
            <p>With a controller, the controller column is the only one it changes, so a controller never moves a
              keyboard key.</p>
          </div>
          <div class="spec"><dl>
            <dt>Per Switch button</dt><dd>Two keys and one controller input</dd>
            <dt>Sets</dt><dd>Exploring and battles</dd>
            <dt>Also</dt><dd>Mouse sensitivity, vibration, the shortcut wheel on or off</dd>
          </dl></div>
        </div>
        <figure class="whole">
          <img src="../screenshots/75-controls-dualsense.jpg" loading="lazy" alt="The overlay's Controls page with a DualSense: the mouse's sensitivities and buttons, then each Switch button with its keys and its PlayStation symbol">
          <figcaption>Controls, with a DualSense</figcaption>
        </figure>
      </div>
    </article>

    <article id="mouse">
      <div class="bar"><span class="q">5</span><h2>Mouse buttons</h2><span class="cat">Controls</span></div>
      <div class="body">
        <div class="top">
          <div class="prose">
            <p>What the left and right buttons, the wheel press and turning the wheel do, for exploring and for battles.
              Step through with ‹ ›, or pick from a list of every Switch button named by what it does there.</p>
            <p>The mouse also turns the camera; <kbd>Alt</kbd> frees it.</p>
          </div>
          <div class="spec"><dl>
            <dt>Parts</dt><dd>Left, right, wheel press, wheel up, wheel down</dd>
            <dt>Sets</dt><dd>Exploring and battles</dd>
          </dl></div>
        </div>

    <article id="quick-look">

      <div class="body">
        <div class="top">
          <div class="prose">
            <p>A card over the running game with what every button does, in the game's current mode: press <kbd>F2</kbd>,

              none of your presses while it shows.</p>
          </div>

            <dt>Pages</dt><dd>Exploring, Battle, Cutscene</dd>

    <article id="hud">
      <div class="bar"><span class="q">7</span><h2>Performance HUD</h2><span class="cat">Look</span></div>
      <div class="body">
        <div class="top">
          <div class="prose">
            <p>Frames per second with the 1% and 0.1% lows, a frame-time graph, the GPU's and the game's time per frame,
              CPU and memory, and with frame generation the frames shown and the game's own. <kbd>F3</kbd> steps it:
              off, compact, detailed. The Overlay page picks its corner, its parts, its size and how see-through it is,
              with a live preview.</p>
          </div>
          <div class="spec"><dl>
            <dt>Opens with</dt><dd><kbd>F3</kbd></dd>
            <dt>Forms</dt><dd>Compact or detailed</dd>
            <dt>Screenshots</dt><dd><kbd>F12</kbd> includes it</dd>
          </dl></div>
        </div>
        <figure class="whole">
          <img src="../screenshots/11-hud-in-town.jpg" loading="lazy" alt="Riding a bike down snowy Ordinary Street at 4K with the detailed performance HUD">
          <figcaption>The detailed HUD at 4K</figcaption>
        </figure>
      </div>
    </article>

    <article id="shortcut-wheel">
      <div class="bar"><span class="q">8</span><h2>Shortcut wheel</h2><span class="cat">Controls</span></div>
      <div class="body">
        <div class="top">
          <div class="prose">
            <p>All eight of the field's shortcuts with the mouse: hold the key bound to L (<kbd>1</kbd>) while
              exploring, point towards one, let go of the key. Let go in the middle to do nothing. The D-pad's four sit
              where the D-pad points, the hold-L four on the diagonals; the ones that can't be used there are greyed out.</p>
          </div>
