`launcher/package.py`:

```py
"""Make the downloads of a release (decisions 0052, 0054).

    python launcher/package.py [launcher]    the launcher: the NSIS installer and a portable zip, into work/package/dist/
                                             (on Linux: an AppImage, decision 0071)
    python launcher/package.py --stage-only  only work/package/builder/ (no Rust build)
    python launcher/package.py game          the game's build code alone (~3 MB), into work/package/game/: a game
                                             update the launcher downloads (tag vX.Y.Z)

What ships next to the launcher, in a folder called builder/:

    python/    the official embeddable Python, its ._pth pointing at src/
    src/       this repo's build code at one commit (git archive: committed files only, never the working tree)
    tools/     glslang.exe and hactool.exe, from their official releases
    licenses/  the licence of each

On Linux builder/ holds src/, tools/hactool (built here from its pinned source: hactool has no Linux release),
sdl3/ (built here too: Ubuntu 24.04 has no SDL3 package; a system SDL3 wins) and licenses/ only: Python, the compiler, glslang and SDL3 are the distribution's (decision 0071).

Every download is pinned to an exact version and SHA-256. Nothing from the game is ever in here (rule 1): src/ holds
only committed files, and the stage is refused if a game-data file type turns up. The compiler is not shipped: the
launcher downloads it on the first build (tools/yw4/deps.py fetch_toolchain).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import io
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tarfile
import urllib.request
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
OUT = REPO / "work" / "package"
CACHE = OUT / "cache"
STAGE = OUT / "builder"
DIST = OUT / "dist"
GAME_DIST = OUT / "game"

PYTHON_ZIP = ("https://www.python.org/ftp/python/3.13.5/python-3.13.5-embed-amd64.zip",
              "7d2650fd9d1b9d002d4a315d5f354247fd6a44f30517c7ef577b08f57a0fb6d9")
GLSLANG_ZIP = ("https://github.com/KhronosGroup/glslang/releases/download/16.6.0/glslang-16.6.0-windows-x86_64-release.zip",
               "82bf434e69b9bb4829de7e2b4bc2c5e7a7861e53d66cf75e5cc70f5f694a8d9b")
HACTOOL_ZIP = ("https://github.com/SciresM/hactool/releases/download/1.4.0/hactool-1.4.0-win.zip",
               "36e9a221c8a7949c86ada9388eb703c90663aedfe9f65b6032429614c5e1abe8")
GLSLANG_LICENSE = ("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KhronosGroup/glslang/16.6.0/LICENSE.txt",
                   "17e70c676e1521ff3e4686f04a2053d93a7e28a33be8de7ec37ab0ff72feb677")
HACTOOL_SRC = ("https://github.com/SciresM/hactool/archive/refs/tags/1.4.0.tar.gz",
               "1373c98ef8c58da42cb1e81b361283955caad0e1b8b5ad389b0ee49b7a21da43")
SDL3_SRC = ("https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/releases/download/release-3.4.18/SDL3-3.4.18.tar.gz",
            "9c75cf16330322c217dedd2e0609f1124f1b54b8633e763467b4684d0f4334a3")
HACTOOL_LICENSE = ("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SciresM/hactool/1.4.0/LICENSE",
                   "bde8a8c9f1fdcecaec2dd6f4733ed939a5ff2317a72126668e61ecae049eb5ab")

# what the build steps read: everything else in the repo (docs, tests, dev tools, the launcher itself) stays out
SOURCES = ["VERSION", "LICENSE", "target.toml", "recomp", "runtime", "third_party", "tools/yw4"]
GAME_DATA = {".nso", ".nca", ".nsp", ".xci", ".nsz", ".keys", ".ncz", ".istorage"}


def fetch(pin: tuple[str, str], name: str) -> bytes:
    url, want = pin
    path = CACHE / name
    if not path.is_file():
        CACHE.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        print(f"downloading {url}")
        with urllib.request.urlopen(url) as r, open(path, "wb") as f:
            shutil.copyfileobj(r, f)
    data = path.read_bytes()
    got = hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
    if got != want:
        path.unlink()
        raise SystemExit(f"{name}: SHA-256 {got}, expected {want}")
    return data


def git(*args: str) -> bytes:
    return subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(REPO), *args], capture_output=True, check=True).stdout


def game_tree(ref: str, dest: Path) -> str:
    """The game's build code at `ref` into `dest`: committed files only (git archive), the commit (recomp/build.py's
    build stamp: a player's PC has no git) and release.toml, which the launcher reads before using it."""
    shutil.rmtree(dest, ignore_errors=True)
    with tarfile.open(fileobj=io.BytesIO(git("archive", "--format=tar", ref, "--", *SOURCES))) as t:
        t.extractall(dest, filter="data")
    commit = git("rev-parse", "--short=7", ref).decode().strip()
    (dest / "COMMIT").write_text(commit + "\n")
    code = (dest / "tools" / "yw4" / "build_install.py").read_text()
    protocol = re.search(r"^PROTOCOL = (\d+)", code, re.M)
    min_launcher = re.search(r'^MIN_LAUNCHER = "([\d.]+)"', code, re.M)
    if not (protocol and min_launcher):
        raise SystemExit("tools/yw4/build_install.py: no PROTOCOL or MIN_LAUNCHER")
    version = (dest / "VERSION").read_text().strip()
    (dest / "release.toml").write_text(
        "# Written by launcher/package.py (decision 0054): what the launcher checks before using this game code.\n"
        f'version = "{version}"\ncommit = "{commit}"\nprotocol = {protocol[1]}\nmin_launcher = "{min_launcher[1]}"\n')
    bad = [p for p in dest.rglob("*") if p.suffix.lower() in GAME_DATA]
    if bad:
        raise SystemExit(f"game data in the game code, refusing: {bad[:5]}")
    return commit


WRONG_FILE_NAME = "WRONG FILE - READ ME.txt"
WRONG_FILE_NOTE = """\
You downloaded the wrong file.

This zip is a game update for the YW4 Recomp launcher. It isn't the game,
and there is nothing in it to open or install yourself.

What you want is the launcher. Download it here:
https://github.com/ILFforever/YW4Recomp/releases/latest

  - YW4-Recomp-Launcher-<version>-setup.exe      (installer)
  - YW4-Recomp-Launcher-<version>-portable.zip   (no install)

The launcher sets up the game from your own copy and downloads updates
like this one by itself: press Update on the Play screen.
""".replace("\n", "\r\n")  # Windows line ends, so Notepad shows the lines on any version


def game(ref: str) -> None:
    """The game update: the game code as one zip, files at its top level."""
    tree = OUT / "game-tree"
    commit = game_tree(ref, tree)
    version = (tree / "VERSION").read_text().strip()
    GAME_DIST.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out = GAME_DIST / f"yw4recomp-game-{version}.zip"
    with zipfile.ZipFile(out, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as z:
        for p in sorted(tree.rglob("*")):
            if p.is_file():
                z.write(p, p.relative_to(tree).as_posix())
        # Players who download this zip by hand from the release page find only build code in it: say what to get
        # instead (owner, 2026-11-14). The launcher unpacks it with the rest and never reads it.
        z.writestr(WRONG_FILE_NAME, WRONG_FILE_NOTE)
    shutil.rmtree(tree)
    digest = hashlib.sha256(out.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    print(f"{out.name}: {out.stat().st_size / 1e6:.1f} MB, {ref} = {commit}, SHA-256 {digest}")
    print(f"publish: gh release create v{version} --target {commit} --title \"YW4 Recomp {version}\" \"{out}\"")


def linux_hactool() -> None:
    """hactool for Linux, built from its pinned 1.4.0 source with the system's compiler (only libc linked)."""
    src = CACHE / "hactool-build"
    shutil.rmtree(src, ignore_errors=True)
    src.mkdir(parents=True)
    with tarfile.open(fileobj=io.BytesIO(fetch(HACTOOL_SRC, "hactool-1.4.0.tar.gz"))) as t:
        t.extractall(src, filter="data")
    top = src / "hactool-1.4.0"
    shutil.copy(top / "config.mk.template", top / "config.mk")
    subprocess.run(["make", f"-j{os.cpu_count() or 4}"], cwd=top, check=True, capture_output=True)
    shutil.copy(top / "hactool", STAGE / "tools" / "hactool")
    (STAGE / "tools" / "hactool").chmod(0o755)
    shutil.copy(top / "LICENSE", STAGE / "licenses" / "hactool.txt")


def linux_sdl3() -> None:
    """SDL3 for Linux players whose distribution has none (Ubuntu 24.04), built from the pinned source of the version
    the Windows build uses (tools/yw4/deps.py SDL_VERSION). SDL loads X11, Wayland, PulseAudio and PipeWire at run time
    (dlopen), so one build works across distributions; the packager's system needs their headers to build them in.
    Its pkg-config file is made relocatable (${pcfiledir}): the AppImage is mounted at a different path each run."""
    src = CACHE / "sdl3-build"
    shutil.rmtree(src, ignore_errors=True)
    src.mkdir(parents=True)
    with tarfile.open(fileobj=io.BytesIO(fetch(SDL3_SRC, "SDL3-3.4.18.tar.gz"))) as t:
        t.extractall(src, filter="data")
    top, build_dir, prefix = src / "SDL3-3.4.18", src / "build", STAGE / "sdl3"
    subprocess.run(["cmake", "-S", str(top), "-B", str(build_dir), "-G", "Ninja", "-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release",
                    f"-DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX={prefix}", "-DCMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR=lib", "-DSDL_SHARED=ON",
                    "-DSDL_STATIC=OFF", "-DSDL_TESTS=OFF", "-DSDL_EXAMPLES=OFF", "-DSDL_INSTALL_DOCS=OFF"],
                   check=True, capture_output=True)
    subprocess.run(["cmake", "--build", str(build_dir)], check=True, capture_output=True)
    subprocess.run(["cmake", "--install", str(build_dir)], check=True, capture_output=True)
    pc = prefix / "lib" / "pkgconfig" / "sdl3.pc"
    pc.write_text(re.sub(r"^prefix=.*$", "prefix=${pcfiledir}/../..", pc.read_text(), count=1, flags=re.M))
    shutil.rmtree(prefix / "lib" / "cmake", ignore_errors=True)  # the build reads pkg-config only
    shutil.copy(top / "LICENSE.txt", STAGE / "licenses" / "sdl3.txt")
    # the video and audio parts this build can load: a missing one means its headers were missing here
    cache = (build_dir / "CMakeCache.txt").read_text()
    for opt in ("SDL_X11", "SDL_WAYLAND", "SDL_PULSEAUDIO", "SDL_PIPEWIRE", "SDL_ALSA"):
        m = re.search(rf"^{opt}:BOOL=(\w+)", cache, re.M)
        print(f"sdl3: {opt} {m[1] if m else '?'}")


def stage(ref: str) -> None:
    shutil.rmtree(STAGE, ignore_errors=True)
    (STAGE / "tools").mkdir(parents=True)
    (STAGE / "licenses").mkdir()
    if sys.platform != "win32":
        linux_hactool()
        linux_sdl3()
        stage_src(ref)
        return

    py = STAGE / "python"
    with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(fetch(PYTHON_ZIP, "python.zip"))) as z:
        z.extractall(py)
    # The ._pth decides Python's whole import path (no PATH, no registry, no current folder). It stays as shipped:
    # the launcher names the game code's folder on each run (its own copy or a game update, decision 0054).
    if not next(py.glob("python*._pth"), None):
        raise SystemExit("the embeddable Python has no ._pth file")
    shutil.copy(py / "LICENSE.txt", STAGE / "licenses" / "python.txt")

    with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(fetch(GLSLANG_ZIP, "glslang.zip"))) as z:
        (STAGE / "tools" / "glslang.exe").write_bytes(z.read("bin/glslang.exe"))
    with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(fetch(HACTOOL_ZIP, "hactool.zip"))) as z:
        (STAGE / "tools" / "hactool.exe").write_bytes(z.read("hactool.exe"))
    (STAGE / "licenses" / "glslang.txt").write_bytes(fetch(GLSLANG_LICENSE, "glslang-license.txt"))
    (STAGE / "licenses" / "hactool.txt").write_bytes(fetch(HACTOOL_LICENSE, "hactool-license.txt"))

    stage_src(ref)


def stage_src(ref: str) -> None:
    commit = game_tree(ref, STAGE / "src")
    shutil.copy(STAGE / "src" / "LICENSE", STAGE / "licenses" / "yw4recomp.txt")

    bad = [p for p in STAGE.rglob("*") if p.suffix.lower() in GAME_DATA]
    if bad:
        raise SystemExit(f"game data in the stage, refusing: {bad[:5]}")
    files = [p for p in STAGE.rglob("*") if p.is_file()]
    print(f"stage: {len(files)} files, {sum(p.stat().st_size for p in files) / 1e6:.0f} MB, {ref} = {commit}")


def rust_host() -> str:
    """The Rust compiler's own target ("x86_64-pc-windows-msvc", "x86_64-pc-windows-gnu", ...); "" without rustc."""
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(["rustc", "-vV"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
    except (subprocess.CalledProcessError, FileNotFoundError):
        return ""
    return next((line.split(":", 1)[1].strip() for line in out.splitlines() if line.startswith("host:")), "")


def version_tuple(text: str) -> tuple[int, ...]:
    return tuple(int(p) for p in text.split("-")[0].split("."))


def check_tauri_cli(launcher: Path) -> None:
    """cargo's Tauri CLI at least the version package.json pins for Windows (the one the AppImage was made with). An
    older one fails late with only "failed to run linuxdeploy": tauri-cli 2.10.1 did on a player's PC (issue #13)."""
    want = json.loads((launcher / "package.json").read_text())["devDependencies"]["@tauri-apps/cli"].lstrip("^~=")
    hint = f"install it with: cargo install tauri-cli --version {want} --locked"
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(["cargo", "tauri", "--version"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    except OSError:
        raise SystemExit(f"cargo isn't on the PATH; {hint}")
    have = out.split()[-1] if out.split() else ""
    try:
        old = version_tuple(have) < version_tuple(want)
    except ValueError:
        raise SystemExit(f"cargo's Tauri CLI is missing ({out.strip() or 'no `cargo tauri`'}); {hint}")
    if old:
        raise SystemExit(f"cargo's Tauri CLI is {have}, older than {want}: its AppImage tools fail to bundle; {hint}")


def build_linux() -> None:
    """The AppImage (tauri.linux.conf.json), with builder/ and themes/ as its resources. Cargo builds in a folder of
    its own (YW4_LINUX_TARGET, default ~/.cache/yw4-launcher-target), never the repo's target/ that the Windows build
    uses; the Tauri CLI is cargo's (`cargo install tauri-cli --version 2.12.4`, checked: check_tauri_cli):
    node_modules holds Windows' CLI."""
    launcher = REPO / "launcher"
    check_tauri_cli(launcher)
    version = (launcher / "VERSION").read_text().strip()
    target = Path(os.environ.get("YW4_LINUX_TARGET", Path.home() / ".cache" / "yw4-launcher-target"))
    overrides = OUT / "tauri.package.linux.json"
    overrides.write_text(json.dumps({
        "version": version,
        "bundle": {"resources": {STAGE.as_posix() + "/": "builder/", (launcher / "ui" / "themes").as_posix() + "/": "themes/"}},
    }, indent=2))
    # linuxdeploy (the AppImage tool Tauri fetches) is an AppImage itself: unpacked instead of mounted, so no FUSE
    env = {**os.environ, "CARGO_TARGET_DIR": str(target), "APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN": "1"}
    subprocess.run(["cargo", "tauri", "build", "--bundles", "appimage", "--config", str(overrides)],
                   cwd=launcher, env=env, check=True)
    shutil.rmtree(DIST, ignore_errors=True)
    DIST.mkdir(parents=True)
    images = list((target / "release" / "bundle" / "appimage").glob(f"*{version}*.AppImage"))
    if len(images) != 1:
        raise SystemExit(f"expected one AppImage, found {images}")
    out = DIST / f"YW4-Recomp-Launcher-{version}-x86_64.AppImage"
    shutil.copy(images[0], out)
    out.chmod(0o755)
    print(f"{out.name}: {out.stat().st_size / 1e6:.0f} MB")


def build() -> None:
    if sys.platform != "win32":
        build_linux()
        return
    launcher = REPO / "launcher"
    version = (REPO / "launcher" / "VERSION").read_text().strip()  # the launcher's own number (0054)
    # only for this build: a plain `cargo build` has no stage and must keep working without one
    overrides = OUT / "tauri.package.json"
    # the GNU Rust build links WebView2 through WebView2Loader.dll (an MSVC build links it in): it has to sit next to
    # the launcher, or Windows refuses to start it (2026-11-09: a friend's fresh install said the DLL was missing).
    # Cargo's build puts it in target/release; a first build makes it, so build once before bundling.
    # Only that build: an MSVC Rust (GitHub's build check, rustup's default on Windows) has neither DLL to ship.
    release = launcher / "src-tauri" / "target" / "release"
    loader = release / "WebView2Loader.dll"
    dlls: dict[str, str] = {}
    if rust_host().endswith(("-windows-gnu", "-windows-gnullvm")):
        if not loader.is_file():
            subprocess.run(["cargo", "build", "--release"], cwd=launcher / "src-tauri", check=True)
        shutil.copy(loader, OUT / "WebView2Loader.dll")
        # the same build links Rust's unwinder from llvm-mingw's libunwind.dll (the toolchain's bin, on the PATH for
        # the build): it ships next to the launcher as well
        clang = shutil.which("clang")
        unwind = Path(clang).parent / "libunwind.dll" if clang else None
        if not unwind or not unwind.is_file():
            raise SystemExit("libunwind.dll not found: put llvm-mingw's bin on the PATH")
        shutil.copy(unwind, OUT / "libunwind.dll")
        # the bundle copies both into target/release; the launcher's own build script runs from there with
        # libunwind.dll loaded, so a copy left from the last build can't be overwritten (os error 32): start without them
        for dll in ("WebView2Loader.dll", "libunwind.dll"):
            (release / dll).unlink(missing_ok=True)
            dlls[(OUT / dll).as_posix()] = dll
    # the installer's own pictures and icon (installer_art.py), drawn for this version; only here, like the stage
    sys.path.insert(0, str(launcher))
    import installer_art
    sidebar, header = installer_art.draw(OUT / "installer", version)
    overrides.write_text(json.dumps({
        "version": version,
        "mainBinaryName": "YW4 Recomp",
        "bundle": {
            # the launcher's themes (themes.rs): files anyone can copy into this folder, so they ship next to the launcher
            "resources": {**dlls, STAGE.as_posix() + "/": "builder/", (REPO / "launcher" / "ui" / "themes").as_posix() + "/": "themes/"},
            "windows": {"nsis": {
                "installerIcon": (launcher / "src-tauri" / "icons" / "icon.ico").as_posix(),
                "sidebarImage": sidebar.as_posix(),
                "headerImage": header.as_posix(),
            }},
        },
    }, indent=2))
    npx = shutil.which("npx")
    if not npx:
        raise SystemExit("npx not found: install Node.js")
    subprocess.run([npx, "tauri", "build", "--config", str(overrides)], cwd=launcher, check=True)

    shutil.rmtree(DIST, ignore_errors=True)
    DIST.mkdir(parents=True)
    installers = list((release / "bundle" / "nsis").glob(f"*{version}*.exe"))
    if len(installers) != 1:
        raise SystemExit(f"expected one installer, found {installers}")
    shutil.copy(installers[0], DIST / f"YW4-Recomp-Launcher-{version}-setup.exe")

    with zipfile.ZipFile(DIST / f"YW4-Recomp-Launcher-{version}-portable.zip", "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as z:
        z.write(release / "YW4 Recomp.exe", "YW4 Recomp/YW4 Recomp.exe")
        for dll in dlls.values():  # the GNU Rust build's (above); none with MSVC
            z.write(OUT / dll, f"YW4 Recomp/{dll}")
        # the installer's resources: builder\ and themes\ (themes.rs finds those next to the exe; the zip had no
        # themes until 1.1.0, so a portable launcher had none, nor its game's overlay)
        for folder in ("builder", "themes"):
            for p in (release / folder).rglob("*"):
                if p.is_file():
                    z.write(p, Path("YW4 Recomp") / p.relative_to(release))
    for p in DIST.iterdir():
        print(f"{p.name}: {p.stat().st_size / 1e6:.0f} MB")


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("what", nargs="?", choices=("launcher", "game"), default="launcher")
    ap.add_argument("--stage-only", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--ref", default="HEAD", help="the commit whose build code ships (default: HEAD)")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if args.what == "game":
        game(args.ref)
        return 0
    stage(args.ref)
    if not args.stage_only:
        if git("status", "--porcelain", "--", "launcher"):
            print("note: launcher/ has uncommitted changes, and they will be in this build", file=sys.stderr)
        build()
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

```toml
[package]
name = "yw4-recomp-launcher"
version = "1.3.0"
description = "YW4 Recomp launcher: sets up the game from the player's own dump, builds it and starts it"
license = "MIT"
edition = "2021"

[build-dependencies]
tauri-build = { version = "2", features = [] }

[dependencies]
tauri = { version = "2", features = ["protocol-asset"] }
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1"
tauri-plugin-dialog = "2"
sha2 = "0.10"
toml = "0.8"

[profile.release]
# a small launcher: it only shows screens and runs the build steps. Thin LTO over 16 units, not full LTO on 1:
# packaging after a launcher change went from ~163 s of Rust compile to ~47 s (2026-11-13, owner's 16 threads),
# for 8.9 MB instead of 8.0 MB; the launcher's own speed doesn't matter
opt-level = "s"
lto = "thin"
codegen-units = 16
strip = true

# Windows' own API, already in the build through Tauri: free disk space, starting tools without a console window
[target.'cfg(windows)'.dependencies]
windows-sys = { version = "0.61", features = ["Win32_Storage_FileSystem", "Win32_Foundation", "Win32_System_Diagnostics_Debug", "Win32_UI_Shell", "Win32_UI_WindowsAndMessaging"] }
```

`launcher/src-tauri/src/buildrun.rs`:

```rs
// Screen 4, Build: runs the build tools (bundled in a download, decision 0052) into the install folder
// and tells the screen how far it is (decision 0050). Each Python step runs with YW4_PROGRESS=1 and its
// "@progress <step> <done> <total> <what>" lines go to the screen as they come; everything else goes to the log.
//
//   <install>\data\     exefs\, romfs\ (extracted or copied), dlc\ (checked add-ons, copied)
//   <install>\work\     the build: exefs\ (checked), recomp\, shaders\, build\yw4.exe + game.ini, deps\
//   <install>\mods\  screenshots\  logs\   (save\ and settings.ini too, when kept in the install folder)
//   <install>\builder\toolchain\   the compiler, downloaded on the first build; Free up space deletes it
//   <install>\config.toml   the tools' config for this install (YW4_CONFIG)
//
// A step whose result is already there is skipped, so Build after a Cancel picks up where it stopped.

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::io::{BufRead, BufReader};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::process::{Child, Stdio};
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use tauri::{AppHandle, Emitter, Manager};
use crate::platform;

#[derive(Deserialize, Clone)]
pub struct Plan {
    mode: String,                   // "files" or "folders"
    paths: HashMap<String, String>, // screen 1's choices
    install: String,
    fsr: bool,
    dlss: bool,
    saves: String,                  // "install" or "appdata"
    #[serde(default)]
    fresh: bool,                    // extract or copy the game files again, though the install already has them
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Running {
    child: Mutex<Option<Child>>,
    cancel: AtomicBool,
    busy: AtomicBool,
}

/// Is a build running? (ready.rs: the game set aside by an update is put back only when none is.)
pub fn building(app: &AppHandle) -> bool {
    app.try_state::<Arc<Running>>().map_or(false, |r| r.busy.load(Ordering::SeqCst))
}


#[derive(Serialize, Clone)]
struct StepEvent { id: String, state: String }
#[derive(Serialize, Clone)]
struct ProgressEvent { step: String, done: u64, total: u64, what: String }
#[derive(Serialize, Clone)]
struct DoneEvent { ok: bool, message: String }

/// What runs the build (decision 0052). A download has builder\ next to the launcher (launcher/package.py): its own
/// Python, the build code and tools, nothing taken from the PC. A launcher built with plain `cargo build` has no
/// builder\ and uses the repo it was built from, with the repo's Python and config.local.toml. On Linux a download's
/// builder/ holds the build code and hactool only: Python, the compiler, glslang and SDL3 are the distribution's
/// (decision 0071; tools/yw4/system.py checks them as the build's first step).
struct Builder {
    python: PathBuf,
    src: PathBuf,        // the folder the build's Python modules run from
    tools: Option<PathBuf>,  // builder\tools; None = the repo's
}

fn bundled_dir(app: &AppHandle) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    let b = plain_path(app.path().resource_dir().ok()?).join("builder");
    if cfg!(windows) { b.join("python").join("python.exe").is_file().then_some(b) } else { b.join("src").is_dir().then_some(b) }
}

/// Windows' long-path form `\\?\C:\...` (Tauri gives the resource folder that way) back to `C:\...`, for the
/// config file people read. A network path (`\\?\UNC\...`) is left as it is.
fn plain_path(p: PathBuf) -> PathBuf {
    match p.to_str().and_then(|s| s.strip_prefix(r"\\?\")) {
        Some(rest) if !rest.starts_with("UNC\\") => PathBuf::from(rest),
        _ => p,
    }
}

/// The launcher's own copy of the game code (builder\src), in a download.
pub fn bundled_src(app: &AppHandle) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    bundled_dir(app).map(|b| b.join("src"))
}

/// In a download the game code is the newest this launcher can run: its own or a downloaded game update
/// (update.rs, decision 0054).
fn builder(app: &AppHandle, inst: &Path) -> Builder {
    match bundled_dir(app) {
        Some(b) => {
            let code = crate::update::game_code(&b.join("src"), inst);
            let python = if cfg!(windows) { b.join("python").join("python.exe") } else { platform::python() };
            Builder { python, src: code.dir, tools: Some(b.join("tools")) }
        }
        None => {
            let p = Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("..").join("..");
            Builder { python: platform::python(), src: p.canonicalize().unwrap_or(p), tools: None }
        }
    }
}

/// True in a download: the Options screen then counts the compiler's download and disk space.
#[tauri::command]
pub fn builder_bundled(app: AppHandle) -> bool {
    bundled_dir(&app).is_some()
}

/// The current build's log file (<install>\logs\build_last.log), so a bug report can attach the last build's log.
static BUILD_LOG: Mutex<Option<std::fs::File>> = Mutex::new(None);

fn emit_log(app: &AppHandle, line: &str) {
    if let Ok(mut f) = BUILD_LOG.lock() {
        if let Some(f) = f.as_mut() { use std::io::Write; let _ = writeln!(f, "{line}"); }
    }
    let _ = app.emit("build-log", line.to_string());
}

/// The repo's own [tools] (compiler, glslang), when running from the repo.
fn repo_tools(repo: &Path) -> toml::Table {
    std::fs::read_to_string(repo.join("config.local.toml")).ok()
        .and_then(|s| s.parse::<toml::Table>().ok())
        .and_then(|t| t.get("tools").and_then(|v| v.as_table()).cloned())
        .unwrap_or_default()
}

fn lit(p: &Path) -> String {
    format!("'{}'", p.display())  // a TOML literal string: no escapes, Windows paths can't contain '
}

/// The game code's protocol (release.toml, or build_install.py --protocol).
fn code_protocol(b: &Builder) -> i64 {
    if let Ok(s) = std::fs::read_to_string(b.src.join("release.toml")) {
        if let Ok(t) = s.parse::<toml::Table>() {
            if let Some(p) = t.get("protocol").and_then(|v| v.as_integer()) {
                return p;
            }
        }
    }
    let mut cmd = crate::platform::command(&b.python);
    cmd.arg("-u").arg("-c").arg(BOOT).arg(&b.src).arg("tools.yw4.build_install").arg("--protocol")
        .current_dir(&b.src).stdout(Stdio::piped()).stderr(Stdio::null());
    platform::hidden(&mut cmd);
    cmd.output().ok()
        .and_then(|o| String::from_utf8(o.stdout).ok())
        .and_then(|s| s.trim().parse::<i64>().ok())
        .unwrap_or(1)
}

fn write_config(b: &Builder, plan: &Plan, inst: &Path) -> std::io::Result<PathBuf> {
    let get = |k: &str| plan.paths.get(k).filter(|v| !v.is_empty()).map(PathBuf::from);
    let mut s = String::from("# Written by the YW4 Recomp launcher for this install folder (decision 0050).\n[input]\n");
    s += &format!("exefs_dir = {}\nromfs_dir = {}\n", lit(&inst.join("data/exefs")), lit(&inst.join("data/romfs")));
    if let Some(b) = get("base") { s += &format!("base_nsp = {}\n", lit(&b)); }
    if let Some(u) = get("update") { s += &format!("update_nsp = {}\n", lit(&u)); }
    s += &format!("dlc_dir = {}\n[output]\nwork_dir = {}\n[tools]\n", lit(&inst.join("data/dlc")), lit(&inst.join("work")));
    if let Some(tools) = &b.tools {
        if cfg!(windows) {
            s += &format!("cc = {}\n", lit(&inst.join("builder/toolchain/llvm-mingw/bin/clang.exe")));
            s += &format!("glslang = {}\nhactool_exe = {}\n", lit(&tools.join("glslang.exe")), lit(&tools.join("hactool.exe")));
        } else if tools.join("hactool").is_file() {
            // Linux: the compiler and glslang are the system's (tools/yw4/system.py finds them)
            s += &format!("hactool_exe = {}\n", lit(&tools.join("hactool")));
        }
    } else {
        let tools = repo_tools(&b.src);
        for key in ["cc", "glslang", "hactool_exe"] {
            if let Some(v) = tools.get(key).and_then(|v| v.as_str()).filter(|v| !v.is_empty()) {
                s += &format!("{key} = {}\n", lit(Path::new(v)));
            }
        }
    }
    if let Some(k) = get("keys") { s += &format!("keys_dir = {}\n", lit(&k)); }
    let path = inst.join("config.toml");
    std::fs::write(&path, s)?;
    Ok(path)
}

/// `python -c BOOT <code folder> <module> <args>`: runs <module> as `python -m` would, from that folder.
const BOOT: &str = "import runpy, sys; sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1]); m = sys.argv[2]; sys.argv = [m] + sys.argv[3:]; \
                    runpy.run_module(m, run_name='__main__', alter_sys=True)";

/// One run of the game code's Python (`python -m <module> <args>`), its lines to the screen; Err on failure or
/// Cancel. The build's own lines (decision 0054): `@steps <json>` the list of steps (the launcher adds its DLC
/// copy at the end), `@step <id> <state>` each step starting and ending, `@progress` the bar.
fn python(app: &AppHandle, run: &Running, b: &Builder, cfg: &Path, module: &str, args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    if run.cancel.load(Ordering::SeqCst) { return Err("cancelled".into()); }
    // The game code's folder goes first on Python's path (tools/yw4/build_install.py BOOT does the same for each
    // step it starts): the bundled Python's ._pth file names no code folder, and a game update lives in its own.
    let mut cmd = crate::platform::command(&b.python);
    cmd.arg("-u").arg("-c").arg(BOOT).arg(&b.src).arg(module).args(args).current_dir(&b.src)
        .env("YW4_CONFIG", cfg).env("YW4_PROGRESS", "1").env("PYTHONIOENCODING", "utf-8")
        .stdout(Stdio::piped()).stderr(Stdio::piped());
    platform::own_group(&mut cmd);  // Cancel ends the step and everything it started
    if b.tools.is_some() {
        // A player's own CC would override the compiler we tested. Python's caches go in the build folder: the
        // launcher's folder stays as installed, so uninstalling leaves nothing.
        cmd.env_remove("CC").env("PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX", cfg.with_file_name("work").join("pycache"));
        // Linux: the download's SDL3, used only where the system has none (tools/yw4/system.py, decision 0071)
        if let Some(sdl) = b.tools.as_ref().and_then(|t| t.parent()).map(|d| d.join("sdl3")).filter(|d| d.is_dir()) {
            cmd.env("YW4_SDL3_DIR", sdl);
        }
    }
    platform::hidden(&mut cmd);
    emit_log(app, &format!("> python -m {module} {}", args.join(" ")));
    let mut child = cmd.spawn().map_err(|e| format!("couldn't start Python ({e})"))?;
    let out = child.stdout.take().unwrap();
    let err = child.stderr.take().unwrap();
    *run.child.lock().unwrap() = Some(child);
    let app2 = app.clone();
    let err_thread = std::thread::spawn(move || {  // stderr: the log, and the last lines for an error message
        let mut tail = Vec::new();
        for l in BufReader::new(err).lines().map_while(Result::ok) {
            emit_log(&app2, &l);
            tail.push(l);
            if tail.len() > 8 { tail.remove(0); }
        }
        tail.join("\n")
    });
    for line in BufReader::new(out).lines().map_while(Result::ok) {
        if let Some(rest) = line.strip_prefix("@steps ") {
            if let Ok(mut list) = serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(rest) {
                if let Some(a) = list.as_array_mut() {
                    a.push(serde_json::json!({ "id": "dlc", "label": "Copying DLC", "seconds": 1, "parts": {} }));
                }
                let _ = app.emit("build-steps", list);
            }
            continue;
        }
        if let Some((id, state)) = line.strip_prefix("@step ").and_then(|r| r.split_once(' ')) {
            let _ = app.emit("build-step", StepEvent { id: id.into(), state: state.into() });
            continue;
        }
        if let Some(rest) = line.strip_prefix("@progress ") {
            let mut it = rest.splitn(4, ' ');
            let (step, done, total, what) = (it.next(), it.next(), it.next(), it.next().unwrap_or(""));
            if let (Some(step), Some(Ok(done)), Some(Ok(total))) = (step, done.map(str::parse), total.map(str::parse)) {
                let _ = app.emit("build-progress", ProgressEvent { step: step.into(), done, total, what: what.into() });
                continue;
            }
        }
        emit_log(app, &line);
    }
    let tail = err_thread.join().unwrap_or_default();
    let status = run.child.lock().unwrap().take().map(|mut c| c.wait());
    if run.cancel.load(Ordering::SeqCst) { return Err("cancelled".into()); }
    match status {
        Some(Ok(s)) if s.success() => Ok(()),
        _ => Err(if tail.is_empty() { format!("{module} failed") } else { tail }),
    }
}

/// The checked add-ons, copied into data\dlc (the game checks them again on boot, decision 0049).
fn copy_dlc(app: &AppHandle, plan: &Plan, inst: &Path) -> Result<(), String> {
    let dst = inst.join("data/dlc");
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&dst).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let Some(src) = plan.paths.get("dlc").filter(|d| !d.is_empty()) else { return Ok(()) };
    // The player may have deleted their originals after the first build (the Ready screen offers it): the add-ons
    // already copied into data\dlc are what the game uses, so a missing source folder is fine.
    if !Path::new(src).is_dir() {
        emit_log(app, &format!("DLC folder {src} is gone: keeping the add-ons already in data\\dlc"));
        return Ok(());
    }
    let mut n = 0;
    for p in std::fs::read_dir(src).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?.flatten().map(|e| e.path()) {
        if p.extension().map_or(false, |x| x.eq_ignore_ascii_case("nsp")) && crate::check::dlc_index_of(&p).is_some() {
            let d = dst.join(p.file_name().unwrap());
            if !d.is_file() {
                std::fs::copy(&p, &d).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
            }
            n += 1;
        }
    }
    emit_log(app, &format!("{n} add-on(s) copied"));
    Ok(())
}

/// If data\dlc has a recognised add-on whose data\dlc-romfs\<index>\ isn't unpacked yet (added after building, or
/// recognised only since: 2026-11-13, a ticket-less add-on 2 the build had passed over), runs
/// `python -m tools.yw4.extract --dlc-only` so the game can read it (decision 0056). Until then the game leaves such
/// an add-on out (svc_misc.c): opening one that isn't there stopped the game at the mail delivery.
pub fn ensure_dlc_extracted(app: &AppHandle, inst: &Path) {
    let dlc = inst.join("data").join("dlc");
    let romfs = inst.join("data").join("dlc-romfs");
    let needed = std::fs::read_dir(&dlc).into_iter().flatten().flatten().map(|e| e.path()).any(|p| {
        p.extension().map_or(false, |x| x.eq_ignore_ascii_case("nsp"))
            && crate::check::dlc_index_of(&p).map_or(false, |i| !romfs.join(i.to_string()).is_dir())
    });
    let cfg = inst.join("config.toml");
    if !needed || !cfg.is_file() { return; }
    let b = builder(app, inst);
    let mut cmd = crate::platform::command(&b.python);
    cmd.args(["-u", "-c", BOOT]).arg(&b.src).args(["tools.yw4.extract", "--dlc-only"]).current_dir(&b.src)
        .env("YW4_CONFIG", &cfg).env("PYTHONIOENCODING", "utf-8");
    if b.tools.is_some() { cmd.env("PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX", inst.join("work").join("pycache")); }
    platform::hidden(&mut cmd);
    let _ = cmd.status();
}

/// Records keys_dir in the install's config.toml when the player supplies prod.keys later on the DLC tab.
pub fn save_keys_dir(inst: &Path, keys: &Path) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    let path = inst.join("config.toml");
    let text = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap_or_default();
    let mut lines: Vec<String> = text.lines().filter(|l| !l.trim_start().starts_with("keys_dir")).map(String::from).collect();
    lines.push(format!("keys_dir = {}", lit(keys)));
    std::fs::write(&path, lines.join("\n") + "\n")
}

/// The whole build: the game code's own steps (tools.yw4.build_install, decision 0054), then the DLC copy. The
/// launcher knows no step of the game's; a game update can change them.
fn run_all(app: &AppHandle, run: &Running, plan: &Plan) -> Result<(), String> {
    let inst = PathBuf::from(&plan.install);
    for d in ["data", "work", "mods", "screenshots", "logs"] {
        std::fs::create_dir_all(inst.join(d)).map_err(|e| format!("can't create {}: {e}", inst.join(d).display()))?;
    }
    if let Ok(mut f) = BUILD_LOG.lock() { *f = std::fs::File::create(inst.join("logs").join("build_last.log")).ok(); }
    emit_log(app, &format!("YW4 Recomp Launcher {}", crate::update::LAUNCHER.trim()));
    let b = builder(app, &inst);
    let icon_src = b.src.join("work").join("icon");
    let icon_dst = inst.join("work").join("icon");
    if icon_src.is_dir() && !icon_dst.is_dir() {
        let _ = std::fs::create_dir_all(&icon_dst);
        for name in ["icon.jpg", "yw4.ico", "icon.png"] {
            if icon_src.join(name).is_file() {
                let _ = std::fs::copy(icon_src.join(name), icon_dst.join(name));
            }
        }
    }
    emit_log(app, &format!("game code: {}", b.src.display()));
    let cfg = write_config(&b, plan, &inst).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let mut args: Vec<String> = vec!["--mode".into(), plan.mode.clone(), "--saves".into(), plan.saves.clone()];
    if plan.mode == "folders" {
        let get = |k: &str| plan.paths.get(k).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
        args.extend(["--exefs".into(), get("exefs"), "--romfs".into(), get("romfs")]);
    }
    if b.tools.is_some() && cfg!(windows) {  // a download: the compiler comes on the first build; from the repo the
                                             // repo's own, on Linux the system's
        args.extend(["--toolchain".into(), inst.join("builder").join("toolchain").to_string_lossy().into_owned()]);
    }
    if plan.fresh {
        if code_protocol(&b) >= 2 {
            args.push("--fresh-files".into());
        } else {
            emit_log(app, "fresh files aren't supported by that game code");
        }
    }
    if !plan.fsr { args.push("--no-fsr".into()); }
    if !plan.dlss { args.push("--no-dlss".into()); }
    if let Err(e) = python(app, run, &b, &cfg, "tools.yw4.build_install", &args) {
        if run.cancel.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
            // Cancel ended the build's processes at once, so it couldn't put back the game it had set aside
            run.cancel.store(false, Ordering::SeqCst);
            let _ = python(app, run, &b, &cfg, "tools.yw4.build_install", &["--recover".into()]);
            run.cancel.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
        }
        return Err(e);
    }
    let _ = app.emit("build-step", StepEvent { id: "dlc".into(), state: "start".into() });
    let r = copy_dlc(app, plan, &inst).and_then(|()| python(app, run, &b, &cfg, "tools.yw4.extract", &["--dlc-only".into()]));
    let _ = app.emit("build-step", StepEvent { id: "dlc".into(), state: if r.is_ok() { "done" } else { "failed" }.into() });
    if r.is_ok() && b.tools.is_some() {
        crate::update::drop_other_game_code(&inst, &b.src);  // older downloaded game code isn't needed any more
    }
    r
}

#[tauri::command]
pub fn start_build(app: AppHandle, plan: Plan) -> Result<(), String> {
    if crate::ready::exe_in_use(&plan.install) {
        return Err("Close the game first, then build again.".into());
    }
    let run = app.state::<Arc<Running>>().inner().clone();
    if run.busy.swap(true, Ordering::SeqCst) {
        return Err("a build is already running".into());
    }
    run.cancel.store(false, Ordering::SeqCst);
    std::thread::spawn(move || {
        let r = run_all(&app, &run, &plan);
        if let Err(e) = &r { emit_log(&app, &format!("the build failed: {e}")); }
        if let Ok(mut f) = BUILD_LOG.lock() { *f = None; }  // closed: the player can open or send it
        run.busy.store(false, Ordering::SeqCst);
        let _ = app.emit("build-done", match r {
            Ok(()) => DoneEvent { ok: true, message: String::new() },
            Err(e) => DoneEvent { ok: false, message: e },
        });
    });
    Ok(())
}

/// Stops the build: the running step and everything it started (translate's worker processes too).
#[tauri::command]
pub fn cancel_build(app: AppHandle) {
    let run = app.state::<Arc<Running>>().inner().clone();
    run.cancel.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
    let pid = run.child.lock().unwrap().as_ref().map(|c| c.id());
    if let Some(pid) = pid {
        platform::kill_tree(pid);
    }
}

```

`launcher/src-tauri/src/check.rs`:

```rs
// Screen 2, Check: the quick checks of the player's files (seconds; nothing is unpacked or changed). The exact
// version check (the SHA-256 of the game code, target.toml [main]) needs the files extracted, so it runs as the first
// step of the build. Formats as in tools/yw4/pfs0.py and xci.py; title IDs and the known DLC from target.toml.

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::fs::File;
use std::io::{Read, Seek, SeekFrom};
use std::path::Path;

/// The repo's target.toml, built in: the one game build this project supports.
const TARGET: &str = include_str!("../../../target.toml");

#[derive(Deserialize)]
pub struct Request {
    mode: String,                   // "files" (NSP/XCI) or "folders" (extracted)
    paths: HashMap<String, String>, // field id -> chosen path
}

#[derive(Serialize)]
pub struct Row {
    label: String,
    state: &'static str, // "ok", "warn" (fine, but note it), "bad" (can't continue)
    detail: String,
}

fn row(label: &str, state: &'static str, detail: impl Into<String>) -> Row {
    Row { label: label.into(), state, detail: detail.into() }
}

struct Target {
    app: u64,
    dlc: HashMap<String, u32>, // sha256 of a content NCA body (past 0xC00) -> add-on index
    romfs_bytes: u64,
}

fn target() -> Target {
    let t: toml::Value = TARGET.parse().expect("target.toml");
    let app = u64::from_str_radix(t["title"]["application_id"].as_str().unwrap_or("0"), 16).unwrap_or(0);
    let mut dlc = HashMap::new();
    if let Some(table) = t.get("dlc").and_then(|d| d.as_table()) {
        for (i, h) in table {
            if let (Ok(i), Some(h)) = (i.parse::<u32>(), h.as_str()) {
                dlc.insert(h.to_lowercase(), i);
            }
        }
    }
    let romfs_bytes = t.get("extracted").and_then(|e| e.get("romfs_bytes")).and_then(|b| b.as_integer()).unwrap_or(0) as u64;
    Target { app, dlc, romfs_bytes }
}

/// One file in an NSP (PFS0) or an XCI's secure partition (HFS0): name, absolute offset, size.
struct Entry {
    name: String,
    offset: u64,
    size: u64,
}

fn read_at(f: &mut File, at: u64, n: usize) -> std::io::Result<Vec<u8>> {
    f.seek(SeekFrom::Start(at))?;
    let mut b = vec![0u8; n];
    f.read_exact(&mut b)?;
    Ok(b)
}

fn u32le(b: &[u8], o: usize) -> u32 { u32::from_le_bytes(b[o..o + 4].try_into().unwrap()) }
fn u64le(b: &[u8], o: usize) -> u64 { u64::from_le_bytes(b[o..o + 8].try_into().unwrap()) }

/// A PFS0 (entry 0x18 bytes) or HFS0 (0x40 bytes) table at `at`.
fn archive(f: &mut File, at: u64, magic: &[u8; 4], entry_size: usize) -> Option<Vec<Entry>> {
    let head = read_at(f, at, 16).ok()?;
    if &head[..4] != magic {
        return None;
    }
    let (count, strtab) = (u32le(&head, 4) as usize, u32le(&head, 8) as usize);
    if count > 4096 || strtab > 1 << 20 {
        return None;
    }
    let table = read_at(f, at + 16, count * entry_size + strtab).ok()?;
    let names = &table[count * entry_size..];
    let data = at + 16 + (count * entry_size + strtab) as u64;
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for i in 0..count {
        let e = &table[i * entry_size..];
        let name_off = u32le(e, 16) as usize;
        let end = names[name_off.min(names.len())..].iter().position(|&c| c == 0).map_or(names.len(), |p| name_off + p);
        let name = String::from_utf8_lossy(&names[name_off.min(end)..end]).into_owned();
        out.push(Entry { name, offset: data + u64le(e, 0), size: u64le(e, 8) });
    }
    Some(out)
}

/// The files of an NSP, or of an XCI's secure partition (a 0x1000-byte key area in front is allowed).
fn contents(path: &Path) -> Result<(Vec<Entry>, bool), String> {
    let mut f = File::open(path).map_err(|e| format!("can't open it ({e})"))?;
    if let Some(e) = archive(&mut f, 0, b"PFS0", 0x18) {
        return Ok((e, false));
    }
    for start in [0u64, 0x1000] {
        if read_at(&mut f, start + 0x100, 4).ok().as_deref() == Some(b"HEAD") {
            let root = u64le(&read_at(&mut f, start + 0x130, 8).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?, 0);
            let parts = archive(&mut f, start + root, b"HFS0", 0x40).ok_or("its partition table is damaged")?;
            let secure = parts.iter().find(|p| p.name == "secure").ok_or("it has no game partition")?;
            return archive(&mut f, secure.offset, b"HFS0", 0x40).map(|e| (e, true)).ok_or("its game partition is damaged".into());
        }
    }
    Err("it isn't an NSP or XCI".into())
}

/// The bytes of one file inside an NSP or XCI (at most `max`), else None.
fn entry_bytes(path: &Path, e: &Entry, max: u64) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    if e.size > max { return None; }
    read_at(&mut File::open(path).ok()?, e.offset, e.size as usize).ok()
}

/// Is this .tik a common ticket, whose title key the build takes from the ticket itself (tools/yw4/extract.py
/// ticket_title_key)? A personalised one needs the key from title.keys.
fn common_ticket(d: &[u8]) -> bool {
    if d.len() < 4 { return false; }
    let (sig, pad) = match u32le(d, 0) {
        0x10000 | 0x10003 => (0x200, 0x3C),
        0x10001 | 0x10004 => (0x100, 0x3C),
        0x10002 | 0x10005 => (0x3C, 0x40),
        _ => return false,
    };
    let body = 4 + sig + pad;
    d.len() >= body + 0x170 && d[body + 0x141] == 0
}

/// The rights IDs of an NSP's tickets that need title.keys: those its own common tickets don't carry the key for.
fn rights_needing_keys(path: &Path, entries: &[Entry]) -> Vec<String> {
    entries.iter().filter(|e| e.name.ends_with(".tik"))
        .filter(|e| !entry_bytes(path, e, 0x1000).is_some_and(|d| common_ticket(&d)))
        .filter_map(|e| Some(e.name.strip_suffix(".tik")?.to_lowercase()))
        .collect()
}

/// Title IDs named by an NSP's metadata XML (<Id>0x...</Id> in its .cnmt.xml), for NSPs without a ticket
/// (2026-11-09: a base game NSP whose NCAs need no title key carried no .tik, and was taken for another game).
fn cnmt_titles(path: &Path, entries: &[Entry]) -> Vec<u64> {
    entries.iter().filter(|e| e.name.ends_with(".cnmt.xml"))
        .filter_map(|e| entry_bytes(path, e, 0x10000))
        .filter_map(|d| {
            let t = String::from_utf8_lossy(&d).to_lowercase();
            let i = t.find("<id>0x")? + 6;
            u64::from_str_radix(t.get(i..i + 16)?, 16).ok()
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Title IDs named by an NSP's tickets (the first 16 hex digits of each .tik's name: its rights ID).
fn ticket_titles(entries: &[Entry]) -> Vec<(u64, String)> {
    entries.iter().filter_map(|e| {
        let rid = e.name.strip_suffix(".tik")?.to_lowercase();
        Some((u64::from_str_radix(rid.get(..16)?, 16).ok()?, rid))
    }).collect()
}

/// The add-on index of one DLC NSP: its content NCA body's SHA-256 looked up in target.toml [dlc].
pub fn dlc_index_of(path: &Path) -> Option<u32> {
    dlc_index(path, &target())
}

/// One file in a DLC folder: its add-on index, or why the game leaves it out (shown on the DLC tab).
pub fn dlc_check(path: &Path) -> Result<u32, &'static str> {
    if path.is_dir() || !path.extension().map_or(false, |x| x.eq_ignore_ascii_case("nsp")) {
        return Err("The game only reads .nsp files");
    }
    let Ok((entries, false)) = contents(path) else { return Err("Can't be read as an NSP file") };
    if let Some(i) = dlc_index(path, &target()) {
        return Ok(i);
    }
    // An add-on's content is at most 222 MiB (the 4++ Upgrade Pack); the game's and update's are GiBs
    if entries.iter().any(|e| e.name.ends_with(".nca") && e.size > 256 << 20) {
        return Err("The game or an update, not an add-on");
    }
    Err("Not a known copy of an add-on of this game")
}

/// This install already has all the game files from its last build: the same test as the build's own
/// (tools/yw4/build_install.py game_files), so what this says is what the build will do.
#[tauri::command]
pub async fn extracted_files(install: String) -> bool {
    tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking(move || {
        let data = Path::new(&install).join("data");
        data.join("exefs").join("main").is_file() && folder_bytes(&data.join("romfs")).0 == target().romfs_bytes
    })
    .await
    .unwrap_or(false)
}

/// An add-on's title ID from its index: the application's + 0x1000 + index (target.toml).
pub fn dlc_title_id(index: u32) -> String {
    format!("{:016X}", target().app + 0x1000 + index as u64)
}

pub fn folder_size(dir: &Path) -> (u64, u64) {
    folder_bytes(dir)
}

fn dlc_index(path: &Path, t: &Target) -> Option<u32> {
    let (entries, _) = contents(path).ok()?;
    let mut f = File::open(path).ok()?;
    // The body past the 0xC00-byte header is hashed (decision 0049): ticket-removal tools rewrite the header and
    // rename the file, so neither the name nor the whole file identifies an add-on.
    const HEADER: u64 = 0xC00;
    for e in entries.iter().filter(|e| {
        e.name.ends_with(".nca") && !e.name.ends_with(".cnmt.nca") && e.size > HEADER && e.size <= 256 << 20
    }) {
        f.seek(SeekFrom::Start(e.offset + HEADER)).ok()?;
        let mut h = Sha256::new();
        std::io::copy(&mut (&mut f).take(e.size - HEADER), &mut h).ok()?;
        let hex: String = h.finalize().iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect();
        if let Some(&i) = t.dlc.get(&hex) {
            return Some(i);
        }
    }
    None
}

fn dlc_row(dir: Option<&String>, has_keys: bool, t: &Target) -> Row {
    let Some(dir) = dir.filter(|d| !d.is_empty()) else {
        return row("DLC", "ok", "None chosen. You can add it later without rebuilding");
    };
    let Ok(list) = std::fs::read_dir(dir) else { return row("DLC", "bad", "Can't open the DLC folder") };
    let mut found = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
    let mut nsps = 0;
    for p in list.flatten().map(|e| e.path()) {
        if p.extension().map_or(false, |x| x.eq_ignore_ascii_case("nsp")) {
            nsps += 1;
            if let Some(i) = dlc_index(&p, t) {
                found.insert(i);
            }
        }
    }
    // NSPs that failed the check: the DLC tab names each with its reason after the build
    let out = if nsps > found.len() { format!(" · {} not recognised (left out)", nsps - found.len()) } else { String::new() };
    match found.len() {
        0 if nsps == 0 => row("DLC", "warn", "No NSP files in that folder"),
        0 => row("DLC", "warn", format!("No known add-ons of this game in that folder{out}")),
        n if found.contains(&100) && !has_keys => row("DLC", "warn",
            format!("{n} of {} add-ons found{out} · Yo-kai Watch 4++ Upgrade needs prod.keys (choose Keys folder or add later)", t.dlc.len())),
        n => row("DLC", "ok", format!("{n} of {} add-ons found and checked{out}", t.dlc.len())),
    }
}

fn keys_row(dir: Option<&String>, rights: &[String]) -> Row {
    let Some(dir) = dir.filter(|d| !d.is_empty()) else { return row("Keys", "bad", "Choose the folder with prod.keys") };
    let dir = Path::new(dir);
    if !dir.join("prod.keys").is_file() {
        return row("Keys", "bad", "No prod.keys in that folder");
    }
    if rights.is_empty() {
        return row("Keys", "ok", "prod.keys found");
    }
    let title_keys = std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("title.keys")).unwrap_or_default().to_lowercase();
    let missing = rights.iter().filter(|r| !title_keys.lines().any(|l| l.trim_start().starts_with(r.as_str()))).count();
    if missing == 0 {
        row("Keys", "ok", "prod.keys and the title keys these files need")
    } else if title_keys.is_empty() {
        row("Keys", "bad", "The NSP files also need title.keys in that folder")
    } else {
        row("Keys", "bad", format!("title.keys lacks {missing} key(s) these files need"))
    }
}

fn check_files(paths: &HashMap<String, String>, t: &Target) -> Vec<Row> {
    let upd_id = t.app | 0x800;
    let mut rows = Vec::new();
    let mut rights = Vec::new();
    let base_path = paths.get("base").filter(|p| !p.is_empty());
    let mut base_is_xci = false;
    match base_path.map(|p| contents(Path::new(p))) {
        None => rows.push(row("Base game", "bad", "Choose the base game")),
        Some(Err(e)) => rows.push(row("Base game", "bad", format!("This file can't be used: {e}"))),
        Some(Ok((entries, xci))) => {
            base_is_xci = xci;
            let titles = ticket_titles(&entries);
            let path = Path::new(base_path.unwrap());
            let named = cnmt_titles(path, &entries);
            if xci {
                rows.push(row("Base game", "ok", "Game card image (XCI)"));
            } else if titles.iter().any(|(id, _)| *id == t.app) || named.contains(&t.app) {
                rows.push(row("Base game", "ok", format!("Yo-kai Watch 4++ · {:016X}", t.app)));
            } else if titles.is_empty() && named.is_empty() {
                rows.push(row("Base game", "warn", "No ticket or metadata to check it by: checked while building"));
            } else {
                rows.push(row("Base game", "bad", "This NSP isn't Yo-kai Watch 4++"));
            }
            rights.extend(rights_needing_keys(path, &entries));
        }
    }
    match paths.get("update").filter(|p| !p.is_empty()).map(|p| contents(Path::new(p))) {
        None if base_is_xci => rows.push(row("Update", "warn", "None chosen: fine if your XCI includes 2.2.0 (checked while building)")),
        None => rows.push(row("Update", "bad", "Choose the 2.2.0 update NSP")),
        Some(Err(e)) => rows.push(row("Update", "bad", format!("This file can't be used: {e}"))),
        Some(Ok((entries, _))) => {
            let titles = ticket_titles(&entries);
            let path = Path::new(paths.get("update").unwrap());
            let named = cnmt_titles(path, &entries);
            if titles.iter().any(|(id, _)| *id == upd_id) || named.contains(&upd_id) {
                rows.push(row("Update", "ok", format!("An update of this game · {upd_id:016X}")));
            } else if titles.is_empty() && named.is_empty() {
                rows.push(row("Update", "warn", "No ticket or metadata to check it by: checked while building"));
            } else {
                rows.push(row("Update", "bad", "This NSP isn't an update of Yo-kai Watch 4++"));
            }
            rights.extend(rights_needing_keys(path, &entries));
        }
    }
    let krow = keys_row(paths.get("keys"), &rights);
    let has_keys = krow.state == "ok";
    rows.push(krow);
    rows.push(dlc_row(paths.get("dlc"), has_keys, t));
    rows
}

fn folder_bytes(dir: &Path) -> (u64, u64) {
    let (mut bytes, mut files) = (0u64, 0u64);
    let mut stack = vec![dir.to_path_buf()];
    while let Some(d) = stack.pop() {
        for e in std::fs::read_dir(&d).into_iter().flatten().flatten() {
            match e.file_type() {
                Ok(t) if t.is_dir() => stack.push(e.path()),
                Ok(_) => { bytes += e.metadata().map(|m| m.len()).unwrap_or(0); files += 1; }
                Err(_) => {}
            }
        }
    }
    (bytes, files)
}

fn check_folders(paths: &HashMap<String, String>, t: &Target) -> Vec<Row> {
    let mut rows = Vec::new();
    match paths.get("exefs").filter(|p| !p.is_empty()).map(Path::new) {
        None => rows.push(row("ExeFS", "bad", "Choose the ExeFS folder")),
        Some(d) if d.join("main").is_file() && d.join("sdk").is_file() => rows.push(row("ExeFS", "ok", "main and sdk found")),
        Some(_) => rows.push(row("ExeFS", "bad", "No main and sdk in that folder")),
    }
    match paths.get("romfs").filter(|p| !p.is_empty()).map(Path::new) {
        None => rows.push(row("RomFS", "bad", "Choose the RomFS folder")),
        Some(d) => {
            let (bytes, files) = folder_bytes(d);
            if files == 0 {
                rows.push(row("RomFS", "bad", "That folder is empty"));
            } else if bytes == t.romfs_bytes {
                rows.push(row("RomFS", "ok", format!("{files} files, the exact size of 2.2.0")));
            } else {
                rows.push(row("RomFS", "bad", format!("{files} files, but not the size of 2.2.0 with the update applied")));
            }
        }
    }
    let mut has_keys = false;
    if let Some(k) = paths.get("keys").filter(|p| !p.is_empty()) {
        let r = keys_row(Some(k), &[]);
        has_keys = r.state == "ok";
        rows.push(r);
    }
    rows.push(dlc_row(paths.get("dlc"), has_keys, t));
    rows
}

/// The quick checks of screen 2. Runs off the window's thread (the RomFS walk and DLC hashes take a moment).
#[tauri::command]
pub async fn check_game(req: Request) -> Vec<Row> {
    tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking(move || {
        let t = target();
        let mut rows = if req.mode == "folders" { check_folders(&req.paths, &t) } else { check_files(&req.paths, &t) };
        rows.push(row("Version", "ok", "Checked exactly while building (the game code's hash)"));
        rows
    })
    .await
    .unwrap_or_default()
}
```

```rs
// YW4 Recomp launcher (decision 0050): the screens are plain HTML/CSS/JS in launcher/ui, shown in Windows' own
// WebView2; this side does what a web page can't (files, processes, starting the game). One command so far.

// No console window behind the launcher in release builds.
#![cfg_attr(not(debug_assertions), windows_subsystem = "windows")]

mod buildrun;
mod check;
mod options;
mod platform;
mod ready;
mod themes;
mod update;

/// The launcher's own number (launcher/VERSION, decisions 0047 and 0054): apart from the game's, so a launcher fix
/// never asks for a rebuild. Shown in the status bar next to the game's.
#[tauri::command]
fn launcher_version() -> String {
    update::LAUNCHER.trim().to_string()
}

/// The project's GitHub page in the player's browser. Only this one address: the screens can't open others.
#[tauri::command]
fn open_project_page() -> Result<(), String> {
    platform::open("https://github.com/ILFforever/YW4Recomp")
}

/// The launcher's links, a fixed set: the project page and its issues (Help, Report a problem) and Settings'
/// Buy me a coffee. Nothing else can be opened.
#[tauri::command]
fn open_link(which: String) -> Result<(), String> {
    let url = match which.as_str() {
        "project" => "https://github.com/ILFforever/YW4Recomp",
        "issues" => "https://github.com/ILFforever/YW4Recomp/issues",
        "coffee" => "https://buymeacoffee.com/ilfforever",
        _ => return Err("unknown link".into()),
    };
    platform::open(url)
}

/// Help: the licence texts that ship with the launcher (builder\licenses, from launcher/package.py), if any.
#[tauri::command]
fn licences_folder(app: tauri::AppHandle, open: bool) -> bool {
    use tauri::Manager;
    let Some(dir) = app.path().resource_dir().ok().map(|d| d.join("builder").join("licenses")).filter(|d| d.is_dir())
        else { return false };
    if open { let _ = platform::open(&dir); }
    true
}

/// For testing and screenshots: YW4_LAUNCHER_SCREEN=<screen> opens straight on that screen, without the
/// welcome popup. None for players.
#[tauri::command]
fn start_screen() -> Option<String> {
    std::env::var("YW4_LAUNCHER_SCREEN").ok().filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
}

/// For tests: YW4_LAUNCHER_PATHS = "mode;id=path;id=path…" fills screen 1 (with YW4_LAUNCHER_SCREEN=check).
#[tauri::command]
fn test_paths() -> Option<String> {
    std::env::var("YW4_LAUNCHER_PATHS").ok().filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
}

/// No Windows error boxes from what the launcher starts ("SDL3.dll was not found" from a broken install's
/// yw4.exe): the error mode is inherited by child processes, and the launcher reports such failures itself.
pub fn quiet_errors() {
    #[cfg(windows)]
    unsafe {
        use windows_sys::Win32::System::Diagnostics::Debug::{SetErrorMode, SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS, SEM_NOOPENFILEERRORBOX};
        SetErrorMode(SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS | SEM_NOOPENFILEERRORBOX);
    }
}

fn main() {
    quiet_errors();
    tauri::Builder::default()
        .plugin(tauri_plugin_dialog::init())  // the file and folder pickers (Browse…)
        .manage(std::sync::Arc::new(buildrun::Running::default()))  // the build in progress (screen 4)
        // The launcher never fills the screen (owner, 2026-11-05). tauri.conf.json makes it a fixed size, maximising off;
        // Windows can still maximise a window itself (Win+Up, dragging it to the top edge): undo that.
        .on_window_event(|window, event| {
            if let tauri::WindowEvent::Resized(size) = event {
                if window.is_maximized().unwrap_or(false) {
                    let _ = window.unmaximize();
                    return;
                }
                // snap layouts and other programs can size it past the cap too: back inside 1600 x 1000
                let scale = window.scale_factor().unwrap_or(1.0);
                let (w, h) = (size.width as f64 / scale, size.height as f64 / scale);
                if w > 1600.5 || h > 1000.5 {
                    let _ = window.set_size(tauri::LogicalSize::new(w.min(1600.0), h.min(1000.0)));
                }
            }
        })
        .invoke_handler(tauri::generate_handler![launcher_version, open_project_page, open_link, licences_folder, start_screen, test_paths, check::check_game, check::extracted_files,
            themes::list_themes, themes::read_theme, options::gpu_names, options::disk_space, buildrun::start_build, buildrun::cancel_build, buildrun::builder_bundled, update::check_updates, update::download_game_update, update::game_news, update::open_release_page,
            update::download_launcher_update, update::run_launcher_update,
            ready::load_state, ready::save_state, ready::install_info, ready::set_dlc_keys, ready::set_mod_enabled, ready::play, ready::open_folder, ready::open_shot,
            ready::free_space, ready::originals, ready::delete_originals, ready::make_shortcuts, ready::move_saves, ready::game_full_screen, ready::set_game_full_screen, ready::game_cheats, ready::set_game_cheat, ready::uninstall_info, ready::uninstall, ready::save_report, ready::open_report_github, ready::show_report,
            ready::locate_installed_game, ready::locate_game])
        .run(tauri::generate_context!())
        .expect("the launcher window could not start");
}
```

```rs
// Screen 3, Options: what the PC has (graphics cards, free space where the game will go).

use serde::Serialize;
use std::path::Path;

/// The graphics cards' names (platform.rs: Windows' Win32_VideoController, Linux's Vulkan devices or lspci).
#[tauri::command]
pub async fn gpu_names() -> Vec<String> {
    tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking(crate::platform::gpu_names).await.unwrap_or_default()
}

#[derive(Serialize)]
pub struct Space {
    free: u64,      // bytes free on the drive the folder would be on
    drive: String,  // e.g. "C:"
}

/// Free space for an install folder that may not exist yet: measured at its nearest existing parent.
#[tauri::command]
pub fn disk_space(path: String) -> Option<Space> {
    let mut p = Path::new(&path);
    while !p.exists() {
        p = p.parent()?;
    }
    let drive = p.components().next().map(|c| c.as_os_str().to_string_lossy().into_owned()).unwrap_or_default();
    crate::platform::free_bytes(p).map(|free| Space { free, drive })
}
```
