```js
// ---- start: a test switch can open a given screen without the popup (YW4_LAUNCHER_SCREEN, for screenshots)
(async () => {
  let screen = null;
  try { screen = invoke ? await invoke('start_screen') : null; } catch (e) { /* none */ }
  if (screen === 'check' || screen === 'build') {
    // tests: paths from YW4_LAUNCHER_PATHS (mode;id=path;...; "install=" sets the install folder), then run that screen
    const spec = (invoke ? await invoke('test_paths') : null) || '';
    const [m, ...pairs] = spec.split(';');
    if (m === 'files' || m === 'folders') mode = m;
    for (const p of pairs) {
      const i = p.indexOf('=');
      if (i <= 0) continue;
      if (p.slice(0, i) === 'install') options.install = p.slice(i + 1);
      else chosen[mode][p.slice(0, i)] = p.slice(i + 1);
    }
    document.querySelectorAll('.mode').forEach((b) => b.setAttribute('aria-checked', String(b.dataset.mode === mode)));
    renderFields();
    if (screen === 'check') { show('check'); runCheck(); return; }
    await loadOptions();  // the graphics card decides DLSS
    show('build');
    startBuild('first');
    return;
  }
  if (screen === 'files-ready') {  // screenshots of the ready state: example paths, nothing real is read
    Object.assign(chosen.files, { base: 'D:\\Switch\\Yo-kai Watch 4++ [BASE].nsp',
      update: 'D:\\Switch\\Yo-kai Watch 4++ 2.2.0 [UPD].nsp', keys: 'D:\\Switch\\keys' });
    renderFields();
    screen = 'files';
  }
  if (screen === 'options') { show('options'); loadOptions(); return; }
  if (screen === 'settings' || screen === 'cheats') {  // screenshots of Settings and Settings › Cheats › Manage
    try { inst = invoke ? await invoke('load_state') : null; } catch (e) { inst = null; }
    if (inst) {
      if (screen === 'cheats') await showCheats();
      else await showSettings();
      return;
    }
  }
  if (screen && screen !== 'ready') { show(screen); return; }
  // a built install: straight to Play (the welcome popup is for the first run)
  try { inst = invoke ? await invoke('load_state') : null; } catch (e) { inst = null; }
  syncSettingsButton();
  if (inst) { showReady(); return; }
  show('home');
  let hidden = false;
  try { hidden = localStorage.getItem(HIDE) === '1'; } catch (e) { /* storage unavailable: show it */ }
  if (!hidden) welcome.showModal();
})();
```

`launcher/ui/themes.js`:

```js
// Launcher themes: the look only. A theme is a CSS file of colour tokens (the :root values at the top of style.css)
// in the themes folder next to the launcher. The Rust side lists the folder and reads a chosen file (themes.rs), so a
// new or edited file shows up without a rebuild. 'recomp' is the built-in look and has no file.
// The Look control is a dropdown: each theme shows two dots from its own palette. The choice is kept on this PC.
const themeInvoke = window.__TAURI__ ? window.__TAURI__.core.invoke : null;
// dots: the gold and the deep colour, for the swatches (the built-in look's values from style.css)
let THEMES = [{ id: 'recomp', name: 'YW4 Recomp', dots: ['oklch(80% 0.12 85)', 'oklch(27% 0.09 295)'] }];
const THEME_KEY = 'yw4-launcher-theme';
let themeAt = 0;

// A theme's two swatch colours, read from its file: --gold and --violet-deep (a theme without them shows grey).
function dotsOf(css) {
  const pick = (name) => (css.match(new RegExp(`${name}:\\s*([^;]+);`)) || [])[1] || '#999';
  return [pick('--gold'), pick('--violet-deep')];
}

async function refreshThemes() {
  if (!themeInvoke) return;
  try {
    const list = await themeInvoke('list_themes');
    if (!Array.isArray(list) || !list.length) return;
    for (const t of list) {
      if (t.id === 'recomp') t.dots = THEMES[0].dots;
      else {
        try { t.dots = dotsOf(await themeInvoke('read_theme', { id: t.id })); } catch (e) { t.dots = ['#999', '#999']; }
      }
    }
    THEMES = list;
  } catch (e) { /* keep the built-in one */ }
}

function savedThemeId() {
  try { return localStorage.getItem(THEME_KEY); } catch (e) { return null; }  // no storage: the built-in look
}

function dotsInto(el, dots) {
  el.textContent = '';
  for (const c of dots) {
    const s = document.createElement('span');
    s.style.background = c;
    el.append(s);
  }
}

// Shows theme i: its CSS is read now, applied as the page's style sheet, and kept. Names it on the button.
async function applyTheme(i) {
  themeAt = ((i % THEMES.length) + THEMES.length) % THEMES.length;
  const t = THEMES[themeAt];
  let css = '';
  if (t.id !== 'recomp' && themeInvoke) {
    try { css = await themeInvoke('read_theme', { id: t.id }); } catch (e) { css = ''; }
  }
  const style = document.getElementById('theme-css');
  if (style) style.textContent = css;
  try { localStorage.setItem(THEME_KEY, t.id); } catch (e) { /* not kept */ }
  const name = document.getElementById('set-look-name');
  if (name) name.textContent = t.name;
  const dots = document.getElementById('look-dots');
  if (dots) dotsInto(dots, t.dots);
}

// ---- the dropdown
const lookBtn = document.getElementById('look-btn');
const lookMenu = document.getElementById('look-menu');

function renderMenu() {
  lookMenu.textContent = '';
  THEMES.forEach((t, i) => {
    const item = document.createElement('button');
    item.type = 'button';
    item.className = 'look-item';
    item.setAttribute('role', 'option');
    item.setAttribute('aria-selected', String(i === themeAt));
    const dots = document.createElement('span');
    dots.className = 'look-dots';
    dotsInto(dots, t.dots);
    const name = document.createElement('span');
    name.className = 'look-item-name';
    name.textContent = t.name;
    item.append(dots, name);
    item.addEventListener('click', async () => { closeMenu(); await applyTheme(i); lookBtn.focus(); });
    lookMenu.append(item);
  });
}

async function openMenu() {
  await refreshThemes();  // a file added or changed since the last time shows now
  themeAt = Math.max(0, THEMES.findIndex((t) => t.id === (THEMES[themeAt] || {}).id));
  renderMenu();
  lookMenu.hidden = false;
  lookBtn.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
  lookMenu.querySelector('[aria-selected="true"]')?.focus();
}

function closeMenu() {
  lookMenu.hidden = true;
  lookBtn.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
}

lookBtn.addEventListener('click', () => (lookMenu.hidden ? openMenu() : closeMenu()));
document.addEventListener('pointerdown', (e) => {
  if (!lookMenu.hidden && !e.target.closest('.look')) closeMenu();
});
document.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
  if (e.key === 'Escape' && !lookMenu.hidden) { closeMenu(); lookBtn.focus(); }
});

(async () => {
  await refreshThemes();
  const i = THEMES.findIndex((t) => t.id === savedThemeId());
  await applyTheme(i < 0 ? 0 : i);
})();

```

`recomp/README.md`:

```md
# recomp/

The AArch64 → C recompiler (Python, see `docs/decisions/0006`). Its output is derived from game code and goes to `work/`, never into the repo.

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `lift.py` | Single-instruction translation: one `Form` per encoding layout, emitting C that works on a `CPUState` (`runtime/include/yw4cpu.h`) |
| `function.py` | Whole-function translation: finds function bodies by following control flow, branches, calls, jump tables, PC-relative values (`docs/decisions/0007`) |
| `translate.py` | Translates `main` and the `sdk` into `work/recomp/` (both version-locked), resolving symbols between them (decision 0014) |
| `overrides.toml` | Functions whose body is replaced by a call to native runtime code, by symbol, each with a reason (decision 0016) |
| `build.py` | Compiles `work/recomp/` + `runtime/src/` into `work/build/yw4.exe` (incremental, parallel); `--run` starts it on `main.bin` |
| `functest.py` | Whole-function tests: code from `tests/functest/` compiled and run on the Pi vs. its translation on the host |
| `golden.py` | Makes test cases per form and runs them on the ARM64 reference machine (`pi/`) to get golden results |
| `check.py` | Compiles the lifted C for every test case on the host and compares against the golden results |
| `coverage.py` | How much of `main` the lifter handles, and what to implement next |
| `pi/` | Runs test instructions (`harness.c`) and test functions (`funcrun.c`) natively on ARM64 Linux; `testcase.h` is shared with the host checkers |

Workflow when adding or changing a form:

```
python -m recomp.golden <form>     # needs [tools] pi_host / pi_key
python -m recomp.check <form>      # must print "all forms match" (no Pi needed; also try --ubsan)
python -m recomp.coverage          # see what's still missing
```

After changing control flow or function translation:

```
python -m recomp.functest          # must print "all functions match"
python -m recomp.translate         # main + sdk -> work/recomp/ (prints what is untranslated)
python -m recomp.build --run       # build yw4.exe and run it (stops at the first unimplemented SVC)
```

```

`recomp/__init__.py`:

```py
"""ARM64 -> C static recompiler for YW4 (see docs/decisions/0006)."""

```

`recomp/build.py`:

```py
"""Build the recompiled game: work/recomp/*.c + runtime/src/*.c + musl's math -> work/build/yw4.exe.

    python -m recomp.build           compile what changed, link
    python -m recomp.build --run     ... then run it on work/exefs/ (main.bin, sdk.bin)

Uses [tools] cc (Clang recommended, decision 0007) with -O2. Objects go to
work/build/obj/; a source is recompiled when it, or any header, is newer than its object.
The executable is built from the game's code, so it stays in work/ (never commit or share).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import concurrent.futures
import hashlib
import json
import os
import platform
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import tomllib
from pathlib import Path

import shutil

from tools.yw4 import config, deps, progress
from tools.yw4 import fsr_linux as fsr_linux_build

from . import check

RUNTIME = check.REPO / "runtime"
CFLAGS = ["-std=c11", "-O2", "-ffp-contract=off", "-Wall", "-Wno-unused-label"]
# The runtime's few C++ files (NVIDIA Streamline's headers are C++): no exceptions or RTTI, so no C++ runtime library
CXXFLAGS = ["-std=c++17", "-O2", "-ffp-contract=off", "-Wall", "-fno-exceptions", "-fno-rtti"]
if sys.platform != "win32":
    # glibc under -std=c11 hides what is POSIX and not ISO C (localtime_r, realpath, setenv, fseeko, off_t, S_IFDIR,
    # ftruncate, strnlen...): 13 runtime files failed on Linux without this (2026-11-12). MinGW shows them anyway.
    CFLAGS.append("-D_GNU_SOURCE")
target_flags = check.target_flags  # the host CPU (decision 0034); musl keeps its verified flags

# musl 1.1.19's math (third_party/musl, decision 0013). These are the flags its results were
# verified with against the sdk (tools/yw4/sdkref.py --check uses this same list): no FMA
# contraction, no builtins (the host must not constant-fold with its own libm).
MUSL = check.REPO / "third_party" / "musl"
MUSL_CFLAGS = ["-std=c99", "-O2", "-ffp-contract=off", "-fno-builtin", "-frounding-math",
               "-include", str(MUSL / "yw4" / "glue.h"), f"-I{MUSL / 'yw4'}", f"-I{MUSL / 'src' / 'internal'}"]


def musl_sources() -> list[Path]:
    return sorted((MUSL / "src" / "math").glob("*.c"))


def sources(cfg: config.Config) -> list[Path]:
    gen = cfg.work_dir / "recomp"
    return (sorted(gen.glob("*.c")) + sorted((RUNTIME / "src").glob("*.c")) + sorted((RUNTIME / "src").glob("*.cpp"))
            + musl_sources())


def version_source(cfg: config.Config) -> Path:
    """<work_dir>/build/version.c: which build this is (decision 0047), rewritten only when it changes so a
    build of the same commit relinks nothing new. The number is the repo's VERSION file; the commit is git's
    (+dirty with uncommitted changes to tracked files), else a COMMIT file (a release download has no git),
    else "unknown"."""
    repo = check.REPO
    version = (repo / "VERSION").read_text().strip()
    commit = "unknown"
    try:
        run = lambda *a: subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), *a], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
        commit = run("rev-parse", "--short=7", "HEAD").strip()
        if run("status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=no").strip():
            commit += "+dirty"
    except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
        if (repo / "COMMIT").is_file():
            commit = (repo / "COMMIT").read_text().strip() or "unknown"
    day = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d", time.gmtime())
    text = ("/* Generated by recomp.build (decision 0047). */\n"
            f'const char yw4_version[] = "{version}";\n'
            f'const char yw4_git_commit[] = "{commit}";\n'
            f'const char yw4_build_date[] = "{day}";\n')
    src = cfg.work_dir / "build" / "version.c"
    src.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if not src.is_file() or src.read_text() != text:
        src.write_text(text)
    print(f"YW4 Recomp {version} ({commit}, {day})")
    return src


def dlc_source(cfg: config.Config) -> Path:
    """<work_dir>/build/dlc_known.c: target.toml's [dlc] table, the add-ons the game unlocks when it finds their
    content NCA on boot (decision 0049; runtime/src/svc_misc.c). Rewritten only when it changes."""
    table = tomllib.loads((check.REPO / "target.toml").read_text()).get("dlc", {})
    rows = "".join(f'    {{{int(i)}, "{h.lower()}"}},\n' for i, h in sorted(table.items(), key=lambda kv: int(kv[0])))
    rows = rows or '    {0, ""},\n'  # C needs one element
    text = ("/* Generated by recomp.build from target.toml [dlc] (decision 0049). */\n#include <stddef.h>\n"
            f'#include "{(RUNTIME / "src" / "dlc_known.h").as_posix()}"\n'
            "const Yw4DlcKnown yw4_dlc_known[] = {\n" + rows + "};\n"
            f"const size_t yw4_ndlc_known = {len(table)};\n")
    src = cfg.work_dir / "build" / "dlc_known.c"
    src.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if not src.is_file() or src.read_text() != text:
        src.write_text(text)
    return src


def wheel_icons_source(cfg: config.Config) -> Path:
    """<work_dir>/build/wheel_icons.c: the shortcut wheel's icons (decision 0075), game pictures taken from the
    player's own files by tools.yw4.wheel_icons into <work_dir>/wheel/icons.bin (rule 1: never in the repo, as the
    exe's icon, decision 0048). Without that file yw4_wheel_icon returns NULL and the wheel draws arrows. Rewritten
    only when it changes."""
    data = cfg.work_dir / "wheel" / "icons.bin"
    head = "/* Generated by recomp.build (decision 0075). */\n#include <stddef.h>\n#include <stdint.h>\n"
    body = "const uint8_t *yw4_wheel_icon(int slot, int *w, int *h) { (void)slot, (void)w, (void)h; return NULL; }\n"
    if data.is_file():
        raw = data.read_bytes()
        icons, off = [], 8
        if raw[:8] == b"YW4WHEEL":
            for _ in range(8):
                w, h = int.from_bytes(raw[off:off + 2], "little"), int.from_bytes(raw[off + 2:off + 4], "little")
                icons.append((w, h, raw[off + 4:off + 4 + w * h * 4]))
                off += 4 + w * h * 4
        if len(icons) == 8 and all(len(px) == w * h * 4 and w and h for w, h, px in icons):
            arrays = "".join(f"static const uint8_t icon{i}[] = {{{','.join(map(str, px))}}};\n"
                             for i, (w, h, px) in enumerate(icons))
            table = ",".join(f"{{icon{i}, {w}, {h}}}" for i, (w, h, px) in enumerate(icons))
            body = (arrays + "static const struct { const uint8_t *px; int w, h; } icons[8] = {" + table + "};\n"
                    "const uint8_t *yw4_wheel_icon(int slot, int *w, int *h) {\n"
                    "    if (slot < 1 || slot > 8) return NULL;\n"
                    "    *w = icons[slot - 1].w, *h = icons[slot - 1].h;\n"
                    "    return icons[slot - 1].px;\n}\n")
        else:
            print(f"wheel icons: {data} is not a wheel icon file; the wheel draws arrows", file=sys.stderr)
    text = head + body
    src = cfg.work_dir / "build" / "wheel_icons.c"
    src.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if not src.is_file() or src.read_text() != text:
        src.write_text(text)
    return src


def newest_header(cfg: config.Config) -> float:
    headers = list((RUNTIME / "include").glob("*.h")) + list((cfg.work_dir / "recomp").glob("*.h"))
    return max(h.stat().st_mtime for h in headers)


# What generated code includes: funcs.h -> yw4rt.h -> yw4cpu.h -> yw4fp.h, and yw4load.h for
# image_info.c only. Other runtime headers changing doesn't rebuild the ~150 generated files.
GENERATED_HEADERS = ("yw4rt.h", "yw4cpu.h", "yw4fp.h")


def generated_header(cfg: config.Config, src: Path) -> float:
    names = GENERATED_HEADERS + (("yw4load.h",) if src.name == "image_info.c" else ())
    headers = [RUNTIME / "include" / n for n in names] + list((cfg.work_dir / "recomp").glob("*.h"))
    return max(h.stat().st_mtime for h in headers)


# How long each file takes to compile, so the slowest start first. Handed out in name order, the few generated files
# that take minutes (main_062, main_069, main_070) started late and ran alone at the end: the Linux tester's build
# spent its last 4-5 of 7 minutes on them with the other cores idle (2026-11-13). A file's cost is its own time from
# the last build here (<objdir>/compile_times.json), else the time measured on the owner's PC that ships with the
# code (recomp/compile_cost.json: generated files' names and seconds only, measured at translate.py's CHUNK), else
# a guess from its size.
COST_TABLE = Path(__file__).with_name("compile_cost.json")


def load_times(path: Path) -> dict[str, float]:
    try:
        return {k: float(v) for k, v in json.loads(path.read_text()).items()}
    except (OSError, ValueError, AttributeError):
        return {}


def compile_one(cc: str, src: Path, obj: Path, includes: list[str]) -> str | None:
    flags = (MUSL_CFLAGS if MUSL in src.parents else
             [*(CXXFLAGS if src.suffix == ".cpp" else CFLAGS), *target_flags(), *includes])
    proc = subprocess.run([cc, *flags, "-c", str(src), "-o", str(obj)], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        return f"{src.name}:\n{proc.stderr[-2000:]}"
    if proc.stderr.strip():
        print(proc.stderr[-1000:], file=sys.stderr)
    return None


def native_shaders(cfg: config.Config) -> bool:
    """Our own renderer's shaders (runtime/shaders/*.vert, *.frag, *.comp; decision 0024) to SPIR-V in
    work/build/shaders/, where the runtime reads them. Without glslang only a warning: the
    native passes then stay off."""
    from . import shader
    out = cfg.work_dir / "build" / "shaders"
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    exe = shader.glslang(cfg)
    srcs = sorted([*(RUNTIME / "shaders").glob("*.vert"), *(RUNTIME / "shaders").glob("*.frag"),
                   *(RUNTIME / "shaders").glob("*.comp")])
    # shared code the programs #include (*.glsl): a change rebuilds them all
    newest_include = max((p.stat().st_mtime for p in (RUNTIME / "shaders").glob("*.glsl")), default=0)
    for src in srcs:
        spv = out / (src.name + ".spv")
        if spv.exists() and spv.stat().st_mtime >= max(src.stat().st_mtime, newest_include):
            continue
        if not exe:
            print(f"warning: no glslang ([tools] glslang): {src.name} not compiled", file=sys.stderr)
            continue
        r = subprocess.run([exe, "-V", "--target-env", "vulkan1.3", "-o", str(spv), str(src)],
                           capture_output=True, text=True)
        if r.returncode != 0:
            print(f"{src.name}:\n{r.stdout}{r.stderr}", file=sys.stderr)
            return False
        print(f"compiled {src.name}")
    return True


DEV_INI_HEADER = "# Written by recomp.build from config.local.toml"


def dev_game_ini(cfg: config.Config) -> None:
    """<work_dir>/build/game.ini, so `yw4` with no arguments starts the game from this config's folders (decision
    0050's file): the game files and both DLC folders, which a bare `yw4 <exefs> <romfs>` run doesn't know.
    A launcher install writes its own game.ini after the build (tools/yw4/build_install.py); that one is left alone."""
    ini = cfg.work_dir / "build" / "game.ini"
    if ini.is_file() and not ini.read_text(errors="replace").startswith(DEV_INI_HEADER):
        return
    lines = [f"{DEV_INI_HEADER}; rebuilt on every build. Run yw4 with no arguments to use it.",
             f"YW4_EXEFS={(cfg.work_dir / 'exefs').resolve().as_posix()}",
             f"YW4_ROMFS={cfg.romfs_dir.resolve().as_posix()}"]
    lines += [f"{k}={Path(v).resolve().as_posix()}" for k, v in cfg.dlc_env().items()]
    ini.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--run", action="store_true", help="run the result on work/exefs/")
    ap.add_argument("--jobs", type=int, default=os.cpu_count() or 4)
    ap.add_argument("--no-fsr", action="store_true", help="leave out AMD FSR (decision 0039)")
    ap.add_argument("--no-dlss", action="store_true", help="leave out NVIDIA DLSS and Streamline (decision 0040)")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        cfg = config.load()
    except config.ConfigError as e:
        print(f"config error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    if not (cfg.work_dir / "recomp" / "image_info.c").is_file():
        print("no generated code; run python -m recomp.translate first", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    cc = check.host_cc()
    objdir = cfg.work_dir / "build" / "obj"
    objdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    includes = [f"-I{RUNTIME / 'include'}", f"-I{cfg.work_dir / 'recomp'}"]
    # The window (decision 0019): SDL3 (fetched on Windows, the system's elsewhere), Vulkan headers
    includes.append(f"-I{check.REPO / 'third_party' / 'vulkan' / 'include'}")
    includes.append(f"-I{check.REPO / 'third_party' / 'stb'}")  # stb_truetype: the HUD's font (hud.c)
    feature_defs: list[str] = []
    if sys.platform == "win32":
        sdl = deps.fetch_sdl(cfg)
        includes.append(f"-I{sdl / 'include'}")
        sdl_libs = [str(sdl / "lib" / "libSDL3.dll.a")]
        # AMD FSR (decision 0039): headers to compile gpu_fsr.c against, DLLs copied next to yw4.exe below
        if not args.no_fsr:
            fsr = deps.fetch_fsr(cfg) / "Kits" / "FidelityFX"
            includes.append(f"-I{fsr / 'api' / 'include'}")
            feature_defs.append("-DYW4_FSR=1")
        # NVIDIA DLSS (decision 0040): headers, the static NGX library (made for MSVC: runtime/src/msvc_shim.c
        # supplies the few runtime pieces it needs, empty stand-ins satisfy its default-library requests), the DLL
        if not args.no_dlss:
            dlss = deps.fetch_dlss(cfg)
            includes.append(f"-I{dlss / 'include'}")
            feature_defs.append("-DYW4_DLSS=1")
            stub = dlss / "stub"
            if not (stub / "libmsvcprt.a").is_file():
                stub.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
                ar = Path(cc).with_name("llvm-ar.exe")
                for name in ("msvcprt", "OLDNAMES"):
                    subprocess.run([str(ar), "rc", str(stub / f"lib{name}.a")], check=True)
            sdl_libs += [str(dlss / "lib" / "Windows_x86_64" / "x64" / "nvsdk_ngx_d.lib"), f"-L{stub}"]
            # NVIDIA Streamline (DLSS frame generation and Reflex): headers; its DLLs are loaded at run time, copied below
            sl = deps.fetch_streamline(cfg)
            includes.append(f"-I{sl / 'include'}")
            feature_defs.append("-DYW4_STREAMLINE=1")
    else:
        try:
            pc = lambda *a: subprocess.run(["pkg-config", *a, "sdl3"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.split()
            includes += pc("--cflags")
            sdl_libs = pc("--libs")
        except (subprocess.CalledProcessError, FileNotFoundError):
            print("error: SDL3 not found via pkg-config (install sdl3 / libsdl3-dev)", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        # NVIDIA DLSS upscaling on Linux (decision 0073): NVIDIA's static NGX library (built with GCC: C++ runtime and
        # dlopen) and its DLSS library, copied next to yw4 below. No frame generation or Reflex: Streamline is Windows only
        if not args.no_dlss and platform.machine() in ("x86_64", "AMD64"):
            dlss = deps.fetch_dlss(cfg)
            includes.append(f"-I{dlss / 'include'}")
            feature_defs.append("-DYW4_DLSS=1")
            sdl_libs += [str(dlss / "lib" / "Linux_x86_64" / "libnvsdk_ngx.a"), "-lstdc++", "-ldl"]
        # AMD FSR upscaling on Linux (decision 0073): built from AMD's SDK v1.1.4 source (tools/yw4/fsr_linux.py), its
        # headers here, libamd_fidelityfx_vk.so copied next to yw4 below and opened at run time (dlopen)
        if not args.no_fsr and platform.machine() in ("x86_64", "AMD64"):
            try:
                fsr_linux = fsr_linux_build.fetch_fsr_linux(cfg)
            except (RuntimeError, OSError) as e:  # an optional extra: the game builds without it (TAA in its place)
                print(f"fsr: could not build AMD FSR for Linux, the game is built without it:\n{e}", file=sys.stderr)
            else:
                includes.append(f"-I{fsr_linux / 'include' / 'ffx_api'}")
                feature_defs.append("-DYW4_FSR=1")
                sdl_libs.append("-ldl")
    includes += feature_defs
    hdr = newest_header(cfg)
    # runtime/src/*.h are private to the runtime: changing one doesn't rebuild generated code
    rt_hdr = max([hdr, *(h.stat().st_mtime for h in (RUNTIME / "src").glob("*.h"))])
    musl_hdr = max(h.stat().st_mtime for h in MUSL.rglob("*.h"))
    # other compiler flags than the objects were built with (another YW4_MARCH): everything but musl again
    stamp = objdir / "flags.txt"
    flags_now = " ".join([*CFLAGS, *target_flags()])
    stale_flags = not stamp.exists() or stamp.read_text().strip() != flags_now
    # another set of --no-fsr / --no-dlss: only the runtime's own files read those defines
    feature_stamp = objdir / "features.txt"
    features_now = " ".join(feature_defs)
    stale_features = not feature_stamp.exists() or feature_stamp.read_text().strip() != features_now
    # the runtime's sources by content, not only their times: objects newer than the sources yet built from other ones
    # (another copy of the code, an update unpacked with older file times) were linked as they were, half old, half
    # new (2026-11-11, 0.9.3: "undefined symbol: yw4_read_watch_arm" after "compiling 0 of 285 files")
    source_stamp = objdir / "runtime_sources.txt"
    digest = hashlib.sha1()
    for f in sorted([*(RUNTIME / "src").iterdir(), *(RUNTIME / "include").glob("*.h")]):
        if f.is_file():
            digest.update(f.name.encode() + b"\0" + f.read_bytes())
    sources_now = digest.hexdigest()
    stale_features = stale_features or not source_stamp.exists() or source_stamp.read_text().strip() != sources_now
    todo, objs = [], []
    for src in sources(cfg):
        rt = src.parent == RUNTIME / "src"
        musl = MUSL in src.parents
        obj = objdir / (("rt_" if rt else "musl_" if musl else "") + src.stem + ".o")
        objs.append(obj)
        dep = musl_hdr if musl else rt_hdr if rt else generated_header(cfg, src)
        if not obj.exists() or obj.stat().st_mtime < max(src.stat().st_mtime, dep) or (stale_flags and not musl) or (stale_features and rt):
            todo.append((src, obj))
    # small generated files, each its own object: a new commit or DLC table recompiles only them
    for gsrc in (version_source(cfg), dlc_source(cfg), wheel_icons_source(cfg)):
        gobj = objdir / (gsrc.stem + ".o")
        objs.append(gobj)
        if not gobj.exists() or gobj.stat().st_mtime < gsrc.stat().st_mtime:
            todo.append((gsrc, gobj))
    # The game's icon in the exe (decision 0048): only when tools.yw4.icon made it from the user's own files
    ico = cfg.work_dir / "icon" / "yw4.ico"
    res = objdir / "icon_res.o"
    if sys.platform == "win32" and ico.is_file():
        if not res.exists() or res.stat().st_mtime < ico.stat().st_mtime:
            rc = objdir / "icon.rc"
            rc.write_text(f'1 ICON "{ico.as_posix()}"\n')  # resource 1: Explorer's icon and the window's (window.c)
            r = subprocess.run([str(Path(cc).with_name("llvm-windres.exe")), str(rc), "-O", "coff", "-o", str(res)],
                               capture_output=True, text=True)
            if r.returncode:
                print(f"icon resource failed:\n{r.stderr[-1000:]}", file=sys.stderr)
                return 1
        objs.append(res)
    else:
        res.unlink(missing_ok=True)

    times_file = objdir / "compile_times.json"
    measured = {**load_times(COST_TABLE), **load_times(times_file)}
    todo.sort(key=lambda t: measured.get(t[0].name, t[0].stat().st_size / 1e6 * 8), reverse=True)  # ~8 s per MB
    t0 = time.time()
    print(f"compiling {len(todo)} of {len(objs)} files with {Path(cc).name} ({args.jobs} jobs)")
    errors = []
    # Progress counts source bytes, not files: the few biggest generated files take minutes each, so a file count
    # races to the end and then sits there. One log line per finished file, and while nothing finishes, a line every
    # 15 s naming the files still compiling (so a long wait doesn't look like a hang).
    sizes = {src: src.stat().st_size for src, _ in todo}
    total_bytes = sum(sizes.values()) or 1
    started: dict[Path, float] = {}
    took_s: dict[str, float] = {}

    def compile_timed(src: Path, obj: Path) -> str | None:
        started[src] = time.time()
        r = compile_one(cc, src, obj, includes)
        took_s[src.name] = round(time.time() - started[src], 1)
        return r

    def took(s: float) -> str:
        return f"{s:.0f} s" if s < 90 else f"{s / 60:.0f} min"

    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(args.jobs) as pool:
        futures = {pool.submit(compile_timed, src, obj): src for src, obj in todo}
        pending, done_n, done_bytes, quiet_since = set(futures), 0, 0, time.time()
        while pending:
            finished, pending = concurrent.futures.wait(pending, timeout=15,
                                                        return_when=concurrent.futures.FIRST_COMPLETED)
            now = time.time()
            for fut in finished:
                src = futures[fut]
                done_n += 1
                done_bytes += sizes[src]
                if fut.result():
                    errors.append(fut.result())
                print(f"{src.name} done ({took(now - started.get(src, t0))}) · {done_n} of {len(todo)}", flush=True)
                progress.report("compile", done_bytes, total_bytes, f"{done_n}/{len(todo)}")
                quiet_since = now
            if pending and now - quiet_since >= 15:
                running = sorted(((now - started[futures[f]], futures[f].name) for f in pending if futures[f] in started),
                                 reverse=True)
                print("still compiling: " + ", ".join(f"{n} ({took(s)})" for s, n in running[:6]), flush=True)
                quiet_since = now
    times_file.write_text(json.dumps({**load_times(times_file), **took_s}, indent=0, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
    print(f"compiled in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s", flush=True)
    if errors:
        print("\n".join(errors), file=sys.stderr)
        print(f"{len(errors)} file(s) failed", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    stamp.write_text(flags_now + "\n")
    feature_stamp.write_text(features_now + "\n")
    source_stamp.write_text(sources_now + "\n")
    exe = cfg.work_dir / "build" / ("yw4.exe" if sys.platform == "win32" else "yw4")
    # winmm: timeBeginPeriod; gdi32: the game icon read back for the in-game overlay (gamelogo.c); math on Linux
    libs = [*sdl_libs, "-pthread"] + (["-lwinmm", "-lpsapi", "-lgdi32"] if sys.platform == "win32" else ["-lm"])
    if sys.platform == "win32":
        shutil.copy2(sdl / "bin" / "SDL3.dll", exe.parent / "SDL3.dll")  # found next to yw4.exe
        if not args.no_fsr:
            for dll in deps.FSR_DLLS:  # amd_fidelityfx_loader_vk.dll loads the upscaler from its own folder
                shutil.copy2(fsr / "signedbin" / dll, exe.parent / dll)
        else:
            for dll in deps.FSR_DLLS:
                (exe.parent / dll).unlink(missing_ok=True)
        if not args.no_dlss:
            shutil.copy2(dlss / "lib" / "Windows_x86_64" / "rel" / "nvngx_dlss.dll", exe.parent / "nvngx_dlss.dll")
            for dll in deps.SL_DLLS:  # Streamline finds its plugins next to yw4.exe
                shutil.copy2(sl / "bin" / "x64" / dll, exe.parent / dll)
        else:
            (exe.parent / "nvngx_dlss.dll").unlink(missing_ok=True)
            for dll in deps.SL_DLLS:
                (exe.parent / dll).unlink(missing_ok=True)
    else:
        # Linux: an SDL3 outside the system's folders (the launcher's own builder/sdl3, decision 0071, or one built by
        # hand) goes next to yw4, which finds it there through its run path ($ORIGIN): no LD_LIBRARY_PATH to set
        try:
            libdir = subprocess.run(["pkg-config", "--variable=libdir", "sdl3"], capture_output=True, text=True,
                                    check=True).stdout.strip()
        except (subprocess.CalledProcessError, FileNotFoundError):
            libdir = ""
        so = Path(libdir) / "libSDL3.so.0" if libdir else None
        if so and so.is_file() and not libdir.startswith(("/usr/", "/lib")):
            (exe.parent / "libSDL3.so.0").unlink(missing_ok=True)
            shutil.copy2(so.resolve(), exe.parent / "libSDL3.so.0")
            libs.append("-Wl,-rpath,$ORIGIN")
        # NGX finds the DLSS library in the folder gpu_dlss.c names: yw4's own
        dlss_so = exe.parent / deps.DLSS_SO
        if "-DYW4_DLSS=1" in feature_defs:
            shutil.copy2(deps.dlss_dir(cfg) / "lib" / "Linux_x86_64" / "rel" / deps.DLSS_SO, dlss_so)
        else:
            dlss_so.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        fsr_so = exe.parent / "libamd_fidelityfx_vk.so"
        if "-DYW4_FSR=1" in feature_defs:
            shutil.copy2(fsr_linux_build.out_dir(cfg) / "lib" / fsr_linux_build.LIB, fsr_so)
        else:
            fsr_so.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    progress.report("link", 0, 1)
    print(f"linking {len(objs)} objects into {exe.name}", flush=True)
    t_link = time.time()
    # the ~270 objects go in a response file: in a deep folder (an install path) the command line would pass
    # Windows' 32,767-character limit. Forward slashes and quotes: clang reads it with GNU quoting rules.
    rsp = objdir / "link.rsp"
    rsp.write_text("\n".join(f'"{Path(o).as_posix()}"' for o in objs) + "\n")
    link = subprocess.run([cc, "-o", str(exe), f"@{rsp}", *libs], capture_output=True, text=True)
    progress.report("link", 1, 1)
    if link.returncode != 0:
        print(f"link failed:\n{link.stderr[-3000:]}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print(f"linked {exe.name} ({time.time() - t_link:.0f} s)")
    print(f"built {exe} in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s")
    if not native_shaders(cfg):
        return 1
    dev_game_ini(cfg)
    if args.run:
        save = cfg.work_dir / "save"  # the game's save data (the owner's: never commit)
        save.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        shots = cfg.work_dir / "screenshots"  # F12 / YW4_SCREENSHOTS (images of the game: never commit)
        shots.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        env = {**os.environ, "YW4_SCREENSHOT_DIR": os.environ.get("YW4_SCREENSHOT_DIR", str(shots))}
        for k, v in cfg.dlc_env().items():  # the owner's DLC folder; the game checks each file (decision 0049)
            env.setdefault(k, v)
        return subprocess.run([str(exe), str(cfg.work_dir / "exefs"), str(cfg.romfs_dir), str(save)], env=env).returncode
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

`recomp/check.py`:

```py
"""Check lifted instructions against golden results from real hardware.

    python -m recomp.check                  every form with golden files
    python -m recomp.check addsub_imm       only these forms
    python -m recomp.check --opt=-O0        another optimisation level (default -O2)
    python -m recomp.check --ubsan          trap on undefined behaviour in the lifted C

Golden files live in tests/golden/ (xz-compressed, made by recomp.golden), so
this needs neither the Pi nor the game.

For each form, translates every test encoding with recomp.lift, builds one C
test program with the host compiler (CC, default gcc), feeds it the same input
lines the Pi got, and compares output line by line. Mismatches are printed
with the disassembly-free details needed to debug: encoding, the registers
that differ, expected vs actual.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import lzma
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from . import lift

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
INCLUDE = REPO / "runtime" / "include"
PI_DIR = REPO / "recomp" / "pi"
GOLDEN = REPO / "tests" / "golden"


def target_flags() -> list[str]:
    """The host CPU the game code and runtime are compiled for, and these checks with them (decision
    0034): the 2003 baseline x86-64 (every PC) unless YW4_MARCH names another (x86-64-v3 = AVX2, Intel
    since 2013, AMD since 2015; native = this PC only). v3 alone measured no gain (2026-10-28). Results
    are the same on any of them: -ffp-contract=off keeps every multiply and add separate, and nothing
    reorders floating point."""
    return [f"-march={os.environ.get('YW4_MARCH', 'x86-64')}"]

PROGRAM = r"""
#include "yw4cpu.h"
#include "testcase.h"

static int run(uint32_t enc, CPUState *ctx) {
    switch (enc) {
%s
    default: return 0;
    }
    return 1;
}

int main(void) {
    test_mem_init();
    uint64_t base = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)test_mem;
    TestState t;
    uint32_t enc;
    uint64_t inmask, outmask;
    while (test_read(stdin, &enc, &t, &inmask, &outmask)) {
        test_rebase(&t, inmask, base);
        CPUState s = {0};
        memcpy(s.x, t.x, sizeof t.x);
        s.sp = t.sp;
        s.nzcv = t.nzcv;
        memcpy(s.v, t.v, sizeof t.v);
        s.fpcr = (uint32_t)t.fpcr;
        if (!run(enc, &s)) { printf("%%08" PRIx32 " UNSUPPORTED\n", enc); continue; }
        memcpy(t.x, s.x, sizeof t.x);
        t.sp = s.sp;
        t.nzcv = s.nzcv;
        memcpy(t.v, s.v, sizeof t.v);
        test_rebase(&t, outmask, 0 - base);
        test_write(stdout, enc, &t);
    }
    return 0;
}
"""


# Case lines (pi/testcase.h): field 0 enc, 1-31 x0-x30, 32 sp, 33 nzcv, 34-65 v0-v31, then
# fpcr, inmask, outmask (input) or the memory changes (output).
#
# Stored compactly in tests/golden/: a register the test doesn't care about holds filler(),
# a fixed pseudo-random value per (encoding, field), written as "*"; an output line lists
# only the fields that differ from its input ("k=value,..." or "=" for none).
STATE = range(1, 66)


def filler(enc: int, k: int) -> str:
    v = int.from_bytes(hashlib.blake2b(f"{enc:08x}/{k}".encode(), digest_size=16).digest(), "little")
    return f"{v:032x}" if 34 <= k < 66 else f"{v & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF:x}"


def compact_in(line: str) -> str:
    f = line.split()
    enc = int(f[0], 16)
    return " ".join("*" if k in STATE and f[k] == filler(enc, k) else f[k] for k in range(len(f)))


def expand_in(line: str) -> str:
    f = line.split()
    enc = int(f[0], 16)
    return " ".join(filler(enc, k) if x == "*" else x for k, x in enumerate(f))


def compact_out(inp: str, out: str) -> str:
    i, o = inp.split(), out.split()
    if len(o) != 67:
        return out  # malformed: keep as is
    diff = ",".join(f"{k}={o[k]}" for k in STATE if o[k] != i[k])
    return f"{o[0]} {diff or '='} {o[66]}"


def expand_out(inp: str, line: str) -> str:
    c = line.split()
    if len(c) != 3:
        return line
    o = inp.split()[:66]
    if c[1] != "=":
        for item in c[1].split(","):
            k, v = item.split("=")
            o[int(k)] = v
    o[0] = c[0]
    return " ".join(o + [c[2]])


def read_golden(path: Path) -> list[str]:
    return lzma.decompress(path.read_bytes()).decode().splitlines()


def write_golden(path: Path, lines: list[str]) -> None:
    path.write_bytes(lzma.compress(("\n".join(lines) + "\n").encode(), preset=9))


def load_cases(name: str) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
    """Full (expanded) input and expected output lines of a form."""
    inputs = [expand_in(x) for x in read_golden(GOLDEN / f"{name}.in.xz")]
    expected = [expand_out(i, x) for i, x in zip(inputs, read_golden(GOLDEN / f"{name}.out.xz"))]
    return inputs, expected


def host_cc() -> str:
    """The host C compiler: $CC, else [tools] cc from config.local.toml, else gcc."""
    if os.environ.get("CC"):
        return os.environ["CC"]
    try:
        from tools.yw4 import config
        return config.load().cc or "gcc"
    except Exception:  # no config: the checker still works with gcc
        return "gcc"


def build_program(encodings: list[int], exe: Path, flags: list[str]) -> None:
    """Encodings the lifter rejects are left out; they then print UNSUPPORTED and mismatch."""
    cases = []
    for enc in encodings:
        try:
            cases.append(f"    case 0x{enc:08x}u: {{ {lift.lift(enc)} }} break;")
        except lift.LiftError:
            pass
    src = exe.with_suffix(".c")
    src.write_text(PROGRAM % "\n".join(cases))
    proc = subprocess.run([host_cc(), "-std=c11", *flags, "-ffp-contract=off", "-Wall", "-Werror", f"-I{INCLUDE}", f"-I{PI_DIR}",
                           "-o", str(exe), str(src), str(REPO / "runtime" / "src" / "crypto.c")],
                          capture_output=True, text=True)
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"compile failed:\n{proc.stderr[-3000:]}")


def describe_diff(inp: str, want: str, got: str) -> str:
    i, w, g = inp.split(), want.split(), got.split()
    names = ["enc"] + [f"x{k}" for k in range(31)] + ["sp", "nzcv"] + [f"v{k}" for k in range(32)] + ["mem"]
    diffs = [f"{names[k]}: in={i[k] if k < 66 else '-'} want={w[k]} got={g[k] if k < len(g) else '?'}"
             for k in range(1, len(w)) if k >= len(g) or w[k] != g[k]]
    return f"  {w[0]}  " + "; ".join(diffs)


def check_form(name: str, tmp: Path, flags: list[str]) -> tuple[int, int, list[str]]:
    inputs, expected = load_cases(name)
    encodings = sorted({int(line.split()[0], 16) for line in inputs})
    exe = tmp / f"check_{name}.exe"
    build_program(encodings, exe, flags)
    proc = subprocess.run([str(exe)], input="\n".join(inputs) + "\n", capture_output=True, text=True)
    actual = proc.stdout.splitlines()
    bad = [describe_diff(i, w, a) for i, w, a in zip(inputs, expected, actual) if w != a]
    if len(actual) != len(expected):
        bad.append(f"  output has {len(actual)} lines, expected {len(expected)} "
                   f"(exit code {proc.returncode}: the lifted code may have crashed)")
    return len(inputs), len(bad), bad


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("forms", nargs="*")
    ap.add_argument("--show", type=int, default=8, help="mismatches to print per form")
    ap.add_argument("--opt", default="-O2", help="host compiler optimisation level")
    ap.add_argument("--ubsan", action="store_true", help="trap on undefined behaviour in the lifted C")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    names = args.forms or sorted(p.name[:-len(".in.xz")] for p in GOLDEN.glob("*.in.xz"))
    if not names:
        print(f"no golden files in {GOLDEN}; run python -m recomp.golden first", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    flags = [args.opt, *target_flags()] + (["-fsanitize=undefined", "-fsanitize-undefined-trap-on-error"] if args.ubsan else [])
    failed = 0
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as t:
        for name in names:
            total, nbad, bad = check_form(name, Path(t), flags)
            status = "ok" if nbad == 0 else f"{nbad} MISMATCHES"
            print(f"{name:15} {total:6} cases  {status}")
            for line in bad[:args.show]:
                print(line)
            failed += nbad > 0
    print("all forms match" if not failed else f"{failed} form(s) failed")
    return 1 if failed else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

`recomp/ci.py`:

```py
"""Compile everything that needs no game files: the runtime, musl's math and our own shaders.

    python -m recomp.ci [--work DIR] [--jobs N] [--no-fsr] [--no-dlss]

For GitHub's build check (.github/workflows/build.yml) and for a quick look before a push: does our own code
still compile on this system? It is the compile half of recomp.build with the same flags (taken from there, so
the two can't drift apart), without the game's translated code, so nothing is linked and nothing runs. No
config.local.toml is needed. The compiler is $CC, else [tools] cc when there is a config, else gcc.

What it can't tell: whether the translated game compiles, links or plays. That needs a player's own files, which
are never on GitHub (rule 1).

SDL3's headers: `pkg-config sdl3` off Windows when it finds them, else the pinned Windows package's (headers
only; they are the same on every system). On Windows the AMD FSR, NVIDIA DLSS and Streamline headers are
fetched as recomp.build fetches them, so the files that use them are compiled too.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import concurrent.futures
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace

from tools.yw4 import deps

from . import build, check


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--work", type=Path, help="where downloads and objects go (default: a temporary folder)")
    ap.add_argument("--jobs", type=int, default=os.cpu_count() or 4)
    ap.add_argument("--no-fsr", action="store_true", help="without AMD FSR's headers (Windows)")
    ap.add_argument("--no-dlss", action="store_true", help="without NVIDIA DLSS's and Streamline's headers (Windows)")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        work = (args.work or Path(tmp)).resolve()
        work.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        # what the build's helpers read from a config: only where generated files go, and which glslang
        cfg = SimpleNamespace(work_dir=work, glslang=None)
        cc = check.host_cc()
        includes = [f"-I{build.RUNTIME / 'include'}", f"-I{check.REPO / 'third_party' / 'vulkan' / 'include'}",
                    f"-I{check.REPO / 'third_party' / 'stb'}"]
        sdl: list[str] = []
        if sys.platform != "win32":
            try:
                sdl = subprocess.run(["pkg-config", "--cflags", "sdl3"], capture_output=True, text=True,
                                     check=True).stdout.split()
            except (subprocess.CalledProcessError, FileNotFoundError):
                pass
        includes += sdl or [f"-I{deps.fetch_sdl(cfg) / 'include'}"]
        if sys.platform == "win32":
            if not args.no_fsr:
                includes += [f"-I{deps.fetch_fsr(cfg) / 'Kits' / 'FidelityFX' / 'api' / 'include'}", "-DYW4_FSR=1"]
            if not args.no_dlss:
                includes += [f"-I{deps.fetch_dlss(cfg) / 'include'}", "-DYW4_DLSS=1",
                             f"-I{deps.fetch_streamline(cfg) / 'include'}", "-DYW4_STREAMLINE=1"]
        srcs = (sorted((build.RUNTIME / "src").glob("*.c")) + sorted((build.RUNTIME / "src").glob("*.cpp"))
                + build.musl_sources() + [build.version_source(cfg), build.dlc_source(cfg),
                                          build.wheel_icons_source(cfg)])
        objdir = work / "ci_obj"
        objdir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        version = subprocess.run([cc, "--version"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.splitlines()[:1]
        print(f"compiling {len(srcs)} files with {' '.join(version) or cc} ({args.jobs} jobs)", flush=True)
        t0 = time.time()
        with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(args.jobs) as pool:
            # musl and the runtime both have a log.c: the folder's name keeps their objects apart
            errors = [e for e in pool.map(
                lambda s: build.compile_one(cc, s, objdir / f"{s.parent.name}_{s.stem}.o", includes), srcs) if e]
        if errors:
            print("\n".join(errors), file=sys.stderr)
            print(f"{len(errors)} of {len(srcs)} file(s) failed", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        print(f"{len(srcs)} files compiled in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s")
        from . import shader
        if not shader.glslang(cfg):
            print("no glslang (glslangValidator on PATH): our shaders not compiled")
        elif not build.native_shaders(cfg):
            return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

`recomp/coverage.py`:

```py
"""How much of main's code the lifter can translate.

    python -m recomp.coverage

Walks every 4-byte word in .text (only inside functions from the Ghidra
export, so padding and data islands don't count) and reports:
- instructions handled by a lifter form, per form
- unhandled instructions by top-level ARM64 encoding group, and the most
  common unhandled sub-groups, to decide what to implement next
Counts only, no game data is written.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import collections
import json
import struct
import sys

from tools.yw4 import config, recon

from . import lift


def group(enc: int) -> str:
    """Top-level ARM64 encoding group (Arm ARM C4.1, op0 = bits 28:25)."""
    op0 = (enc >> 25) & 0xF
    if op0 in (0b1000, 0b1001):
        return "data processing (immediate)"
    if op0 in (0b1010, 0b1011):
        return "branches / exceptions / system"
    if op0 & 0b0101 == 0b0100:
        return "loads and stores"
    if op0 & 0b0111 == 0b0101:
        return "data processing (register)"
    if op0 & 0b0111 == 0b0111:
        return "SIMD and floating point"
    return "unallocated / reserved"


def subgroup(enc: int) -> str:
    """Rough finer grouping for the unhandled list (top 10 bits, with a readable hint)."""
    g = group(enc)
    if g == "branches / exceptions / system":
        if enc & 0x7C000000 == 0x14000000:
            return "B / BL"
        if enc & 0xFE000000 == 0xD6000000:
            return "BR / BLR / RET"
        if enc & 0x7E000000 == 0x34000000:
            return "CBZ / CBNZ"
        if enc & 0x7E000000 == 0x36000000:
            return "TBZ / TBNZ"
        if enc & 0xFF000010 == 0x54000000:
            return "B.cond"
        if enc & 0xFFC00000 == 0xD5000000:
            return "system (MRS/MSR/barriers/hints)"
        return "exceptions / other"
    if g == "loads and stores":
        if enc & 0x3B000000 == 0x39000000:
            return "load/store unsigned offset"
        if enc & 0x3A000000 == 0x28000000:
            return "load/store pair"
        if enc & 0x3B200C00 == 0x38200800:
            return "load/store register offset"
        if enc & 0x3B200000 == 0x38000000:
            return "load/store unscaled / pre / post index"
        if enc & 0x3B000000 == 0x18000000:
            return "load literal"
        if enc & 0x3F000000 == 0x08000000:
            return "exclusive / acquire / release"
        return "SIMD load/store and other"
    if g == "data processing (immediate)" and enc & 0x1F000000 == 0x10000000:
        return "ADR / ADRP"
    return g


def main() -> int:
    try:
        cfg = config.load()
        image, mods = recon.load_main(cfg)
    except config.ConfigError as e:
        print(f"config error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    funcs = json.loads((cfg.work_dir / "ghidra" / "main.functions.json").read_text())["functions"]
    text_size = mods["main"]["segments"]["text"]["size"]

    covered: set[int] = set()
    for f in funcs:
        for lo, hi in f.get("ranges", [[f["entry"], f["entry"] + f["size"]]]):
            covered.update(range(lo & ~3, min(hi, text_size), 4))

    handled = collections.Counter()
    groups = collections.Counter()
    unhandled = collections.Counter()
    invalid = 0
    for off in sorted(covered):
        enc = struct.unpack_from("<I", image, off)[0]
        g = group(enc)
        groups[g] += 1
        form = lift.find_form(enc)
        if form and form.valid(enc):
            handled[form.name] += 1
        else:
            if form:
                invalid += 1
            unhandled[subgroup(enc)] += 1

    total = len(covered)
    done = sum(handled.values())
    print(f"instructions in functions: {total:,}")
    print(f"handled by the lifter:     {done:,} ({100 * done / total:.1f}%)")
    print(f"matched a form but invalid: {invalid:,}")
    print("\n== by top-level group")
    for g, n in groups.most_common():
        print(f"{n:10,} {100 * n / total:5.1f}%  {g}")
    print("\n== handled, per form")
    for name, n in handled.most_common():
        print(f"{n:10,}  {name}")
    print("\n== not yet handled")
    for name, n in unhandled.most_common():
        print(f"{n:10,} {100 * n / total:5.1f}%  {name}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

`recomp/functest.py`:

```py
"""Whole-function tests: real compiled ARM64 code vs. its translation (decision 0007).

    python -m recomp.functest               build, run on the Pi, translate, compare
    python -m recomp.functest --cases 200   argument sets per test function (default 40)

The test functions are our own code (tests/functest/). The Pi compiles them as
ARMv8.0 without SIMD and links them into a flat image like main (flat.ld), then
runs every t_* function natively (pi/funcrun.c). The same image is translated by
recomp.function, compiled on the host, and run on the same inputs. Return values
and every changed byte of the scratch buffer must match.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import random
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from tools.yw4 import config

from . import check, function, golden

SRC = check.REPO / "tests" / "functest"
PI_DIR, INCLUDE = check.PI_DIR, check.INCLUDE
DISPATCH = check.REPO / "runtime" / "src" / "dispatch.c"
# What dispatch.c uses from the rest of the runtime (locks, crash reports, watchpoints); the
# test functions never get there, so stand-ins do (single-threaded, no watchpoints).
STUBS = r"""
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
void host_lock(void *l) { (void)l; }
void host_unlock(void *l) { (void)l; }
int host_readable(uint64_t addr, uint64_t size) { (void)addr; (void)size; return 1; }
int yw4_call_stack(const void *ctx, uint64_t *out, int n) { (void)ctx; (void)out; (void)n; return 0; }
void yw4_setjmp_resume(uint64_t target) { (void)target; abort(); }
_Noreturn void yw4_stop(void) { abort(); }
int yw4_write_watch_arm(uint64_t addr, uint64_t size) { (void)addr; (void)size; return -1; }
"""
REMOTE_DIR = "yw4-functest"

CFLAGS = ("-O2 -mcpu=cortex-a57 -mgeneral-regs-only -fno-jump-tables -ffreestanding -fno-builtin "
          "-fno-tree-loop-distribute-patterns -fPIE -fno-stack-protector "
          "-fno-asynchronous-unwind-tables -fno-unwind-tables")
BUILD = f"""set -e
gcc {CFLAGS} -c funcs.c -o funcs.o
gcc -c jumptable.S -o jumptable.o
gcc -c atomics.S -o atomics.o
if readelf -rW funcs.o jumptable.o atomics.o | grep -q -E 'ABS64|GOT|TLS'; then
    echo 'test code needs load-time relocations; the flat image cannot have them' >&2; exit 1
fi
ld -T flat.ld -o funcs.elf funcs.o jumptable.o atomics.o
objcopy -O binary funcs.elf funcs.bin
nm funcs.elf > funcs.sym
gcc -O1 -Wall -o funcrun funcrun.c
"""

DRIVER = r"""
#include "yw4rt.h"
#include "testcase.h"

%(protos)s

%(functions)s

static const FuncEntry funcs[] = {
%(table)s
};
uint64_t yw4_image_base, yw4_sdk_base;

static uint8_t image[1 << 22] __attribute__((aligned(4096)));

const Yw4CodeModule yw4_code[] = {{"test", &yw4_image_base, sizeof image, funcs, %(nfuncs)d}};
const size_t yw4_ncode = 1;
static uint8_t stack[1 << 20] __attribute__((aligned(16)));

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    FILE *img = fopen(argv[1], "rb");
    if (!img) { perror(argv[1]); return 1; }
    fread(image, 1, sizeof image, img);
    fclose(img);
    yw4_image_base = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)image;
    test_mem_init();
    uint64_t mem = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)test_mem;
    char line[512];
    while (fgets(line, sizeof line, stdin)) {
        char *p = line;
        CPUState ctx = {0};
        uint64_t off = strtoull(p, &p, 16);
        for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) ctx.x[i] = strtoull(p, &p, 16);
        uint64_t inmask = strtoull(p, &p, 16);
        for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++)
            if (inmask >> i & 1) ctx.x[i] += mem;
        ctx.sp = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)(stack + sizeof stack);
        yw4_resolve(yw4_image_base + off)(&ctx);
        printf("%%" PRIx64 " %%" PRIx64 " ", off, ctx.x[0]);
        test_write_mem(stdout);
    }
    return 0;
}
"""


def build_on_pi(cfg: config.Config, out: Path) -> None:
    opts = golden.ssh_base(cfg)
    files = [SRC / "funcs.c", SRC / "jumptable.S", SRC / "atomics.S", SRC / "flat.ld", PI_DIR / "funcrun.c", PI_DIR / "testcase.h"]
    subprocess.run(["ssh", *opts, cfg.pi_host, f"mkdir -p {REMOTE_DIR}"], check=True)
    subprocess.run(["scp", "-q", *opts, *map(str, files), f"{cfg.pi_host}:{REMOTE_DIR}/"], check=True)
    subprocess.run(["ssh", *opts, cfg.pi_host, f"cd {REMOTE_DIR} && sh -s"], input=BUILD.encode(), check=True)
    subprocess.run(["scp", "-q", *opts, f"{cfg.pi_host}:{REMOTE_DIR}/funcs.bin",
                    f"{cfg.pi_host}:{REMOTE_DIR}/funcs.sym", str(out)], check=True)


def read_symbols(path: Path) -> dict[str, int]:
    syms = {}
    for line in path.read_text().splitlines():
        parts = line.split()
        if len(parts) == 3:
            syms[parts[2]] = int(parts[0], 16)
    return syms


def make_cases(tests: dict[str, int], count: int, rng: random.Random) -> list[str]:
    lines = []
    for off in tests.values():
        for _ in range(count):
            buf = 0x8000 + 8 * rng.randrange(0x200)
            args = [buf] + [golden.random_value(rng) for _ in range(3)]
            lines.append(" ".join(f"{v:x}" for v in [off, *args, 1]))
    return lines


def translate(image: bytes, syms: dict[str, int]) -> tuple[str, list[int]]:
    code = function.Code(image, syms["__text_end"])
    entries = {v for k, v in syms.items() if code.is_code(v) and not k.startswith("__")}
    for off in range(0, code.text_end, 4):
        f = function.decode_flow(code.word(off), off)
        if f and f.kind == "bl":
            entries.add(f.target)
    funcs = [function.discover(code, e, entries) for e in sorted(entries)]
    problems = [p for fn in funcs for p in fn.problems]
    if problems:
        raise RuntimeError("flow problems: " + "; ".join(problems))
    stats = function.EmitStats()
    src = "\n\n".join(function.emit_function(code, fn, entries, lambda e: f"{e:08x}", stats) for fn in funcs)
    if stats.unimplemented:
        raise RuntimeError(f"untranslated instructions in the test image: {stats.unimplemented}")
    order = sorted(entries)
    return DRIVER % {
        "protos": "\n".join(f"void {function.fname(e)}(CPUState *ctx);" for e in order),
        "functions": src,
        "table": ",\n".join(f"    {{{e:#x}, {function.fname(e)}}}" for e in order),
        "nfuncs": len(order),
    }, sorted(fn.entry for fn in funcs if fn.jump_tables)


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--cases", type=int, default=40)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=1)
    ap.add_argument("--opt", default="-O2", help="host compiler optimisation level")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        cfg = config.load()
    except config.ConfigError as e:
        print(f"config error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    out = cfg.work_dir / "functest"
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    build_on_pi(cfg, out)
    image = (out / "funcs.bin").read_bytes()
    syms = read_symbols(out / "funcs.sym")
    tests = {k: v for k, v in sorted(syms.items()) if k.startswith("t_")}
    cases = make_cases(tests, args.cases, random.Random(args.seed))

    proc = subprocess.run(["ssh", *golden.ssh_base(cfg), cfg.pi_host, f"cd {REMOTE_DIR} && ./funcrun funcs.bin"],
                          input="\n".join(cases) + "\n", capture_output=True, text=True)
    if proc.returncode != 0 or len(proc.stdout.splitlines()) != len(cases):
        print(f"funcrun failed ({proc.returncode}): {proc.stderr.strip()[-500:]}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    expected = proc.stdout.splitlines()

    src, with_tables = translate(image, syms)
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as t:
        c, exe, stubs = Path(t) / "functest.c", Path(t) / "functest.exe", Path(t) / "stubs.c"
        c.write_text(src)
        stubs.write_text(STUBS)
        cc = check.host_cc()
        build = subprocess.run([cc, "-std=c11", args.opt, *check.target_flags(), "-ffp-contract=off", "-Wall",
                                "-Wno-unused-label", f"-I{INCLUDE}", f"-I{PI_DIR}", "-o", str(exe), str(c),
                                str(DISPATCH), str(stubs)],
                               capture_output=True, text=True)
        if build.returncode != 0:
            print(f"host compile failed:\n{build.stderr[-3000:]}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        run = subprocess.run([str(exe), str(out / "funcs.bin")], input="\n".join(cases) + "\n",
                             capture_output=True, text=True)
        actual = run.stdout.splitlines()

    names = {v: k for k, v in tests.items()}
    bad: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for i, want in enumerate(expected):
        got = actual[i] if i < len(actual) else "(no output: the translated code crashed)"
        if got != want:
            off = int(want.split()[0], 16)
            bad.setdefault(names[off], []).append(f"    in:   {cases[i]}\n    want: {want[:200]}\n    got:  {got[:200]}")
    if run.returncode != 0:
        print(f"translated program exited with {run.returncode}: {run.stderr.strip()[-300:]}")
    for name in tests:
        status = f"{len(bad[name])} MISMATCHES" if name in bad else "ok"
        print(f"{name:20} {args.cases:4} cases  {status}")
        for line in bad.get(name, [])[:2]:
            print(line)
    print(f"functions with recognised jump tables: {', '.join(f'{e:#x}' for e in with_tables) or 'none'}")
    print("all functions match" if not bad else f"{len(bad)} function(s) failed")
    return 1 if bad else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

`recomp/function.py`:

```py
"""Translate whole guest functions to C (decision 0007).

A guest function becomes `void f_<offset>(CPUState *ctx)`:

    straight-line code   recomp.lift, one C statement block per instruction
    B / B.cond / CBZ / TBZ inside the function   goto L_<offset>
    branch to another function's entry           tail call (TAILCALL)
    BL                   set x30 to the guest return address, call f_<target>
    BLR                  same, through yw4_resolve(target)
    BR                   jump table -> switch on the target address; otherwise an indirect tail call
    RET                  return
    ADR / ADRP / LDR (literal)   yw4_image_base + a constant offset

Function bodies are found by following control flow from each entry point, not
from Ghidra's sizes (which cut some functions short). Code reachable from two
entries is translated into both functions, which is correct, only bigger.

Offsets are from the start of the image (the same offsets as everywhere else
in the project); the image is loaded at yw4_image_base.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import re
import struct
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from . import lift
from .lift import bits, sign_extend


@dataclass
class Code:
    """A flat guest image: `data` at offset 0, instructions in [0, text_end).

    base: the C variable holding the module's load address (decision 0014: main is
    yw4_image_base, the sdk yw4_sdk_base); prefix: what its function names start with."""
    data: bytes
    text_end: int
    base: str = "yw4_image_base"
    prefix: str = "f_"

    def word(self, off: int) -> int:
        return struct.unpack_from("<I", self.data, off)[0]

    def is_code(self, off: int) -> bool:
        return 0 <= off < self.text_end and off % 4 == 0


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- control flow decode

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Flow:
    kind: str                 # b, cond, bl, blr, br, ret, trap
    target: int | None = None
    cond: str | None = None   # C expression: branch taken (for kind == "cond")
    reg: int | None = None    # BLR/BR/RET register


def decode_flow(enc: int, pc: int) -> Flow | None:
    """Control-flow instructions; None for everything else."""
    if enc & 0x7C000000 == 0x14000000:                       # B, BL
        target = pc + sign_extend(bits(enc, 25, 0), 26) * 4
        return Flow("bl" if enc >> 31 else "b", target)
    if enc & 0xFF000010 == 0x54000000:                       # B.cond
        target = pc + sign_extend(bits(enc, 23, 5), 19) * 4
        return Flow("cond", target, f"cond_holds(ctx->nzcv, {bits(enc, 3, 0)})")
    if enc & 0x7E000000 == 0x34000000:                       # CBZ, CBNZ
        target = pc + sign_extend(bits(enc, 23, 5), 19) * 4
        op = "!=" if bits(enc, 24, 24) else "=="
        return Flow("cond", target, f"{lift.rd_reg(bits(enc, 4, 0), bits(enc, 31, 31))} {op} 0")
    if enc & 0x7E000000 == 0x36000000:                       # TBZ, TBNZ
        target = pc + sign_extend(bits(enc, 18, 5), 14) * 4
        bit = bits(enc, 31, 31) << 5 | bits(enc, 23, 19)
        op = "!=" if bits(enc, 24, 24) else "=="
        return Flow("cond", target, f"((({lift.rd_reg(bits(enc, 4, 0), 1)}) >> {bit}) & 1) {op} 0")
    if enc & 0xFFFFFC1F == 0xD63F0000:
        return Flow("blr", reg=bits(enc, 9, 5))
    if enc & 0xFFFFFC1F == 0xD61F0000:
        return Flow("br", reg=bits(enc, 9, 5))
    if enc & 0xFFFFFC1F == 0xD65F0000:
        return Flow("ret", reg=bits(enc, 9, 5))
    if enc & 0xFFFF0000 == 0 or enc & 0xFFE0001F in (0xD4200000, 0xD4400000):  # UDF, BRK, HLT
        return Flow("trap")
    if enc == 0xE7FFDEFE:  # unallocated in A64; main uses it as a trap word on assert-failure paths
        return Flow("trap")
    return None


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- PC-relative and system

def image_addr(off: int, base: str = "yw4_image_base") -> str:
    return f"({base} + {off:#x}ull)"


def emit_pc_relative(enc: int, pc: int, base: str = "yw4_image_base") -> str | None:
    """ADR, ADRP and integer LDR (literal): the PC is known at translation time."""
    if enc & 0x1F000000 == 0x10000000:                       # ADR, ADRP
        imm = sign_extend(bits(enc, 23, 5) << 2 | bits(enc, 30, 29), 21)
        value = (pc & ~0xFFF) + (imm << 12) if enc >> 31 else pc + imm
        return lift.wr_reg(bits(enc, 4, 0), 1, image_addr(value, base)) or ";"
    if enc & 0x3F000000 == 0x18000000:                       # LDR (literal), integer
        opc, t = bits(enc, 31, 30), bits(enc, 4, 0)
        addr = image_addr(pc + sign_extend(bits(enc, 23, 5), 19) * 4, base)
        if opc == 0:
            return lift.wr_reg(t, 1, f"ld32({addr})") or ";"
        if opc == 1:
            return lift.wr_reg(t, 1, f"ld64({addr})") or ";"
        if opc == 2:
            return lift.wr_reg(t, 1, f"(uint64_t)(int64_t)(int32_t)ld32({addr})") or ";"
        return ";"  # PRFM (literal)
    return None


def emit_system(enc: int) -> str | None:
    if enc & 0xFFFFF01F == 0xD503201F:                       # NOP, YIELD, WFE, ... (hints)
        return ";"
    if enc & 0xFFFFF0FF in (0xD50330BF, 0xD503309F):         # DMB, DSB
        return "__atomic_thread_fence(__ATOMIC_SEQ_CST);"
    if enc & 0xFFFFF0FF == 0xD50330DF:                       # ISB
        return ";"
    if enc & 0xFFFFF0FF == 0xD503305F:                       # CLREX: drop the exclusive reservation
        return "ctx->excl_size = 0;"
    if enc & 0xFFE0001F == 0xD4000001:                       # SVC #imm: the kernel (decision 0014)
        return f"yw4_svc(ctx, {(enc >> 5) & 0xFFFF:#x});"
    sysreg, t = (enc >> 5) & 0xFFFF, enc & 31
    if enc & 0xFFF00000 == 0xD5300000 and sysreg in MRS_REGS:  # MRS Xt, <reg>
        return f"ctx->x[{t}] = {MRS_REGS[sysreg]};" if t != 31 else ";"
    if enc & 0xFFF00000 == 0xD5100000 and sysreg in MSR_REGS:  # MSR <reg>, Xt
        return MSR_REGS[sysreg].format(x="0" if t == 31 else f"ctx->x[{t}]")
    if enc & 0xFFFFFFE0 in CACHE_OPS:                        # DC CVAU/CVAC/CIVAC, IC IVAU: no cache to maintain
        return ";"
    return None


# System registers the sdk reads and writes (op0:op1:CRn:CRm:op2 = encoding bits 20:5)
MRS_REGS = {
    0xDE83: "ctx->tpidrro_el0",          # TPIDRRO_EL0: the thread-local region, set by the kernel
    0xDE82: "ctx->tpidr_el0",            # TPIDR_EL0
    0xDF01: "yw4_cntpct()",              # CNTPCT_EL0: the 19.2 MHz system counter
    0xD801: "0x8444C004ull",             # CTR_EL0 of the Cortex-A57: 64-byte cache lines
    0xDA20: "(uint64_t)ctx->fpcr",       # FPCR
    0xDA21: "(uint64_t)ctx->fpsr",       # FPSR (not modelled: always what was last written)
}
MSR_REGS = {
    0xDE82: "ctx->tpidr_el0 = {x};",
    0xDA20: "yw4_msr_fpcr(ctx, {x});",   # decision 0008: only the default mode is supported
    0xDA21: "ctx->fpsr = (uint32_t){x};",
}
CACHE_OPS = {0xD50B7B20, 0xD50B7A20, 0xD50B7E20, 0xD50B7520}  # DC CVAU, DC CVAC, DC CIVAC, IC IVAU (Rt cleared)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- jump tables

def written_regs(code: Code, off: int) -> set[int]:
    """X registers an instruction may write. Over-approximates: a wrong "yes" only makes
    the jump-table search give up."""
    enc = code.word(off)
    f = decode_flow(enc, off)
    if f:
        return set(range(19)) | {30} if f.kind in ("bl", "blr") else set()  # calls clobber x0-x18, x30
    form = lift.find_form(enc)
    if form and form.mem:
        a = form.mem(enc)
        if a:
            regs = set(a.regs) if a.load else set()
            if a.writeback:
                regs.add(a.n)
            return regs - {31}
    if enc & 0x3F000000 == 0x08000000:                       # exclusives: Rt and the status Rs
        return {bits(enc, 4, 0), bits(enc, 20, 16)}
    if enc & 0x3A000000 == 0x28000000:                       # other pairs (SIMD): writeback only
        return {bits(enc, 9, 5)}
    if enc & 0x0E000000 == 0x0E000000:                       # SIMD/FP data processing
        to_gp = enc & 0x5F20FC00 == 0x1E200000 or enc & 0x9FE0FC00 in (0x0E002C00, 0x0E003C00)
        return {bits(enc, 4, 0)} if to_gp else set()         # FMOV/FCVT* to GP, SMOV/UMOV
    return {bits(enc, 4, 0)}


def trace_constant(code: Code, off: int, reg: int, lowest: int) -> int | None:
    """Image offset held in `reg` just before `off`, if the last write to it (scanning back
    to `lowest`) is an ADRP, optionally followed by ADD #imm and register moves."""
    extra = 0
    for o in range(off - 4, lowest - 4, -4):
        if reg not in written_regs(code, o):
            continue
        e = code.word(o)
        if e & 0xFFC00000 == 0x91000000:                     # add xR, xS, #imm
            extra += bits(e, 21, 10)
            reg = bits(e, 9, 5)
        elif e & 0xFFE0FFE0 == 0xAA0003E0:                   # mov xR, xS
            reg = bits(e, 20, 16)
        elif e & 0x9F000000 == 0x90000000:                   # adrp xR, page
            imm = sign_extend(bits(e, 23, 5) << 2 | bits(e, 30, 29), 21)
            return (o & ~0xFFF) + (imm << 12) + extra
        else:
            return None
        if reg == 31:
            return None
    return None


def find_jump_table(code: Code, br_off: int, reg: int, lowest: int, window: int = 32) -> list[int] | None:
    """Targets of a Clang switch table ending in `br reg`, or None if the pattern isn't there.

        cmp   wI, #N             ; bound: N+1 entries
        b.hi  default
        ...                      ; xT = table, set by adrp/add (often hoisted out of a loop)
        ldrsw xA, [xT, xIdx, lsl #2]
        add   reg, xA, xT        ; entries are int32 offsets from the table
        br    reg

    Unrelated instructions may be interleaved. The result only decides which labels the
    BR's switch can jump to and which code gets discovered; any other target still goes
    through yw4_resolve, so a wrong guess fails loudly rather than silently.
    """
    lo = max(br_off - 4 * window, lowest)
    o = br_off - 4
    while o >= lo:                                           # add reg, xA, xT (no shift)
        e = code.word(o)
        if e & 0xFFE0FC00 == 0x8B000000 and bits(e, 4, 0) == reg:
            break
        if reg in written_regs(code, o):
            return None
        o -= 4
    else:
        return None
    pair = {bits(e, 9, 5), bits(e, 20, 16)}
    o -= 4
    while o >= lo:                                           # ldrsw xA, [xT, xIdx, lsl #2]
        e = code.word(o)
        if e & 0xFFE0FC00 == 0xB8A07800 and bits(e, 4, 0) in pair and bits(e, 9, 5) in pair:
            break
        o -= 4
    else:
        return None
    ldr_off, rt = o, bits(e, 9, 5)
    bound = None
    o -= 4
    while o >= lo:                                           # b.hi / b.ls guarding the table
        e = code.word(o)
        if e & 0xFC000000 == 0x14000000 or e == 0xD65F03C0:  # b / ret: the table's block starts after it
            bound = guard_into(code, o + 4, lowest, br_off)  # and is entered by a branch to it, not by falling in
            if bound is not None:                            # (sdk+0x446df0: `cmp x8, #5; b.ls` far above, while
                break                                        # the `cmp w8, #4; b.ls` just before belongs to a loop)
        if e & 0xFF00001E == 0x54000008 or e & 0xFF00001F == 0x54000000:  # HI/LS, or EQ (below)
            eq = e & 0xFF00001F == 0x54000000                # `cmp w, #N; b.eq`: the index was masked to 0..N, so N entries
            o -= 4
            lo_cmp = max(br_off - 4 * 8 * window, lowest)    # the compiler can schedule much code in between
            while o >= lo_cmp:                               # the flag-setting compare before it
                e = code.word(o)
                if e & 0x7FE00C10 == 0x7A400800 and not eq:  # ccmp xN/wN, #imm, #nzcv, cond
                    bound = bits(e, 20, 16)                  # `cmp a, #0; ccmp idx, #N, #2, ne; b.hi`:
                    break                                    # the last compare is the index's bound
                if e & 0x7F80001F == 0x7100001F and not bits(e, 22, 22):
                    bound = bits(e, 21, 10) - eq             # cmp xN/wN, #imm (subs xzr, ..)
                    if bound < 0:
                        bound = None
                    break
                if e & 0x1F000000 in (0x11000000, 0x0B000000) and bits(e, 29, 29):
                    return None                              # some other flag setter
                o -= 4
            break
        o -= 4
    table = trace_constant(code, ldr_off, rt, lowest)
    if bound is None:
        return None
    if table is not None:
        return table_targets(code, table, bound)
    # The table's address was loaded by code the compiler placed after the branch (the
    # register is set once, in a block laid out later). Take an `adrp xRt` (+ `add xRt, xRt,
    # #imm`) anywhere nearby whose table has only code addresses near the branch in it.
    for cand in nearby_tables(code, rt, lowest, br_off):
        targets = table_targets(code, cand, bound, near=br_off)
        if targets is not None:
            return targets
    return None


def guard_into(code: Code, start: int, lowest: int, br_off: int) -> int | None:
    """The bound of a switch whose dispatch block at `start` is entered by `cmp xI, #N; b.ls start` (N+1 entries)
    or `b.lo start` (N entries) somewhere in the function before it, else None."""
    o = max(lowest, br_off - 0x4000)
    while o < start:
        e = code.word(o)
        if e & 0xFF000010 == 0x54000000 and e & 0xF in (3, 9):  # b.lo / b.ls
            imm = bits(e, 23, 5)
            if imm & 0x40000:
                imm -= 0x80000
            if o + 4 * imm == start:
                for back in range(1, 9):                       # its compare, just before it
                    c = code.word(o - 4 * back)
                    if c & 0x7F80001F == 0x7100001F and not bits(c, 22, 22):
                        n = bits(c, 21, 10)
                        return n if e & 0xF == 9 else (n - 1 if n else None)
                    if c & 0x1F000000 in (0x11000000, 0x0B000000) and bits(c, 29, 29):
                        break                                  # another flag setter: not ours
        o += 4
    return None


def table_targets(code: Code, table: int, bound: int, near: int | None = None) -> list[int] | None:
    """The bound+1 case targets of the int32 offset table at `table`, or None if any isn't code
    (or, with `near`, isn't within 64 KiB of it)."""
    targets = []
    for k in range(bound + 1):
        if table + 4 * k + 4 > len(code.data):
            return None
        t = table + struct.unpack_from("<i", code.data, table + 4 * k)[0]
        if not code.is_code(t) or (near is not None and abs(t - near) > 0x10000):
            return None
        targets.append(t)
    return targets


def nearby_tables(code: Code, reg: int, lowest: int, br_off: int, reach: int = 0x8000) -> list[int]:
    """Addresses `adrp xreg` (+ `add xreg, xreg, #imm` right after) builds within `reach` of the branch."""
    found = []
    for o in range(max(lowest, br_off - reach), min(code.text_end, br_off + reach), 4):
        e = code.word(o)
        if e & 0x9F000000 != 0x90000000 or bits(e, 4, 0) != reg:
            continue
        imm = sign_extend(bits(e, 23, 5) << 2 | bits(e, 30, 29), 21)
        addr = (o & ~0xFFF) + (imm << 12)
        n = code.word(o + 4) if o + 4 < code.text_end else 0
        if n & 0xFFC00000 == 0x91000000 and bits(n, 9, 5) == reg and bits(n, 4, 0) == reg:
            addr += bits(n, 21, 10)
        found.append(addr)
    return found


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- discovery

@dataclass
class Function:
    entry: int
    body: set[int] = field(default_factory=set)
    jump_tables: dict[int, list[int]] = field(default_factory=dict)  # BR offset -> targets
    problems: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)


def discover(code: Code, entry: int, entries: set[int]) -> Function:
    """Every instruction reachable from `entry` without entering another function."""
    fn = Function(entry)
    work = [entry]

    def follow(t: int) -> None:
        if t == entry or t not in entries:
            work.append(t)

    while work:
        off = work.pop()
        while off not in fn.body:
            if not code.is_code(off):
                fn.problems.append(f"flow leaves .text at {off:#x}")
                break
            fn.body.add(off)
            enc = code.word(off)
            f = decode_flow(enc, off)
            nxt = off + 4
            if f is None or f.kind in ("bl", "blr"):
                pass
            elif f.kind == "cond":
                follow(f.target)
            elif f.kind == "b":
                follow(f.target)
                break
            elif f.kind == "br":
                targets = find_jump_table(code, off, f.reg, entry)
```
