```py
    vec2 cell = floor(gl_FragCoord.xy / max(yw4_pcss.tune.w, 1.0));
    float a = 6.2831853 * fract(52.9829189 * fract(dot(cell, vec2(0.06711056, 0.00583715))));
    return mat2(cos(a), sin(a), -sin(a), cos(a));
}
float yw4_pcss_remember(vec2 key, float lit) {
    if (yw4_seen_n < 2) {
        yw4_seen_key[yw4_seen_n] = key;
        yw4_seen_lit[yw4_seen_n] = lit;
        yw4_seen_n++;
    }
    return lit;
}"""


def pcss_helper(dim: str) -> str:
    """yw4_shadow for a SHADOWARRAY2D (c: x, y, layer, reference) or SHADOW2D (x, y, reference) map."""
    if dim == "SHADOWARRAY2D":
        sig = "sampler2DArrayShadow s, sampler2DArray d, vec4 c"
        game, key, layer, ref = "texture(s, c)", "c.zw", "c.z", "c.w"
        fetch = "textureLod(d, vec3({uv}, c.z), 0.0).r"
        test = "texture(s, vec4({uv}, c.z, c.w))"
    else:
        sig = "sampler2DShadow s, sampler2D d, vec3 c"
        game, key, layer, ref = "texture(s, c)", "vec2(-1.0, c.z)", "0.0", "c.z"
        fetch = "textureLod(d, {uv}, 0.0).r"
        test = "texture(s, vec3({uv}, c.z))"
    tap = "c.xy + rot * YW4_DISK[i] * {r}"
    return f"""\
float yw4_shadow({sig}) {{
    if (yw4_pcss.mode.x < 0.5) return {game};
    if (yw4_pcss.tune.y == 3.0) return {test.format(uv="c.xy")};
    if (yw4_pcss.tune.y == 4.0) return {fetch.format(uv="c.xy")};
    if (yw4_pcss.tune.y == 5.0) return {ref} > {fetch.format(uv="c.xy")} ? 1.0 : 0.0;
    if (yw4_pcss.tune.y == 6.0) return {ref};
    for (int i = 0; i < yw4_seen_n; i++)
        if (yw4_seen_key[i] == {key}) return yw4_seen_lit[i];
    mat2 rot = yw4_pcss_rotation();
    float r;
    if (yw4_pcss.tune.z > 0.5 && yw4_search_layer == {layer}) {{
        if (yw4_search_r < 0.0) return yw4_pcss_remember({key}, {test.format(uv="c.xy")});
        r = yw4_search_r;
    }} else {{
        float gaps = 0.0, casters = 0.0;
        for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++) {{
            float z = {fetch.format(uv=tap.format(r="yw4_pcss.mode.z"))};
            float gap = {ref} - z;
            if (gap > yw4_pcss.tune.x) {{ gaps += gap; casters += 1.0; }}
        }}
        if (yw4_pcss.tune.y == 1.0) return casters * (1.0 / 16.0);
        yw4_search_layer = {layer}, yw4_search_r = -1.0;
        if (casters == 0.0) return yw4_pcss_remember({key}, {test.format(uv="c.xy")});
        r = clamp(gaps / casters * yw4_pcss.scale[min(int({layer} + 0.5), 3)], yw4_pcss.mode.w, yw4_pcss.mode.z);
        yw4_search_r = r;
    }}
    if (yw4_pcss.tune.y == 2.0) return r / yw4_pcss.mode.z;
    float lit = 0.0;
    for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++)
        lit += {test.format(uv=tap.format(r="r"))};
    return yw4_pcss_remember({key}, lit * (1.0 / 16.0));
}}"""


def iface_text(iface: dict, names: dict[int, str] | None = None) -> str:
    """The interface for the runtime (gpu.c), one item per line:
    c <slot> [name] (constant buffer, with the engine's name for it from the shader's header),
    r <slot> <hex mask> | * (its 16-byte rows 0-63 the program reads; *: also at computed addresses),
    t <slot> <target> (texture), i <slot> (image),
    s <n> (storage buffer), a <location> f|u (vertex input type),
    d <slot> <target> (a shadow map's raw depth, for yw4_shadow), p 0 (yw4_shadow's settings)."""
    names = names or {}
    lines = [f"c {n} {names[n]}" if n in names else f"c {n}" for n in iface["cbuffers"]]
    computed = set(iface.get("cbuffer_computed", []))
    for n in iface["cbuffers"]:
        rows = iface.get("cbuffer_rows", {}).get(str(n), [])
        mask = sum(1 << r for r in rows if r < 64)
        lines.append(f"r {n} *" if n in computed or any(r >= 64 for r in rows) else f"r {n} {mask:x}")
    lines += [f"t {k} {v}" for k, v in iface["textures"].items()]
    lines += [f"d {k} {v}" for k, v in iface.get("depth", {}).items()]
    if iface.get("depth"):
        lines.append("p 0")
    lines += [f"i {k}" for k in iface["images"]]
    lines += [f"s {n}" for n in iface["storage"]]
    if iface["stage"] == "vert":
        lines += [f"a {k} {v}" for k, v in iface["inputs"].items()]
        if iface.get("position"):
            lines.append(f"m {iface['position']}")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def position_source(text: str) -> str | None:
    """Where a vertex program's position comes from, when it is simple enough for the runtime to work
    out a draw's corners without running the program (gpu_draw.c, widescreen): "<slot> <row x> <row y>
    <row z> <row w>" when it is one constant buffer's 16-byte rows each dotted with vertex input 0 (DP4),
    as the UI's programs do; "in" when it is input 0 as it is (full-screen passes); else None."""
    slots = {m.group(1): int(m.group(2))
             for m in re.finditer(r"CBUFFER\s+(\w+)\[\]\s*=\s*\{\s*program\.buffer\[(\d+)\]", text)}
    rows: dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[int, int]] = {}  # (register, component) -> (slot, row) loaded there
    # (register, component) -> the row it holds dotted with input 0, or ("in", component of input 0)
    dots: dict[tuple[str, str], tuple] = {}
    pos: dict[str, tuple] = {}

    def dest(t: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
        m = re.fullmatch(r"(.*?)(?:\.([xyzw]+))?", t.strip())
        return m.group(1), m.group(2) or SWZ

    for ln in text.splitlines():
        m = re.match(r"\s*([A-Z0-9]+)(?:\.[A-Z0-9]+)*\s+(.*);", ln)
        if not m or ln.lstrip().startswith(("CBUFFER", "ATTRIB", "OUTPUT", "TEMP", "OPTION")):
            continue
        op, args = m.group(1), split_args(m.group(2))
        if not args:
            continue
        reg, mask = dest(args[0])
        values: dict[str, tuple[int, int] | None] = {}
        if op == "LDC" and len(args) == 2 and (c := re.fullmatch(r"(\w+)\[(\d+)\]", args[1])) and c.group(1) in slots:
            values = {k: (slots[c.group(1)], int(c.group(2)) >> 4) for k in mask}
            for k in mask:
                rows[reg, k] = values[k]
            for k in mask:
                dots.pop((reg, k), None)
            continue
        if op == "DP4" and len(args) == 3:
            a, b = parse_operand(args[1]), parse_operand(args[2])
            if b.text == "vertex.attrib[0]":
                a, b = b, a
            src = {rows.get((b.text, k)) for k in b.swizzle}
            ok = a.text == "vertex.attrib[0]" and a.swizzle == SWZ and not (a.neg or b.neg or a.abs or b.abs)
            row = src.pop() if ok and len(src) == 1 and b.swizzle == SWZ else None
            values = {k: row for k in mask}
        elif op == "MOV" and len(args) == 2:
            s = parse_operand(args[1])
            values = {k: None if s.neg or s.abs else
                      ("in", s.swizzle[SWZ.index(k)]) if s.text == "vertex.attrib[0]" else
                      dots.get((s.text, s.swizzle[SWZ.index(k)])) for k in mask}
        else:
            values = {k: None for k in mask}
        for k in mask:
            rows.pop((reg, k), None)
            if reg == "result.position":
                if values[k] is None:
                    pos.pop(k, None)
                else:
                    pos[k] = values[k]
            elif values[k] is None:
                dots.pop((reg, k), None)
            else:
                dots[reg, k] = values[k]
    if len(pos) != 4:
        return None
    if all(pos[k] == ("in", k) for k in SWZ):
        return "in"
    if len({s for s, _ in pos.values()}) != 1 or pos["x"][0] == "in":
        return None
    return " ".join(str(v) for v in [pos["x"][0]] + [pos[k][1] for k in SWZ])


def translate(key: str, stage: str, text: str) -> tuple[str, dict]:
    glsl, iface = Translator(key, stage, text).translate()
    if stage == "vert":
        iface["position"] = position_source(text)
    return glsl, iface


def glslang(cfg: config.Config) -> str | None:
    """[tools] glslang, else glslangValidator from the Vulkan SDK or PATH."""
    import os
    if cfg.glslang:
        return str(cfg.glslang) if cfg.glslang.is_file() else None
    sdk = os.environ.get("VULKAN_SDK")
    if sdk and (Path(sdk) / "Bin" / "glslangValidator.exe").is_file():
        return str(Path(sdk) / "Bin" / "glslangValidator.exe")
    return shutil.which("glslangValidator") or shutil.which("glslang")


def one_shader(job) -> tuple[str, str, str | None, list[str] | None]:
    """Translate one shader, write its GLSL, interface and .iface, then compile it when glslang is given.
    Returns (key, stage, translation error or None, glslang errors or None); runs in a worker process."""
    f, out, exe, names = job
    key, stage = f.name.split(".")[:2]
    try:
        glsl, iface = translate(key, stage, f.read_text())
    except (ShaderError, KeyError, ValueError) as e:
        msg = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}" if not isinstance(e, ShaderError) else str(e)
        return key, stage, re.sub(r"\d+", "N", msg)[:70], None
    g = out / f"{key}.{stage}"
    g.write_text(glsl)
    (out / f"{key}.json").write_text(json.dumps(iface))
    (out / f"{key}.iface").write_text(iface_text(iface, names))
    if not exe:
        return key, stage, None, None
    # A failure without an ERROR line isn't the shader's: glslang didn't run through (killed, out of memory, the .spv
    # held by a virus scanner), so it is tried again, and if it still fails its exit code and output are the message
    # (2026-11-11: a friend's update stopped at "2 (no message)" for shaders that compile everywhere else).
    for attempt in range(3):
        r = subprocess.run([exe, "-V", "--target-env", "vulkan1.2", "-o", str(g) + ".spv", str(g)],
                           capture_output=True, text=True)
        msgs = [ln for ln in (r.stdout + r.stderr).splitlines() if ln.startswith("ERROR") and "compilation" not in ln]
        if not r.returncode or msgs:
            break
        time.sleep(0.5 * (attempt + 1))
    if r.returncode and not msgs:
        out_lines = [ln.strip() for ln in (r.stdout + r.stderr).splitlines() if ln.strip() and ln.strip() != str(g)]
        msgs = [f"glslang exit code {r.returncode:#x}" + (f": {out_lines[-1]}" if out_lines else ", no output")]
    return key, stage, None, msgs if r.returncode else None


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--check", action="store_true", help="compile the GLSL to SPIR-V with glslangValidator")
    ap.add_argument("keys", nargs="*", help="only these shader keys")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    cfg = config.load(require_exefs=False)
    src = cfg.work_dir / "shaders" / "asm"
    out = cfg.work_dir / "shaders" / "glsl"
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    files = sorted(src.glob("*.asm"))
    if not files:
        print("no shaders: run python -m tools.yw4.shaders first", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    if args.keys:
        files = [f for f in files if f.name.split(".")[0] in args.keys]
    exe = glslang(cfg) if args.check else None
    if args.check and not exe:
        print("glslang not found: install the Vulkan SDK or set [tools] glslang", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    # the engine's names for the constant buffers, from the shaders' headers (tools/yw4/shaders.py)
    index_path = cfg.work_dir / "shaders" / "index.json"
    index = json.loads(index_path.read_text()) if index_path.is_file() else {}
    errors: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    bad_compile = []
    # One shader per job, on every core: translating is Python (one core per process), and each job compiles its
    # own shader right away, so the two halves overlap.
    jobs = [(f, out, exe, {r["slot"]: r["name"] for r in index.get(f.name.split(".")[0], {}).get("resources", [])
                           if r["kind"] == "cbuffer"}) for f in files]
    from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor
    with ProcessPoolExecutor() as pool:
        for i, (key, stage, err, msgs) in enumerate(pool.map(one_shader, jobs, chunksize=8), 1):
            progress.report("shaders", i, len(jobs), every=0.25)
            if err is not None:
                errors.setdefault(err, []).append(key)
            elif msgs is not None:
                bad_compile.append((key, stage, msgs))
    done = len(files) - sum(len(v) for v in errors.values())
    print(f"translated {done}/{len(files)}")
    for msg, keys in sorted(errors.items(), key=lambda kv: -len(kv[1])):
        print(f"  {len(keys):4} {msg}  (e.g. {keys[0]})")
    if exe:
        print(f"glslang: {done - len(bad_compile)}/{done} compile")
        kinds: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
        for key, stage, msg in bad_compile:
            first = re.sub(r"^ERROR: \S+:\d+: ", "", msg[0]) if msg else "(no message)"
            kinds.setdefault(re.sub(r"\d+", "N", first)[:110], []).append(f"{key}.{stage}")
        for msg, keys in sorted(kinds.items(), key=lambda kv: -len(kv[1]))[:12]:
            print(f"  {len(keys):4} {msg}  (e.g. {keys[0]})")
    return 0 if not errors and not bad_compile else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

`recomp/translate.py`:

```py
"""Translate main and the sdk to C (decisions 0007, 0014).

    python -m recomp.translate              write work/recomp/
    python -m recomp.translate --report     statistics only, write nothing

Both modules are version-locked (main by target.toml [main], the sdk by [sdk]).
Entry points per module: .eh_frame_hdr starts, address-taken targets, defined
function symbols, every BL target, and for main also Ghidra's function entries.
Output (derived from the game's code, so it stays in work/ and is never committed):

    work/recomp/funcs.h          prototypes: f_<offset> (main), s_<offset> (sdk)
    work/recomp/main_NNN.c       main's functions, CHUNK per file (for a parallel build)
    work/recomp/sdk_NNN.c        the sdk's functions
    work/recomp/func_table.c     yw4_code[]: each module's sorted function table (yw4_resolve)
    work/recomp/image_info.c     yw4_modules[]: what the loader needs (sizes, hashes, relocations)

Functions listed in recomp/overrides.toml get a body that calls native runtime code
instead (decision 0016).

Symbols are resolved here, not at run time: both modules are known, so every symbolic
relocation becomes "module + offset" in load order (main first, then the sdk, as the
Switch's dynamic loader searches), or 0 for weak symbols nobody defines.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import collections
import hashlib
import struct
import sys
import tomllib
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from tools.yw4 import config, progress, recon, reloc, sdkref

from . import coverage, function

# Functions per generated file. 100, not 500 (2026-11-13): a few hundred functions in main (the old main_070's)
# take minutes to compile, and at 500 a file each they ran alone at the end of the build; at 100 the owner's 16
# threads stay busy to the end (382 -> ~295 s). recomp/compile_cost.json is measured at this size: change one, remeasure.
CHUNK = 100

R_RELATIVE, SYMBOL_RELOCS = reloc.R_AARCH64_RELATIVE, (reloc.R_AARCH64_ABS64, reloc.R_AARCH64_GLOB_DAT,
                                                   reloc.R_AARCH64_JUMP_SLOT)
STT_FUNC = 2
DT_INIT = 0xC
NO_MODULE = 0xFFFFFFFF
INIT_START = "_ZN2nn4init5StartEmmPFvvES2_"  # nn::init::Start(u64, u64, void (*)(), void (*)())
OVERRIDES = Path(__file__).with_name("overrides.toml")


@dataclass
class Module:
    name: str            # also the file in work/exefs/ (<name>.bin) and the C file prefix
    prefix: str          # function names
    base: str            # C variable holding the load address
    preferred: int       # where the runtime tries to put it (inside the 39-bit space)
    image: bytes
    info: dict
    code: function.Code

    @property
    def mem_size(self) -> int:
        return (max(len(self.image), reloc.read_mod0(self.image).bss_end) + 0xFFF) & ~0xFFF


def load_modules(cfg: config.Config) -> list[Module]:
    """main, then the sdk: load order, which is also symbol search order. The sdk goes right
    after main, 2 MiB aligned; main stays at its Switch address (decision 0010)."""
    main_image, mods = recon.load_main(cfg)  # each refuses a build that doesn't match target.toml
    sdk_image, sdk_info = sdkref.load_sdk(cfg)
    out = []
    for name, prefix, base, image, info in (("main", "f_", "yw4_image_base", main_image, mods["main"]),
                                            ("sdk", "s_", "yw4_sdk_base", sdk_image, sdk_info)):
        code = function.Code(image, info["segments"]["text"]["size"], base, prefix)
        preferred = 0x7100000000 if not out else (out[-1].preferred + out[-1].mem_size + 0x1FFFFF) & ~0x1FFFFF
        out.append(Module(name, prefix, base, preferred, image, info, code))
    return out


def raw_dynsym(image: bytes, info: dict) -> list[tuple[str, int, int, int]]:
    """(name, type, section index, value) for every .dynsym entry, in index order."""
    names = recon.dynsym_names(image, info)
    ro = info["segments"]["ro"]["mem_offset"]
    start, size = info["dynsym"]
    out = []
    for i in range(size // 24):
        _, st_info, _, shndx, value, _ = struct.unpack_from("<IBBHQQ", image, ro + start + 24 * i)
        out.append((names[i], st_info & 0xF, shndx, value))
    return out


def load_overrides(modules: list[Module]) -> dict[str, dict[int, str]]:
    """Per module: function offset -> the native function that replaces its body."""
    out: dict[str, dict[int, str]] = {m.name: {} for m in modules}
    for o in tomllib.loads(OVERRIDES.read_text()).get("override", []):
        m = next((m for m in modules if m.name == o["module"]), None)
        if m is None:
            raise RuntimeError(f"overrides.toml: no module {o['module']!r}")
        funcs = {name: v for name, typ, shndx, v in raw_dynsym(m.image, m.info) if shndx and typ == STT_FUNC}
        if o["symbol"] not in funcs:
            raise RuntimeError(f"overrides.toml: {m.name} defines no function {o['symbol']}")
        out[m.name][funcs[o["symbol"]]] = o["native"]
    return out


def load_hooks(modules: list[Module]) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[int, str]], dict[str, dict[int, dict[int, str]]]]:
    """Per module: function offset -> the native hook that runs before its body (decision 0024),
    and function offset -> {instruction offset -> hook} for hooks with an `at` inside the body
    (decision 0042). Hooks name game functions by offset (game code has no symbols)."""
    entry: dict[str, dict[int, str]] = {m.name: {} for m in modules}
    inside: dict[str, dict[int, dict[int, str]]] = {m.name: {} for m in modules}
    for h in tomllib.loads(OVERRIDES.read_text()).get("hook", []):
        if h["module"] not in entry:
            raise RuntimeError(f"overrides.toml: no module {h['module']!r}")
        fn = int(h["offset"], 16)
        if "at" in h:
            inside[h["module"]].setdefault(fn, {})[int(h["at"], 16)] = h["native"]
        else:
            entry[h["module"]][fn] = h["native"]
    return entry, inside


def guest_symbols(modules: list[Module]) -> list[tuple[str, int, int]]:
    """(symbol, module index, offset) for each [[guest_symbol]] in overrides.toml."""
    out = []
    for g in tomllib.loads(OVERRIDES.read_text()).get("guest_symbol", []):
        i = next((i for i, m in enumerate(modules) if m.name == g["module"]), None)
        if i is None:
            raise RuntimeError(f"overrides.toml: no module {g['module']!r}")
        m = modules[i]
        funcs = {name: v for name, typ, shndx, v in raw_dynsym(m.image, m.info) if shndx and typ == STT_FUNC}
        if g["symbol"] not in funcs:
            raise RuntimeError(f"overrides.toml: {m.name} defines no function {g['symbol']}")
        out.append((g["symbol"], i, funcs[g["symbol"]]))
    return out


def entry_points(cfg: config.Config, m: Module) -> set[int]:
    code = m.code
    entries = set(recon.eh_frame_function_starts(code.data))
    entries |= recon.address_taken_functions(code.data, code.text_end)
    entries |= {v for _, typ, shndx, v in raw_dynsym(m.image, m.info) if shndx and typ == STT_FUNC}
    if m.name == "main":  # the starts found by Ghidra that the rules above miss (decision 0051)
        extra = Path(__file__).with_name("main_extra_functions.txt").read_text().splitlines()
        entries |= {int(line, 16) for line in extra if line and not line.startswith("#")}
    for off in range(0, code.text_end, 4):  # BL targets
        f = function.decode_flow(code.word(off), off)
        if f and f.kind == "bl" and code.is_code(f.target):
            entries.add(f.target)
    return {e for e in entries if code.is_code(e)}


def resolve_relocations(modules: list[Module]) -> tuple[list[list], list[list], collections.Counter]:
    """Per module: RELATIVE (offset, addend) and symbolic (offset, module index, value)."""
    syms = [raw_dynsym(m.image, m.info) for m in modules]
    defined = [{name: value for name, _, shndx, value in s if shndx} for s in syms]
    unresolved: collections.Counter = collections.Counter()
    relative, symbolic = [], []
    for i, m in enumerate(modules):
        rel, sym = [], []
        for r in reloc.read_relocs(m.image):
            if r.type == R_RELATIVE:
                rel.append((r.offset, r.addend))
            elif r.type in SYMBOL_RELOCS:
                name = syms[i][r.sym][0]
                where = next((j for j, d in enumerate(defined) if name in d), None)
                if where is None:  # weak and defined nowhere (linker markers): 0
                    unresolved[name] += 1
                    sym.append((r.offset, NO_MODULE, 0))
                else:
                    sym.append((r.offset, where, (defined[where][name] + r.addend) & (2**64 - 1)))
            else:
                raise RuntimeError(f"{m.name}: unsupported relocation type {r.type}")
        relative.append(rel)
        symbolic.append(sym)
    return relative, symbolic, unresolved


def image_info(modules: list[Module], relative: list[list], symbolic: list[list], npdm: bytes,
               gsyms: list[tuple[str, int, int]]) -> str:
    """Loader tables (decisions 0010, 0014): per module its size, hash, relocations, DT_INIT."""
    out = ['#include "yw4load.h"\n']
    rows = []
    for i, m in enumerate(modules):
        rel = ",\n".join(f"    {{{o:#x}, {a:#x}}}" for o, a in relative[i]) or "    {0, 0}"
        sym = ",\n".join(f"    {{{o:#x}, {mod:#x}, {v:#x}}}" for o, mod, v in symbolic[i]) or "    {0, 0, 0}"
        out.append(f"static const Yw4Relative relative_{m.name}[] = {{\n{rel}\n}};\n"
                   f"static const Yw4SymReloc symrelocs_{m.name}[] = {{\n{sym}\n}};\n")
        init = reloc.read_dynamic(m.image, reloc.read_mod0(m.image)).get(DT_INIT, 0)
        rows.append(f'    {{"{m.name}", "{m.name}.bin", "{hashlib.sha256(m.image).hexdigest()}", {len(m.image)}, '
                    f"{m.mem_size:#x}, {m.preferred:#x}, &{m.base},\n"
                    f"     relative_{m.name}, {len(relative[i])}, symrelocs_{m.name}, {len(symbolic[i])}, {init:#x}, "
                    f"{m.info['segments']['ro']['mem_offset']:#x}, {m.info['segments']['data']['mem_offset']:#x}}}")
    start = {name: v for name, _, shndx, v in raw_dynsym(modules[1].image, modules[1].info) if shndx}[INIT_START]
    if npdm[:4] != b"META":
        raise RuntimeError("main.npdm: no META header")
    stack = struct.unpack_from("<I", npdm, 0x1C)[0]
    out.append("const Yw4Module yw4_modules[] = {\n" + ",\n".join(rows) + "\n};\n"
               f"const size_t yw4_nmodules = {len(modules)};\n"
               f"const uint64_t yw4_entry_init_start = {start:#x};  /* nn::init::Start, in the sdk */\n"
               f"const uint64_t yw4_main_stack_size = {stack:#x};  /* main thread, from the NPDM */\n"
               f"const uint32_t yw4_main_priority = {npdm[0xE]};\n")
    rows = ",\n".join(f'    {{"{name}", {i}, {off:#x}}}' for name, i, off in gsyms)
    out.append(f"const Yw4GuestSymbol yw4_guest_symbols[] = {{\n{rows or '    {0, 0, 0}'}\n}};\n"
               f"const size_t yw4_nguest_symbols = {len(gsyms)};\n")
    return "\n".join(out)


def write_if_changed(path, text: str) -> None:
    """Keeps the timestamp of unchanged files, so recomp.build only recompiles what changed."""
    if not path.exists() or path.read_text() != text:
        path.write_text(text)


SETJMP = ("_setjmp", "setjmp", "__setjmp")


def plt_slot(code: function.Code, e: int) -> int | None:
    """The GOT slot a PLT stub at e jumps through (adrp x16; ldr x17, [x16, #o]; add x16, x16, #o;
    br x17), or None."""
    if e + 16 > code.text_end:
        return None
    w = [code.word(e + 4 * i) for i in range(4)]
    if (w[0] & 0x9F00001F != 0x90000010 or w[1] & 0xFFC003FF != 0xF9400211
            or w[2] & 0xFFC003FF != 0x91000210 or w[3] != 0xD61F0220):
        return None
    page = ((w[0] >> 29) & 3 | ((w[0] >> 5) & 0x7FFFF) << 2) << 12
    if page & (1 << 32):
        page -= 1 << 33
    return (e & ~0xFFF) + page + ((w[1] >> 10) & 0xFFF) * 8


def setjmp_entries(modules: list[Module], symbolic: list[list], entries: list[set[int]]) -> list[frozenset[int]]:
    """Per module, the functions that are setjmp: its definition, and PLT stubs to it (decision 0018)."""
    where = set()
    for i, m in enumerate(modules):
        for name, typ, shndx, v in raw_dynsym(m.image, m.info):
            if shndx and typ == STT_FUNC and name in SETJMP:
                where.add((i, v))
    out = []
    for i, m in enumerate(modules):
        got = {o: (mod, v) for o, mod, v in symbolic[i]}
        found = {v for mod, v in where if mod == i}
        found |= {e for e in entries[i] if got.get(plt_slot(m.code, e)) in where}
        out.append(frozenset(found))
    return out


# Each function is found and translated on its own (nothing is shared between functions but the counts in
# EmitStats), so worker processes take slices of the sorted entries; the results come back in that order, so the
# output is the same as one process's. The module image and tables go to each worker once (initializer).
_work = None


def _work_init(*args) -> None:
    global _work
    _work = args


def _work_batch(batch: list[int]) -> tuple[list[tuple[function.Function, str]], function.EmitStats]:
    code, prefix, entries, overrides, setjmps, hooks, at_hooks = _work
    stats = function.EmitStats()
    out = []
    for e in batch:
        fn = function.discover(code, e, entries)
        native = overrides.get(e)
        if native:  # the address stays a function; its body is the native code
            src = (f"void {native}(CPUState *ctx);  /* override (recomp/overrides.toml) */\n"
                   f"void {function.fname(e, prefix)}(CPUState *ctx) {{ {native}(ctx); }}")
        else:
            src = function.emit_function(code, fn, entries, coverage.subgroup, stats, setjmps,
                                         hooks.get(e), at_hooks.get(e))
        out.append((fn, src))
    return out, stats


def translate(cfg: config.Config, m: Module, overrides: dict[int, str], entries: set[int],
              setjmps: frozenset[int], hooks: dict[int, str],
              at_hooks: dict[int, dict[int, str]]) -> tuple[list[function.Function], list[str]]:
    code = m.code
    order = sorted(entries)
    batches = [order[i:i + 256] for i in range(0, len(order), 256)]
    stats = function.EmitStats()
    funcs, sources = [], []
    from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor
    with ProcessPoolExecutor(initializer=_work_init,
                             initargs=(code, m.prefix, entries, overrides, setjmps, hooks, at_hooks)) as pool:
        for done, part in pool.map(_work_batch, batches):
            for fn, src in done:
                funcs.append(fn)
                sources.append(src)
            progress.report("translate", len(funcs), len(order), m.name, every=0.25)
            for g, n in part.unimplemented.items():
                stats.unimplemented[g] = stats.unimplemented.get(g, 0) + n
            stats.cached += part.cached
            stats.not_cached += part.not_cached
    missing = (set(overrides) | set(hooks) | set(at_hooks)) - {fn.entry for fn in funcs}
    if missing:
        raise RuntimeError(f"{m.name}: overridden or hooked functions not found: {sorted(map(hex, missing))}")

    brs = collections.Counter()
    for fn in funcs:
        for off in fn.body:
            f = function.decode_flow(code.word(off), off)
            if f and f.kind == "br":
                brs["jump table" if off in fn.jump_tables else "indirect tail call"] += 1
    translated = sum(len(fn.body) for fn in funcs)
    unique = len(set().union(*(fn.body for fn in funcs)))
    problems = [p for fn in funcs for p in fn.problems]
    unimpl = sum(stats.unimplemented.values())
    print(f"== {m.name} (preferred base {m.preferred:#x}, {m.mem_size:#x} bytes)")
    print(f"functions:               {len(funcs):,}")
    print(f"instructions translated: {translated:,} ({unique:,} unique, "
          f"{translated - unique:,} duplicated into more than one function)")
    print(f"untranslated (traps):    {unimpl:,} ({100 * unimpl / translated:.2f}%)")
    for g, n in sorted(stats.unimplemented.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]):
        print(f"    {n:10,}  {g}")
    print(f"BR: {dict(brs)}")
    print(f"overridden by native code: {len(overrides)}; hooked: {len(hooks)}; setjmp functions: {len(setjmps)}")
    print(f"registers in locals: {stats.cached:,} functions; in the CPUState: {stats.not_cached:,} (decision 0035)")
    print(f"flow problems: {len(problems)}")
    for p in problems[:10]:
        print(f"    {p}")
    return funcs, sources


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--report", action="store_true", help="print statistics, write nothing")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        cfg = config.load()
        modules = load_modules(cfg)
    except config.ConfigError as e:
        print(f"config error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    overrides = load_overrides(modules)
    hooks, at_hooks = load_hooks(modules)
    relative, symbolic, unresolved = resolve_relocations(modules)
    entries = [entry_points(cfg, m) for m in modules]
    setjmps = setjmp_entries(modules, symbolic, entries)
    results = [translate(cfg, m, overrides[m.name], entries[i], setjmps[i], hooks[m.name], at_hooks[m.name])
               for i, m in enumerate(modules)]
    print(f"== relocations: " + ", ".join(f"{m.name} {len(relative[i]):,} relative + {len(symbolic[i]):,} symbolic"
                                          for i, m in enumerate(modules)))
    print(f"   weak symbols defined nowhere (-> 0): {dict(unresolved)}")
    if args.report:
        return 0

    out = cfg.work_dir / "recomp"
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    header = "/* Generated by recomp.translate from the owner's copy of the game. Do not commit. */\n"
    protos, tables, entries = [], [], []
    nfiles_total = 0
    for m, (funcs, sources) in zip(modules, results):
        nfiles = (len(sources) + CHUNK - 1) // CHUNK
        nfiles_total += nfiles
        for old in out.glob(f"{m.name}_*.c"):
            if old.stem[len(m.name) + 1:].isdigit() and int(old.stem[len(m.name) + 1:]) >= nfiles:
                old.unlink()
        for i in range(0, len(sources), CHUNK):
            write_if_changed(out / f"{m.name}_{i // CHUNK:03}.c",
                             f"{header}#include \"funcs.h\"\n\n" + "\n\n".join(sources[i:i + CHUNK]) + "\n")
        protos += [f"void {function.fname(fn.entry, m.prefix)}(CPUState *ctx);" for fn in funcs]
        rows = ",\n".join(f"    {{{fn.entry:#x}, {function.fname(fn.entry, m.prefix)}}}" for fn in funcs)
        tables.append(f"static const FuncEntry funcs_{m.name}[] = {{\n{rows}\n}};\n")
        entries.append(f'    {{"{m.name}", &{m.base}, {m.mem_size:#x}, funcs_{m.name}, {len(funcs)}}}')
    write_if_changed(out / "funcs.h", f"{header}#pragma once\n#include \"yw4rt.h\"\n" + "\n".join(protos) + "\n")
    write_if_changed(out / "func_table.c",
                     f"{header}#include \"funcs.h\"\n\n" + "\n".join(tables) +
                     "\nconst Yw4CodeModule yw4_code[] = {\n" + ",\n".join(entries) + "\n};\n"
                     f"const size_t yw4_ncode = {len(modules)};\n")
    npdm = (cfg.exefs_dir / "main.npdm").read_bytes()
    write_if_changed(out / "image_info.c", header + image_info(modules, relative, symbolic, npdm, guest_symbols(modules)))
    print(f"wrote {out} ({nfiles_total} source files + func_table.c, image_info.c)")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

`runtime/README.md`:

```md
# runtime/

The native runtime the recompiled `main` and `sdk` link against (decisions 0005, 0014): the kernel (system calls, threads, memory), system services, and graphics (NVN on Vulkan).

So far:
- `include/yw4cpu.h`: the guest CPU state and the helpers generated code uses (flags, conditions, rotates, divides, memory access).
- `include/yw4rt.h` + `src/dispatch.c`: what generated functions call into: module bases, indirect-call lookup across modules (`yw4_resolve`), tail-call macros and traps (decisions 0007, 0014).
- `include/yw4load.h`, `src/loader.c`, `src/sha256.c`, `src/main.c`: load and relocate `main` and `sdk` (refusing any other build), host callbacks, start-up through the sdk's `nn::init::Start` (decisions 0010, 0014).
- `src/hle*.c`, `src/heap.c`: native versions of sdk functions written before 0014; unused since the sdk is recompiled, kept until the recompiled sdk passes the same checks.
- `src/hle.h`, `src/hle_os.c`, `src/hle_diag.c`, `src/hle_mem.c`, `src/heap.c`: first sdk imports: start-up memory, diag logging/asserts, `nn::mem::StandardAllocator` on a TLSF heap (decision 0011).
- `src/hle_libc.c`, `src/hle_string.c`: musl start-up (`__nnmusl_init_dso`), static-local guards, and the exact C library functions: memory, strings, ctype, integer parsing (decision 0012).
- `src/hle_math.c`: the 40 libm imports, bit-exact with the sdk: musl 1.1.19 (`third_party/musl`) plus exact instruction models; checked with `python -m tools.yw4.sdkref --check` (decision 0013).
- `src/crypto.c`: AES/SHA instructions (Crypto extension).
- `src/ipc.h`, `src/ipc.c`, `src/ipc_simple.h`, `src/svc_*.c`: IPC message codec, sessions and domains, and the native system services (decision 0014). `YW4_TRACE_IPC=1` traces requests; `YW4_IPC_STUB=1` stubs unknown ones for surveying.
- `src/romfs.h`, `src/romfs.c`: the game's RomFS as a virtual image of the owner's folder (decision 0014).
- `src/kernel.h`, `src/kernel.c`: the Horizon kernel the recompiled sdk calls through `SVC`: memory map, heap, threads (one host thread each) and their synchronisation, events, shared and transfer memory, system counter, `FPCR` writes (decisions 0014, 0015). `YW4_TRACE_SVC=1` traces calls. Stops print a guest backtrace; `python -m tools.yw4.where -` adds symbol names to `sdk+0x...` addresses in piped output.
- `src/nvn.c`, `src/nvn.h`, `src/nvn_objects.c`, `src/nvn_cmdbuf.c`, `src/tegra.c`: NVN, entered through the `nvnBootstrapLoader` override (decision 0016); headless objects, command recording and the Tegra texture layout (decision 0017). Unwritten NVN functions stop with their name.
- `src/svc_hid.c`, `src/svc_nifm.c`, `src/svc_audio.c`, `src/svc_acc.c`: input (shared memory, still zeroed), network (offline), audio (`audout` timed at 48 kHz), the one user account.
- `src/savefs.c`: save data as host folders, `<save dir>/<program id>/<user id>/` (yw4's third argument; `build.py --run` uses `<work_dir>/save`).
- `src/setjmp.c`: the guest's setjmp/longjmp in recompiled code (decision 0018).
- `src/window.c`, `src/window.h`: the window (SDL3) and the Vulkan presenter; screenshots (decision 0019).
- `src/pixels.c`: NVN colour formats on the CPU (clear colours, display pixels).
- `src/vi.c`: `nn::vi` overrides and the 60 Hz vsync thread (decision 0017).
- `src/host.h`, `src/host.c`: what the kernel needs from the host OS (threads, locks, condition variables, monotonic clock), for Windows and Linux (decision 0015).

```

`runtime/include/yw4cpu.h`:

```h
/* Guest CPU state and helpers shared by generated code and the runtime.
 *
 * Semantics follow the Arm ARM (DDI 0487) pseudocode for ARMv8.0.
 * Needs a compiler with unsigned __int128 (GCC/Clang on 64-bit hosts).
 */
#ifndef YW4CPU_H
#define YW4CPU_H

#include <stdint.h>
#include <string.h>

/* One SIMD/FP register. Lane 0 is the lowest-addressed (little-endian), as on ARM. */
typedef union {
    uint8_t b[16];
    uint16_t h[8];
    uint32_t s[4];
    uint64_t d[2];
    float f[4];
    double df[2];
} v128;

typedef struct {
    uint64_t x[31];  /* x0..x30 */
    uint64_t sp;
    uint64_t nzcv;   /* N=bit31 Z=bit30 C=bit29 V=bit28, as in the NZCV register */
    v128 v[32];      /* v0..v31 (b/h/s/d/q views of the same register) */
    uint32_t fpcr;   /* not used yet: main never changes it (docs/decisions/0008) */
    uint32_t fpsr;   /* cumulative FP exception flags: not modelled, main never reads them */
    /* Exclusive monitor (LDXR/STXR, decision 0009): address and value of the last exclusive
     * load; excl_size = 0 means no reservation. */
    uint64_t excl_addr;
    uint64_t excl_val;
    uint32_t excl_size;
    /* Thread pointers (decision 0014): TPIDRRO_EL0 is set by the kernel (the thread-local
     * region), TPIDR_EL0 by the thread itself. */
    uint64_t tpidrro_el0;
    uint64_t tpidr_el0;
} CPUState;

#define NZCV_N 0x80000000u
#define NZCV_Z 0x40000000u
#define NZCV_C 0x20000000u
#define NZCV_V 0x10000000u

/* AddWithCarry(x, y, carry_in): returns the sum, writes NZCV to *flags. */
static inline uint64_t awc64(uint64_t a, uint64_t b, unsigned c, uint64_t *flags) {
    unsigned __int128 us = (unsigned __int128)a + b + c;
    __int128 ss = (__int128)(int64_t)a + (int64_t)b + c;
    uint64_t r = (uint64_t)us;
    *flags = (r >> 63) << 31 | (uint64_t)(r == 0) << 30 | (uint64_t)((us >> 64) & 1) << 29 |
             (uint64_t)((__int128)(int64_t)r != ss) << 28;
    return r;
}

static inline uint32_t awc32(uint32_t a, uint32_t b, unsigned c, uint64_t *flags) {
    uint64_t us = (uint64_t)a + b + c;
    int64_t ss = (int64_t)(int32_t)a + (int32_t)b + c;
    uint32_t r = (uint32_t)us;
    *flags = (uint64_t)(r >> 31) << 31 | (uint64_t)(r == 0) << 30 | ((us >> 32) & 1) << 29 |
             (uint64_t)((int64_t)(int32_t)r != ss) << 28;
    return r;
}

/* NZ from a result, C and V cleared (logical ops with S). */
static inline uint64_t nz64(uint64_t r) { return (r >> 63) << 31 | (uint64_t)(r == 0) << 30; }
static inline uint64_t nz32(uint32_t r) { return (uint64_t)(r >> 31) << 31 | (uint64_t)(r == 0) << 30; }

/* ConditionHolds(cond) for cond = 0..15 (EQ NE CS CC MI PL VS VC HI LS GE LT GT LE AL NV). */
static inline int cond_holds(uint64_t nzcv, unsigned cond) {
    int n = (nzcv >> 31) & 1, z = (nzcv >> 30) & 1, c = (nzcv >> 29) & 1, v = (nzcv >> 28) & 1;
    int r;
    switch (cond >> 1) {
    case 0: r = z; break;
    case 1: r = c; break;
    case 2: r = n; break;
    case 3: r = v; break;
    case 4: r = c && !z; break;
    case 5: r = n == v; break;
    case 6: r = n == v && !z; break;
    default: r = 1; break;
    }
    if ((cond & 1) && cond != 15) r = !r;
    return r;
}

static inline uint64_t ror64(uint64_t v, unsigned s) { s &= 63; return s ? (v >> s) | (v << (64 - s)) : v; }
static inline uint32_t ror32(uint32_t v, unsigned s) { s &= 31; return s ? (v >> s) | (v << (32 - s)) : v; }
static inline uint64_t asr64(uint64_t v, unsigned s) { return (uint64_t)((int64_t)v >> s); }
static inline uint32_t asr32(uint32_t v, unsigned s) { return (uint32_t)((int32_t)v >> s); }

static inline uint64_t clz64(uint64_t v) { return v ? (uint64_t)__builtin_clzll(v) : 64; }
static inline uint32_t clz32(uint32_t v) { return v ? (uint32_t)__builtin_clz(v) : 32; }
/* CountLeadingSignBits: CLZ of x<N-1:1> EOR x<N-2:0>, an (N-1)-bit value. */
static inline uint64_t cls64(uint64_t v) { return clz64((v ^ (v >> 1)) & 0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFull) - 1; }
static inline uint32_t cls32(uint32_t v) { return clz32((v ^ (v >> 1)) & 0x7FFFFFFFu) - 1; }

static inline uint64_t rbit64(uint64_t v) {
    v = ((v >> 1) & 0x5555555555555555ull) | ((v & 0x5555555555555555ull) << 1);
    v = ((v >> 2) & 0x3333333333333333ull) | ((v & 0x3333333333333333ull) << 2);
    v = ((v >> 4) & 0x0F0F0F0F0F0F0F0Full) | ((v & 0x0F0F0F0F0F0F0F0Full) << 4);
    return __builtin_bswap64(v);
}
static inline uint32_t rbit32(uint32_t v) { return (uint32_t)(rbit64(v) >> 32); }

static inline uint64_t rev16_64(uint64_t v) {
    return ((v >> 8) & 0x00FF00FF00FF00FFull) | ((v & 0x00FF00FF00FF00FFull) << 8);
}
static inline uint32_t rev16_32(uint32_t v) { return ((v >> 8) & 0x00FF00FFu) | ((v & 0x00FF00FFu) << 8); }
static inline uint64_t rev32_64(uint64_t v) {
    return (uint64_t)__builtin_bswap32((uint32_t)v) | (uint64_t)__builtin_bswap32((uint32_t)(v >> 32)) << 32;
}

static inline uint64_t udiv64(uint64_t n, uint64_t m) { return m ? n / m : 0; }
static inline uint32_t udiv32(uint32_t n, uint32_t m) { return m ? n / m : 0; }
static inline uint64_t sdiv64(uint64_t n, uint64_t m) {
    if (m == 0) return 0;
    if ((int64_t)m == -1) return 0 - n; /* avoids INT64_MIN / -1 overflow in C */
    return (uint64_t)((int64_t)n / (int64_t)m);
}
static inline uint32_t sdiv32(uint32_t n, uint32_t m) {
    if (m == 0) return 0;
    if ((int32_t)m == -1) return 0 - n;
    return (uint32_t)((int32_t)n / (int32_t)m);
}

static inline uint64_t umulh64(uint64_t a, uint64_t b) {
    return (uint64_t)(((unsigned __int128)a * b) >> 64);
}
static inline uint64_t smulh64(uint64_t a, uint64_t b) {
    return (uint64_t)(((__int128)(int64_t)a * (int64_t)b) >> 64);
}

/* CRC32B/H/W/X and CRC32C*: the bit-reflected CRC update without inversion, over the low
 * `bytes` bytes of `data` (Arm ARM: BitReverse(acc) and the polynomial division, done
 * here in the equivalent reflected form). */
static inline uint32_t crc32_update(uint32_t acc, uint64_t data, int bytes, uint32_t poly_reflected) {
    for (int i = 0; i < 8 * bytes; i++) {
        acc ^= (uint32_t)(data >> i) & 1;
        acc = (acc >> 1) ^ (poly_reflected & (0u - (acc & 1)));
    }
    return acc;
}

/* Crypto extension (runtime/src/crypto.c): AES and SHA-1/SHA-256 steps on whole registers,
 * as in the Arm ARM pseudocode. d is read and written; n/m are inputs. */
typedef enum { YW4_AESE, YW4_AESD, YW4_AESMC, YW4_AESIMC } Yw4AesOp;
void yw4_aes(Yw4AesOp op, v128 *d, const v128 *n);
typedef enum { YW4_SHA1C, YW4_SHA1P, YW4_SHA1M, YW4_SHA1SU0, YW4_SHA256H, YW4_SHA256H2, YW4_SHA256SU1,
               YW4_SHA1H, YW4_SHA1SU1, YW4_SHA256SU0 } Yw4ShaOp;
void yw4_sha(Yw4ShaOp op, v128 *d, const v128 *n, const v128 *m);

/* Guest memory. Guest addresses are host addresses (decision 0005), so these are plain
 * host accesses. memcpy keeps them legal for unaligned addresses and under strict aliasing;
 * compilers turn each into one load/store instruction. Assumes a little-endian host. */
static inline uint8_t ld8(uint64_t a) { return *(const uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)a; }
static inline uint16_t ld16(uint64_t a) { uint16_t v; memcpy(&v, (const void *)(uintptr_t)a, 2); return v; }
static inline uint32_t ld32(uint64_t a) { uint32_t v; memcpy(&v, (const void *)(uintptr_t)a, 4); return v; }
static inline uint64_t ld64(uint64_t a) { uint64_t v; memcpy(&v, (const void *)(uintptr_t)a, 8); return v; }
static inline void st8(uint64_t a, uint8_t v) { *(uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)a = v; }
static inline void st16(uint64_t a, uint16_t v) { memcpy((void *)(uintptr_t)a, &v, 2); }
static inline void st32(uint64_t a, uint32_t v) { memcpy((void *)(uintptr_t)a, &v, 4); }
static inline void st64(uint64_t a, uint64_t v) { memcpy((void *)(uintptr_t)a, &v, 8); }

#include "yw4fp.h"

/* Vector FADD/FSUB/FMUL/FDIV on `count` lanes (the rest of the register zero), as the
 * per-lane f32_/f64_ helpers give it: all lanes at once with SSE, and only if a lane's
 * result is a NaN, every lane again through the helper (which applies ARM's NaN rules).
 * by_elem: m's lane `idx` for every lane (FMUL by element). */
#if defined(__x86_64__)
#define YW4_VFP_BINOP(name, ps, pd)                                                          \
    static inline v128 vf32_##name(v128 n, v128 m, int count) {                              \
        v128 r;                                                                              \
        __m128 z = ps(_mm_loadu_ps(n.f), _mm_loadu_ps(m.f));                                 \
        _mm_storeu_ps(r.f, z);                                                               \
        if (count == 2) r.d[1] = 0;                                                          \
        if (__builtin_expect(_mm_movemask_ps(_mm_cmpunord_ps(z, z)) & ((1 << count) - 1), 0)) \
            for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) r.s[i] = f32_##name(n.s[i], m.s[i]);             \
        return r;                                                                            \
    }                                                                                        \
    static inline v128 vf32_##name##_elem(v128 n, uint32_t k, int count) {                   \
        v128 m;                                                                              \
        m.s[0] = m.s[1] = m.s[2] = m.s[3] = k;                                               \
        return vf32_##name(n, m, count);                                                     \
    }                                                                                        \
    static inline v128 vf64_##name(v128 n, v128 m) {                                         \
        v128 r;                                                                              \
        __m128d z = pd(_mm_loadu_pd(n.df), _mm_loadu_pd(m.df));                              \
        _mm_storeu_pd(r.df, z);                                                              \
        if (__builtin_expect(_mm_movemask_pd(_mm_cmpunord_pd(z, z)), 0))                     \
            for (int i = 0; i < 2; i++) r.d[i] = f64_##name(n.d[i], m.d[i]);                 \
        return r;                                                                            \
    }
YW4_VFP_BINOP(add, _mm_add_ps, _mm_add_pd)
YW4_VFP_BINOP(sub, _mm_sub_ps, _mm_sub_pd)
YW4_VFP_BINOP(mul, _mm_mul_ps, _mm_mul_pd)
YW4_VFP_BINOP(div, _mm_div_ps, _mm_div_pd)
#undef YW4_VFP_BINOP
#else
#define YW4_VFP_BINOP(name)                                                                  \
    static inline v128 vf32_##name(v128 n, v128 m, int count) {                              \
        v128 r = {{0}};                                                                      \
        for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) r.s[i] = f32_##name(n.s[i], m.s[i]);                 \
        return r;                                                                            \
    }                                                                                        \
    static inline v128 vf32_##name##_elem(v128 n, uint32_t k, int count) {                   \
        v128 r = {{0}};                                                                      \
        for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) r.s[i] = f32_##name(n.s[i], k);                      \
        return r;                                                                            \
    }                                                                                        \
    static inline v128 vf64_##name(v128 n, v128 m) {                                         \
        v128 r;                                                                              \
        for (int i = 0; i < 2; i++) r.d[i] = f64_##name(n.d[i], m.d[i]);                     \
        return r;                                                                            \
    }
YW4_VFP_BINOP(add)
YW4_VFP_BINOP(sub)
YW4_VFP_BINOP(mul)
YW4_VFP_BINOP(div)
#undef YW4_VFP_BINOP
#endif

#endif

```

`runtime/include/yw4fp.h`:

```h
/* Floating-point helpers with ARM semantics (Arm ARM pseudocode, FPCR = 0: round to nearest
 * even, no flush-to-zero, no default-NaN mode; decision 0008).
 *
 * Values are passed as raw bit patterns (uint32_t = single, uint64_t = double) so nothing
 * depends on how the host treats NaNs. For non-NaN inputs and results, IEEE arithmetic on
 * x86-64 SSE rounds exactly like ARM, so the plain C operation is used. NaNs differ: ARM
 * returns the first signalling NaN (quietened), else the first quiet NaN, else the default
 * NaN (positive), while x86 produces a negative "indefinite" NaN and picks NaN operands in
 * instruction-operand order. Every helper therefore fixes up NaN results explicitly.
 *
 * FPSR exception flags are not modelled (main never reads FPSR).
 * Build generated code with -ffp-contract=off and without -ffast-math.
 */
#ifndef YW4FP_H
#define YW4FP_H

#include <math.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <string.h>

/* Exact square root and fused multiply-add. Library sqrt()/fma() are not always correctly
 * rounded (MinGW's double versions are off by one ulp on hard cases; found by the Pi tests),
 * so use the CPU instructions: SSE2 sqrtsd and FMA3 vfmadd (x86-64 CPUs since 2013). */
#if defined(__x86_64__)
#include <immintrin.h>
static inline double yw4_sqrt(double x) { return _mm_cvtsd_f64(_mm_sqrt_sd(_mm_setzero_pd(), _mm_set_sd(x))); }
static inline float yw4_sqrtf(float x) { return _mm_cvtss_f32(_mm_sqrt_ss(_mm_set_ss(x))); }
__attribute__((target("fma"))) static inline double yw4_fma(double a, double b, double c) {
    return _mm_cvtsd_f64(_mm_fmadd_sd(_mm_set_sd(a), _mm_set_sd(b), _mm_set_sd(c)));
}
#else
static inline double yw4_sqrt(double x) { return __builtin_sqrt(x); }
static inline float yw4_sqrtf(float x) { return __builtin_sqrtf(x); }
static inline double yw4_fma(double a, double b, double c) { return __builtin_fma(a, b, c); }
#endif

static inline float f32_of(uint32_t b) { float f; memcpy(&f, &b, 4); return f; }
static inline double f64_of(uint64_t b) { double f; memcpy(&f, &b, 8); return f; }
static inline uint32_t bits_f32(float f) { uint32_t b; memcpy(&b, &f, 4); return b; }
static inline uint64_t bits_f64(double f) { uint64_t b; memcpy(&b, &f, 8); return b; }

#define F32_DEFAULT_NAN 0x7FC00000u
#define F64_DEFAULT_NAN 0x7FF8000000000000ull

static inline int f32_isnan(uint32_t a) { return (a & 0x7FFFFFFFu) > 0x7F800000u; }
static inline int f64_isnan(uint64_t a) { return (a & 0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFull) > 0x7FF0000000000000ull; }
static inline int f32_issnan(uint32_t a) { return f32_isnan(a) && !(a & 0x00400000u); }
static inline int f64_issnan(uint64_t a) { return f64_isnan(a) && !(a & 0x0008000000000000ull); }

/* FPProcessNaNs for two operands. Returns 1 and sets *r if either is a NaN. */
static inline int f32_nans2(uint32_t a, uint32_t b, uint32_t *r) {
    if (f32_issnan(a)) { *r = a | 0x00400000u; return 1; }
    if (f32_issnan(b)) { *r = b | 0x00400000u; return 1; }
    if (f32_isnan(a)) { *r = a; return 1; }
    if (f32_isnan(b)) { *r = b; return 1; }
    return 0;
}
static inline int f64_nans2(uint64_t a, uint64_t b, uint64_t *r) {
    if (f64_issnan(a)) { *r = a | 0x0008000000000000ull; return 1; }
    if (f64_issnan(b)) { *r = b | 0x0008000000000000ull; return 1; }
    if (f64_isnan(a)) { *r = a; return 1; }
    if (f64_isnan(b)) { *r = b; return 1; }
    return 0;
}

/* Two-operand arithmetic: the host operation first. A NaN operand always gives a NaN
 * result, so a non-NaN result is final and the NaN rules only run when the result is a NaN:
 * NaN operands as ARM picks them, else (inf - inf, 0 * inf, 0 / 0, ...) the default NaN. */
#define YW4_FP_BINOP(name, op)                                                       \
    static inline uint32_t f32_##name(uint32_t a, uint32_t b) {                      \
        uint32_t r = bits_f32(f32_of(a) op f32_of(b));                               \
        if (__builtin_expect(!f32_isnan(r), 1)) return r;                            \
        return f32_nans2(a, b, &r) ? r : F32_DEFAULT_NAN;                            \
    }                                                                                \
    static inline uint64_t f64_##name(uint64_t a, uint64_t b) {                      \
        uint64_t r = bits_f64(f64_of(a) op f64_of(b));                               \
        if (__builtin_expect(!f64_isnan(r), 1)) return r;                            \
        return f64_nans2(a, b, &r) ? r : F64_DEFAULT_NAN;                            \
    }
YW4_FP_BINOP(add, +)
YW4_FP_BINOP(sub, -)
YW4_FP_BINOP(mul, *)
YW4_FP_BINOP(div, /)
#undef YW4_FP_BINOP

static inline uint32_t f32_sqrt(uint32_t a) {
    if (f32_isnan(a)) return f32_issnan(a) ? a | 0x00400000u : a;
    uint32_t r = bits_f32(yw4_sqrtf(f32_of(a)));
    return f32_isnan(r) ? F32_DEFAULT_NAN : r;
}
static inline uint64_t f64_sqrt(uint64_t a) {
    if (f64_isnan(a)) return f64_issnan(a) ? a | 0x0008000000000000ull : a;
    uint64_t r = bits_f64(yw4_sqrt(f64_of(a)));
    return f64_isnan(r) ? F64_DEFAULT_NAN : r;
}

/* FMAX/FMIN: NaNs propagate; max(+0, -0) = +0 and min(+0, -0) = -0. */
static inline uint32_t f32_max(uint32_t a, uint32_t b) {
    uint32_t r;
    if (f32_nans2(a, b, &r)) return r;
    float x = f32_of(a), y = f32_of(b);
    if (x == y) return a & b;  /* equal: only zeros can differ, and then only in sign */
    return x > y ? a : b;
}
static inline uint32_t f32_min(uint32_t a, uint32_t b) {
    uint32_t r;
    if (f32_nans2(a, b, &r)) return r;
    float x = f32_of(a), y = f32_of(b);
    if (x == y) return a | b;
    return x < y ? a : b;
}
static inline uint64_t f64_max(uint64_t a, uint64_t b) {
    uint64_t r;
    if (f64_nans2(a, b, &r)) return r;
    double x = f64_of(a), y = f64_of(b);
    if (x == y) return a & b;
    return x > y ? a : b;
}
static inline uint64_t f64_min(uint64_t a, uint64_t b) {
    uint64_t r;
    if (f64_nans2(a, b, &r)) return r;
    double x = f64_of(a), y = f64_of(b);
    if (x == y) return a | b;
    return x < y ? a : b;
}

/* FMAXNM/FMINNM: a single quiet NaN is ignored (the number wins); otherwise as FMAX/FMIN. */
static inline uint32_t f32_maxnm(uint32_t a, uint32_t b) {
    if (f32_isnan(a) && !f32_issnan(a) && !f32_isnan(b)) return b;
    if (f32_isnan(b) && !f32_issnan(b) && !f32_isnan(a)) return a;
    return f32_max(a, b);
}
static inline uint32_t f32_minnm(uint32_t a, uint32_t b) {
    if (f32_isnan(a) && !f32_issnan(a) && !f32_isnan(b)) return b;
    if (f32_isnan(b) && !f32_issnan(b) && !f32_isnan(a)) return a;
    return f32_min(a, b);
}
static inline uint64_t f64_maxnm(uint64_t a, uint64_t b) {
    if (f64_isnan(a) && !f64_issnan(a) && !f64_isnan(b)) return b;
    if (f64_isnan(b) && !f64_issnan(b) && !f64_isnan(a)) return a;
    return f64_max(a, b);
}
static inline uint64_t f64_minnm(uint64_t a, uint64_t b) {
    if (f64_isnan(a) && !f64_issnan(a) && !f64_isnan(b)) return b;
    if (f64_isnan(b) && !f64_issnan(b) && !f64_isnan(a)) return a;
    return f64_min(a, b);
}

/* FCMP/FCMPE: NZCV = 0011 unordered, 0110 equal, 1000 less, 0010 greater. */
static inline uint64_t f32_cmp(uint32_t a, uint32_t b) {
    if (f32_isnan(a) || f32_isnan(b)) return 0x30000000u;
    float x = f32_of(a), y = f32_of(b);
    return x == y ? 0x60000000u : x < y ? 0x80000000u : 0x20000000u;
}
static inline uint64_t f64_cmp(uint64_t a, uint64_t b) {
    if (f64_isnan(a) || f64_isnan(b)) return 0x30000000u;
    double x = f64_of(a), y = f64_of(b);
    return x == y ? 0x60000000u : x < y ? 0x80000000u : 0x20000000u;
}

/* FCVT between single and double. NaNs keep sign and the top payload bits, and are quietened. */
static inline uint64_t f32_to_f64(uint32_t a) {
    if (f32_isnan(a))
        return (uint64_t)(a >> 31) << 63 | 0x7FF8000000000000ull | (uint64_t)(a & 0x003FFFFFu) << 29;
    return bits_f64((double)f32_of(a));
}
static inline uint32_t f64_to_f32(uint64_t a) {
    if (f64_isnan(a))
        return (uint32_t)(a >> 63) << 31 | 0x7FC00000u | (uint32_t)((a >> 29) & 0x003FFFFFu);
    return bits_f32((float)f64_of(a));
}

/* Round to an integral value in a mode: 'n' nearest even, 'a' nearest away from zero,
 * 'p' toward +inf, 'm' toward -inf, 'z' toward zero. Written out instead of using libm
 * (MinGW's round() gets 0.49999997 wrong; found by the Pi tests). Exact: x - trunc(x)
 * is always representable, and the sign of zero results is kept. */
static inline double yw4_round(double x, char mode) {
    if (!(__builtin_fabs(x) < 4503599627370496.0)) return x;  /* NaN, inf, or already integral (>= 2^52) */
    double t = __builtin_copysign((double)(int64_t)x, x);
    double frac = x - t, one = __builtin_copysign(1.0, x);
    switch (mode) {
    case 'n':
        if (__builtin_fabs(frac) > 0.5 || (__builtin_fabs(frac) == 0.5 && ((int64_t)t & 1))) t += one;
        break;
    case 'a':
        if (__builtin_fabs(frac) >= 0.5) t += one;
        break;
    case 'p':
        if (frac > 0) t += 1.0;
        break;
    case 'm':
        if (frac < 0) t -= 1.0;
        break;
    default:
        break;
    }
    return t;
}

/* FRECPS / FRSQRTS: 2 - a*b and (3 - a*b) / 2, fused (one rounding). The NaN rules see -a.
 *
 * Single precision: a float product is exact in double, but c + product is not, and
 * rounding that sum to double and then to float can round twice wrongly (seen on the Pi:
 * when c is far below the product's last bit, the double sum drops it and the float
 * rounding becomes a false tie). yw4_add_odd() therefore rounds the double sum *to odd*:
 * TwoSum gives the exact error, and a nonzero error forces the last bit to 1. Rounding a
 * round-to-odd double (53 bits >= 24 + 2) to float gives the correctly rounded result. */
static inline double yw4_add_odd(double x, double y) {
    double s = x + y;
    if (__builtin_isinf(s)) return s;
    double bb = s - x, err = (x - (s - bb)) + (y - bb);  /* TwoSum: s + err == x + y exactly */
    uint64_t u = bits_f64(s);
    if (err != 0 && !(u & 1)) u += ((err > 0) == (s > 0)) ? 1 : -1;  /* step away from / toward zero */
    return f64_of(u);
}
/* Special cases shared by the step functions: 1 and *r set if they decide the result.
 * `a` is already negated. */
static inline int f32_step_special(uint32_t a, uint32_t b, uint32_t inf_times_zero, uint32_t *r) {
    if (f32_nans2(a, b, r)) return 1;
    int infa = (a & 0x7FFFFFFFu) == 0x7F800000u, infb = (b & 0x7FFFFFFFu) == 0x7F800000u;
    int zeroa = !(a & 0x7FFFFFFFu), zerob = !(b & 0x7FFFFFFFu);
    if ((infa && zerob) || (zeroa && infb)) { *r = inf_times_zero; return 1; }
    if (infa || infb) { *r = ((a ^ b) & 0x80000000u) | 0x7F800000u; return 1; }
    return 0;
}
static inline int f64_step_special(uint64_t a, uint64_t b, uint64_t inf_times_zero, uint64_t *r) {
    const uint64_t mag = 0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFull, inf = 0x7FF0000000000000ull;
    if (f64_nans2(a, b, r)) return 1;
    int infa = (a & mag) == inf, infb = (b & mag) == inf, zeroa = !(a & mag), zerob = !(b & mag);
    if ((infa && zerob) || (zeroa && infb)) { *r = inf_times_zero; return 1; }
    if (infa || infb) { *r = ((a ^ b) & ~mag) | inf; return 1; }
    return 0;
}
static inline uint32_t f32_recps(uint32_t a, uint32_t b) {
    uint32_t r;
    a ^= 0x80000000u;
    if (f32_step_special(a, b, 0x40000000u, &r)) return r;  /* 2.0 */
    return bits_f32((float)yw4_add_odd(2.0, (double)f32_of(a) * (double)f32_of(b)));
}
static inline uint32_t f32_rsqrts(uint32_t a, uint32_t b) {
    uint32_t r;
    a ^= 0x80000000u;
    if (f32_step_special(a, b, 0x3FC00000u, &r)) return r;  /* 1.5 */
    return bits_f32((float)(yw4_add_odd(3.0, (double)f32_of(a) * (double)f32_of(b)) / 2.0));  /* halving is exact */
}
static inline uint64_t f64_recps(uint64_t a, uint64_t b) {
    uint64_t r;
    a ^= 0x8000000000000000ull;
    if (f64_step_special(a, b, 0x4000000000000000ull, &r)) return r;
    return bits_f64(yw4_fma(f64_of(a), f64_of(b), 2.0));
}
static inline uint64_t f64_rsqrts(uint64_t a, uint64_t b) {
    /* Rounds 3 - a*b, then halves: differs from ARM only if the result is subnormal. */
    uint64_t r;
    a ^= 0x8000000000000000ull;
    if (f64_step_special(a, b, 0x3FF8000000000000ull, &r)) return r;
    return bits_f64(yw4_fma(f64_of(a), f64_of(b), 3.0) * 0.5);
}

/* FMADD/FMLA: FPMulAdd(addend, op1, op2) = addend + op1*op2 with one rounding. Callers
 * negate operands first for FMSUB/FNMADD/FNMSUB/FMLS, as the pseudocode does (a NaN's sign
 * flips too). NaNs: signalling before quiet, in the order addend, op1, op2; a quiet-NaN
 * addend with inf*0 gives the default NaN. Single precision: the product is exact in
 * double, then one round-to-odd add (see yw4_add_odd), then rounding to float. */
static inline int f32_nans3(uint32_t a, uint32_t b, uint32_t c, uint32_t *r) {
    if (f32_issnan(a)) { *r = a | 0x00400000u; return 1; }
    if (f32_issnan(b)) { *r = b | 0x00400000u; return 1; }
    if (f32_issnan(c)) { *r = c | 0x00400000u; return 1; }
    if (f32_isnan(a)) { *r = a; return 1; }
    if (f32_isnan(b)) { *r = b; return 1; }
    if (f32_isnan(c)) { *r = c; return 1; }
    return 0;
}
static inline int f64_nans3(uint64_t a, uint64_t b, uint64_t c, uint64_t *r) {
    if (f64_issnan(a)) { *r = a | 0x0008000000000000ull; return 1; }
    if (f64_issnan(b)) { *r = b | 0x0008000000000000ull; return 1; }
    if (f64_issnan(c)) { *r = c | 0x0008000000000000ull; return 1; }
    if (f64_isnan(a)) { *r = a; return 1; }
    if (f64_isnan(b)) { *r = b; return 1; }
    if (f64_isnan(c)) { *r = c; return 1; }
    return 0;
}
static inline uint32_t f32_muladd(uint32_t a, uint32_t n, uint32_t m) {
    uint32_t r;
    int inf_n = (n & 0x7FFFFFFFu) == 0x7F800000u, inf_m = (m & 0x7FFFFFFFu) == 0x7F800000u;
    int zero_n = !(n & 0x7FFFFFFFu), zero_m = !(m & 0x7FFFFFFFu);
    int done = f32_nans3(a, n, m, &r);
    if (f32_isnan(a) && !f32_issnan(a) && ((inf_n && zero_m) || (zero_n && inf_m))) return F32_DEFAULT_NAN;
    if (done) return r;
    r = bits_f32((float)yw4_add_odd((double)f32_of(a), (double)f32_of(n) * (double)f32_of(m)));
    return f32_isnan(r) ? F32_DEFAULT_NAN : r;
}
static inline uint64_t f64_muladd(uint64_t a, uint64_t n, uint64_t m) {
    const uint64_t mag = 0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFull, inf = 0x7FF0000000000000ull;
    uint64_t r;
    int inf_n = (n & mag) == inf, inf_m = (m & mag) == inf, zero_n = !(n & mag), zero_m = !(m & mag);
    int done = f64_nans3(a, n, m, &r);
    if (f64_isnan(a) && !f64_issnan(a) && ((inf_n && zero_m) || (zero_n && inf_m))) return F64_DEFAULT_NAN;
    if (done) return r;
    r = bits_f64(yw4_fma(f64_of(n), f64_of(m), f64_of(a)));
    return f64_isnan(r) ? F64_DEFAULT_NAN : r;
}

/* FRECPE / FRSQRTE: 8-bit estimates from the Arm ARM tables (RecipEstimate,
 * RecipSqrtEstimate), on a 52-bit fraction like the pseudocode. */
#define YW4_M52 0x000FFFFFFFFFFFFFull
static inline uint32_t yw4_recip_estimate(uint32_t a) {
    a = a * 2 + 1;
    uint32_t b = (1u << 19) / a;
    return (b + 1) / 2;
}
static inline uint32_t yw4_rsqrt_estimate(uint32_t a) {
    if (a < 256) {
        a = a * 2 + 1;
    } else {
        a = (a >> 1) << 1;
        a = (a + 1) * 2;
    }
    uint32_t b = 512;
    while ((uint64_t)a * (b + 1) * (b + 1) < (1ull << 28)) b++;
    return (b + 1) / 2;
}
/* Shared core. bias = 127 or 1023; mant_bits = 23 or 52; returns (sign-less) exponent and
 * the 52-bit result fraction. */
static inline void yw4_recpe_core(int exp, uint64_t frac, int bias, int *rexp, uint64_t *rfrac) {
    if (exp == 0) {
        if (!(frac >> 51 & 1)) { exp = -1; frac = (frac << 2) & YW4_M52; }
        else frac = (frac << 1) & YW4_M52;
    }
    uint32_t scaled = 0x100 | (uint32_t)(frac >> 44);
    int e = 2 * bias - 1 - exp;
    uint64_t f = (uint64_t)(yw4_recip_estimate(scaled) & 0xFF) << 44;
    if (e == 0) f = 1ull << 51 | f >> 1;
    else if (e == -1) { f = 1ull << 50 | f >> 2; e = 0; }
    *rexp = e;
    *rfrac = f;
}
static inline void yw4_rsqrte_core(int exp, uint64_t frac, int bias, int *rexp, uint64_t *rfrac) {
    if (exp == 0) {
        while (!(frac >> 51 & 1)) { frac = (frac << 1) & YW4_M52; exp--; }
        frac = (frac << 1) & YW4_M52;
    }
    uint32_t scaled = (exp & 1) == 0 ? 0x100 | (uint32_t)(frac >> 44) : 0x80 | (uint32_t)(frac >> 45);
    *rexp = (3 * bias - 1 - exp) / 2;
    *rfrac = (uint64_t)(yw4_rsqrt_estimate(scaled) & 0xFF) << 44;
}
static inline uint32_t f32_recpe(uint32_t a) {
    uint32_t sign = a & 0x80000000u, mag = a & 0x7FFFFFFFu;
    if (f32_isnan(a)) return a | 0x00400000u;
    if (mag == 0x7F800000u) return sign;
    if (mag < 0x00200000u) return sign | 0x7F800000u;  /* 0 or below 2^-128: the result overflows */
    int e;
    uint64_t f;
    yw4_recpe_core((int)(mag >> 23), (uint64_t)(mag & 0x7FFFFF) << 29, 127, &e, &f);
    return sign | (uint32_t)(e & 0xFF) << 23 | (uint32_t)(f >> 29);
}
static inline uint64_t f64_recpe(uint64_t a) {
    uint64_t sign = a & 0x8000000000000000ull, mag = a & 0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFull;
    if (f64_isnan(a)) return a | 0x0008000000000000ull;
    if (mag == 0x7FF0000000000000ull) return sign;
    if (mag < 0x0004000000000000ull) return sign | 0x7FF0000000000000ull;  /* below 2^-1024 */
    int e;
    uint64_t f;
    yw4_recpe_core((int)(mag >> 52), mag & YW4_M52, 1023, &e, &f);
    return sign | (uint64_t)(e & 0x7FF) << 52 | f;
}
static inline uint32_t f32_rsqrte(uint32_t a) {
    uint32_t mag = a & 0x7FFFFFFFu;
    if (f32_isnan(a)) return a | 0x00400000u;
    if (mag == 0) return a | 0x7F800000u;            /* +-0 -> +-inf */
    if (a >> 31) return F32_DEFAULT_NAN;             /* negative */
    if (mag == 0x7F800000u) return 0;
    int e;
    uint64_t f;
    yw4_rsqrte_core((int)(mag >> 23), (uint64_t)(mag & 0x7FFFFF) << 29, 127, &e, &f);
    return (uint32_t)(e & 0xFF) << 23 | (uint32_t)(f >> 29);
}
static inline uint64_t f64_rsqrte(uint64_t a) {
    uint64_t mag = a & 0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFull;
    if (f64_isnan(a)) return a | 0x0008000000000000ull;
    if (mag == 0) return a | 0x7FF0000000000000ull;
    if (a >> 63) return F64_DEFAULT_NAN;
    if (mag == 0x7FF0000000000000ull) return 0;
    int e;
    uint64_t f;
    yw4_rsqrte_core((int)(mag >> 52), mag & YW4_M52, 1023, &e, &f);
    return (uint64_t)(e & 0x7FF) << 52 | f;
}

/* FRINT*: round to an integral value in the same format (signs of zero kept, NaNs quietened). */
static inline uint32_t f32_rint(uint32_t a, char mode) {
    if (f32_isnan(a)) return a | 0x00400000u;
    return bits_f32((float)yw4_round((double)f32_of(a), mode));  /* exact both ways */
}
static inline uint64_t f64_rint(uint64_t a, char mode) {
    if (f64_isnan(a)) return a | 0x0008000000000000ull;
    return bits_f64(yw4_round(f64_of(a), mode));
}

/* Float -> integer with a rounding mode (see yw4_round), saturating; NaN converts to 0
 * (FPToFixed). */
static inline int64_t yw4_to_s64(double x, char mode) {
    if (x != x) return 0;
    x = yw4_round(x, mode);
    if (x >= 9223372036854775808.0) return INT64_MAX;
    if (x < -9223372036854775808.0) return INT64_MIN;
    return (int64_t)x;
}
static inline uint64_t yw4_to_u64(double x, char mode) {
    if (x != x) return 0;
    x = yw4_round(x, mode);
    if (x >= 18446744073709551616.0) return UINT64_MAX;
    if (x <= 0) return 0;
    return (uint64_t)x;
}
static inline int32_t yw4_to_s32(double x, char mode) {
    if (x != x) return 0;
    x = yw4_round(x, mode);
    if (x >= 2147483648.0) return INT32_MAX;
    if (x < -2147483648.0) return INT32_MIN;
    return (int32_t)x;
}
static inline uint32_t yw4_to_u32(double x, char mode) {
    if (x != x) return 0;
    x = yw4_round(x, mode);
    if (x >= 4294967296.0) return UINT32_MAX;
    if (x <= 0) return 0;
    return (uint32_t)x;
}

#endif
```

`runtime/include/yw4load.h`:

```h
/* Loading the recompiled modules into host memory (decisions 0010, 0014).
 *
 * The tables below are generated by recomp.translate (work/recomp/image_info.c) from the
 * owner's main and sdk; the image bytes themselves are read from disk at start-up, never
 * built in. Symbols are already resolved at translation time (load order main, sdk).
 */
#ifndef YW4LOAD_H
#define YW4LOAD_H

#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#include "yw4rt.h"

/* R_AARCH64_RELATIVE: *(base + offset) = base + addend */
typedef struct {
    uint64_t offset;
    int64_t addend;
} Yw4Relative;

/* ABS64 / GLOB_DAT / JUMP_SLOT, resolved: *(base + offset) = base of `module` + value,
 * or 0 for module = YW4_NO_MODULE (weak symbols nobody defines). */
typedef struct {
    uint64_t offset;
    uint32_t module;
    uint64_t value;
} Yw4SymReloc;

enum { YW4_MAIN = 0, YW4_SDK = 1, YW4_NO_MODULE = 0xFFFFFFFFu };

typedef struct {
    const char *name;
    const char *file;           /* in the exefs work directory */
    const char *sha256;         /* of the flat image: the version lock */
    uint64_t file_size, mem_size, preferred_base;
    uint64_t *base;             /* set by the loader */
    const Yw4Relative *relative;
    size_t nrelative;
    const Yw4SymReloc *symrelocs;
    size_t nsymrelocs;
    uint64_t dt_init;           /* offset of DT_INIT (registers the module, runs its constructors) */
    uint64_t ro_offset, data_offset;  /* .text is [0, ro), .rodata [ro, data), .data + .bss [data, mem_size) */
} Yw4Module;

/* Generated */
extern const Yw4Module yw4_modules[];
extern const size_t yw4_nmodules;
extern const uint64_t yw4_entry_init_start;  /* sdk offset of nn::init::Start */
extern const uint64_t yw4_main_stack_size;    /* from the NPDM */
extern const uint32_t yw4_main_priority;

/* Guest functions native code calls by name (recomp/overrides.toml [[guest_symbol]]). */
typedef struct {
    const char *name;
    uint32_t module;
    uint64_t offset;
} Yw4GuestSymbol;
extern const Yw4GuestSymbol yw4_guest_symbols[];
extern const size_t yw4_nguest_symbols;
/* The guest address of one of them; stops if it isn't listed. */
uint64_t yw4_guest_symbol(const char *name);

/* Runtime: the guest address space (decision 0014), all inside the 39-bit space games may
 * assume. The kernel reports these regions through svcGetInfo. */
#define YW4_GUEST_LO 0x7000000000ull
#define YW4_GUEST_HI 0x7800000000ull
#define YW4_STACK_BASE 0x7000000000ull      /* guest stacks */
#define YW4_STACK_SIZE 0x0040000000ull
#define YW4_TLR_BASE 0x7040000000ull        /* thread-local regions (TPIDRRO_EL0) */
#define YW4_TLR_SIZE 0x0000100000ull        /* 256 threads * 4 KiB */
#define YW4_HOST_FN_BASE 0x7080000000ull    /* guest addresses of host callbacks */
#define YW4_HEAP_BASE 0x7200000000ull       /* svcSetHeapSize: reserved, committed as it grows */
#define YW4_HEAP_SIZE 0x0180000000ull
#define YW4_ALIAS_BASE 0x7400000000ull      /* svcMapMemory targets */
#define YW4_ALIAS_SIZE 0x0100000000ull

/* Reserves the 32 GiB guest address space (0x7000000000 - 0x7800000000) early:
 * heap with write tracking, thread-local regions, and all gaps between them. 0 on success. */
int yw4_guest_memory_init(void);

/* Zeroed read/write memory, at `want` if that range is free (0 = anywhere), else anywhere. */
void *yw4_reserve(uint64_t want, size_t size);
/* Address space only, at exactly `want` (NULL if taken); yw4_commit makes parts of it
 * usable (zeroed), yw4_decommit gives memory back. */
void *yw4_reserve_range(uint64_t want, size_t size);
int yw4_commit(uint64_t addr, size_t size);
void yw4_reserve_free(uint64_t lo, uint64_t hi);  /* see loader.c */
void yw4_decommit(uint64_t addr, size_t size);
/* Changes at every yw4_decommit: answers that guest memory is mapped (gbuffer.c) hold while it stays the same. */
extern volatile uint32_t yw4_memory_generation;
/* 1: every page of [addr, addr + size) has guest memory (the runtime's own record, no system call); 0: not;
 * -1: outside the guest's range (ask host_readable). */
int yw4_guest_mapped(uint64_t addr, uint64_t size);
/* Sleeps the calling host thread (no-op for ns <= 0). */
void yw4_host_sleep_ns(int64_t ns);

/* Reads, verifies (size + SHA-256) and relocates every module from `exefs_dir`. Returns 0 on
 * success; prints why not. */
int yw4_load_modules(const char *exefs_dir);

/* A guest address that, when called, runs `fn` on the calling guest thread. */
uint64_t yw4_host_function(GuestFn fn);
/* The same, with a pointer `fn` gets back from yw4_host_data(): one host function can then
 * stand behind many addresses. Read it first thing, before calling any guest code. */
uint64_t yw4_host_function_data(GuestFn fn, void *data);
void *yw4_host_data(void);

/* SHA-256 of a buffer as 64 lowercase hex digits + NUL. */
void yw4_sha256_hex(const uint8_t *data, size_t len, char out[65]);
/* The same in pieces, for files too big to hold at once (add-on NCAs, svc_misc.c): init, update with each chunk
 * in order, then final writes the hex digest. */
typedef struct {
    uint32_t h[8];
    uint64_t len;     /* bytes so far */
    uint8_t buf[64];  /* the start of a block not yet full */
} Yw4Sha256;
void yw4_sha256_init(Yw4Sha256 *c);
void yw4_sha256_update(Yw4Sha256 *c, const uint8_t *data, size_t len);
void yw4_sha256_final_hex(Yw4Sha256 *c, char out[65]);

#endif
```

`runtime/include/yw4rt.h`:

```h
/* What generated code needs from the runtime besides the CPU helpers in yw4cpu.h.
 *
 * Every guest function is `void f_<offset>(CPUState *ctx)` (decision 0007).
 */
#ifndef YW4RT_H
#define YW4RT_H

#include <setjmp.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#include "yw4cpu.h"

typedef void (*GuestFn)(CPUState *ctx);

/* Host addresses of the recompiled modules: main and the sdk (decision 0014). Guest
 * addresses are host addresses (decision 0005), so PC-relative values and return addresses
 * are module offsets plus these. Must be 4 KiB aligned, because ADRP results are computed
 * at translation time from page offsets. */
extern uint64_t yw4_image_base;
extern uint64_t yw4_sdk_base;

/* The recompiler's tables of every translated function, one per module, sorted by offset
 * (generated func_table.c). */
typedef struct {
    uint64_t offset;
    GuestFn fn;
} FuncEntry;
typedef struct {
    const char *name;
    const uint64_t *base;   /* where the module was loaded */
    uint64_t size;          /* image + .bss */
    const FuncEntry *funcs;
    size_t nfuncs;
} Yw4CodeModule;
extern const Yw4CodeModule yw4_code[];
extern const size_t yw4_ncode;

/* "main+0x1234", "sdk+0x56" or the raw address, for messages. Returns buf. */
const char *yw4_describe(uint64_t addr, char buf[48]);

/* Function at a guest address, or NULL. */
GuestFn yw4_lookup(uint64_t addr);

/* Probes (dispatch.c): every recompiled function starts with
 * `if (yw4_probe_any) yw4_probe(ctx, entry)`; YW4_PROBE lists the functions to log. */
extern int yw4_probe_any;
void yw4_probe(CPUState *ctx, uint64_t addr);
void yw4_probe_init(void);  /* after the modules are loaded */
void yw4_watch_init(void);  /* YW4_WATCH data watch, uses the probes */

/* Optional extra lookup tried first (the loader uses it for import stub addresses). */
extern GuestFn (*yw4_lookup_hook)(uint64_t addr);

/* Function at a guest address for an indirect call or tail call (BLR, BR).
 * Traps if no translated function starts there. */
GuestFn yw4_resolve(uint64_t target);

/* The same as a record that never changes or moves, one per target: each indirect call site
 * keeps a pointer to the last one it used (a single pointer, so threads can't see it torn)
 * and only asks again when the target differs. */
typedef struct {
    uint64_t addr;
    GuestFn fn;
} Yw4Target;
const Yw4Target *yw4_resolve_target(uint64_t target);
#define YW4_TARGET(t, c_)                                                          \
    static const Yw4Target *cs_;                                                   \
    const Yw4Target *c_ = __atomic_load_n(&cs_, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);                 \
    if (__builtin_expect(!c_ || c_->addr != (t), 0)) {                             \
        c_ = yw4_resolve_target(t);                                                \
        __atomic_store_n(&cs_, c_, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);                              \
    }

/* setjmp in recompiled code (decision 0018, runtime/src/setjmp.c): the translator puts a
 * host setjmp(jb) (the C library's, not __builtin_setjmp: see 0018) at each call to the
 * guest's setjmp and registers it here, so the guest longjmp's branch to `ret` can come
 * back into this frame. yw4_resolve calls yw4_setjmp_resume on a miss; it does not return
 * if `target` is a registered point. */
void yw4_setjmp_register(CPUState *ctx, uint64_t ret, jmp_buf jb);
void yw4_setjmp_resume(uint64_t target);

/* An instruction the recompiler can't translate yet, or a guest trap (UDF/BRK). */
_Noreturn void yw4_unimplemented(CPUState *ctx, uint64_t pc, uint32_t enc);
_Noreturn void yw4_guest_trap(CPUState *ctx, uint64_t pc, uint32_t enc);

/* System instructions (decision 0014, runtime/src/kernel.c): SVC #imm, the system counter
 * (CNTPCT_EL0, 19.2 MHz as on the Switch), and writes to FPCR (only the default mode is
 * supported, decision 0008). */
void yw4_svc(CPUState *ctx, uint32_t imm);
uint64_t yw4_cntpct(void);
void yw4_msr_fpcr(CPUState *ctx, uint64_t value);

/* Tail call to another guest function. Clang guarantees no host stack growth with musttail,
 * which matters for loops that go through tail calls; other compilers usually optimise the
 * plain call+return to a jump at -O2 but don't promise it. */
#if defined(__clang__)
/* Wrapped in a block: right after a label, a bare attribute would attach to a declaration. */
#define TAILCALL(f) do { __attribute__((musttail)) return f(ctx); } while (0)
#define TAILCALL_INDIRECT(t) do { uint64_t t_ = (t); YW4_TARGET(t_, c_) __attribute__((musttail)) return c_->fn(ctx); } while (0)
#else
#define TAILCALL(f) do { f(ctx); return; } while (0)
#define TAILCALL_INDIRECT(t) do { uint64_t t_ = (t); YW4_TARGET(t_, c_) c_->fn(ctx); return; } while (0)
#endif

#endif

```

`runtime/shaders/aa.glsl`:

```glsl
// Shared by the anti-aliasing pass (runtime/src/gpu_aa.c): the target's size, and the curve between the
// game's linear HDR colour and the perceptual one the edge detection and blending work on (reversible).
// params (TAA): history valid, debug view, motion scale x, y
layout(push_constant) uniform AaPush { vec4 metrics; vec4 params; } aa;  // metrics: 1/w, 1/h, w, h

vec3 aa_encode(vec3 c) { c = max(c, vec3(0.0)); return sqrt(c / (1.0 + c)); }
vec3 aa_decode(vec3 e) { e = clamp(e, vec3(0.0), vec3(0.999)); e *= e; return e / (1.0 - e); }

```

`runtime/shaders/aa_depth_upscale.frag`:

```frag
#version 460
// Upscaling (runtime/src/gpu_aa.c): the 3D's depth, stretched into the output-sized depth image, so the draws
// after the anti-aliasing point (the UI, and world markers such as the "!" above people, which the game hides
// behind what stands in front) test against it as before. Nearest texel: depths don't blend.
layout(set = 0, binding = 0) uniform sampler2D depth;
layout(location = 0) in vec2 v_uv;

void main() {
    ivec2 size = textureSize(depth, 0);
    gl_FragDepth = texelFetch(depth, clamp(ivec2(v_uv * vec2(size)), ivec2(0), size - 1), 0).r;
}
```

`runtime/shaders/aa_test.frag`:

```frag
#version 460
#extension GL_GOOGLE_include_directive : require
// Anti-aliasing self-test (YW4_AA_DEBUG=3, runtime/src/gpu_aa.c): in place of the scene, hard-edged stripes at
// shallow angles (about 5 degrees in the upper half, 20 in the lower), grey on black, already in the perceptual
// curve. Working SMAA or FXAA turns their staircases into ramps.

    float slope = p.y < 0.5 * aa.metrics.w ? 0.09 : 0.36;
```
