`runtime/shaders/shadow_mask.frag`:

```frag
#version 460
#extension GL_KHR_shader_subgroup_quad : require
#extension GL_EXT_texture_shadow_lod : require
// Our version of the shadow mask's fragment program 06d03ad7 (docs/frame.md "Lighting stage"): per
// half-size pixel, how much of the sun reaches the surface there, from the cascaded shadow maps.
// Same interface as the game's program (with the soft shadows of decision 0025 in it, as the
// translated one has them). Every operation is in the game's order (fma where it fuses), so the
// result is bit-identical to it; names are what the values seem to be.
//
// Inputs:
//   constants 8 (view: rows 20-23 the inverse projection, row 31 .zw the tap spread in map units),
//   12 (sun shadow: row 0 the light direction in view space, row 2 the depth bias (x constant, y
//   slope, z largest), row 3 .xy near and far for the fade, row 4+c .xy cascade c's tap spread,
//   row 7+c the cascade's range (.y its far end, row 8+c .x the next one's start), rows 10+4c..12+4c
//   view to light view, rows 22+4c..25+4c light view to map, rows 34+4c..37+4c view to map for the
//   centre lookup and the texel grid)
//   textures: 0 the G-buffer normal (rgb × 2 − 1), 1 the half-size depth, 15 the cascades' shadow
//   maps (a depth compare; its raw depth for the soft shadows' blocker search)
// Output: x how much is in shadow (1 in shadow, 0 lit: the map compare gives 1 where something is nearer the
// sun), faded out toward the far end; y and z the linear depth; w 0. With no cascade at this depth: (0, 1, 0, 0),
// no shadow.

layout(set = 1, binding = 8, std140) uniform View { vec4 d[4096]; } view;
layout(set = 1, binding = 12, std140) uniform Sun { vec4 d[4096]; } sun;
layout(set = 1, binding = 16) uniform sampler2D gbuffer_normal;
layout(set = 1, binding = 17) uniform sampler2D half_depth;
layout(set = 1, binding = 31) uniform sampler2DArrayShadow shadow_maps;
layout(set = 1, binding = 111) uniform sampler2DArray shadow_depth;  // the same maps' raw depth
// contact (ours, only this program reads it): steps (0 off), ray length and thickness in view units, debug
layout(set = 1, binding = 95, std140) uniform YW4PCSS { vec4 mode; vec4 scale; vec4 tune; vec4 contact; } yw4_pcss;

layout(location = 3) in vec4 v_uv;

layout(location = 0) out vec4 o_mask;

// yw4_shadow: one shadow map compare, soft (PCSS) or the game's. The same text recomp/shader.py
// (PCSS_COMMON, pcss_helper("SHADOWARRAY2D")) puts into the translated program: keep the two alike. Ours only:
// the blocker search takes every other tap (8 of 16: as good, 0.3-0.7 ms less at 4K); mode.y bit 2 filters with every other tap,
// the disk turned a golden angle each frame (bits 3 up: the frame mod 256), for the anti-aliasing's frame
// blending to average (SOFT SHADOW SAMPLES).
const vec2 YW4_DISK[16] = vec2[16](
    vec2(-0.94201624, -0.39906216), vec2(0.94558609, -0.76890725), vec2(-0.09418410, -0.92938870),
    vec2(0.34495938, 0.29387760), vec2(-0.91588581, 0.45771432), vec2(-0.81544232, -0.87912464),
    vec2(-0.38277543, 0.27676845), vec2(0.97484398, 0.75648379), vec2(0.44323325, -0.97511554),
    vec2(0.53742981, -0.47373420), vec2(-0.26496911, -0.41893023), vec2(0.79197514, 0.19090188),
    vec2(-0.24188840, 0.99706507), vec2(-0.81409955, 0.91437590), vec2(0.19984126, 0.78641367),
    vec2(0.14383161, -0.14100790));
vec2 yw4_seen_key[2];
float yw4_seen_lit[2];
int yw4_seen_n = 0;
float yw4_search_layer = -1.0, yw4_search_r = -1.0;
mat2 yw4_pcss_rotation() {
    vec2 cell = floor(gl_FragCoord.xy / max(yw4_pcss.tune.w, 1.0));
    float a = 6.2831853 * fract(52.9829189 * fract(dot(cell, vec2(0.06711056, 0.00583715))));
    int m = int(yw4_pcss.mode.y);
    if ((m & 4) != 0) a += 2.39996323 * float(m >> 3);  // ours: turned a golden angle each frame
    return mat2(cos(a), sin(a), -sin(a), cos(a));
}
float yw4_pcss_remember(vec2 key, float lit) {
    if (yw4_seen_n < 2) {
        yw4_seen_key[yw4_seen_n] = key;
        yw4_seen_lit[yw4_seen_n] = lit;
        yw4_seen_n++;
    }
    return lit;
}
// One depth compare at level 0 (the maps have one level). The game's program uses an implicit level, which reads
// the neighbouring pixels' coordinates; ours skips the lookups for some pixels (main, "ours, faster") and the soft
// shadows return early per pixel, so a neighbour may not be running, and the implicit level is then undefined.
// NVIDIA didn't mind; AMD's Windows driver made the shadows flicker (issue #8). An explicit level asks nothing
// of the neighbours. (Ours only: the translated program keeps texture(), its control flow stays the game's.)
float shadow_cmp(sampler2DArrayShadow s, vec4 c) {
    return textureLod(s, c, 0.0);
}

float yw4_shadow(sampler2DArrayShadow s, sampler2DArray d, vec4 c) {
    if (yw4_pcss.mode.x < 0.5) return shadow_cmp(s, c);
    if (yw4_pcss.tune.y == 3.0) return shadow_cmp(s, vec4(c.xy, c.z, c.w));
    if (yw4_pcss.tune.y == 4.0) return textureLod(d, vec3(c.xy, c.z), 0.0).r;
    if (yw4_pcss.tune.y == 5.0) return c.w > textureLod(d, vec3(c.xy, c.z), 0.0).r ? 1.0 : 0.0;
    if (yw4_pcss.tune.y == 6.0) return c.w;
    for (int i = 0; i < yw4_seen_n; i++)
        if (yw4_seen_key[i] == c.zw) return yw4_seen_lit[i];
    mat2 rot = yw4_pcss_rotation();
    float r;
    if (yw4_pcss.tune.z > 0.5 && yw4_search_layer == c.z) {
        if (yw4_search_r < 0.0) return yw4_pcss_remember(c.zw, shadow_cmp(s, vec4(c.xy, c.z, c.w)));
        r = yw4_search_r;
    } else {
        float gaps = 0.0, casters = 0.0;
        for (int i = 0; i < 16; i += 2) {  // ours, faster: every other tap (the 16-tap choice removed 2026-11-18)
            float z = textureLod(d, vec3(c.xy + rot * YW4_DISK[i] * yw4_pcss.mode.z, c.z), 0.0).r;
            float gap = c.w - z;
            if (gap > yw4_pcss.tune.x) { gaps += gap; casters += 1.0; }
        }
        if (yw4_pcss.tune.y == 1.0) return casters * (2.0 / 16.0);
        yw4_search_layer = c.z, yw4_search_r = -1.0;
        if (casters == 0.0) return yw4_pcss_remember(c.zw, shadow_cmp(s, vec4(c.xy, c.z, c.w)));
        r = clamp(gaps / casters * yw4_pcss.scale[min(int(c.z + 0.5), 3)], yw4_pcss.mode.w, yw4_pcss.mode.z);
        yw4_search_r = r;
    }
    if (yw4_pcss.tune.y == 2.0) return r / yw4_pcss.mode.z;
    float lit = 0.0;
    int fstep = (int(yw4_pcss.mode.y) & 4) != 0 ? 2 : 1;  // ours, faster: every other tap, turned each frame
    for (int i = 0; i < 16; i += fstep)
        lit += shadow_cmp(s, vec4(c.xy + rot * YW4_DISK[i] * r, c.z, c.w));
    return yw4_pcss_remember(c.zw, lit * (float(fstep) / 16.0));
}

// The sign of t as -1, 0 or 1, made the game's way (two compares as integers), so that 0 and -0 give +0.
int sign_of(float t) {
    return int(t > 0.0) - int(t < 0.0);
}

// A tap point beside the surface in light view, slid along the light's depth (z) back onto the
// plane through `at` with normal `n` (both in light view); `s` is the sign that orients the normal.
// Where n's part along the slide is 0 the result is NaN, as in the game.
vec3 onto_plane(vec3 tap, vec3 at, vec3 n, float s) {
    vec3 sn = s * n;
    float d = (dot(at, sn) + -dot(sn, tap)) / -(-s * sn.z);
    return fma(vec3(-s * d), vec3(0.0, 0.0, -1.0), tap);
}

// A light-view point in cascade c's map: (u, v, depth).
vec3 to_map(vec4 p, int c) {
    float w = dot(sun.d[25 + 4 * c], p);
    vec2 uv = vec2(dot(sun.d[22 + 4 * c], p), -dot(sun.d[23 + 4 * c], p)) + w;
    return vec3(uv * 0.5, dot(sun.d[24 + 4 * c], p)) / w;
}

// The view-space position in cascade c's map through rows 34-37: (u, v, depth).
vec3 to_grid(vec4 pos, int c) {
    float w = dot(pos, sun.d[37 + 4 * c]);
    vec2 uv = w + vec2(dot(pos, sun.d[34 + 4 * c]), -dot(pos, sun.d[35 + 4 * c]));
    return vec3(uv * 0.5, dot(pos, sun.d[36 + 4 * c])) / w;
}

// How far `uv` is from the centre of its texel in the 1024 grid (the larger axis).
float texel_offset(vec2 uv) {
    vec2 o = fma(floor(uv * 1024.0) + 0.5, vec2(0.0009765625), -uv);
    return max(abs(o.y), abs(o.x));
}

// The depth bias: grows with the distance from the texel centre over the surface's slope to the light.
float bias_of(float slope_distance, float n_dot_l) {
    vec3 b = sun.d[2].xyz;
    return min(fma(b.y, clamp(slope_distance / n_dot_l, 0.0, 1.0), b.x), b.z);
}

// Ours: contact shadows. Small details the cascades are too coarse for (feet on the ground, props on a table):
// a short march from the surface toward the sun across the half-size depth; where the picture is in front of the
// ray by less than the thickness, something on screen sits between the surface and the sun. The projection is
// the inverse of rows 20-23, which carry this frame's AA shift (cb8_scaled_copy), so the march lines up with the
// shifted depth. Returns how much is in shadow: a hit near the start 1, one toward the end of the ray less.
// `jitter` (0..1) moves the steps along the ray (contact_smoothed spreads it over each 2x2 block of pixels).
// No early exit (issue #19, #8): every pixel runs all the steps, "off the screen" and "the first hit" kept in flags,
// so the four pixels of a 2x2 block are together again at contact_smoothed's swaps. With break / return they left
// the loop at different steps, and Vulkan only promises they meet again with maximal reconvergence: NVIDIA's driver
// did, AMD's (likely) didn't, and a swap read a neighbour's value never written (black bars on AMD). The result is
// the same as before: the first hit's 1 - t², 0 with none or once the ray has left the screen.
float contact_shadow(vec3 pos, vec3 n, vec3 l, float jitter) {
    mat4 proj = inverse(transpose(mat4(view.d[20], view.d[21], view.d[22], view.d[23])));
    int steps = int(yw4_pcss.contact.x);
    float len = yw4_pcss.contact.y, thick = yw4_pcss.contact.z;
    float dist = -pos.z;
    // off the surface a little, more with distance (the depth is coarser there), so it doesn't shadow itself
    vec3 start = pos + n * (dist * 0.002);
    bool done = false;  // the ray left the screen (was a break), or hit (was a return)
    float result = 0.0;
    ivec2 size = textureSize(half_depth, 0);
    for (int i = 0; i < steps; i++) {
        float t = (float(i) + jitter) / float(steps);
        vec3 p = start + l * (len * t);
        vec4 c = proj * vec4(p, 1.0);
        bool ahead = c.w > 0.0;
        vec2 ndc = c.xy / (ahead ? c.w : 1.0);
        vec2 suv = vec2(ndc.x * 0.5 + 0.5, 0.5 - ndc.y * 0.5);
        bool on_screen = ahead && !any(lessThan(suv, vec2(0.0))) && !any(greaterThan(suv, vec2(1.0)));
        done = done || !on_screen;
        // the texel itself, not a blend: at an outline (a pole against the ground) a filtered read is a depth
        // between the two that nothing has, and it looked like a blocker beside thin things (clamped: off the
        // screen it is read and not used)
        vec2 cuv = clamp(suv, vec2(0.0), vec2(1.0));
        ivec2 texel = min(ivec2(cuv * vec2(size)), size - 1);
        vec4 sc = vec4(ndc, texelFetch(half_depth, texel, 0).x, 1.0);
        float scene_z = dot(view.d[22], sc) / dot(view.d[23], sc);
        float gap = scene_z - p.z;  // > 0: the picture there is nearer the camera than the ray
        // (hits right beside the pixel count: skipping them, for the hairline beside posts, also dropped the thin
        // line under a wall's cap or an eave once it was only a texel or two tall, so it faded with distance)
        // How squarely the blocker faces the camera there: seen edge-on (a post's outline, |n.v| near 0) its
        // depth says nothing about how thick it is behind, and rays passing behind a post's side drew a line
        // on the ground beside it, so those don't count. A face seen at a slant (a wall's cap looking along
        // the wall) still counts, with the thickness widened by the slant: its depth there spreads over more
        // of the view, and at 0.07 the line under the cap faded out as the view turned.
        // (Asking whether the ray comes out in front again can't tell a post from a wall's thin cap: the ray
        // under a cap comes out over its top, and the cap's line went too.)
        vec3 hn = normalize(fma(textureLod(gbuffer_normal, cuv, 0.0).xyz, vec3(2.0), vec3(-1.0)));
        vec3 hp = vec3(dot(view.d[20], sc), dot(view.d[21], sc), dot(view.d[22], sc)) / dot(view.d[23], sc);
        float facing = abs(dot(hn, normalize(hp)));
        bool hit = gap > dist * 0.001 && facing > 0.15 && gap < thick / max(facing, 0.25);
        result = (!done && hit) ? 1.0 - t * t : result;
        done = done || hit;
    }
    return result;
}

// Contact shadows smoothed: the four pixels of a 2x2 block march with the steps a quarter step apart, then
// share their results (the GPU runs a block together, so the swaps are nearly free): where they agree the
// result is that of a ray with four times the steps; a random start per pixel instead left dots (a bush's
// shade on a wall). Only neighbours at about the same depth count, so nothing bleeds across an outline.
// Called by every pixel of the block (uniform control flow): the swaps need all four. Pixels that don't use the
// result (the sky and anything past the last cascade, surfaces facing away from the sun: the mask is 0 or 1
// there whatever it finds) get 0 and are left out of their neighbours' average.
// A block where no pixel uses it skips the march (2026-11-18: the march ran everywhere, sky included). The four
// decide together: `used` is swapped first, while all four still run, so the branch is the same for the whole block
// and they meet again at the swaps below (issue #19, #8: a branch that splits a block is what broke them on AMD).
// The result is unchanged: a skipped pixel's 0 was 0 before, and its weight in the average 0.
float contact_smoothed(vec3 pos, vec3 n) {
    uvec2 q = uvec2(gl_FragCoord.xy) & 1u;
    float jitter = (float(q.x + 2u * q.y) + 0.5) * 0.25;
    vec3 l = normalize(sun.d[0].xyz);
    float used = -pos.z <= sun.d[9].y && dot(n, l) > 1e-4 ? 1.0 : 0.0;
    vec3 us = vec3(subgroupQuadSwapHorizontal(used), subgroupQuadSwapVertical(used), subgroupQuadSwapDiagonal(used));
    bool block_uses = used + us.x + us.y + us.z > 0.0;  // the same in all four pixels
    float c = block_uses ? contact_shadow(pos, n, l, jitter) * used : 0.0;
    float z = pos.z, near = -z * 0.02;
    vec3 cs = vec3(subgroupQuadSwapHorizontal(c), subgroupQuadSwapVertical(c), subgroupQuadSwapDiagonal(c));
    vec3 zs = vec3(subgroupQuadSwapHorizontal(z), subgroupQuadSwapVertical(z), subgroupQuadSwapDiagonal(z));
    vec3 wt = vec3(lessThan(abs(zs - z), vec3(near))) * us;
    return (c + dot(cs, wt)) / (1.0 + wt.x + wt.y + wt.z);
}

void main() {
    vec2 uv = v_uv.xy;

    // 1. Position: the half-size depth back through the inverse projection.
    float depth = textureLod(half_depth, uv, 0.0).x;
    vec4 clip = vec4(fma(v_uv.xy, vec2(2.0, -2.0), vec2(-1.0, 1.0)), depth, 1.0);
    float y = dot(clip, view.d[21]);
    float z = dot(view.d[22], clip);
    float w = dot(clip, view.d[23]);
    float x = dot(clip, view.d[20]);
    vec3 pos = vec3(x, y, z) / w;

    // Ours: contact shadows, here for every pixel (their smoothing swaps results within 2x2 blocks; see below)
    float contact = 0.0;
    if (yw4_pcss.contact.x > 0.5) {
        vec3 cn = normalize(fma(textureLod(gbuffer_normal, uv, 0.0).xyz, vec3(2.0), vec3(-1.0)));
        contact = contact_smoothed(pos, cn);
    }

    // 2. Cascade: the first whose range reaches this depth; toward the end of cascades 0 and 1 a
    // blend weight toward the next one.
    int cascade = -1, next = -1;
    float blend = 0.0;
    for (int c = 0; c < 3; c++) {
        float far_end = sun.d[7 + c].y;
        if (far_end >= -pos.z) {
            if (c < 2) {
                float next_start = sun.d[8 + c].x;
                blend = clamp((-pos.z + -next_start) / (-next_start + far_end), 0.0, 1.0);
                next = c + 1;
            }
            cascade = c;
            break;
        }
    }
    // (an if, not an early return, as the game has it: lookups take their level of detail from the
    // neighbouring pixels, which must still be running)
    if (cascade < 0) {
        o_mask = vec4(0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0);
    } else {
        // 3. Normal and N·L; a surface facing away from the sun counts as in shadow.
        vec3 n = fma(textureLod(gbuffer_normal, uv, 0.0).xyz, vec3(2.0), vec3(-1.0));
        n = inversesqrt(abs(dot(n, n))) * n;
        float n_dot_l = dot(n, sun.d[0].xyz);
        float facing_away = -n_dot_l >= -9.999999750e-05 ? 1.0 : 0.0;

        // The fade of step 6 (by the linear depth toward the far end), worked out first: see below.
        vec2 range = sun.d[3].xy;
        float lin = range.x / fma(-depth, -range.x + range.y, range.y);
        float s = clamp(lin, 0.0, 1.0);

        // Ours, faster, the same result: a surface facing away from the sun ends up in shadow (1) whatever the
        // lookups find, and a fully faded one ends up 0 (1 - s² = 0): neither needs them.
        float shadow = 1.0;
        if (facing_away == 0.0 && s < 1.0) {
            // 4. Five lookups in the cascade: four taps beside the surface along the light's x and y,
            // kept on its plane, and the centre.
            int c = cascade;
            float layer = float(c);
            vec4 p = vec4(pos, 1.0);
            vec4 r10 = sun.d[10 + 4 * c], r11 = sun.d[11 + 4 * c], r12 = sun.d[12 + 4 * c];
            vec3 at = vec3(dot(p, r10), dot(p, r11), dot(p, r12));  // the surface in light view
            vec3 ln = vec3(dot(n, r10.xyz), dot(n, r11.xyz), dot(r12.xyz, n));
            ln = inversesqrt(abs(dot(ln, ln))) * ln;  // its normal in light view
            vec2 spread = view.d[31].zw * sun.d[4 + c].xy;
            int sx = sign_of(ln.x * -spread.x), sy = sign_of(ln.y * -spread.y);

            vec3 centre = to_grid(p, c);
            float inv_sin = inversesqrt(abs(fma(-n_dot_l, n_dot_l, 1.0)));
            float bias = bias_of(texel_offset(centre.xy) / inv_sin, n_dot_l);

            if (yw4_pcss.mode.x >= 0.5 && (int(yw4_pcss.mode.y) & 1) != 0) {
                // ours, faster: with soft shadows on, one soft lookup at the centre. Its 16 taps spread far wider
                // than the game's five points (less than a texel apart), so the five only cost four more filters.
                shadow = max(yw4_shadow(shadow_maps, shadow_depth, vec4(centre.xy, layer, centre.z + -bias)), facing_away);
            } else {
                vec3 right = onto_plane(at + vec3(spread.x, 0.0, 0.0), at, ln, float(-sx));
                vec3 left = onto_plane(at + vec3(-spread.x, 0.0, 0.0), at, ln, float(sx));
                vec3 up = onto_plane(at + vec3(0.0, spread.y, 0.0), at, ln, float(-sy));
                vec3 down = onto_plane(fma(vec3(0.0, spread.y, 0.0), vec3(1.0, -1.0, 1.0), at), at, ln, float(sy));
                vec3 right_map = to_map(vec4(right, 1.0), c);
                vec3 left_map = to_map(vec4(left, 1.0), c);
                vec3 up_map = to_map(vec4(up, 1.0), c);
                vec3 down_map = to_map(vec4(down, 1.0), c);

                // in the game's order: the soft shadows remember earlier lookups of this pixel
                float lit_left = yw4_shadow(shadow_maps, shadow_depth, vec4(left_map.xy, layer, left_map.z + -bias));
                float lit_right = yw4_shadow(shadow_maps, shadow_depth, vec4(right_map.xy, layer, right_map.z + -bias));
                float lit_centre = yw4_shadow(shadow_maps, shadow_depth, vec4(centre.xy, layer, centre.z + -bias));
                float lit_up = yw4_shadow(shadow_maps, shadow_depth, vec4(up_map.xy, layer, up_map.z + -bias));
                float lit_down = yw4_shadow(shadow_maps, shadow_depth, vec4(down_map.xy, layer, down_map.z + -bias));
                float sum = lit_down + (lit_up + (lit_left + (lit_right + lit_centre)));
                shadow = max(sum * 0.199951172, facing_away);  // the average (0.2 in half precision)
            }

            // 5. Toward the next cascade: one centre lookup there, mixed in by the blend weight.
            if (next > 0) {
                vec3 g = to_grid(p, next);
                float b = bias_of((1.0 / inv_sin) * texel_offset(g.xy), n_dot_l);
                float lit_next = max(yw4_shadow(shadow_maps, shadow_depth, vec4(g.xy, float(next), g.z + -b)), facing_away);
                shadow = fma(blend, -shadow + lit_next, shadow);
            }

            if (yw4_pcss.contact.x > 0.5) {
                shadow = yw4_pcss.contact.w == 1.0 ? contact : max(shadow, contact);  // debug 1: contact alone
            }
        }

        // 6. Fade out toward the far end.
        o_mask = vec4(fma(-s * s, shadow, shadow), lin, lin, 0.0);
    }
}

```

`runtime/shaders/shadow_skinned.vert`:

```vert
// Skinned shadow casters (decision 0024): as the game's 71faac..., up to 8 bones per vertex.
// Weights: eight 16-bit numbers in four 32-bit words (low half, high half); bone indices: eight
// bytes in four 16-bit words, paired with the weights the same way. Bones 5-8 only when the
// fifth weight isn't 0. The blended 3x4 matrix moves the vertex (weights sum to 65535), then
// projection x view x world (push constants) as in shadow_static.vert. The order of the
// multiply-adds is the game's: high half of word 0 first, then low 0, low 1, high 1; then low
// 2, high 2, low 3, high 3.
#version 450

layout(location = 0) in vec4 position;
layout(location = 1) in uvec4 weights;
layout(location = 2) in uvec4 bones;

layout(set = 0, binding = 0, std140) uniform Palette {
    vec4 row[3 * 256];  // the submesh's bones, 3x4 each
} palette;

layout(push_constant) uniform Draw {
    vec4 row[4];  // projection x view x world, row-major
} draw;

void main() {
    uint b0 = bones.x & 255u, b1 = bones.x >> 8, b2 = bones.y & 255u, b3 = bones.y >> 8;
    float w0 = float(weights.x & 65535u), w1 = float(weights.x >> 16);
    float w2 = float(weights.y & 65535u), w3 = float(weights.y >> 16);
    vec4 m[3];
    for (int r = 0; r < 3; r++) {
        vec4 s = w1 * palette.row[b1 * 3u + uint(r)];
        s = fma(vec4(w0), palette.row[b0 * 3u + uint(r)], s);
        s = fma(vec4(w2), palette.row[b2 * 3u + uint(r)], s);
        m[r] = fma(palette.row[b3 * 3u + uint(r)], vec4(w3), s);
    }
    float w4 = float(weights.z & 65535u);
    if (w4 > 0.0) {
        uint b4 = bones.z & 255u, b5 = bones.z >> 8, b6 = bones.w & 255u, b7 = bones.w >> 8;
        float w5 = float(weights.z >> 16), w6 = float(weights.w & 65535u), w7 = float(weights.w >> 16);
        for (int r = 0; r < 3; r++) {
            vec4 s = fma(palette.row[b4 * 3u + uint(r)], vec4(w4), m[r]);
            s = fma(vec4(w5), palette.row[b5 * 3u + uint(r)], s);
            s = fma(palette.row[b6 * 3u + uint(r)], vec4(w6), s);
            m[r] = fma(palette.row[b7 * 3u + uint(r)], vec4(w7), s);
        }
    }
    const float unit = 1.525902190e-05;  // 1 / 65535
    vec4 v = vec4(dot(position * m[0], vec4(unit)), dot(position * m[1], vec4(unit)),
                  dot(position * m[2], vec4(unit)), position.w);
    gl_Position = vec4(dot(v, draw.row[0]), dot(v, draw.row[1]), dot(v, draw.row[2]), dot(draw.row[3], v));
}

```

`runtime/shaders/shadow_skinned4.vert`:

```vert
// Skinned shadow casters with up to 4 bones per vertex (decision 0024): as the game's 26b707...
// Weights are floats (the vertex format turns them into 0..1), bone indices whole numbers, both
// in the formats and at the offsets the game's draw had (bindings 1 and 2). The blended 3x4
// matrix moves the vertex, then projection x view x world (push constants) as in
// shadow_static.vert. The order of the multiply-adds is the game's: bone y first, then x, z, w.
#version 450

layout(location = 0) in vec4 position;
layout(location = 1) in vec4 weights;
layout(location = 2) in uvec4 bones;

layout(set = 0, binding = 0, std140) uniform Palette {
    vec4 row[3 * 256];  // the submesh's bones, 3x4 each
} palette;

layout(push_constant) uniform Draw {
    vec4 row[4];  // projection x view x world, row-major
} draw;

void main() {
    uvec4 b = bones * 3u;
    vec4 m[3];
    for (int r = 0; r < 3; r++) {
        vec4 s = weights.y * palette.row[b.y + uint(r)];
        s = fma(vec4(weights.x), palette.row[b.x + uint(r)], s);
        s = fma(vec4(weights.z), palette.row[b.z + uint(r)], s);
        m[r] = fma(palette.row[b.w + uint(r)], vec4(weights.w), s);
    }
    vec4 v = vec4(dot(position, m[0]), dot(position, m[1]), dot(position, m[2]), position.w);
    gl_Position = vec4(dot(v, draw.row[0]), dot(v, draw.row[1]), dot(v, draw.row[2]), dot(draw.row[3], v));
}

```

`runtime/shaders/shadow_static.vert`:

```vert
// Static shadow casters (decision 0024): the game's depth-only shader b320bd... computes each
// clip coordinate as dot(row, position) with the rows of projection x view x world; so does
// this one, with the rows in push constants. No fragment stage: depth only.
#version 450

layout(location = 0) in vec3 position;

layout(push_constant) uniform Draw {
    vec4 row[4];  // projection x view x world, row-major
} draw;

void main() {
    vec4 v = vec4(position, 1.0);
    gl_Position = vec4(dot(draw.row[0], v), dot(draw.row[1], v), dot(draw.row[2], v), dot(draw.row[3], v));
}

```

`runtime/shaders/shadow_wind.vert`:

```vert
// Wind-swayed shadow casters (decision 0024): as the game's fa9033... (instanced) and 61ebac...
// (not), always with the cut-out fragment program. The position after copy x world (one row set
// per copy in the copies ring; the world's alone for 61ebac) is moved by the wind in world space,
// then projection x view:
// - the wind map (vs texture 12) at the position's xz (cb6 row 47: scale, offset) gives a height
//   band (z, w) and a bend direction (x, y); s: where the vertex is in the band, -1..1;
// - the wind noise (vs texture 11) at two scales (cb7 row 3: x, z) of xz plus wind direction x
//   time (cb6 row 36: xy, w), offset by the vertex's phase (weights.z), scaled by cb7 row 3 (y, w)
//   and the vertex's weights (x, y);
// - offset = noise x strength (cb6 row 36 z x cb7 row 0 x) + bend x (1 - s^2) x weight x cb7 row 0 y.
// The operations are the game's, in its order. The draw's constants are a header entry in the ring.
#version 450

layout(location = 0) in vec3 position;
layout(location = 1) in vec4 uv;
layout(location = 2) in vec4 weights;

struct Copy {
    vec4 row[4];
    vec4 extra;
};
layout(set = 1, binding = 0, std430) readonly buffer Copies {
    Copy copy[];
} copies;

layout(set = 0, binding = 1) uniform sampler2D noise;     // vs texture 11
layout(set = 0, binding = 2) uniform sampler2D wind_map;  // vs texture 12

layout(push_constant) uniform Draw {
    vec4 vp[4];       // projection x view, row-major
    float threshold;  // the material's: vertex constant buffer 3, byte 12
    uint header;      // the draw's constants in the ring: cb6 rows 36, 47, cb7 rows 0, 3
} draw;

layout(location = 3) out vec4 cut;

void main() {
    Copy hd = copies.copy[draw.header];
    vec4 c36 = hd.row[0], c47 = hd.row[1], c70 = hd.row[2], c73 = hd.row[3];
    Copy c = copies.copy[gl_InstanceIndex];
    vec4 v = vec4(position, 1.0);
    vec3 p = vec3(dot(c.row[0], v), dot(c.row[1], v), dot(c.row[2], v));

    vec4 m = textureLod(wind_map, (p.xz - c47.zw) * c47.xy, 0.0);
    float band = m.z - m.w;
    float s = (p.y - fma(band, 0.5, m.w)) / band * 2.0;
    vec2 q = fma(c36.xy, vec2(c36.w), p.xz);
    float sa = min(abs(s), 1.0);
    vec2 qx = fma(q, vec2(1.0 / c73.x), vec2(weights.z));
    vec2 qz = fma(q, vec2(1.0 / c73.z), vec2(weights.z));
    vec3 na = textureLod(noise, qz, 0.0).xyz - 0.5;
    vec3 nb = textureLod(noise, qx, 0.0).xyz - 0.5;
    vec3 sway = fma(nb * c73.y, vec3(weights.x), weights.y * (c73.w * na));
    float k = -sa * sa;
    vec3 bend = vec3(fma(k, m.x, m.x), 0.0, fma(k, m.y, m.y));
    bend = clamp(weights.y + weights.x, 0.0, 1.0) * bend;
    bend = c70.y * bend;
    vec4 w = vec4(fma(sway, vec3(c36.z * c70.x), bend) + p, 1.0);

    gl_Position = vec4(dot(draw.vp[0], w), dot(draw.vp[1], w), dot(draw.vp[2], w), dot(draw.vp[3], w));
    cut = vec4(uv.xy, draw.threshold, 1.0);
}

```

`runtime/shaders/sharpen.glsl`:

```glsl
// SHARPENING's filter (decision 0076), shared by taa_output.frag (the 3D, in the perceptual curve) and
// ui_sharpen.frag (text and menus, in the window image's own values). Both have values in 0..1.
//
// The method of AMD FidelityFX RCAS ("robust contrast-adaptive sharpening", FSR's own sharpener, MIT licence), so
// TAA, DLSS, OFF, FXAA and SMAA sharpen the way FSR does at the same setting. The pixel e is pushed away from its
// four neighbours (b above, h below, d left, f right) by one weight (a "lobe") for all three colours, as large as
// the neighbours allow without the result leaving 0..1 in any colour, at most RCAS_LIMIT, then scaled by the amount.
// Soft detail gets a strong push; strong edges get less, so they don't ring. The amount is FSR's sharpness: 0..1,
// in stops (1.0 the full lobe, 0.5 half of it, 0.0 a quarter); 0 or below means none (the callers skip it).
// The first filter here (a push clamped to the neighbours' range) stopped gaining on soft texture: on DLSS its MAX
// came out like FSR's MEDIUM, and stronger looked blocky before it caught up (issue #11, 2026-11-16).
const float RCAS_LIMIT = 0.25 - 1.0 / 16.0;

vec3 sharpen(vec3 e, vec3 b, vec3 h, vec3 d, vec3 f, float amount) {
    float con = exp2(-2.0 * (1.0 - clamp(amount, 0.0, 1.0)));  // FSR's sharpness -> RCAS's weight, 2 stops down to 0
    vec3 mn4 = min(min(b, h), min(d, f)), mx4 = max(max(b, h), max(d, f));
    // the most negative lobe each colour takes before the result would go below 0 (hit_min) or above 1 (hit_max)
    vec3 hit_min = min(mn4, e) / max(4.0 * mx4, vec3(1e-5));
    vec3 hit_max = (1.0 - max(mx4, e)) / min(4.0 * mn4 - 4.0, vec3(-1e-5));
    vec3 l = max(-hit_min, hit_max);
    float lobe = max(-RCAS_LIMIT, min(max(l.r, max(l.g, l.b)), 0.0)) * con;
    return (lobe * (b + h + d + f) + e) / (4.0 * lobe + 1.0);
}

```

`runtime/shaders/sky_fog.frag`:

```frag
// The engine's sky and aerial perspective (game program 627287, with the quad 3ef32a at the far plane): per
// pixel a camera ray, a sky gradient by the ray's height, and scattering toward the sun (Rayleigh and a
// Henyey-Greenstein-like Mie phase) over the distance and height, from a small fog image looked up edge-aware.
// Every operation in the game's order (its fused multiply-adds, reciprocals and odd steps such as (v + 1) - 1),
// so the result can match it bit for bit; the names are ours. docs/frame.md "Lighting stage".
#version 460

layout(set = 1, binding = 0, std140) uniform Pass {
    vec4 c;  // x field of view, y aspect, z ray length
} pass;

layout(set = 1, binding = 6, std140) uniform Light {
    vec4 rows[4];  // row 2: the sun's direction
} light;

layout(set = 1, binding = 8, std140) uniform Camera {
    vec4 rows[48];  // 0 position, 1-2 axes, 32 fog texel, 34-46 sky and fog settings, 47 horizon
} cam;

layout(set = 1, binding = 29) uniform sampler2D fog_depth;  // texture 13
layout(set = 1, binding = 30) uniform sampler2D fog;        // texture 14 (z: how much fog)

layout(location = 1) in vec4 base;  // the quad's colour (0)
layout(location = 3) in vec4 uv;    // xy the pixel, z the ray scale

layout(location = 0) out vec4 o_colour;

const vec3 luma = vec3(0.298909992, 0.586610019, 0.114480004);

void main() {
    // the camera ray
    float half_fov = pass.c.x * 0.5;
    float c_ = cos(half_fov);
    float tan_half = sin(half_fov) / c_;
    float k = uv.z * tan_half;
    vec2 ndc = fma(uv.yx, vec2(-2.0, 2.0), vec2(1.0, -1.0));
    vec2 plane = ndc * k;
    vec3 ax1 = cam.rows[1].xyz, ax2 = cam.rows[2].xyz;
    vec3 side = fma(ax1.yzx, ax2.zxy, -(ax1.zxy * ax2.yzx));
    vec3 ray = fma(vec3(plane.y * pass.c.y), side, fma(vec3(uv.z), ax1, plane.x * ax2));
    float rs = inversesqrt(abs(dot(ray, ray)));
    float ray_y = rs * ray.y;
    vec3 d = vec3(rs * ray.x, ray_y, rs * ray.z) * pass.c.z;
    float inv_len = inversesqrt(abs(dot(d, d)));

    // the sky gradient by the ray's height
    vec2 horizon = cam.rows[47].xy;
    float lo = (horizon.y + 1.0) * 0.115999997, hi = (horizon.x + 1.0) * 0.216000006;
    float m = min(0.00400000019 / inv_len, 1.0);
    vec3 dn = inv_len * d;
    float h = dn.y * m;
    float rcp_a = 1.0 / fma(horizon.x + 1.0, 0.216000006, -lo), rcp_b = 1.0 / lo;
    vec4 t = clamp(vec4(fma(dn.y, m, -lo), h, fma(dn.y, m, lo), fma(dn.y, m, hi)) * vec4(rcp_a, rcp_b, rcp_b, rcp_a), 0.0, 1.0);
    vec3 c34 = cam.rows[34].xyz, c35 = cam.rows[35].xyz, c36 = cam.rows[36].xyz, c37 = cam.rows[37].xyz, c38 = cam.rows[38].xyz;
    vec3 below_far = fma(vec3(t.w), c37 + -c38, c38);
    vec3 below_near = fma(vec3(t.z), -c37 + c36, c37);
    float cos_sun = dot(dn, light.rows[2].xyz);
    vec2 up = clamp(vec2(h, fma(dn.y, m, hi)) / hi, 0.0, 1.0);
    vec3 sky = h >= -lo ? below_near : below_far;
    vec3 band = fma(vec3(t.y), c35 + -c36, c36);
    if (!(h >= 0.0)) band = sky;
    float above = h >= 0.0 ? 1.0 : 0.0;
    vec3 top = fma(vec3(t.x), c34 + -c35, c35);
    vec3 ground = h >= lo ? top : band;  // the colour toward the ray
    vec3 c40 = cam.rows[40].xyz, c41 = cam.rows[41].xyz, c42 = cam.rows[42].xyz;
    vec3 sky_low = fma(vec3(up.y), c41 + -c42, c42);
    vec3 sky_high = fma(vec3(up.x), c40 + -c41, c41);

    // how much fog: height falloff, and the fog image looked up edge-aware around the pixel
    float height = fma(ray_y, pass.c.z, cam.rows[0].y);
    vec2 falloff = cam.rows[45].xy;
    float height_fog = exp2(((height + -falloff.x) * falloff.y) * -1.44269502);
    vec2 texel = cam.rows[32].xy;
    vec2 near = vec2(texture(fog_depth, uv.xy + -vec2(texel.x, 0.0)).x,    // left
                     texture(fog_depth, vec2(uv.x - 0.0, uv.y + -texel.y)).x);  // up
    vec2 right_at = uv.xy + vec2(texel.x, 1.0);
    right_at = right_at + vec2(0.0, -1.0);
    vec2 far = vec2(texture(fog_depth, right_at).x, texture(fog_depth, vec2(0.0, texel.y) + uv.xy).x);
    vec2 span = -near + far;
    vec2 edge = vec2(lessThan(vec2(0.0), abs(span)));
    vec2 rcp = vec2(1.0 / span.x, 1.0 / span.y);
    vec2 f = clamp(fma(-near, rcp, rcp), 0.0, 1.0);
    f = fma(edge, f + -0.5, vec2(0.5));
    vec2 sx = f.x * vec2(texel.x, 0.0), sy = vec2(0.0, texel.y) * f.y;
    vec2 at = fma(sy, vec2(2.0), -vec2(0.0, texel.y)) + fma(sx, vec2(2.0), -vec2(texel.x, 0.0));
    float fog_amount = texture(fog, at + uv.xy).z;
    float dist = 1.0 / inv_len;
    float fog_alpha = clamp(fog_amount + cam.rows[44].y, 0.0, 1.0);

    // scattering
    vec3 sky_col = fma(vec3(above), sky_high + -sky_low, sky_low);
    vec4 c43 = cam.rows[43];
    vec2 depth_in = max(vec2(dist + c43.x, dist + cam.rows[45].z), vec2(0.0));
    vec2 c46 = cam.rows[46].xy;
    vec4 optical = vec4(depth_in.x * c43.y, depth_in.x * c43.z, depth_in.y * cam.rows[45].w, depth_in.y * c46.x) * 1.44269502;
    float g = cam.rows[44].x;
    vec2 g2 = fma(vec2(g), vec2(g), vec2(2.0, 1.0));
    float hg = log2(abs(-dot(vec2(cos_sun), vec2(g)) + g2.y)) * 1.5;
    float hg_norm = fma(-g * g, 1.0 / g2.x, 1.0 / g2.x);
    float cos2 = cos_sun * cos_sun;
    float mie = (fma(cos2, exp2(-hg), exp2(-hg)) * hg_norm) * 0.119366206;
    float rayleigh = min(fma(cos2, 0.0596831031, 0.0596831031) * 12.0, 1.0);
    vec4 absorbed = -vec4(exp2(optical.x), exp2(optical.y), exp2(optical.z), exp2(optical.w)) + 1.0;
    vec4 amounts = vec4(rayleigh, mie, height_fog, mie * height_fog) * absorbed;
    vec2 sat_zw = clamp(amounts.zw, 0.0, 1.0);
    float ground_luma = dot(ground, luma);
    vec3 scattered = fma(vec3(amounts.y), sky_col, sat_zw.y * sky_col);
    vec3 c39 = cam.rows[39].xyz;
    float c39_luma = dot(c39, luma);
    vec3 grey_ground = fma(vec3(clamp(depth_in.x * c43.w, 0.0, 1.0)), -ground_luma + ground, vec3(ground_luma));
    vec3 grey_far = fma(vec3(clamp(depth_in.y * c46.y, 0.0, 1.0)), -c39_luma + c39, vec3(c39_luma));
    vec4 sum = vec4(amounts.x * grey_ground, amounts.x) + vec4(grey_far * sat_zw.x, amounts.z);
    vec3 colour = sum.xyz + scattered;
    float keep = max(-sum.w + 1.0, 0.0) * max(fma(mie, -absorbed.y, 1.0), 0.0);
    o_colour.xyz = fma(base.xyz, vec3(keep), fog_alpha * colour);
    o_colour.w = base.w;
}

```

`runtime/shaders/smaa.glsl`:

```glsl
// SMAA (third_party/smaa, MIT) for the anti-aliasing pass (runtime/src/gpu_aa.c): the target's size from
// the push constant, the ultra preset (half the high preset's edge threshold: on the game's soft, low-contrast
// edges the high preset left jaggies FXAA smoothed; a test pattern showed SMAA itself works, YW4_AA_DEBUG=3).
// A file defines SMAA_INCLUDE_VS or SMAA_INCLUDE_PS as 0 first.
// Bindings: 0 the encoded scene, 1 edges, 2 area texture, 3 search texture, 4 blend weights.
#include "aa.glsl"
#define SMAA_RT_METRICS aa.metrics
#define SMAA_GLSL_4
#define SMAA_PRESET_ULTRA
#include "../../third_party/smaa/SMAA.hlsl"

#if SMAA_INCLUDE_VS
vec2 smaa_fullscreen() {  // one triangle over the target, (0, 0) at the top-left
    vec2 uv = vec2((gl_VertexIndex << 1) & 2, gl_VertexIndex & 2);
    gl_Position = vec4(uv * 2.0 - 1.0, 0.0, 1.0);
    return uv;
}
#endif
```

`runtime/shaders/taa_output.frag`:

```frag
#version 460
#extension GL_GOOGLE_include_directive : require
// The anti-aliasing's last pass: a result in the perceptual curve (TAA's blend, DLSS's output, or the encoded scene
// for OFF / FXAA / SMAA) written back to the game's target in its linear colour, sharpened by params.x (the
// SHARPENING setting, 0 off .. 1 max; sharpen.glsl, decision 0076).
#include "aa.glsl"
#include "sharpen.glsl"
layout(set = 0, binding = 0) uniform sampler2D result;
layout(location = 0) out vec4 o_color;

vec3 at(ivec2 p) { return texelFetch(result, clamp(p, ivec2(0), ivec2(aa.metrics.zw) - 1), 0).rgb; }

void main() {
    ivec2 p = ivec2(gl_FragCoord.xy);
    vec3 c = at(p);
    if (aa.params.x <= 0.0) {  // SHARPENING off: a plain copy
        o_color = vec4(aa_decode(c), 1.0);
        return;
    }
    vec3 sharp = sharpen(c, at(p + ivec2(0, -1)), at(p + ivec2(0, 1)), at(p + ivec2(-1, 0)), at(p + ivec2(1, 0)),
                         aa.params.x);
    o_color = vec4(aa_decode(sharp), 1.0);
}

```

`runtime/shaders/taa_resolve.frag`:

```frag
#version 460
#extension GL_GOOGLE_include_directive : require
// Temporal anti-aliasing (runtime/src/gpu_aa.c): the 3D draws are shifted by a different fraction of a pixel
// every frame (gpu_taa_jitter), so blending each frame into the history gathers many samples per pixel.
// Last frame's result is fetched where this pixel was then, from the game's own motion vectors (G-buffer
// target 0: this frame's screen position minus last frame's, in 0..1 screen units), with a sharp
// Catmull-Rom filter, and pulled into the range of colours around the pixel now, so things that appeared,
// left or moved on their own (the game's motion is often the camera's only) don't leave trails.
// Works in the perceptual curve (aa.glsl); writes the new history in it.
#include "aa.glsl"
layout(set = 0, binding = 0) uniform sampler2D current;  // aa_encode.frag's output (this frame, shifted)
layout(set = 0, binding = 1) uniform sampler2D motion;   // the game's motion target
layout(set = 0, binding = 4) uniform sampler2D history;  // last frame's result
layout(location = 0) in vec2 v_uv;
layout(location = 0) out vec4 o_color;

vec3 to_ycocg(vec3 c) { return vec3(dot(c, vec3(0.25, 0.5, 0.25)), dot(c, vec3(0.5, 0.0, -0.5)), dot(c, vec3(-0.25, 0.5, -0.25))); }
vec3 to_rgb(vec3 c) { return vec3(c.x + c.y - c.z, c.x + c.z, c.x - c.y - c.z); }

// Catmull-Rom in 5 bilinear taps (the 4 corner taps' weights are small enough to leave out)
vec3 history_at(vec2 uv) {
    vec2 size = aa.metrics.zw, pos = uv * size, c1 = floor(pos - 0.5) + 0.5, f = pos - c1;
    vec2 w0 = f * (-0.5 + f * (1.0 - 0.5 * f)), w1 = 1.0 + f * f * (-2.5 + 1.5 * f);
    vec2 w2 = f * (0.5 + f * (2.0 - 1.5 * f)), w3 = f * f * (-0.5 + 0.5 * f);
    vec2 w12 = w1 + w2, t0 = (c1 - 1.0) / size, t3 = (c1 + 2.0) / size, t12 = (c1 + w2 / w12) / size;
    vec3 r = textureLod(history, vec2(t12.x, t0.y), 0.0).rgb * (w12.x * w0.y) +
             textureLod(history, vec2(t0.x, t12.y), 0.0).rgb * (w0.x * w12.y) +
             textureLod(history, t12, 0.0).rgb * (w12.x * w12.y) +
             textureLod(history, vec2(t3.x, t12.y), 0.0).rgb * (w3.x * w12.y) +
             textureLod(history, vec2(t12.x, t3.y), 0.0).rgb * (w12.x * w3.y);
    float sum = w12.x * w0.y + w0.x * w12.y + w12.x * w12.y + w3.x * w12.y + w12.x * w3.y;
    return max(r / sum, vec3(0.0));
}

// h moved toward the box's centre until it is inside the box
vec3 clip_to_box(vec3 lo, vec3 hi, vec3 h) {
    vec3 c = 0.5 * (hi + lo), e = 0.5 * (hi - lo) + 1e-5, v = h - c, a = abs(v / e);
    float m = max(a.x, max(a.y, a.z));
    return m > 1.0 ? c + v / m : h;
}

void main() {
    ivec2 p = ivec2(gl_FragCoord.xy), size = ivec2(aa.metrics.zw), msize = textureSize(motion, 0);
    vec3 cur = to_ycocg(texelFetch(current, p, 0).rgb), lo = cur, hi = cur, m1 = vec3(0.0), m2 = vec3(0.0);
    vec2 mv = vec2(0.0);
    for (int y = -1; y <= 1; y++)
        for (int x = -1; x <= 1; x++) {
            ivec2 q = clamp(p + ivec2(x, y), ivec2(0), size - 1);
            vec3 c = to_ycocg(texelFetch(current, q, 0).rgb);
            lo = min(lo, c), hi = max(hi, c), m1 += c, m2 += c * c;
            // the longest motion around: the edges of a moving thing take its motion, not the background's
            vec2 v = texelFetch(motion, q * msize / size, 0).xy;
            if (dot(v, v) > dot(mv, mv)) mv = v;
        }
    mv *= aa.params.zw;  // the game's screen y runs upwards here when the window origin is flipped
    if (aa.params.y == 4.0) {  // YW4_AA_DEBUG=4 (a second run of this pass, not into the history): the motion, x red, y green, scaled by 50
        o_color = vec4(aa_encode(vec3(abs(mv) * 50.0, 0.0)), 1.0);
        return;
    }
    vec2 prev = v_uv - mv;
    if (aa.params.x < 0.5 || any(lessThan(prev, vec2(0.0))) || any(greaterThan(prev, vec2(1.0)))) {
        o_color = vec4(to_rgb(cur), 1.0);  // no history here: start from this frame
        return;
    }
    if (aa.params.y == 5.0) {  // YW4_AA_DEBUG=5: how far last frame's result, moved, is from this frame (x4)
        o_color = vec4(aa_encode(abs(history_at(prev) - to_rgb(cur)) * 4.0), 1.0);
        return;
    }
    // variance box, inside the neighbourhood's own range
    vec3 mean = m1 / 9.0, sd = sqrt(max(m2 / 9.0 - mean * mean, vec3(0.0)));
    vec3 hist = clip_to_box(max(lo, mean - 1.25 * sd), min(hi, mean + 1.25 * sd), to_ycocg(history_at(prev)));
    // a tenth of the new frame, up to a quarter while moving fast (less smear on quick turns)
    float a = mix(0.1, 0.25, clamp(length(mv * aa.metrics.zw) / 16.0, 0.0, 1.0));
    o_color = vec4(max(to_rgb(mix(hist, cur, a)), vec3(0.0)), 1.0);
}
```

`runtime/shaders/tonemap.frag`:

```frag
// The engine's tone mapping (game program 22d015, with the quad abf6e5): the lit scene's colour through an
// extended Reinhard curve on its luminance, scaled by the eye adaptation's brightness (a storage buffer), and
// blended in by a strength that a G-buffer flag changes per pixel. Operations in the game's order (its
// fused multiply-adds, divisions and reciprocals), so the result can match it bit for bit.
// docs/frame.md "Lighting stage".
#version 460

layout(set = 1, binding = 0, std140) uniform Tone {
    vec4 a;  // x white point, y exposure, z strength, w strength scale where flagged
    vec4 b;  // x adaptation rate, y adaptation target
} tone;

layout(set = 1, binding = 64, std430) readonly buffer Adaptation {
    float brightness;  // the eye adaptation's current brightness
} adaptation;

layout(set = 1, binding = 16) uniform sampler2D scene;  // texture 0: the lit scene
layout(set = 1, binding = 18) uniform sampler2D flags;  // texture 2: z holds the flag in bit 0 (as /255)

layout(location = 3) in vec4 uv;

layout(location = 0) out vec4 o_colour;

void main() {
    float flagged = (int(trunc(fma(texture(flags, uv.xy).z, 255.0, 0.5))) & 1) != 0 ? 1.0 : 0.0;
    vec4 colour = max(texture(scene, uv.xy), vec4(0.0));
    float lum = dot(colour.xyz, vec3(0.298828125, 0.586425781, 0.114501953));

    float adapted = fma(tone.b.x, -adaptation.brightness + tone.b.y, adaptation.brightness) + 0.00100000005;
    float white2 = tone.a.x * tone.a.x;
    float l = (lum * tone.a.y) / adapted;
    float curve = fma(l / white2, l, l) / (l + 1.0);  // L (1 + L / white^2) / (1 + L)

    vec3 mapped = fma(colour.xxyz * curve, vec4(1.0 / (lum + 9.999999750e-05)), -colour.xxyz).yzw;  // each channel x curve / lum, minus itself
    float strength = fma(fma(tone.a.w, flagged, -flagged), tone.a.z, tone.a.z);
    o_colour.xyz = fma(vec3(strength), mapped, colour.xyz);
    o_colour.w = colour.w;
}

```

`runtime/shaders/ui_sharpen.frag`:

```frag
#version 460
#extension GL_GOOGLE_include_directive : require
// SHARPEN TEXT AND MENUS (decision 0076): the presented window image, game UI included, sharpened like the 3D
// (sharpen.glsl) in its own 0..1 values, written back over it. The 3D was sharpened already at the anti-aliasing
// point, so a pixel that still equals the picture as it was there (`before`: the scene before the UI, copied into
// an image like this one where the window shows it) is left alone; only what the UI changed is sharpened.
// params: x the amount, y 1 when `before` is this frame's (else, a frame with no 3D such as the title or a
// full-screen menu, everything is UI).
#include "aa.glsl"
#include "sharpen.glsl"
layout(set = 0, binding = 0) uniform sampler2D presented;  // a copy of the window image
layout(set = 0, binding = 1) uniform sampler2D before;     // the scene before the UI, at the window image's size
layout(location = 0) out vec4 o_color;

vec4 at(ivec2 p) { return texelFetch(presented, clamp(p, ivec2(0), ivec2(aa.metrics.zw) - 1), 0); }

void main() {
    ivec2 p = ivec2(gl_FragCoord.xy);
    vec4 c = at(p);
    if (aa.params.y > 0.5) {
        vec3 b = texelFetch(before, p, 0).rgb;
        if (all(lessThan(abs(c.rgb - b), vec3(1.5 / 255.0)))) {  // the 3D, untouched by the UI
            o_color = c;
            return;
        }
    }
    vec3 sharp = sharpen(c.rgb, at(p + ivec2(0, -1)).rgb, at(p + ivec2(0, 1)).rgb, at(p + ivec2(-1, 0)).rgb,
                         at(p + ivec2(1, 0)).rgb, aa.params.x);
    o_color = vec4(sharp, c.a);
}
```

`runtime/src/ai_trace.c`:

```c
/* YW4_TRACE_AI=1: who in the game evaluates the battle AI's conditions (debugging only).
 *
 * The AI tables (gamedata/battle/ai/..._ai.cfg.bin: party_ai, enemy_ai, ...) hold their conditions as small encoded
 * expressions (base64 in the file): "00 00 00 00 <size> <count>", then e.g. 35 <u32 function hash> ... 32 <u32 constant>
 * ... 78 (a comparison). A background thread looks for one of party_ai's expressions in the game's memory every 3
 * seconds, decoded first, else as the file's base64 text, and puts a read watch (host.c) on the first copy found: the
 * reads are reported with the reader's guest call stack (kernel.c). That names the evaluator, the next step to reading
 * the AI's rules. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "host.h"
#include "kernel.h"
#include "yw4load.h"
#include "yw4rt.h"

#ifdef _WIN32
#include <windows.h>

/* party_ai's condition 23 (an HP check, the hash 0x4e97c967 then 0x8996b8e1 and a constant 300): decoded and as base64 */
static const uint8_t EXPR[] = {0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x1e, 0x0b, 0x35, 0x67, 0xc9, 0x97, 0x4e, 0x00, 0x01, 0x00, 0x32,
                               0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x78, 0x35, 0xe1, 0xb8, 0x96, 0x89, 0x00, 0x01, 0x00, 0x32,
                               0x00, 0x00, 0x01, 0x2c, 0x71, 0x8f};
static const char EXPR64[] = "AAAAAB4LNWfJl04AAQAyAAAAAHg14biWiQABADIAAAEscY8=";

/* The first copy of `pat` in the game's committed memory, or 0. */
static uint64_t find(const void *pat, size_t n) {
    for (uint64_t a = YW4_GUEST_LO; a < YW4_GUEST_HI;) {
        MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION mbi;
        if (!VirtualQuery((void *)(uintptr_t)a, &mbi, sizeof mbi)) break;
        uint64_t base = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)mbi.BaseAddress, end = base + mbi.RegionSize;
        if (mbi.State == MEM_COMMIT && (mbi.Protect & (PAGE_READWRITE | PAGE_READONLY)) && !(mbi.Protect & PAGE_GUARD)) {
            const uint8_t *p = (const uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)base, *e = p + mbi.RegionSize;
            for (; p + n <= e; p++) {
                p = memchr(p, ((const uint8_t *)pat)[0], (size_t)(e - p - n + 1));
                if (!p) break;
                if (!memcmp(p, pat, n)) return (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)p;
            }
        }
        a = end > a ? end : a + 4096;
    }
    return 0;
}

static void search(void *arg) {
    (void)arg;
    for (int round = 0; round < 200; round++) {  /* 10 minutes */
        Sleep(3000);
        /* the expression's core from its first call on (the game may keep it without the 4-byte header and the size) */
        uint64_t at = find(EXPR + 6, 19);
        int decoded = at != 0;
        if (!at && round >= 20) at = find(EXPR64, sizeof EXPR64 - 1);  /* after a minute: the base64 text */
        if (!at) continue;
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: ai: party_ai's condition 23 found %s at %#llx\n", decoded ? "decoded" : "as base64 text",
                (unsigned long long)at);
        yw4_read_watch_arm(at, decoded ? 19 : sizeof EXPR64 - 1, 40);
        return;
    }
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: ai: party_ai's condition 23 not found in memory\n");
}

/* YW4_TRACE_AI=2: from the loader instead. The cfg reader's handler for BTL_AI_COND_DATA entries (main+0x3db1e0, the
 * table at main_000.c's schema registrations: hash ddd4ac39) fills a 0x30-byte record at [[[x0]+0x20]+0x30]: +0 the
 * condition's name hash, +4..+0x1c floats (-1 = unset), +0x20 flags, +0x28 the decoded expression (or 0).
 * Loads come in batches: battle_ai's 30 at start-up, the fight's own tables (party_ai, enemy_ai, ...) when a battle
 * begins. Once a batch is complete, a read watch goes on the page holding most of its expressions:
 * the reads name the code that evaluates them (reads from the loader's path, main+0x990888, are its linking). */
extern void (*yw4_entry_hook)(CPUState *ctx, uint64_t addr);  /* dispatch.c */
enum { MAX_RECS = 8192 };
static uint64_t cond_fn, recs[MAX_RECS];
static volatile long nrecs, batch, batch_start;
static volatile LONG64 last_load_ms;

static uint64_t peek(uint64_t p) {
    return p >= 0x7000000000ull && p < 0x7800000000ull && !(p & 7) ? *(const uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)p : 0;
}

static void dump_rec(const char *what, uint64_t r) {
    const uint32_t *w = (const uint32_t *)(uintptr_t)r;
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: ai: %s record %#llx:", what, (unsigned long long)r);
    for (int i = 0; i < 12; i++) fprintf(stderr, " %08x", w[i]);
    uint64_t p = peek(r + 0x28);
    if (p) {
        fprintf(stderr, "  [+0x28]:");
        for (int i = 0; i < 24; i++) fprintf(stderr, " %02x", ((const uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)p)[i]);
    }
    fprintf(stderr, "\n");
}

/* The evaluator (main+0x97f770, found by the watch above, 2026-11-12) calls a query by its hash: a sorted table of
 * 0x18-byte entries (+8 the u32 hash, +0x10 the function) at [[x0+0x208]+8], [x0+0x208] starting with an s16 count.
 * The first evaluation writes the table out: which function answers which query. */
static uint64_t vm_fn;
static void dump_queries(CPUState *ctx) {
    uint64_t reg = peek(ctx->x[0] + 0x208);
    if (!reg) return;
    const uint8_t *h = (const uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)reg;
    int16_t n;
    memcpy(&n, h, 2);
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: ai: query table at %#llx:", (unsigned long long)reg);
    for (int i = 0; i < 32; i++) fprintf(stderr, " %02x", h[i]);
    fprintf(stderr, "\nyw4: ai: %d queries\n", n);
    uint64_t e = peek(reg + 8);
    for (int i = 0; e && i < n && i < 400; i++, e += 0x18) {
        uint64_t q0 = *(const uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)e, fn = peek(e + 0x10);
        uint32_t hash = *(const uint32_t *)(uintptr_t)(e + 8);
        char a[48], name[64] = "";
        if (q0 >= 0x7000000000ull && q0 < 0x7800000000ull) {  /* a name? */
            const char *c = (const char *)(uintptr_t)q0;
            int k = 0;
            while (k < 63 && c[k] >= 0x20 && c[k] < 0x7f) name[k] = c[k], k++;
            name[k] = 0;
        }
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: ai: query %08x -> %s  (+0 %#llx%s%s)\n", hash, yw4_describe(fn, a), (unsigned long long)q0,
                name[0] ? " = " : "", name);
    }
}

static void cond_hook(CPUState *ctx, uint64_t addr) {
    if (addr == vm_fn) {
        static int dumped;
        if (!dumped) dumped = 1, dump_queries(ctx);
        return;
    }
    if (addr != cond_fn) return;
    uint64_t rec = peek(peek(peek(ctx->x[0]) + 0x20) + 0x30);
    if (!rec || nrecs >= MAX_RECS) return;
    uint64_t now = GetTickCount64();
    if (!nrecs || now - (uint64_t)last_load_ms > 3000) {  /* a new batch */
        batch++, batch_start = nrecs;
        uint64_t st[10];
        int k = yw4_call_stack(ctx, st, 10);
        char a[48];
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: ai: batch %ld of condition records starts at %#llx, loaded from:\n", batch,
                (unsigned long long)rec);
        for (int j = 0; j < k; j++) fprintf(stderr, "       %s\n", yw4_describe(st[j] - 4, a));
    }
    recs[nrecs++] = rec;
    last_load_ms = (LONG64)now;
}

static void watch_after_loads(void *arg) {
    (void)arg;
    long done = 0;
    for (;;) {
        Sleep(2000);
        if (batch == done || GetTickCount64() - (uint64_t)last_load_ms < 8000) continue;
        long b = batch, from = batch_start, to = nrecs;
        done = b;
        int with = 0;
        for (long i = from; i < to; i++) with += peek(recs[i] + 0x28) != 0;
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: ai: batch %ld complete: %ld records, %d with an expression\n", b, to - from, with);
        for (long i = from; i < to && i < from + 6; i++) dump_rec("e.g.", recs[i]);
        /* the first batch (battle_ai, at start-up) is what a fight reads: no other batch came in one (2026-11-12) */
        /* the page with the most expressions of this batch, and their span in it */
        uint64_t best = 0;
        int best_n = 0;
        for (long i = from; i < to; i++) {
            uint64_t p = peek(recs[i] + 0x28) & ~4095ull;
            if (!p) continue;
            int n = 0;
            for (long j = from; j < to; j++) n += (peek(recs[j] + 0x28) & ~4095ull) == p;
            if (n > best_n) best_n = n, best = p;
        }
        if (!best) continue;
        uint64_t lo = best + 4096, hi = best;
        for (long i = from; i < to; i++) {
            uint64_t p = peek(recs[i] + 0x28);
            if ((p & ~4095ull) != best) continue;
            if (p < lo) lo = p;
            if (p + 0x40 > hi) hi = p + 0x40;
        }
        if (hi > best + 4096) hi = best + 4096;
        /* the records may follow the expressions on the same page: the linker reads those at every battle start, and
         * they used up the reports (2026-11-12); the watch stops short of the first record above the expressions */
        for (long i = 0; i < nrecs; i++)
            if (recs[i] >= lo && recs[i] < hi) hi = recs[i];
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: ai: %d expressions of batch %ld on page %#llx: watching their reads\n", best_n, b,
                (unsigned long long)best);
        yw4_read_watch_arm(lo, hi - lo, 120);
        return;
    }
}

void ai_trace_start(void) {
    const char *e = getenv("YW4_TRACE_AI");
    if (e && *e == '2') {
        cond_fn = yw4_image_base + 0x3db1e0;
        vm_fn = yw4_image_base + 0x97f770;
        yw4_entry_hook = cond_hook;
        yw4_probe_any = 1;
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: ai: logging the battle AI's condition records as they load (YW4_TRACE_AI=2)\n");
        host_thread_start(watch_after_loads, NULL, 1 << 16);
        return;
    }
    if (!e || *e != '1') return;
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: ai: looking for the battle AI's conditions in memory (YW4_TRACE_AI)\n");
    host_thread_start(search, NULL, 1 << 20);
}
#else
void ai_trace_start(void) {}
#endif

```

`runtime/src/battle.c`:

```c
/* Battles: whether the game's battle scene is running, for the controls' battle set of keys (bindings.c).
 *
 * The battle scene is a yw::CSceneBattle (vtable main+0x14cbcf0, 18 functions). Of its own functions, four run
 * once every frame of a battle and none outside one (counted 2026-11-01 in the owner's battle: 600 calls per 600
 * frames, 0 before and after; two others ran once at its start). The hook on one of them notes the time; a
 * battle is on while that was less than a quarter second ago. The game's own code then runs as usual. */
#include <stdint.h>

#include "battle.h"
#include "host.h"
#include "yw4rt.h"

static int64_t last_frame_ns;

int yw4_hook_battle_frame(CPUState *ctx) {
    (void)ctx;
    __atomic_store_n(&last_frame_ns, host_now_ns(), __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    return 0;
}

int battle_active(void) {
    int64_t t = __atomic_load_n(&last_frame_ns, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
    return t && host_now_ns() - t < 250000000;
}

```

`runtime/src/bindings.c`:

```c
/* The controls (bindings.h): a table of Switch inputs, each with two keyboard/mouse keys and one gamepad input,
 * read into the Switch controller state every time the window polls; the panel page that changes them;
 * the mouse turning the camera (hook inside f_846260); and the on-screen button icons following the bindings
 * and the device in use: keyboard and mouse, or a PlayStation, Xbox or Nintendo controller (hook on f_a8c3f0). */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include <SDL3/SDL.h>

#include "battle.h"
#include "bindings.h"
#include "gaiji_create.h"
#include "mousemenu.h"
#include "pause.h"
#include "run.h"
#include "savefs.h"
#include "settings.h"
#include "shortcutwheel.h"
#include "window.h"
#include "yw4fp.h"
#include "yw4load.h"
#include "yw4rt.h"

/* A gamepad input: a button (SDL_GamepadButton), a stick or trigger pushed one way, or a face button by its
 * name (PAD_FACE + 0..3: A, B, X, Y as printed on the connected controller: confirm on a PlayStation pad is
 * cross, on a Nintendo one the right button). */
enum { PAD_NONE = -1, PAD_AXIS = 100, PAD_FACE = 200 };
/* An input of ours that the game never sees (Run / Walk, run.c): read here, not sent as a Switch button */
enum { INPUT_OURS = -2 };
#define AXIS(a, positive) (PAD_AXIS + (a) * 2 + (positive))

typedef struct {
    const char *group, *name, *id;  /* id: the name in the settings file */
    int bit;                        /* the Switch button; -1 for a stick direction; INPUT_OURS for one of ours */
    int stick, sign;                /* the stick direction: 0 left x, 1 left y, 2 right x, 3 right y; +1/-1 */
    int keys[BIND_KEYS];            /* the starting binding: SDL_Scancode or MOUSE_BIND_* */
    int pad;
} Input;

/* The starting keys are the owner's own (2026-11-13: "ship my keys as defaults"); the battle set's are below. */
static const Input inputs[] = {

     * hints, every button having a job already (owner, 2026-11-18) */
    {"BUTTONS", "RUN", "RUN", INPUT_OURS, 0, 0, {SDL_SCANCODE_LSHIFT}, SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_LEFT_STICK},
```
