```c
enum { SHEET_NX, SHEET_KEY, SHEET_PAD };

/* "N/A" for a button with nothing bound (owner, 2026-11-15): one icon per style, our drawings (gaiji_create.h),
 * written over keyboard-sheet cells the hints never show (bindings_patch_sheet); that sheet is always on. */
static int na_written;
static int na_ready(void) { return __atomic_load_n(&na_written, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE); }
static uint32_t na_crc(int i) {
    static uint32_t crcs[GAIJI_NAS];
    if (!crcs[i]) crcs[i] = gaiji_crc(gaiji_na_at[i].name);
    return crcs[i];
}
static int na_style(uint32_t crc) {  /* which N/A icon a name is, or -1 */
    if (!na_ready()) return -1;
    for (int i = 0; i < GAIJI_NAS; i++)
        if (na_crc(i) == crc) return i;
    return -1;
}

/* The icon to show for a Switch icon name the game asked for, or 0 to leave it; *sheet: which sheet it is in. */
static uint32_t gaiji_swap(uint32_t crc, int *sheet) {
    int i = 0;
    while (i < n_nx_names && nx_names[i].crc != crc) i++;
    if (i == n_nx_names) return 0;  /* not a button: one of the game's own icons */
    int g = nx_names[i].glyph, style = nx_names[i].style, row = glyphs[g].row;
    sets_ready();
    const Bound *use = sets[battle_active() ? SET_BATTLE : SET_FIELD];  /* the keys in use now */
    if (!using_pad) {
        /* the title's Continue: its hint's X Delete shows the X key, which deletes there (savefs.c; the X key is
         * the game's Minus elsewhere, so the X button's own key would be another; owner, 2026-11-17) */
        static int in_x = -2;
        if (in_x == -2) in_x = input_by_id("X");
        if (row == in_x && savefs_diary_open() && scene_on_title())
            return *sheet = SHEET_KEY, gaiji_crc(key_gaiji(SDL_SCANCODE_X));
        /* the row's first key that has an icon, else its mouse part (the keyboard first: owner, 2026-11-13); in
         * battles the mouse first (owner, 2026-11-13: you attack and aim with the mouse there, so the hint shows
         * the mouse button, not U or O). Groups (a stick, the whole D-pad) keep the Switch icon: the keyboard sheet
         * has none for a set of keys */
        const int battle = battle_active() != 0;
        const int *mouse = mouse_map[battle ? SET_BATTLE : SET_FIELD];
        /* the battle's Stopwatching menu: Switch enemy is R, and ZR does it too. When every key of R is also an A
         * key (the default battle set's E), pressing it chooses the menu's line instead, so the hint shows ZR's key,
         * the one that works there (the owner's F; owner, 2026-11-15) */
        static int in_a = -2, in_r, in_zr;
        if (in_a == -2) in_a = input_by_id("A"), in_r = input_by_id("R"), in_zr = input_by_id("ZR");
        if (battle && row == in_r && in_a >= 0 && in_zr >= 0 && mousemenu_stopwatch()) {
            int clash = 1, any = 0;
            for (int k = 0; k < BIND_KEYS; k++) {
                int sc = use[in_r].keys[k];
                if (!sc) continue;
                any = 1;
                if (sc != use[in_a].keys[0] && sc != use[in_a].keys[1]) clash = 0;
            }
            if (any && clash && (use[in_zr].keys[0] || use[in_zr].keys[1])) row = in_zr;
        }
        /* and L (switch ally there) shows the left stick press's key, which presses it there (bindings_read) */
        static int hl = -2, hls;
        if (hl == -2) hl = input_by_id("L"), hls = input_by_id("LS_PRESS");
        if (battle && row == hl && hls >= 0 && mousemenu_stopwatch() && !use[hl].keys[0] && !use[hl].keys[1] &&
            (use[hls].keys[0] || use[hls].keys[1]))
            row = hls;  /* only when L has no key of its own: else its own key shows */
        int has_key = 0;
        for (int pass = 0; row >= 0 && pass < 2; pass++) {
            if (pass == !battle) {  /* the mouse: pass 0 in battles, pass 1 when exploring */
                for (int p = 0; p < BMOUSE_PARTS; p++)
                    if (mouse[p] == row) return *sheet = SHEET_KEY, gaiji_crc(key_gaiji(mouse_code[p]));
            } else {
                for (int k = 0; k < BIND_KEYS; k++) {
                    const char *name = use[row].keys[k] ? key_gaiji(use[row].keys[k]) : NULL;
                    has_key |= use[row].keys[k] != 0;
                    if (name) return *sheet = SHEET_KEY, gaiji_crc(name);
                }
            }
        }
        /* nothing bound to it (a key without an icon of its own keeps the Switch icon): N/A (owner, 2026-11-15) */
        if (row >= 0 && !has_key && na_ready()) return *sheet = SHEET_KEY, na_crc(GAIJI_NA_KEY);
        return 0;
    }
    int shown = g;
    if (row >= 0) {
        if (use[row].pad == PAD_NONE && na_ready())  /* no pad input bound to it: N/A, in the hints' style */
            return *sheet = SHEET_KEY, na_crc(hint_style() == STYLE_PLAYSTATION ? GAIJI_NA_PS
                                              : hint_style() == STYLE_XBOX      ? GAIJI_NA_XBOX
                                                                                : GAIJI_NA_NX);
        int p = glyph_for_pad(resolve(use[row].pad));
        if (p >= 0) shown = p;
    }
    if (hint_style() != STYLE_NINTENDO) return *sheet = SHEET_PAD, pad_crc[shown];
    if (shown == g) return 0;
    char name[48];
    nx_name(shown, style, name, sizeof name);
    if (!nx_has(name)) nx_name(shown, 0, name, sizeof name);  /* that icon lacks the style: the plain one */
    return gaiji_crc(name);
}

/* The keyboard, PlayStation and Xbox sheets' icons fill less of their cell than the Switch ones (more empty
 * border), so they are drawn this much larger, around the same centre. */
static float icon_scale(int sheet) {
    static float scale[3];
    if (!scale[SHEET_KEY]) {
        const char *k = getenv("YW4_KEY_ICON_SCALE"), *p = getenv("YW4_PAD_ICON_SCALE");
        scale[SHEET_NX] = 1.0f;
        scale[SHEET_KEY] = k && atof(k) > 0 ? (float)atof(k) : 1.5f;
        scale[SHEET_PAD] = p && atof(p) > 0 ? (float)atof(p) : 1.25f;
    }
    return scale[sheet];
}

/* The keyboard sheet's mouse icons fill more of their cell than its keys: at the keys' scale they looked too large
 * (owner, 2026-11-04: 1.3% smaller, 0.987; 2026-11-11: "still too large", 30% smaller again, 0.987 x 0.7). They get
 * this much of the keys' scale (YW4_MOUSE_ICON_SCALE); centred in the same place. */
static float mouse_icon_scale(uint32_t crc) {
    static uint32_t crcs[7];
    static float k;
    if (!k) {
        static const int ids[7] = {MOUSE_BIND_LEFT, MOUSE_BIND_RIGHT, MOUSE_BIND_MIDDLE, MOUSE_BIND_X1, MOUSE_BIND_X2,
                                   MOUSE_BIND_WHEEL_UP, MOUSE_BIND_WHEEL_DOWN};
        for (int i = 0; i < 7; i++) crcs[i] = gaiji_crc(key_gaiji(ids[i]));
        const char *e = getenv("YW4_MOUSE_ICON_SCALE");
        k = e && atof(e) > 0 ? (float)atof(e) : 0.69f;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < 7; i++)
        if (crcs[i] == crc) return k;
    return 1.0f;
}

/* A request's box: +4 x (left), +8 y (middle), +0xc and +0x10 its size, in pixels. */
typedef struct {
    int32_t x, y, h, w;
} Box;

static Box box_get(uint64_t req) {
    return (Box){(int32_t)ld32(req + 4), (int32_t)ld32(req + 8), (int32_t)ld32(req + 0xc), (int32_t)ld32(req + 0x10)};
}

/* What each request had from the game, by request address: a request changed once still holds our name and
 * box next frame if the game didn't write it again, and must be changed again from the game's. */
enum { REMEMBERED = 4096 };
static struct {
    uint64_t req;
    uint32_t game, shown;
    Box game_box, shown_box;
} remembered[REMEMBERED];

static void gc_follow(void);  /* the PlayStation sheet's middle buttons, below */

int yw4_hook_gaiji_render(CPUState *ctx) {
    uint64_t main_base = *yw4_modules[YW4_MAIN].base;
    uint64_t sheets = ld64(main_base + 0x58654f8);
    uint32_t nsheets = ld32(main_base + 0x5865500);
    if (!sheets || nsheets < 5 || ctx->x[0] != ld64(sheets)) return 0;  /* only before sheet 0 */
    ready();
    gaiji_init();
    gc_follow();
    uint64_t ps = ld64(sheets), xbox = ld64(sheets + 8), key = ld64(sheets + 16);
    if (ps) st8(ps + 0x1c, (uint8_t)(using_pad && hint_style() == STYLE_PLAYSTATION));
    if (xbox) st8(xbox + 0x1c, (uint8_t)(using_pad && hint_style() == STYLE_XBOX));
    if (key) st8(key + 0x1c, 1);
    uint64_t reqs = ctx->x[2];
    uint32_t n = (uint32_t)ctx->x[3];
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        uint64_t req = reqs + (uint64_t)i * 0x38;
        uint32_t now = ld32(req);
        if (!now) continue;
        unsigned slot = (unsigned)(((req >> 3) * 2654435761u) % REMEMBERED);
        Box box = box_get(req);
        int ours = remembered[slot].req == req && remembered[slot].shown == now &&
                   !memcmp(&remembered[slot].shown_box, &box, sizeof box);
        uint32_t game = ours ? remembered[slot].game : now;
        Box game_box = ours ? remembered[slot].game_box : box;
        int sheet = SHEET_NX;
        uint32_t shown = gaiji_swap(game, &sheet);
        if (!shown) shown = game;
        Box shown_box = game_box;
        if (sheet != SHEET_NX) {
            float mk = sheet == SHEET_KEY ? mouse_icon_scale(shown) : 1.0f;
            float k = icon_scale(sheet) * mk;
            int na = na_style(shown);  /* N/A in the keyboard sheet: the size of its style's own icons */
            if (na >= 0) k = na == GAIJI_NA_KEY ? icon_scale(SHEET_KEY) : na == GAIJI_NA_NX ? 1.0f : icon_scale(SHEET_PAD);
            /* the box is whole pixels of the HUD's 1080-line space: rounded to the nearest (the mouse icons were
             * rounded down while they were only 1.3% smaller, under half a pixel) */
            float round_add = 0.5f;
            (void)mk;
            shown_box.h = (int32_t)((float)game_box.h * k + round_add);
            shown_box.w = (int32_t)((float)game_box.w * k + round_add);
            shown_box.x = game_box.x - (shown_box.w - game_box.w) / 2;
        }
        if (shown != now) st32(req, shown);
        if (memcmp(&shown_box, &box, sizeof box)) {
            st32(req + 4, (uint32_t)shown_box.x), st32(req + 8, (uint32_t)shown_box.y);
            st32(req + 0xc, (uint32_t)shown_box.h), st32(req + 0x10, (uint32_t)shown_box.w);
        }
        remembered[slot].req = req, remembered[slot].game = game, remembered[slot].shown = shown;
        remembered[slot].game_box = game_box, remembered[slot].shown_box = shown_box;
    }
    return 0;
}

/* ---- the PlayStation sheet's middle buttons (owner, 2026-11-13). The game ships only a PS4 sheet, so its Minus
 * icon (gaiji_bt09, at 104,104 in the 256 x 256 BC7 sheet) is the PS4 touchpad: the wrong button on every
 * PlayStation pad (auto battle is on Create on a DualSense, Share on a DualShock 4, Select on a PS3 pad), and its
 * Plus icon (gaiji_bt10, at 156,0) says OPTIONS, which a PS3 pad calls Start. Those cells are rewritten in the
 * game's memory for the pad in use, in the Options icon's style: the word above a small dark pill. Rows 0-23 are
 * our drawing (gaiji_create.h, from tools/yw4/gaiji_create.py: the word and the pill's top, which Options hides
 * under its word); rows 24-47 are the Options icon's own, from the same texture, so no game art is in the repo.
 *
 * The first time, before the texture's first upload (gpu.c), the sheet is known by the touchpad icon's blocks (a
 * fingerprint); its Options top half is kept here then, to put back. After that the hint hook (game thread) writes
 * the cells again when the PlayStation model changes, and tells the GPU layer (gpu_note_written), which uploads the
 * texture again. Before each such write the cells must still be what we wrote (else the memory is something else
 * now and is left alone). */
#include "gpu.h"

enum { GC_CELL = 48, GC_TOP = 24, GC_ROW = GC_CELL / 4 * 16, GC_HALF = GC_TOP / 4 * GC_ROW };
static uint8_t *gc_texels;  /* the sheet's storage once found (set once, by the GPU thread) */
static TexLayout gc_layout;
static uint8_t gc_options_top[GC_HALF], gc_body[GC_HALF];  /* bt10's own rows 0-23 and 24-47 */
static int gc_model;                                       /* the model the cells are written for (3, 4, 5) */
static uint64_t gc_print9, gc_print10;                     /* what the cells hold now */

/* The Xbox sheet: an Xbox 360 pad's Back and Start (a left and a right triangle) in place of View and Menu, in the
 * middle 6 x 4 blocks of the two circle icons (x 12-35, y 16-31 of the cell; the circle's edge stays the game's).
 * Found the same way (the View icon's fingerprint); the game's own middles are kept, to put back for other pads. */
enum { XB_X = 12, XB_Y = 16, XB_W = 24, XB_H = 16, XB_SIZE = XB_W / 4 * XB_H / 4 * 16 };
static uint8_t *gc_xb_texels;
static TexLayout gc_xb_layout;
static uint8_t gc_xb_view[XB_SIZE], gc_xb_menu[XB_SIZE];
static int gc_xb_mode = -1;  /* written for: 1 an Xbox 360 pad, 0 others (the game's View and Menu) */
static uint64_t gc_xb_print9, gc_xb_print10;

int bindings_ps_model(void) { return ps_model; }
int bindings_xbox360(void) { return xbox360; }

static uint64_t gc_fnv(const uint8_t *p, size_t n) {
    uint64_t h = 0xcbf29ce484222325ull;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; i++) h = (h ^ p[i]) * 0x100000001b3ull;
    return h;
}

/* both cells for a model, into the sheet; their fingerprints kept */
static void gc_write(uint8_t *texels, int model) {
    uint8_t cell[2 * GC_HALF];
    const TexLayout *L = &gc_layout;
    int word9 = model == 3 ? GAIJI_WORD_SELECT : model == 4 ? GAIJI_WORD_SHARE : GAIJI_WORD_CREATE;
    memcpy(cell, gaiji_word_top[word9], GC_HALF);
    memcpy(cell + GC_HALF, gc_body, GC_HALF);
    tegra_write_region(L, texels, 0, 0, 104, 104, 0, GC_CELL, GC_CELL, 1, cell);
    gc_print9 = gc_fnv(cell, sizeof cell);
    memcpy(cell, model == 3 ? gaiji_word_top[GAIJI_WORD_START] : gc_options_top, GC_HALF);
    tegra_write_region(L, texels, 0, 0, 156, 0, 0, GC_CELL, GC_CELL, 1, cell);
    gc_print10 = gc_fnv(cell, sizeof cell);
    gc_model = model;
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: hints: PlayStation sheet: %s and %s (PS%d)\n",
            model == 3 ? "SELECT" : model == 4 ? "SHARE" : "CREATE", model == 3 ? "START" : "OPTIONS", model);
}

static void xb_found(const TexLayout *L, uint8_t *texels);

void bindings_patch_sheet(const TexLayout *L, uint32_t nvn_format, uint8_t *texels) {
    if (texels && (nvn_format == 0x4D || nvn_format == 0x4E) && L->width == 620 && L->height == 620 && L->depth == 1 &&
        L->layers == 1 && !__atomic_load_n(&na_written, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)) {
        /* the keyboard sheet (known by its E key's blocks): the four N/A icons over cells the hints never show,
         * once, before its first upload */
        uint8_t cell[2 * GC_HALF];
        tegra_read_region(L, texels, 0, 0, 52, 156, 0, GC_CELL, GC_CELL, 1, cell);
        if (gc_fnv(cell, sizeof cell) == GAIJI_KEY_E_PRINT) {
            for (int i = 0; i < GAIJI_NAS; i++)
                tegra_write_region(L, texels, 0, 0, gaiji_na_at[i].x, gaiji_na_at[i].y, 0, GC_CELL, GC_CELL, 1, gaiji_na[i]);
            __atomic_store_n(&na_written, 1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
            fprintf(stderr, "yw4: hints: keyboard sheet: N/A icons written\n");
        }
        return;
    }
    if (!texels || (nvn_format != 0x4D && nvn_format != 0x4E) || L->width != 256 || L->height != 256 ||
        L->depth != 1 || L->layers != 1)
        return;
    uint8_t cell[2 * GC_HALF];
    tegra_read_region(L, texels, 0, 0, 104, 104, 0, GC_CELL, GC_CELL, 1, cell);
    uint64_t h = gc_fnv(cell, sizeof cell);
    if (h == GAIJI_XBOX_VIEW_PRINT && !__atomic_load_n(&gc_xb_texels, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)) xb_found(L, texels);
    if (h != GAIJI_TOUCHPAD_PRINT || __atomic_load_n(&gc_texels, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)) return;
    gc_layout = *L;
    tegra_read_region(L, texels, 0, 0, 156, 0, 0, GC_CELL, GC_CELL, 1, cell);
    memcpy(gc_options_top, cell, GC_HALF);
    memcpy(gc_body, cell + GC_HALF, GC_HALF);
    gc_write(texels, ps_model);  /* before the upload this is called from: nothing more to tell the GPU layer */
    __atomic_store_n(&gc_texels, texels, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);  /* only now may the hint hook write too */
}

static void xb_write(uint8_t *texels, int mode) {
    const TexLayout *L = &gc_xb_layout;
    const uint8_t *a = mode ? gaiji_xbox_back : gc_xb_view, *b = mode ? gaiji_xbox_start : gc_xb_menu;
    tegra_write_region(L, texels, 0, 0, 104 + XB_X, 104 + XB_Y, 0, XB_W, XB_H, 1, a);
    tegra_write_region(L, texels, 0, 0, 156 + XB_X, 0 + XB_Y, 0, XB_W, XB_H, 1, b);
    gc_xb_print9 = gc_fnv(a, XB_SIZE), gc_xb_print10 = gc_fnv(b, XB_SIZE);
    gc_xb_mode = mode;
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: hints: Xbox sheet: %s\n", mode ? "Back and Start (Xbox 360)" : "View and Menu");
}

static void xb_found(const TexLayout *L, uint8_t *texels) {
    gc_xb_layout = *L;
    tegra_read_region(L, texels, 0, 0, 104 + XB_X, 104 + XB_Y, 0, XB_W, XB_H, 1, gc_xb_view);
    tegra_read_region(L, texels, 0, 0, 156 + XB_X, 0 + XB_Y, 0, XB_W, XB_H, 1, gc_xb_menu);
    gc_xb_print9 = gc_fnv(gc_xb_view, XB_SIZE), gc_xb_print10 = gc_fnv(gc_xb_menu, XB_SIZE);
    gc_xb_mode = 0;
    if (xbox360) xb_write(texels, 1);  /* before the upload this is called from */
    __atomic_store_n(&gc_xb_texels, texels, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
}

/* the Xbox sheet again when the pad changed between an Xbox 360 pad and others */
static void xb_follow(void) {
    uint8_t *texels = __atomic_load_n(&gc_xb_texels, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
    if (!texels || gc_xb_mode == xbox360) return;
    uint8_t a[XB_SIZE], b[XB_SIZE];
    tegra_read_region(&gc_xb_layout, texels, 0, 0, 104 + XB_X, 104 + XB_Y, 0, XB_W, XB_H, 1, a);
    tegra_read_region(&gc_xb_layout, texels, 0, 0, 156 + XB_X, 0 + XB_Y, 0, XB_W, XB_H, 1, b);
    if (gc_fnv(a, XB_SIZE) != gc_xb_print9 || gc_fnv(b, XB_SIZE) != gc_xb_print10) {
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: hints: Xbox sheet changed under us; its icons are left as they are\n");
        __atomic_store_n(&gc_xb_texels, NULL, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
        return;
    }
    xb_write(texels, xbox360);
    gpu_note_written((uint64_t)(uintptr_t)texels, tegra_total_size(&gc_xb_layout));
}

/* the hint hook, each frame: the cells again when the PlayStation model (or Xbox 360 or not) changed */
static void gc_follow(void) {
    xb_follow();
    uint8_t *texels = __atomic_load_n(&gc_texels, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
    if (!texels || gc_model == ps_model) return;
    uint8_t cell[2 * GC_HALF];
    tegra_read_region(&gc_layout, texels, 0, 0, 104, 104, 0, GC_CELL, GC_CELL, 1, cell);
    uint64_t p9 = gc_fnv(cell, sizeof cell);
    tegra_read_region(&gc_layout, texels, 0, 0, 156, 0, 0, GC_CELL, GC_CELL, 1, cell);
    if (p9 != gc_print9 || gc_fnv(cell, sizeof cell) != gc_print10) {  /* not ours any more: leave it */
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: hints: PlayStation sheet changed under us; its icons are left as they are\n");
        __atomic_store_n(&gc_texels, NULL, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
        return;
    }
    gc_write(texels, ps_model);
    gpu_note_written((uint64_t)(uintptr_t)texels, tegra_total_size(&gc_layout));
}

/* ---- the panel page */

static int row, col, capturing;
static uint64_t capture_since;
/* The controller was used last (window.c used_pad): the binding rows keep to the controller column, so a pad can't
 * change or clear a keyboard key (owner, 2026-11-13). The keyboard and mouse still reach every column. */
static int pad_only;
void bindings_pad_only(int on) {
    pad_only = on;
    if (on && !capturing) col = BIND_KEYS;
}

int bindings_capturing(void) {
    if (capturing && SDL_GetTicks() - capture_since > 5000) capturing = 0;
    return capturing;
}
void bindings_cancel(void) { capturing = 0; }

void bindings_select(int r, int c) {
    if (capturing || r < 0 || r >= NROWS) return;
    row = r;
    if (c >= 0 && c < BIND_COLS) col = c;
    if (pad_only) col = BIND_KEYS;
}

void bindings_action(int action) {
    sets_ready();
    if (pad_only && !capturing) col = BIND_KEYS;
    int sens = row - SENS_ROW;  /* the sensitivity rows' axis */
    switch (action) {
    /* the ends stop the choice (no wrapping round: holding a direction stops at the last row) */
    case SETTINGS_UP: row = row > 0 ? row - 1 : 0; break;
    case SETTINGS_DOWN: row = row < NROWS - 1 ? row + 1 : NROWS - 1; break;
    case SETTINGS_LEFT:
    case SETTINGS_RIGHT:
        if (row == SET_ROW) {
            edit_set = !edit_set;
        } else if (row >= SENS_ROW && row < SENS_ROW + NMOUSE) {
            if (action == SETTINGS_LEFT && sens_index(sens) > 0) sens_choice[sens]--, settings_save();
            if (action == SETTINGS_RIGHT && sens_index(sens) < NSENS - 1) sens_choice[sens]++, settings_save();
        } else if (row == RUMBLE_ROW) {
            int next = !window_rumble_enabled();
            window_rumble_set_enabled(next);
            if (next) window_rumble_test();
            settings_save();
        } else if (row == LAYOUT_ROW) {
            nintendo_layout = !nintendo_layout, settings_save();
        } else if (row == WHEEL_ROW) {
            swheel_set_enabled(!swheel_enabled()), settings_save();
        } else if (row == RUN_ROW) {  /* the ends stop, as the sensitivities */
            int m = run_mode() + (action == SETTINGS_RIGHT ? 1 : -1);
            if (m >= 0 && m < RUN_MODES) run_mode_set(m), settings_save();
        } else if (row == MOUSE_ROW) {  /* the Mouse buttons row opens its page (gamemenu.c): nothing here */
        } else if (!pad_only) {  /* a pad stays on its own column */
            col = action == SETTINGS_LEFT ? (col > 0 ? col - 1 : 0) : (col < BIND_COLS - 1 ? col + 1 : BIND_COLS - 1);
        }
        break;
    case SETTINGS_ACCEPT:
        if (row == SET_ROW) {
            edit_set = !edit_set;
        } else if (row >= SENS_ROW && row < SENS_ROW + NMOUSE) {
            sens_choice[sens] = (sens_index(sens) + 1) % NSENS, settings_save();
        } else if (row == RUMBLE_ROW) {
            int next = !window_rumble_enabled();
            window_rumble_set_enabled(next);
            if (next) window_rumble_test();
            settings_save();
        } else if (row == LAYOUT_ROW) {
            nintendo_layout = !nintendo_layout, settings_save();
        } else if (row == WHEEL_ROW) {
            swheel_set_enabled(!swheel_enabled()), settings_save();
        } else if (row == RUN_ROW) {
            run_mode_set((run_mode() + 1) % RUN_MODES), settings_save();
        } else if (row == RESET_ROW) {
            /* the exploring set back to the starting keys; the battle set to a copy of the exploring set */
            if (edit_set == SET_BATTLE) copy_exploring_to_battle();
            else reset_set(SET_FIELD);
            settings_save();
        } else if (row == MOUSE_ROW) {  /* opens its page (gamemenu.c) */
        } else if (row == RUN_INPUT_ROW && run_mode() == RUN_DEFAULT) {  /* greyed out: it does nothing */
        } else {
            capturing = 1, capture_since = SDL_GetTicks();
        }
        break;
    case SETTINGS_CLEAR:
        if (row >= SENS_ROW && row < SENS_ROW + NMOUSE) sens_choice[sens] = SENS_DEFAULT, settings_save();
        if (row == RUMBLE_ROW) {
            window_rumble_set_enabled(1);
            window_rumble_test();
            settings_save();
        }
        if (row == LAYOUT_ROW) nintendo_layout = 0, settings_save();
        if (row == WHEEL_ROW) swheel_set_enabled(1), settings_save();  /* back to its start: on */
        if (row == RUN_ROW) run_mode_set(RUN_DEFAULT), settings_save();  /* back to the game's */
        if (row_input(row) < 0 || (row == RUN_INPUT_ROW && run_mode() == RUN_DEFAULT)) break;
        if (col < BIND_KEYS) bound[row_input(row)].keys[col] = 0;
        else bound[row_input(row)].pad = PAD_NONE;
        settings_save();
        break;
    }
}

int bindings_capture_key(int scancode) {
    if (!bindings_capturing()) return 0;
    capturing = 0;
    if (col < BIND_KEYS) {  /* a key for a key column; the other key of the row cleared if it is the same */
        for (int k = 0; k < BIND_KEYS; k++)
            if (bound[row_input(row)].keys[k] == scancode) bound[row_input(row)].keys[k] = 0;
        bound[row_input(row)].keys[col] = scancode;
        using_pad = 0;
        settings_save();
    }  /* a key while waiting for a gamepad input cancels */
    return 1;
}

/* A mouse part pressed while a key column waits: that part now presses this row's Switch input, in the set shown
 * (the mouse's own binding, mouse_map; the row's keys stay). The side buttons aren't bound (owner, 2026-11-13). */
static int capture_mouse_part(int part) {
    if (!bindings_capturing() || col >= BIND_KEYS || part < 0) return 0;
    capturing = 0;
    mouse_map[edit_set][part] = row_input(row);
    using_pad = 0;
    settings_save();
    return 1;
}
int bindings_capture_mouse(int button) {
    return capture_mouse_part(button == SDL_BUTTON_LEFT ? BMOUSE_LEFT : button == SDL_BUTTON_RIGHT ? BMOUSE_RIGHT
                              : button == SDL_BUTTON_MIDDLE ? BMOUSE_MID : -1);
}
int bindings_capture_wheel(int y) { return capture_mouse_part(y > 0 ? BMOUSE_WHEEL_UP : BMOUSE_WHEEL_DOWN); }

/* ---- the Mouse buttons page (gamemenu.c) */
int bindings_mouse_get(int set, int part) {
    sets_ready();
    return set >= 0 && set < NSETS && part >= 0 && part < BMOUSE_PARTS ? mouse_map[set][part] : -1;
}
void bindings_mouse_set(int set, int part, int input) {
    sets_ready();
    if (set < 0 || set >= NSETS || part < 0 || part >= BMOUSE_PARTS || input < -1 || input >= NINPUTS) return;
    mouse_map[set][part] = input;
    settings_save();
}
/* the inputs a mouse part can press: the buttons and the D-pad (not a stick's directions) */
int bindings_mouse_choices(int *out, int max) {
    int n = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < NINPUTS && n < max; i++)
        if (inputs[i].bit >= 0) out[n++] = i;
    return n;
}
int bindings_on_mouse_row(void) { return row == MOUSE_ROW; }
int bindings_set_shown(void) { return edit_set; }

int bindings_capture_button(int button) {
    if (!bindings_capturing()) return 0;
    capturing = 0;
    if (col == BIND_KEYS) bound[row_input(row)].pad = button, using_pad = 1, settings_save();
    return 1;
}

int bindings_capture_axis(int axis, int value) {
    if (!bindings_capturing() || col != BIND_KEYS || (value < 24000 && value > -24000)) return 0;
    capturing = 0;
    bound[row_input(row)].pad = AXIS(axis, value > 0);
    using_pad = 1;
    settings_save();
    return 1;
}

/* The other Switch input that a key or gamepad input also presses, or -1. On a pad, Run sharing a button with one of
 * the game's is meant (no button is free; owner, 2026-11-18): not marked. */
static int also_used(int self, int key, int pad) {
    for (int i = 0; i < NINPUTS; i++) {
        if (i == self) continue;
        for (int k = 0; k < BIND_KEYS; k++)
            if (key && bound[i].keys[k] == key) return i;
        if (pad != PAD_NONE && resolve(bound[i].pad) == resolve(pad) && self != RUN_INPUT && i != RUN_INPUT) return i;
    }
    return -1;
}

static void input_title(int i, char *s, size_t n) {
    if (inputs[i].group[0] == 'B') snprintf(s, n, "%s", inputs[i].name);
    else snprintf(s, n, "%s %s", inputs[i].group, inputs[i].name);
}
void bindings_input_title(int i, char *s, size_t n) {
    if (i >= 0 && i < NINPUTS) input_title(i, s, n);
    else if (n) *s = 0;
}

/* An input's row: its two keys and its gamepad input, each marked when another input has it too. */
static void input_row(BindRow *r, int i) {
    memset(r, 0, sizeof *r);
    r->group = inputs[i].group, r->name = inputs[i].name, r->id = inputs[i].id;
    for (int k = 0; k < BIND_KEYS; k++) {
        snprintf(r->cells[k], BIND_NAME, "%s", key_name(bound[i].keys[k]));
        r->conflict[k] = also_used(i, bound[i].keys[k], PAD_NONE) >= 0;
    }
    snprintf(r->cells[BIND_KEYS], BIND_NAME, "%s", pad_label(bound[i].pad));
    r->conflict[BIND_KEYS] = also_used(i, 0, bound[i].pad) >= 0;
}

int bindings_rows(BindRow *rows, int max, int *sel_row, int *sel_col, char *help, int help_size) {
    sets_ready();
    int n = 0;
    static const char *const sens_names[NMOUSE] = {"HORIZONTAL", "VERTICAL"};
    for (int a = 0; a < NMOUSE && n < max; a++) {
        BindRow *r = &rows[n++];
        memset(r, 0, sizeof *r);
        r->group = "MOUSE", r->name = sens_names[a], r->value = 1;
        snprintf(r->cells[0], BIND_NAME, "%sX", sens_values[sens_index(a)]);
    }
    if (n < max) {  /* the Mouse buttons row: the overlay draws it as a way into its page */
        BindRow *r = &rows[n++];
        memset(r, 0, sizeof *r);
        r->group = "MOUSE", r->name = "BUTTONS", r->value = 1;
        snprintf(r->cells[0], BIND_NAME, "OPEN");
    }
    if (n < max) {  /* the shortcut wheel: an On / Off pill (gamemenu.c) */
        BindRow *r = &rows[n++];
        memset(r, 0, sizeof *r);
        r->group = "MOUSE", r->name = "SHORTCUT WHEEL", r->value = 1;
        snprintf(r->cells[0], BIND_NAME, "%s", swheel_enabled() ? "ON" : "OFF");
    }
    if (n < max) {
        BindRow *r = &rows[n++];
        memset(r, 0, sizeof *r);
        r->group = "CONTROLLER", r->name = "VIBRATION", r->value = 1;
        snprintf(r->cells[0], BIND_NAME, "%s", window_rumble_enabled() ? "ON" : "OFF");
    }
    if (n < max) {
        BindRow *r = &rows[n++];
        memset(r, 0, sizeof *r);
        r->group = "CONTROLLER", r->name = "NINTENDO ICONS", r->value = 1;
        snprintf(r->cells[0], BIND_NAME, "%s", nintendo_layout ? "ON" : "OFF");
    }
    if (n < max) {  /* RUNNING (RUN_ROW), a setting in both sets, then the Run key under it (RUN_INPUT_ROW) */
        BindRow *r = &rows[n++];
        memset(r, 0, sizeof *r);
        r->group = "RUNNING", r->name = "MODE", r->value = 1;
        snprintf(r->cells[0], BIND_NAME, "%s", run_mode_name(run_mode()));
    }
    if (n < max) {
        input_row(&rows[n], RUN_INPUT);
        rows[n++].disabled = run_mode() == RUN_DEFAULT;  /* greyed out where it does nothing (owner, 2026-11-18) */
    }
    if (n < max) {
        BindRow *r = &rows[n++];
        memset(r, 0, sizeof *r);
        r->group = "KEYS FOR", r->name = "SET", r->value = 1;
        snprintf(r->cells[0], BIND_NAME, "%s", edit_set ? "BATTLES" : "EXPLORING");
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < RUN_INPUT && n < max; i++) input_row(&rows[n++], i);  /* the Switch's inputs */
    if (n < max) {
        BindRow *r = &rows[n++];
        memset(r, 0, sizeof *r);
        r->name = edit_set ? "COPY THE EXPLORING KEYS" : "RESET ALL TO THE STARTING KEYS";
    }
    *sel_row = row, *sel_col = col;
    char title[48], other[48];
    /* each: "WHAT IT IS|HOW TO CHANGE IT" (BIND_HELP_SPLIT): the overlay keeps the second part on its own line, in
     * the same place for every row (owner, 2026-11-18) */
    if (row >= SENS_ROW && row < SENS_ROW + NMOUSE) {
        int a = row - SENS_ROW;
        snprintf(help, (size_t)help_size,
                 "HOW FAST THE CAMERA TURNS %s WITH THE MOUSE: %sX (1.0X TO START), IN BOTH SETS. A CLICK IN THE "
                 "WINDOW GIVES THE MOUSE TO THE GAME, ALT TAKES IT BACK.|LEFT/RIGHT: CHANGE. DELETE OR X: BACK TO 1.0X.",
                 a ? "UP AND DOWN" : "LEFT AND RIGHT", sens_values[sens_index(a)]);
        return n;
    }
    if (row == MOUSE_ROW) {
        snprintf(help, (size_t)help_size,
                 "WHAT THE LEFT AND RIGHT BUTTONS, THE WHEEL PRESS AND TURNING THE WHEEL DO, FOR EXPLORING AND FOR "
                 "BATTLES.|ENTER OR CLICK: OPEN.");
        return n;
    }
    if (row == WHEEL_ROW) {
        snprintf(help, (size_t)help_size,
                 "WHILE EXPLORING, HOLD THE L KEY (1 TO START) AND POINT THE MOUSE AT A SHORTCUT, THEN LET GO TO USE IT. "
                 "LET GO IN THE MIDDLE TO USE NOTHING. L AND THE ARROW KEYS STILL WORK. NOW %s.|LEFT/RIGHT OR "
                 "ENTER/A: TOGGLE.",
                 swheel_enabled() ? "ON" : "OFF");
        return n;
    }
    if (row == RUMBLE_ROW) {
        snprintf(help, (size_t)help_size,
                 "WHETHER CONTROLLER VIBRATION AND HAPTICS ARE ENABLED: %s. WHEN TURNED ON, THE CONTROLLER RUMBLES FOR "
                 "A SECOND AS A TEST.|LEFT/RIGHT OR ENTER/A: TOGGLE.",
                 window_rumble_enabled() ? "ON" : "OFF");
        return n;
    }
    if (row == LAYOUT_ROW) {
        snprintf(help, (size_t)help_size,
                 "FOR NINTENDO-STYLE CONTROLLERS THAT THE GAME SEES AS AN XBOX CONTROLLER: %s. WHEN ON, THE BUTTON "
                 "ICONS SHOW THE LETTERS PRINTED ON YOUR CONTROLLER. THE BUTTONS KEEP THEIR PLACES.|LEFT/RIGHT OR "
                 "ENTER/A: TOGGLE.",
                 nintendo_layout ? "ON" : "OFF");
        return n;
    }
    if (row == SET_ROW) {
        snprintf(help, (size_t)help_size,
                 "WHICH KEYS THIS PAGE SHOWS AND CHANGES: THE ONES FOR EXPLORING OR THE ONES FOR BATTLES. THE GAME "
                 "USES EACH SET BY ITSELF, SO A KEY CAN DO ONE THING ON THE FIELD AND ANOTHER IN A BATTLE.%s|"
                 "LEFT/RIGHT: SWITCH.",
                 battle_active() ? " A BATTLE IS ON NOW." : "");
        return n;
    }
    if (row == RUN_ROW) {
        static const char *const what[RUN_MODES] = {
            "THE GAME'S: HOLD B TO RUN, TAP B TO JUMP. THE RUN KEY DOES NOTHING.",
            "YOU ALWAYS RUN. HOLD RUN TO WALK. B STILL JUMPS.",
            "RUN TURNS RUNNING ON AND OFF. IT TURNS OFF WHEN A BATTLE STARTS. B STILL JUMPS.",
            "HOLD RUN TO RUN. B STILL JUMPS, AND STILL RUNS WHEN HELD."};
        snprintf(help, (size_t)help_size, "%s|LEFT/RIGHT: CHANGE. DELETE OR X: BACK TO DEFAULT.", what[run_mode()]);
        return n;
    }
    if (row == RESET_ROW) {
        snprintf(help, (size_t)help_size, edit_set ? "MAKES THE BATTLE KEYS THE SAME AS THE EXPLORING KEYS.|ENTER OR A: COPY."
                                                   : "PUTS EVERY KEY AND GAMEPAD BUTTON BACK TO HOW IT STARTED.|ENTER OR A: "
                                                     "RESET.");
        return n;
    }
    int in = row_input(row);
    input_title(in, title, sizeof title);
    int key = col < BIND_KEYS ? bound[in].keys[col] : 0, pad = col == BIND_KEYS ? bound[in].pad : PAD_NONE;
    int o = also_used(in, key, pad);
    if (o >= 0) input_title(o, other, sizeof other);
    /* the first part: ours say what they do here; the game's are left empty for the overlay (its action names) */
    char what[160] = "";
    if (in == RUN_INPUT) {  /* by the RUNNING mode below it */
        static const char *const by_mode[RUN_MODES] = {
            "OFF IN THE DEFAULT RUNNING MODE, WHERE B HOLDS TO RUN. PICK ANOTHER MODE ABOVE TO USE IT.", "HOLD TO WALK.",
            "PRESS TO START OR STOP RUNNING.", "HOLD TO RUN."};
        if (run_mode() == RUN_DEFAULT) snprintf(what, sizeof what, "%s", by_mode[RUN_DEFAULT]);  /* names it already */
        else snprintf(what, sizeof what, "%s (RUNNING MODE: %s.)", by_mode[run_mode()], run_mode_name(run_mode()));
    }
    if (bindings_capturing())
        snprintf(help, (size_t)help_size,
                 col < BIND_KEYS ? "%s|PRESS THE KEY OR CLICK MOUSE FOR %s NOW. A GAMEPAD BUTTON CANCELS."
                                 : "%s|PRESS THE GAMEPAD BUTTON, OR PUSH THE STICK OR TRIGGER, FOR %s NOW. A KEY CANCELS.",
                 what, title);
    else if (o >= 0)
        snprintf(help, (size_t)help_size, "%s|%s ALSO PRESSES %s. BOTH WORK, BUT THE GAME SEES THEM TOGETHER.", what,
                 col < BIND_KEYS ? key_name(key) : pad_label(pad), other);
    else
        snprintf(help, (size_t)help_size, "%s|ENTER OR A: CHANGE. DELETE OR X: CLEAR.%s", what,
                 in == RUN_INPUT && run_mode() == RUN_DEFAULT ? " DISABLED WHILE RUNNING MODE IS DEFAULT."
                 : col == BIND_KEYS                          ? " BUTTONS ARE NAMED AS ON YOUR CONTROLLER."
                                                             : "");
    return n;
}

/* ---- the settings file */

int bindings_load_line(const char *name, const char *value) {
    for (int a = 0; a < NMOUSE; a++)
        if (!strcmp(name, sens_env[a])) {
            if (!getenv(name)) sens_choice[a] = sens_from(value);
            return 1;
        }
    if (!strcmp(name, "YW4_MOUSE_SENS")) {  /* the older single setting: both, unless set on their own */
        if (!getenv(name) && !getenv(sens_env[0])) sens_choice[0] = sens_from(value);
        if (!getenv(name) && !getenv(sens_env[1])) sens_choice[1] = sens_from(value);
        return 1;
    }
    if (!strcmp(name, "YW4_RUMBLE")) {
        if (!getenv(name)) window_rumble_set_enabled(!strcmp(value, "1") || !strcmp(value, "ON") || !strcmp(value, "on"));
        return 1;
    }
    if (!strcmp(name, "YW4_SHORTCUT_WHEEL")) {  /* the environment wins, as for the others */
        const char *v = getenv(name) ? getenv(name) : value;
        swheel_set_enabled(!strcmp(v, "1") || !strcmp(v, "ON") || !strcmp(v, "on"));
        return 1;
    }
    if (!strcmp(name, "YW4_RUN_MODE")) {  /* run.c reads the environment itself, so it wins */
        if (!getenv(name)) run_mode_set(atoi(value));
        return 1;
    }
    if (!strcmp(name, "YW4_NINTENDO_LAYOUT")) {
        const char *e = getenv(name);  /* the environment wins, as for every setting */
        if (e) value = e;
        nintendo_layout = !strcmp(value, "1") || !strcmp(value, "ON") || !strcmp(value, "on");
        return 1;
    }
    ready();
    int set = SET_FIELD;
    if (!strncmp(name, "BATTLE_", 7)) {
        if (!battle_set_known) {
            battle_starting_set();  /* each BATTLE_ line then changes its own key */
            battle_set_known = 1;
        }
        set = SET_BATTLE, name += 7;
    }
    Bound *b = sets[set];
    for (int p = 0; p < BMOUSE_PARTS; p++)  /* the mouse's own lines: MOUSE_LEFT=Y, - for none */
        if (!strcmp(name, mouse_save[p])) {
            mouse_map[set][p] = strcmp(value, "-") ? input_by_id(value) : -1;
            return 1;
        }
    for (int i = 0; i < NINPUTS; i++) {
        char want[32];
        for (int k = 0; k < BIND_KEYS; k++) {
            snprintf(want, sizeof want, "KEY%d_%s", k + 1, inputs[i].id);
            if (!strcmp(name, want)) {
                if (set == SET_FIELD) file_keys = 1, file_run |= i == RUN_INPUT;  /* migrate_hints */
                int code = key_from_name(value), part = mouse_part(code);
                /* a mouse button in a key slot (files before the Mouse buttons page, 2026-11-13): it becomes the
                 * mouse's own binding and the slot is freed; the side buttons are dropped */
                if (part >= 0) mouse_map[set][part] = i, code = 0;
                else if (code == MOUSE_BIND_X1 || code == MOUSE_BIND_X2) code = 0;
                b[i].keys[k] = code;
                return 1;
            }
        }
        snprintf(want, sizeof want, "PAD_%s", inputs[i].id);
        if (!strcmp(name, want)) {
            b[i].pad = pad_from_name(value);
            /* the first defaults went by the Switch's positions (A on the right button): those become the
             * controller's own A, B, X, Y */
            static const char *const old[4] = {"EAST", "SOUTH", "NORTH", "WEST"};
            if (i < 4 && !strcmp(value, old[i])) b[i].pad = PAD_FACE + i;
            return 1;
        }
    }
    return 0;
}

void bindings_save(FILE *f) {
    sets_ready();
    fprintf(f, "# Controls: two keys (SDL key names) and one gamepad input per Switch input; - for none.\n"
               "# MOUSE_LEFT/RIGHT/MID/WHEEL_UP/WHEEL_DOWN: the Switch input that part of the mouse presses.\n"
               "# BATTLE_...: the same for battles.\n");
    for (int s = 0; s < NSETS; s++) {
        const char *pre = s == SET_BATTLE ? "BATTLE_" : "";
        for (int i = 0; i < NINPUTS; i++) {
            for (int k = 0; k < BIND_KEYS; k++)
                fprintf(f, "%sKEY%d_%s=%s\n", pre, k + 1, inputs[i].id, key_save_name(sets[s][i].keys[k]));
            fprintf(f, "%sPAD_%s=%s\n", pre, inputs[i].id, pad_name(sets[s][i].pad));
        }
        for (int p = 0; p < BMOUSE_PARTS; p++)
            fprintf(f, "%s%s=%s\n", pre, mouse_save[p], mouse_map[s][p] >= 0 ? inputs[mouse_map[s][p]].id : "-");
    }
    for (int a = 0; a < NMOUSE; a++) fprintf(f, "%s=%s\n", sens_env[a], sens_values[sens_index(a)]);
    fprintf(f, "YW4_RUMBLE=%d\n", window_rumble_enabled());
    fprintf(f, "YW4_SHORTCUT_WHEEL=%d\n", swheel_enabled());
    fprintf(f, "YW4_NINTENDO_LAYOUT=%d\n", nintendo_layout);
    fprintf(f, "YW4_RUN_MODE=%s\n", run_mode_save(run_mode()));
}
```

```h
 * can always be undone from the panel. */
```

`runtime/src/bloom.c`:

```c
/* Our bloom pass, the engine side (decision 0037, docs/frame.md "Post-processing").
 *
 * The engine's bloom is main+0x802e40(device, renderer): a bright pass, three levels blurred across and
 * down, and a composite onto the scene. A hook (recomp/overrides.toml) runs before it and gathers what
 * those 8 draws use, straight from the renderer object: its images (0x28-byte records from +0x2e28;
 * record +0x10 is a texture view whose first word + 0x18 is the guest NVNtexture) and its settings. Our
 * pass (gpu_post.c) is recorded into the device's command buffer in their place.
 *
 * YW4_BLOOM=native: ours, and the hook skips the engine's function. YW4_BLOOM=check: the engine draws as
 * usual, and ours draws the same into copies first; after the game's composite the two are compared
 * texel by texel (gpu_post.c). YW4_BLOOM=game: the engine's. Default: ours; the settings panel (F1, BLOOM)
 * switches while playing.
 *
 * When the engine's function is skipped, the engine's record of what is bound (texture slots, constant
 * buffers, the program) stays as it was, and so do the game's commands, because none of the engine's bloom
 * commands are sent either: the two agree. Setting that record as the function would would make the engine
 * skip bindings the GPU never got. What it changes that is not a binding is done here (skipped_effects).
 */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "post.h"
#include "yw4rt.h"

enum { MODE_GAME, MODE_CHECK, MODE_NATIVE };
static int mode = -1;

#define U8(a) (*(const uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)(a))
#define U16W(a) (*(uint16_t *)(uintptr_t)(a))
#define U32W(a) (*(uint32_t *)(uintptr_t)(a))
#define U64(a) (*(const uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)(a))
#define F32(a) (*(const float *)(uintptr_t)(a))

static int bloom_mode(void) {
    int m = __atomic_load_n(&mode, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
    if (m >= 0) return m;
    const char *s = getenv("YW4_BLOOM");
    m = s && !strcmp(s, "game") ? MODE_GAME : s && !strcmp(s, "check") ? MODE_CHECK : MODE_NATIVE;
    int unset = -1;
    if (__atomic_compare_exchange_n(&mode, &unset, m, 0, __ATOMIC_ACQ_REL, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) && m != MODE_GAME)
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: bloom: %s\n", m == MODE_CHECK ? "ours checked against the game's" : "ours");
    return __atomic_load_n(&mode, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
}

int bloom_native(void) { return bloom_mode() == MODE_NATIVE; }

void bloom_toggle(void) {
    int m = bloom_native() ? MODE_GAME : MODE_NATIVE;
    __atomic_store_n(&mode, m, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: bloom: %s (settings panel)\n", m == MODE_NATIVE ? "ours" : "the game's");
}

/* The guest NVNtexture of the renderer's image record i, or 0. */
static uint64_t record_texture(uint64_t renderer, unsigned i) {
    uint64_t rec = renderer + 0x2e28 + 0x28ull * i, view = U64(rec + 0x10);
    return view && U64(view) ? U64(view) + 0x18 : 0;
}

/* What the engine's bloom changes besides its bindings, as it does it: the device's flag +0x45da bit 0, the
 * "render target read as a texture" bits in +0x45ac for every image it binds (0x12 when the record's
 * +0x22 or +0x23 is set, else 0x10), and its draw statistics (+0x4654 draws, +0x4658 count / 3: 8 quads of
 * 4 vertices). */
static void skipped_effects(uint64_t device, uint64_t renderer, const unsigned *records, int n) {
    U16W(device + 0x45da) |= 1;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        uint64_t rec = renderer + 0x2e28 + 0x28ull * records[i];
        U32W(device + 0x45ac) |= U8(rec + 0x22) || U8(rec + 0x23) ? 0x12u : 0x10u;
    }
    U32W(device + 0x4654) += 8;
    U32W(device + 0x4658) += 8 * (4 / 3);
}

/* hook on main+0x802e40 (device, renderer), before its body */
int yw4_hook_bloom(CPUState *ctx) {
    int m = bloom_mode();
    if (m == MODE_GAME) return 0;
    uint64_t device = ctx->x[0], renderer = ctx->x[1];
    static const unsigned records[BLOOM_IMAGES] = {0, 11, 9, 20, 19, 22, 21, 24, 23};
    BloomPass p;
    memset(&p, 0, sizeof p);
    for (int i = 0; i < BLOOM_IMAGES; i++) {
        uint64_t g = record_texture(renderer, records[i]);
        if (!g) {
            static int logged;
            if (!logged++) fprintf(stderr, "yw4: bloom: image record %u has no texture: the game's bloom\n", records[i]);
            return 0;
        }
        const NvnTexture *t = HOST(NvnTexture, g);  /* the runtime's texture, named by the guest object */
        if (!t) return 0;
        memcpy(&p.tex[i], t, sizeof p.tex[i]);
    }
    /* bright pass: (+0x800, +0x80c) for the scene, (+0x7f0, +0x7fc) for the half image; with +0x388d set,
     * each threshold is at least 1 */
    memcpy(p.bright, (const void *)(uintptr_t)(renderer + 0x800), 16);
    memcpy(p.bright + 4, (const void *)(uintptr_t)(renderer + 0x7f0), 16);
    if (U8(renderer + 0x388d)) {
        if (p.bright[3] < 1.0f) p.bright[3] = 1.0f;
        if (p.bright[7] < 1.0f) p.bright[7] = 1.0f;
    }
    for (int l = 0; l < 3; l++) p.step[l] = F32(renderer + 0x7c0 + 4 * l);
    float *c = p.composite;
    c[0] = F32(renderer + 0x7d0), c[1] = F32(renderer + 0x7e0), c[2] = F32(renderer + 0x7d4), c[3] = F32(renderer + 0x7e4);
    c[4] = F32(renderer + 0x7d8), c[5] = F32(renderer + 0x7e8);
    p.check = m == MODE_CHECK;
    nvn_record_native(ctx, U64(device + 0x10d0) + 0xd8, gpu_bloom_pass, &p, sizeof p);
    if (m != MODE_NATIVE) return 0;
    skipped_effects(device, renderer, records, BLOOM_IMAGES);
    return 1;
}

```

`runtime/src/bones.c`:

```c
/* Native skeleton matrices (decision 0036).
 *
 * main+0xa77390 and main+0xa79c00 turn a skeleton's local bone transforms into matrices:
 * bone 0's local matrix, then for every other bone parent matrix x local matrix, in bone
 * order. The second one also calls main+0xa7a530 after a bone whose byte in a per-bone table
 * says so. They are the hottest game code on the main thread (about a quarter of its busy
 * time in a busy scene), and the recompiled versions run ~23 host instructions per ARM one.
 * The hooks (recomp/overrides.toml) do the same work here, with the same float operations in
 * the same order, so the results are bit-identical; YW4_BONES=check proves that in game.
 *
 * Arguments: x0 = the skeleton object (+0x18: its definition), x1 = the output matrices,
 * x2 = the local transforms, both 0x30 bytes per bone; x3 is passed on to the helpers; the
 * flag in w3 bit 0 (w4 for the second function) asks for main+0xa77c30 to build a bone whose
 * parent's scale isn't the usual one. Local transform: scale (x, y, z, -) at +0x00, rotation
 * quaternion (x, y, z, w) at +0x10, translation (x, y, z) at +0x20. Matrix: 3 rows of 4
 * floats, translation in the 4th column.
 * Definition: +0x20 bone count (u16), +0x22 bit 0 = the second mode below, the parent table
 * (u16 per bone) at 4 * (u16 +0x2a) + 4 * (u16 +0xa) and the second function's per-bone byte
 * table at 4 * (u16 +0x2e) + 4 * (u16 +0xa).
 *
 * What we don't do, so the game's code does it (decided before anything is written):
 *  - the definition's second mode (+0x22 bit 0), which tracks non-uniform scale down the
 *    hierarchy in a bit set and rebuilds such bones from their column lengths (frecpe);
 *  - any NaN in a local transform, and any parent that doesn't come before its child.
 * Without NaN inputs every NaN comes from an invalid operation, which ARM gives as the
 * default NaN and x86 as a negative one, so our results are fixed up to the ARM one.
 *
 * YW4_BONES=game: the game's code only. YW4_BONES=check: run the game's code, then ours from
 * the same inputs, compare every float and keep the game's results (the helpers run twice).
 * Default (native): ours.
 */
#include <emmintrin.h>
#include <inttypes.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "yw4rt.h"

enum { MODE_GAME, MODE_CHECK, MODE_NATIVE };
static int mode = -1;
static _Thread_local int in_original;  /* check mode: the game's own run of the function */

static GuestFn fn_scaled, fn_extra, fn_first, fn_second;  /* main+0xa77c30, 0xa7a530, the two */

static struct { uint64_t calls, native, other_mode, odd_input, scaled, extra, checked, mismatches; } st;
#define COUNT(f) __atomic_add_fetch(&st.f, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED)

#define U8(a) (*(const uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)(a))
#define U16(a) (*(const uint16_t *)(uintptr_t)(a))
#define U64(a) (*(const uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)(a))
#define FP(a) ((float *)(uintptr_t)(a))

static void init_mode(void) {
    const char *s = getenv("YW4_BONES");
    int m = s && !strcmp(s, "game") ? MODE_GAME : s && !strcmp(s, "check") ? MODE_CHECK : MODE_NATIVE;
    uint64_t b = yw4_image_base;
    fn_scaled = yw4_lookup(b + 0xa77c30), fn_extra = yw4_lookup(b + 0xa7a530);
    fn_first = yw4_lookup(b + 0xa77390), fn_second = yw4_lookup(b + 0xa79c00);
    if (!fn_scaled || !fn_extra || !fn_first || !fn_second) m = MODE_GAME;
    int unset = -1;
    if (!__atomic_compare_exchange_n(&mode, &unset, m, 0, __ATOMIC_ACQ_REL, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)) return;
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: bones: %s\n", m == MODE_GAME ? "the game's code" : m == MODE_CHECK
                                          ? "ours checked against the game's" : "ours");
}

static void report(void) {
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: bones: %" PRIu64 " calls, ours %" PRIu64 ", game's (second mode %" PRIu64
            ", odd input %" PRIu64 "); scaled-parent bones %" PRIu64 ", extra calls %" PRIu64
            "; checked %" PRIu64 ", mismatches %" PRIu64 "\n", st.calls, st.native, st.other_mode,
            st.odd_input, st.scaled, st.extra, st.checked, st.mismatches);
}

static int has_nan(const float *f, int n) {
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        uint32_t b;
        memcpy(&b, &f[i], 4);
        if ((b & 0x7FFFFFFFu) > 0x7F800000u) return 1;
    }
    return 0;
}

/* NaN lanes become ARM's default NaN. */
static inline __m128 arm_nan(__m128 v) {
    __m128 nan = _mm_cmpunord_ps(v, v);
    return _mm_or_ps(_mm_andnot_ps(nan, v), _mm_and_ps(nan, _mm_castsi128_ps(_mm_set1_epi32(0x7FC00000))));
}

/* A local transform as a matrix: the game's quaternion -> rotation (with its lane mask on
 * x, y, z), translation in column 3, then column c times scale c. */
static void local_matrix(uint64_t l, const uint32_t mask[4], __m128 r[3]) {
    const float *q = FP(l + 0x10), *sc = FP(l), *t = FP(l + 0x20);
    float m[3];
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
        uint32_t b;
        memcpy(&b, &q[i], 4);
        b &= mask[i];
        memcpy(&m[i], &b, 4);
    }
    float s = 2.0f / ((q[2] * q[2] + q[0] * q[0]) + (q[3] * q[3] + q[1] * q[1]));
    float ax = m[0] * s, ay = m[1] * s, az = m[2] * s, w = q[3];
    float xw = ax * w, yw = ay * w, zw = az * w;
    float xx = ax * m[0], yy = ay * m[1], zz = az * m[2];
    float xy = ay * m[0], yz = az * m[1], zx = ax * m[2];
    __m128 scale = _mm_setr_ps(sc[0], sc[1], sc[2], 1.0f);
    r[0] = _mm_mul_ps(_mm_setr_ps(1.0f - (yy + zz), xy - zw, zx + yw, t[0]), scale);
    r[1] = _mm_mul_ps(_mm_setr_ps(zw + xy, 1.0f - (zz + xx), yz - xw, t[1]), scale);
    r[2] = _mm_mul_ps(_mm_setr_ps(zx - yw, yz + xw, 1.0f - (xx + yy), t[2]), scale);
}

static void store_rows(uint64_t o, const __m128 r[3]) {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) _mm_storeu_ps(FP(o + 16 * i), arm_nan(r[i]));
}

/* Our version. Returns 0, having written nothing, when the game's code must do it. */
static int native(CPUState *ctx, int second) {
    uint64_t obj = ctx->x[0], out = ctx->x[1], loc = ctx->x[2], arg3 = ctx->x[3];
    uint64_t def = U64(obj + 0x18);
    if (U8(def + 0x22) & 1) { COUNT(other_mode); return 0; }
    uint32_t n = U16(def + 0x20);
    uint64_t parents = def + 4ull * U16(def + 0x2a) + 4ull * U16(def + 0xa);
    uint64_t extras = def + 4ull * U16(def + 0x2e) + 4ull * U16(def + 0xa);
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < (n ? n : 1); i++) {
        const float *l = FP(loc + 0x30ull * i);
        if (has_nan(l, 3) || has_nan(l + 4, 7) || (i && U16(parents + 2ull * i) >= i)) {
            COUNT(odd_input);
            return 0;
        }
    }
    uint64_t b = yw4_image_base;
    uint32_t mask[4];
    memcpy(mask, (const void *)(uintptr_t)(b + 0x5864fb0), 16);
    __m128 last = _mm_loadu_ps(FP(b + 0x5864f00));  /* times each parent row's column 3 */
    const float *usual = FP(b + 0x150e100);         /* the scale that needs no main+0xa77c30 */
    int scaled_check = (second ? ctx->x[4] : arg3) & 1;
    uint64_t sp = ctx->sp, fp = ctx->x[29];
    __m128 r[3];
    local_matrix(loc, mask, r);
    store_rows(out, r);
    for (uint32_t i = 1; i < U16(U64(obj + 0x18) + 0x20); i++) {
        uint64_t li = loc + 0x30ull * i, oi = out + 0x30ull * i;
        uint32_t p = U16(parents + 2ull * i);
        uint64_t lp = loc + 0x30ull * p, op = out + 0x30ull * p;
        const float *ps = FP(lp), *pm = FP(op);
        if (scaled_check && !(ps[0] == usual[0] && ps[1] == usual[1] && ps[2] == usual[2])) {
            COUNT(scaled);
            ctx->sp = sp - (second ? 0x90 : 0x80), ctx->x[29] = ctx->sp + 0x70;
            ctx->x[0] = oi, ctx->x[1] = li, ctx->x[2] = lp;
            memcpy(&ctx->v[0], pm, 16), memcpy(&ctx->v[1], pm + 4, 16), memcpy(&ctx->v[2], pm + 8, 16);
            ctx->x[30] = b + (second ? 0xa79dc8 : 0xa7754c);
            fn_scaled(ctx);  /* the first function passes its w3, the second whatever x3 holds */
            if (!second) ctx->x[3] = (uint32_t)arg3;
        } else {
            __m128 l[3], o[3];
            local_matrix(li, mask, l);
            for (int k = 0; k < 3; k++) {
                const float *row = pm + 4 * k;
                o[k] = _mm_add_ps(_mm_add_ps(_mm_add_ps(_mm_mul_ps(l[0], _mm_set1_ps(row[0])),
                                                        _mm_mul_ps(l[1], _mm_set1_ps(row[1]))),
                                             _mm_mul_ps(l[2], _mm_set1_ps(row[2]))),
                                  _mm_mul_ps(last, _mm_set1_ps(row[3])));
            }
            store_rows(oi, o);
        }
        uint32_t e = second ? (U8(extras + i) >> 1) & 15 : 0;
        if (e) {
            COUNT(extra);
            ctx->sp = sp - 0x90, ctx->x[29] = ctx->sp + 0x70;
            ctx->x[0] = oi, ctx->x[1] = e, ctx->x[2] = li, ctx->x[3] = arg3;
            ctx->x[30] = b + 0xa79fcc;
            fn_extra(ctx);
        }
    }
    ctx->sp = sp, ctx->x[29] = fp;
    COUNT(native);
    return 1;
}

/* Check mode: the game's run, then ours from the same starting matrices; the game's stays. */
static int check(CPUState *ctx, int second) {
    uint32_t n = U16(U64(ctx->x[0] + 0x18) + 0x20);
    size_t size = 0x30ull * (n ? n : 1);
    float *out = FP(ctx->x[1]);
    float *before = malloc(size), *want = malloc(size);
    memcpy(before, out, size);
    CPUState game = *ctx;
    in_original = 1;
    (second ? fn_second : fn_first)(&game);
    in_original = 0;
    memcpy(want, out, size);
    memcpy(out, before, size);
    CPUState ours = *ctx;
    if (native(&ours, second)) {
        uint64_t c = COUNT(checked);
        int bad = 0;
        for (size_t i = 0; i < size / 4; i++) {
            if (!memcmp(&out[i], &want[i], 4)) continue;
            if (bad++ < 4) {
                uint32_t g, w;
                memcpy(&g, &out[i], 4), memcpy(&w, &want[i], 4);
                fprintf(stderr, "yw4: bones: MISMATCH f_%s bone %zu float %zu: ours %08x (%g) game %08x (%g)\n",
                        second ? "a79c00" : "a77390", i / 12, i % 12, g, out[i], w, want[i]);
            }
        }
        if (bad) COUNT(mismatches);
        if (c % 20000 == 0) report();
    }
    memcpy(out, want, size);
    free(before), free(want);
    *ctx = game;
    return 1;
}

static int hook(CPUState *ctx, int second) {
    if (in_original) return 0;
    if (__builtin_expect(__atomic_load_n(&mode, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) < 0, 0)) init_mode();
    if (mode == MODE_GAME) return 0;
    if (COUNT(calls) % 500000 == 0) report();
    return mode == MODE_CHECK ? check(ctx, second) : native(ctx, second);
}

int yw4_hook_bones_a77390(CPUState *ctx) { return hook(ctx, 0); }
int yw4_hook_bones_a79c00(CPUState *ctx) { return hook(ctx, 1); }

```

`runtime/src/bugreport.c`:

```c
/* The bug report's zip and GitHub link (bugreport.h). Runs on the present's thread while the overlay shows (the
 * game is paused), so taking a moment to read and write a few MB is fine. */
#include <dirent.h>
#include <stdarg.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>
#include <time.h>
#ifdef _WIN32
#define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#include <direct.h>
#include <windows.h>
#undef GPTR  /* windows.h's; hle.h (through savefs.h) has its own */
#define MKDIR(p) _mkdir(p)
#else
#define MKDIR(p) mkdir(p, 0777)
#endif

#include <SDL3/SDL.h>

#include "bugreport.h"
#include "savefs.h"
#include "settings.h"
#include "version.h"
#include "vk.h"

const char *yw4_log_path(void);  /* log.c */

#define REPO_ISSUES "https://github.com/ILFforever/YW4Recomp/issues/new"
#define GAME_VERSION "2.2.0"

/* ---- bytes */

typedef struct {
    uint8_t *p;
    size_t n, cap;
} Buf;

static void put(Buf *b, const void *d, size_t n) {
    if (b->n + n > b->cap) {
        size_t cap = b->cap ? b->cap : 4096;
        while (cap < b->n + n) cap *= 2;
        uint8_t *q = realloc(b->p, cap);
        if (!q) return;
        b->p = q, b->cap = cap;
    }
    memcpy(b->p + b->n, d, n);
    b->n += n;
}
static void put16(Buf *b, unsigned v) { uint8_t x[2] = {(uint8_t)v, (uint8_t)(v >> 8)}; put(b, x, 2); }
static void put32(Buf *b, uint32_t v) { uint8_t x[4] = {(uint8_t)v, (uint8_t)(v >> 8), (uint8_t)(v >> 16), (uint8_t)(v >> 24)}; put(b, x, 4); }
static void putf(Buf *b, const char *fmt, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3)));
static void putf(Buf *b, const char *fmt, ...) {
    char s[2048];
    va_list ap;
    va_start(ap, fmt);
    int n = vsnprintf(s, sizeof s, fmt, ap);
    va_end(ap);
    if (n > 0) put(b, s, (size_t)(n < (int)sizeof s ? n : (int)sizeof s - 1));
}

static int read_file(const char *path, Buf *out) {
    FILE *f = fopen(path, "rb");
    if (!f) return -1;
    char chunk[65536];
    size_t got;
    while ((got = fread(chunk, 1, sizeof chunk, f)) > 0) put(out, chunk, got);
    fclose(f);
    return 0;
}

/* ---- a zip that stores its files (method 0), names in UTF-8 */

static uint32_t crc32_of(const uint8_t *p, size_t n) {
    static uint32_t table[256];
    if (!table[1])
        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < 256; i++) {
            uint32_t c = i;
            for (int k = 0; k < 8; k++) c = c & 1 ? 0xEDB88320u ^ (c >> 1) : c >> 1;
            table[i] = c;
        }
    uint32_t c = 0xFFFFFFFFu;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; i++) c = table[(c ^ p[i]) & 255] ^ (c >> 8);
    return c ^ 0xFFFFFFFFu;
}

typedef struct {
    char name[260];
    uint32_t crc, size, offset;
} Entry;

typedef struct {
    Buf out;
    Entry e[256];
    int n;
    unsigned dtime, ddate;  /* MS-DOS time and date of the report */
} Zip;

static void zip_add(Zip *z, const char *name, const uint8_t *data, size_t size) {
    if (z->n >= (int)(sizeof z->e / sizeof *z->e)) return;
    Entry *e = &z->e[z->n++];
    snprintf(e->name, sizeof e->name, "%s", name);
    e->crc = crc32_of(data, size), e->size = (uint32_t)size, e->offset = (uint32_t)z->out.n;
    put32(&z->out, 0x04034b50), put16(&z->out, 20), put16(&z->out, 0x0800), put16(&z->out, 0);
    put16(&z->out, z->dtime), put16(&z->out, z->ddate);
    put32(&z->out, e->crc), put32(&z->out, e->size), put32(&z->out, e->size);
    put16(&z->out, (unsigned)strlen(e->name)), put16(&z->out, 0);
    put(&z->out, e->name, strlen(e->name));
    if (size) put(&z->out, data, size);
}

static void zip_end(Zip *z) {
    uint32_t start = (uint32_t)z->out.n;
    for (int i = 0; i < z->n; i++) {
        const Entry *e = &z->e[i];
        put32(&z->out, 0x02014b50), put16(&z->out, 20), put16(&z->out, 20), put16(&z->out, 0x0800), put16(&z->out, 0);
        put16(&z->out, z->dtime), put16(&z->out, z->ddate);
        put32(&z->out, e->crc), put32(&z->out, e->size), put32(&z->out, e->size);
        put16(&z->out, (unsigned)strlen(e->name)), put16(&z->out, 0), put16(&z->out, 0), put16(&z->out, 0),
            put16(&z->out, 0);
        put32(&z->out, 0), put32(&z->out, e->offset);
        put(&z->out, e->name, strlen(e->name));
    }
    uint32_t size = (uint32_t)z->out.n - start;
    put32(&z->out, 0x06054b50), put16(&z->out, 0), put16(&z->out, 0), put16(&z->out, (unsigned)z->n),
        put16(&z->out, (unsigned)z->n);
    put32(&z->out, size), put32(&z->out, start), put16(&z->out, 0);
}

static void zip_file(Zip *z, const char *name, const char *path) {
    Buf b = {0};
    if (read_file(path, &b) == 0) zip_add(z, name, b.p, b.n);
    free(b.p);
}

/* every file under dir, as prefix/<path inside dir> */
static void zip_dir(Zip *z, const char *dir, const char *prefix, int depth) {
    DIR *d = opendir(dir);
    if (!d || depth > 8) {
        if (d) closedir(d);
        return;
    }
    struct dirent *de;
    while ((de = readdir(d))) {
        if (!strcmp(de->d_name, ".") || !strcmp(de->d_name, "..")) continue;
        char path[1024], name[600];
        snprintf(path, sizeof path, "%s/%s", dir, de->d_name);
        snprintf(name, sizeof name, "%s/%s", prefix, de->d_name);
        struct stat st;
        if (stat(path, &st) != 0) continue;
        if ((st.st_mode & S_IFMT) == S_IFDIR) zip_dir(z, path, name, depth + 1);
        else zip_file(z, name, path);
    }
    closedir(d);
}

/* ---- what goes in */

/* the paused picture as a 24-bit BMP, made smaller by whole steps until it is at most 1600 wide */
static void picture_bmp(const BugReport *r, Buf *out) {
    int k = 1;
    while (r->picture_w / k > 1600) k++;
    int w = r->picture_w / k, h = r->picture_h / k, row = (w * 3 + 3) & ~3;
    uint32_t size = 54 + (uint32_t)row * (uint32_t)h;
    put16(out, 0x4d42), put32(out, size), put32(out, 0), put32(out, 54);
    put32(out, 40), put32(out, (uint32_t)w), put32(out, (uint32_t)h), put16(out, 1), put16(out, 24), put32(out, 0);
    put32(out, (uint32_t)row * (uint32_t)h), put32(out, 2835), put32(out, 2835), put32(out, 0), put32(out, 0);
    uint8_t *line = calloc((size_t)row, 1);
    if (!line) return;
    for (int y = h - 1; y >= 0; y--) {  /* bottom row first */
        for (int x = 0; x < w; x++) {
            unsigned s[3] = {0, 0, 0};
            for (int j = 0; j < k; j++)
                for (int i = 0; i < k; i++) {
                    const uint8_t *p = r->picture + ((size_t)(y * k + j) * r->picture_w + (size_t)(x * k + i)) * 4;
                    s[0] += p[0], s[1] += p[1], s[2] += p[2];
                }
            line[x * 3 + 0] = (uint8_t)(s[2] / (unsigned)(k * k));  /* B G R */
            line[x * 3 + 1] = (uint8_t)(s[1] / (unsigned)(k * k));
            line[x * 3 + 2] = (uint8_t)(s[0] / (unsigned)(k * k));
        }
        put(out, line, (size_t)row);
    }
    free(line);
}

static void windows_version(char *out, size_t n) {
#ifdef _WIN32
    typedef LONG(WINAPI * RtlGetVersionFn)(OSVERSIONINFOW *);
    RtlGetVersionFn get = (RtlGetVersionFn)(void *)GetProcAddress(GetModuleHandleA("ntdll.dll"), "RtlGetVersion");
    OSVERSIONINFOW v = {.dwOSVersionInfoSize = sizeof v};
    if (get && get(&v) == 0) {
        snprintf(out, n, "Windows %s (%lu.%lu.%lu)", v.dwBuildNumber >= 22000 ? "11" : "10", v.dwMajorVersion,
                 v.dwMinorVersion, v.dwBuildNumber);
        return;
    }
    snprintf(out, n, "Windows");
#else
    snprintf(out, n, "%s", SDL_GetPlatform());
#endif
}

static void gpu_line(char *out, size_t n) {
    const VkPhysicalDeviceProperties *p = &vk.props;
    if (!p->deviceName[0]) {
        snprintf(out, n, "unknown");
        return;
    }
    uint32_t v = p->driverVersion;
    if (p->vendorID == 0x10DE)  /* NVIDIA's own numbering: 581.57 */
        snprintf(out, n, "%s (driver %u.%02u)", p->deviceName, v >> 22 & 0x3ff, v >> 14 & 0xff);
    else
        snprintf(out, n, "%s (driver %u.%u.%u)", p->deviceName, VK_API_VERSION_MAJOR(v), VK_API_VERSION_MINOR(v),
                 VK_API_VERSION_PATCH(v));
}

static void version_line(char *out, size_t n) {
    snprintf(out, n, "%s (%s, built %s)", yw4_version, yw4_git_commit, yw4_build_date);
}

int bugreport_save(const BugReport *r, char *path, size_t n) {
    time_t now = time(NULL);
    struct tm t;
#ifdef _WIN32
    localtime_s(&t, &now);
#else
    localtime_r(&now, &t);
#endif
    const char *dir = getenv("YW4_REPORT_DIR");
    if (!dir || !*dir) dir = "reports";
    MKDIR(dir);
    char stamp[32], rel[600];
    strftime(stamp, sizeof stamp, "%Y-%m-%d_%H%M%S", &t);
    snprintf(rel, sizeof rel, "%s/yw4_report_%s.zip", dir, stamp);
#ifdef _WIN32
    if (!_fullpath(path, rel, n)) snprintf(path, n, "%s", rel);
#else
    if (!realpath(dir, path)) snprintf(path, n, "%s", rel);
    else snprintf(path + strlen(path), n - strlen(path), "/yw4_report_%s.zip", stamp);
#endif
    static Zip z;  /* large: not on the stack */
    memset(&z, 0, sizeof z);
    z.dtime = (unsigned)(t.tm_hour << 11 | t.tm_min << 5 | t.tm_sec / 2);
    z.ddate = (unsigned)((t.tm_year - 80) << 9 | (t.tm_mon + 1) << 5 | t.tm_mday);

    char ver[128], gpu[300], os[96], when[32];
    version_line(ver, sizeof ver), gpu_line(gpu, sizeof gpu), windows_version(os, sizeof os);
    strftime(when, sizeof when, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M", &t);
    Buf txt = {0};
    putf(&txt, "YW4 Recomp bug report\r\n\r\nWhat's wrong: %s\r\nHow often: %s\r\nWhat happened:\r\n", r->kind[0] ? r->kind : "-",
         r->often[0] ? r->often : "-");
    put(&txt, r->text, strlen(r->text));
    putf(&txt, "\r\n\r\nVersion: %s\r\nGame: Yo-kai Watch 4++ %s\r\nGPU: %s\r\nSystem: %s\r\nWindow: %dx%d\r\nTime: %s\r\n",
         ver, GAME_VERSION, gpu, os, r->window_w, r->window_h, when);
    putf(&txt, "Attached: %s%s%s\r\n", r->attach & BUG_ATTACH_SHOT ? "screenshot " : "",
         r->attach & BUG_ATTACH_LOG ? "log settings " : "", r->attach & BUG_ATTACH_SAVE ? "save" : "");
    zip_add(&z, "report.txt", txt.p, txt.n);
    free(txt.p);

    if ((r->attach & BUG_ATTACH_SHOT) && r->picture && r->picture_w > 0 && r->picture_h > 0) {
        Buf bmp = {0};
        picture_bmp(r, &bmp);
        zip_add(&z, "screenshot.bmp", bmp.p, bmp.n);
        free(bmp.p);
    }
    if (r->attach & BUG_ATTACH_LOG) {
        if (yw4_log_path()[0]) zip_file(&z, "log.txt", yw4_log_path());
        if (settings_file_name()[0]) zip_file(&z, "settings.ini", settings_file_name());
    }
    if ((r->attach & BUG_ATTACH_SAVE) && savefs_root()[0]) zip_dir(&z, savefs_root(), "save", 0);
    zip_end(&z);

    FILE *f = fopen(rel, "wb");
    int ok = f && fwrite(z.out.p, 1, z.out.n, f) == z.out.n;
    if (f) ok = fclose(f) == 0 && ok;
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: bug report: %s %s (%d files, %zu bytes)\n", ok ? "saved" : "NOT saved", path, z.n, z.out.n);
    free(z.out.p);
    return ok ? 0 : -1;
}

/* ---- the link */

/* opens url in the browser (or Explorer); YW4_REPORT_OPEN=0 (test runs): only writes it in the log */
static void open_url(const char *url) {
    const char *e = getenv("YW4_REPORT_OPEN");
    if (e && *e == '0') {
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: bug report: would open %s\n", url);
        return;
    }
    if (!SDL_OpenURL(url)) fprintf(stderr, "yw4: bug report: can't open %s: %s\n", url, SDL_GetError());
}

static void url_add(char *url, size_t n, const char *key, const char *value, size_t max) {
    size_t at = strlen(url);
    at += (size_t)snprintf(url + at, at < n ? n - at : 0, "&%s=", key);
    static const char hex[] = "0123456789ABCDEF";
    size_t used = 0;
    for (const unsigned char *p = (const unsigned char *)value; *p && at + 4 < n; p++, used++) {
        unsigned char ch = *p;
        if (used >= max && (ch & 0xC0) != 0x80) break;  /* long: cut, but never inside a character */
        if ((ch >= 'A' && ch <= 'Z') || (ch >= 'a' && ch <= 'z') || (ch >= '0' && ch <= '9') || ch == '-' ||
            ch == '_' || ch == '.' || ch == '~') {
            url[at++] = (char)ch;
        } else {
            url[at++] = '%', url[at++] = hex[ch >> 4], url[at++] = hex[ch & 15];
        }
    }
    url[at < n ? at : n - 1] = 0;
}

void bugreport_open_github(const BugReport *r) {
    static char url[12000];
    char title[200], ver[128], gpu[300], os[96], pc[420];
    /* the title: the kind and the start of what happened */
    snprintf(title, sizeof title, "%s%s%.80s", r->kind[0] ? r->kind : "Bug", r->text[0] ? ": " : "", r->text);
    version_line(ver, sizeof ver), gpu_line(gpu, sizeof gpu), windows_version(os, sizeof os);
    snprintf(pc, sizeof pc, "%s, %s", gpu, os);
    snprintf(url, sizeof url, "%s?template=bug.yml", REPO_ISSUES);
    url_add(url, sizeof url, "title", title, 120);
    url_add(url, sizeof url, "what", r->text, 4000);
    url_add(url, sizeof url, "often", r->often, 40);
    url_add(url, sizeof url, "version", ver, 120);
    url_add(url, sizeof url, "pc", pc, 300);
    open_url(url);
}

void bugreport_show_folder(const char *zip) {
    char url[1200] = "file:///";
    size_t at = strlen(url);
    for (const char *p = zip; *p && at + 1 < sizeof url; p++) url[at++] = *p == '\\' ? '/' : *p;
    url[at] = 0;
    char *slash = strrchr(url, '/');  /* the folder, not the zip (which Windows would open as a folder too) */
    if (slash && slash > url + 8) *slash = 0;
    open_url(url);
}
```

`runtime/src/c11_keywords.h`:

```h
/* C11 keywords that C++ spells differently. The runtime is C11, but a few C++ files include its headers
 * (gpu_dlssg.cpp: NVIDIA Streamline's headers are C++). g++ stops on `_Noreturn` and `_Thread_local` (issue #12);
 * clang++ takes them as extensions. C++ has `[[noreturn]]` and `thread_local` in the same places.
 *
 * YW4_NORETURN: a function that never returns, in either language; the runtime's headers use it.
 *
 * For C++ only, `_Noreturn` and `_Thread_local` themselves are defined as the C++ words, so the headers that keep the
 * C11 spelling work too when this one comes first: runtime/include/yw4rt.h (the generated code's header: a change
 * there makes every player's build recompile all of the generated code) and the thread-locals in nvn.h and
 * gpu_internal.h. */
#ifndef YW4_C11_KEYWORDS_H
#define YW4_C11_KEYWORDS_H

#if defined(__cplusplus)
#define YW4_NORETURN [[noreturn]]
#ifndef _Noreturn
#define _Noreturn [[noreturn]]
#endif
#ifndef _Thread_local
#define _Thread_local thread_local
#endif
#else
#define YW4_NORETURN _Noreturn
#endif

#endif
```
