`runtime/src/discord_ipc.h`:

```h
/* Discord's local IPC (decision 0077): the few messages Rich Presence needs, over the socket the Discord app
 * opens on this PC. No library: a frame is an 8-byte header (op, length, both little-endian u32) and that many
 * bytes of JSON. Windows: the named pipe \\.\pipe\discord-ipc-N; Linux: the socket discord-ipc-N in
 * $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, $TMPDIR, $TMP, $TEMP or /tmp (also their Flatpak and Snap subfolders); N from 0 to 9.
 * Nothing here knows about the game (discord.c does), so tests can drive it against a stand-in server. */
#ifndef YW4_DISCORD_IPC_H
#define YW4_DISCORD_IPC_H

#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>

enum { DISCORD_OP_HANDSHAKE = 0, DISCORD_OP_FRAME = 1, DISCORD_OP_CLOSE = 2, DISCORD_OP_PING = 3, DISCORD_OP_PONG = 4 };

typedef struct {
    intptr_t h;  /* Windows: the pipe's HANDLE; Linux: the socket's descriptor */
    int open;
} DiscordIpc;

/* What the profile shows; NULL or "" leaves a field out. start: when the game started (Unix seconds), 0 none. */
typedef struct {
    const char *details, *state, *large_image, *large_text;    int64_t start;
    const char *button_label, *button_url;  /* one link button under the card (both, or none) */
} DiscordActivity;

/* Connects to the first Discord socket that answers, or to `path` alone when it isn't NULL (tests). 0: connected. */
int discord_ipc_connect(DiscordIpc *c, const char *path);
void discord_ipc_close(DiscordIpc *c);
/* One frame out. 0: sent; -1: the connection is gone (closed). */
int discord_ipc_send(DiscordIpc *c, uint32_t op, const char *json);
/* One frame in, waiting at most wait_ms for it to start: 1 a frame (its JSON in buf, cut to n - 1 bytes and ended
 * with 0), 0 none yet, -1 the connection is gone (closed). */
int discord_ipc_recv(DiscordIpc *c, uint32_t *op, char *buf, size_t n, int wait_ms);

/* The frame for op and json in out (header + JSON): its length, or 0 if it doesn't fit in cap. */
size_t discord_frame(uint8_t *out, size_t cap, uint32_t op, const char *json);
/* The handshake's JSON: {"v":1,"client_id":"<id>"}. Its length, or 0 if it doesn't fit. */
size_t discord_handshake_json(char *out, size_t n, const char *client_id);
/* SET_ACTIVITY's JSON for this process (pid) with the activity, or clearing it (a NULL). Its length, or 0. */
size_t discord_activity_json(char *out, size_t n, long pid, const DiscordActivity *a, unsigned nonce);

#endif

```

`runtime/src/dispatch.c`:

```c
/* Indirect calls and traps for recompiled code (decisions 0007, 0014). */
#include <inttypes.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "host.h"
#include "kernel.h"
#include "yw4rt.h"

GuestFn (*yw4_lookup_hook)(uint64_t addr);

static const Yw4CodeModule *module_of(uint64_t addr) {
    for (size_t i = 0; i < yw4_ncode; i++) {
        const Yw4CodeModule *m = &yw4_code[i];
        if (*m->base && addr - *m->base < m->size) return m;
    }
    return NULL;
}

const char *yw4_describe(uint64_t addr, char buf[48]) {
    const Yw4CodeModule *m = module_of(addr);
    if (m) snprintf(buf, 48, "%s+%#" PRIx64, m->name, addr - *m->base);
    else snprintf(buf, 48, "%#" PRIx64, addr);
    return buf;
}

/* ---- probes: log calls to chosen guest functions, no rebuild needed.
 * YW4_PROBE=main+0x9f6170,sdk+0x1234,...: each recompiled function starts with
 * `if (yw4_probe_any) yw4_probe(ctx, entry)`, so a call to a listed function prints its
 * first four arguments and its caller (YW4_PROBE_LIMIT per function, default 20;
 * YW4_PROBE_BT=1 adds the call stack). Addresses must be function entries. */

enum { MAX_PROBES = 64 };
int yw4_probe_any;
static uint64_t probes[MAX_PROBES];
static long probe_hits[MAX_PROBES];
static int nprobes;
static long probe_limit = 20;
static int probe_bt;

void yw4_probe_init(void) {
    const char *s = getenv("YW4_PROBE");
    if (!s || !*s) return;
    if (getenv("YW4_PROBE_LIMIT")) probe_limit = atol(getenv("YW4_PROBE_LIMIT"));
    probe_bt = getenv("YW4_PROBE_BT") && *getenv("YW4_PROBE_BT") != '0';
    while (*s && nprobes < MAX_PROBES) {
        char mod[16] = "";
        size_t n = strcspn(s, "+,");
        if (n < sizeof mod && s[n] == '+') {
            memcpy(mod, s, n);
            s += n + 1;
        }
        char *e;
        uint64_t off = strtoull(s, &e, 16), base = 0;
        for (size_t i = 0; i < yw4_ncode; i++)
            if (!strcmp(yw4_code[i].name, mod)) base = *yw4_code[i].base;
        if (mod[0] && !base) fprintf(stderr, "yw4: probe: no module %s\n", mod);
        else probes[nprobes++] = base + off;
        s = *e == ',' ? e + 1 : e;
        if (e == s && *s) break;
    }
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: probe: %d function(s)\n", nprobes);
    yw4_probe_any = nprobes > 0;
}

/* YW4_PROBE_UNIQUE=1: print a call only when its call stack (12 deep) is new: the
 * different paths that reach a function, however often it runs. Implies YW4_PROBE_BT. */
static int probe_unique = -1;

static int stack_is_new(const CPUState *ctx, uint64_t addr) {
    enum { SEEN = 8192 };
    static uint64_t seen[SEEN];
    static int nseen;
    uint64_t st[12], h = addr * 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15ull;
    int k = yw4_call_stack(ctx, st, 12);
    for (int j = 0; j < k; j++) h = (h ^ st[j]) * 0x100000001B3ull;
    for (int j = 0; j < nseen; j++)
        if (seen[j] == h) return 0;
    if (nseen < SEEN) seen[nseen++] = h;
    return 1;
}

/* YW4_WALK_LAYERS=1 (with main+0x9f6170 in YW4_PROBE): when the render thread draws a
 * layer (x2 = layer item; its draw list is *(*(item + 0x20) + 0x20), nodes linked at +0x30,
 * node[0] = draw object), print per layer every 300 calls: nodes, and how many the
 * renderer skips (layer kind 1 and object byte +0x1d1 == 0, or the node's mask byte +0x20
 * has the kind's bit). From the decompiled walker main+0xa45890. */
static void walk_layer(const CPUState *ctx) {
    static long calls;
    if (calls++ % 300 >= 8) return;  /* a few layers, now and then */
    uint64_t item = ctx->x[2];
    if (!item) return;
    uint8_t kind = *(const uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)(item + 8);
    uint64_t list = *(const uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)(item + 0x20);
    if (!list) return;
    uint64_t node = *(const uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)(list + 0x20);
    int n = 0, skipped = 0;
    for (; node && n < 100000; node = *(const uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)(node + 0x30), n++) {
        uint64_t obj = *(const uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)node;
        uint64_t o = *(const uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)(obj + 0x108) ? *(const uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)(obj + 0x108) : obj;
        if ((kind == 1 && !*(const uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)(o + 0x1d1)) ||
            ((1u << (kind & 31)) & *(const uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)(node + 0x20)))
            skipped++;
    }
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: layer %#" PRIx64 " kind %u: %d draw objects, %d skipped by the renderer\n", item, kind, n,
            skipped);
}

/* YW4_WATCH=<hex address>:<size>: a data watch. Every function entry (probes on) compares
 * the watched bytes with their last value; a change is printed with the function being
 * entered and its call stack: the writer is that function's caller, or ran just before.
 * Slow (a check on every call), for short runs. Heap addresses repeat from run to run. */
static uint64_t watch_addr, watch_last;
static unsigned watch_size;

static void watch_check(const CPUState *ctx, uint64_t addr) {
    uint64_t v = 0;
    memcpy(&v, (const void *)(uintptr_t)watch_addr, watch_size);
    uint64_t old = __atomic_exchange_n(&watch_last, v, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    if (old == v) return;
    char a[48], b[48];
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: watch %#" PRIx64 ": %#" PRIx64 " -> %#" PRIx64 " at entry of %s (from %s)\n", watch_addr, old, v,
            yw4_describe(addr, a), yw4_describe(ctx->x[30] - 4, b));
    uint64_t st[10];
    int k = yw4_call_stack(ctx, st, 10);
    for (int j = 1; j < k; j++) fprintf(stderr, "       %s\n", yw4_describe(st[j] - 4, a));
}

/* YW4_WATCHW=<hex address>:<size>: a real write watchpoint (host page protection,
 * Windows): every write reports the writing guest thread's call stack. Armed once the
 * address is mapped (checked at function entries). */
static uint64_t watchw_addr, watchw_size;

void yw4_watch_init(void) {
    const char *w = getenv("YW4_WATCHW");
    if (w && *w) {
        char *e;
        watchw_addr = strtoull(w, &e, 16);
        watchw_size = *e == ':' ? strtoull(e + 1, NULL, 10) : 8;
        yw4_probe_any = 1;
    }
    if (getenv("YW4_TRACE_RENDER_JOBS") || getenv("YW4_TRACE_DRAWLIST")) yw4_probe_any = 1;
    const char *s = getenv("YW4_WATCH");
    if (!s || !*s) return;
    char *e;
    watch_addr = strtoull(s, &e, 16);
    watch_size = *e == ':' ? (unsigned)strtoul(e + 1, NULL, 10) : 8;
    if (watch_size > 8) watch_size = 8;
    yw4_probe_any = 1;
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: watch %#" PRIx64 " (%u bytes)\n", watch_addr, watch_size);
}

/* YW4_TRACE_RENDER_JOBS=<frame>: the render thread's job list (decision 0023). Each frame
 * the render thread (main+0x979790) calls fn(device, a, b) for every node of the list at
 * [device+0x3210] (node: +8 fn, +0x10 a, +0x18 b, +0x30 next); main+0x971ad0 is a job that
 * runs a sub-list the same way. Prints every job run while presented frames <frame> to
 * <frame>+2 are current: the function, a, b and the byte at b+8 (the layer kind, when b is
 * a layer item). Lines starting "list" mark each start of the list walk. */
static int jobs_from = -2;
uint64_t yw4_frames_presented;  /* set by the present (nvn_objects.c) */

static void trace_render_job(const CPUState *ctx, uint64_t addr) {
    static uint64_t base;
    if (!base)
        for (size_t i = 0; i < yw4_ncode; i++)
            if (!strcmp(yw4_code[i].name, "main")) base = *yw4_code[i].base;
    uint64_t ret = ctx->x[30] - base;
    if (ret != 0x979840 && ret != 0x979854 && ret != 0x971afc) return;
    uint64_t frame = __atomic_load_n(&yw4_frames_presented, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    if (frame < (uint64_t)jobs_from || frame >= (uint64_t)jobs_from + 3) return;
    if (ret == 0x979840) {  /* main+0x9737f0, called before each walk of the list */
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: render jobs: t%04x list (presented frame %" PRIu64 ")\n",
                (unsigned)((uintptr_t)ctx >> 4 & 0xFFFF), frame);
        return;
    }
    char a[48];
    uint64_t b = ctx->x[2];
    unsigned kind = b >= 0x7000000000ull && b < 0x7800000000ull ? *(const uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)(b + 8) : 0xFFu;
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: render job t%04x %s%-14s a=%#" PRIx64 " b=%#" PRIx64 " [b+8]=%u\n",
            (unsigned)((uintptr_t)ctx >> 4 & 0xFFFF), ret == 0x971afc ? "    " : "", yw4_describe(addr, a), ctx->x[1], b,
            kind);
}

/* Called at every guest function entry while probes are on (YW4_TRACE_DRAWLIST sets it). */
void (*yw4_entry_hook)(CPUState *ctx, uint64_t addr);

void yw4_probe(CPUState *ctx, uint64_t addr) {
    if (yw4_entry_hook) yw4_entry_hook(ctx, addr);
    if (jobs_from == -2) {
        const char *j = getenv("YW4_TRACE_RENDER_JOBS");
        jobs_from = j && *j ? atoi(j) : -1;
    }
    if (jobs_from >= 0) trace_render_job(ctx, addr);
    if (watchw_size) {
        static unsigned tries;
        if (tries++ % 4096 == 0 && host_readable(watchw_addr, watchw_size)) {
            yw4_write_watch_arm(watchw_addr, watchw_size);
            watchw_size = 0;
        }
    }
    /* the watched memory is only readable once the game has mapped it */
    if (watch_size) {
        static int readable;
        static unsigned tries;
        if (!readable && tries++ % 4096 == 0) readable = host_readable(watch_addr, watch_size);
        if (readable) watch_check(ctx, addr);
    }
    static int walk = -1;
    if (walk < 0) walk = getenv("YW4_WALK_LAYERS") && *getenv("YW4_WALK_LAYERS") != '0';
    if (walk && probe_hits[0] >= 0) {
        char a[48];
        if (!strcmp(yw4_describe(addr, a), "main+0x9f6170")) walk_layer(ctx);
    }
    if (probe_unique < 0) {
        probe_unique = getenv("YW4_PROBE_UNIQUE") && *getenv("YW4_PROBE_UNIQUE") != '0';
        if (probe_unique) probe_bt = 1;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < nprobes; i++) {
        if (probes[i] != addr) continue;
        /* YW4_PROBE_X0=<hex>: only calls with that x0; YW4_PROBE_DUMP=<bytes>: then x0's first bytes as floats */
        static uint64_t only_x0 = ~0ull, dump = ~0ull;
        if (only_x0 == ~0ull) only_x0 = getenv("YW4_PROBE_X0") ? strtoull(getenv("YW4_PROBE_X0"), NULL, 16) : 0;
        if (dump == ~0ull) dump = getenv("YW4_PROBE_DUMP") ? strtoull(getenv("YW4_PROBE_DUMP"), NULL, 0) : 0;
        if (only_x0 && ctx->x[0] != only_x0) continue;
        /* YW4_PROBE_DUMP_PTR=<off>[,<off>...]: dump at the pointer found at x0+off (then at that +off, ...) */
        uint64_t at = ctx->x[0];
        for (const char *pp = getenv("YW4_PROBE_DUMP_PTR"); pp && *pp && at;) {
            char *pe;
            uint64_t off = strtoull(pp, &pe, 0);
            at = host_readable(at + off, 8) ? *(const uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)(at + off) : 0;
            pp = *pe == ',' ? pe + 1 : "";
        }
        if (dump && at && host_readable(at, dump)) {
            fprintf(stderr, "yw4: dump %s frame %" PRIu64 ":", yw4_describe(addr, (char[48]){0}),
                    __atomic_load_n(&yw4_frames_presented, __ATOMIC_RELAXED));
            for (uint64_t o = 0; o + 4 <= dump; o += 4) {
                float f;
                memcpy(&f, (const void *)(uintptr_t)(at + o), 4);
                fprintf(stderr, " %g", (double)f);
            }
            fputc('\n', stderr);
        }
        long n = __atomic_add_fetch(&probe_hits[i], 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
        if (probe_unique ? !stack_is_new(ctx, addr) : n > probe_limit) return;
        char a[48], b[48];
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: probe %s #%ld from %s: x0=%#" PRIx64 " x1=%#" PRIx64 " x2=%#" PRIx64 " x3=%#" PRIx64
                " s0=%g s1=%g s2=%g (frame %" PRIu64 ")\n",
                yw4_describe(addr, a), n, yw4_describe(ctx->x[30] - 4, b), ctx->x[0], ctx->x[1], ctx->x[2], ctx->x[3],
                (double)ctx->v[0].f[0], (double)ctx->v[1].f[0], (double)ctx->v[2].f[0],
                __atomic_load_n(&yw4_frames_presented, __ATOMIC_RELAXED));
        /* YW4_PROBE_MEM=x0+0xf4:1,x0+0xa0:8,...: also print memory at register + offset
         * (size 1, 2, 4 or 8 bytes), to see the fields a function tests */
        static const char *mem = (const char *)1;
        if (mem == (const char *)1) mem = getenv("YW4_PROBE_MEM");
        /* pointer chains: x0+8*+0x78:2 = 2 bytes at (the pointer at x0+8) + 0x78 */
        for (const char *m = mem; m && *m;) {
            char *e;
            const char *start = m;
            uint64_t p = 0, v = 0;
            if (*m == '@') {  /* @main+0x56b82c8:1: a module-relative address */
                char mod[16] = "";
                size_t n = strcspn(m + 1, "+");
                if (n < sizeof mod) memcpy(mod, m + 1, n);
                for (size_t i = 0; i < yw4_ncode; i++)
                    if (!strcmp(yw4_code[i].name, mod)) p = *yw4_code[i].base;
                e = (char *)m + 1 + n;
            } else if (*m == 'x') {
                unsigned reg = (unsigned)strtoul(m + 1, &e, 10);
                p = reg < 31 ? ctx->x[reg] : 0;
            } else {
                break;
            }
            int ok = 1;
            for (;;) {
                if (*e == '+') p += strtoull(e + 1, &e, 16);
                if (*e != '*') break;
                e++;
                if (p < 0x7000000000ull || p >= 0x7800000000ull) ok = 0;
                p = ok ? *(const uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)p : 0;
            }
            unsigned size = *e == ':' ? (unsigned)strtoul(e + 1, &e, 10) : 8;
            if (ok && p >= 0x7000000000ull && p < 0x7800000000ull) memcpy(&v, (const void *)(uintptr_t)p, size <= 8 ? size : 8);
            fprintf(stderr, "       [%.*s] = %#" PRIx64 "%s\n", (int)(e - start), start, v, ok ? "" : " (bad pointer)");
            m = *e == ',' ? e + 1 : e;
        }
        if (probe_bt) {
            uint64_t st[12];
            int k = yw4_call_stack(ctx, st, 12);
            for (int j = 1; j < k; j++) fprintf(stderr, "       %s\n", yw4_describe(st[j] - 4, a));
        }
        return;
    }
}

GuestFn yw4_lookup(uint64_t addr) {
    if (yw4_lookup_hook) {
        GuestFn fn = yw4_lookup_hook(addr);
        if (fn) return fn;
    }
    const Yw4CodeModule *m = module_of(addr);
    if (!m) return NULL;
    uint64_t off = addr - *m->base;
    size_t lo = 0, hi = m->nfuncs;
    while (lo < hi) {
        size_t mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
        if (m->funcs[mid].offset < off) lo = mid + 1;
        else hi = mid;
    }
    return lo < m->nfuncs && m->funcs[lo].offset == off ? m->funcs[lo].fn : NULL;
}

/* One Yw4Target per target address, made on first use and never freed, in an open-addressed
 * table that only grows (the game has a few thousand indirect-call targets). */
static HostLock targets_lock = HOST_LOCK_INIT;
static Yw4Target **targets;
static size_t targets_cap, targets_n;

/* The records a thread has asked for, by target: a call site that calls more than one target (a virtual call on
 * objects of several classes) misses its own one-record cache often, and every miss took the table's lock: with
 * yw4_resolve, ~7% of the main thread in the busy street (2026-11-02, YW4_PROFILE). Records never move or go. */
#define TARGET_CACHE 4096
static _Thread_local const Yw4Target *target_cache[TARGET_CACHE];

const Yw4Target *yw4_resolve_target(uint64_t target) {
    unsigned slot = (unsigned)((target >> 2) ^ (target >> 14)) & (TARGET_CACHE - 1);
    const Yw4Target *seen = target_cache[slot];
    if (seen && seen->addr == target) return seen;  /* game functions only (below) */
    GuestFn fn = yw4_resolve(target);  /* traps, or longjmps to a setjmp point, if there's none */
    host_lock(&targets_lock);
    if (targets_n * 2 >= targets_cap) {  /* grow: rehash into twice the room */
        size_t cap = targets_cap ? targets_cap * 2 : 8192;
        Yw4Target **t = calloc(cap, sizeof *t);
        if (!t) yw4_exit(3, __FILE__, __LINE__);
        for (size_t i = 0; i < targets_cap; i++)
            if (targets[i]) {
                size_t j = (targets[i]->addr >> 2) & (cap - 1);
                while (t[j]) j = (j + 1) & (cap - 1);
                t[j] = targets[i];
            }
        free(targets);
        targets = t, targets_cap = cap;
    }
    size_t j = (target >> 2) & (targets_cap - 1);
    while (targets[j] && targets[j]->addr != target) j = (j + 1) & (targets_cap - 1);
    if (!targets[j]) {
        Yw4Target *t = malloc(sizeof *t);
        if (!t) yw4_exit(3, __FILE__, __LINE__);
        t->addr = target, t->fn = fn;
        targets[j] = t, targets_n++;
    }
    const Yw4Target *r = targets[j];
    host_unlock(&targets_lock);
    if (!(yw4_lookup_hook && yw4_lookup_hook(target))) target_cache[slot] = r;  /* not a host callback */
    return r;
}

/* Indirect calls (virtual calls, function pointers) go through here a lot: a small
 * per-thread cache saves the binary search for the targets seen most recently. */
#define RESOLVE_CACHE 4096
static _Thread_local struct {
    uint64_t target;
    GuestFn fn;
} resolve_cache[RESOLVE_CACHE];

GuestFn yw4_resolve(uint64_t target) {
    unsigned slot = (unsigned)((target >> 2) ^ (target >> 14)) & (RESOLVE_CACHE - 1);
    if (target && resolve_cache[slot].target == target) return resolve_cache[slot].fn;  /* game functions only */
    /* A host callback (the loader's hook): its lookup also sets the call's data, so it is never cached. The hook
     * stays installed once the first callback is registered (at start-up): cached only while there was none, the
     * cache was off for the whole game, every indirect call a binary search (2026-11-02). */
    GuestFn fn = yw4_lookup_hook ? yw4_lookup_hook(target) : NULL;
    if (fn) return fn;
    fn = yw4_lookup(target);
    if (fn) resolve_cache[slot].target = target, resolve_cache[slot].fn = fn;
    if (!fn) {
        yw4_setjmp_resume(target);  /* a longjmp back to a setjmp's return address? */
        char where[48];
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: indirect call to %s: no translated function there\n", yw4_describe(target, where));
        yw4_stop();
    }
    return fn;
}

_Noreturn void yw4_unimplemented(CPUState *ctx, uint64_t pc, uint32_t enc) {
    (void)ctx;
    char where[48];
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: untranslated instruction %08" PRIx32 " at %s\n", enc, yw4_describe(pc, where));
    abort();
}

_Noreturn void yw4_guest_trap(CPUState *ctx, uint64_t pc, uint32_t enc) {
    (void)ctx;
    char where[48];
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: guest trap %08" PRIx32 " at %s\n", enc, yw4_describe(pc, where));
    abort();
}
```

`runtime/src/dof.c`:

```c
/* Our distance blur, the engine side (decision 0038, docs/frame.md "Distance blur").
 *
 * The engine's distance blur is main+0x8007d0(device, renderer): the scene shrunk into the half-size image,
 * blur rounds between that and its pair (main+0x7f3620), and a composite onto the scene by depth. A hook
 * (recomp/overrides.toml) runs before it and gathers what those draws use from the renderer object: its image
 * records 0 (scene), 9 and 10 (the half-size pair) and 42 (the G-buffer's depth), the number of rounds, the blur
 * radius and spread, and the focus settings, computed into the same constants as the engine computes them (the
 * Gaussian weights with the sdk's expf, which is musl's: runtime/src/hle_math.c). Our pass (gpu_post.c) is
 * recorded into the device's command buffer in their place.
 *
 * Not ours, so the engine's function runs: the variant with renderer +0x2c70 set (a depth-aware shrink with a
 * lookup texture, a different composite), and a depth record without its descriptor.
 *
 * YW4_DOF_PASS=native: ours, and the hook skips the engine's function. check: the engine draws as usual and ours
 * draws the same into copies first, compared after the game's composite (gpu_post.c). game: the engine's.
 * Default: ours; the settings panel (F1, DISTANCE BLUR PASS) switches while playing.
 * As with bloom (bloom.c), the engine's record of what is bound is left as it was; what it changes that is not
 * a binding is done here (skipped_effects).
 */
#include <math.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "post.h"
#include "yw4rt.h"

float musl_expf(float);  /* the sdk's expf (hle_math.c) */

enum { MODE_GAME, MODE_CHECK, MODE_NATIVE };
static int mode = -1;
static int blur_mode_v = -1;  /* the shared blur rounds' (YW4_BLUR_PASS) */
static _Thread_local int in_original;  /* the blur hook's check: the game's own run of f_7f3620 */
static uint64_t variant_seen;  /* calls left to the game: the +0x2c70 variant */

#define U8(a) (*(const uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)(a))
#define U16(a) (*(const uint16_t *)(uintptr_t)(a))
#define U32(a) (*(const uint32_t *)(uintptr_t)(a))
#define U64(a) (*(const uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)(a))
#define F32(a) (*(const float *)(uintptr_t)(a))
#define U16W(a) (*(uint16_t *)(uintptr_t)(a))
#define U32W(a) (*(uint32_t *)(uintptr_t)(a))

static int dof_mode(void) {
    int m = __atomic_load_n(&mode, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
    if (m >= 0) return m;
    const char *s = getenv("YW4_DOF_PASS");
    m = s && !strcmp(s, "game") ? MODE_GAME : s && !strcmp(s, "check") ? MODE_CHECK : MODE_NATIVE;
    int unset = -1;
    if (__atomic_compare_exchange_n(&mode, &unset, m, 0, __ATOMIC_ACQ_REL, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) && m != MODE_GAME)
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: distance blur: %s\n", m == MODE_CHECK ? "ours checked against the game's" : "ours");
    return __atomic_load_n(&mode, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
}

int dof_native(void) { return dof_mode() == MODE_NATIVE; }

void dof_toggle(void) {
    int m = dof_native() ? MODE_GAME : MODE_NATIVE;
    __atomic_store_n(&mode, m, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: distance blur: %s (settings panel)\n", m == MODE_NATIVE ? "ours" : "the game's");
}

/* The renderer's image record i: its guest NVNtexture (record +0x10 is a view, its first word + 0x18), or 0. */
static uint64_t record_texture(uint64_t renderer, unsigned i) {
    uint64_t rec = renderer + 0x2e28 + 0x28ull * i, view = U64(rec + 0x10);
    return view && U64(view) ? U64(view) + 0x18 : 0;
}

/* f_7f3620's weights for radius r: exp(-k^2 / 2r^2) for k = 0..7, over twice their sum, the centre counted twice
 * in the shader. In its order and precision (float, the sum left to right). */
static void gauss_weights(float r, float w[8]) {
    float r2 = r * r;
    float e0 = musl_expf(-0.0f / r2), e1 = musl_expf(-0.5f / r2), e2 = musl_expf(-2.0f / r2), e3 = musl_expf(-4.5f / r2);
    float e4 = musl_expf(-8.0f / r2), e5 = musl_expf(-12.5f / r2), e6 = musl_expf(-18.0f / r2);
    float e7 = musl_expf(-24.5f / r2);
    float sum = e0 + 0.0f + e1 + e2 + e3 + e4 + e5 + e6 + e7;
    sum = sum + sum;
    w[0] = e0 / sum, w[1] = e1 / sum, w[2] = e2 / sum, w[3] = e3 / sum;
    w[4] = e4 / sum, w[5] = e5 / sum, w[6] = e6 / sum, w[7] = e7 / sum;
}

/* What the engine's distance blur changes besides its bindings, as it does it: the device's flag +0x45da bit 0,
 * the "render target read as a texture" bits in +0x45ac for every image it binds (0x12 when the record's +0x22
 * or +0x23 is set, else 0x10), and its draw statistics (+0x4654 draws, +0x4658 count / 3). */
static void skipped_effects(uint64_t device, uint64_t renderer, uint32_t draws) {
    static const unsigned records[] = {0, 9, 10, 42};
    U16W(device + 0x45da) |= 1;
    for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof records / sizeof *records; i++) {
        uint64_t rec = renderer + 0x2e28 + 0x28ull * records[i];
        U32W(device + 0x45ac) |= U8(rec + 0x22) || U8(rec + 0x23) ? 0x12u : 0x10u;
    }
    U32W(device + 0x4654) += draws;
    U32W(device + 0x4658) += draws * (4 / 3);
}

/* hook on main+0x8007d0 (device, renderer), before its body */
int yw4_hook_dof(CPUState *ctx) {
    int m = dof_mode();
    if (m == MODE_GAME) return 0;
    uint64_t device = ctx->x[0], renderer = ctx->x[1];
    uint32_t rounds = U32(renderer + 0x868);
    if (!rounds) return 0;  /* the engine draws nothing either */
    if (U8(renderer + 0x2c70)) {
        if (!variant_seen++) fprintf(stderr, "yw4: distance blur: the depth-aware variant: the game's\n");
        return 0;
    }
    uint64_t desc = U64(renderer + 0x34c0);  /* the depth record's descriptor: its size at u16 +4, +6 */
    static const unsigned records[DOF_IMAGES] = {0, 9, 10, 42};
    DofPass p;
    memset(&p, 0, sizeof p);
    for (int i = 0; i < DOF_IMAGES; i++) {
        uint64_t g = record_texture(renderer, records[i]);
        const NvnTexture *t = g ? HOST(NvnTexture, g) : NULL;
        if (!t) {
            static int logged;
            if (!logged++) fprintf(stderr, "yw4: distance blur: image record %u has no texture: the game's\n", records[i]);
            return 0;
        }
        memcpy(&p.tex[i], t, sizeof p.tex[i]);
    }
    p.rounds = rounds > 32 ? 32 : rounds;
    {   /* the blur's settings when they change (battles use more rounds than towns), the first 32 times */
        static uint32_t last_rounds, changes;
        static float last_radius, last_spread;
        float radius = F32(renderer + 0x864), spread = F32(renderer + 0x860);
        if ((rounds != last_rounds || radius != last_radius || spread != last_spread) && changes++ < 32)
            fprintf(stderr, "yw4: distance blur: %u rounds, radius %g, spread %g\n", rounds, radius, spread);
        last_rounds = rounds, last_radius = radius, last_spread = spread;
    }
    gauss_weights(F32(renderer + 0x864), p.weights);
    p.spread = F32(renderer + 0x860);
    float n = F32(renderer + 0x86c);
    p.texel[0] = n / (float)U16(desc + 4), p.texel[1] = n / (float)U16(desc + 6);
    /* the composite's fragment constants, as the engine computes them */
    float near = F32(renderer + 0x5c0), far = F32(renderer + 0x5c4);
    float f0 = F32(renderer + 0x850), f1 = F32(renderer + 0x854), f2 = F32(renderer + 0x858), f3 = F32(renderer + 0x85c);
    float range = f1 - f0;
    float *c = p.focus;
    c[0] = near * far, c[1] = near - far, c[2] = near - f0, c[3] = range != 0.0f ? 1.0f / range : 0.0f;
    c[4] = f2, c[5] = 1.0f - f3, c[6] = f2 != 0.0f ? 1.0f / f2 : 0.0f, c[7] = f3 != 0.0f ? 1.0f / f3 : 0.0f;
    p.far = far;
    p.check = m == MODE_CHECK;
    nvn_record_native(ctx, U64(device + 0x10d0) + 0xd8, gpu_dof_pass, &p, sizeof p);
    if (m != MODE_NATIVE) return 0;
    skipped_effects(device, renderer, 2 + 2 * p.rounds);
    return 1;
}

/* ---- the engine's shared blur rounds: main+0x7f3620(radius s0, device x0, spread pair x1, rounds w2, target id w3,
 * down attachment w4, across attachment w5, record a x6, record b x7). Per round it blurs record a across into
 * the target's attachment w5 (record b) and record b down into attachment w4 (record a), with the weights of
 * gauss_weights and the spread over the target's size. Its callers: the distance blur above (whose own pass draws
 * these rounds when it is ours), main+0x7f1bf0, main+0x804570, main+0x80a0a0. YW4_BLUR_PASS=native: ours; check:
 * ours into copies, then the game's, compared (gpu_post.c); default: the game's.
 * NOT the battles' blur (2026-10-29, probes in a battle): f_7f1bf0 and this function never run there. The battle's
 * 12 rounds at 960x540 are a loop of their own in the render job main+0x897d90 (below). */

static int blur_mode(void) {
    int m = __atomic_load_n(&blur_mode_v, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
    if (m >= 0) return m;
    const char *s = getenv("YW4_BLUR_PASS");
    m = s && !strcmp(s, "native") ? MODE_NATIVE : s && !strcmp(s, "check") ? MODE_CHECK : MODE_GAME;
    int unset = -1;
    if (__atomic_compare_exchange_n(&blur_mode_v, &unset, m, 0, __ATOMIC_ACQ_REL, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) && m != MODE_GAME)
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: blur rounds: %s\n", m == MODE_CHECK ? "ours checked against the game's" : "ours");
    return __atomic_load_n(&blur_mode_v, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
}

int blur_native(void) { return blur_mode() == MODE_NATIVE; }

static int fast_v = -1;

int blur_fast(void) {
    int f = __atomic_load_n(&fast_v, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
    if (f < 0) {
        const char *e = getenv("YW4_BLUR_FAST");  /* on unless 0: the owner saw no difference (2026-10-29) */
        f = !(e && *e && !atoi(e));
        __atomic_store_n(&fast_v, f, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    }
    return f;
}

void blur_fast_toggle(void) {
    int f = !blur_fast();
    __atomic_store_n(&fast_v, f, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: blur rounds: %s (settings panel)\n", f ? "fast" : "the game's");
}

/* ---- the battles' blur: the render job main+0x897d90(device x0, job x1), queued by main+0x89ac00 from
 * main+0x311f40. It copies into target job+0 (attachment 2), then n rounds: across into target job+2 attachment 4,
 * down into its attachment 2, with the Gaussian weights of the shared rounds (radius job+0x10); then back into
 * target job+0. The job (work/ghidra/897d90.c): u16 +0 target a, u16 +2 target b, f32 +4 strength, f32 +8 / +0xc
 * spread across / down, f32 +0x10 radius, i32 +0x14 rounds at most; n = (uint)(strength * (max - 1) + 1) (12 in
 * the battles seen), each step spread * strength / the image's size.
 * BATTLE BLUR fast: the game draws it from a copy of the job with m = ceil(n / 4) rounds, strength 1 and the
 * spreads times strength * sqrt(n / m): the same total width (a Gaussian's width grows with the square root of
 * the rounds) for a quarter of the passes. Guest addresses are host addresses, so the copy can live here. */
int yw4_hook_battle_blur(CPUState *ctx) {
    static _Thread_local uint8_t copy[0x20] __attribute__((aligned(16)));
    uint64_t job = ctx->x[1];
    if (!job) return 0;
    float strength = F32(job + 4);
    int32_t max = (int32_t)U32(job + 0x14);
    uint32_t n = (uint32_t)(strength * (float)(max - 1) + 1.0f);
    int fast = blur_fast() && n >= 2;
    uint32_t m = fast ? (n + 3) / 4 : n;
    {   /* what it blurs and how, when that changes, the first 64 times */
        static uint32_t last_n, last_m, changes;
        if ((n != last_n || m != last_m) && changes++ < 64)
            fprintf(stderr, "yw4: battle blur: %u rounds (strength %g of %d) drawn as %u%s, radius %g, spread %g %g\n", n,
                    strength, max, m, fast ? " (fast)" : "", F32(job + 0x10), F32(job + 8), F32(job + 0xc));
        last_n = n, last_m = m;
    }
    if (!fast) return 0;
    float k = strength * sqrtf((float)n / (float)m);
    memcpy(copy, (const void *)(uintptr_t)job, sizeof copy);
    float one = 1.0f, sx = F32(job + 8) * k, sy = F32(job + 0xc) * k;
    int32_t mm = (int32_t)m;
    memcpy(copy + 4, &one, 4), memcpy(copy + 8, &sx, 4), memcpy(copy + 0xc, &sy, 4), memcpy(copy + 0x14, &mm, 4);
    ctx->x[1] = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)copy;
    return 0;  /* the game's job draws from the copy */
}

/* A record pointer's texture (the record's +0x10 view, its first word + 0x18), copied; 0 if none. */
static int record_copy(uint64_t rec, NvnTexture *out) {
    uint64_t view = rec ? U64(rec + 0x10) : 0, g = view && U64(view) ? U64(view) + 0x18 : 0;
    const NvnTexture *t = g ? HOST(NvnTexture, g) : NULL;
    if (!t) return 0;
    memcpy(out, t, sizeof *out);
    return 1;
}

int yw4_hook_blur(CPUState *ctx) {
    if (in_original) return 0;
    int m = blur_mode();
    if (blur_fast()) m = MODE_NATIVE;  /* the fast rounds are ours (and not checked: they differ) */
    if (m == MODE_GAME) return 0;
    uint64_t device = ctx->x[0], spread = ctx->x[1], ra = ctx->x[6], rb = ctx->x[7];
    uint32_t rounds = (uint32_t)ctx->x[2];
    BlurPass p;
    memset(&p, 0, sizeof p);
    if (!rounds || !record_copy(ra, &p.a) || !record_copy(rb, &p.b)) return 0;
    p.rounds = rounds > 31 ? 32 : rounds;
    gauss_weights(ctx->v[0].f[0], p.weights);
    /* over the target's size: the engine's is its render target's (u16 +0x3a, +0x3c), the records' images' */
    p.step[0] = F32(spread) / (float)p.b.width, p.step[1] = F32(spread + 4) / (float)p.b.height;
    {   /* what is blurred and how much, when it changes, the first 32 times */
        static uint32_t last_rounds, changes;
        static uint64_t last_a;
        if ((rounds != last_rounds || ra != last_a) && changes++ < 32)
            fprintf(stderr, "yw4: blur rounds: %u rounds of %ux%u (from main+%#llx), radius %g\n", rounds, p.a.width,
                    p.a.height, (unsigned long long)(ctx->x[30] - yw4_image_base), ctx->v[0].f[0]);
        last_rounds = rounds, last_a = ra;
    }
    uint64_t cmd = U64(device + 0x10d0) + 0xd8;
    p.check = m == MODE_CHECK;
    nvn_record_native(ctx, cmd, gpu_blur_pass, &p, sizeof p);
    if (m == MODE_CHECK) {  /* the game's rounds now, then the comparison */
        static GuestFn original;
        if (!original) original = yw4_lookup(yw4_image_base + 0x7f3620);
        if (!original) return 0;
        in_original = 1;
        original(ctx);
        in_original = 0;
        nvn_record_native(ctx, cmd, gpu_blur_check_end, &p, sizeof p);
        return 1;
    }
    U16W(device + 0x45da) |= 1;  /* what f_7f3900 changes besides bindings, per pass (see skipped_effects) */
    for (int i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
        uint64_t rec = i ? rb : ra;
        U32W(device + 0x45ac) |= U8(rec + 0x22) || U8(rec + 0x23) ? 0x12u : 0x10u;
    }
    U32W(device + 0x4654) += 2 * p.rounds;
    U32W(device + 0x4658) += 2 * p.rounds * (4 / 3);
    return 1;
}
```

```c
/* nn::ec, the eShop: there is none here. The game's "additional content" menu entry opens the
 * shop's add-on list as a library applet; it just returns at once (as if the shop were closed).
 * Delivery's "Download Code" opens the shop's enter-code page the same way: a popup says that this
 * needs the Nintendo eShop, then it returns (passwords are typed in the game's own keyboard popup,
 * swkbd.c). Overrides of the sdk functions (recomp/overrides.toml). */
#include <stdio.h>

#include "gamemenu.h"
#include "host.h"
#include "window.h"
#include "yw4load.h"

/* ShowShopAddOnContentList(const UserHandle &) -> Result */
void yw4_ec_ShowShopAddOnContentList(CPUState *c) { c->x[0] = 0; }

/* ShowShopEnterCodeScene(const UserHandle &) -> Result. Before this override the sdk's own code ran and asked
 * for a library applet (CreateLibraryApplet), which stops the run. The game waits here, as on the Switch while
 * the shop shows: its last frame is shown again with the popup (window_repaint), until OK. */
void yw4_ec_ShowShopEnterCodeScene(CPUState *c) {
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: ec: the shop's enter-code page asked for (download code): not here\n");
    if (window_repaint(1) == 0) {
        gamemenu_message_begin("Download codes aren't available",
                               "Download codes are entered in the Nintendo eShop, which this PC version doesn't "
                               "have. Passwords still work: choose Password instead.");
        char ignored[8];
        while (!gamemenu_prompt_take(ignored, sizeof ignored)) {
            window_repaint(0);
            host_sleep_ns(16 * 1000000LL);
        }
        window_repaint(0);
    }
    c->x[0] = 0;
}
```

```h
/* What happened in a run, as data (perf.c): one JSON object per line in <perf folder>/perf_<time>.jsonl, next to
 * the per-frame perf_<time>.csv of the same run. The test tools read it instead of searching the log's text
 * (tools/dev/scene.py). Written and flushed as each thing happens, so a run that is killed keeps its lines.
 *
 *     {"kind":"stall","frame":5086,"t":71.204,"ms":52.9,"where":"gpu thread"}
 *
 * kind: screenshot (path), set (name, value: YW4_SET_AT), stall (ms, where; for the GPU thread also pipelines,
 * images and their ms), ab (pass, target, depth, differ, texels: a same-frame A/B's count), fatal (text),
 * unreached (what, frame: scheduled for a frame the run never got to), minimap (what, target, ...: the minimap
 * watch, gpu_watch.c), geometry_missed (addr, size: a small vertex range rewritten before its pages showed it,
 * gpu.c; the first 64), end (frames). Off with the performance
 * log (YW4_PERF=0). Any thread. */
#ifndef YW4_EVENTS_H
#define YW4_EVENTS_H

#include <stdint.h>

/* `fields`: more members as JSON text, printf style, without braces or a leading comma ("\"ms\":%.1f"); NULL for
 * none. Only for numbers and texts that need no escaping (names of ours). */
void yw4_event(const char *kind, uint64_t frame, const char *fields, ...);
/* One text member, escaped (a path, a message). */
void yw4_event_text(const char *kind, uint64_t frame, const char *key, const char *text);

#endif
```

`runtime/src/framerate.c`:

```c
/* The frame rate: 30 (the game's), 60 (the default), 120, 144, the display's refresh (vsync) or no limit, switchable while playing (YW4_FPS, panel FRAME RATE).
 *
 * nnMain paces itself. A static constructor sets the byte at main+0x56b82e8 to 2 (vsyncs per frame, n) and
 * main+0x56b82e9 to 1 (limiter on). nnMain reads n once at start:
 *   - present interval n (nvnWindowSetPresentInterval), so the display shows each frame for n vsyncs;
 *   - its own limiter (main+0x950c3c): it sleeps until the frame took (n - 1) / 60 + 0.015 s (31.7 ms for 2),
 *     then spins on the tick counter;
 *   - 60 / n as the rate for a once-a-second GPU load check (main+0x9503c0): GPU time from two timestamps, over
 *     96% of a frame lowers the dynamic resolution (u16 main+0x56b82ce, the 3D view's lines, 900 at most) by 18
 *     lines, under 88% raises it. Our timestamps are not the GPU's (nvn_cmdbuf.c writes none with the GPU on),
 *     so it stays at 900 whatever n says (watched 2026-10-29: 12,413 writes, all 900).
 * The game's time step is not n: every frame it measures the real time since the last one (system tick,
 * clamped to 0.2 s, main+0x94ee78) and stores it at main+0x586527c, and the tasks scale their work by it.
 * So faster frames keep the game's speed: walk replays at 60 and ~140 frames/s end in the same place, and
 * battles play right at high frame rates (owner 2026-10-29).
 *
 * Because n is read only once, the hook on nnMain's start sets it to 0 (no limiter, interval 0) and the rate
 * is held here instead, at the present: 30 and 60 wait for the 60 Hz vsync (every 2nd / every one, as the
 * game's own interval did), 120 and 144 sleep to a timer, unlimited doesn't wait. Above 60 the window
 * presents with MAILBOX or IMMEDIATE (window.c), so the monitor's refresh doesn't cap it.
 *
 * Vsync (YW4_FPS=vsync): no wait here; the swapchain presents with FIFO, so each frame waits for the display's
 * refresh and the rate locks to it (120 on a 120 Hz screen). Running free at about the refresh rate shows the
 * frames at uneven refreshes: the menus' scrolling background stuttered (owner, 2026-10-30, 120 Hz screen;
 * smooth at 30, an even divisor). Known gap: chosen at start it locks (frame intervals 8.3 ms, 95% within 8.6 on
 * the owner's 120 Hz laptop screen); switched to while playing, the swapchain is made again with FIFO, yet the
 * intervals stay loose (95% within 11 ms) on that hybrid-GPU laptop, so the panel says it applies after a restart.
 * A wait on the display's own refresh (DwmFlush) may fix it. While frame generation runs it paces the frames itself
 * (MAILBOX), so this applies only without it (2D screens drop it: gpu_fg.c, gpu_dlssg.cpp).
 *
 * YW4_FRAME_VSYNCS=<n>: the old way, the game's own pacing with that n (2 = the game's original), fixed for
 * the run; the panel row then does nothing. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "framerate.h"
#include "gpu.h"
#include "host.h"
#include "kernel.h"
#include "window.h"
#include "yw4load.h"
#include "yw4rt.h"

static const int rates[] = {30, 60, 120, 144, -1, 0};  /* -1: the display's refresh (vsync) */
enum { NRATES = sizeof rates / sizeof *rates };

static int index_v = -1;
static int game_paces, game_n;  /* YW4_FRAME_VSYNCS given: the game's limiter with that n, not ours */

int framerate_index(void) {
    int i = __atomic_load_n(&index_v, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
    if (i >= 0) return i;
    const char *e = getenv("YW4_FPS");
    int want = e && !strcmp(e, "vsync") ? -1 : e && *e ? atoi(e) : 60;  /* 60 by default (owner, 2026-11-13); 30 is the game's own */
    i = 1;  /* an unknown value: 60 */
    for (int k = 0; k < NRATES; k++)
        if (rates[k] == want) i = k;
    __atomic_store_n(&index_v, i, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    return i;
}

void framerate_cycle(void) {
    int i = (framerate_index() + 1) % NRATES;
    __atomic_store_n(&index_v, i, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    if (rates[i] < 0) fprintf(stderr, "yw4: frame rate: the display's refresh (settings panel)\n");
    else if (rates[i]) fprintf(stderr, "yw4: frame rate: %d frames/s (settings panel)\n", rates[i]);
    else fprintf(stderr, "yw4: frame rate: no limit (settings panel)\n");
}

int framerate_hz(void) { return game_paces ? (game_n ? 60 / game_n : 0) : rates[framerate_index()]; }

/* How a cap of hz (30 or 60) is held: 0 by the emulated vsync thread's tick (ours), 1 by a deadline aligned to the
 * display's refresh (from Quandiy's fork). Measured 2026-11-12 (decision 0064): at 30 refresh has about an eighth
 * of the tick's long frames on 120 and 60 Hz displays, at 60 the two are the same and refresh costs CPU, so the
 * default is refresh at 30 and the tick at 60. YW4_PACE=refresh or tick: that way at both. Read once. */
int framerate_pacing(int hz) {
    static int force = -2;  /* -1 the default, 0 tick, 1 refresh */
    if (force == -2) {
        const char *e = getenv("YW4_PACE");
        force = e && !strcmp(e, "refresh") ? 1 : e && !strcmp(e, "tick") ? 0 : -1;
    }
    return force >= 0 ? force : hz == 30;
}

void framerate_wait(void) {
    static int said_tick;       /* the rate the log last named the tick wait for (0: not, or the other way since) */
    static uint64_t next_flip;  /* vsync count the next frame may show at (30 / 60) */
    static int64_t due;         /* host time the next frame may show at (120 / 144) */
    if (game_paces) return;     /* the game's limiter and interval did it */
    int hz = framerate_hz();
    yw4_vsync_start();
    /* A full-screen video (gpu_movie_screen: the title menu's background, the opening movie) is held at 30, its own
     * rate, whatever the cap. A 30 frames/s video at 60 shows each picture for 2 frames; when 60 doesn't divide the
     * display's refresh (165 Hz: 2.75 refreshes a frame) and there is no variable refresh, those frames stay 2 or
     * 3 refreshes in an uneven order, so the pictures stayed 30 or 36 ms at random and the video stuttered (the
     * game itself gave every picture exactly 2 frames, YW4_MOVIE_LOG). At 30 they alternate 30, 36, 30, 36 ms,
     * which looks smooth (PresentMon, owner's 165 Hz laptop, 2026-11-18). YW4_MOVIE_30=0 turns it off. */
    static int movie_30 = -1, said_movie;
    if (movie_30 < 0) movie_30 = !(getenv("YW4_MOVIE_30") && !strcmp(getenv("YW4_MOVIE_30"), "0"));
    int movie = movie_30 && hz != 30 && gpu_movie_screen();
    if (movie != said_movie) {
        said_movie = movie;
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: frame rate: %s\n", movie ? "a video is playing: 30 frames/s, its own rate, until it ends"
                                                       : "the video ended: back to the panel's frame rate");
    }
    if (movie) hz = 30;
    /* Refresh (the default at 30, framerate_pacing; from Quandiy's fork, where it was the default at both): a
     * deadline on this thread, its period a whole number of the display's refreshes (4 x 8.33 ms on a 120 Hz screen
     * at 30, so every frame shows for the same refreshes and the phase doesn't drift). A late frame starts the
     * deadline again from now, where the tick wait would lose a whole tick: at 30 that turned frames a little over
     * 33 ms into 50 ms ones (decision 0064). */
    int pace_refresh = framerate_pacing(hz);
    if ((hz == 30 || hz == 60) && pace_refresh) {
        next_flip = 0;
        double refresh = window_refresh_hz();
        int64_t period = 1000000000ll / hz;
        if (refresh > 1.0) {
            double k = refresh / hz;
            long whole = (long)(k + 0.5);
            if (whole >= 1 && k / (double)whole > 0.99 && k / (double)whole < 1.01)
                period = (int64_t)((double)whole * 1e9 / refresh + 0.5);
        }
        static int64_t said_period;  /* the log names the way and its period, again when either changes */
        if (period != said_period) {
            said_period = period, said_tick = 0;
            fprintf(stderr, "yw4: pacing: refresh, period %.3f ms at %.2f Hz (%d frames/s)\n", (double)period / 1e6,
                    refresh, hz);
        }
        int64_t now = host_now_ns();
        if (!due || now - due > period / 2) due = now;  /* first frame, or late: start again from now, no burst */
        if (due - now > 1000000) host_sleep_ns(due - now - 1000000);  /* the timer is good to ~1 ms: spin the rest */
        while (host_now_ns() < due) {}
        due += period;
        return;
    }
    if (hz == 30 || hz == 60) {
        if (said_tick != hz) {
            said_tick = hz;
            fprintf(stderr, "yw4: pacing: tick (%d frames/s: %s 60 Hz vsync tick)\n", hz, hz == 30 ? "every 2nd" : "every");
        }
        uint64_t now = yw4_vsync_count();
        if (next_flip < now + 1) next_flip = now + 1;
        yw4_wait_vsync(next_flip);
        next_flip += hz == 30 ? 2 : 1;
        due = 0;
        return;
    }
    next_flip = 0;
    if (hz <= 0) return;  /* no limit, or vsync: the swapchain's FIFO waits */
    int64_t period = 1000000000ll / hz, now = host_now_ns();
    if (!due || now - due > 3 * period) due = now;  /* first frame, or fell far behind: don't burst to catch up */
    if (due - now > 1000000) host_sleep_ns(due - now - 1000000);  /* the timer is good to ~1 ms: spin the rest */
    while (host_now_ns() < due) {}
    due += period;
}

/* The game's time step of its latest frame, seconds (main+0x586527c, nnMain stores it each frame). */
float framerate_game_dt(void) {
    return *(const float *)(uintptr_t)(*yw4_modules[YW4_MAIN].base + 0x586527c);
}

int yw4_hook_nnmain(CPUState *ctx) {
    (void)ctx;
    uint8_t *n = (uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)(*yw4_modules[YW4_MAIN].base + 0x56b82e8);
    const char *e = getenv("YW4_FRAME_VSYNCS");
    game_paces = e && *e;
    int v = game_paces ? atoi(e) : 0;
    game_n = v;
    if (game_paces) fprintf(stderr, "yw4: frame rate: the game's own pacing, %d vsyncs per frame (game's %d)\n", v, *n);
    else if (framerate_hz() < 0) fprintf(stderr, "yw4: frame rate: the display's refresh, ours (the game's limiter off)\n");
    else if (framerate_hz()) fprintf(stderr, "yw4: frame rate: %d frames/s, ours (the game's limiter off)\n", framerate_hz());
    else fprintf(stderr, "yw4: frame rate: no limit, ours (the game's limiter off)\n");
    *n = (uint8_t)v;
    return 0;
}

/* Motions that must last a moment before a character may leave them, above 30 frames/s (issue #9).
 *
 * main+0x1c6170(action, dt) runs once a frame for each character's action state machine (main+0x1bcd70). It adds
 * dt to the time spent in the current motion (action+0xafc) and, once that reaches the motion's least time
 * (motion+0xb8, motion = action+0xae8, when bit 0 of motion+0xc1 is set), sets "may leave" (action+0xb1e). The
 * state machine (main+0x1c2aa0) only moves on from some states once that is set; while it waits it asks for the
 * same state again, which starts the motion again and sets its time back to 0.
 *
 * The jump's take-off (state 0x11) has a least time of about one 60 Hz frame. At 30 and 60 frames/s the first
 * frame's dt reaches it, the jump moves on to the air (state 0x10) with its full height (1.4). At 120 one dt
 * (1/120 s) falls short, the take-off restarts every frame and its time never grows: the player stays in the
 * take-off, whose height is 0.8, and a running jump is a small hop (measured 2026-11-14 with YW4_REPLAY_HZ: peak
 * +0.63 at 120 against +1.38 at 60).
 *
 * The game was made for 30 frames/s, where a motion's first frame always counts 1/30 s. So here a motion's time
 * counts at least 1/30 s for this check: after the game's own update, a motion that hasn't reached its least time
 * but whose least time is 1/30 s or less may be left, as it could after one frame on the Switch. Longer least
 * times are counted as before, and at 30 frames/s (dt >= 1/30) nothing changes. YW4_MOTION_TIME_FIX=0 turns it
 * off (to compare). */
static _Thread_local int motion_in_original;

int yw4_hook_motion_time(CPUState *ctx) {
    static int on = -1;
    if (on < 0) on = !(getenv("YW4_MOTION_TIME_FIX") && !strcmp(getenv("YW4_MOTION_TIME_FIX"), "0"));
    if (!on || motion_in_original) return 0;
    static GuestFn original;
    if (!original) original = yw4_lookup(*yw4_modules[YW4_MAIN].base + 0x1c6170);
    if (!original) return 0;
    const float least_frame = 1.0f / 30.0f;
    uint64_t action = ctx->x[0];
    float dt = ctx->v[0].f[0];
    motion_in_original = 1;
    original(ctx);
    motion_in_original = 0;
    if (!(dt < least_frame)) return 1;
    uint8_t *may_leave = (uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)(action + 0xb1e);
    uint64_t motion = *(const uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)(action + 0xae8);
    if (*may_leave || !motion || !(*(const uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)(motion + 0xc1) & 1)) return 1;
    float in_motion = *(const float *)(uintptr_t)(action + 0xafc);
    float least = *(const float *)(uintptr_t)(motion + 0xb8);
    if (in_motion < least_frame && least <= least_frame) *may_leave = 1;
    return 1;
}

```

`runtime/src/framerate.h`:

```h
/* The frame rate (framerate.c): the game's own limiter is off, the present holds the rate the panel picks. */
#pragma once

#include <stdint.h>

int framerate_index(void);  /* the panel's option: 0 30, 1 60, 2 120, 3 144, 4 vsync, 5 unlimited */
void framerate_cycle(void);
int framerate_hz(void);     /* frames per second to hold, 0 = no limit, -1 = the display's refresh (vsync) */
float framerate_game_dt(void);  /* the game's time step of its latest frame, seconds */
void framerate_wait(void);  /* at the present, on the presenting thread: until this frame's time is up */
int framerate_pacing(int hz); /* a cap of 30 or 60: 0 the vsync tick, 1 the display's refresh (default at 30; YW4_PACE) */

```

`runtime/src/game_ini.c`:

```c
/* game.ini: how yw4.exe runs on its own, without arguments (decision 0050).
 *
 * The launcher writes it next to yw4.exe; a double-click then starts the game. One `YW4_...=value` per line, as
 * in settings.ini, `#` starts a comment. The game's folders:
 *
 *   YW4_EXEFS=../data/exefs        main.bin and sdk.bin (python -m tools.yw4.ingest)
 *   YW4_ROMFS=../data/romfs        the game's RomFS
 *   YW4_SAVE=save                  save data (optional: main.c's default_save_dir without it)
 *
 * and any other variable of docs/debugging.md (YW4_DLC_DIR, YW4_MODS, YW4_SETTINGS_FILE, YW4_HOME...). A value
 * naming a path (the variable's name ends in _DIR, _FILE, _HOME, or is one of the three above or YW4_MODS) is
 * relative to game.ini's folder, so the install folder can be moved. A variable already in the environment wins
 * over its line, as with settings.ini. With arguments on the command line, game.ini is not read. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include <SDL3/SDL_filesystem.h>

#include "game_ini.h"

static void set_env(const char *name, const char *value) {
#ifdef _WIN32
    _putenv_s(name, value);
#else
    setenv(name, value, 1);
#endif
}

static int ends_with(const char *s, const char *tail) {
    size_t n = strlen(s), m = strlen(tail);
    return n >= m && !strcmp(s + n - m, tail);
}

static int is_path(const char *name) {
    return !strcmp(name, "YW4_EXEFS") || !strcmp(name, "YW4_ROMFS") || !strcmp(name, "YW4_SAVE") ||
           !strcmp(name, "YW4_MODS") || ends_with(name, "_DIR") || ends_with(name, "_FILE") || ends_with(name, "_HOME");
}

static int is_absolute(const char *p) {
    return p[0] == '/' || p[0] == '\\' || (p[0] && p[1] == ':');
}

int game_ini_load(void) {
    const char *base = SDL_GetBasePath();  /* the exe's folder, ending in a separator */
    char path[1100];
    snprintf(path, sizeof path, "%sgame.ini", base ? base : "");
    FILE *f = fopen(path, "r");
    if (!f) return 0;
    char line[1100];
    int n = 0;
    while (fgets(line, sizeof line, f)) {
        line[strcspn(line, "\r\n")] = 0;
        char *eq = strchr(line, '=');
        if (line[0] == '#' || !eq || strncmp(line, "YW4_", 4) != 0) continue;
        *eq = 0;
        const char *value = eq + 1;
        if (getenv(line)) continue;  /* the environment wins */
        char full[2200];
        if (is_path(line) && *value && !is_absolute(value) && strcmp(value, "none") != 0) {
            snprintf(full, sizeof full, "%s%s", base ? base : "", value);
            value = full;
        }
        set_env(line, value);
        n++;
    }
    fclose(f);
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: game.ini: %d setting(s) from %s\n", n, path);
    return 1;
}

```

```h
/* game.ini next to yw4.exe: the game's folders and settings when it is started without arguments (game_ini.c,
 * decision 0050). */
#pragma once

/* Reads game.ini into the environment (a variable already set wins); 1 if there was one. */
int game_ini_load(void);
```

`runtime/src/gamelogo.c`:

```c
/* The game's logo for the in-game overlay's header: the game's own icon, which recomp.build puts into yw4.exe as
 * icon resource 1 when tools.yw4.icon made it from the player's files (decision 0048; game data, never in the
 * repo). Read back from the program's resources at 256 x 256 as RGBA; NULL without one (no icon was built in,
 * or not Windows): the overlay then draws its clock. */
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

#ifdef _WIN32
#define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#include <windows.h>
#endif

const uint8_t *game_logo(int *w, int *h);

const uint8_t *game_logo(int *w, int *h) {
    static uint8_t *px;
    static int tried, lw, lh;
#ifdef _WIN32
    if (!tried) {
        tried = 1;
        HICON ic = (HICON)LoadImageW(GetModuleHandleW(NULL), MAKEINTRESOURCEW(1), IMAGE_ICON, 256, 256, LR_DEFAULTCOLOR);
        ICONINFO ii;
        if (ic && GetIconInfo(ic, &ii)) {
            BITMAP bm;
            if (ii.hbmColor && GetObjectW(ii.hbmColor, sizeof bm, &bm) && bm.bmWidth > 0 && bm.bmHeight > 0) {
                BITMAPINFO bi = {.bmiHeader = {.biSize = sizeof(BITMAPINFOHEADER), .biWidth = bm.bmWidth,
                                               .biHeight = -bm.bmHeight, .biPlanes = 1, .biBitCount = 32,
                                               .biCompression = BI_RGB}};
                uint8_t *p = malloc((size_t)bm.bmWidth * (size_t)bm.bmHeight * 4);
                HDC dc = GetDC(NULL);
                if (p && GetDIBits(dc, ii.hbmColor, 0, (UINT)bm.bmHeight, p, &bi, DIB_RGB_COLORS)) {
                    size_t n = (size_t)bm.bmWidth * (size_t)bm.bmHeight;
                    int any_alpha = 0;
                    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; i++) any_alpha |= p[i * 4 + 3];
                    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; i++) {  /* BGRA -> RGBA; an icon without alpha is opaque */
                        uint8_t t = p[i * 4];
                        p[i * 4] = p[i * 4 + 2], p[i * 4 + 2] = t;
                        if (!any_alpha) p[i * 4 + 3] = 255;
                    }
                    px = p, lw = bm.bmWidth, lh = bm.bmHeight;
                } else {
                    free(p);
                }
                ReleaseDC(NULL, dc);
            }
            if (ii.hbmColor) DeleteObject(ii.hbmColor);
            if (ii.hbmMask) DeleteObject(ii.hbmMask);
        }
        if (ic) DestroyIcon(ic);
    }
#else
    (void)tried;
#endif
    *w = lw, *h = lh;
    return px;
}
```
