```c
    {'4', {0x02, 0x06, 0x0A, 0x12, 0x1F, 0x02, 0x02}}, {'5', {0x1F, 0x10, 0x1E, 0x01, 0x01, 0x11, 0x0E}},
    {'6', {0x06, 0x08, 0x10, 0x1E, 0x11, 0x11, 0x0E}}, {'7', {0x1F, 0x01, 0x02, 0x04, 0x08, 0x08, 0x08}},
    {'8', {0x0E, 0x11, 0x11, 0x0E, 0x11, 0x11, 0x0E}}, {'9', {0x0E, 0x11, 0x11, 0x0F, 0x01, 0x02, 0x0C}},
    {'A', {0x0E, 0x11, 0x11, 0x1F, 0x11, 0x11, 0x11}}, {'B', {0x1E, 0x11, 0x11, 0x1E, 0x11, 0x11, 0x1E}},
    {'C', {0x0E, 0x11, 0x10, 0x10, 0x10, 0x11, 0x0E}}, {'D', {0x1C, 0x12, 0x11, 0x11, 0x11, 0x12, 0x1C}},
    {'E', {0x1F, 0x10, 0x10, 0x1E, 0x10, 0x10, 0x1F}}, {'F', {0x1F, 0x10, 0x10, 0x1E, 0x10, 0x10, 0x10}},
    {'G', {0x0E, 0x11, 0x10, 0x17, 0x11, 0x11, 0x0F}}, {'H', {0x11, 0x11, 0x11, 0x1F, 0x11, 0x11, 0x11}},
    {'I', {0x0E, 0x04, 0x04, 0x04, 0x04, 0x04, 0x0E}}, {'J', {0x07, 0x02, 0x02, 0x02, 0x02, 0x12, 0x0C}},
    {'K', {0x11, 0x12, 0x14, 0x18, 0x14, 0x12, 0x11}}, {'L', {0x10, 0x10, 0x10, 0x10, 0x10, 0x10, 0x1F}},
    {'M', {0x11, 0x1B, 0x15, 0x15, 0x11, 0x11, 0x11}}, {'N', {0x11, 0x11, 0x19, 0x15, 0x13, 0x11, 0x11}},
    {'O', {0x0E, 0x11, 0x11, 0x11, 0x11, 0x11, 0x0E}}, {'P', {0x1E, 0x11, 0x11, 0x1E, 0x10, 0x10, 0x10}},
    {'Q', {0x0E, 0x11, 0x11, 0x11, 0x15, 0x12, 0x0D}}, {'R', {0x1E, 0x11, 0x11, 0x1E, 0x14, 0x12, 0x11}},
    {'S', {0x0F, 0x10, 0x10, 0x0E, 0x01, 0x01, 0x1E}}, {'T', {0x1F, 0x04, 0x04, 0x04, 0x04, 0x04, 0x04}},
    {'U', {0x11, 0x11, 0x11, 0x11, 0x11, 0x11, 0x0E}}, {'V', {0x11, 0x11, 0x11, 0x11, 0x11, 0x0A, 0x04}},
    {'W', {0x11, 0x11, 0x11, 0x15, 0x15, 0x15, 0x0A}}, {'X', {0x11, 0x11, 0x0A, 0x04, 0x0A, 0x11, 0x11}},
    {'Y', {0x11, 0x11, 0x11, 0x0A, 0x04, 0x04, 0x04}}, {'Z', {0x1F, 0x01, 0x02, 0x04, 0x08, 0x10, 0x1F}},
    {'.', {0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x0C, 0x0C}}, {':', {0x00, 0x0C, 0x0C, 0x00, 0x0C, 0x0C, 0x00}},
    {'%', {0x18, 0x19, 0x02, 0x04, 0x08, 0x13, 0x03}}, {'/', {0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x04, 0x08, 0x10, 0x00}},
    {'-', {0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x1F, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00}}, {'(', {0x02, 0x04, 0x08, 0x08, 0x08, 0x04, 0x02}},
    {')', {0x08, 0x04, 0x02, 0x02, 0x02, 0x04, 0x08}}, {'>', {0x08, 0x04, 0x02, 0x01, 0x02, 0x04, 0x08}},
    {'<', {0x02, 0x04, 0x08, 0x10, 0x08, 0x04, 0x02}}, {',', {0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x0C, 0x04, 0x08}},
    {'\'', {0x0C, 0x04, 0x08, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00}}, {'!', {0x04, 0x04, 0x04, 0x04, 0x04, 0x00, 0x04}},
    {'?', {0x0E, 0x11, 0x01, 0x02, 0x04, 0x00, 0x04}},
    /* for key names on the controls page */
    {'[', {0x0E, 0x08, 0x08, 0x08, 0x08, 0x08, 0x0E}}, {']', {0x0E, 0x02, 0x02, 0x02, 0x02, 0x02, 0x0E}},
    {';', {0x00, 0x0C, 0x0C, 0x00, 0x0C, 0x04, 0x08}}, {'=', {0x00, 0x00, 0x1F, 0x00, 0x1F, 0x00, 0x00}},
    {'+', {0x00, 0x04, 0x04, 0x1F, 0x04, 0x04, 0x00}}, {'\\', {0x00, 0x10, 0x08, 0x04, 0x02, 0x01, 0x00}},
    {'`', {0x08, 0x04, 0x02, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00}}, {'*', {0x00, 0x04, 0x15, 0x0E, 0x15, 0x04, 0x00}},
    {'#', {0x0A, 0x0A, 0x1F, 0x0A, 0x1F, 0x0A, 0x0A}},
    /* controller symbols (bindings.c writes them as \x01..\x08): arrows up, down, left, right, then the
     * PlayStation shapes triangle, circle, square, cross */
    {'\x01', {0x00, 0x04, 0x04, 0x0E, 0x0E, 0x1F, 0x00}}, {'\x02', {0x00, 0x1F, 0x0E, 0x0E, 0x04, 0x04, 0x00}},
    {'\x03', {0x01, 0x03, 0x07, 0x0F, 0x07, 0x03, 0x01}}, {'\x04', {0x10, 0x18, 0x1C, 0x1E, 0x1C, 0x18, 0x10}},
    {'\x05', {0x04, 0x04, 0x0A, 0x0A, 0x11, 0x1F, 0x00}}, {'\x06', {0x00, 0x0E, 0x11, 0x11, 0x11, 0x0E, 0x00}},
    {'\x07', {0x00, 0x1F, 0x11, 0x11, 0x11, 0x1F, 0x00}}, {'\x08', {0x00, 0x11, 0x0A, 0x04, 0x0A, 0x11, 0x00}},
};

static const uint8_t *glyph(char c) {
    if (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') c = (char)(c - 'a' + 'A');
    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof glyphs / sizeof glyphs[0]; i++)
        if (glyphs[i].c == c) return glyphs[i].rows;
    return NULL;
}

enum { CELL_W = 6, CELL_H = 9, MARGIN = 4 };

typedef struct {
    uint8_t *rgba;
    int w, h;  /* the image */
    int bw, bh;  /* the box: nothing is drawn outside it */
} Canvas;

static void put(const Canvas *cv, int x, int y, const uint8_t col[3]) {
    if (x < 0 || y < 0 || x >= cv->bw || y >= cv->bh) return;
    uint8_t *p = cv->rgba + ((size_t)y * cv->w + x) * 4;
    p[0] = col[0], p[1] = col[1], p[2] = col[2], p[3] = 255;
}

static void text(const Canvas *cv, int x0, int y0, const char *s, const uint8_t col[3]) {
    for (int k = 0; s[k]; k++, x0 += CELL_W) {
        const uint8_t *g = glyph(s[k]);
        if (!g) continue;
        for (int r = 0; r < 7; r++)
            for (int c = 0; c < 5; c++)
                if (g[r] >> (4 - c) & 1) put(cv, x0 + c, y0 + r, col);
    }
}

/* ---- the settings panel, in the style of the game's own menus: a cream card with a dark outline and
 * rounded corners, a purple title bar, teal group labels, the chosen row on a yellow bar, the current
 * option on a pink chip, and a box explaining the chosen setting. Drawn at a small size; window.c scales
 * it up by whole steps with the window. */

static const uint8_t CREAM[3] = {252, 246, 232}, OUTLINE[3] = {64, 40, 82}, PURPLE[3] = {104, 54, 150},
                     PURPLE2[3] = {136, 78, 186}, TEAL[3] = {22, 146, 158}, ROWSEL[3] = {255, 229, 120},
                     INK[3] = {58, 44, 72}, MUTED[3] = {165, 154, 172}, PINK[3] = {226, 66, 136},
                     ORANGE[3] = {240, 140, 24}, DESC[3] = {226, 244, 240}, WHITE2[3] = {255, 255, 255},
                     LOCKED[3] = {196, 190, 202};  /* a greyed-out row's chosen option */

static void fill(const Canvas *cv, int x, int y, int w, int h, const uint8_t col[3]) {
    for (int j = y; j < y + h; j++)
        for (int i = x; i < x + w; i++) put(cv, i, j, col);
}

/* A box with corners rounded by r and, if `line`, a one-texel outline. */
static void box(const Canvas *cv, int x, int y, int w, int h, int r, const uint8_t col[3], const uint8_t *line) {
    for (int j = 0; j < h; j++)
        for (int i = 0; i < w; i++) {
            int dx = i < r ? r - i : i >= w - r ? i - (w - 1 - r) : 0;
            int dy = j < r ? r - j : j >= h - r ? j - (h - 1 - r) : 0;
            int d2 = dx * dx + dy * dy, r2 = r * r;
            if (d2 > r2 + r) continue;  /* outside the rounded corner */
            int edge = i == 0 || j == 0 || i == w - 1 || j == h - 1 || d2 > r2 - r;
            put(cv, x + i, y + j, line && edge ? line : col);
        }
}

/* Text twice the size (the title). */
static void text2(const Canvas *cv, int x0, int y0, const char *s, const uint8_t col[3]) {
    for (int k = 0; s[k]; k++, x0 += 2 * CELL_W) {
        const uint8_t *g = glyph(s[k]);
        if (!g) continue;
        for (int r = 0; r < 7; r++)
            for (int c = 0; c < 5; c++)
                if (g[r] >> (4 - c) & 1) fill(cv, x0 + 2 * c, y0 + 2 * r, 2, 2, col);
    }
}

/* s broken into lines of at most `cols` characters at spaces; returns the count (at most max). */
static int wrap(const char *s, int cols, char lines[][96], int max) {
    int n = 0;
    while (*s && n < max) {
        while (*s == ' ') s++;
        int len = (int)strlen(s), cut = len;
        if (len > cols) {
            cut = cols;
            while (cut > 0 && s[cut] != ' ') cut--;
            if (!cut) cut = cols;
        }
        if (cut > 95) cut = 95;
        memcpy(lines[n], s, (size_t)cut), lines[n][cut] = 0;
        n++, s += cut;
    }
    return n;
}

/* The card both pages are drawn on: a square card in a dark frame (the window copies overlays without
 * blending, so nothing can be see-through, and rounded corners inside a square frame looked off), its
 * title bar square too, with the page's name. */
enum { CARD_PAD = 10, CARD_HEADER = 26 };

static void card(const Canvas *cv, int pw, int ph, int page) {
    fill(cv, 0, 0, pw, ph, OUTLINE);
    fill(cv, 2, 2, pw - 4, ph - 4, CREAM);
    fill(cv, 2, 2, pw - 4, CARD_HEADER - 2, PURPLE);
    for (int x = 2; x < pw - 2; x += 4) put(cv, x, CARD_HEADER - 1, PURPLE2);
    /* page: 0 the settings, 1 the controls, 2 the settings' developer page */
    static const char *const titles[] = {"SETTINGS", "CONTROLS", "DEVELOPER"},
                             *const keys[] = {"F1 / B: CLOSE", "F2 / B: CLOSE", "ESC / B: BACK"};
    text2(cv, CARD_PAD + 2, 6, titles[page], WHITE2);
    text(cv, pw - CARD_PAD - (int)strlen(keys[page]) * CELL_W, 10, keys[page], ROWSEL);
}

static void hint(const Canvas *cv, int pw, int y, const char *s) {
    text(cv, (pw - (int)strlen(s) * CELL_W) / 2, y + 2, s, MUTED);
}

void panel_render(uint8_t *rgba, int w, int h, const SettingRow *rows, int n, int selected, int developer,
                  int *used_w, int *used_h) {
    enum { PAD = 10, ROW_H = 13, NAME_COLS = 21, GAP = 3, HEADER = 26, DESC_LINES = 5, SLIDER_COLS = 22 };
    /* the width: the widest row (name and all its options) */
    int cols = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        int c = 2 + NAME_COLS + 2;
        for (int k = 0; k < rows[i].noptions; k++) c += (int)strlen(rows[i].options[k]) + GAP;
        if (rows[i].slider) c += SLIDER_COLS + 8;
        if (c > cols) cols = c;
    }
    int pw = 2 * PAD + cols * CELL_W, text_cols = (pw - 2 * PAD - 12) / CELL_W;
    /* the height: title, rows with their group labels, the description box sized for the longest text (so the
     * card doesn't change size while moving), the key hints */
    int groups = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) groups += !i || strcmp(rows[i].category, rows[i - 1].category);
    int help_lines = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        char l[DESC_LINES][96];
        int k = wrap(rows[i].help, text_cols, l, DESC_LINES);
        if (k > help_lines) help_lines = k;
    }
    int desc_h = (help_lines + 2) * 10 + 10;
    int ph = HEADER + 8 + (n + groups) * ROW_H + 6 + desc_h + 6 + 14;
    /* the developer page (opened from the settings page) keeps the settings page's size: it doesn't jump and its
     * texts fit */
    static int settings_w, settings_h;
    if (!developer) settings_w = pw, settings_h = ph;
    if (pw < settings_w) pw = settings_w, text_cols = (pw - 2 * PAD - 12) / CELL_W;
    if (ph < settings_h) ph = settings_h;
    Canvas cv = {rgba, w, h, pw < w ? pw : w, ph < h ? ph : h};
    card(&cv, pw, ph, developer ? 2 : 0);
    /* rows */
    int y = HEADER + 8;
    int optx = PAD + (2 + NAME_COLS) * CELL_W;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        if (!i || strcmp(rows[i].category, rows[i - 1].category)) {
            text(&cv, PAD, y + 2, rows[i].category, TEAL);
            int lx = PAD + ((int)strlen(rows[i].category) + 1) * CELL_W;
            fill(&cv, lx, y + 5, pw - PAD - lx, 1, TEAL);
            y += ROW_H;
        }
        int sel = i == selected;
        if (sel) box(&cv, PAD - 4, y - 1, pw - 2 * PAD + 8, ROW_H, 4, ROWSEL, NULL);
        int off = rows[i].disabled != NULL;  /* greyed out: can't be changed now */
        text(&cv, PAD + 2 * CELL_W, y + 2, rows[i].name, off ? MUTED : INK);
        if (rows[i].link) {  /* opens a page: "OPEN >" on a chip when chosen */
            if (sel) {
                text(&cv, PAD + 2, y + 2, ">", PINK);
                box(&cv, optx - 3, y, 6 * CELL_W + 5, ROW_H - 2, 3, ORANGE, NULL);
                text(&cv, optx, y + 2, "OPEN >", WHITE2);
            } else {
                text(&cv, optx, y + 2, "OPEN >", MUTED);
            }
            y += ROW_H;
            continue;
        }
        if (sel && !off) text(&cv, PAD + 2, y + 2, ">", PINK), text(&cv, optx - 2 * CELL_W, y + 2, "<", PINK);
        if (rows[i].slider) {  /* a track with a knob at the value, then the value on a chip */
            int tw = SLIDER_COLS * CELL_W, ty = y + ROW_H / 2 - 1;
            float f = rows[i].frac < 0 ? 0 : rows[i].frac > 1 ? 1 : rows[i].frac;
            fill(&cv, optx, ty, tw, 2, MUTED);
            fill(&cv, optx, ty, (int)(tw * f), 2, off ? LOCKED : sel ? ORANGE : PINK);
            box(&cv, optx + (int)(tw * f) - 2, y + 1, 5, ROW_H - 4, 2, off ? LOCKED : sel ? ORANGE : PINK, NULL);
            int vx = optx + tw + 3 * CELL_W, len = (int)strlen(rows[i].value);
            box(&cv, vx - 3, y, len * CELL_W + 5, ROW_H - 2, 3, off ? LOCKED : sel ? ORANGE : PINK, NULL);
            text(&cv, vx, y + 2, rows[i].value, WHITE2);
            if (sel && !off) text(&cv, vx + (len + 1) * CELL_W, y + 2, ">", PINK);
            y += ROW_H;
            continue;
        }
        int x = optx;
        for (int k = 0; k < rows[i].noptions; k++) {
            int len = (int)strlen(rows[i].options[k]);
            if (k == rows[i].current) {
                box(&cv, x - 3, y, len * CELL_W + 5, ROW_H - 2, 3, off ? LOCKED : sel ? ORANGE : PINK, NULL);
                text(&cv, x, y + 2, rows[i].options[k], WHITE2);
            } else {
                text(&cv, x, y + 2, rows[i].options[k], sel && !off ? INK : MUTED);
            }
            x += (len + GAP) * CELL_W;
        }
        if (sel && !off) text(&cv, x - (GAP - 1) * CELL_W, y + 2, ">", PINK);
        y += ROW_H;
    }
    /* the chosen setting explained: its name, what it does, what the current option means; at the bottom */
    y = ph - desc_h - 26;
    y += 6;
    const SettingRow *r = selected >= 0 && selected < n ? &rows[selected] : NULL;
    box(&cv, PAD - 4, y, pw - 2 * PAD + 8, desc_h, 5, DESC, TEAL);
    if (r) {
        int ty = y + 6;
        text(&cv, PAD + 2, ty, r->name, TEAL);
        ty += 10;
        char l[DESC_LINES][96];
        int k = wrap(r->help, text_cols, l, DESC_LINES);
        for (int j = 0; j < k; j++, ty += 10) text(&cv, PAD + 2, ty, l[j], INK);
        char note[128];
        if (r->link) snprintf(note, sizeof note, "ENTER OR A: OPEN. ESCAPE OR B THERE: BACK");
        else if (r->disabled) snprintf(note, sizeof note, "OFF FOR NOW: %s", r->disabled);
        else snprintf(note, sizeof note, "%s: %s", r->options[r->current], r->notes[r->current] ? r->notes[r->current] : "");
        text(&cv, PAD + 2, y + desc_h - 14, note, r->disabled ? MUTED : PINK);
    }
    y += desc_h + 6;
    hint(&cv, pw, y, developer ? "UP/DOWN: CHOOSE   LEFT/RIGHT: CHANGE   ESC/B: BACK"
                               : "UP/DOWN: CHOOSE   LEFT/RIGHT: CHANGE   F2, L/R: CONTROLS");
    *used_w = cv.bw, *used_h = cv.bh;
}

static int same_group(const BindRow *a, const BindRow *b) {
    return a->group && b->group ? !strcmp(a->group, b->group) : a->group == b->group;
}

/* The controls page: a row per Switch input in groups, its two keys and gamepad input in columns, the
 * chosen cell on a chip (pink, orange when its key also presses another input), and the explanation box. */
void controls_render(uint8_t *rgba, int w, int h, const BindRow *rows, int n, int row, int col, int capturing,
                     const char *help, int *used_w, int *used_h) {
    enum { PAD = CARD_PAD, ROW_H = 13, NAME_COLS = 19, CELL_COLS = 16, DESC_LINES = 4, SHOWN = 13, LINES = 64 };
    int pw = 2 * PAD + (2 + NAME_COLS + BIND_COLS * CELL_COLS) * CELL_W, text_cols = (pw - 2 * PAD - 12) / CELL_W;
    /* the lines: a group's label, then its rows; SHOWN of them at a time (so the card is as tall as the
     * settings page and scales up the same), scrolled to keep the chosen row in view with a line around it */
    int line_row[LINES], nlines = 0, sel_line = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n && nlines + 2 <= LINES; i++) {
        if (!i || !same_group(&rows[i], &rows[i - 1])) line_row[nlines++] = -1 - i;  /* label of i's group */
        if (i == row) sel_line = nlines;
        line_row[nlines++] = i;
    }
    static int first;
    if (sel_line - 1 < first) first = sel_line - 1;
    if (sel_line + 2 > first + SHOWN) first = sel_line + 2 - SHOWN;
    if (first > nlines - SHOWN) first = nlines - SHOWN;
    if (first < 0) first = 0;
    int desc_h = DESC_LINES * 10 + 12;
    int ph = CARD_HEADER + 8 + ROW_H + SHOWN * ROW_H + 6 + desc_h + 6 + 14;
    Canvas cv = {rgba, w, h, pw < w ? pw : w, ph < h ? ph : h};
    card(&cv, pw, ph, 1);
    int y = CARD_HEADER + 8, cellx = PAD + (2 + NAME_COLS) * CELL_W;
    static const char *const heads[BIND_COLS] = {"KEY", "OTHER KEY", "GAMEPAD"};
    for (int c = 0; c < BIND_COLS; c++) text(&cv, cellx + c * CELL_COLS * CELL_W, y + 2, heads[c], TEAL);
    /* more above / below: small teal triangles at the right edge */
    for (int k = 0; k < 4; k++) {
        if (first > 0) fill(&cv, pw - PAD - 4 - k, y + 2 + k, 2 * k + 1, 1, TEAL);
        if (first + SHOWN < nlines) fill(&cv, pw - PAD - 4 - k, y + ROW_H * (SHOWN + 1) + 3 - k, 2 * k + 1, 1, TEAL);
    }
    y += ROW_H;
    for (int li = first; li < nlines && li < first + SHOWN; li++, y += ROW_H) {
        if (line_row[li] < 0) {  /* the group's label and line (none above the reset row) */
            const BindRow *r = &rows[-1 - line_row[li]];
            const char *g = r->group ? r->group : "";
            text(&cv, PAD, y + 3, g, TEAL);
            int lx = PAD + ((int)strlen(g) + (*g ? 1 : 0)) * CELL_W;
            fill(&cv, lx, y + 6, pw - PAD - lx, 1, TEAL);
            continue;
        }
        int i = line_row[li], sel = i == row;
        if (sel) box(&cv, PAD - 4, y - 1, pw - 2 * PAD + 8, ROW_H, 4, ROWSEL, NULL);
        if (sel) text(&cv, PAD + 2, y + 2, ">", PINK);
        text(&cv, PAD + 2 * CELL_W, y + 2, rows[i].name, INK);
        if (!rows[i].group) continue;
        if (rows[i].value) {  /* a setting: its value between arrows, on a chip when chosen */
            char s[CELL_COLS + 8];
            snprintf(s, sizeof s, "< %s >", rows[i].cells[0]);
            if (sel) {
                box(&cv, cellx - 3, y, (int)strlen(s) * CELL_W + 5, ROW_H - 2, 3, PINK, NULL);
                text(&cv, cellx, y + 2, s, WHITE2);
            } else {
                text(&cv, cellx, y + 2, s, INK);
            }
            continue;
        }
        for (int c = 0; c < BIND_COLS; c++) {
            char s[CELL_COLS];
            snprintf(s, sizeof s, "%s", sel && c == col && capturing ? (c < BIND_KEYS ? "PRESS A KEY" : "PRESS INPUT")
                                                                     : rows[i].cells[c]);
            int x = cellx + c * CELL_COLS * CELL_W;
            if (sel && c == col) {
                box(&cv, x - 3, y, (int)strlen(s) * CELL_W + 5, ROW_H - 2, 3,
                    rows[i].conflict[c] && !capturing ? ORANGE : PINK, NULL);
                text(&cv, x, y + 2, s, WHITE2);
            } else {
                text(&cv, x, y + 2, s, rows[i].conflict[c] ? ORANGE : !strcmp(s, "-") ? MUTED : INK);
            }
        }
    }
    y = CARD_HEADER + 8 + ROW_H + SHOWN * ROW_H;
    y += 6;
    box(&cv, PAD - 4, y, pw - 2 * PAD + 8, desc_h, 5, DESC, TEAL);
    char l[DESC_LINES][96];
    int k = wrap(help, text_cols, l, DESC_LINES);
    for (int j = 0; j < k; j++) text(&cv, PAD + 2, y + 6 + j * 10, l[j], capturing ? PINK : INK);
    y += desc_h + 6;
    hint(&cv, pw, y, "ARROWS: MOVE  ENTER/A: CHANGE  DEL/X: CLEAR  F1, L/R: SETTINGS");
    *used_w = cv.bw, *used_h = cv.bh;
}
```

`runtime/src/hud.h`:

```h
/* The performance HUD (F3 or YW4_HUD=1): a few lines of numbers and a frame-time graph drawn on
 * the CPU with a built-in 5x7 font into a small RGBA image, which window.c copies onto the window's
 * top-left corner after the game's frame. Not in F12 screenshots (they read the game's frame). */
#ifndef YW4_HUD_H
#define YW4_HUD_H

#include <stdint.h>

#include "bindings.h"
#include "settings.h"

enum { HUD_COLS = 40, HUD_LINES = 8, HUD_POINTS = 180 };

typedef struct {
    char lines[HUD_LINES][HUD_COLS];
    int nlines;
    float frame_ms[HUD_POINTS], work_ms[HUD_POINTS];  /* the graph, oldest first */
    int npoints;
    float target_ms;  /* drawn as a line: the game's frame pacing */
    /* the same numbers as values, for the styled HUD (hud_style.c); valid 0: no frames yet (lines[0] says why) */
    int valid;
    float target_fps;  /* the FRAME RATE setting; 0: none (vsync, unlimited) */
    float fps, low1, low01;              /* the last 30 frames' rate; the 1% and 0.1% lows of the last 600 */
    float frame_avg_ms, min_ms, max_ms;  /* frame time: average, lowest, highest of the last 600 */
    float work_avg_ms, gpu_ms;           /* the game's work and the GPU's busy time per frame; gpu_ms < 0: not yet */
    float cpu_pct, cpu_cores;            /* the whole CPU's share, and in cores */
    int ncpu;
    float draws, ram_mb;
    float shown_fps;                     /* frames on screen with frame generation; 0: off */
    const char *fg;                      /* "DLSS" or "FSR" */
} HudContent;

/* The HUD's parts in its detailed form: FPS and 1% low, the frame-time graph, GPU and CPU time, frame
 * generation. */
enum { HUD_PART_FPS = 1, HUD_PART_GRAPH = 2, HUD_PART_TIMES = 4, HUD_PART_FG = 8, HUD_PART_ALL = 15 };
/* perf.c: the HUD's lines and graph: compact (one line), or the detailed one's chosen parts. */
void yw4_perf_hud(HudContent *c, int compact, unsigned parts);

/* hud_style.c: the HUD as a see-through card (premultiplied RGBA, w x h) at s pixels per unit: compact (a chip) or
 * the detailed card with the chosen parts (HUD_PART_*). *used_w x *used_h: in, the part the last drawing in this
 * image touched, cleared first (0: the whole image); out, the part drawn. */
void hud_style_render(uint8_t *rgba, int w, int h, const HudContent *c, int compact, unsigned parts, float s,
                      int *used_w, int *used_h);

/* shadow.c: whose shadow casters are drawn ("ORIGINAL": the game's, "CUSTOM": our pass, "CHECK"). */
const char *shadow_mode_name(void);
/* gpu.c: the shadow maps' size (1024 is the game's). */
int gpu_shadow_res(void);
/* gpu.c: the 3D view's height (900 is the game's). */
int gpu_res_height(void);
/* gpu.c: texture filtering, 0 the game's, else anisotropic up to this. */
int gpu_aniso(void);
/* gpu_draw.c: PCSS (soft contact shadows), 0 off, 1..3 = x1, x2, x4. */
int gpu_pcss_level(void);
/* gbuffer.c: our G-buffer programs on. */
int gbuffer_native(void);

/* window.c: the HUD's scale, the settings panel's HUD SCALE slider: 0 auto (grows with the window), else the scale. */
float hud_scale_get(void);
void hud_scale_set(float v);
/* hud_style.c: the HUD's background, the HUD OPACITY slider: 0 (only the numbers) to 1. */
float hud_opacity_get(void);
void hud_opacity_set(float v);

/* The settings panel (settings.h) the same way: every row with all its options, the current one boxed. */
void panel_render(uint8_t *rgba, int w, int h, const SettingRow *rows, int n, int selected, int developer,
                  int *used_w, int *used_h);
/* The panel's controls page (bindings.h) the same way: the chosen row and column, whether it waits for an
 * input, and the text for the explanation box. */
void controls_render(uint8_t *rgba, int w, int h, const BindRow *rows, int n, int row, int col, int capturing,
                     const char *help, int *used_w, int *used_h);

#endif
```

`runtime/src/hud_style.c`:

```c
/* The performance HUD's look (2026-11-05/06, owner's design canvas, layout C): a rounded, see-through violet card
 * like the in-game overlay's. A big frame rate on top, then the 1% and 0.1% lows, the frame-time graph as a line under
 * a dashed target, and a grid of the times and resources. With frame generation on, the big number is the frames on
 * screen with DLSS or FSR beside it in large letters, and the game's own FPS goes small on the right; the big number's
 * colour still follows the game's own FPS, because generated frames can look fine while the game runs slow.
 * Labels are lilac in the overlay's font; digits in its rounded font (M PLUS Rounded: its digits differ by under 2%).
 * Numbers are coloured by how they are doing (green on target, amber slow, red well off). Drawn on the CPU with ui.c
 * into a see-through (premultiplied) image, which window.c blends onto the picture. The parts and the compact form
 * are the Overlay page's choices. */
#include <math.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "hud.h"
#include "theme.h"
#include "ui.h"

/* the card's colours follow the theme (theme.h); the numbers' traffic-light colours stay the same in every theme */
enum { GOOD = 0x7fe0a0, WARN = 0xf0c060, BAD = 0xff8a8a };
#define TEXT (theme_colors()->hud_text)
#define LABEL (theme_colors()->hud_label)
#define CARD (theme_colors()->hud_card)
#define PLOT (theme_colors()->hud_plot)
#define TARGET (theme_colors()->hud_target)

/* the fonts: numbers, and the small words between them */
enum { NUM = UI_ROUNDED_700, WORD = UI_GOTHIC_700 };
#define WORD_PX 10.5f

enum { PAD_X = 12, PAD_Y = 9, GAP = 7, MAX_PIECES = 4, MAX_TILES = 6 };
/* the card's sizes, in the design's units */
enum { MIN_INNER = 206, HERO_H = 36, LOWS_H = 18, LOW2_X = 84, GRAPH_H = 34, WORD_LH = 14, NUM_LH = 17, TILE_GAP = 6 };

/* a piece of a line of text; more: extra space before it */
typedef struct {
    const char *text;
    int font;
    float px;
    uint32_t rgb;
    float more;
} Piece;

/* The card's background (the HUD OPACITY slider, YW4_HUD_OPACITY=0..1). The default is a slider step close to the
 * designed 0.72. The border and the graph's plate fade with it below that, so at 0 only the numbers are left. */
#define OPACITY_DEFAULT 0.70f
static float hud_opacity = -1.0f;

float hud_opacity_get(void) {
    float v;
    __atomic_load(&hud_opacity, &v, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);  /* the generic form: _n takes no float before Clang 19 */
    if (v < 0) {
        const char *e = getenv("YW4_HUD_OPACITY");
        v = e && *e ? (float)atof(e) : OPACITY_DEFAULT;
        v = v < 0 ? 0 : v > 1 ? 1 : v;
        __atomic_store(&hud_opacity, &v, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    }
    return v;
}

void hud_opacity_set(float v) { __atomic_store(&hud_opacity, &v, __ATOMIC_RELEASE); }

/* the card: its fill at the slider's opacity, its border fading with it */
static void card(const UiCanvas *c, float w, float h, float r) {
    float op = hud_opacity_get(), fade = op < OPACITY_DEFAULT ? op / OPACITY_DEFAULT : 1;
    ui_card(c, 0.5f, 0.5f, w, h, r, CARD, op, 1, 0xffffff, 0.14f * fade);
}

/* the colour of a rate against the target: green at it, amber a little under, red well under; none: white */
static uint32_t rate_rgb(float v, float target) {
    if (target <= 0) return TEXT;
    return v >= target * 0.97f ? GOOD : v >= target * 0.85f ? WARN : BAD;
}

/* the colour of a time per frame against the frame's budget */
static uint32_t time_rgb(float ms, float budget) {
    return ms <= budget * 0.8f ? GOOD : ms <= budget ? WARN : BAD;
}

/* The width of a text, every digit counted as a 0: the digits differ by a little, which would make the pieces after a
 * number, and a card as wide as its text, tremble as the number changes. */
static float stable_w(int font, float px, const char *text) {
    char t[32];
    size_t i = 0;
    for (; text[i] && i + 1 < sizeof t; i++) t[i] = text[i] >= '0' && text[i] <= '9' ? '0' : text[i];
    t[i] = 0;
    return ui_text_w(font, px, t);
}

static float line_w(const Piece *p, int n) {
    float w = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) w += stable_w(p[i].font, p[i].px, p[i].text) + (i ? GAP + p[i].more : 0);
    return w;
}

/* pieces side by side at (x, y) on one baseline, in a line box lh high */
static void line(const UiCanvas *c, float x, float y, float lh, const Piece *p, int n) {
    float base = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        float b = ui_baseline(p[i].font, p[i].px, lh);
        if (b > base) base = b;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        if (i) x += GAP + p[i].more;
        ui_text(c, p[i].font, p[i].px, x, y + base - ui_baseline(p[i].font, p[i].px, lh), lh, p[i].text, p[i].rgb);
        x += stable_w(p[i].font, p[i].px, p[i].text);
    }
}

/* the frame times, oldest left; the target dashed; up to twice the budget */
static void graph_draw(const UiCanvas *cv, const HudContent *c, float x, float y, float w, float budget) {
    float h = GRAPH_H, top = budget * 2.0f;
    for (int i = 0; i < c->npoints; i++)
        if (c->frame_ms[i] > top) top = c->frame_ms[i];
    float op = hud_opacity_get();
    ui_card(cv, x, y, w, h, 6, PLOT, 0.6f * (op < OPACITY_DEFAULT ? op / OPACITY_DEFAULT : 1), 0, 0, 0);
    float ty = y + h - 3 - (budget / top) * (h - 6);
    for (float dx = 0; dx < w; dx += 8) ui_rect(cv, x + dx, ty, 4, 1, TARGET, 0.9f);
    float step = w / (float)(c->npoints - 1);
    for (int i = 1; i < c->npoints; i++) {  /* a 2-unit line: each step's vertical span, as a thin column */
        float y0 = y + h - 3 - (c->frame_ms[i - 1] / top) * (h - 6);
        float y1 = y + h - 3 - (c->frame_ms[i] / top) * (h - 6);
        float lo = y0 < y1 ? y0 : y1, hi = y0 < y1 ? y1 : y0;
        ui_rect(cv, x + (float)(i - 1) * step, lo - 1, step + 0.5f, hi - lo + 2,
                c->frame_ms[i] > budget * 1.25f ? WARN : GOOD, 1);
    }
}

void hud_style_render(uint8_t *rgba, int w, int h, const HudContent *c, int compact, unsigned parts, float s,
                      int *used_w, int *used_h) {
    /* only what the last drawing touched (the rest is still clear); none known: everything */
    if (*used_w > 0 && *used_h > 0) {
        for (int j = 0; j < *used_h && j < h; j++) memset(rgba + (size_t)j * (size_t)w * 4, 0, (size_t)*used_w * 4);
    } else {
        memset(rgba, 0, (size_t)w * (size_t)h * 4);
    }
    UiCanvas cv = {rgba, w, h, s, 0, 0};
    char b[12][32];
    int k = 0;
#define B(...) (snprintf(b[k], sizeof b[k], __VA_ARGS__), b[k++])
    float budget = c->target_ms > 0 ? c->target_ms : 33.3f;

    if (!c->valid) {  /* no frames yet, or the log is off: its one line */
        float tw = ui_text_w(WORD, 12, c->nlines ? c->lines[0] : ""), cw = tw + 2 * PAD_X, ch = 30;
        card(&cv, cw, ch, 10);
        ui_text_in(&cv, WORD, 12, PAD_X, 0.5f, 0, ch, 0, c->nlines ? c->lines[0] : "", LABEL);
        *used_w = (int)ceilf((cw + 1) * s), *used_h = (int)ceilf((ch + 1) * s);
        return;
    }

    uint32_t rate = rate_rgb(c->fps, c->target_fps);  /* the game's own, with frame generation too */

    if (compact) {  /* a chip: the frame rate; frame generation: the frames on screen, its name, then the game's */
        Piece p[MAX_PIECES];
        int n = 0;
        if (c->shown_fps > 0) {
            p[n++] = (Piece){B("%.0f", c->shown_fps), NUM, 18, rate, 0};
            p[n++] = (Piece){c->fg, NUM, 13, TEXT, 0};
            p[n++] = (Piece){B("%.0f", c->fps), NUM, 12, TEXT, 5};
        } else {
            p[n++] = (Piece){B("%.0f", c->fps), NUM, 18, rate, 0};
        }
        p[n++] = (Piece){"FPS", WORD, 11, LABEL, 0};
        float cw = line_w(p, n) + 2 * PAD_X, ch = 30;
        card(&cv, cw, ch, 10);
        line(&cv, PAD_X + 0.5f, 0.5f, ch, p, n);
        *used_w = (int)ceilf((cw + 1) * s), *used_h = (int)ceilf((ch + 1) * s);
        return;
    }

    /* the detailed card, by the Overlay page's parts: measured first for the card's size */
    int fps_on = parts & HUD_PART_FPS, times_on = parts & HUD_PART_TIMES;
    int shown_on = (parts & HUD_PART_FG) && c->shown_fps > 0;
    int graph_on = (parts & HUD_PART_GRAPH) && c->npoints > 1;

    Piece hero[2];
    const char *small = NULL;  /* the game's own frame rate on the right, when the big number is the frames on screen */
    int hero_on = fps_on || shown_on;
    if (shown_on) {
        hero[0] = (Piece){B("%.0f", c->shown_fps), NUM, 30, rate, 0};
        hero[1] = (Piece){c->fg, NUM, 20, TEXT, 0};
        if (fps_on) small = B("%.1f", c->fps);
    } else {
        hero[0] = (Piece){B("%.1f", c->fps), NUM, 30, rate, 0};
        hero[1] = (Piece){"FPS", NUM, 20, TEXT, 0};
    }
    Piece low1[2] = {{"1% low", WORD, WORD_PX, LABEL, 0}, {B("%.1f", c->low1), NUM, 12, TEXT, 0}};
    Piece low01[2] = {{"0.1% low", WORD, WORD_PX, LABEL, 0}, {B("%.1f", c->low01), NUM, 12, TEXT, 0}};

    struct {
        const char *label, *value;
        uint32_t rgb;
    } tiles[MAX_TILES];
    int nt = 0;
#define TILE(l, v, col) (tiles[nt].label = (l), tiles[nt].value = (v), tiles[nt].rgb = (col), nt++)
    if (fps_on) {
        TILE("Frame", B("%.1f ms", c->frame_avg_ms), TEXT);
        TILE("Max", B("%.1f ms", c->max_ms), c->max_ms > budget * 1.25f ? WARN : TEXT);
    }
    if (times_on) {
        if (c->gpu_ms >= 0) TILE("GPU", B("%.1f ms", c->gpu_ms), time_rgb(c->gpu_ms, budget));
        else TILE("GPU", "- ms", TEXT);
        TILE("Game", B("%.1f ms", c->work_avg_ms), time_rgb(c->work_avg_ms, budget));
        TILE("CPU", B("%.0f%%", c->cpu_pct), TEXT);
        TILE("RAM", B("%.1f GB", c->ram_mb / 1024.0f), TEXT);
    }
#undef TILE

    float inner = MIN_INNER;
    if (hero_on) {
        float hw = line_w(hero, 2) + (small ? GAP + stable_w(NUM, 12, small) : 0);
        if (hw > inner) inner = hw;
    }
    if (fps_on && LOW2_X + line_w(low01, 2) > inner) inner = LOW2_X + line_w(low01, 2);
    int tile_rows = (nt + 2) / 3;
    float tile_h = WORD_LH + NUM_LH, ch = 2 * PAD_Y;
    if (hero_on) ch += HERO_H;
    if (fps_on) ch += LOWS_H;
    int above = hero_on || fps_on;  /* something above the graph, and below it */
    if (graph_on) ch += GRAPH_H + (above ? 5 : 0) + (nt ? 7 : 0);
    else if (above && nt) ch += TILE_GAP;
    if (nt) ch += (float)tile_rows * tile_h + (float)(tile_rows - 1) * TILE_GAP;
    float cw = inner + 2 * PAD_X;

    card(&cv, cw, ch, 12);
    float x = PAD_X + 0.5f, y = PAD_Y + 0.5f;
    if (hero_on) {
        line(&cv, x, y, HERO_H, hero, 2);
        if (small) {  /* value over word, ending at the card's right, in the middle of the big line */
            float right = x + inner, top = y + (HERO_H - NUM_LH - WORD_LH) * 0.5f;
            ui_text(&cv, NUM, 12, right - stable_w(NUM, 12, small), top, NUM_LH, small, TEXT);
            ui_text_in(&cv, WORD, WORD_PX, right - inner, top + NUM_LH, inner, WORD_LH, 2, "FPS", LABEL);
        }
        y += HERO_H;
    }
    if (fps_on) {
        line(&cv, x, y, LOWS_H, low1, 2);
        line(&cv, x + LOW2_X, y, LOWS_H, low01, 2);
        y += LOWS_H;
    }
    if (graph_on) {
        if (above) y += 5;
        graph_draw(&cv, c, x, y, inner, budget);
        y += GRAPH_H + (nt ? 7 : 0);
    } else if (above && nt) {
        y += TILE_GAP;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < nt; i++) {  /* three to a row: the label over the value */
        float tx = x + (float)(i % 3) * (inner / 3), ty = y + (float)(i / 3) * (tile_h + TILE_GAP);
        ui_text(&cv, WORD, WORD_PX, tx, ty, WORD_LH, tiles[i].label, LABEL);
        ui_text(&cv, NUM, 12, tx, ty + WORD_LH, NUM_LH, tiles[i].value, tiles[i].rgb);
    }
#undef B
    *used_w = (int)ceilf((cw + 1) * s), *used_h = (int)ceilf((ch + 1) * s);
    if (*used_w > w) *used_w = w;
    if (*used_h > h) *used_h = h;
}

```

`runtime/src/ipc.c`:

```c
/* IPC message codec, sessions, domains and the service registry (decision 0014).
 *
 * Message layout (Switchbrew "IPC_Marshalling"), 32-bit words at the start of the TLR:
 *   word 0  type (bits 0-15), number of X / A / B / W descriptors (16-19, 20-23, 24-27, 28-31)
 *   word 1  raw data size in words (0-9), C descriptor mode (10-13), handle descriptor (31)
 *   [handle descriptor: send PID (0), copy count (1-4), move count (5-8); PID; handles]
 *   X descriptors (2 words), A, B, W descriptors (3 words each)
 *   raw data, starting 16-byte aligned: [domain header], "SFCI", version, command, token, args
 *   C descriptors after the raw data
 * The reply replaces the request: type 0, optional handles, then "SFCO", 0, result, 0, output.
 * LAS Recomp's runtime/ipc.c (MIT) was the cross-check for this layout.
 */
#include <inttypes.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "hle.h"
#include "ipc.h"
#include "host.h"

#define R_OK 0u
#define R_NOT_FOUND 0xF201u
#define R_INVALID_HANDLE 0xE401u

/* ---- registry: every native service, by the name sm:GetServiceHandle uses */

static const struct {
    const char *name;
    ServiceHandler handler;
} registry[] = {
    {"sm:", svc_sm},
    {"appletOE", svc_appletOE},
    {"apm", svc_apm},
    {"lm", svc_lm},
    {"aoc:u", svc_aoc_u},
    {"pctl", svc_pctl},
    {"pctl:s", svc_pctl},  /* the same interface with other access rights */
    {"pctl:a", svc_pctl},
    {"pctl:r", svc_pctl},
    {"time:u", svc_time},
    {"time:a", svc_time},
    {"time:s", svc_time},
    {"fsp-srv", svc_fsp_srv},
    {"acc:u0", svc_acc},
    {"hid", svc_hid},
    {"nifm:u", svc_nifm},
    {"audren:u", svc_audren},
    {"audout:u", svc_audout},
};

static int stub_mode(void) {
    static int on = -1;
    if (on < 0) {
        const char *s = getenv("YW4_IPC_STUB");
        on = s && *s && *s != '0';
    }
    return on;
}

Service *ipc_service_new(const char *name, ServiceHandler handler, void *state) {
    Service *s = calloc(1, sizeof *s);
    if (!s) yw4_exit(3, __FILE__, __LINE__);
    s->name = name;
    s->handler = handler;
    s->state = state;
    return s;
}

void ipc_unimplemented(Service *s, IpcRequest *req, IpcResponse *resp) {
    if (!stub_mode()) {
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: unimplemented IPC command %u on %s (%u bytes of arguments, X%d A%d B%d C%d, "
                        "%d copy / %d move handles)\n", req->cmd, s->name, req->data_size, req->nx, req->na, req->nb,
                req->nc, req->ncopy, req->nmove);
        yw4_stop();
    }
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: [stub] %s command %u -> success, zeroed output\n", s->name, req->cmd);
    ipc_out_size(resp, 0x40);
}

Service *ipc_service_lookup(const char *name) {
    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof registry / sizeof *registry; i++)
        if (!strcmp(registry[i].name, name)) return ipc_service_new(registry[i].name, registry[i].handler, NULL);
    if (!stub_mode()) return NULL;
    char *copy = malloc(strlen(name) + 1);
    strcpy(copy, name);
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: [stub] service %s\n", name);
    return ipc_service_new(copy, ipc_unimplemented, NULL);
}

void ipc_return_object(IpcResponse *resp, Service *s) { resp->objects[resp->nobjects++] = s; }

/* ---- sessions */

typedef struct {
    Service *objects[256];         /* object id -> interface; 0 is never used */
} Domain;

typedef struct {
    KObject obj;
    Service *svc;
    Domain *domain;                /* set once converted; shared by clones */
} Session;

static uint32_t session_new(Service *s, Domain *domain) {
    Session *k = calloc(1, sizeof *k);
    if (!k) yw4_exit(3, __FILE__, __LINE__);
    k->obj.type = KOBJ_SESSION;
    k->svc = s;
    k->domain = domain;
    s->refs++;
    return yw4_handle_new(&k->obj);
}

static void service_release(Service *s) {
    if (s && --s->refs == 0) free(s);
}

uint32_t ipc_connect_named_port(const char *name, uint32_t *handle) {
    if (strcmp(name, "sm:") != 0) {  /* the only named port an application uses */
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: ConnectToNamedPort(\"%s\"): unknown port\n", name);
        return R_NOT_FOUND;
    }
    *handle = session_new(ipc_service_lookup("sm:"), NULL);
    return R_OK;
}

static Session *session_get(uint32_t handle) {
    KObject *o = yw4_handle_get(handle);
    return o && o->type == KOBJ_SESSION ? (Session *)o : NULL;
}

int ipc_close_handle(uint32_t handle) {
    Session *k = session_get(handle);
    if (!k) return 0;
    yw4_handle_close(handle);
    if (!k->domain) service_release(k->svc);  /* a domain's objects are closed one by one */
    free(k);
    return 1;
}

/* ---- decoding */

static uint64_t abw_address(const uint32_t *w) {
    return w[1] | (uint64_t)(w[2] >> 28) << 32 | (uint64_t)((w[2] >> 2) & 7) << 36;
}

/* Fills req from the message; returns the raw data region (where padding starts). */
static uint32_t *decode(uint32_t *msg, IpcRequest *req, uint32_t *raw_words) {
    req->type = msg[0] & 0xFFFF;
    int nx = (msg[0] >> 16) & 0xF, na = (msg[0] >> 20) & 0xF, nb = (msg[0] >> 24) & 0xF, nw = (msg[0] >> 28) & 0xF;
    *raw_words = msg[1] & 0x3FF;
    uint32_t cmode = (msg[1] >> 10) & 0xF;
    uint32_t *p = msg + 2;
    if (msg[1] & 0x80000000u) {
        uint32_t hd = *p++;
        if (hd & 1) {
            req->pid = p[0] | (uint64_t)p[1] << 32;
            p += 2;
        }
        req->ncopy = (hd >> 1) & 0xF;
        req->nmove = (hd >> 5) & 0xF;
        for (int i = 0; i < req->ncopy; i++) req->copy_handles[i] = *p++;
        for (int i = 0; i < req->nmove; i++) req->move_handles[i] = *p++;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < nx; i++, p += 2) {
        req->x[i].addr = p[1] | (uint64_t)((p[0] >> 12) & 0xF) << 32 | (uint64_t)((p[0] >> 6) & 7) << 36;
        req->x[i].size = p[0] >> 16;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < na; i++, p += 3) {
        req->a[i].size = p[0] | (uint64_t)((p[2] >> 24) & 0xF) << 32;
        req->a[i].addr = abw_address(p);
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < nb; i++, p += 3) {
        req->b[i].size = p[0] | (uint64_t)((p[2] >> 24) & 0xF) << 32;
        req->b[i].addr = abw_address(p);
    }
    p += 3 * nw;  /* exchange buffers: none seen yet */
    req->nx = nx, req->na = na, req->nb = nb;
    if (cmode >= 2) {
        uint32_t *c = p + *raw_words;
        req->nc = cmode == 2 ? 1 : (int)cmode - 2;
        for (int i = 0; i < req->nc && i < 8; i++) {
            req->c[i].addr = c[2 * i] | (uint64_t)(c[2 * i + 1] & 0xFFFF) << 32;
            req->c[i].size = c[2 * i + 1] >> 16;
        }
    }
    return p;
}

/* ---- control messages (on the session itself, not a service command) */

static void control(Session *k, IpcRequest *req, IpcResponse *resp) {
    switch (req->cmd) {
    case 0:  /* ConvertCurrentObjectToDomain -> object id */
        k->domain = calloc(1, sizeof *k->domain);
        if (!k->domain) yw4_exit(3, __FILE__, __LINE__);
        k->domain->objects[1] = k->svc;
        IPC_OUT(uint32_t, 0) = 1;
        ipc_out_size(resp, 4);
        return;
    case 2: case 4:  /* CloneCurrentObject(Ex) -> a new session to the same object */
        resp->move_handles[resp->nmove++] = session_new(k->svc, k->domain);
        return;
    case 3:  /* QueryPointerBufferSize */
        IPC_OUT(uint16_t, 0) = 0x8000;
        ipc_out_size(resp, 4);
        return;
    default:
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: unimplemented IPC control command %u on %s\n", req->cmd, k->svc->name);
        yw4_exit(3, __FILE__, __LINE__);
    }
}

/* ---- one request */

uint32_t ipc_send_request(uint32_t handle, uint64_t message) {
    Session *k = session_get(handle);
    if (!k) {
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: SendSyncRequest on handle %#x, which is not a session\n", handle);
        return R_INVALID_HANDLE;
    }
    uint32_t *msg = GPTR(message);
    IpcRequest req = {0};
    IpcResponse resp = {0};
    uint32_t raw_words;
    uint32_t *raw = decode(msg, &req, &raw_words);
    uint8_t *payload = (uint8_t *)(((uintptr_t)raw + 15) & ~(uintptr_t)15);
    uint32_t base = req.type & ~2u;  /* 6/7 = 4/5 with a context token */

    if (req.type == 2) {  /* close the session */
        ipc_close_handle(handle);
        return R_OK;
    }
    int domain = 0;
    Service *target = k->svc;
    if (base == 4 && k->domain) {
        domain = 1;
        uint8_t dcmd = payload[0];
        uint32_t object = *(uint32_t *)(payload + 4);
        if (object >= 256 || !k->domain->objects[object]) {
            fprintf(stderr, "yw4: IPC to missing domain object %u on %s\n", object, k->svc->name);
            yw4_exit(3, __FILE__, __LINE__);
        }
        if (dcmd == 2) {  /* close this domain object */
            service_release(k->domain->objects[object]);
            k->domain->objects[object] = NULL;
            goto reply;
        }
        target = k->domain->objects[object];
        payload += 16;
    }
    if (memcmp(payload, "SFCI", 4) != 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: IPC request to %s without SFCI header (type %u)\n", target->name, req.type);
        yw4_exit(3, __FILE__, __LINE__);
    }
    req.cmd = *(uint32_t *)(payload + 8);
    req.data = payload + 16;
    req.data_size = raw_words * 4 > 32 ? raw_words * 4 - 32 : 0;
    static int trace = -1;
    if (trace < 0) {
        const char *e = getenv("YW4_TRACE_IPC");
        trace = e && *e && *e != '0';
    }
    if (base == 4)
        target->handler(target, &req, &resp);
    else if (base == 5)
        control(k, &req, &resp);
    else {
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: IPC message type %u not supported\n", req.type);
        yw4_exit(3, __FILE__, __LINE__);
    }

reply:;
    uint32_t object_ids[8];
    int nobject_ids = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < resp.nobjects; i++) {
        if (domain) {  /* a new object in the same domain */
            int id = 1;
            while (id < 256 && k->domain->objects[id]) id++;
            if (id == 256) {
                fprintf(stderr, "yw4: IPC domain of %s is full\n", k->svc->name);
                yw4_exit(3, __FILE__, __LINE__);
            }
            k->domain->objects[id] = resp.objects[i];
            resp.objects[i]->refs++;
            object_ids[nobject_ids++] = (uint32_t)id;
        } else {  /* a new session */
            resp.move_handles[resp.nmove++] = session_new(resp.objects[i], NULL);
        }
    }

    memset(msg, 0, 0x100);
    int handles = resp.ncopy || resp.nmove;
    uint32_t payload_words = 4 + (resp.data_size + 3) / 4 + (domain ? 4 + (uint32_t)nobject_ids : 0);
    msg[0] = 0;
    msg[1] = (payload_words + 4) | (handles ? 0x80000000u : 0);  /* + up to 4 words of alignment */
    uint32_t *q = msg + 2;
    if (handles) {
        *q++ = (uint32_t)resp.ncopy << 1 | (uint32_t)resp.nmove << 5;
        for (int i = 0; i < resp.ncopy; i++) *q++ = resp.copy_handles[i];
        for (int i = 0; i < resp.nmove; i++) *q++ = resp.move_handles[i];
    }
    uint32_t *out = (uint32_t *)(((uintptr_t)q + 15) & ~(uintptr_t)15);
    if (domain) {
        out[0] = (uint32_t)nobject_ids;
        out += 4;
    }
    memcpy(out, "SFCO", 4);
    out[1] = 0;
    out[2] = resp.result;
    out[3] = 0;
    memcpy(out + 4, resp.data, resp.data_size);
    for (int i = 0; i < nobject_ids; i++) out[4 + (resp.data_size + 3) / 4 + i] = object_ids[i];
    if (trace)
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: ipc %s cmd %u (%u bytes in) -> result %#x, %u bytes out, %d handles, %d objects\n",
                target->name, req.cmd, req.data_size, resp.result, resp.data_size, resp.ncopy + resp.nmove,
                resp.nobjects);
    return R_OK;
}

```

`runtime/src/ipc.h`:

```h
/* IPC between the recompiled sdk and native system services (decision 0014).
 *
 * The sdk sends requests with svcSendSyncRequest: the message sits in the calling thread's
 * thread-local region (Switchbrew "IPC_Marshalling": a HIPC header with handle and buffer
 * descriptors, then a CMIF payload "SFCI" + command id + arguments). ipc.c decodes it into
 * an IpcRequest, the service's handler fills an IpcResponse, and ipc.c writes the reply
 * ("SFCO" + result + output) back over the request.
 *
 * Unknown services and commands stop the program with their name and number, so the next
 * thing to implement is obvious. YW4_IPC_STUB=1 instead answers them with "success, zeroed
 * output" and logs each one: for surveying what the game needs, not for playing.
 */
#ifndef IPC_H
#define IPC_H

#include <stdint.h>

#include "hle.h"
#include "kernel.h"

typedef struct {
    uint64_t addr, size;
} IpcBuffer;

typedef struct {
    uint32_t type;                 /* 4 request, 5 control, 2 close (+2: with context) */
    uint32_t cmd;                  /* CMIF command id */
    const uint8_t *data;           /* arguments after the 16-byte CMIF header */
    uint32_t data_size;
    uint64_t pid;                  /* if the client sent its process id */
    uint32_t copy_handles[8], move_handles[8];
    int ncopy, nmove;
    IpcBuffer x[8], a[8], b[8], c[8];  /* pointer (X), send (A), receive (B), receive-list (C) */
    int nx, na, nb, nc;
} IpcRequest;

typedef struct Service Service;

typedef struct {
    uint32_t result;
    uint8_t data[0x200];
    uint32_t data_size;
    uint32_t copy_handles[8], move_handles[8];
    int ncopy, nmove;
    Service *objects[8];           /* new interfaces to return: sessions, or domain objects */
    int nobjects;
} IpcResponse;

typedef void (*ServiceHandler)(Service *s, IpcRequest *req, IpcResponse *resp);

struct Service {
    const char *name;
    ServiceHandler handler;
    void *state;
    int refs;                      /* sessions and domain slots holding it */
};

/* Argument/output helpers for handlers. */
#define IPC_IN(type, off) (*(const type *)(req->data + (off)))
#define IPC_OUT(type, off) (*(type *)(resp->data + (off)))
static inline void ipc_out_size(IpcResponse *resp, uint32_t n) { if (n > resp->data_size) resp->data_size = n; }

/* Output buffer i of a command declared "auto select": the client sends it as a B buffer, or
 * (small ones) as a C receive-list buffer with an empty B in the same place. Writing to the
 * C address directly is what the kernel's copy-back would do. {0, 0} if there is none. */
static inline IpcBuffer ipc_out_buffer(const IpcRequest *req, int i) {
    if (i < req->nb && req->b[i].size) return req->b[i];
    if (i < req->nc) return req->c[i];
    return (IpcBuffer){0, 0};
}

Service *ipc_service_new(const char *name, ServiceHandler handler, void *state);
void ipc_return_object(IpcResponse *resp, Service *s);
/* A named service from the registry (ipc.c), or NULL / a stub (YW4_IPC_STUB=1). */
Service *ipc_service_lookup(const char *name);
/* The default branch of every handler: stops, or logs and succeeds in stub mode. */
void ipc_unimplemented(Service *s, IpcRequest *req, IpcResponse *resp);

/* Kernel side (kernel.c): ConnectToNamedPort, SendSyncRequest(WithUserBuffer), CloseHandle. */
uint32_t ipc_connect_named_port(const char *name, uint32_t *handle);
uint32_t ipc_send_request(uint32_t handle, uint64_t message);
int ipc_close_handle(uint32_t handle);  /* 1 if it was a session */

/* Services (svc_*.c) */
void svc_sm(Service *s, IpcRequest *req, IpcResponse *resp);
void svc_appletOE(Service *s, IpcRequest *req, IpcResponse *resp);
void svc_apm(Service *s, IpcRequest *req, IpcResponse *resp);
void svc_lm(Service *s, IpcRequest *req, IpcResponse *resp);
void svc_aoc_u(Service *s, IpcRequest *req, IpcResponse *resp);
void svc_pctl(Service *s, IpcRequest *req, IpcResponse *resp);
void svc_time(Service *s, IpcRequest *req, IpcResponse *resp);
void svc_fsp_srv(Service *s, IpcRequest *req, IpcResponse *resp);
void svc_acc(Service *s, IpcRequest *req, IpcResponse *resp);
void svc_hid(Service *s, IpcRequest *req, IpcResponse *resp);
void svc_nifm(Service *s, IpcRequest *req, IpcResponse *resp);
void svc_audren(Service *s, IpcRequest *req, IpcResponse *resp);
void svc_audout(Service *s, IpcRequest *req, IpcResponse *resp);

/* The one user account (svc_acc.c): its 16-byte id. */
void yw4_account_user_id(uint8_t out[16]);

#endif

```

`runtime/src/ipc_simple.h`:

```h
/* Table-driven answers for IPC commands that need no logic: "succeed", "return this
 * constant", or "return an event nothing signals" (decision 0014). Most of a service's
 * commands are like that; the handler keeps real code only for the rest. */
#ifndef IPC_SIMPLE_H
#define IPC_SIMPLE_H

#include "ipc.h"

typedef enum { SIMPLE_OK, SIMPLE_U8, SIMPLE_U32, SIMPLE_U64, SIMPLE_EVENT } SimpleKind;

typedef struct {
    uint32_t cmd;
    SimpleKind kind;
    uint64_t value;
    const char *name;  /* Switchbrew's name for the command: documentation only */
} SimpleCommand;

/* Answers req from the table; 0 if the command isn't in it. */
static inline int ipc_simple(const SimpleCommand *table, size_t n, IpcRequest *req, IpcResponse *resp) {
    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        const SimpleCommand *c = &table[i];
        if (c->cmd != req->cmd) continue;
        switch (c->kind) {
        case SIMPLE_OK: break;
        case SIMPLE_U8: IPC_OUT(uint8_t, 0) = (uint8_t)c->value; ipc_out_size(resp, 1); break;
        case SIMPLE_U32: IPC_OUT(uint32_t, 0) = (uint32_t)c->value; ipc_out_size(resp, 4); break;
        case SIMPLE_U64: IPC_OUT(uint64_t, 0) = c->value; ipc_out_size(resp, 8); break;
        case SIMPLE_EVENT: {
            uint32_t h;
            yw4_event_new(&h);
            resp->copy_handles[resp->ncopy++] = h;
            break;
        }
        }
        return 1;
    }
    return 0;
}

#define IPC_SIMPLE(table, req, resp) ipc_simple(table, sizeof table / sizeof *table, req, resp)

#endif

```

`runtime/src/kernel.c`:

```c
/* The Horizon kernel as the recompiled sdk sees it (decisions 0014, 0015).
 *
 * The sdk talks to the kernel only through SVC instructions: arguments in x0-x7, result
 * code in w0, outputs in x1.. (Switchbrew "SVC"). Each one is implemented when the game
 * first reaches it; an unimplemented SVC stops with its number, as unimplemented imports
 * used to. LAS Recomp's kernel (github.com/peiikai/LASRecomp, runtime/kernel.c, MIT) was the
 * reference for argument layouts and result codes; Atmosphère's kernel (mesosphere) for
 * what the synchronisation calls do, step by step.
 *
 * Threads (decision 0015): every guest thread is a host thread with its own CPUState and
 * thread-local region. One lock (klock) guards all kernel and service state: every SVC
 * runs holding it, and a thread that blocks waits on its own host condition variable,
 * which releases the lock meanwhile. Guest code itself runs without the lock, truly in
 * parallel; priorities and core masks are recorded but the host schedules.
 *
 * YW4_TRACE_SVC=1 prints every call.
 */
#include <inttypes.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "hle.h"
#include "host.h"
#include "ipc.h"
#include "kernel.h"
#include "nvn.h"
#include "yw4load.h"

/* Result codes (module 1, the kernel) */
#define R_OK 0u
#define R_INVALID_SIZE 0xCA01u
#define R_INVALID_ADDRESS 0xCC01u
#define R_OUT_OF_MEMORY 0xD001u
#define R_OUT_OF_RESOURCE 0xD201u
#define R_INVALID_PRIORITY 0xE001u
#define R_INVALID_HANDLE 0xE401u
#define R_TIMEOUT 0xEA01u
#define R_CANCELLED 0xEC01u
#define R_OUT_OF_RANGE 0xEE01u
#define R_INVALID_ENUM 0xF001u
#define R_INVALID_STATE 0xFA01u

#define WAITERS_BIT 0x40000000u  /* in a mutex word: other threads are waiting */

#define PSEUDO_CURRENT_THREAD 0xFFFF8000u
#define PSEUDO_CURRENT_PROCESS 0xFFFF8001u

#define PROGRAM_ID 0x010086C00AF7C000ull  /* Yo-kai Watch 4++ (CLAUDE.md) */
#define TOTAL_MEMORY 0xCD500000ull        /* application pool of a 4 GiB Switch */

static HostLock klock;

/* ---- memory map, for svcQueryMemory */

typedef struct {
    uint64_t addr, size;
    uint32_t type, perm;
} Region;

#define MAX_REGIONS 256
static Region regions[MAX_REGIONS];
static int nregions;

static void region_add(uint64_t addr, uint64_t size, uint32_t type, uint32_t perm) {
    if (nregions == MAX_REGIONS) {
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: kernel: too many memory regions\n");
        yw4_exit(3, __FILE__, __LINE__);
    }
    int i = nregions++;
    while (i > 0 && regions[i - 1].addr > addr) {  /* kept sorted by address */
        regions[i] = regions[i - 1];
        i--;
    }
    regions[i] = (Region){addr, size, type, perm};
}

static void region_remove(uint64_t addr) {
    for (int i = 0; i < nregions; i++)
        if (regions[i].addr == addr) {
            memmove(&regions[i], &regions[i + 1], (size_t)(nregions - i - 1) * sizeof *regions);
            nregions--;
            return;
        }
}

/* The writable regions (heap, the modules' data, mappings), up to max: for memscan.c (YW4_MEMSCAN). Stacks and
 * thread-local regions are left out. */
int yw4_memory_rw_regions(uint64_t *addr, uint64_t *size, int max) {
    host_lock(&klock);
    int n = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < nregions && n < max; i++)
        if (regions[i].perm == PERM_RW && regions[i].type != MEM_STACK && regions[i].type != MEM_THREAD_LOCAL)
            addr[n] = regions[i].addr, size[n] = regions[i].size, n++;
    host_unlock(&klock);
    return n;
}

/* svcQueryMemory's MemoryInfo: the region containing addr, or the unmapped gap around it. */
static void query_memory(uint64_t addr, uint64_t out) {
    struct {
        uint64_t addr, size;
        uint32_t type, attr, perm, ipc_refcount, device_refcount, pad;
    } info = {0};
    uint64_t gap_lo = 0, gap_hi = 1ull << 39;
    for (int i = 0; i < nregions; i++) {
        const Region *r = &regions[i];
        if (addr - r->addr < r->size) {
            info.addr = r->addr, info.size = r->size, info.type = r->type, info.perm = r->perm;
            memcpy(GPTR(out), &info, sizeof info);
            return;
        }
        if (r->addr + r->size <= addr) gap_lo = r->addr + r->size;
        else if (r->addr < gap_hi) gap_hi = r->addr;
    }
    info.addr = gap_lo, info.size = gap_hi - gap_lo;  /* MEM_UNMAPPED, no permissions */
    memcpy(GPTR(out), &info, sizeof info);
}

/* ---- heap */

static uint64_t heap_size;

static uint32_t set_heap_size(uint64_t size) {
    if (size % 0x200000 || size > YW4_HEAP_SIZE) return R_INVALID_SIZE;
    if (size > heap_size && yw4_commit(YW4_HEAP_BASE + heap_size, size - heap_size)) return R_OUT_OF_MEMORY;
    if (size < heap_size) yw4_decommit(YW4_HEAP_BASE + size, heap_size - size);
    heap_size = size;
    region_remove(YW4_HEAP_BASE);
    if (size) region_add(YW4_HEAP_BASE, size, MEM_HEAP, PERM_RW);
    return R_OK;
}

/* ---- threads */

typedef enum {
    WAIT_NONE,
    WAIT_SYNC,     /* WaitSynchronization: for one of wait_objs to be signalled */
    WAIT_LOCK,     /* ArbitrateLock: for the mutex at addr to be handed over */
    WAIT_CONDVAR,  /* WaitProcessWideKeyAtomic: for a signal on the key at addr */
    WAIT_ADDRESS,  /* WaitForAddress: for SignalToAddress on addr */
} WaitKind;

#define MAX_WAIT_OBJECTS 0x40  /* Horizon's limit for WaitSynchronization */

typedef struct KThread KThread;
struct KThread {
    KObject obj;
    uint64_t id;
    int32_t priority, core;
    CPUState *ctx;
    uint64_t entry, tlr;
    int slot;            /* index of its thread-local region */
    int started, exited, handle_closed;
    HostCond cond;
    /* The current wait (klock held for all of these). */
    WaitKind wait;
    int woken;
    int forever;         /* the wait has no timeout: not counted in nrunnable meanwhile */
    uint32_t result;     /* what the wait ends with */
    int32_t index;       /* WAIT_SYNC: which object */
    uint64_t seq;        /* order of arrival, for FIFO among equal priorities */
    uint64_t addr;       /* WAIT_LOCK: mutex; WAIT_CONDVAR: key; WAIT_ADDRESS: address */
    uint64_t mutex;      /* WAIT_CONDVAR: the mutex to take back when signalled */
    uint32_t tag;        /* WAIT_LOCK/WAIT_CONDVAR: the value that marks this thread as owner */
    int cancel_pending;  /* CancelSynchronization while not in WAIT_SYNC */
    KObject *objs[MAX_WAIT_OBJECTS];
    int32_t nobjs;
    KThread *next;       /* all threads */
    void *host;          /* the host thread, for its CPU time (performance log) */
    int64_t cpu_last;    /* its CPU time at the last report */
    int roles;           /* YW4_ROLE_* seen on it */
};

/* Thread-local regions: one 4 KiB page per thread slot (Horizon packs 0x200-byte regions
 * eight to a page; a page each is simpler and the guest can't tell). */
#define MAX_THREADS 256
#define TLR_STRIDE 0x1000ull
static KThread *slots[MAX_THREADS];

#define GUEST_THREAD_HOST_STACK (16u << 20)  /* host stack per guest thread: reserved, not committed */

static KThread *threads;            /* every thread not yet freed */
static KThread main_thread;
static uint64_t next_thread_id = 1, next_seq;
static int nrunnable;               /* started, not exited, not in a wait without timeout */
static _Thread_local KThread *cur;  /* the guest thread this host thread runs */

/* ---- handles */

#define MAX_HANDLES 4096
static KObject *handles[MAX_HANDLES];

uint32_t yw4_handle_new(KObject *o) {
    for (uint32_t i = 1; i < MAX_HANDLES; i++)
        if (!handles[i]) {
            handles[i] = o;
            return 0x100 + i;
        }
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: kernel: out of handles\n");
    yw4_exit(3, __FILE__, __LINE__);
}

KObject *yw4_handle_get(uint32_t h) {
    if (h == PSEUDO_CURRENT_THREAD) return &cur->obj;
    return h - 0x100 < MAX_HANDLES ? handles[h - 0x100] : NULL;
}

void yw4_handle_close(uint32_t h) {
    if (h - 0x100 < MAX_HANDLES) handles[h - 0x100] = NULL;
}

static KThread *thread_get(uint32_t h) {
    KObject *o = yw4_handle_get(h);
    return o && o->type == KOBJ_THREAD ? (KThread *)o : NULL;
}

static uint32_t *u32p(uint64_t a) { return GPTR(a); }

/* The guest call stack, from the frame-pointer chain (x29 -> [previous x29, return address]). */
static void backtrace(const CPUState *ctx) {
    char where[48];
    uint64_t fp = ctx->x[29];
    fprintf(stderr, "     guest backtrace:\n");
    for (int i = 0; i < 16 && fp >= YW4_GUEST_LO && fp < YW4_GUEST_HI && !(fp & 7); i++) {
        uint64_t ret = *(const uint64_t *)GPTR(fp + 8);
        if (!ret) break;
        fprintf(stderr, "       %s\n", yw4_describe(ret - 4, where));
        fp = *(const uint64_t *)GPTR(fp);
    }
}

/* YW4_WATCHW: a write to the watched bytes, on the writing thread (host.c watchpoint) */
static void write_watch_report(uint64_t pc, uint64_t addr) {
    char where[48];
    /* the pc also relative to a function of ours, so llvm-nm on yw4.exe can name the recompiled function */
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: write to %#" PRIx64 " by guest thread %" PRIu64 " (host pc %#" PRIx64 " = yw4_describe%+lld)\n",
            addr, cur ? cur->id : 0, pc, (long long)(pc - (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&yw4_describe));
    if (!cur) return;
    uint64_t st[12];
    int k = yw4_call_stack(cur->ctx, st, 12);
    for (int i = 0; i < k; i++) fprintf(stderr, "       %s\n", yw4_describe(st[i] - 4, where));
}

int yw4_write_watch_arm(uint64_t addr, uint64_t size) {
    int r = host_write_watch(addr, size, write_watch_report);
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: write watch on %#" PRIx64 " (%" PRIu64 " bytes) %s\n", addr, size, r ? "failed" : "armed");
    return r;
}

/* YW4_TRACE_AI (ai_trace.c): a read of the watched bytes, on the reading guest thread: who reads them, and its callers */
static void read_watch_report(uint64_t pc, uint64_t addr) {
    char where[48];
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: ai: read of %#" PRIx64 " by guest thread %" PRIu64 " (host pc %#" PRIx64 " = yw4_describe%+lld)\n",
            addr, cur ? cur->id : 0, pc, (long long)(pc - (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&yw4_describe));
    if (!cur) return;
    uint64_t st[12];
    int k = yw4_call_stack(cur->ctx, st, 12);
    for (int i = 0; i < k; i++) fprintf(stderr, "       %s\n", yw4_describe(st[i] - 4, where));
}

int yw4_read_watch_arm(uint64_t addr, uint64_t size, long reports) {
    int r = host_read_watch(addr, size, reports, read_watch_report);
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: ai: read watch on %#" PRIx64 " (%" PRIu64 " bytes, %ld reports) %s\n", addr, size, reports,
            r ? "failed" : "armed");
    return r;
}

int yw4_call_stack(const CPUState *ctx, uint64_t *out, int n) {
    uint64_t fp = ctx->x[29];
    int k = 0;
    if (k < n) out[k++] = ctx->x[30];  /* the caller of a native function: its return address */
    for (; k < n && fp >= YW4_GUEST_LO && fp < YW4_GUEST_HI && !(fp & 7); k++) {
        uint64_t ret = *(const uint64_t *)GPTR(fp + 8);
        if (!ret) break;
        out[k] = ret;
        fp = *(const uint64_t *)GPTR(fp);
    }
    return k;
}

/* ---- host crashes (a bad guest pointer, or a runtime bug): say where the guest was */

static void report_crash(const char *what, uint64_t pc, uint64_t addr) {
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: crash: %s at host pc %#" PRIx64 ", address %#" PRIx64 "\n", what, pc, addr);
    if (cur) yw4_stop();  /* the guest thread and its backtrace */
    yw4_exit(3, __FILE__, __LINE__);
}

void yw4_kernel_lock(void) { host_lock(&klock); }
void yw4_kernel_unlock(void) { host_unlock(&klock); }

_Noreturn void yw4_stop(void) {
    fprintf(stderr, "     on thread %" PRIu64 "\n", cur->id);
    backtrace(cur->ctx);
    yw4_exit(3, __FILE__, __LINE__);
}

/* ---- waiting and waking (klock held) */

static int is_signaled(const KObject *o) {
    if (o->type == KOBJ_EVENT) return ((const KEvent *)o)->signaled;
    return ((const KThread *)o)->exited;  /* KOBJ_THREAD: WaitSynchronization only accepts these two */
}

/* Ends t's wait with `result`; it runs again once it gets klock. */
static void end_wait(KThread *t, uint32_t result) {
    if (t->forever) {  /* runnable from now on, even before it gets klock back */
        t->forever = 0;
        nrunnable++;
    }
    t->wait = WAIT_NONE;
    t->result = result;
    t->woken = 1;
    host_cond_signal(&t->cond);
}

/* t would be served before u: higher priority (lower number), then first come. */
static int before(const KThread *t, const KThread *u) {
    return t->priority != u->priority ? t->priority < u->priority : t->seq < u->seq;
}

/* The best thread waiting as `kind` on `addr`, and how many wait so (NULL, 0 if none). */
static KThread *first_waiter(WaitKind kind, uint64_t addr, int *count) {
    KThread *best = NULL;
    int n = 0;
    for (KThread *t = threads; t; t = t->next)
        if (t->wait == kind && t->addr == addr) {
            n++;
            if (!best || before(t, best)) best = t;
        }
    if (count) *count = n;
    return best;
}

static const char *const wait_names[] = {"running", "WaitSynchronization", "ArbitrateLock (mutex)",
                                         "WaitProcessWideKeyAtomic (condition variable)", "WaitForAddress"};

/* Every guest thread waits for something only another guest thread could do: nothing will
 * ever run again. (Waits on host-signalled events, like vsync, don't count: a host thread
 * ends them.) So this is a real deadlock, or a missing kernel/service feature: stop and show
 * where everyone is. */
static _Noreturn void all_blocked(void) {
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: kernel: every guest thread waits forever:\n");
    for (KThread *t = threads; t; t = t->next) {
        if (!t->started || t->exited) continue;
        fprintf(stderr, "   thread %" PRIu64 " (priority %d): %s", t->id, t->priority, wait_names[t->wait]);
        if (t->wait != WAIT_NONE && t->wait != WAIT_SYNC) fprintf(stderr, " at %#" PRIx64, t->addr);
        fprintf(stderr, "\n");
        backtrace(t->ctx);
    }
    yw4_exit(3, __FILE__, __LINE__);
}

/* YW4_DUMP_THREADS_AT=<seconds>[,<seconds>...]: at those times after start, print every
 * guest thread, what it waits for and its call stack (from its registers at its last
 * system call: exact for waiting threads, approximate for running ones). */
static void dump_threads(void) {
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: kernel: threads at %.1f s:\n", (double)host_now_ns() / 1e9);
    for (KThread *t = threads; t; t = t->next) {
        if (!t->started || t->exited) continue;
        fprintf(stderr, "   thread %" PRIu64 " (priority %d): %s", t->id, t->priority, wait_names[t->wait]);
        if (t->wait != WAIT_NONE && t->wait != WAIT_SYNC) fprintf(stderr, " at %#" PRIx64, t->addr);
        fprintf(stderr, "\n");
        backtrace(t->ctx);
    }
}

static void dump_threads_thread(void *arg) {
    const char *s = arg;
    int64_t start = host_now_ns();
    while (*s) {
        char *e;
        double at = strtod(s, &e);
        if (e == s) break;
        int64_t due = start + (int64_t)(at * 1e9) - host_now_ns();
        if (due > 0) host_sleep_ns(due);
        host_lock(&klock);
        dump_threads();
        host_unlock(&klock);
        s = *e == ',' ? e + 1 : e;
    }
}

void yw4_dump_threads_start(void) {
    const char *s = getenv("YW4_DUMP_THREADS_AT");
    if (s && *s) host_thread_start(dump_threads_thread, (void *)s, 1 << 16);
}

/* Blocks the current thread in the wait it has set up, for at most timeout_ns (< 0: no
 * limit). Returns the result its waker gave, or R_TIMEOUT. host_can_wake: a host thread may
 * end this wait (a host-signalled event), so it doesn't count as blocked forever. */
static uint32_t wait_current_ex(int64_t timeout_ns, int host_can_wake) {
    KThread *t = cur;
    t->woken = 0;
    t->seq = next_seq++;
    int forever = timeout_ns < 0;
    int64_t deadline = forever ? 0 : host_now_ns() + timeout_ns;
    t->forever = forever && !host_can_wake;
    if (t->forever && --nrunnable == 0) all_blocked();
    while (!t->woken) {
        int64_t left = forever ? -1 : deadline - host_now_ns();
        if (!forever && left <= 0) break;
        host_cond_wait(&t->cond, &klock, left);
    }
    if (!t->woken) {  /* timed out: leaving whatever list it was on is just this */
        t->wait = WAIT_NONE;
        t->result = R_TIMEOUT;
    }
    return t->result;
}

static uint32_t wait_current(int64_t timeout_ns) { return wait_current_ex(timeout_ns, 0); }

/* An object became signalled: wake everyone waiting on it. */
static void wake_sync_waiters(const KObject *o) {
    for (KThread *t = threads; t; t = t->next)
        if (t->wait == WAIT_SYNC)
            for (int32_t i = 0; i < t->nobjs; i++)
                if (t->objs[i] == o) {
                    t->index = i;
                    end_wait(t, R_OK);
                    break;
                }
}

static uint32_t wait_synchronization(uint64_t handles_addr, int32_t n, int64_t timeout, int32_t *index) {
    KThread *t = cur;
    if (n < 0 || n > MAX_WAIT_OBJECTS) return R_OUT_OF_RANGE;
    const uint32_t *hs = GPTR(handles_addr);
    for (int32_t i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        KObject *o = yw4_handle_get(hs[i]);
        if (!o) return R_INVALID_HANDLE;
        if (o->type != KOBJ_EVENT && o->type != KOBJ_THREAD) {
            fprintf(stderr, "yw4: kernel: WaitSynchronization on a handle of kind %d: not implemented\n", o->type);
            yw4_exit(3, __FILE__, __LINE__);
        }
        t->objs[i] = o;
    }
    if (t->cancel_pending) {
        t->cancel_pending = 0;
        return R_CANCELLED;
    }
    for (int32_t i = 0; i < n; i++)
        if (is_signaled(t->objs[i])) {
            *index = i;
            return R_OK;
        }
    if (timeout == 0) return R_TIMEOUT;
    int host_can_wake = 0;
    for (int32_t i = 0; i < n; i++)
        if (t->objs[i]->type == KOBJ_EVENT && ((KEvent *)t->objs[i])->host_signalled) host_can_wake = 1;
    t->nobjs = n;
    t->wait = WAIT_SYNC;
    uint32_t r = wait_current_ex(timeout, host_can_wake);
    *index = r == R_OK ? t->index : -1;
    return r;
}

/* ---- the thread's life */

static uint64_t tlr_address(int slot) { return YW4_TLR_BASE + (uint64_t)slot * TLR_STRIDE; }

static int tlr_alloc(KThread *t) {
    for (int i = 0; i < MAX_THREADS; i++)
        if (!slots[i]) {
            if (yw4_commit(tlr_address(i), TLR_STRIDE)) return -1;
            memset(GPTR(tlr_address(i)), 0, TLR_STRIDE);  /* a reused slot starts clean too */
            slots[i] = t;
            t->slot = i;
            t->tlr = tlr_address(i);
            return 0;
        }
    return -1;
}

/* Frees a thread once it has exited and its handle is closed: nothing can refer to it. */
static void thread_free_if_done(KThread *t) {
    if (!t->exited || !t->handle_closed || t == &main_thread) return;
    for (KThread **p = &threads; *p; p = &(*p)->next)
        if (*p == t) {
            *p = t->next;
            break;
        }
    slots[t->slot] = NULL;
    free(t->ctx);
    free(t);
}

static void thread_exit(KThread *t) {
    t->exited = 1;
    nrunnable--;
    wake_sync_waiters(&t->obj);  /* a thread's handle is signalled when it ends */
    if (nrunnable == 0) {
        for (KThread *u = threads; u; u = u->next)
            if (u->started && !u->exited) all_blocked();  /* the others all wait forever */
    }
    thread_free_if_done(t);
}

/* ExitThread leaves the guest code through a jump back to the thread's host entry
 * (setjmp/longjmp of the C library: see decision 0018 for why not __builtin_setjmp). */
static _Thread_local jmp_buf *exit_jump;

static void thread_main(void *p) {
    KThread *t = p;
    jmp_buf jump;
    cur = t;
    t->host = host_thread_self();
    host_thread_set_priority(t->host, t->priority);
    exit_jump = &jump;
    yw4_profile_thread(YW4_ROLE_ANY, 0);  /* YW4_PROFILE=hitch samples them all */
    if (setjmp(jump) == 0) {
        yw4_resolve(t->entry)(t->ctx);
        host_lock(&klock);  /* the entry function returned: the thread ends as if by ExitThread */
        thread_exit(t);
        host_unlock(&klock);
    }
    /* Here after ExitThread too, which already did thread_exit; t may be freed by now. */
}

static uint32_t create_thread(uint64_t entry, uint64_t arg, uint64_t stack_top, int32_t priority, int32_t core,
                              uint32_t *handle) {
    if (priority < 0 || priority > 63) return R_INVALID_PRIORITY;
    if (core == -2) core = main_thread.core;  /* the process's ideal core */
    if (core < 0 || core > 2) {
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: kernel: CreateThread on core %d: not implemented\n", core);
        yw4_exit(3, __FILE__, __LINE__);
    }
    KThread *t = calloc(1, sizeof *t);
    CPUState *ctx = calloc(1, sizeof *ctx);
    if (!t || !ctx || tlr_alloc(t)) {
        free(t), free(ctx);
        return R_OUT_OF_RESOURCE;
    }
    t->obj.type = KOBJ_THREAD;
    t->id = next_thread_id++;
    t->priority = priority, t->core = core;
    t->entry = entry;
    t->ctx = ctx;
    host_cond_init(&t->cond);
    ctx->x[0] = arg;
    ctx->sp = stack_top & ~15ull;
    ctx->tpidrro_el0 = t->tlr;
    t->next = threads;
    threads = t;
    *handle = yw4_handle_new(&t->obj);
    return R_OK;
}

static uint32_t start_thread(uint32_t handle) {
    KThread *t = thread_get(handle);
    if (!t) return R_INVALID_HANDLE;
    if (t->started) return R_INVALID_STATE;
    t->started = 1;
    nrunnable++;
    if (host_thread_start(thread_main, t, GUEST_THREAD_HOST_STACK)) {
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: kernel: cannot start a host thread\n");
        yw4_exit(3, __FILE__, __LINE__);
    }
    return R_OK;
}

void yw4_thread_role(int role) {
    if (cur) cur->roles |= role;
}

uint64_t yw4_thread_id(void) { return cur ? cur->id : 0; }

/* One line per guest thread that used CPU since the last call: its share of one core over
   `interval_ns`, entry point, priority, core and roles. For the performance summary. */
void yw4_thread_cpu_report(FILE *f, int64_t interval_ns) {
    host_lock(&klock);
    for (KThread *t = threads; t; t = t->next) {
        if (!t->host || t->exited) continue;
        int64_t now = host_thread_cpu_ns(t->host), used = now - t->cpu_last;
        t->cpu_last = now;
        if (interval_ns <= 0 || used * 100 < interval_ns) continue;  /* under 1% */
        fprintf(f, "    thread %" PRIu64 ": %3.0f%% of a core  entry %#" PRIx64 " prio %d core %d%s%s\n", t->id,
                100.0 * (double)used / (double)interval_ns, t->entry, t->priority, t->core,
                t->roles & YW4_ROLE_PRESENT ? "  [presents]" : "", t->roles & YW4_ROLE_SUBMIT ? "  [submits GPU work]" : "");
    }
    host_unlock(&klock);
}

uint32_t yw4_kernel_init(CPUState *ctx, uint64_t stack, uint64_t stack_size) {
    host_lock_init(&klock);
    host_install_crash_handler(report_crash);
    host_timer_init();
    for (size_t i = 0; i < yw4_nmodules; i++) {  /* as Horizon maps an NSO: three regions */
        const Yw4Module *m = &yw4_modules[i];
        uint64_t b = *m->base;
        region_add(b, m->ro_offset, MEM_CODE_STATIC, PERM_RX);                                  /* .text */
        region_add(b + m->ro_offset, m->data_offset - m->ro_offset, MEM_CODE_STATIC, PERM_R);    /* .rodata */
        region_add(b + m->data_offset, m->mem_size - m->data_offset, MEM_CODE_MUTABLE, PERM_RW); /* .data, .bss */
    }
    region_add(stack, stack_size, MEM_STACK, PERM_RW);
    /* The heap's and the thread-local regions' ranges first, then everything else that is
     * free: later mappings are commits (reserved at main() entry if not already). */
    /* the heap with write tracking: the draw path re-uploads textures the CPU wrote (0021) */
    if (yw4_guest_memory_init()) {
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: kernel: cannot reserve the heap and thread-local regions\n");
        yw4_exit(3, __FILE__, __LINE__);
    }
    region_add(YW4_TLR_BASE, MAX_THREADS * TLR_STRIDE, MEM_THREAD_LOCAL, PERM_RW);
    yw4_dump_threads_start();

    KThread *t = &main_thread;
    t->obj.type = KOBJ_THREAD;
    t->id = next_thread_id++;
    t->priority = (int32_t)yw4_main_priority;
    t->core = 0;  /* the NPDM's default core */
    t->ctx = ctx;
    t->started = 1;
    host_cond_init(&t->cond);
    if (tlr_alloc(t)) {
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: kernel: cannot make the main thread's thread-local region\n");
        yw4_exit(3, __FILE__, __LINE__);
    }
    ctx->tpidrro_el0 = t->tlr;
    threads = t;
    nrunnable = 1;
    cur = t;
    t->host = host_thread_self();
    host_thread_set_priority(t->host, t->priority);
    return yw4_handle_new(&t->obj);
}

/* ---- events */

KEvent *yw4_event_new(uint32_t *handle) {
    KEvent *e = calloc(1, sizeof *e);
    if (!e) yw4_exit(3, __FILE__, __LINE__);
    e->obj.type = KOBJ_EVENT;
    *handle = yw4_handle_new(&e->obj);
    return e;
}

void yw4_event_signal_from_host(KEvent *e) {
    host_lock(&klock);
    yw4_event_signal(e);
    host_unlock(&klock);
}

void yw4_event_signal(KEvent *e) {
    e->signaled = 1;
    wake_sync_waiters(&e->obj);
}
void yw4_event_clear(KEvent *e) { e->signaled = 0; }

static KEvent *event_get(uint32_t h) {
    KObject *o = yw4_handle_get(h);
    return o && o->type == KOBJ_EVENT ? (KEvent *)o : NULL;
}

/* ---- shared memory */

KSharedMemory *yw4_shared_memory_new(uint64_t size, void (*on_map)(KSharedMemory *), uint32_t *handle) {
    KSharedMemory *m = calloc(1, sizeof *m);
    if (!m) yw4_exit(3, __FILE__, __LINE__);
    m->obj.type = KOBJ_SHARED_MEMORY;
    m->size = size;
    m->on_map = on_map;
    *handle = yw4_handle_new(&m->obj);
    return m;
}

static uint32_t map_shared_memory(uint32_t handle, uint64_t addr, uint64_t size) {
    KObject *o = yw4_handle_get(handle);
    if (!o || o->type != KOBJ_SHARED_MEMORY) return R_INVALID_HANDLE;
    KSharedMemory *m = (KSharedMemory *)o;
    if (size != m->size || addr & 0xFFF) return R_INVALID_SIZE;
    if (yw4_commit(addr, size)) {  /* the game chose a free range (reserved at start-up): put memory there */
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: kernel: cannot map shared memory at %#" PRIx64 "\n", addr);
        yw4_exit(3, __FILE__, __LINE__);
    }
    region_add(addr, size, MEM_SHARED, PERM_RW);
    m->guest_addr = addr;
    if (m->on_map) m->on_map(m);
    return R_OK;
}

/* ---- transfer memory */

static uint32_t create_transfer_memory(uint64_t addr, uint64_t size, uint32_t perm, uint32_t *handle) {
    if ((addr | size) & 0xFFF || !size) return R_INVALID_SIZE;
    if (perm != PERM_NONE && perm != PERM_R && perm != PERM_RW) return R_INVALID_ENUM;  /* InvalidNewMemoryPermission */
    KTransferMemory *m = calloc(1, sizeof *m);
    if (!m) yw4_exit(3, __FILE__, __LINE__);
    m->obj.type = KOBJ_TRANSFER_MEMORY;
    m->addr = addr, m->size = size, m->perm = perm;
    *handle = yw4_handle_new(&m->obj);
    return R_OK;
}

KTransferMemory *yw4_transfer_memory_get(uint32_t handle) {
    KObject *o = yw4_handle_get(handle);
    return o && o->type == KOBJ_TRANSFER_MEMORY ? (KTransferMemory *)o : NULL;
}

/* ---- mutexes and condition variables (mesosphere KConditionVariable)
 *
 * The sdk's mutex is a word in guest memory: 0 = free, else the owner's tag (its thread
 * handle), with WAITERS_BIT once someone waits. Taking and releasing a free mutex is pure
 * guest code (exclusive load/store, decision 0009); the kernel is only called when there is
 * contention. A condition variable is a key word: 1 while someone may be waiting. Guest
 * code writes these words concurrently, so the kernel changes them atomically too. */

/* ArbitrateUnlock and the first half of WaitProcessWideKeyAtomic: hand the mutex to its
 * best waiter (WAITERS_BIT kept if others still wait), or free it. */
static void release_lock(uint64_t mutex) {
    int n;
    KThread *next = first_waiter(WAIT_LOCK, mutex, &n);
    __atomic_store_n(u32p(mutex), next ? next->tag | (n > 1 ? WAITERS_BIT : 0) : 0, __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST);
    if (next) end_wait(next, R_OK);
}

static uint32_t arbitrate_lock(uint32_t owner, uint64_t mutex, uint32_t tag) {
```
