`runtime/src/mat4.h`:

```h
/* 4x4 float matrices as the game's shaders use them: row-major, out[i] = dot(row i, v). */
#ifndef YW4_MAT4_H
#define YW4_MAT4_H

#include <stdint.h>
#include <string.h>

typedef struct { float m[16]; } Mat4;

static inline Mat4 mat4_mul(const Mat4 *a, const Mat4 *b) {
    Mat4 r;
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++)
        for (int j = 0; j < 4; j++) {
            /* from the first product, not from 0: 0 + -0 would make a -0 of the game's +0 */
            float s = a->m[i * 4] * b->m[j];
            for (int k = 1; k < 4; k++) s += a->m[i * 4 + k] * b->m[k * 4 + j];
            r.m[i * 4 + j] = s;
        }
    return r;
}

/* 16 floats at a guest address */
static inline Mat4 mat4_load(uint64_t addr) {
    Mat4 r;
    memcpy(r.m, (const void *)(uintptr_t)addr, sizeof r.m);
    return r;
}

/* the largest difference between n floats, relative to the larger value (absolute below 1) */
static inline float mat4_diff(const float *a, const float *b, int n) {
    float worst = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        float d = a[i] - b[i], s = (a[i] < 0 ? -a[i] : a[i]) > 1 ? (a[i] < 0 ? -a[i] : a[i]) : 1;
        if (d < 0) d = -d;
        if (d / s > worst) worst = d / s;
    }
    return worst;
}

#endif

```

`runtime/src/memscan.c`:

```c
/* YW4_MEMSCAN=<value>@<frame>,<frame>,...: a memory search for finding a game value, as a cheat finder does (tests;
 * first use: the Crank-a-kai's spins left today, 2026-11-14). YW4_MEMSCAN=<value>@live: the samples are taken when
 * Insert or F8 is pressed instead (a player at the game: replays drift where the world's timing differs), and the list is
 * written after every press from the second on.
 *
 * At the first frame, every 2-byte and 4-byte number in the game's writable memory (heap, the modules' data) that
 * equals <value> is noted (aligned; 1-byte numbers are left out: the heap also holds textures and models, where a
 * byte of 30 is everywhere). At each later frame their values are read again. At the last frame the log lists the
 * ones that changed, most changes first, with each one's values over the frames:
 *
 *     yw4: memscan: 0x7012345678 u32: 30 30 29 29 28 27 ...
 *
 * Run it with a replay of the change (tools.dev.run --replay): the replay repeats the same frames. The game's threads
 * keep running while it reads, so a value read mid-write is possible (and harmless here). */
#include <inttypes.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "kernel.h"
#include "yw4load.h"


enum { MAX_FRAMES = 64, MAX_CANDIDATES = 8 << 20, SHOW = 60 };

typedef struct {
    uint64_t addr;
    uint8_t wide;  /* 1: u32, 0: u16 */
} Cand;

static int parsed, nframes, live, pending;
static uint64_t frames[MAX_FRAMES];
static int64_t value;
static Cand *cand;
static uint32_t *seen;  /* [candidate * MAX_FRAMES + frame index] */
static size_t ncand;

static void parse(void) {
    parsed = 1;
    const char *e = getenv("YW4_MEMSCAN");
    if (!e || !*e) return;
    char *end;
    value = strtoll(e, &end, 10);
    if (*end != '@') {
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: memscan: YW4_MEMSCAN=<value>@<frame>,<frame>,... expected\n");
        return;
    }
    if (!strcmp(end + 1, "live")) {
        live = 1;
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: memscan: press F8 (or Insert) to take a sample (the first finds the places holding %" PRId64 ")\n",
                value);
        return;
    }
    for (const char *p = end + 1; *p && nframes < MAX_FRAMES;) {
        unsigned long long f = strtoull(p, &end, 10);
        if (end == p) break;
        frames[nframes++] = f;
        p = *end == ',' ? end + 1 : end;
    }
}

static uint32_t read_at(const Cand *c) {
    const void *p = (const void *)(uintptr_t)c->addr;
    if (c->wide) { uint32_t v; memcpy(&v, p, 4); return v; }
    uint16_t v;
    memcpy(&v, p, 2);
    return v;
}

static void first_scan(void) {
    uint64_t addr[64], size[64];
    int n = yw4_memory_rw_regions(addr, size, 64);
    cand = malloc(sizeof *cand * MAX_CANDIDATES);
    if (!cand) return;
    uint64_t scanned = 0;
    for (int r = 0; r < n; r++) {
        const uint8_t *b = (const uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)addr[r];
        for (uint64_t o = 0; o + 4 <= size[r] && ncand < MAX_CANDIDATES; o += 2) {
            uint16_t h;
            memcpy(&h, b + o, 2);
            if (o % 4 == 0) {
                uint32_t w;
                memcpy(&w, b + o, 4);
                if ((int64_t)w == value) { cand[ncand++] = (Cand){addr[r] + o, 1}; continue; }
            }
            if ((int64_t)h == value && ncand < MAX_CANDIDATES) cand[ncand++] = (Cand){addr[r] + o, 0};
        }
        scanned += size[r];
    }
    seen = calloc(ncand ? ncand : 1, sizeof *seen * MAX_FRAMES);
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: memscan: %zu places hold %" PRId64 " in %d regions (%" PRIu64 " MiB)%s\n", ncand, value, n,
            scanned >> 20, ncand == MAX_CANDIDATES ? ": the list is full, later places left out" : "");
}

static int changes(size_t i) {
    int c = 0;
    for (int k = 1; k < nframes; k++) c += seen[i * MAX_FRAMES + k] != seen[i * MAX_FRAMES + k - 1];
    return c;
}

/* A counter: it changes, and only ever steps one way and stays near the value searched for (within 15), as a count of
 * things left or used does. Busy scratch memory changes far more often and jumps about. */
static int steady(size_t i) {
    const uint32_t *v = &seen[i * MAX_FRAMES];
    int down = 1, up = 1;
    for (int k = 0; k < nframes; k++) {
        if ((int64_t)v[k] > value + 15 || (int64_t)v[k] < value - 15) return 0;
        if (k && v[k] > v[k - 1]) down = 0;
        if (k && v[k] < v[k - 1]) up = 0;
    }
    return down || up;
}

static int by_steady_then_changes(const void *a, const void *b) {
    size_t x = *(const size_t *)a, y = *(const size_t *)b;
    if (steady(x) != steady(y)) return steady(y) - steady(x);
    return changes(y) - changes(x);
}

/* Live mode, a press after each change: the value never went up and every change was a step of exactly one (a crank),
 * at least two of them, staying within 15 of the value searched for. A press where it stayed the same doesn't spoil it:
 * the first live run (2026-11-15) lost the two places reading 30 29 28 at its fourth press, where neither went down. */
static int down_at_every_press(size_t i) {
    const uint32_t *v = &seen[i * MAX_FRAMES];
    int steps = 0;
    for (int k = 1; k < nframes; k++) {
        if (v[k] > v[k - 1] || (int64_t)v[k] < value - 15) return 0;
        if (v[k] < v[k - 1]) {
            if (v[k - 1] - v[k] != 1) return 0;
            steps++;
        }
    }
    return steps >= 2;
}

/* The places that read one step down at each of the first presses (from the third): their values at every later press,
 * whatever they do then, so a counter that stops changing (moved, or a press with no crank) still shows in the log. */
enum { MAX_SHORT = 16 };
static size_t shortlist[MAX_SHORT], nshort;

static void shortlist_report(void) {
    if (!nshort && nframes == 3)
        for (size_t i = 0; i < ncand && nshort < MAX_SHORT; i++) {
            const uint32_t *v = &seen[i * MAX_FRAMES];
            if (v[0] == (uint32_t)value && v[1] + 1 == v[0] && v[2] + 1 == v[1]) shortlist[nshort++] = i;
        }
    for (size_t j = 0; j < nshort; j++) {
        size_t i = shortlist[j];
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: memscan: shortlist %#" PRIx64 " %s:", cand[i].addr, cand[i].wide ? "u32" : "u16");
        for (int k = 0; k < nframes; k++) fprintf(stderr, " %u", seen[i * MAX_FRAMES + k]);
        fputc('\n', stderr);
    }
}

/* From the third press on: if exactly one place went down at every press, a write watch on it (kernel.c, host.c page
 * protection) logs every write with the guest function and its callers, with no limit: who changes it (leaving the
 * menu). Not the read watch: its 60 reports could all go to a reader every frame before the menu is left, and when
 * they run out it opens the page, which would end a write watch on the same page too. Every such place is listed. */
static void arm_when_found(void) {
    static int armed;
    if (nframes >= 3) shortlist_report();
    if (armed || nframes < 3) return;
    size_t found = 0, at = 0;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < ncand; i++)
        if (down_at_every_press(i)) {
            found++, at = i;
            fprintf(stderr, "yw4: memscan: down at every press: %#" PRIx64 " %s:", cand[i].addr, cand[i].wide ? "u32" : "u16");
            for (int k = 0; k < nframes; k++) fprintf(stderr, " %u", seen[i * MAX_FRAMES + k]);
            fputc('\n', stderr);
        }
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: memscan: %zu place(s) went down one at a time, never up\n", found);
    /* two is common (the first run: the menu's count and the saved one, it seems): one write watch at a time, so the
     * first of them; the other is in the list above */
    if (found < 1 || found > 2) return;
    if (found == 2)
        for (size_t i = 0; i < ncand; i++)
            if (down_at_every_press(i)) { at = i; break; }
    armed = 1;
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: memscan: the value is at %#" PRIx64 ": watching who writes it\n", cand[at].addr);
    yw4_write_watch_arm(cand[at].addr, cand[at].wide ? 4 : 2);
}

static void report(void) {
    size_t *idx = malloc(sizeof *idx * (ncand ? ncand : 1)), m = 0, nsteady = 0;
    if (!idx) return;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < ncand; i++)
        if (changes(i)) idx[m++] = i, nsteady += steady(i) != 0;
    qsort(idx, m, sizeof *idx, by_steady_then_changes);
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: memscan: %zu of them count steadily one way within 15 of %" PRId64 " (listed first)\n", nsteady,
            value);
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: memscan: %zu of %zu places changed over %d frames", m, ncand, nframes);
    for (int k = 0; k < nframes; k++) fprintf(stderr, "%s%" PRIu64, k ? "," : " (", frames[k]);
    fprintf(stderr, ")\n");
    for (size_t j = 0; j < m && j < SHOW; j++) {
        size_t i = idx[j];
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: memscan: %#" PRIx64 " %s:", cand[i].addr, cand[i].wide ? "u32" : "u16");
        for (int k = 0; k < nframes; k++) fprintf(stderr, " %u", seen[i * MAX_FRAMES + k]);
        fputc('\n', stderr);
    }
    free(idx);
}

/* "main+0x1234" for an address inside a module, else the address */
static void where(uint64_t a, char *out, size_t n) {
    for (size_t m = 0; m < yw4_nmodules; m++) {
        uint64_t b = *yw4_modules[m].base;
        if (a - b < yw4_modules[m].mem_size) {
            snprintf(out, n, "%s+%#" PRIx64, yw4_modules[m].name, a - b);
            return;
        }
    }
    snprintf(out, n, "%#" PRIx64, a);
}

/* YW4_PEEK=<addr>[,<addr>...]: each address's u32 in the log every 300 frames (is a value at the same place every
 * run?). YW4_PTRSCAN=<addr>@<frame>: at that frame, every 8-byte value in writable memory that points into the
 * 64 KiB below <addr> (the start of the object holding it), modules' data first: a fixed place in main's data that
 * leads to the value is how a cheat finds it in every run. */
static void peek_and_ptrscan(uint64_t frame) {
    static int read_env;
    static uint64_t peek[8], ptr_target, ptr_frame;
    static int npeek;
    if (!read_env) {
        read_env = 1;
        for (const char *p = getenv("YW4_PEEK"); p && *p && npeek < 8;) {
            char *end;
            peek[npeek] = strtoull(p, &end, 16);
            if (end == p) break;
            npeek++;
            p = *end == ',' ? end + 1 : end;
        }
        const char *e = getenv("YW4_PTRSCAN");
        if (e && *e) {
            char *end;
            ptr_target = strtoull(e, &end, 16);
            ptr_frame = *end == '@' ? strtoull(end + 1, NULL, 10) : 0;
        }
    }
    if (npeek && frame % 300 == 0)
        for (int i = 0; i < npeek; i++) {
            uint32_t v;
            memcpy(&v, (const void *)(uintptr_t)peek[i], 4);
            fprintf(stderr, "yw4: peek: frame %" PRIu64 ": %#" PRIx64 " = %u\n", frame, peek[i], v);
        }
    if (ptr_target && frame == ptr_frame) {
        uint64_t addr[64], size[64];
        int n = yw4_memory_rw_regions(addr, size, 64), shown = 0;
        uint64_t lo = ptr_target - 0x10000, hi = ptr_target;
        for (int pass = 0; pass < 2; pass++)  /* modules' data first, then the heap */
            for (int r = 0; r < n; r++) {
                char w[48];
                where(addr[r], w, sizeof w);
                int in_module = strchr(w, '+') != NULL;
                if (in_module != (pass == 0)) continue;
                const uint8_t *b = (const uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)addr[r];
                for (uint64_t o = 0; o + 8 <= size[r] && shown < 80; o += 8) {
                    uint64_t v;
                    memcpy(&v, b + o, 8);
                    if (v < lo || v > hi) continue;
                    char at[48];
                    where(addr[r] + o, at, sizeof at);
                    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: ptrscan: %s holds %#" PRIx64 " (target - %#" PRIx64 ")\n", at, v, ptr_target - v);
                    shown++;
                }
            }
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: ptrscan: %d pointer(s) into the 64 KiB below %#" PRIx64 "\n", shown, ptr_target);
    }
}

/* YW4_FINDBYTES=<hex bytes, ?? for any>[@<n>]: at an F8 / Insert press, every place in writable memory holding that
 * byte pattern is listed, and a write watch (every write, with the guest function and its callers) is put on the first
 * byte of match n (default 0). One watch per run: host.c's write watch can't be moved once armed. First use: the
 * Crank-a-kai's count, one byte in the save (2026-11-15): "?? 1e ?? 00 00 00 00 00 00 09" = count, the day's limit
 * (30), a byte that read 8, then the save's next bytes. */
static int find_pending;

static void find_bytes(void) {
    static int done;
    const char *e = getenv("YW4_FINDBYTES");
    if (done || !e || !*e) return;
    done = 1;
    uint8_t pat[64], any[64];
    int n = 0, pick = 0;
    for (const char *p = e; *p && *p != '@' && n < 64;) {
        if (*p == ' ' || *p == ',') { p++; continue; }
        if (p[0] == '?' && p[1] == '?') { any[n] = 1, pat[n++] = 0, p += 2; continue; }
        char hex[3] = {p[0], p[1] ? p[1] : 0, 0};
        any[n] = 0, pat[n++] = (uint8_t)strtoul(hex, NULL, 16);
        p += p[1] ? 2 : 1;
    }
    const char *at = strchr(e, '@');
    if (at) pick = atoi(at + 1);
    uint64_t addr[64], size[64], found[32];
    int nr = yw4_memory_rw_regions(addr, size, 64), nf = 0;
    for (int r = 0; r < nr; r++) {
        const uint8_t *b = (const uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)addr[r];
        for (uint64_t o = 0; o + (uint64_t)n <= size[r]; o++) {
            int k = 0;
            while (k < n && (any[k] || b[o + k] == pat[k])) k++;
            if (k < n) continue;
            if (nf < 32) found[nf] = addr[r] + o;
            nf++;
            char w[48];
            where(addr[r] + o, w, sizeof w);
            fprintf(stderr, "yw4: findbytes: match %d at %s:", nf - 1, w);
            for (int j = -4; j < n + 4; j++)  /* 4 bytes either side, inside the region */
                if ((int64_t)o + j >= 0 && o + j < size[r]) fprintf(stderr, " %02x", b[o + j]);
            fputc('\n', stderr);
        }
    }
    fprintf(stderr, "yw4: findbytes: %d match(es) for \"%s\"\n", nf, e);
    if (pick < nf && pick < 32) {
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: findbytes: watching writes to match %d, %#" PRIx64 "\n", pick, found[pick]);
        yw4_write_watch_arm(found[pick], (uint64_t)n);  /* the whole pattern: the value may sit after a context prefix */
    }
}

void yw4_memscan_key(void) {
    if (!parsed) parse();
    if (live) __atomic_store_n(&pending, 1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    __atomic_store_n(&find_pending, 1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
}

void yw4_memscan_frame(uint64_t frame) {
    if (__atomic_exchange_n(&find_pending, 0, __ATOMIC_ACQ_REL)) find_bytes();
    peek_and_ptrscan(frame);
    if (!parsed) parse();
    if (live) {
        if (!__atomic_exchange_n(&pending, 0, __ATOMIC_ACQ_REL) || nframes == MAX_FRAMES) return;
        int k = nframes++;
        frames[k] = frame;
        if (k == 0) first_scan();
        for (size_t i = 0; i < ncand; i++) seen[i * MAX_FRAMES + k] = read_at(&cand[i]);
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: memscan: sample %d at frame %" PRIu64 "\n", k + 1, frame);
        if (k) report(), arm_when_found();
        return;
    }
    for (int k = 0; k < nframes; k++) {
        if (frames[k] != frame) continue;
        if (k == 0) first_scan();
        for (size_t i = 0; i < ncand; i++) seen[i * MAX_FRAMES + k] = read_at(&cand[i]);
        if (k == nframes - 1) report();
    }
}

```

`runtime/src/modmerge.c`:

```c
/* Merging several mods' copies of one game data file (decision 0068).
 *
 * Two mods that ship the same file can't both be laid over the game: the later one's copy replaces the earlier
 * one's. For Level-5's .cfg.bin data files (items, shops, NPCs, ...) most mods change a few entries of a big list,
 * and different mods change different entries, so a merge against the game's own copy keeps all of them, the way
 * a three-way merge in version control does: each mod's copy is compared with the game's entry by entry (a Myers
 * diff), and every changed run of entries is taken from the mod that changed it. Two mods changing the same entries
 * is a real clash; then nothing is merged and the later mod's copy is used, as before.
 *
 * The game's copy is usually inside one of its CRI .cpk archives, so this file also reads those (the format notes
 * are in tools/yw4/cpk.py, which this follows).
 */
#include "modmerge.h"

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#define EMPTY 0xFFFFFFFFu

static void *xmalloc(size_t n) {
    void *p = malloc(n ? n : 1);
    if (!p) {
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: mods: out of memory\n");
        exit(3);
    }
    return p;
}

static uint32_t le32(const uint8_t *p) { return (uint32_t)p[0] | (uint32_t)p[1] << 8 | (uint32_t)p[2] << 16 | (uint32_t)p[3] << 24; }
static uint16_t be16(const uint8_t *p) { return (uint16_t)(p[0] << 8 | p[1]); }
static uint32_t be32(const uint8_t *p) { return (uint32_t)p[0] << 24 | (uint32_t)p[1] << 16 | (uint32_t)p[2] << 8 | p[3]; }
static uint64_t be64(const uint8_t *p) { return (uint64_t)be32(p) << 32 | be32(p + 4); }

/* ---- CRI .cpk archives: an @UTF table (big-endian) in the "CPK " header chunk gives TocOffset; the "TOC " chunk's
 * table lists DirName, FileName, FileSize (stored), ExtractSize, FileOffset (from the TOC chunk). */

typedef struct {
    const uint8_t *b;
    size_t n;
    uint32_t rows_off, str_off, nrows;
    uint16_t row_len;
    int ncols;
    struct {
        const char *name;
        uint8_t storage, type;
        size_t at;  /* the constant's place in b, or the value's place in a row */
    } cols[64];
} Utf;

static int utf_size(uint8_t type) {
    static const int sizes[12] = {1, 1, 2, 2, 4, 4, 8, 8, 4, 8, 4, 8};
    return type < 12 ? sizes[type] : -1;
}

static int utf_open(Utf *u, const uint8_t *b, size_t n) {
    if (n < 0x20 || memcmp(b, "@UTF", 4)) return -1;
    u->b = b, u->n = n;
    u->rows_off = be16(b + 10) + 8u, u->str_off = be32(b + 12) + 8u;
    u->ncols = be16(b + 24), u->row_len = be16(b + 26), u->nrows = be32(b + 28);
    if (u->ncols > 64 || u->str_off >= n || u->rows_off + (uint64_t)u->row_len * u->nrows > n) return -1;
    size_t pos = 0x20, row_at = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < u->ncols; i++) {
        if (pos + 5 > n) return -1;
        uint8_t flags = b[pos];
        uint32_t name = be32(b + pos + 1);
        pos += 5;
        if (u->str_off + name >= n || !memchr(b + u->str_off + name, 0, n - u->str_off - name)) return -1;
        u->cols[i].name = (const char *)b + u->str_off + name;
        u->cols[i].storage = flags & 0xF0, u->cols[i].type = flags & 0x0F;
        int sz = utf_size(u->cols[i].type);
        if (sz < 0) return -1;
        if (u->cols[i].storage == 0x30) {
            u->cols[i].at = pos;
            pos += (size_t)sz;
        } else if (u->cols[i].storage == 0x50) {
            u->cols[i].at = row_at;
            row_at += (size_t)sz;
        }
    }
    return row_at <= u->row_len ? 0 : -1;
}

/* A column's value in a row: *s for a string column, *v for a number; 0 if the column isn't there. */
static int utf_get(const Utf *u, uint32_t row, const char *name, uint64_t *v, const char **s) {
    for (int i = 0; i < u->ncols; i++) {
        if (strcmp(u->cols[i].name, name)) continue;
        size_t at;
        if (u->cols[i].storage == 0x30) at = u->cols[i].at;
        else if (u->cols[i].storage == 0x50) at = u->rows_off + (size_t)row * u->row_len + u->cols[i].at;
        else return 0;
        const uint8_t *p = u->b + at;
        switch (u->cols[i].type) {
        case 0: case 1: *v = p[0]; return 1;
        case 2: case 3: *v = be16(p); return 1;
        case 4: case 5: *v = be32(p); return 1;
        case 6: case 7: *v = be64(p); return 1;
        case 0xA: {
            uint32_t o = be32(p);
            if (u->str_off + o >= u->n || !memchr(u->b + u->str_off + o, 0, u->n - u->str_off - o)) return 0;
            *s = (const char *)u->b + u->str_off + o;
            return 1;
        }
        default: return 0;
        }
    }
    return 0;
}

static uint8_t *read_at(FILE *f, uint64_t at, size_t n) {
    uint8_t *b = xmalloc(n);
#ifdef _WIN32
    int bad = _fseeki64(f, (long long)at, SEEK_SET);
#else
    int bad = fseeko(f, (off_t)at, SEEK_SET);
#endif
    if (bad || fread(b, 1, n, f) != n) {
        free(b);
        return NULL;
    }
    return b;
}

/* A chunk ("CPK ", "TOC "): 16-byte head with the table's size at +8, the @UTF table after it. */
static uint8_t *read_chunk(FILE *f, uint64_t at, const char *magic, size_t *n) {
    uint8_t *head = read_at(f, at, 16);
    if (!head) return NULL;
    uint64_t size = (uint64_t)le32(head + 8) | (uint64_t)le32(head + 12) << 32;
    int ok = !memcmp(head, magic, 4) && size >= 0x20 && size < (1u << 30);
    free(head);
    if (!ok) return NULL;
    *n = (size_t)size;
    return read_at(f, at + 16, (size_t)size);
}

/* CRILAYLA: the first 0x100 output bytes stored raw; the rest an LZ stream read backwards, bits MSB first, output
 * written from the end; flag 0 = an 8-bit literal, 1 = a 13-bit distance (+3) and a length 3 + 2,3,5,8,8...-bit
 * fields while a field is all ones. */
static uint8_t *crilayla(const uint8_t *src, size_t n, size_t *out_n) {
    if (n < 16 || memcmp(src, "CRILAYLA", 8)) return NULL;
    uint32_t size = le32(src + 8), prefix = le32(src + 12);
    if ((uint64_t)prefix + 0x110 > n) return NULL;
    size_t total = (size_t)size + 0x100;
    uint8_t *out = xmalloc(total);
    memcpy(out, src + 0x10 + prefix, 0x100);
    int64_t pos = (int64_t)0x10 + prefix - 1;
    unsigned cur = 0, left = 0;
    int bad = 0;
#define BITS(nbits, v)                                                         \
    do {                                                                       \
        unsigned n_ = (nbits);                                                 \
        (v) = 0;                                                               \
        while (n_) {                                                           \
            if (!left) {                                                       \
                if (pos < 0x10) { bad = 1; break; }                            \
                cur = src[pos--], left = 8;                                    \
            }                                                                  \
            unsigned t_ = n_ < left ? n_ : left;                               \
            (v) = ((v) << t_) | ((cur >> (left - t_)) & ((1u << t_) - 1));     \
            left -= t_, n_ -= t_;                                              \
        }                                                                      \
    } while (0)
    int64_t w = (int64_t)total - 1;
    while (w >= 0x100 && !bad) {
        unsigned flag;
        BITS(1, flag);
        if (bad) break;
        if (flag) {
            unsigned back, v;
            BITS(13, back);
            back += 3;
            unsigned length = 3;
            static const unsigned widths[3] = {2, 3, 5};
            int more = 1;
            for (int i = 0; i < 3 && more; i++) {
                BITS(widths[i], v);
                length += v;
                more = v == (1u << widths[i]) - 1;
            }
            while (more && !bad) {
                BITS(8, v);
                length += v;
                more = v == 0xFF;
            }
            for (unsigned i = 0; i < length && w >= 0x100; i++, w--) {
                if ((uint64_t)w + back >= total) { bad = 1; break; }
                out[w] = out[w + back];
            }
        } else {
            unsigned v;
            BITS(8, v);
            out[w--] = (uint8_t)v;
        }
    }
#undef BITS
    if (bad) {
        free(out);
        return NULL;
    }
    *out_n = total;
    return out;
}

uint8_t *cpk_read_file(const char *cpk_path, const char *inner_path, size_t *n) {
    FILE *f = fopen(cpk_path, "rb");
    if (!f) return NULL;
    uint8_t *result = NULL, *hb = NULL, *tb = NULL;
    size_t hn = 0, tn = 0;
    Utf h, t;
    uint64_t toc = 0;
    const char *s = NULL;
    if (!(hb = read_chunk(f, 0, "CPK ", &hn)) || utf_open(&h, hb, hn) || !utf_get(&h, 0, "TocOffset", &toc, &s) || !toc)
        goto done;
    if (!(tb = read_chunk(f, toc, "TOC ", &tn)) || utf_open(&t, tb, tn)) goto done;
    for (uint32_t r = 0; r < t.nrows; r++) {
        const char *dir = "", *name = "";
        uint64_t stored = 0, extract = 0, off = 0, v = 0;
        utf_get(&t, r, "DirName", &v, &dir);
        if (!utf_get(&t, r, "FileName", &v, &name)) continue;
        size_t dl = strlen(dir);
        if (dl ? strncmp(inner_path, dir, dl) || inner_path[dl] != '/' || strcmp(inner_path + dl + 1, name)
               : strcmp(inner_path, name))
            continue;
        utf_get(&t, r, "FileSize", &stored, &s);
        utf_get(&t, r, "ExtractSize", &extract, &s);
        utf_get(&t, r, "FileOffset", &off, &s);
        if (!stored || stored > (1u << 30) || extract > (1u << 30)) break;
        uint8_t *data = read_at(f, toc + off, (size_t)stored);
        if (!data) break;
        if (extract && extract != stored) {
            size_t got = 0;
            uint8_t *raw = crilayla(data, (size_t)stored, &got);
            free(data);
            if (!raw || got != extract) {
                free(raw);
                break;
            }
            data = raw, stored = extract;
        }
        result = data, *n = (size_t)stored;
        break;
    }
done:
    free(hb);
    free(tb);
    fclose(f);
    return result;
}

/* ---- Level-5 .cfg.bin: u32 entry count, string table offset, its size, its string count; the entries (u32 name
 * crc, u8 value count, 2-bit value types four to a byte (0 string, 1 int, 2 float), 0xFF to a 4-byte boundary, u32
 * values; a string is an offset into the table, 0xFFFFFFFF for none); 0xFF to 16; the strings, each once, in the
 * order the entries first use them; 0xFF to 16; then the entry names' table (kept as it is). Measured on the
 * game's 2.2.0 files: a file written back this way is byte-for-byte the game's (cfgbin_rewrite, the check). */

typedef struct {
    uint32_t crc;
    uint8_t k;
    const uint8_t *types, *vals;  /* in the file it came from */
    const char *st;               /* that file's string table */
    uint64_t h;
} Ent;

typedef struct {
    Ent *e;
    uint32_t count;
    const uint8_t *tail;
    size_t ntail;
} Cfg;

static unsigned vtype(const Ent *e, unsigned i) { return (e->types[i / 4] >> (2 * (i % 4))) & 3; }

static uint64_t fnv(uint64_t h, const void *p, size_t n) {
    const uint8_t *b = p;
    while (n--) h = (h ^ *b++) * 1099511628211ull;
    return h;
}

static int cfg_parse(const uint8_t *b, size_t n, Cfg *c) {
    memset(c, 0, sizeof *c);
    if (n < 16) return -1;
    uint32_t count = le32(b), st_off = le32(b + 4), st_len = le32(b + 8);
    if (st_off > n || st_len > n - st_off || count > n / 8) return -1;
    const char *st = (const char *)b + st_off;
    c->e = xmalloc(sizeof *c->e * (count ? count : 1));
    size_t p = 16;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        if (p + 5 > st_off) goto bad;
        Ent *e = &c->e[i];
        e->crc = le32(b + p), e->k = b[p + 4], e->st = st;
        p += 5;
        size_t tl = (e->k + 3u) / 4;
        if (p + tl > st_off) goto bad;
        e->types = b + p;
        p = (p + tl + 3) & ~(size_t)3;
        if (p + 4u * e->k > st_off) goto bad;
        e->vals = b + p;
        p += 4u * e->k;
        uint64_t h = fnv(1469598103934665603ull, &e->crc, 4);
        h = fnv(h, &e->k, 1);
        for (unsigned j = 0; j < e->k; j++) {
            unsigned t = vtype(e, j);
            uint32_t v = le32(e->vals + 4 * j);
            h = fnv(h, &t, sizeof t);
            if (t == 0 && v != EMPTY) {
                if (v >= st_len || !memchr(st + v, 0, st_len - v)) goto bad;
                h = fnv(h, st + v, strlen(st + v) + 1);
            } else {
                h = fnv(h, &v, 4);
            }
        }
        e->h = h;
    }
    size_t tail = ((size_t)st_off + st_len + 15) & ~(size_t)15;
    c->count = count;
    c->tail = b + (tail < n ? tail : n), c->ntail = tail < n ? n - tail : 0;
    return 0;
bad:
    free(c->e);
    c->e = NULL;
    return -1;
}

static int ent_eq(const Ent *a, const Ent *b) {
    if (a->h != b->h || a->crc != b->crc || a->k != b->k) return 0;
    for (unsigned j = 0; j < a->k; j++) {
        unsigned t = vtype(a, j);
        if (t != vtype(b, j)) return 0;
        uint32_t x = le32(a->vals + 4 * j), y = le32(b->vals + 4 * j);
        if (t == 0 && x != EMPTY && y != EMPTY) {
            if (strcmp(a->st + x, b->st + y)) return 0;
        } else if (x != y) {
            return 0;
        }
    }
    return 1;
}

typedef struct {
    uint8_t *b;
    size_t n, cap;
} Buf;

static void put(Buf *o, const void *p, size_t n) {
    if (o->n + n > o->cap) {
        while (o->n + n > o->cap) o->cap = o->cap ? 2 * o->cap : 4096;
        uint8_t *nb = realloc(o->b, o->cap);
        if (!nb) {
            fprintf(stderr, "yw4: mods: out of memory\n");
            exit(3);
        }
        o->b = nb;
    }
    memcpy(o->b + o->n, p, n);
    o->n += n;
}
static void put32(Buf *o, uint32_t v) {
    uint8_t b[4] = {(uint8_t)v, (uint8_t)(v >> 8), (uint8_t)(v >> 16), (uint8_t)(v >> 24)};
    put(o, b, 4);
}
static void pad(Buf *o, size_t to) {
    static const uint8_t ff = 0xFF;
    while (o->n % to) put(o, &ff, 1);
}

typedef struct {
    const char *str;
    uint32_t off;
} Str;

/* Writes entries (from any of the parsed files) as one file, with the strings laid out anew. */
static uint8_t *cfg_write(const Ent *e, size_t count, const uint8_t *tail, size_t ntail, size_t *out_n) {
    Buf o = {0}, s = {0};
    uint8_t zero[16] = {0};
    put(&o, zero, 16);
    size_t cap = 64;
    while (cap < 4 * count) cap <<= 1;
    Str *tab = calloc(cap, sizeof *tab);
    if (!tab) exit(3);
    uint32_t nstr = 0;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        const Ent *x = &e[i];
        put32(&o, x->crc);
        put(&o, &x->k, 1);
        put(&o, x->types, (x->k + 3u) / 4);
        pad(&o, 4);
        for (unsigned j = 0; j < x->k; j++) {
            uint32_t v = le32(x->vals + 4 * j);
            if (vtype(x, j) == 0 && v != EMPTY) {
                const char *str = x->st + v;
                size_t h = (size_t)fnv(1469598103934665603ull, str, strlen(str)) & (cap - 1);
                while (tab[h].str && strcmp(tab[h].str, str)) h = (h + 1) & (cap - 1);
                if (!tab[h].str) {
                    if (nstr + 1 > cap / 2) {  /* keep the table at most half full: grow it */
                        size_t ncap = cap * 2;
                        Str *nt = calloc(ncap, sizeof *tab);
                        if (!nt) exit(3);
                        for (size_t q = 0; q < cap; q++) {
                            if (!tab[q].str) continue;
                            size_t g = (size_t)fnv(1469598103934665603ull, tab[q].str, strlen(tab[q].str)) & (ncap - 1);
                            while (nt[g].str) g = (g + 1) & (ncap - 1);
                            nt[g] = tab[q];
                        }
                        free(tab);
                        tab = nt, cap = ncap;
                        h = (size_t)fnv(1469598103934665603ull, str, strlen(str)) & (cap - 1);
                        while (tab[h].str) h = (h + 1) & (cap - 1);
                    }
                    tab[h].str = str, tab[h].off = (uint32_t)s.n;
                    put(&s, str, strlen(str) + 1);
                    nstr++;
                }
                v = tab[h].off;
            }
            put32(&o, v);
        }
    }
    pad(&o, 16);
    uint32_t st_off = (uint32_t)o.n, st_len = (uint32_t)s.n;
    if (s.n) put(&o, s.b, s.n);
    if (ntail) {
        pad(&o, 16);
        put(&o, tail, ntail);
    }
    uint32_t head[4] = {(uint32_t)count, st_off, st_len, nstr};
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
        uint8_t *p = o.b + 4 * i;
        p[0] = (uint8_t)head[i], p[1] = (uint8_t)(head[i] >> 8), p[2] = (uint8_t)(head[i] >> 16), p[3] = (uint8_t)(head[i] >> 24);
    }
    free(tab);
    free(s.b);
    *out_n = o.n;
    return o.b;
}

uint8_t *cfgbin_rewrite(const uint8_t *b, size_t n, size_t *out_n) {
    Cfg c;
    if (cfg_parse(b, n, &c)) return NULL;
    uint8_t *r = cfg_write(c.e, c.count, c.tail, c.ntail, out_n);
    free(c.e);
    return r;
}

/* ---- the diff: runs of base entries [i1, i2) a mod replaced with its entries [j1, j2) (an insert when i1 == i2) */

typedef struct {
    uint32_t i1, i2, j1, j2;
    int mod;
} Hunk;

typedef struct {
    Hunk *h;
    size_t n, cap;
} Hunks;

static void add_hunk(Hunks *hs, Hunk h) {
    if (hs->n == hs->cap) {
        hs->cap = hs->cap ? 2 * hs->cap : 64;
        Hunk *nh = realloc(hs->h, sizeof *nh * hs->cap);
        if (!nh) exit(3);
        hs->h = nh;
    }
    hs->h[hs->n++] = h;
}

enum { MAX_EDITS = 6000 };  /* more changes than this in one file: not merged (keeps the diff's memory small) */

/* Myers' O((N+M)D) diff of a[0..n) against b[0..m), after the common start and end are taken off. */
static int diff(const Ent *a, uint32_t n, const Ent *b, uint32_t m, int mod, Hunks *out) {
    uint32_t p = 0;
    while (p < n && p < m && ent_eq(&a[p], &b[p])) p++;
    uint32_t s = 0;
    while (s < n - p && s < m - p && ent_eq(&a[n - 1 - s], &b[m - 1 - s])) s++;
    const Ent *A = a + p, *B = b + p;
    int N = (int)(n - p - s), M = (int)(m - p - s);
    if (!N && !M) return 0;
    int max = N + M < MAX_EDITS ? N + M : MAX_EDITS;
    int *v = xmalloc(sizeof *v * (size_t)(2 * max + 3));
    int **trace = xmalloc(sizeof *trace * (size_t)(max + 1));
    int off = max + 1, D = -1;
    v[off + 1] = 0;
    for (int d = 0; d <= max && D < 0; d++) {
        for (int k = -d; k <= d; k += 2) {
            int x = (k == -d || (k != d && v[off + k - 1] < v[off + k + 1])) ? v[off + k + 1] : v[off + k - 1] + 1;
            int y = x - k;
            while (x < N && y < M && ent_eq(&A[x], &B[y])) x++, y++;
            v[off + k] = x;
            if (x >= N && y >= M) D = d;
        }
        trace[d] = xmalloc(sizeof(int) * (size_t)(2 * d + 1));
        for (int k = -d; k <= d; k++) trace[d][k + d] = v[off + k];
        if (D >= 0) break;
    }
    int ok = D >= 0;
    if (ok) {
        /* walk back from the end: each step is one deleted entry of A or one inserted entry of B */
        typedef struct { int x, y, del; } Op;
        Op *ops = xmalloc(sizeof *ops * (size_t)(D + 1));
        int nops = 0, x = N, y = M;
        for (int d = D; d > 0; d--) {
            int k = x - y;
            const int *pv = trace[d - 1];
#define PV(kk) pv[(kk) + (d - 1)]
            int down = k == -d || (k != d && PV(k - 1) < PV(k + 1));
            int pk = down ? k + 1 : k - 1;
            int px = PV(pk), py = px - pk;
#undef PV
            int mx = down ? px : px + 1, my = down ? py + 1 : py;  /* the point right after this step's edit */
            while (x > mx && y > my) x--, y--;                      /* the equal run after it */
            ops[nops++] = down ? (Op){px, py, 0} : (Op){px, py, 1};
            x = px, y = py;
        }
        Hunk cur = {0, 0, 0, 0, mod};
        int open = 0;
        for (int i = nops - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
            Op o = ops[i];
            if (open && (uint32_t)o.x == cur.i2 && (uint32_t)o.y == cur.j2) {
                if (o.del) cur.i2++; else cur.j2++;
                continue;
            }
            if (open) add_hunk(out, (Hunk){cur.i1 + p, cur.i2 + p, cur.j1 + p, cur.j2 + p, mod});
            cur = (Hunk){(uint32_t)o.x, (uint32_t)o.x + (o.del ? 1u : 0u), (uint32_t)o.y, (uint32_t)o.y + (o.del ? 0u : 1u), mod};
            open = 1;
        }
        if (open) add_hunk(out, (Hunk){cur.i1 + p, cur.i2 + p, cur.j1 + p, cur.j2 + p, mod});
        free(ops);
    }
    for (int d = 0; d <= (D >= 0 ? D : max); d++) free(trace[d]);
    free(trace);
    free(v);
    return ok ? 0 : -1;
}

/* Two mods' changes collide: they share base entries, or one inserts inside the other's run (an insert at the
 * edge of a run is fine: it goes before the run). Two inserts at one place collide too (which goes first?). */
static int collide(const Hunk *a, const Hunk *b) {
    int ea = a->i1 == a->i2, eb = b->i1 == b->i2;
    if (!ea && !eb) return (a->i1 > b->i1 ? a->i1 : b->i1) < (a->i2 < b->i2 ? a->i2 : b->i2);
    if (ea && eb) return a->i1 == b->i1;
    const Hunk *ins = ea ? a : b, *run = ea ? b : a;
    return run->i1 < ins->i1 && ins->i1 < run->i2;
}

static int by_place(const void *x, const void *y) {
    const Hunk *a = x, *b = y;
    if (a->i1 != b->i1) return a->i1 < b->i1 ? -1 : 1;
    if (a->i2 != b->i2) return a->i2 < b->i2 ? -1 : 1;  /* an insert before the run that starts there */
    return a->mod - b->mod;
}

uint8_t *cfgbin_merge(const uint8_t *base, size_t nbase, const uint8_t *const *mods, const size_t *nmod, int nmods,
                      size_t *out_n, int *clash_a, int *clash_b) {
    *clash_a = *clash_b = -1;
    if (nmods < 1) return NULL;
    Cfg bc, *mc = xmalloc(sizeof *mc * (size_t)nmods);
    int parsed = 0, ok = !cfg_parse(base, nbase, &bc);
    Hunks hs = {0};
    uint8_t *result = NULL;
    for (int i = 0; ok && i < nmods; i++) {
        ok = !cfg_parse(mods[i], nmod[i], &mc[i]);
        if (!ok) break;
        parsed++;
        /* the entry names' table: a mod that added new kinds of entries can't be merged into the game's */
        ok = mc[i].ntail == bc.ntail && !memcmp(mc[i].tail, bc.tail, bc.ntail) && !diff(bc.e, bc.count, mc[i].e, mc[i].count, i, &hs);
    }
    if (ok) {
        qsort(hs.h, hs.n, sizeof *hs.h, by_place);
        for (size_t i = 0; i < hs.n && ok; i++)
            for (size_t j = i + 1; j < hs.n && hs.h[j].i1 <= hs.h[i].i2 && ok; j++)
                if (hs.h[i].mod != hs.h[j].mod && collide(&hs.h[i], &hs.h[j])) {
                    ok = 0;
                    *clash_a = hs.h[i].mod < hs.h[j].mod ? hs.h[i].mod : hs.h[j].mod;
                    *clash_b = hs.h[i].mod < hs.h[j].mod ? hs.h[j].mod : hs.h[i].mod;
                }
        if (ok) {
            size_t total = bc.count;
            for (size_t i = 0; i < hs.n; i++) total += (hs.h[i].j2 - hs.h[i].j1), total -= (hs.h[i].i2 - hs.h[i].i1);
            Ent *e = xmalloc(sizeof *e * (total ? total : 1));
            size_t w = 0;
            uint32_t pos = 0;
            for (size_t i = 0; i < hs.n; i++) {
                const Hunk *h = &hs.h[i];
                while (pos < h->i1) e[w++] = bc.e[pos++];
                for (uint32_t j = h->j1; j < h->j2; j++) e[w++] = mc[h->mod].e[j];
                pos = h->i2;
            }
            while (pos < bc.count) e[w++] = bc.e[pos++];
            result = cfg_write(e, w, bc.tail, bc.ntail, out_n);
            free(e);
        }
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < parsed; i++) free(mc[i].e);
    free(mc);
    free(bc.e);
    free(hs.h);
    return result;
}
```

`runtime/src/modmerge.h`:

```h
/* Merging several mods' copies of one game data file (decision 0068). */
#ifndef YW4_MODMERGE_H
#define YW4_MODMERGE_H

#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>

/* One file out of a CRI .cpk archive (the game's archives: names in a TOC, CRILAYLA compression), by its full path
 * as the archive lists it ("data/common/gamedata/item/item_config_0.13.66.cfg.bin"). malloc'd, NULL if not there. */
uint8_t *cpk_read_file(const char *cpk_path, const char *inner_path, size_t *n);

/* Level-5 .cfg.bin files: base = the game's copy, mods[0..nmods) the mods' copies in load order. Every entry a mod
 * changed, added or removed against the base is kept, from every mod. Returns the merged file (malloc'd), or NULL
 * when it can't be merged: two mods change the same entries (*clash_a, *clash_b: their indices), or a copy isn't a
 * cfg.bin this code understands (both -1). */
uint8_t *cfgbin_merge(const uint8_t *base, size_t nbase, const uint8_t *const *mods, const size_t *nmod, int nmods,
                      size_t *out_n, int *clash_a, int *clash_b);

/* The file written back from its own entries, for the self-check: equal to the input when the writer is right. */
uint8_t *cfgbin_rewrite(const uint8_t *b, size_t n, size_t *out_n);

#endif
```

`runtime/src/mousemenu.c`:

```c
/* The mouse in the game's menus: the Yo-kai Pad (the X menu's 4 x 3 icon grid) and the pages it opens.
 *
 * The Switch game has no touch or mouse input, but every menu (yw::CMenuCursor and the 68 yw::CMenu* classes
 * built on it) still has the PC build's virtual methods, and menu events reach them through one queue
 * (f_9ed590 -> the menu's handler f_6dc700). Hooks on five of them (overrides.toml; this = the menu) tell us
 * what the Pad (yw::CMainMenu) and the pages it opens do:
 *   - OnChangeFocus (slot 40, f_6c68f0; x1 -> u32 hash of the control whose focus moved): a menu opened or its
 *     focus moved. f_9f3e90(menu, hash, 0) finds the control; for non-scrolling grids its u16 at +0x13c is the
 *     focused slot. For scrolling lists (lives::CMenuListView, pointed to by the list-view container control's
 *     +0x118), +0x11c is the selected row in the full list, (+0x114) + (+0xb0) is the top visible row on screen
 *     (+0x114 is the ring buffer's top slot and +0xb0 is its top buffer row count), and +0x128 is the total item
 *     count, so the focused visible row on screen is (+0x11c) - ((+0x114) + (+0xb0)).
 *   - OnBack (slot 27, f_6c59f0): B closed the whole Pad (or a sub-page that handles its own B).
 *   - OnDecideFocus (slot 42, f_6c6ba0): an item or icon was chosen; a page or sub-dialog usually opens over the
 *     current screen.
 *   - OnOpenEndLayer / OnCloseEndLayer (slots 31 / 32, f_6c5fa0 / f_6c6040): one of the menu's layers finished
 *     opening / closing. They balance (69 each for the whole Pad, 4 each for the Members popup, 12-42 each for
 *     sub-pages), so a screen is in front again when, after a choice, the count of open layers has gone up and
 *     come back to what it was then (deeper pages keep it up).
 * The hooks only set state; the window's thread shows the cursor while the Pad is open and turns the mouse into
 * the menu's own inputs: while a known screen is in front, hovering an item/icon steps the focus there with D-pad
 * presses (one at a time, each checked against the focus the screen then has), a left click moves there and
 * presses A, the scroll wheel steps one row up or down per notch in lists (or L/R on the Pad grid to cycle between
 * Pages 1 and 2), and a right click presses B anywhere in the Pad. So the game runs its normal paths: sounds,
 * animations, page changes. A press lasts until the game has read the input twice (window_input_reads), so a
 * stall can't swallow it.
 *
 * Positions are measured in the 1280 x 720 menu space (the 16:9 middle of the picture, the menus stay 16:9 at
 * any aspect ratio). YW4_MOUSE_MENUS=0 turns it off; YW4_MOUSE_LOG=1 logs menu focus, decision and layer hooks. */
#include <math.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include <SDL3/SDL.h>

#include "mousemenu.h"
#include "window.h"
#include "yw4rt.h"

#define PAD_GRID_HASH 0x6098c54du
#define PAD_VTABLE 0x14c0a88u  /* yw::CMainMenu's vtable (address point), main-relative */

enum { BTN_A = 1 << 0, BTN_B = 1 << 1, BTN_L = 1 << 6, BTN_R = 1 << 7, BTN_LEFT = 1 << 12, BTN_UP = 1 << 13, BTN_RIGHT = 1 << 14, BTN_DOWN = 1 << 15 };
enum { PAGE_NONE, PAGE_OPENING, PAGE_OPEN };  /* a page over the active screen: none, chosen but not open yet, open */
enum { SCR_HOVER = 1 << 0, SCR_CLICK = 1 << 1, SCR_WHEEL = 1 << 2 };

typedef struct {
    const char *name;
    uint32_t vtable;       /* main-relative vtable address point of the menu class */
    uint32_t hash;         /* control hash passed to OnChangeFocus when selection moves */
    uint32_t lv_hash;      /* list-view container control hash (ctrl+0x118 -> lives::CMenuListView), or 0 */
    int cols, rows;        /* visible columns and rows on screen */
    float x0, y0, dx, dy;  /* first slot's centre (x0, y0) and step (dx, dy) in 1280 x 720 menu space */
    float hw, hh;          /* half-width and half-height of each slot's hit box in 1280 x 720 menu space */
    unsigned flags;        /* SCR_* */
} Screen;

/* Measured in the 1280 x 720 menu space from screenshots and OnChangeFocus logs (decision 0057). */

    /* Soulmate 8-row scrolling list (yw::CMenuKonkatsuList) */
    {"soulmate",         0x14c0498u, 0x933f4e58u, 0x596edf43u, 1, 8, 288.5f, 191.5f,   0.0f, 58.65f, 222.0f,  27.5f, SCR_HOVER | SCR_CLICK | SCR_WHEEL},
    /* Watch Skills 6-character row (its own class, vt main+0x14c6b78, focus hash 0x5b8ae332; the old row had the
     * News notice's class and hash). Characters measured 2026-11-16 at x about 144, 264, 384, 504, 640, 744, y 200 .. 640. */
    {"watch_skills",     0x14c6b78u, 0x5b8ae332u, 0,           6, 1, 144.0f, 420.0f, 120.0f,   0.0f,  60.0f, 220.0f, SCR_HOVER | SCR_CLICK},
    /* Organize Members "What will you do?" 6-row action popup (yw::CMenuSubWindow) */
    {"members_action",   0x14c7b78u, 0xb2869aecu, 0,           1, 6, 519.6f, 268.0f,   0.0f,  48.0f, 103.6f,  20.0f, SCR_HOVER | SCR_CLICK},
};
enum { NSCREENS = sizeof screens / sizeof *screens };

/* Watch Skills (vt main+0x14c6b78): LEFT and RIGHT move the character highlight, but the game does not report that move
 * through OnChangeFocus (control 0x5b8ae332 keeps focus index 0; replay runs Q and R on 2026-11-16: screenshots show the
 * highlight move Cole -> Summer -> Hammy -> ...). So the mouse keeps its own count: 0 when the screen opens from the Pad,
 * +1 for each RIGHT and -1 for each LEFT the mouse sends. Presses by the player's keys are not counted. */
#define WATCH_SKILLS_VTABLE 0x14c6b78u
static int wsk_index;         /* the character highlighted on Watch Skills, by the mouse's count */

/* Written by the hooks (the game's threads), read by the window's thread. */
static int pad_open;          /* the Pad (or a page it opened) is on screen */
static int active_idx = -1;   /* index in screens[] currently active, or -1 */
static uint64_t active_menu;  /* menu object pointer of the active screen */
static uint64_t active_ctrl;  /* control pointer for active_screen->hash */
static uint64_t active_lv;    /* lives::CMenuListView pointer for active_screen->lv_hash, or 0 */
static int layers_open;       /* open layers on active_menu */
static int page;              /* PAGE_* */
static int page_base;         /* layers_open when an item/icon was chosen on active_menu */
static uint64_t page_since;   /* SDL ticks of the choice */
static int wheel_steps;       /* queued wheel notches (+ up, - down) from the window thread */

static int enabled(void) {
    static int e = -1;
    if (e < 0) {
        const char *v = getenv("YW4_MOUSE_MENUS");
        e = !(v && *v == '0');
    }
    return e;
}

static int script_on(void) {
    static int on = -1;
    if (on < 0) on = getenv("YW4_MOUSE_SCRIPT") && *getenv("YW4_MOUSE_SCRIPT");
    return on;
}

static int menu_log_on(void) {
    static int on = -1;
    if (on < 0) {
        const char *v = getenv("YW4_MOUSE_LOG");
        on = (v && *v != '0') || script_on();
    }
    return on;
}

int mousemenu_open(void) {
    return enabled() && __atomic_load_n(&pad_open, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
}

/* Conversations (owner, 2026-11-15): the talk window is one menu class for the whole conversation (its text pages
 * one-item controls, a choice list a control of N items, hash 0xac75395 for Eyepo's three); the field's HUD menu
 * focuses and reopens its layers when the conversation ends (seen with YW4_MOUSE_LOG at a save point). */
#define TALK_VTABLE 0x14c8598u
#define FIELD_HUD_VTABLE 0x14c5698u
static int talking;
int mousemenu_talking(void) { return enabled() && __atomic_load_n(&talking, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE); }

/* The map (its menu class, vt main+0x14c14f8, opened as SceneMenu ee2d9d06; seen 2026-11-15): open from its first
 * focus until the field's HUD comes back, as a conversation. The left stick pans it, the right stick zooms. */
#define MAP_VTABLE 0x14c14f8u
static int map_shown;
static uint64_t map_event_ms;  /* the map's last focus, back or layer (SDL ticks) */
int mousemenu_map(void) { return enabled() && __atomic_load_n(&map_shown, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE); }

/* The field HUD's shortcut cross was updated (shortcutwheel.c's hook): the field is back. Mirapo's list is this map
 * class too, and backed out of (B twice) the field's HUD menu doesn't focus again, so the map stayed "shown" and the
 * shortcut wheel never opened again (owner, 2026-11-16). The cross isn't updated while the map is up; half a second
 * after the map's last event, so an update just as it opens doesn't count. */
/* Naviwoof Guide (vt main+0x14c2df8, seen 2026-11-16): a row of pins, left and right; the row is one control, so
 * moving along it focuses nothing. Up from its first focus until it is backed out of or the field is back; while up
 * the mouse's wheel steps left and right, its clicks confirm and go back (bindings.c; owner, 2026-11-16). */
#define NAVIWOOF_VTABLE 0x14c2df8u
static int naviwoof;
static uint64_t naviwoof_ms;
int mousemenu_naviwoof(void) { return enabled() && __atomic_load_n(&naviwoof, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE); }

void mousemenu_field_hud_seen(void) {
    uint64_t now = SDL_GetTicks();
    if (__atomic_load_n(&naviwoof, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) && now - __atomic_load_n(&naviwoof_ms, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) >= 500) {
        __atomic_store_n(&naviwoof, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
        if (menu_log_on()) fprintf(stderr, "yw4: menu: Naviwoof Guide gone (the field's HUD is updated again)\n");
    }
    if (!__atomic_load_n(&map_shown, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)) return;
    if (now - __atomic_load_n(&map_event_ms, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) < 500) return;
    __atomic_store_n(&map_shown, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    if (menu_log_on()) fprintf(stderr, "yw4: menu: map gone (the field's HUD is updated again)\n");
}

/* The battle's Stopwatching menu (Pin / Items / Switch Members, vt main+0x14c6e58) and the pages it opens (Switch
 * Members, vt main+0x14c7028, a grid six wide; Items, vt main+0x14c73c8): up while the last menu focus was one of
 * them (or a Yes / No box over them); the fight's own menus focus as soon as it goes on. Seen 2026-11-15. Two rules
 * failed first (the owner: after an item, the clicks stayed the menu's): "until the menu closes a layer while in
 * front" (other menus focus first) and "until the fight's HUD focuses" (the menu's list focuses again after it); its
 * layer counts don't balance either. While up the clicks confirm and go back (bindings.c); the wheel already moves
 * it. */
#define STOPWATCH_VTABLE 0x14c6e58u
#define STOPWATCH_MEMBERS_VTABLE 0x14c7028u
#define STOPWATCH_ITEMS_VTABLE 0x14c73c8u
#define STOPWATCH_LIST_HASH 0xbd8d7086u  /* Pin / Items / Switch Members */
#define BATTLE_START_HASH 0xa4f85585u    /* the battle's start: Start Battle / Stopwatching (same class) */
static int stopwatch;
static uint64_t stopwatch_off_at;  /* SDL ms: when a focus outside it turns it off, unless it focuses again first */
int mousemenu_stopwatch(void) {
    if (!enabled()) return 0;
    uint64_t at = __atomic_load_n(&stopwatch_off_at, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
    if (at && SDL_GetTicks() >= at) {
        __atomic_store_n(&stopwatch, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
        __atomic_store_n(&stopwatch_off_at, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    }
    return __atomic_load_n(&stopwatch, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
}

static void talk_note(uint64_t vt) {
    if (vt == TALK_VTABLE) __atomic_store_n(&talking, 1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    else if (vt == MAP_VTABLE) {
        __atomic_store_n(&map_event_ms, SDL_GetTicks(), __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
        __atomic_store_n(&map_shown, 1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    } else if (vt == NAVIWOOF_VTABLE) {
        __atomic_store_n(&naviwoof_ms, SDL_GetTicks(), __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
        __atomic_store_n(&naviwoof, 1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    }
    else if (vt == FIELD_HUD_VTABLE) {
        __atomic_store_n(&talking, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
        __atomic_store_n(&map_shown, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
        __atomic_store_n(&naviwoof, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    }
}

/* The Yes / No box (yw::CMenuGeneralWindow, its two buttons side by side, hash 0xf51efb06: the shop's "Is that
 * correct?", seen 2026-11-15) has the focus: the wheel steps left and right there. Cleared by any other focus. */
#define GENERAL_WINDOW_VTABLE 0x14bfa78u
#define YES_NO_HASH 0xf51efb06u
static int sideways;
int mousemenu_sideways(void) { return enabled() && __atomic_load_n(&sideways, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE); }

int mousemenu_log_on(void) {
    return menu_log_on();
}

static int find_screen(uint64_t vt, uint32_t hash) {
    for (int i = 0; i < NSCREENS; i++)
        if (screens[i].vtable == vt && screens[i].hash == hash) return i;
    return -1;
}

static int is_members_screen(int idx) {
    return idx >= 0 && idx < NSCREENS && screens[idx].vtable == 0x14c1948u &&
           (screens[idx].hash == 0x180cb413u || screens[idx].hash == 0x634fbf8du);
}

/* f_9f3e90(menu, hash, 0): the menu's control with that name hash, or 0. Called from a hook at a function's
 * entry, so the caller's registers are put back afterwards. */
static uint64_t find_control(CPUState *ctx, uint64_t menu, uint32_t hash) {
    static GuestFn fn;
    if (!fn) fn = yw4_lookup(yw4_image_base + 0x9f3e90);
    if (!fn) return 0;
    uint64_t x[31];
    memcpy(x, ctx->x, sizeof x);
    uint64_t sp = ctx->sp;
    ctx->x[0] = menu, ctx->x[1] = hash, ctx->x[2] = 0;
    fn(ctx);
    uint64_t control = ctx->x[0];
    memcpy(ctx->x, x, sizeof x);
    ctx->sp = sp;
    return control;
}

/* OnChangeFocus (main+0x6c68f0), before the game's own: a menu is open or its focus moved. */
int yw4_hook_menu_focus(CPUState *ctx) {
    if (!enabled() || !ctx->x[0] || !ctx->x[1]) return 0;
    uint64_t menu = ctx->x[0];
    uint64_t vt = ld64(menu) - yw4_image_base;
    uint32_t hash = ld32(ctx->x[1]);
    if (menu_log_on()) {
        uint64_t c = find_control(ctx, menu, hash);
        if (c) {
            uint64_t lv = ld64(c + 0x118);
            uint64_t ic = lv ? find_control(ctx, menu, ld32(lv + 0xd0)) : 0;
            fprintf(stderr, "yw4: menu_focus: menu=%#llx vt=%#llx hash=%#x ctrl=%#llx "
                    "138=%d 13a=%d 13c=%u 13e=%d lv=%#llx",
                    (unsigned long long)menu, (unsigned long long)vt, hash, (unsigned long long)c,
                    (int16_t)ld16(c + 0x138), (int16_t)ld16(c + 0x13a), ld16(c + 0x13c),
                    (int16_t)ld16(c + 0x13e), (unsigned long long)lv);
            if (lv) {
                fprintf(stderr, " (vt=%#llx b0=%d b4=%u b8=%u c4=%u d0=%#x 114=%d 11c=%d 120=%d 128=%u ic13c=%d)",
                        (unsigned long long)(ld64(lv) - yw4_image_base),
                        (int32_t)ld32(lv + 0xb0), ld32(lv + 0xb4), ld32(lv + 0xb8), ld32(lv + 0xc4), ld32(lv + 0xd0),
                        (int32_t)ld32(lv + 0x114), (int32_t)ld32(lv + 0x11c), (int32_t)ld32(lv + 0x120),
                        ld32(lv + 0x128), ic ? (int)ld16(ic + 0x13c) : -1);
            }
            fprintf(stderr, "\n");
        } else {
            fprintf(stderr, "yw4: menu_focus: menu=%#llx vt=%#llx hash=%#x ctrl=0\n",
                    (unsigned long long)menu, (unsigned long long)vt, hash);
        }
    }
    talk_note(vt);
    __atomic_store_n(&sideways, vt == GENERAL_WINDOW_VTABLE && hash == YES_NO_HASH, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    /* the last focus decides: the Stopwatching menu's choice list or the battle's start choice, its pages, or a Yes /
     * No box over them: on. The class's info-card controls (0x81f8dde3, 0xcf634eb0: the ally or enemy picked with L or
     * R in the menu, and after the fight goes on) change nothing. Anything else (the fight's HUD menus): off, 0.4 s
     * later, unless the menu focuses or picks again first: Switch Members focuses the fight's HUD for a moment between
     * its picks (owner, 2026-11-15: after Tab the hints went back; the members' second pick). */
    /* a Yes / No box only while the menu is already up: Mirapo's "warp here?" turned it on in the field, where
     * nothing turns it off, and the shortcut wheel stopped opening (owner, 2026-11-16) */
    if ((vt == STOPWATCH_VTABLE && (hash == STOPWATCH_LIST_HASH || hash == BATTLE_START_HASH)) ||
        vt == STOPWATCH_MEMBERS_VTABLE || vt == STOPWATCH_ITEMS_VTABLE ||
        (vt == GENERAL_WINDOW_VTABLE && __atomic_load_n(&stopwatch, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE))) {
        __atomic_store_n(&stopwatch, 1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
        __atomic_store_n(&stopwatch_off_at, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    } else if (!(vt == STOPWATCH_VTABLE && (hash == 0x81f8dde3u || hash == 0xcf634eb0u)) &&
               __atomic_load_n(&stopwatch, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) && !__atomic_load_n(&stopwatch_off_at, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)) {
        __atomic_store_n(&stopwatch_off_at, SDL_GetTicks() + 400, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    }
    if (vt == PAD_VTABLE && hash == PAD_GRID_HASH)
        __atomic_store_n(&pad_open, 1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    if (!__atomic_load_n(&pad_open, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)) return 0;

    int idx = find_screen(vt, hash);
    if (idx >= 0) {
        uint64_t prev_menu = __atomic_load_n(&active_menu, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
        int prev_idx = __atomic_load_n(&active_idx, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
        /* CMemberMenu initializes both members_watcher and members_grid during open,
         * but visual focus starts on members_watcher (0x180cb413). Don't let grid setup
         * clobber initial watcher focus while opening. */
        if (vt == 0x14c1948u && hash == 0x634fbf8du &&
            prev_idx == find_screen(0x14c1948u, 0x180cb413u) &&
            __atomic_load_n(&layers_open, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) == 0) {
            return 0;
        }
        uint64_t ctrl = find_control(ctx, menu, hash);
        uint64_t lv = 0;
        if (screens[idx].lv_hash) {
            uint64_t lv_ctrl = find_control(ctx, menu, screens[idx].lv_hash);
            if (lv_ctrl) lv = ld64(lv_ctrl + 0x118);
        }
        __atomic_store_n(&active_ctrl, ctrl, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
        __atomic_store_n(&active_lv, lv, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
        __atomic_store_n(&active_menu, menu, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
        __atomic_store_n(&active_idx, idx, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
        if (menu != prev_menu || idx != prev_idx) {
            if (menu != prev_menu) __atomic_store_n(&layers_open, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
            if (menu != prev_menu && vt == WATCH_SKILLS_VTABLE) __atomic_store_n(&wsk_index, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
            __atomic_store_n(&page, PAGE_NONE, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
            __atomic_store_n(&wheel_steps, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
        } else if (hash == screens[idx].hash && __atomic_load_n(&page, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) == PAGE_OPEN) {
            /* the screen's own control took the focus again while a page opened over it: that page is closed (Watch
             * Skills: a character's skill tree closed with its layer count not back at the start, so the screen stayed
             * "covered" and ignored the mouse; 2026-11-16) */
            __atomic_store_n(&page, PAGE_NONE, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
            __atomic_store_n(&wheel_steps, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
        }
    }
    return 0;
}

/* OnBack (main+0x6c59f0): B closed the whole Pad (or a sub-page). */
int yw4_hook_menu_back(CPUState *ctx) {
    if (!enabled() || !ctx->x[0]) return 0;
    uint64_t menu = ctx->x[0];
    uint64_t vt = ld64(menu) - yw4_image_base;
    if (menu_log_on())
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: menu_back: menu=%#llx vt=%#llx\n", (unsigned long long)menu, (unsigned long long)vt);
    /* backing out: the next field HUD update ends it at once (the half second guards only the map's opening; a
     * press right after closing it was still refused, owner 2026-11-16) */
    if (vt == MAP_VTABLE) __atomic_store_n(&map_event_ms, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    if (vt == NAVIWOOF_VTABLE) __atomic_store_n(&naviwoof, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);  /* backed out of: gone */
    if (vt == PAD_VTABLE) {
        __atomic_store_n(&pad_open, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
        __atomic_store_n(&active_idx, -1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
        __atomic_store_n(&active_menu, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
        __atomic_store_n(&active_ctrl, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
        __atomic_store_n(&active_lv, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
        __atomic_store_n(&wheel_steps, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    } else if (menu == __atomic_load_n(&active_menu, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) &&
               __atomic_load_n(&page, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) == PAGE_NONE) {
        __atomic_store_n(&active_idx, -1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
        __atomic_store_n(&wheel_steps, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    }
    return 0;
}

/* OnDecideFocus (main+0x6c6ba0): an item or icon was chosen; a page or dialog may open over the screen. */
int yw4_hook_menu_decide(CPUState *ctx) {
    if (!enabled() || !ctx->x[0]) return 0;
    uint64_t menu = ctx->x[0];
    uint64_t vt = ld64(menu) - yw4_image_base;
    if (menu_log_on())
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: menu_decide: menu=%#llx vt=%#llx\n", (unsigned long long)menu, (unsigned long long)vt);
    if (vt == STOPWATCH_VTABLE || vt == STOPWATCH_MEMBERS_VTABLE || vt == STOPWATCH_ITEMS_VTABLE)
        __atomic_store_n(&stopwatch_off_at, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);  /* a pick in it: still open */
    if (menu == __atomic_load_n(&active_menu, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) &&
        __atomic_load_n(&page, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) == PAGE_NONE) {
        __atomic_store_n(&page_base, __atomic_load_n(&layers_open, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE), __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
        __atomic_store_n(&page_since, SDL_GetTicks(), __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
        __atomic_store_n(&page, PAGE_OPENING, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    }
    return 0;
}

/* OnOpenEndLayer (main+0x6c5fa0) / OnCloseEndLayer (main+0x6c6040): a layer finished opening / closing. */
int yw4_hook_menu_layer_opened(CPUState *ctx) {
    if (!enabled() || !ctx->x[0]) return 0;
    uint64_t menu = ctx->x[0];
    uint64_t vt = ld64(menu) - yw4_image_base;
    if (menu_log_on())
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: menu_layer_opened: menu=%#llx vt=%#llx\n", (unsigned long long)menu, (unsigned long long)vt);
    talk_note(vt);
    if (menu == __atomic_load_n(&active_menu, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)) {
        int n = __atomic_add_fetch(&layers_open, 1, __ATOMIC_ACQ_REL);
        if (__atomic_load_n(&page, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) == PAGE_OPENING && n > __atomic_load_n(&page_base, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE))
            __atomic_store_n(&page, PAGE_OPEN, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    } else if (__atomic_load_n(&page, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) == PAGE_OPENING) {
        /* A sub-dialog with its own menu object (e.g. a Help article popup) opened over the active screen. */
        __atomic_add_fetch(&layers_open, 1, __ATOMIC_ACQ_REL);
        __atomic_store_n(&page, PAGE_OPEN, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    }
    return 0;
}

int yw4_hook_menu_layer_closed(CPUState *ctx) {
    if (!enabled() || !ctx->x[0]) return 0;
    uint64_t menu = ctx->x[0];
    uint64_t vt = ld64(menu) - yw4_image_base;
    if (menu_log_on())
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: menu_layer_closed: menu=%#llx vt=%#llx\n", (unsigned long long)menu, (unsigned long long)vt);
    if (menu == __atomic_load_n(&active_menu, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)) {
        int n = __atomic_sub_fetch(&layers_open, 1, __ATOMIC_ACQ_REL);
        if (__atomic_load_n(&page, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) == PAGE_OPEN && n <= __atomic_load_n(&page_base, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE))
            __atomic_store_n(&page, PAGE_NONE, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
        /* The Members 2-button popup (hash 0x48a3835c) lives on the Pad's own menu object and closes 4 layers on B
         * without firing OnChangeFocus on the 4x3 grid; restore the 4x3 grid when its layers close on B. */
        int cur_idx = __atomic_load_n(&active_idx, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
        if (cur_idx >= 0 && screens[cur_idx].hash == 0x48a3835cu &&
            __atomic_load_n(&page, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) == PAGE_NONE) {
            uint64_t grid = find_control(ctx, menu, PAD_GRID_HASH);
            int pad_idx = find_screen(PAD_VTABLE, PAD_GRID_HASH);
            if (grid && pad_idx >= 0) {
                __atomic_store_n(&active_ctrl, grid, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
                __atomic_store_n(&active_lv, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
                __atomic_store_n(&active_idx, pad_idx, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
            }
        }
    } else if (__atomic_load_n(&page, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) == PAGE_OPEN && vt != PAD_VTABLE) {
        int n = __atomic_sub_fetch(&layers_open, 1, __ATOMIC_ACQ_REL);
        if (n <= __atomic_load_n(&page_base, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE))
            __atomic_store_n(&page, PAGE_NONE, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    }
    return 0;
}

/* ---- the window's thread */

int mousemenu_wheel(int dir) {
    if (!enabled() || !__atomic_load_n(&pad_open, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)) return 0;
    int idx = __atomic_load_n(&active_idx, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
    if (idx >= 0 && (screens[idx].flags & SCR_WHEEL) && __atomic_load_n(&page, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) == PAGE_NONE) {
        int cur = __atomic_load_n(&wheel_steps, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
        int next = cur + (dir > 0 ? 1 : -1);
        if (next > 8) next = 8;
        if (next < -8) next = -8;
        __atomic_store_n(&wheel_steps, next, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    }
    return 1;  /* swallow wheel while the Pad is open so field bindings don't fire */
}

/* The currently focused visible slot (0 .. cols*rows - 1) on screen s, or -1. */
static int screen_focus(const Screen *s, uint64_t ctrl, uint64_t lv) {
    if (s->vtable == WATCH_SKILLS_VTABLE) return __atomic_load_n(&wsk_index, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
    if (s->lv_hash) {
        if (!lv) return -1;
        int32_t top = (int32_t)ld32(lv + 0x114) + (int32_t)ld32(lv + 0xb0);
        int32_t sel = (int32_t)ld32(lv + 0x11c);
        if (top < 0) top = 0;
        int vis = sel - top;
        return vis >= 0 && vis < s->cols * s->rows ? vis : -1;
    }
    if (!ctrl) return -1;
    int f = (int)ld16(ctrl + 0x13c);
    return f >= 0 && f < s->cols * s->rows ? f : -1;
}

/* The slot under the mouse (0 .. cols*rows - 1) on screen s, or -1. */
static int slot_at(const Screen *s, uint64_t lv, float mx, float my, int w, int h) {
    if (!s || !(s->flags & (SCR_HOVER | SCR_CLICK)) || w <= 0 || h <= 0) return -1;
    float uw = (float)w, uh = (float)h;  /* the menus' 16:9 area: the largest one in the middle of the picture */
    if (uw * 9.0f > uh * 16.0f) uw = uh * 16.0f / 9.0f;
    else uh = uw * 9.0f / 16.0f;
    float x = (mx - (w - uw) / 2) * 1280.0f / uw, y = (my - (h - uh) / 2) * 720.0f / uh;
    int c = s->cols > 1 ? (int)floorf((x - (s->x0 - s->dx * 0.5f)) / s->dx) : 0;
    int r = s->rows > 1 ? (int)floorf((y - (s->y0 - s->dy * 0.5f)) / s->dy) : 0;
    if (c < 0 || c >= s->cols || r < 0 || r >= s->rows) return -1;
    float cx = s->x0 + s->dx * c, cy = s->y0 + s->dy * r;
    if (fabsf(x - cx) > s->hw || fabsf(y - cy) > s->hh) return -1;
    if (s->lv_hash && lv) {
        int32_t top = (int32_t)ld32(lv + 0x114) + (int32_t)ld32(lv + 0xb0);
        uint32_t total = ld32(lv + 0x128);
        if (top < 0) top = 0;
        if (total > 0 && top + r * s->cols + c >= (int32_t)total) return -1;
    }
    return r * s->cols + c;
}

/* Tests (YW4_MOUSE_SCRIPT=<file>): a scripted mouse instead of the real one, so tests never move the desktop's
 * cursor. Lines "<ms> <x> <y> <buttons> [wheel]": after waiting <ms> (from the Pad opening, then from the line
 * before) the mouse is at (x, y) in the 1280 x 720 menu space with these buttons (1 left, 4 right; SDL's masks;
 * 256 also takes a screenshot) and optional wheel notches (+N up, -N down). */
static int script_step(float *mx, float *my, int w, int h, uint32_t *buttons, uint64_t now) {
    static int loaded, n, at;
    static struct { int ms; float x, y; uint32_t b; int wheel; } lines[256];
    static uint64_t since;
    if (!loaded) {
        loaded = 1;
        const char *p = getenv("YW4_MOUSE_SCRIPT");
        FILE *f = p && *p ? fopen(p, "r") : NULL;
        char l[128];
        while (f && n < 256 && fgets(l, sizeof l, f)) {
            int w_notch = 0;
            int got = sscanf(l, "%d %f %f %u %d", &lines[n].ms, &lines[n].x, &lines[n].y, &lines[n].b, &w_notch);
            if (got >= 4) lines[n].wheel = got >= 5 ? w_notch : 0, n++;
        }
        if (f) fclose(f), fprintf(stderr, "yw4: mouse menus: %d scripted mouse steps from %s\n", n, p);
    }
    if (!n) return 0;
    if (!since) {
        since = now;
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: mouse menus: script step 0: (%g, %g) buttons %u wheel %d\n",
                lines[0].x, lines[0].y, lines[0].b, lines[0].wheel);
        if (lines[0].b & 256) window_request_screenshot();
        if (lines[0].wheel) {
            int w_dir = lines[0].wheel > 0 ? 1 : -1;
            for (int k = 0; k < abs(lines[0].wheel); k++) mousemenu_wheel(w_dir);
        }
    }
    while (at < n - 1 && now - since >= (uint64_t)lines[at + 1].ms) {
        since += (uint64_t)lines[at + 1].ms, at++;
        fprintf(stderr, "yw4: mouse menus: script step %d: (%g, %g) buttons %u wheel %d\n",
                at, lines[at].x, lines[at].y, lines[at].b, lines[at].wheel);
        if (lines[at].b & 256) window_request_screenshot();
        if (lines[at].wheel) {
            int w_dir = lines[at].wheel > 0 ? 1 : -1;
            for (int k = 0; k < abs(lines[at].wheel); k++) mousemenu_wheel(w_dir);
        }
    }
    float uw = (float)w, uh = (float)h;
    if (uw * 9.0f > uh * 16.0f) uw = uh * 16.0f / 9.0f;
    else uh = uw * 9.0f / 16.0f;
    *mx = (w - uw) / 2 + lines[at].x * uw / 1280.0f;
    *my = (h - uh) / 2 + lines[at].y * uh / 720.0f;
    *buttons = lines[at].b & 0xff;
    return 1;
}

uint64_t mousemenu_update(float mx, float my, int w, int h, uint32_t mouse_buttons, int *want_cursor) {
    static uint64_t press, press_until, gap_until, press_reads, gap_reads;  /* the button being pressed now */
    static int step_from = -1;  /* a D-pad step's start focus, until the screen's focus changes */
    static uint64_t step_at;
    static int click_target = -1, hover_target = -1, last_hover = -1, back_wanted, moved, unanswered, pad_page;
    static int last_idx = -1;
    static uint64_t last_menu;
    static uint32_t last_buttons;
    static float last_x = -1, last_y = -1;
    static int target_is_sib;
    *want_cursor = 0;
    if (!enabled()) return 0;
    uint64_t now = SDL_GetTicks();
    int open = __atomic_load_n(&pad_open, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
    if (open) script_step(&mx, &my, w, h, &mouse_buttons, now);
    uint32_t down = mouse_buttons & ~last_buttons;
    last_buttons = mouse_buttons;
    if (!open) {
        press = 0, click_target = hover_target = last_hover = -1, step_from = -1, back_wanted = moved = pad_page = 0;
        target_is_sib = 0;
        last_idx = -1, last_menu = 0;
        last_x = mx, last_y = my;
        return 0;
    }
    *want_cursor = 1;
    int idx = __atomic_load_n(&active_idx, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
    uint64_t menu = __atomic_load_n(&active_menu, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
    const Screen *s = idx >= 0 && idx < NSCREENS ? &screens[idx] : NULL;
    if (idx != last_idx || menu != last_menu) {
        int was_members = is_members_screen(last_idx) && is_members_screen(idx) && menu == last_menu;
        last_idx = idx, last_menu = menu;
        if (!was_members) {
            click_target = hover_target = last_hover = -1, step_from = -1, moved = 0, unanswered = 0;
            target_is_sib = 0;
        } else {
            target_is_sib = 0;
        }
    }
    /* a choice that opened no page (nothing happened in 600 ms on a list or 2 s on the Pad): the screen is still in front */
    uint64_t timeout = s && s->lv_hash ? 600 : 2000;
    if (__atomic_load_n(&page, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) == PAGE_OPENING && now - __atomic_load_n(&page_since, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) > timeout)
        __atomic_store_n(&page, PAGE_NONE, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    int front = s && __atomic_load_n(&page, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) == PAGE_NONE;
    uint64_t ctrl = __atomic_load_n(&active_ctrl, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
    uint64_t lv = __atomic_load_n(&active_lv, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
    int focus = front ? screen_focus(s, ctrl, lv) : -1;
    if (mx != last_x || my != last_y) moved = 1, last_x = mx, last_y = my;
    /* what the mouse asks for, every update (also while a press is under way): a right click is B; on an active
     * screen, a left click on a slot goes there and presses A; moving onto a slot goes there and stays wanted
     * until the focus arrives (a still mouse then leaves the keys and the gamepad alone until it moves onto
     * another slot). A cursor resting on a slot when a screen comes to the front wants nothing until it moves. */
    int under = front ? slot_at(s, lv, mx, my, w, h) : -1;
    int under_sib = -1;
    if (front && is_members_screen(idx)) {
        int idx_watcher = find_screen(0x14c1948u, 0x180cb413u);
        int idx_grid = find_screen(0x14c1948u, 0x634fbf8du);
        int sib = (idx == idx_watcher) ? idx_grid : idx_watcher;
        if (under < 0 && sib >= 0) {
            under_sib = slot_at(&screens[sib], 0, mx, my, w, h);
            if (under_sib >= 0) {
                if (down & SDL_BUTTON_LMASK) {
                    click_target = under_sib;
                    target_is_sib = 1;
                }
                if (under_sib != last_hover) {
                    last_hover = under_sib;
                    if (moved) {
                        hover_target = under_sib;
                        target_is_sib = 1;
                    }
                }
            }
        } else if (under >= 0) {
            target_is_sib = 0;
        }
    }
    if (!front) click_target = hover_target = -1, moved = 0, target_is_sib = 0;
    if (down & SDL_BUTTON_RMASK) {
        back_wanted = 1, click_target = hover_target = -1, target_is_sib = 0;
        __atomic_store_n(&wheel_steps, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    } else if ((down & SDL_BUTTON_LMASK) && under >= 0 && (s->flags & SCR_CLICK)) {
        click_target = under;
        target_is_sib = 0;
    }
    if (under >= 0) {
        if (under != last_hover) {
            last_hover = under;
            if (moved && (s->flags & SCR_HOVER)) {
                hover_target = under;
                target_is_sib = 0;
            }
        }
    } else if (under_sib < 0) {
        last_hover = -1;
    }
    if (hover_target >= 0 && hover_target == focus && !target_is_sib) hover_target = -1;
    /* a press lasts until the game has read the input twice (at least 40 ms), then it is up for as long before the
     * next: by reads, not time, so a stall (a screenshot, a loading hitch) can't swallow a press */
    uint64_t reads = window_input_reads();
    if (menu_log_on()) {
        static uint64_t next_dump;
        if (now >= next_dump) {
            next_dump = now + 500;
            fprintf(stderr, "yw4: mouse menus: state t=%llu screen=%s focus=%d under=%d hover=%d click=%d wheel=%d front=%d\n",
                    (unsigned long long)now, s ? s->name : "none", focus, under, hover_target, click_target,
                    __atomic_load_n(&wheel_steps, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE), front);
        }
    }
    if (press) {
        if (now < press_until || reads < press_reads) return press;
        press = 0, gap_until = now + 40, gap_reads = reads + 2;
    }
    if (now < gap_until || reads < gap_reads) return 0;
    /* a step's answer: the screen's focus changes. The Pad drops a press in a new direction right after a move
     * (its cursor is still animating), so an unanswered step is sent again after 400 ms; after two unanswered
     * steps in a row the mouse stops asking for that slot (one the game won't move to). */
    if (step_from >= 0) {
        if (focus == step_from && now < step_at + 400) return 0;
        if (focus == step_from && ++unanswered >= 2) unanswered = 0, hover_target = click_target = -1;
        if (focus != step_from) unanswered = 0;
        step_from = -1;
    }
    if (back_wanted) back_wanted = 0, press = BTN_B;
    int wheel = __atomic_load_n(&wheel_steps, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
    if (!press && front && wheel != 0 && (s->flags & SCR_WHEEL)) {
        press = s->cols > 1 ? ((pad_page ^= 1) ? BTN_R : BTN_L) : (wheel > 0 ? BTN_UP : BTN_DOWN);
        __atomic_store_n(&wheel_steps, wheel > 0 ? wheel - 1 : wheel + 1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
        hover_target = click_target = -1;
    }
    int target = click_target >= 0 ? click_target : hover_target;
    if (menu_log_on()) {
        static int last_under = -2, last_target = -2, last_front = -1, logged;
        if ((under != last_under || target != last_target || front != last_front) && logged++ < 2000)
            fprintf(stderr, "yw4: mouse menus: screen %s %s, under %d, target %d, focus %d\n",
                    s ? s->name : "none", front ? "in front" : "covered", under, target, focus);
        last_under = under, last_target = target, last_front = front;
    }
    if (!press && front && target_is_sib && is_members_screen(idx)) {
        press = (screens[idx].hash == 0x180cb413u) ? BTN_DOWN : BTN_UP;
        step_from = focus, step_at = now;
    } else if (!press && front && target >= 0 && focus >= 0) {
        int cols = s->cols;
        int dr = target / cols - focus / cols, dc = target % cols - focus % cols;
        if (dr) press = dr > 0 ? BTN_DOWN : BTN_UP;
        else if (dc) {
            press = dc > 0 ? BTN_RIGHT : BTN_LEFT;
            if (s->vtable == WATCH_SKILLS_VTABLE) {  /* the press moves the highlight: count it (see wsk_index) */
                int n = __atomic_load_n(&wsk_index, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) + (dc > 0 ? 1 : -1);
                __atomic_store_n(&wsk_index, n < 0 ? 0 : n > 5 ? 5 : n, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
            }
        } else if (click_target >= 0) {
            if (s->vtable == 0x14c60f8u) {
                float uw = (float)w, uh = (float)h;
                if (uw * 9.0f > uh * 16.0f) uw = uh * 16.0f / 9.0f;
                else uh = uw * 9.0f / 16.0f;
                float x = (mx - (w - uw) / 2) * 1280.0f / uw;
                if (x >= 470.0f && x <= 530.0f) press = BTN_LEFT;
                else if (x >= 730.0f && x <= 798.5f) press = BTN_RIGHT;
            } else {
                press = BTN_A;
            }
            click_target = -1;
        }
        if (press && (dr || dc)) step_from = focus, step_at = now;
    }
    if (press) press_until = now + 40, press_reads = reads + 2;
    return press;
}
```
