`tools/dev/bench.py`:

```py
"""Where the frame time goes: GPU time per pass and CPU time per thread for every scene of the `bench` group.

    python -m tools.dev.bench                    # run every bench scene twice (GPU, CPU), then write the results
    python -m tools.dev.bench lag school         # only those scenes (the others' results are kept)
    python -m tools.dev.bench --parse            # write the results again from the last runs

Each scene runs twice (tools.dev.scene, so the usual checks apply):
- GPU: the owner's settings (a copy), YW4_GPU_PASSES=1; each pass's milliseconds per frame are averaged over the
  run's second half. The bamboo forest runs a third time with YW4_MASK_BREAKDOWN=1 (the shadow mask in four forms).
- CPU: no settings file (1600x900, no anti-aliasing) and YW4_FPS=0, so the GPU isn't the limit, with
  YW4_PROFILE=hitch and a 0 ms threshold: every game thread sampled each millisecond from frame 3000. A sample in a
  wait (fences, condition variables, the GPU worker idling, presents) counts as idle; the rest is split per thread
  by kind of code (functions named with llvm-nm, runtime functions grouped by module from docs/advanced/code-map.js).
  The profile is written at exit, so these runs end at a frame (--frames), not on a timer.

Writes work/bench/bench.json (everything), work/bench/*.csv (one table each) and docs/advanced/bench.js (the
site's snapshot: frame rates, GPU time per pass and the shadow mask's split, with the date, game version, GPU and
settings; nothing per thread or per function). Run it with nothing else open: a second game spoils the timings,
and tools.dev.scene refuses to start while one runs.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import bisect
import collections
import csv
import datetime
import json
import re
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys
import tomllib
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
WORK = ROOT / "work"
OUT = WORK / "bench"
SITE = ROOT / "docs" / "advanced" / "bench.js"
SCENES_TOML = ROOT / "tools" / "dev" / "scenes.toml"
CPU_FROM = 3000
# the bench scenes' names on the site and in the tables (scenes.toml's `about` is for us)
SHORT = {"busy": "Busy town spot", "lag": "Evening street", "lag2": "Town street 2", "lag3": "Town street 3",
         "lag4": "Town street 4", "lategame": "Bamboo forest", "yokaiworld": "Yo-kai World street",
         "walk": "Town walk (moving)", "school": "Schoolyard", "forest": "Forest cutscene", "snowbridge": "Snow bridge",
         "fence": "Fence", "pole": "Pole", "cutscene": "Cutscene", "diary": "Owner's save (Nov 17)"}
CPU_FRAMES = {"walk": 10000}  # the town walk's replay is longer; the rest 7000
MASK_SCENE = "lategame"


def bench_scenes() -> tuple[list[str], dict[str, str]]:
    t = tomllib.loads(SCENES_TOML.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return t["groups"]["bench"], {k: v.get("about", k) for k, v in t.items() if isinstance(v, dict) and "save" in v}


def scene(task: str, name: str, *args: str) -> bool:
    cmd = [sys.executable, "-m", "tools.dev.scene", name, "--task", task, *args]
    print(">>", name, task, " ".join(args), flush=True)
    r = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    out = (r.stdout + r.stderr).strip()
    print("  " + "\n  ".join(out.splitlines()[-4:]), flush=True)
    if "not started" in out:
        print("bench: a run refused to start (above); stopping", flush=True)
        return False
    return True


def run(names: list[str]) -> bool:
    for s in names:
        if not scene("bench_gpu", s, "--settings", "owner", "YW4_GPU_PASSES=1"):
            return False
        if not scene("bench_cpu", s, "--frames", str(CPU_FRAMES.get(s, 7000)), "YW4_FPS=0", "YW4_PROFILE=hitch",
                     "YW4_PROFILE_HITCH_MS=0", f"YW4_PROFILE_FROM={CPU_FROM}"):
            return False
    if MASK_SCENE in names:
        return scene("bench_mask", MASK_SCENE, "--settings", "owner", "YW4_GPU_PASSES=1", "YW4_MASK_BREAKDOWN=1")
    return True


# ---- GPU passes

FS_NAMES: dict[str, str] = {}


def load_names() -> None:
    src = (ROOT / "runtime/src/gpu_draw.c").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    for h, n in re.findall(r'\{0x([0-9a-f]{16})ull, ST_FRAG, "([a-z_0-9]+)', src):
        FS_NAMES[h] = n.replace("_", " ")
    # named in docs/frame.md
    FS_NAMES.update({"06d03ad703b4bee5": "shadow mask", "6b4575fb57b97548": "depth-only copy",
                     "17a09ecce84525a7": "occlusion boxes"})


def pass_label(rest: str) -> str:
    m = re.search(r"\s+vs ([0-9a-f]{16}) fs ([0-9a-f]{16})\s*$", rest)
    target = rest[: m.start()].strip() if m else rest.strip()
    fs = m.group(2) if m else ""
    if not fs or fs == "0" * 16:
        return target  # our own passes are named in the log
    if fs in FS_NAMES:
        return FS_NAMES[fs]
    if "240x135" in target:
        return "occlusion boxes"
    if re.match(r"(400x225|200x112|120x67)", target):
        return "bloom chain (game's)"
    if re.match(r"1600x900 f(17 1600x900 f37|63 1600x900 f17)", target):
        return "G-buffer (other materials)"
    if re.match(r"1600x900 f63 \+ depth 1600x900", target):
        return "scene colour (other materials)"
    return f"other ({target[:22]})"


def who(name: str) -> str:
    if name.startswith("DLSS"):
        return "NVIDIA DLSS"
    if name.startswith("our ") or name in ("shadow mask", "anti-aliasing: DLSS"):
        return "ours"
    return "game's"


def parse_gpu(log: Path) -> dict:
    blocks: list[dict] = []
    for ln in log.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines():
        m = re.match(r"yw4: gpu passes: ([\d.]+) ms of GPU time per frame over (\d+) frames", ln)
        if m:
            blocks.append({"total": float(m.group(1)), "passes": []})
            continue
        m = re.match(r"yw4: gpu passes:\s+([\d.]+) ms\s+([\d.]+) passes \(\s*[\d.]+ ms each\)\s+([\d.]+) draws\s+[\d.]+"
                     r" restarts\s+[\d.]+ uploads\s+(\d+)k vertices\s+(.*)$", ln)
        if m and blocks:
            blocks[-1]["passes"].append({"name": pass_label(m.group(5)), "ms": float(m.group(1)),
                                         "draws": float(m.group(3)), "kverts": int(m.group(4))})
    use = blocks[len(blocks) // 2:] or blocks
    agg: dict[str, dict] = collections.defaultdict(lambda: {"ms": 0.0, "draws": 0.0, "kverts": 0.0})
    for b in use:
        for p in b["passes"]:
            a = agg[p["name"]]
            for k in ("ms", "draws", "kverts"):
                a[k] += p[k] / len(use)
    passes = sorted(({"name": k, "who": who(k), **v} for k, v in agg.items()), key=lambda p: -p["ms"])
    return {"total_ms": statistics.mean(b["total"] for b in use) if use else None, "passes": passes}


def parse_mask(log: Path) -> dict[str, float]:
    forms: dict[str, list[float]] = collections.defaultdict(list)
    for ln in log.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines():
        m = re.search(r"gpu passes:.*\(\s*([\d.]+) ms each\).*shadow mask: (.+?)\s{2,}", ln)
        if m:
            forms[m.group(2)].append(float(m.group(1)))
    return {k: round(statistics.mean(v), 2) for k, v in forms.items()}


def summary(folder: Path) -> dict:
    newest = max(folder.glob("perf_*.txt"), key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime)  # a respawned run can leave two
    txt = newest.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")

    def num(pat: str) -> float | None:
        m = re.search(pat, txt)
        return float(m.group(1)) if m else None

    m = re.search(r"picture now: (.*)", txt)
    return {"fps": num(r"([\d.]+) frames/s average"), "work_ms": num(r"game work ms: avg ([\d.]+)"),
            "gpu_busy_ms": num(r"GPU busy ms: avg ([\d.]+)"), "gpu_wait_ms": num(r"GPU waits avg ([\d.]+)"),
            "game_code_ms": num(r"game code avg ([\d.]+)"), "process_cpu_pct": num(r"process CPU: (\d+)%"),
            "picture": m.group(1).strip() if m else ""}


# ---- CPU profile

WAIT = re.compile(r"wait|sleep|cond_|park|futex|SleepConditionVariable|svc$|^worker$|^present_image$")


def code_map() -> tuple[dict[str, str], dict[str, str]]:
    t = (ROOT / "docs/advanced/code-map.js").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    j = json.loads(t[t.index("{"): t.rindex("}") + 1])
    mods: dict[str, set] = collections.defaultdict(set)
    for f in j["funcs"]:
        mods[f["n"]].add(f["m"])
    return {k: next(iter(v)) for k, v in mods.items() if len(v) == 1}, {n["id"]: n["group"] for n in j["nodes"]}


def category(name: str, fn_mod: dict, groups: dict) -> tuple[str, str]:
    if name.startswith(("f_", "s_")):
        return "Game code (recompiled)", name
    mod = fn_mod.get(name)
    if mod in ("gpu", "gpu_draw", "gpu_queue", "gpu_pcache", "gpu_query", "vk", "window") or (mod or "").startswith("nvn"):
        return "Our graphics translation", f"{name} [{mod}]"
    if mod and groups.get(mod) == "passes":
        return "Our render passes (bones, shadows, G-buffer)", f"{name} [{mod}]"
    return "Our other runtime", f"{name} [{mod}]" if mod else name


def thread_roles(log: Path) -> dict[int, dict]:
    text = log.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    out = {}
    for ln in text[text.rfind("threads, last 600 frames:"):].splitlines()[1:40]:
        m = re.match(r"\s+thread (\d+):\s+(\d+)% of a core.*?(\[(.*)\])?$", ln)
        if not m:
            break
        out[int(m.group(1))] = {"core_pct": int(m.group(2)), "role": m.group(4) or ""}
    return out


def thread_name(tid: int, role: str) -> str:
    if tid == 0:
        return "Our host threads (GPU worker, window)"
    if role == "presents":
        return "Main game thread"
    if role.startswith("submits"):
        return f"Render thread {tid}"
    return f"Game worker {tid}"


def parse_cpu(folder: Path, addrs, names, fn_mod, groups) -> dict | None:
    log = folder / "run.log"
    m = re.search(r"yw4: profile \((\d+) samples\) in (\S+)", log.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"))
    if not m:
        return None
    roles = thread_roles(log)
    th: dict[int, dict] = collections.defaultdict(lambda: {"total": 0, "idle": 0, "cats": collections.Counter(),
                                                            "fns": collections.Counter(), "sys": collections.Counter()})
    for ln in (ROOT / m.group(2)).read_text().splitlines():
        if ln.startswith("#"):
            continue
        k, n = ln.split()
        key, n = int(k, 16), int(n)
        via, tid, off = key >> 63, (key >> 48) & 0x7FFF, key & ((1 << 48) - 1)  # profile.c: caller bit, thread tag
        i = bisect.bisect_right(addrs, off) - 1
        name = names[i] if i >= 0 else f"exe+{off:x}"
        t = th[tid]
        t["total"] += n
        if via and WAIT.search(name):
            t["idle"] += n
        elif via:
            t["sys"][name] += n
            t["cats"]["Windows / driver calls"] += n
        else:
            cat, label = category(name, fn_mod, groups)
            t["cats"][cat] += n
            t["fns"][label] += n
    threads = []
    for tid, t in th.items():
        role = roles.get(tid, {}).get("role", "")
        threads.append({"thread": thread_name(tid, role), "busy_pct": round(100 * (t["total"] - t["idle"]) / t["total"], 1),
                        "cats": {c: round(100 * v / t["total"], 2) for c, v in t["cats"].items()},
                        "top": [(f, round(100 * v / t["total"], 2)) for f, v in t["fns"].most_common(15)],
                        "sys": [(f, round(100 * v / t["total"], 2)) for f, v in t["sys"].most_common(8)]})
    return {"samples": int(m.group(1)), "threads": sorted(threads, key=lambda t: -t["busy_pct"])}


# ---- output

def gpu_name() -> str:
    for log in sorted((WORK / "shots_bench_gpu").glob("*/run.log")):
        m = re.search(r"yw4: window: Vulkan on (.+?) \(API", log.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"))
        if m:
            return m.group(1)
    return ""


def write_csv(name: str, rows: list[dict]) -> None:
    if not rows:
        return
    with open(OUT / name, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=list(rows[0]))
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)


def parse(names: list[str], about: dict[str, str]) -> None:
    load_names()
    sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
    from tools.yw4.profile import symbols
    addrs, syms = symbols(WORK / "build" / ("yw4.exe" if sys.platform == "win32" else "yw4"))
    fn_mod, groups = code_map()
    res = {"date": datetime.date.today().isoformat(), "version": (ROOT / "VERSION").read_text().strip(),
           "gpu_name": gpu_name(), "scenes": {}, "mask": {}}
    for s in names:
        g, c = WORK / "shots_bench_gpu" / s, WORK / "shots_bench_cpu" / s
        e = {"about": SHORT.get(s, about.get(s, s))}
        if (g / "run.log").exists() and list(g.glob("perf_*.txt")):
            e["gpu"] = {"summary": summary(g), **parse_gpu(g / "run.log")}
        if (c / "run.log").exists() and list(c.glob("perf_*.txt")):
            e["cpu"] = {"summary": summary(c), "profile": parse_cpu(c, addrs, syms, fn_mod, groups)}
        if len(e) > 1:
            res["scenes"][s] = e
    mlog = WORK / "shots_bench_mask" / MASK_SCENE / "run.log"
    if mlog.exists():
        res["mask"] = parse_mask(mlog)
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (OUT / "bench.json").write_text(json.dumps(res, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")

    sc = res["scenes"]
    write_csv("scenes.csv", [{"scene": v["about"], **{f"{k}_4k": v["gpu"]["summary"][k] for k in ("fps", "gpu_busy_ms", "work_ms", "gpu_wait_ms")},
                              **{f"{k}_uncapped": (v.get("cpu") or {}).get("summary", {}).get(k) for k in ("fps", "work_ms", "game_code_ms", "process_cpu_pct")}}
                             for v in sc.values() if "gpu" in v])
    write_csv("gpu_passes.csv", [{"scene": v["about"], "pass": p["name"], "who": p["who"], "ms": round(p["ms"], 3),
                                  "draws": round(p["draws"], 1), "kvertices": round(p["kverts"])}
                                 for v in sc.values() if "gpu" in v for p in v["gpu"]["passes"]])
    write_csv("shadow_mask.csv", [{"form": k, "ms": v} for k, v in res["mask"].items()])
    write_csv("cpu_threads.csv", [{"scene": v["about"], "thread": t["thread"], "busy_pct": t["busy_pct"], "category": cat, "pct_of_core": pct}
                                  for v in sc.values() if (v.get("cpu") or {}).get("profile")
                                  for t in v["cpu"]["profile"]["threads"] if t["busy_pct"] >= 3 for cat, pct in t["cats"].items()])
    fns: dict[str, list] = collections.defaultdict(list)
    ncpu = sum(1 for v in sc.values() if (v.get("cpu") or {}).get("profile"))
    for v in sc.values():
        for t in ((v.get("cpu") or {}).get("profile") or {}).get("threads", []):
            for f, pct in t["top"]:
                fns[f].append((pct, t["thread"]))
    write_csv("cpu_functions.csv", sorted(({"function": f, "pct_of_core": round(sum(p for p, _ in v) / max(ncpu, 1), 2),
                                            "mostly_on": collections.Counter(t for _, t in v).most_common(1)[0][0]}
                                           for f, v in fns.items()), key=lambda r: -r["pct_of_core"])[:40])

    # the site's snapshot: no per-thread or per-function detail
    def top_passes(passes: list[dict], n: int = 10) -> list[dict]:
        top = [{"name": p["name"], "who": p["who"], "ms": round(p["ms"], 2)} for p in passes[:n]]
        rest = sum(p["ms"] for p in passes[n:])
        return top + ([{"name": f"{len(passes) - n} smaller passes", "who": "", "ms": round(rest, 2)}] if rest else [])

    first = next((v["gpu"]["summary"]["picture"] for v in sc.values() if "gpu" in v), "")
    site = {"date": res["date"], "version": res["version"], "gpu": res["gpu_name"], "settings": first,
            "scenes": [{"name": v["about"], "fps": v["gpu"]["summary"]["fps"], "gpu_ms": v["gpu"]["summary"]["gpu_busy_ms"],
                        "fps_uncapped": (v.get("cpu") or {}).get("summary", {}).get("fps"), "passes": top_passes(v["gpu"]["passes"])}
                       for v in sc.values() if "gpu" in v],
            "shadow_mask": res["mask"]}
    SITE.write_text("// Written by python -m tools.dev.bench (a snapshot; see its date). Read by docs/advanced/index.html.\n"
                    "window.BENCH = " + json.dumps(site, ensure_ascii=False) + ";\n", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    print(f"bench: {len(sc)} scenes -> {OUT / 'bench.json'}, {SITE.relative_to(ROOT)}")


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("scenes", nargs="*", help="bench scenes to run (default: the whole bench group)")
    ap.add_argument("--parse", action="store_true", help="only write the results from the last runs")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    group, about = bench_scenes()
    if not a.parse and not run(a.scenes or group):
        return 1
    parse(group, about)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

`tools/dev/code_map.py`:

```py
"""The data behind the site's code map (docs/advanced/): every module and function of the C runtime, and who calls whom.

Reads the tracked .c/.cpp/.h files under runtime/src and runtime/include (git ls-files, so only what is committed
or staged counts) and writes docs/advanced/code-map.js. Run it after runtime changes, from the repo root:

    python -m tools.dev.code_map          # rewrite docs/advanced/code-map.js
    python -m tools.dev.code_map --check  # exit 1 if it is out of date (no writes)

What it finds, with plain regular expressions (no compiler):
- A module is a file name without its extension: gpu.c + gpu.h = "gpu".
- Module links: A includes B's header, or names a non-static function defined in B (headers only declare, so
  only .c/.cpp files count as using one).
- Functions: every definition that starts at column 0, static ones too, with its line, length and the comment
  right above it. A function "calls" another when it names it in its body: a direct call, or passing it as a
  function pointer. Calls through pointers at run time and calls inside macros are not seen.
- "(tables)": function names used outside any function, such as handler tables.

The site links each function to GitHub at the commit this ran on, so run it on a clean tree for exact line links.
Areas (GROUPS below) are assigned by hand; a new module without one stops the script with its name.
"""
import argparse
import bisect
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
OUT = ROOT / "docs" / "advanced" / "code-map.js"

GROUPS = {
    "core": "main loader yw4load dispatch yw4cpu yw4fp yw4rt crypto setjmp host game_ini version sha256 sysinfo log "
            "c11_keywords msvc_shim dlc_known mat4",
    "system": "kernel hle hle_diag hle_libc hle_math hle_mem hle_os hle_string heap ipc ipc_simple svc_acc svc_am "
              "svc_audio svc_fs svc_hid svc_misc svc_nifm svc_sm svc_time savefs romfs swkbd vi ec modmerge",
    "nvn": "nvn nvn_cmdbuf nvn_objects nvn_shader tegra pixels",
    "vulkan": "gpu gpu_draw gpu_internal gpu_queue gpu_pcache gpu_query vk window",
    "passes": "gbuffer shadow shadow_mask gpu_shadow bloom dof post gpu_post gpu_aa bones widescreen framerate",
    "upscale": "gpu_fsr gpu_dlss gpu_dlssg gpu_fg",
    "overlay": "gamemenu ui hud hud_style theme settings textin pause shortcutwheel mousemenu gamelogo gaiji_create "
               "bugreport diaryrows cheats battle bindings run discord discord_game discord_ipc",
    "debug": "perf events profile gpu_passes gpu_watch gpu_ab memscan trace_drawlist ai_trace",
}

KEYWORDS = {"if", "while", "for", "switch", "return", "sizeof", "defined", "else", "do", "case"}
DEF = re.compile(r'^([A-Za-z_][^;{}()#=]*?)\b([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*\(([^;{}]*?)\)\s*(?:const\s*)?\{', re.M)
IDENT = re.compile(r'\b[A-Za-z_]\w*\b')
INCLUDE = re.compile(r'^\s*#\s*include\s*"([^"]+)"', re.M)
STRIP = re.compile(r'//[^\n]*|/\*.*?\*/|"(?:\\.|[^"\\\n])*"|\'(?:\\.|[^\'\\\n])*\'', re.S)


def git(*args):
    return subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(ROOT), *args], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout


def strip(src):
    """Comments and string/char literals out, newlines kept (so line numbers still match)."""
    return STRIP.sub(lambda m: "\n" * m.group(0).count("\n") if m.group(0).startswith("/") else '""', src)


def top_comment(src):
    m = re.match(r'\s*(?:/\*(.*?)\*/|((?://[^\n]*\n\s*)+))', src, re.S)
    if not m:
        return ""
    text = m.group(1) or m.group(2)
    text = " ".join(re.sub(r'^\s*(//+|\*+)\s?', '', text, flags=re.M).split())
    s = " ".join(re.split(r'(?<=[.!?])\s+', text)[:2])
    return s[:280] + ("…" if len(s) > 280 else "")


def comment_above(lines, start_line):
    out, i = [], start_line - 2
    while i >= 0:
        s = lines[i].strip()
        if s.startswith(("//", "/*", "*")) or s.endswith("*/"):
            out.append(s)
            i -= 1
        else:
            break
    if not out:
        return ""
    text = re.sub(r'/\*+|\*+/', ' ', "\n".join(reversed(out)))
    text = " ".join(re.sub(r'^\s*(//+|\*+)\s?', '', text, flags=re.M).split())
    return text[:420] + ("…" if len(text) > 420 else "")


def match_brace(text, i):
    depth = 0
    for j in range(i, len(text)):
        if text[j] == "{":
            depth += 1
        elif text[j] == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0:
                return j
    return -1


def build():
    files = [f for f in git("ls-files", "runtime/src", "runtime/include").split() if f.endswith((".c", ".h", ".cpp"))]
    mod_of = lambda f: os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(f))[0]
    raw, clean = {}, {}
    for f in files:
        raw[f] = (ROOT / f).read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        clean[f] = strip(raw[f])

    group_of = {m: g for g, names in GROUPS.items() for m in names.split()}
    mods = {}
    for f in files:
        m = mods.setdefault(mod_of(f), {"id": mod_of(f), "files": [], "loc": 0, "blurb": ""})
        m["files"].append(f)
        m["loc"] += sum(1 for line in raw[f].splitlines() if line.strip())
    missing = sorted(m for m in mods if m not in group_of)
    if missing:
        sys.exit("code_map: no area for " + ", ".join(missing) + " (add it to GROUPS in tools/dev/code_map.py)")
    for m in mods.values():
        m["group"] = group_of[m["id"]]
        m["files"].sort(key=lambda x: (x.endswith(".h"), x))
        m["blurb"] = next((b for b in (top_comment(raw[f]) for f in m["files"]) if b), "")

    # functions: definitions, bodies, file-scope text with the bodies blanked out
    funcs, bodies, scope_text = {}, [], {}
    for f in files:
        mod, text = mod_of(f), clean[f]
        nl = [i for i, c in enumerate(text) if c == "\n"]
        line_of = lambda pos: bisect.bisect_right(nl, pos - 1) + 1
        raw_lines = raw[f].splitlines()
        spans, last_end = [], -1
        for d in DEF.finditer(text):
            if d.start() <= last_end:
                continue
            prefix, name = d.group(1), d.group(2)
            if name in KEYWORDS or prefix.strip() in ("", "else", "return"):
                continue
            end = match_brace(text, d.end() - 1)
            if end < 0:
                continue
            last_end = end
            static = bool(re.search(r'\bstatic\b', prefix))
            key = f"{mod}:{name}" if static else name
            if key in funcs:
                continue
            start_line = line_of(d.start())
            funcs[key] = {"k": key, "n": name, "m": mod, "f": f, "l": line_of(d.start(2)),
                          "len": line_of(end) - start_line + 1, "s": int(static),
                          "d": comment_above(raw_lines, start_line), "c": {}}
            bodies.append((key, mod, text[d.end() - 1:end + 1]))
            spans.append((d.start(), end + 1))
        if not f.endswith(".h"):
            t = list(text)
            for a, b in spans:
                for i in range(a, b):
                    if t[i] != "\n":
                        t[i] = " "
            scope_text[f] = "".join(t)

    def resolve(tok, mod):
        if f"{mod}:{tok}" in funcs:
            return f"{mod}:{tok}"
        return tok if tok in funcs else None

    for key, mod, body in bodies:
        for tok in IDENT.findall(body):
            k = resolve(tok, mod)
            if k and k != key:
                funcs[key]["c"][k] = 1
    for f, text in scope_text.items():
        mod, depth, used = mod_of(f), 0, {}
        for m in re.finditer(r'[{}]|\b[A-Za-z_]\w*\b', text):
            tok = m.group(0)
            if tok == "{":
                depth += 1
            elif tok == "}":
                depth = max(0, depth - 1)
            elif depth > 0 and (k := resolve(tok, mod)):
                used[k] = 1
        if used:
            key = f"{mod}:(tables)"
            funcs[key] = {"k": key, "n": "(tables)", "m": mod, "f": f, "l": 1, "len": 0, "s": 1,
                          "d": "Function names used outside any function: tables of function pointers, handlers and the like.",
                          "c": used}

    # module links: includes, and uses of another module's public functions
    owner = {fn["n"]: fn["m"] for fn in funcs.values() if not fn["s"]}
    edges = defaultdict(lambda: {"include": False, "fns": set()})
    for f in files:
        src = mod_of(f)
        for h in INCLUDE.findall(raw[f]):
            tgt = mod_of(h)
            if tgt in mods and tgt != src:
                edges[(src, tgt)]["include"] = True
        if f.endswith(".h"):
            continue
        for tok in IDENT.findall(clean[f]):
            o = owner.get(tok)
            if o and o != src:
                edges[(src, o)]["fns"].add(tok)

    nodes = [mods[k] for k in sorted(mods)]
    links = [{"source": s, "target": t, "include": e["include"], "fnCount": len(e["fns"]), "fns": sorted(e["fns"])[:60]}
             for (s, t), e in sorted(edges.items())]
    func_list = [{**fn, "c": sorted(fn["c"])} for fn in sorted(funcs.values(), key=lambda x: (x["m"], x["l"], x["k"]))]
    return {"nodes": nodes, "links": links, "funcs": func_list}


def render(data, commit, date):
    payload = json.dumps({"commit": commit, "date": date, **data}, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
    return ("// Generated by python -m tools.dev.code_map from runtime/ — do not edit. Read by docs/advanced/index.html.\n"
            f"window.CODE_MAP = {payload};\n")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--check", action="store_true", help="exit 1 if docs/advanced/code-map.js is out of date")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    data = build()
    if args.check:
        try:
            text = OUT.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            old = json.loads(text[text.index("{"):text.rindex("}") + 1])
        except (OSError, ValueError):
            sys.exit(f"code_map: {OUT.relative_to(ROOT)} is missing or unreadable; run python -m tools.dev.code_map")
        old.pop("commit", None), old.pop("date", None)
        if old != json.loads(json.dumps(data)):
            sys.exit("code_map: docs/advanced/code-map.js is out of date; run python -m tools.dev.code_map")
        print("code_map: up to date")
        return
    commit = git("rev-parse", "HEAD").strip()
    date = git("log", "-1", "--format=%cs").strip()
    OUT.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    OUT.write_text(render(data, commit, date), encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    n_funcs = sum(1 for f in data["funcs"] if f["n"] != "(tables)")
    print(f"code_map: {len(data['nodes'])} modules, {n_funcs} functions, {len(data['links'])} module links "
          f"-> {OUT.relative_to(ROOT)} ({OUT.stat().st_size // 1024} KB)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

`tools/dev/decisions.py`:

```py
"""The decision records' index, and checks that the docs still point at things that exist.

    python -m tools.dev.decisions            write docs/decisions/README.md from the records' headers
    python -m tools.dev.decisions --check    check, write nothing; exit 1 on a problem

Each record (docs/decisions/NNNN-*.md) carries a header right under its title, hidden when Markdown is shown:

    <!-- decision
    state: accepted | plan | proposed | rejected
    date: YYYY-MM-DD
    replaces: none | 0005 (part), 0042
    code: none | runtime/src/gamemenu.c, runtime/src/ui.c
    -->

"Replaced by" is never written by hand: the index works it out from the other records' `replaces`.

--check finds: records without a header or with a bad one; `code` paths that no longer exist; "decision NNNN"
mentions (in the docs, the README, CLAUDE.md and the code) of a record that doesn't exist; relative Markdown links
to files that don't exist; and an index that is out of date. Only the repo's own text files are read (never
work/), so it is quick and needs no game files.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import re
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
DECISIONS = REPO / "docs" / "decisions"
INDEX = DECISIONS / "README.md"
STATES = ("accepted", "plan", "proposed", "rejected")

HEADER = re.compile(r"<!-- decision\n(.*?)\n-->", re.S)
TITLE = re.compile(r"^# (\d{4}) — (.+)$", re.M)
# "decision 0053", "decisions 0047, 0050 and 0054", "Decision 0052"
MENTION = re.compile(r"\b[Dd]ecisions? ((?:\d{4})(?:(?:, | and | or |/)\d{4})*)")
MDLINK = re.compile(r"\]\(([^)\s#]+)(?:#[^)]*)?\)")
# where mentions are looked for: the repo's own text, never work/ or third-party code
SCAN = ["README.md", "CLAUDE.md", "docs", "runtime/src", "runtime/include", "recomp", "tools", "launcher/ui",
        "launcher/src-tauri/src"]
SCAN_EXT = {".md", ".c", ".h", ".cpp", ".py", ".rs", ".js", ".html", ".toml", ".glsl", ".comp", ".frag", ".vert"}


@dataclass
class Record:
    number: str
    title: str
    path: Path
    state: str = ""
    date: str = ""
    replaces: list[tuple[str, bool]] = field(default_factory=list)  # (number, only part)
    code: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    problems: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)


def read_records() -> list[Record]:
    out = []
    for p in sorted(DECISIONS.glob("[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-*.md")):
        text = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        t = TITLE.search(text)
        r = Record(p.name[:4], t.group(2).strip() if t else p.stem, p)
        if not t or t.group(1) != r.number:
            r.problems.append("its title isn't '# NNNN — Title' with its own number")
        h = HEADER.search(text)
        if not h:
            r.problems.append("no '<!-- decision' header")
            out.append(r)
            continue
        fields = {}
        for line in h.group(1).splitlines():
            k, _, v = line.partition(":")
            fields[k.strip()] = v.strip()
        r.state, r.date = fields.get("state", ""), fields.get("date", "")
        if r.state not in STATES:
            r.problems.append(f"state '{r.state}' isn't one of {', '.join(STATES)}")
        if not re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}", r.date):
            r.problems.append(f"date '{r.date}' isn't YYYY-MM-DD")
        rep = fields.get("replaces", "none")
        if rep and rep != "none":
            for part in rep.split(","):
                m = re.fullmatch(r"\s*(\d{4})\s*(\(part\))?\s*", part)
                if m:
                    r.replaces.append((m.group(1), bool(m.group(2))))
                else:
                    r.problems.append(f"replaces '{part.strip()}' isn't 'NNNN' or 'NNNN (part)'")
        code = fields.get("code", "none")
        if code and code != "none":
            r.code = [c.strip() for c in code.split(",") if c.strip()]
        out.append(r)
    return out


def index_text(records: list[Record]) -> str:
    by = {r.number: r for r in records}
    replaced_by: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for r in records:
        for n, part in r.replaces:
            replaced_by.setdefault(n, []).append(f"{r.number}{' (part)' if part else ''}")
    lines = [
        "# Decisions",
        "",
        "Why the project is built the way it is: one record per choice, numbered in the order they were made. This",
        "index is generated from the records' headers by `python -m tools.dev.decisions` (do not edit it by hand);",
        "`--check` also checks the docs' links and the code's `decision NNNN` mentions.",
        "",
        "States: **accepted** (in use), **plan** (agreed, not built yet), **proposed**, **rejected**. *Replaced by*",
        "lists later records that replace a record, or part of it.",
        "",
        "| # | Decision | State | Date | Replaced by | Code |",
        "|---|---|---|---|---|---|",
    ]
    for r in records:
        rb = ", ".join(f"[{x}]({by[x[:4]].path.name})" if x[:4] in by else x for x in replaced_by.get(r.number, []))
        code = ", ".join(f"`{c}`" for c in r.code)
        lines.append(f"| {r.number} | [{r.title}]({r.path.name}) | {r.state} | {r.date} | {rb} | {code} |")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def scan_files() -> list[Path]:
    out = []
    for s in SCAN:
        p = REPO / s
        if p.is_file():
            out.append(p)
        elif p.is_dir():
            out += [f for f in p.rglob("*") if f.is_file() and f.suffix in SCAN_EXT and "node_modules" not in f.parts]
    return out


def check(records: list[Record]) -> list[str]:
    problems = []
    numbers = {r.number for r in records}
    for r in records:
        problems += [f"{r.path.relative_to(REPO).as_posix()}: {p}" for p in r.problems]
        for c in r.code:
            if not (REPO / c).exists():
                problems.append(f"{r.path.relative_to(REPO).as_posix()}: code path {c} doesn't exist")
        for n, _ in r.replaces:
            if n not in numbers:
                problems.append(f"{r.path.relative_to(REPO).as_posix()}: replaces {n}, which doesn't exist")
    for f in scan_files():
        rel = f.relative_to(REPO).as_posix()
        text = f.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        for m in MENTION.finditer(text):
            for n in re.findall(r"\d{4}", m.group(1)):
                if n not in numbers:
                    line = text.count("\n", 0, m.start()) + 1
                    problems.append(f"{rel}:{line}: mentions decision {n}, which doesn't exist")
        if f.suffix != ".md":
            continue
        for m in MDLINK.finditer(text):
            target = m.group(1)
            if re.match(r"[a-z]+:", target):  # http:, https:, mailto:
                continue
            if not (f.parent / target).exists():
                line = text.count("\n", 0, m.start()) + 1
                problems.append(f"{rel}:{line}: links to {target}, which doesn't exist")
    if not INDEX.is_file() or INDEX.read_text(encoding="utf-8") != index_text(records):
        problems.append("docs/decisions/README.md is out of date: run python -m tools.dev.decisions")
    return problems


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--check", action="store_true", help="check, write nothing; exit 1 on a problem")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    records = read_records()
    if args.check:
        problems = check(records)
        for p in problems:
            print(p)
        print(f"{len(records)} decisions, {len(problems)} problem(s)")
        return 1 if problems else 0
    bad = [f"{r.path.name}: {p}" for r in records for p in r.problems]
    if bad:
        print("\n".join(bad), file=sys.stderr)
        print("fix these headers first (python -m tools.dev.decisions --check lists everything)", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    INDEX.write_text(index_text(records), encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    print(f"wrote {INDEX.relative_to(REPO).as_posix()} ({len(records)} decisions)")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

`tools/dev/frame_ab.py`:

```py
"""Compare two renderings within one run: image dumps of alternating frames (A on some, B on others).

    python -m tools.dev.frame_ab --addr 7269783000 --a 1801 1803 1805 --b 1802 1804 [--noise 7268f13000]

Reads work/dump/image_<addr>_f<frame>_0.rgbaf (YW4_DUMP_IMAGE with a list in YW4_DUMP_IMAGE_AT). Pixels that
are identical in all the A frames count as stable; for each B frame it reports how many stable pixels differ
from the first A frame. Things that move between frames still show up, so give --noise an image the B
setting does not change: its count is the motion baseline, and B is right when its count is no larger.

How the G-buffer programs were checked (decision 0026): YW4_GBUFFER_ALTERNATE=1800 (odd GPU frames ours),
YW4_DUMP_IMAGE=<the targets> YW4_DUMP_IMAGE_AT=1801,...,1806 (a frame dumped as F was drawn as F-1).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import struct
import sys

import numpy as np

from tools.yw4 import config


def load(cfg: config.Config, addr: str, frame: int) -> np.ndarray:
    b = (cfg.work_dir / "dump" / f"image_{addr}_f{frame}_0.rgbaf").read_bytes()
    w, h = struct.unpack("<II", b[:8])
    return np.frombuffer(b[8:8 + w * h * 16], dtype="<f4").reshape(h, w, 4)


def report(cfg: config.Config, addr: str, a_frames: list[int], b_frames: list[int], label: str) -> None:
    a = [load(cfg, addr, f) for f in a_frames]
    stable = np.ones(a[0].shape[:2], bool)
    for x in a[1:]:
        stable &= np.all(x == a[0], axis=2)
    for f in b_frames:
        d = np.abs(load(cfg, addr, f) - a[0]).max(axis=2)
        n = int((stable & (d > 0)).sum())
        mx = float(d[stable].max()) if stable.any() else 0.0
        print(f"{label} {addr} frame {f}: {int(stable.sum())} stable pixels, {n} differ (max {mx:.4f})")


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--addr", nargs="+", required=True, help="dumped image addresses (hex, as in the file names)")
    ap.add_argument("--a", nargs="+", type=int, required=True, help="frames with the reference setting")
    ap.add_argument("--b", nargs="+", type=int, required=True, help="frames with the setting under test")
    ap.add_argument("--noise", nargs="*", default=[], help="images the tested setting does not change")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    cfg = config.load(require_exefs=False)
    for addr in a.addr:
        report(cfg, addr, a.a, a.b, "tested")
    for addr in a.noise:
        report(cfg, addr, a.a, a.b, "noise ")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

`tools/dev/minimap.py`:

```py
"""Catch the minimap going blank: run the game with the minimap watch on, then say what it saw.

    python -m tools.dev.minimap run SCENE [--settings none|owner|FILE] [--frames N] [--seconds N]
    python -m tools.dev.minimap play [--save NAME] [--replay FILE]
    python -m tools.dev.minimap report [FOLDER]

`run` plays a scene of tools/dev/scenes.toml (tools.dev.scene: `walk` is the one that moves). `play` starts the
game for the owner to play, with their settings and keys, from a fresh copy of a save (default
save_base_lategame), until they close it: the bug shows "sometimes", and a person walking around finds it sooner
than a replay does. Both end with the report; `report` prints it again for a folder (default: the last one).

The watch itself is in the runtime (runtime/src/gpu_watch.c, YW4_MINIMAP_WATCH=1). Every frame, for each of the
minimap's own images (340x304, 516x460), it counts:

    draws    draws into the image                 (fewer: the game, or we, didn't draw the map)
    clears   colour clears of it
    shown    draws elsewhere that sample it       (0: the image never reached the screen)
    missing  texture slots of its draws with no texture behind them (they read black)
    fresh    textures made or uploaded for its draws in that very frame
    lit      texels brighter than black, per mille (the image read back: the truth about "blank")
    opaque   texels with alpha, per mille

and when a count or the picture drops it writes an event, the pictures before / blank / after (.bmp) and the two
frames' draws with their textures (minimap_<frame>_draws.txt). Everything goes in <work>/shots_minimap/<name>/:
delete it when done (`python -m tools.dev.scene --clean minimap`).

A gap of a few frames is the bug. A long one is the game hiding the minimap (a menu, a loading screen, a
cutscene); the report lists those apart.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from tools.dev import scene
from tools.dev.run import run
from tools.yw4 import config

TASK = "minimap"
SHORT = 90  # frames: a gap up to this long is a suspect, longer is the game hiding the minimap


def load(folder: Path) -> tuple[list[dict], dict[tuple[int, str], dict]]:
    """The watch's events, and its rows by (frame, image): the counts joined with the picture's numbers."""
    events = []
    for f in sorted(folder.glob("perf_*.jsonl")):
        for line in f.read_text(errors="ignore").splitlines():
            try:
                e = json.loads(line)
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                continue  # a line cut short when the game was stopped
            if e.get("kind") == "minimap":
                events.append(e)
    rows: dict[tuple[int, str], dict] = {}
    for name in ("minimap_draws.csv", "minimap_pixels.csv"):
        p = folder / name
        if not p.is_file():
            continue
        with p.open(newline="") as fh:
            for r in csv.DictReader(fh):
                try:
                    key = (int(r["frame"]), r["target"])
                except (KeyError, ValueError, TypeError):
                    continue
                rows.setdefault(key, {}).update({k: v for k, v in r.items() if k not in ("frame", "target")})
    return events, rows


def gaps(events: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    """Each drop with its recovery: {frame, target, of (pixels or draws), frames (None: never came back), event}."""
    out, open_ = [], {}
    for e in events:
        what, target = e.get("what"), e.get("target")
        if what in ("back", "stays"):
            g = open_.pop((target, e.get("of")), None)
            if g:
                g["frames"] = e.get("frames")
                g["stayed"] = what == "stays"
        else:
            of = "pixels" if what == "pixels" else "draws"
            g = {"frame": e["frame"], "target": target, "of": of, "what": what, "frames": None, "stayed": False, "event": e}
            if what != "missing":  # a missing texture is logged once; it has no recovery
                open_[(target, of)] = g
            out.append(g)
    return out


def describe(g: dict) -> str:
    e = g["event"]
    if g["what"] == "pixels":
        return f"picture went blank: lit {e['lit'][0]} -> {e['lit'][1]}, opaque {e['opaque'][0]} -> {e['opaque'][1]} per mille"
    parts = [f"draws into it {e['draws'][0]} -> {e['draws'][1]}", f"on screen {e['shown'][0]} -> {e['shown'][1]}"]
    if e["missing"][1] > e["missing"][0]:
        parts.append(f"missing textures {e['missing'][0]} -> {e['missing'][1]}")
    if e.get("fresh"):
        parts.append(f"{e['fresh']} textures uploaded in that frame")
    return ", ".join(parts)


def table(rows: dict[tuple[int, str], dict], target: str, first: int, last: int) -> list[str]:
    cols = ("draws", "clears", "shown", "missing", "fresh", "verts", "lit_pm", "opaque_pm")
    out = ["      frame " + " ".join(f"{c.removesuffix('_pm'):>7}" for c in cols)]
    for f in range(first, last + 1):
        r = rows.get((f, target))
        if r:
            out.append(f"    {f:7} " + " ".join(f"{r.get(c, '-'):>7}" for c in cols))
    return out


def report(folder: Path) -> int:
    events, rows = load(folder)
    if not rows:
        print(f"no minimap watch files in {folder} (was the game run with YW4_MINIMAP_WATCH=1, and did it reach the world?)")
        return 1
    targets = sorted({t for _, t in rows})
    frames = sorted({f for f, _ in rows})
    print(f"{folder}\nwatched frames {frames[0]} to {frames[-1]}; minimap images: {', '.join(targets)}")
    for t in targets:
        mine = [r for (_, tt), r in rows.items() if tt == t]
        drawn = sorted(int(r["draws"]) for r in mine if "draws" in r and int(r["draws"]))
        lit = sorted(int(r["lit_pm"]) for r in mine if "lit_pm" in r)
        print(f"  {t}: drawn in {len(drawn)} frames" + (f", usually {drawn[len(drawn) // 2]} draws" if drawn else "") +
              (f", usually {lit[len(lit) // 2]} per mille lit" if lit else ", picture never read"))
    all_gaps = gaps(events)
    suspects = [g for g in all_gaps if g["frames"] is not None and g["frames"] <= SHORT and not g["stayed"]]
    other = [g for g in all_gaps if g not in suspects]
    print(f"\n{len(suspects)} short gaps (the bug, if any):" if suspects else "\nno short gap caught.")
    for g in suspects:
        print(f"  frame {g['frame']}, image {g['target']}, {g['frames']} frames: {describe(g)}")
        print("\n".join(table(rows, g["target"], g["frame"] - 3, g["frame"] + g["frames"] + 2)))
        files = sorted(p.name for p in folder.glob(f"minimap_{g['frame']:06d}_*"))
        if files:
            print("    files: " + ", ".join(files))
    if other:
        print(f"\n{len(other)} other changes (long: a menu, a loading screen, a cutscene; or still open at the end):")
        for g in other[:30]:
            how = "to the end of the run" if g["frames"] is None else f"{g['frames']} frames"
            print(f"  frame {g['frame']}, image {g['target']}, {how}: {describe(g)}")
    return 0


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    r = sub.add_parser("run", help="a scene of scenes.toml with the watch on, then the report")
    r.add_argument("scene")
    r.add_argument("--settings", default="owner", help="none (30 frames/s), owner (default: a copy of theirs), or a file")
    r.add_argument("--frames", type=int)
    r.add_argument("--seconds", type=int)
    r.add_argument("env", nargs="*", help="ENV=value for the game")
    p = sub.add_parser("play", help="the owner plays with the watch on until they close the game, then the report")
    p.add_argument("--save", default="save_base_lategame", help="folder in <work>/testsaves (copied first)")
    p.add_argument("--replay", default="load_save.txt", help="file in <work>/inputs that gets into the save")
    p.add_argument("env", nargs="*", help="ENV=value for the game")
    t = sub.add_parser("report", help="the report of a folder again")
    t.add_argument("folder", nargs="?", type=Path)
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    cfg = config.load()
    task_dir = cfg.work_dir / f"shots_{TASK}"

    if a.cmd == "report":
        folder = a.folder
        if not folder:
            done = sorted((d for d in task_dir.glob("*") if (d / "minimap_draws.csv").is_file()),
                          key=lambda d: (d / "minimap_draws.csv").stat().st_mtime)
            if not done:
                print(f"nothing in {task_dir} yet: run or play first")
                return 1
            folder = done[-1]
        return report(folder)

    if a.cmd == "run":
        out = task_dir / a.scene
        args = [a.scene, "--task", TASK, "--settings", a.settings, "YW4_MINIMAP_WATCH=1", f"YW4_MINIMAP_DIR={out}", *a.env]
        if a.frames:
            args += ["--frames", str(a.frames)]
        if a.seconds:
            args += ["--seconds", str(a.seconds)]
        code = scene.main(args)
        if code == 2:  # refused before starting
            return code
        print()
        return report(out) or code

    out = task_dir / "play"
    save = cfg.work_dir / "testsaves" / a.save
    replay = cfg.work_dir / "inputs" / a.replay
    settings = cfg.work_dir / "build" / "settings.ini"
    missing = [str(x) for x in (save, replay, settings) if not x.exists()]
    if missing:
        print("not started: missing " + ", ".join(missing), file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for f in out.glob("*"):  # the last session's files: one session per folder
        if f.is_file():
            f.unlink()
    print(f"play from {a.save}; close the game when the minimap has gone blank a few times. Files in {out}", flush=True)
    env = [f"YW4_SETTINGS_FILE={settings}", "YW4_MOUSE=1", "YW4_AUDIO=1", "YW4_MINIMAP_WATCH=1", f"YW4_MINIMAP_DIR={out}",
           f"YW4_PERF_DIR={out}", *a.env]
    run(cfg, save, replay, 0, False, env, None, None, out / "run.log")
    print()
    return report(out)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

`tools/dev/padtest.c`:

```c
/* padtest: what SDL3 (the game's own copy) sees of a controller, and what the game would do with each button.
 * Built and started by `python -m tools.dev.padtest`. Not part of the game.
 *
 * For each button press it prints the button's place on the pad (bottom, right, left, top), the letter SDL thinks is
 * printed on it, and the Switch button the game gives for it. The game picks Xbox, PlayStation or Nintendo names from
 * the type the pad reports (bindings.c, bindings_read): a pad that reports "Xbox 360" but has A on the right gets
 * the Xbox meaning, so its printed letters and the game's disagree. It also shows how the pad is connected (USB or
 * Bluetooth) and finger positions on a touchpad (PlayStation pads; over Bluetooth only once SDL has switched the pad
 * to its full reports). Quit: Back + Start together, or Ctrl+C. */
#include <stdio.h>

#include <SDL3/SDL.h>

static const char *place(int b) {
    switch (b) {
    case SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_SOUTH: return "BOTTOM face button";
    case SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_EAST: return "RIGHT face button ";
    case SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_WEST: return "LEFT face button  ";
    case SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_NORTH: return "TOP face button   ";
    case SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_BACK: return "Back / View / Minus";
    case SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_START: return "Start / Menu / Plus";
    case SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_GUIDE: return "Guide / Home";
    case SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_LEFT_SHOULDER: return "Left shoulder";
    case SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_RIGHT_SHOULDER: return "Right shoulder";
    case SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_LEFT_STICK: return "Left stick press";
    case SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_RIGHT_STICK: return "Right stick press";
    case SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_DPAD_UP: return "D-pad up";
    case SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_DPAD_DOWN: return "D-pad down";
    case SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_DPAD_LEFT: return "D-pad left";
    case SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_DPAD_RIGHT: return "D-pad right";
    case SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_TOUCHPAD: return "Touchpad click";
    default: return "other button";
    }
}

static const char *label(SDL_GamepadButtonLabel l) {
    static const char *const n[] = {"?", "A", "B", "X", "Y", "Cross", "Circle", "Square", "Triangle"};
    return l >= 0 && l < (int)(sizeof n / sizeof *n) ? n[l] : "?";
}

/* bindings.c's pad_style rule */
static int style_of(SDL_GamepadType t) {
    if (t == SDL_GAMEPAD_TYPE_PS3 || t == SDL_GAMEPAD_TYPE_PS4 || t == SDL_GAMEPAD_TYPE_PS5) return 1;
    if (t >= SDL_GAMEPAD_TYPE_NINTENDO_SWITCH_PRO && t <= SDL_GAMEPAD_TYPE_NINTENDO_SWITCH_JOYCON_PAIR) return 2;
    return 0;
}

/* the Switch button the game gives for a face button (bindings.c's resolve, default bindings) */
static const char *switch_button(int style, int b) {
    if (style == 2) {
        switch (b) {
        case SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_EAST: return "A";
        case SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_SOUTH: return "B";
        case SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_NORTH: return "X";
        case SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_WEST: return "Y";
        }
    } else {
        switch (b) {
        case SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_SOUTH: return "A";
        case SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_EAST: return "B";
        case SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_WEST: return "X";
        case SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_NORTH: return "Y";
        }
    }
    return NULL;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    (void)argc, (void)argv;
    SDL_SetHint(SDL_HINT_JOYSTICK_ALLOW_BACKGROUND_EVENTS, "1");  /* events while the console has focus */
    if (!SDL_Init(SDL_INIT_GAMEPAD)) {
        fprintf(stderr, "padtest: SDL_Init failed: %s\n", SDL_GetError());
        return 1;
    }
    printf("padtest (SDL %d.%d.%d)\n", SDL_VERSIONNUM_MAJOR(SDL_GetVersion()), SDL_VERSIONNUM_MINOR(SDL_GetVersion()),
           SDL_VERSIONNUM_MICRO(SDL_GetVersion()));
    printf("Plug in the controller if it isn't, then press the 4 face buttons one by one.\n");
    printf("Quit: Back + Start together, or Ctrl+C.\n\n");
    fflush(stdout);
    static const char *const style_name[] = {"Xbox", "PlayStation", "Nintendo"};
    SDL_Gamepad *pad = NULL;
    int style = 0, running = 1;
    while (running) {
        SDL_Event e;
        if (!SDL_WaitEventTimeout(&e, 200)) continue;
        switch (e.type) {
        case SDL_EVENT_QUIT: running = 0; break;
        case SDL_EVENT_GAMEPAD_ADDED:
            if (pad) break;
            pad = SDL_OpenGamepad(e.gdevice.which);
            if (!pad) break;
            {
                SDL_GamepadType t = SDL_GetGamepadType(pad);
                style = style_of(t);
                char *map = SDL_GetGamepadMapping(pad);
                printf("Connected: %s\n", SDL_GetGamepadName(pad));
                printf("  reports type: %s (vendor %04x, product %04x)\n", SDL_GetGamepadStringForType(t),
                       SDL_GetGamepadVendor(pad), SDL_GetGamepadProduct(pad));
                printf("  the game uses: %s button names\n", style_name[style]);
                SDL_JoystickConnectionState cs = SDL_GetGamepadConnectionState(pad);
                printf("  connected by: %s\n", cs == SDL_JOYSTICK_CONNECTION_WIRED      ? "USB"
                                               : cs == SDL_JOYSTICK_CONNECTION_WIRELESS ? "wireless (Bluetooth)"
                                                                                        : "unknown");
                printf("  touchpads: %d%s\n", SDL_GetNumGamepadTouchpads(pad),
                       SDL_GetNumGamepadTouchpads(pad) ? " (drag a finger on it)" : "");
                printf("  SDL mapping: %s\n\n", map ? map : "(none)");
                SDL_free(map);
            }
            fflush(stdout);
            break;
        case SDL_EVENT_GAMEPAD_REMOVED:
            if (pad && SDL_GetGamepadID(pad) == e.gdevice.which) {
                SDL_CloseGamepad(pad);
                pad = NULL;
                printf("Controller removed.\n\n");
                fflush(stdout);
            }
            break;
        case SDL_EVENT_GAMEPAD_TOUCHPAD_DOWN:
        case SDL_EVENT_GAMEPAD_TOUCHPAD_UP:
        case SDL_EVENT_GAMEPAD_TOUCHPAD_MOTION: {
            /* a finger: x, y from 0 to 1 across the touchpad; moves at most ten times a second */
            static Uint64 last;
            Uint64 now = SDL_GetTicks();
            if (e.type == SDL_EVENT_GAMEPAD_TOUCHPAD_MOTION && now - last < 100) break;
            last = now;
            printf("Touch finger %d %-5s x %.3f  y %.3f\n", (int)e.gtouchpad.finger,
                   e.type == SDL_EVENT_GAMEPAD_TOUCHPAD_DOWN ? "down" : e.type == SDL_EVENT_GAMEPAD_TOUCHPAD_UP ? "up" : "move",
                   e.gtouchpad.x, e.gtouchpad.y);
            fflush(stdout);
            break;
        }
        case SDL_EVENT_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_DOWN: {
            if (!pad || SDL_GetGamepadID(pad) != e.gbutton.which) break;
            int b = e.gbutton.button;
            const char *sw = switch_button(style, b);
            if (sw)
                printf("%s  SDL thinks it says: %-8s  the game presses Switch %s\n", place(b),
                       label(SDL_GetGamepadButtonLabel(pad, (SDL_GamepadButton)b)), sw);
            else
                printf("%s\n", place(b));
            fflush(stdout);
            if (SDL_GetGamepadButton(pad, SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_BACK) && SDL_GetGamepadButton(pad, SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_START))
                running = 0;
            break;
        }
        }
    }
    if (pad) SDL_CloseGamepad(pad);
    SDL_Quit();
    return 0;
}

```

`tools/dev/padtest.py`:

```py
"""Controller test: press buttons and see what SDL3 and the game make of each one (tools/dev/padtest.c).

    python -m tools.dev.padtest

Builds work/build/padtest(.exe) with the game's compiler and SDL3 (rebuilt when padtest.c changes), then runs it
in this console. Use it when a controller's printed letters and the game's button icons disagree: it shows the
type the pad reports, which names the game picks from that, and for each face button its place, the letter SDL
thinks is printed on it, and the Switch button the game presses.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import subprocess
import sys

from tools.yw4 import config, deps

from recomp import check


def main() -> int:
    cfg = config.load()
    src = check.REPO / "tools" / "dev" / "padtest.c"
    build = cfg.work_dir / "build"
    build.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    exe = build / ("padtest.exe" if sys.platform == "win32" else "padtest")
    if not exe.exists() or exe.stat().st_mtime < src.stat().st_mtime:
        if sys.platform == "win32":
            sdl = deps.fetch_sdl(cfg)  # the game's SDL3; its DLL is already next to yw4.exe in work/build
            flags = [f"-I{sdl / 'include'}", str(sdl / "lib" / "libSDL3.dll.a")]
            dll = build / "SDL3.dll"
            if not dll.exists():
                dll.write_bytes((sdl / "bin" / "SDL3.dll").read_bytes())
        else:
            pc = lambda *a: subprocess.run(["pkg-config", *a, "sdl3"], capture_output=True, text=True,
                                           check=True).stdout.split()
            flags = pc("--cflags") + pc("--libs")
        cc = str(cfg.cc) if getattr(cfg, "cc", None) else "cc"
        cmd = [cc, "-std=c11", "-O1", "-Wall", str(src), *flags, "-o", str(exe)]
        print("building", exe.name)
        if subprocess.run(cmd).returncode:
            return 1
    return subprocess.run([str(exe)]).returncode


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

`tools/dev/perf_compare.py`:

```py
"""Performance of two settings, alternating runs of one replay; averages from the logs' whole-run summaries.

    python -m tools.dev.perf_compare --a YW4_SHADOWS=game --b YW4_SHADOWS=native
                                     [--pairs 3] [--save DIR] [--replay FILE] [--seconds N]

Run-to-run noise is about +-1 ms of game work: compare the averages over all pairs, never one run, and
make sure nothing else is running (a forgotten game spoiled a whole comparison once).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from tools.dev.run import run
from tools.yw4 import config


def periodic(text: str) -> dict[str, float]:
    """A run stopped by the time limit writes no whole-run summary: the periodic ones instead,
    averaged, without the first two (title and loading)."""
    out = {}
    for key, label in (("work", "game work ms"), ("gpu", "GPU busy ms")):
        found = re.findall(label + r": avg ([\d.]+)\s+p50 [\d.]+\s+p95 ([\d.]+)", text)[2:]
        if found:
            out[key] = sum(float(a) for a, _ in found) / len(found)
            out[key + "_p95"] = sum(float(b) for _, b in found) / len(found)
    cpu = [float(x) for x in re.findall(r"process CPU: (\d+)%", text)][2:]
    if cpu:
        out["cpu"] = sum(cpu) / len(cpu)
    return out


def summary(log: Path) -> dict[str, float]:
    text = log.read_text(errors="ignore")
    i = text.rfind("perf, whole run")
    if i < 0:
        return periodic(text)
    part = text[i:i + 2000]
    out = {}
    for key, label in (("work", "game work ms"), ("gpu", "GPU busy ms")):
        m = re.search(label + r": avg ([\d.]+)\s+p50 [\d.]+\s+p95 ([\d.]+)", part)
        if m:
            out[key], out[key + "_p95"] = float(m.group(1)), float(m.group(2))
    m = re.search(r"process CPU: (\d+)%", part)
    if m:
        out["cpu"] = float(m.group(1))
    return out


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--a", nargs="+", required=True, help="ENV=value settings of the first")
    ap.add_argument("--b", nargs="+", required=True, help="... and of the second")
    ap.add_argument("--pairs", type=int, default=3)
    ap.add_argument("--save", type=Path, default=Path("work/testsaves/save_base_walk"))
    ap.add_argument("--replay", type=Path, default=Path("work/inputs/walk.txt"))
    ap.add_argument("--seconds", type=int, default=600)
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    cfg = config.load()
    results = {"a": [], "b": []}
    for i in range(a.pairs):
        for side in ("a", "b"):
            log = run(cfg, a.save, a.replay, a.seconds, True, getattr(a, side))
            s = summary(log)
            results[side].append(s)
            print(f"{side} run {i + 1}: {s}  ({log})")
    for side in ("a", "b"):
        rs = [r for r in results[side] if r]
        if rs:
            avg = {k: sum(r.get(k, 0) for r in rs) / len(rs) for k in rs[0]}
            print(side, " ".join(f"{k} {v:.2f}" for k, v in avg.items()))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

`tools/dev/pipebench.c`:

```c
/* pipebench: times how long the Vulkan driver takes to build a graphics pipeline from one
 * translated fragment shader (work/shaders/glsl/<key>.frag.spv + .iface + .json), cold: the
 * SPIR-V gets a random OpString so the driver's shader cache can't answer (PB_NOSALT=1: as is; PB_SALT=<n>:
 * a fixed one, to test what the cache keys on; PB_FORMAT=<VkFormat>, PB_BLEND=1: other target state).
 *   pipebench.exe <stub vertex .spv> <glsl dir> <key> [<key> ...]
 * Built and run by tools/dev/pipebench.py (README.md).
 * Descriptor bindings follow runtime/src/gpu_draw.c (c: slot, t: 16+slot, d: 96+slot, p: 95,
 * s: 64+n, i: 16+slot; fragment stage = set 1). Vertex stage: a stub that writes gl_Position. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <windows.h>
#include <vulkan/vulkan.h>

static void *read_file(const char *path, size_t *n) {
    FILE *f = fopen(path, "rb");
    if (!f) return NULL;
    fseek(f, 0, SEEK_END);
    *n = (size_t)ftell(f);
    fseek(f, 0, SEEK_SET);
    char *p = malloc(*n + 1);
    fread(p, 1, *n, f);
    p[*n] = 0;
    fclose(f);
    return p;
}

#define CHECK(x) do { VkResult r_ = (x); if (r_) { fprintf(stderr, "%s: %d\n", #x, r_); exit(1); } } while (0)


/* Copy of the SPIR-V with an OpString "<salt>" inserted before the first debug instruction. */
static uint32_t *salted(const uint32_t *w, size_t nw, size_t *out_n, unsigned salt) {
    char s[32];
    int len = snprintf(s, sizeof s, "pipebench%u", salt);
    size_t sw = (size_t)(len + 4) / 4;  /* string words, nul included */
    uint32_t *o = calloc(nw + 2 + sw, 4);
    size_t at = 5;
    while (at < nw) {
        uint32_t op = w[at] & 0xFFFF, wc = w[at] >> 16;
        if (op == 3 || op == 4 || op == 5 || op == 6 || op == 7 || op == 71 || op == 72) break;  /* debug or annotation */
        at += wc;
    }
    memcpy(o, w, at * 4);
    uint32_t id = o[3]++;  /* bound */
    o[at] = (uint32_t)((2 + sw) << 16) | 7;
    o[at + 1] = id;
    memcpy(&o[at + 2], s, (size_t)len);
    memcpy(&o[at + 2 + sw], w + at, (nw - at) * 4);
    *out_n = (nw + 2 + sw) * 4;
    return o;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    if (argc < 4) { fprintf(stderr, "pipebench <stub vertex .spv> <glsl dir> <key>...\n"); return 1; }
    const char *dir = argv[2];
    VkApplicationInfo app = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_APPLICATION_INFO, .apiVersion = VK_API_VERSION_1_3};
    VkInstanceCreateInfo ici = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_INSTANCE_CREATE_INFO, .pApplicationInfo = &app};
    VkInstance inst;
    CHECK(vkCreateInstance(&ici, NULL, &inst));
    uint32_t np = 8;
    VkPhysicalDevice pds[8];
    CHECK(vkEnumeratePhysicalDevices(inst, &np, pds));
    VkPhysicalDevice pd = pds[0];
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < np; i++) {
        VkPhysicalDeviceProperties pr;
        vkGetPhysicalDeviceProperties(pds[i], &pr);
        if (pr.deviceType == VK_PHYSICAL_DEVICE_TYPE_DISCRETE_GPU) pd = pds[i];
    }
    float prio = 1;
    VkDeviceQueueCreateInfo qci = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_DEVICE_QUEUE_CREATE_INFO, .queueCount = 1, .pQueuePriorities = &prio};
    VkPhysicalDeviceVulkan13Features f13 = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PHYSICAL_DEVICE_VULKAN_1_3_FEATURES, .dynamicRendering = VK_TRUE};
    VkDeviceCreateInfo dci = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_DEVICE_CREATE_INFO, .pNext = &f13, .queueCreateInfoCount = 1, .pQueueCreateInfos = &qci};
    VkDevice dev;
    CHECK(vkCreateDevice(pd, &dci, NULL, &dev));

    size_t vn;
    uint32_t *vspv = read_file(argv[1], &vn);  /* #version 460 / void main() { gl_Position = vec4(0.0); } */
    if (!vspv) { fprintf(stderr, "no stub vertex shader %s\n", argv[1]); return 1; }
    VkShaderModuleCreateInfo vmci = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_SHADER_MODULE_CREATE_INFO, .codeSize = vn, .pCode = vspv};
    VkShaderModule vmod;
    CHECK(vkCreateShaderModule(dev, &vmci, NULL, &vmod));
    VkDescriptorSetLayoutCreateInfo empty = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_DESCRIPTOR_SET_LAYOUT_CREATE_INFO};
    VkDescriptorSetLayout set0;
    CHECK(vkCreateDescriptorSetLayout(dev, &empty, NULL, &set0));
    unsigned salt = (unsigned)GetTickCount() ^ (unsigned)GetCurrentProcessId() << 16;
    const char *e = getenv("PB_SALT");
    if (e) salt = (unsigned)atoi(e);
    VkFormat color_fmt = getenv("PB_FORMAT") ? (VkFormat)atoi(getenv("PB_FORMAT")) : VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM;
    int blend = getenv("PB_BLEND") != NULL;

    for (int a = 3; a < argc; a++) {
        char path[1024];
        size_t n;
        snprintf(path, sizeof path, "%s/%s.frag.spv", dir, argv[a]);
        uint32_t *spv = read_file(path, &n);
        if (!spv) { fprintf(stderr, "%s: missing\n", path); continue; }
        size_t sn;
        uint32_t *s = getenv("PB_NOSALT") ? (sn = n, spv) : salted(spv, n / 4, &sn, e ? salt : salt + (unsigned)a);
        snprintf(path, sizeof path, "%s/%s.iface", dir, argv[a]);
        char *iface = read_file(path, &n);
        VkDescriptorSetLayoutBinding lb[64];
        int nb = 0;
        for (char *line = strtok(iface, "\n"); line; line = strtok(NULL, "\n")) {
            char kind;
            unsigned slot;
            if (sscanf(line, "%c %u", &kind, &slot) < 2 || kind == 'a') continue;
            VkDescriptorSetLayoutBinding *l = &lb[nb++];
            *l = (VkDescriptorSetLayoutBinding){.descriptorCount = 1, .stageFlags = VK_SHADER_STAGE_FRAGMENT_BIT};
            switch (kind) {
            case 'c': l->binding = slot, l->descriptorType = VK_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_UNIFORM_BUFFER; break;
            case 't': l->binding = 16 + slot, l->descriptorType = VK_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_COMBINED_IMAGE_SAMPLER; break;
            case 'd': l->binding = 96 + slot, l->descriptorType = VK_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_COMBINED_IMAGE_SAMPLER; break;
            case 'p': l->binding = 95, l->descriptorType = VK_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_UNIFORM_BUFFER; break;
            case 'i': l->binding = 16 + slot, l->descriptorType = VK_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_STORAGE_IMAGE; break;
            case 's': l->binding = 64 + slot, l->descriptorType = VK_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_STORAGE_BUFFER; break;
            default: nb--;
            }
        }
        VkDescriptorSetLayoutCreateInfo lci = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_DESCRIPTOR_SET_LAYOUT_CREATE_INFO, .bindingCount = (uint32_t)nb, .pBindings = lb};
        VkDescriptorSetLayout set1;
        CHECK(vkCreateDescriptorSetLayout(dev, &lci, NULL, &set1));
        VkDescriptorSetLayout sets[2] = {set0, set1};
        VkPipelineLayoutCreateInfo plci = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PIPELINE_LAYOUT_CREATE_INFO, .setLayoutCount = 2, .pSetLayouts = sets};
        VkPipelineLayout layout;
        CHECK(vkCreatePipelineLayout(dev, &plci, NULL, &layout));

        /* colour outputs from the .json "colors": [..] (count of entries) */
        snprintf(path, sizeof path, "%s/%s.json", dir, argv[a]);
        char *json = read_file(path, &n);
        int ncolor = 0;
        char *c = json ? strstr(json, "\"colors\": [") : NULL;
        if (c) for (c += 11; *c && *c != ']'; c++) if (*c >= '0' && *c <= '9' && (c[1] == ',' || c[1] == ']')) ncolor = *c - '0' + 1;
        VkFormat fmts[8];
        VkPipelineColorBlendAttachmentState att[8];
        for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) fmts[i] = color_fmt, att[i] = (VkPipelineColorBlendAttachmentState){.colorWriteMask = 0xF, .blendEnable = (VkBool32)blend,
            .srcColorBlendFactor = VK_BLEND_FACTOR_SRC_ALPHA, .dstColorBlendFactor = VK_BLEND_FACTOR_ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA,
            .srcAlphaBlendFactor = VK_BLEND_FACTOR_ONE, .dstAlphaBlendFactor = VK_BLEND_FACTOR_ZERO};

        VkShaderModuleCreateInfo mci = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_SHADER_MODULE_CREATE_INFO, .codeSize = sn, .pCode = s};
        VkShaderModule fmod;
        CHECK(vkCreateShaderModule(dev, &mci, NULL, &fmod));
        VkPipelineShaderStageCreateInfo st[2] = {
            {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PIPELINE_SHADER_STAGE_CREATE_INFO, .stage = VK_SHADER_STAGE_VERTEX_BIT, .module = vmod, .pName = "main"},
            {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PIPELINE_SHADER_STAGE_CREATE_INFO, .stage = VK_SHADER_STAGE_FRAGMENT_BIT, .module = fmod, .pName = "main"}};
        VkPipelineVertexInputStateCreateInfo vi = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PIPELINE_VERTEX_INPUT_STATE_CREATE_INFO};
        VkPipelineInputAssemblyStateCreateInfo ia = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PIPELINE_INPUT_ASSEMBLY_STATE_CREATE_INFO, .topology = VK_PRIMITIVE_TOPOLOGY_TRIANGLE_LIST};
        VkPipelineViewportStateCreateInfo vp = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PIPELINE_VIEWPORT_STATE_CREATE_INFO, .viewportCount = 1, .scissorCount = 1};
        VkPipelineRasterizationStateCreateInfo rs = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PIPELINE_RASTERIZATION_STATE_CREATE_INFO, .lineWidth = 1};
        VkPipelineMultisampleStateCreateInfo ms = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PIPELINE_MULTISAMPLE_STATE_CREATE_INFO, .rasterizationSamples = VK_SAMPLE_COUNT_1_BIT};
        VkPipelineDepthStencilStateCreateInfo ds = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PIPELINE_DEPTH_STENCIL_STATE_CREATE_INFO};
        VkPipelineColorBlendStateCreateInfo cbs = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PIPELINE_COLOR_BLEND_STATE_CREATE_INFO, .attachmentCount = (uint32_t)ncolor, .pAttachments = att};
        VkDynamicState dyn[] = {VK_DYNAMIC_STATE_VIEWPORT, VK_DYNAMIC_STATE_SCISSOR};
        VkPipelineDynamicStateCreateInfo dy = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PIPELINE_DYNAMIC_STATE_CREATE_INFO, .dynamicStateCount = 2, .pDynamicStates = dyn};
        VkPipelineRenderingCreateInfo ri = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PIPELINE_RENDERING_CREATE_INFO, .colorAttachmentCount = (uint32_t)ncolor, .pColorAttachmentFormats = fmts};
        VkGraphicsPipelineCreateInfo pci = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_GRAPHICS_PIPELINE_CREATE_INFO, .pNext = &ri, .stageCount = 2, .pStages = st,
            .pVertexInputState = &vi, .pInputAssemblyState = &ia, .pViewportState = &vp, .pRasterizationState = &rs,
            .pMultisampleState = &ms, .pDepthStencilState = &ds, .pColorBlendState = &cbs, .pDynamicState = &dy, .layout = layout};
        LARGE_INTEGER f, t0, t1;
        QueryPerformanceFrequency(&f);
        QueryPerformanceCounter(&t0);
        VkPipeline pipe;
        VkResult r = vkCreateGraphicsPipelines(dev, VK_NULL_HANDLE, 1, &pci, NULL, &pipe);
        QueryPerformanceCounter(&t1);
        printf("%s %8.1f ms%s\n", argv[a], (double)(t1.QuadPart - t0.QuadPart) * 1000.0 / (double)f.QuadPart, r ? " (FAILED)" : "");
        fflush(stdout);
        if (!r) vkDestroyPipeline(dev, pipe, NULL);
    }
    return 0;
}
```
