```py
        _na_text(d, S, c, 24, 12, (255, 247, 207, 255), edge=(150, 126, 58, 255))
    elif style in ("xbox", "ps"):
        r = 14
        a = 24 if style == "xbox" else 12
        d = ImageDraw.Draw(big)
        d.ellipse(((c - r - 2) * S, (c - r - 2) * S, (c + r + 2) * S, (c + r + 2) * S), fill=(255, 255, 255, a // 2))
        d.ellipse(((c - r - 1) * S, (c - r - 1) * S, (c + r + 1) * S, (c + r + 1) * S), fill=(255, 255, 255, a))
        d.ellipse(((c - r) * S, (c - r) * S, (c + r) * S, (c + r) * S), fill=(0, 0, 0, 255) if style == "xbox" else (16, 16, 16, 255))
        m = Image.new("L", big.size, 0)
        inset = 1 if style == "xbox" else 1.5
        ImageDraw.Draw(m).ellipse(((c - r + inset) * S, (c - r + inset) * S, (c + r - inset) * S, (c + r - inset) * S), fill=255)
        face = Image.new("RGBA", big.size, (36, 36, 36, 255))
        if style == "xbox":  # near black, a little lighter low down (4 at the top half to 13)
            fd = ImageDraw.Draw(face)
            for y in range(big.height):
                g = int(4 + 9 * max(0.0, (y / S - c) / (r - 1)))
                fd.line([(0, y), (big.width, y)], fill=(g, g, g, 255))
        big.paste(face, (0, 0), m)
        _na_text(ImageDraw.Draw(big), S, c, c, 9.5 if style == "xbox" else 8.5,
                 (255, 255, 255, 255) if style == "xbox" else (225, 225, 230, 255))
    else:  # the Switch circle: its 64 cell's look at 48 (x 0.75)
        r = 24 * 0.75
        shadow = Image.new("RGBA", big.size, (0, 0, 0, 0))
        ImageDraw.Draw(shadow).ellipse(((c - r - 1) * S, (c - r) * S, (c + r + 1) * S, (c + r + 2.5) * S), fill=(34, 20, 120, 90))
        big.alpha_composite(shadow.filter(ImageFilter.GaussianBlur(1.6 * S)))
        d = ImageDraw.Draw(big)
        d.ellipse(((c - r) * S, (c - r + 0.8) * S, (c + r) * S, (c + r + 0.8) * S), fill=(154, 154, 203, 255))  # the rim
        d.ellipse(((c - r) * S, (c - r) * S, (c + r) * S, (c + r - 0.6) * S), fill=(225, 225, 251, 255))
        _na_text(d, S, c, c, 12, (90, 90, 134, 255))
    return big.resize((CELL, CELL), Image.LANCZOS)


def region_blocks(linear: bytes, sheet_w: int, x: int, y: int, w: int, h: int) -> bytes:
    pitch = sheet_w // 4 * 16
    return b"".join(linear[by * pitch + x // 4 * 16: by * pitch + (x + w) // 4 * 16] for by in range(y // 4, (y + h) // 4))


def load_sheet(name: str) -> bytes:
    """A sheet from the owner's font.cpk, as linear rows of BC7 blocks (256 x 256; the keyboard sheet 620 x 620)."""
    font_cpk = config.load().romfs_dir / "data" / "nx" / "font" / "font.cpk"
    entry = next(f for f in cpk.list_files(font_cpk).files if f.path.endswith("/" + name))
    data = cpk.read(font_cpk, entry)
    u16 = lambda off: int.from_bytes(data[off:off + 2], "little")
    nxtch = 4 * (u16(0x0A) + u16(0x3E))
    w = int.from_bytes(data[nxtch + 0x14:nxtch + 0x18], "little")
    h = int.from_bytes(data[nxtch + 0x18:nxtch + 0x1C], "little")
    want = (620, 620) if name == "gaiji_key.g4tx" else (256, 256)
    if (w, h) != want:
        raise SystemExit(f"error: {name} is {w}x{h}, expected {want[0]}x{want[1]}")
    return bytes(deswizzle_bc7(data[nxtch + 0x100:], w, h))


def c_array(fp, name: str, data: bytes, indent: str = "") -> None:
    fp.write(f"{indent}static const unsigned char {name}[{len(data)}] = {{\n")
    for i in range(0, len(data), 16):
        fp.write(indent + "    " + ", ".join(f"0x{b:02x}" for b in data[i:i + 16]) + ",\n")
    fp.write(indent + "};\n")


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="runtime/src/gaiji_create.h")
    ap.add_argument("--preview", help="also save the new icons (with the sheets' own parts) as a PNG")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    ps = load_sheet("gaiji_ps4.g4tx")
    xb = load_sheet("gaiji_xinput.g4tx")
    print_ = fnv1a64(cell_blocks(ps, 256, TOUCHPAD_AT))
    view_print = fnv1a64(cell_blocks(xb, 256, XBOX_VIEW_AT))
    key = load_sheet("gaiji_key.g4tx")
    key_print = fnv1a64(cell_blocks(key, 620, KEY_E_AT))
    na = [encode(draw_na(style)) for style in NA_STYLES]

    tops = [encode(draw_top(word)) for word in WORDS]
    back, start = encode(draw_xbox360("left")), encode(draw_xbox360("right"))
    n = len(tops[0])
    with open(args.out, "w", newline="\n") as fp:
        fp.write("/* Generated by python -m tools.yw4.gaiji_create (our drawings; no game pixels).\n"
                 " * PlayStation sheet: the middle-button words, each as rows 0-23 of an icon (the word and the pill's\n"
                 " * top) in 12 x 6 BC7 blocks, linear rows; the fingerprint (FNV-1a 64) of the touchpad icon's 12 x 12\n"
                 " * blocks. Xbox sheet: an Xbox 360 pad's Back and Start, the middle 6 x 4 blocks of the circle icon\n"
                 " * (x 12-35, y 16-31 of the cell); the fingerprint of the View icon's 12 x 12 blocks. */\n")
        fp.write(f"#define GAIJI_TOUCHPAD_PRINT 0x{print_:016x}ull\n")
        fp.write(f"#define GAIJI_XBOX_VIEW_PRINT 0x{view_print:016x}ull\n")
        fp.write("enum { " + ", ".join(f"GAIJI_WORD_{w}" for w in WORDS) + ", GAIJI_WORDS };\n")
        fp.write(f"static const unsigned char gaiji_word_top[GAIJI_WORDS][{n}] = {{\n")
        for word, blocks in zip(WORDS, tops):
            fp.write(f"    /* {word} */ {{\n")
            for i in range(0, n, 16):
                fp.write("        " + ", ".join(f"0x{b:02x}" for b in blocks[i:i + 16]) + ",\n")
            fp.write("    },\n")
        fp.write("};\n")
        c_array(fp, "gaiji_xbox_back", back)
        c_array(fp, "gaiji_xbox_start", start)
        fp.write("/* Keyboard sheet (620 x 620): \"N/A\", for a button with nothing bound, in each style's look, 12 x 12 BC7\n"
                 " * blocks each, written over cells the hints never show; the fingerprint of the E key's blocks. */\n")
        fp.write(f"#define GAIJI_KEY_E_PRINT 0x{key_print:016x}ull\n")
        fp.write("enum { " + ", ".join(f"GAIJI_NA_{s.upper()}" for s in NA_STYLES) + ", GAIJI_NAS };\n")
        fp.write("static const struct { int x, y; const char *name; } gaiji_na_at[GAIJI_NAS] = {\n")
        for s in NA_STYLES:
            fp.write(f"    {{{NA_KEY_AT[s][0]}, {NA_KEY_AT[s][1]}, \"{NA_KEY_NAMES[s]}\"}},\n")
        fp.write("};\n")
        fp.write(f"static const unsigned char gaiji_na[GAIJI_NAS][{len(na[0])}] = {{\n")
        for s, blocks in zip(NA_STYLES, na):
            fp.write(f"    /* {s} */ {{\n")
            for i in range(0, len(blocks), 16):
                fp.write("        " + ", ".join(f"0x{b:02x}" for b in blocks[i:i + 16]) + ",\n")
            fp.write("    },\n")
        fp.write("};\n")
    print(f"wrote {args.out}: {len(WORDS)} words of {n // 16} blocks, Back and Start of {len(back) // 16}, "
          f"{len(na)} N/A icons; prints {print_:016x} {view_print:016x} {key_print:016x}")

    if args.preview:
        # each icon as the runtime builds it, decoded: the PlayStation words over the Options icon's pill; the
        # Xbox middles in the Menu icon's circle
        body = cell_blocks(ps, 256, (OPTIONS_AT[0], OPTIONS_AT[1] + TOP), CELL - TOP)
        icons = [decode_bc7_to_image(t + body, CELL, CELL).convert("RGBA") for t in tops]
        x0, y0, pw, ph = XBOX_PATCH
        for mid in (back, start):
            cell = bytearray(cell_blocks(xb, 256, XBOX_MENU_AT))
            for by in range(ph // 4):
                row = (y0 // 4 + by) * (CELL // 4 * 16) + x0 // 4 * 16
                cell[row:row + pw // 4 * 16] = mid[by * pw // 4 * 16:(by + 1) * pw // 4 * 16]
            icons.append(decode_bc7_to_image(bytes(cell), CELL, CELL).convert("RGBA"))
        out = Image.new("RGBA", (len(icons) * CELL * 5, CELL * 5), (55, 55, 66, 255))
        for i, icon in enumerate(icons):
            out.alpha_composite(icon.resize((CELL * 5, CELL * 5), Image.NEAREST), (i * CELL * 5, 0))
        out.save(args.preview)
        print(f"preview {args.preview}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

`tools/yw4/ghidra.py`:

```py
"""Run Ghidra headless on main and export function boundaries.

    python -m tools.yw4.ghidra            import + analyze (first run: long), then export
    python -m tools.yw4.ghidra --export   re-run only the export on the existing project

Needs [tools] ghidra_dir (with the Switch loader extension installed) and a
verified ingest. The Ghidra project goes in <work_dir>/ghidra/ because its
database contains the game's code (gitignored, CLAUDE.md rule 1).
Output: <work_dir>/ghidra/main.functions.json (see tools/ghidra/ExportFunctions.java).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import os
import subprocess
import sys

from . import config, ingest, nso, recon

SCRIPT_DIR = config.REPO_ROOT / "tools" / "ghidra"
PROJECT_NAME = "yw4"


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    mode = ap.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    mode.add_argument("--export", action="store_true", help="skip import/analysis, only export")
    mode.add_argument("--seed", action="store_true",
                      help="on the existing project, create functions at every .eh_frame_hdr start "
                           "and address-taken target, re-analyze, then export")
    mode.add_argument("--script", nargs="+", metavar=("NAME.java", "ARG"),
                      help="run one script from tools/ghidra on the existing project (no export)")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    try:
        cfg = config.load()
        if cfg.ghidra_dir is None:
            raise config.ConfigError("[tools] ghidra_dir is not set")
    except config.ConfigError as e:
        print(f"config error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    headless = cfg.ghidra_dir / "support" / ("analyzeHeadless.bat" if sys.platform == "win32" else "analyzeHeadless")
    if not headless.is_file():
        print(f"analyzeHeadless not found under {cfg.ghidra_dir}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    # Same version lock as ingest: never analyze a different build.
    main_nso = cfg.exefs_dir / "main"
    want = ingest.load_target().get("image_sha256", "")
    got = hashlib.sha256(nso.flat_image(main_nso.read_bytes())).hexdigest()
    if not want or got != want:
        print("main does not match target.toml; run python -m tools.yw4.ingest first", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    proj = cfg.work_dir / "ghidra"
    proj.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out_json = proj / "main.functions.json"

    cmd = [str(headless), str(proj), PROJECT_NAME]
    if args.script:
        cmd += ["-process", "main", "-noanalysis", "-scriptPath", str(SCRIPT_DIR),
                "-postScript", *args.script]
        log = proj / f"{args.script[0].removesuffix('.java')}.log"
        return run_headless(cmd, log)
    if args.export or args.seed:
        cmd += ["-process", "main", "-noanalysis", "-scriptPath", str(SCRIPT_DIR)]
    else:
        cmd += ["-import", str(main_nso), "-overwrite", "-scriptPath", str(SCRIPT_DIR)]
    if args.seed:
        image, mods = recon.load_main(cfg)
        text_size = mods["main"]["segments"]["text"]["size"]
        starts = set(recon.eh_frame_function_starts(image))
        starts |= recon.address_taken_functions(image, text_size)
        seed_file = proj / "seed_functions.txt"
        seed_file.write_text("".join(f"{a:#x}\n" for a in sorted(starts) if a < text_size))
        cmd += ["-postScript", "SeedFunctions.java", str(seed_file)]
    cmd += ["-postScript", "ExportFunctions.java", str(out_json)]

    log = proj / ("export.log" if args.export else "seed.log" if args.seed else "analyze.log")
    if run_headless(cmd, log) != 0 or not out_json.is_file():
        return 1
    print(f"wrote {out_json}")
    return 0


def run_headless(cmd: list[str], log) -> int:
    print(" ".join(f'"{c}"' if " " in c else c for c in cmd))
    # Ghidra's default 2 GB heap is too small for a 17 MB .text; allow an override.
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env.setdefault("GHIDRA_HEADLESS_MAXMEM", "12G")
    with log.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        rc = subprocess.run(cmd, stdout=f, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, env=env).returncode
    print(f"analyzeHeadless exit {rc}; log: {log}")
    return rc


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

`tools/yw4/guard.py`:

```py
"""Refuse to commit anything that looks like game data (CLAUDE.md rule 1).

    python -m tools.yw4.guard            check the files staged for commit
    python -m tools.yw4.guard --install  install it as .git/hooks/pre-commit

A second line of defence behind .gitignore: it reads every staged file and
blocks the commit if one starts with a Switch / Level-5 / CRI container
signature, contains a NSO's MOD0 module header, or is suspiciously large.
False positives can be committed with `git commit --no-verify` after checking.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
MAX_BYTES = 2 * 1024 * 1024
# Bundled open-licence fonts (third_party/fonts/README.md) may be larger: the overlay's CJK font is 3.7 MB. Only
# the size limit is lifted for them; the signature checks below still run.
LARGE_OK = ("third_party/fonts/",)
LARGE_OK_SUFFIXES = (".ttf", ".otf")

# Signatures at offset 0.
MAGICS = {
    b"NSO0": "NSO executable",
    b"NRO0": "NRO executable",
    b"PFS0": "PFS0 container (NSP/ExeFS)",
    b"HFS0": "HFS0 container (XCI)",
    b"KIP1": "KIP executable",
    b"CPK ": "CRI CPK archive",
    b"@UTF": "CRI table (ACB/ACF)",
    b"AFS2": "CRI AWB audio bank",
    b"CRID": "CRI USM video",
    b"HBH1": "Level-5 shader binary",
    b"G4TX": "Level-5 texture",
    b"G4MG": "Level-5 model",
    b"G4PK": "Level-5 package",
    b"\x7fELF": "ELF binary",
}

HOOK = """#!/bin/sh
# Installed by `python -m tools.yw4.guard --install` (CLAUDE.md rule 1).
exec python -m tools.yw4.guard
"""


def staged_files() -> list[str]:
    out = subprocess.run(["git", "diff", "--cached", "--name-only", "--diff-filter=ACMR", "-z"],
                         cwd=REPO, capture_output=True, check=True).stdout
    return [p for p in out.decode("utf-8").split("\0") if p]


def staged_blob(path: str) -> bytes:
    return subprocess.run(["git", "show", f":{path}"], cwd=REPO, capture_output=True, check=True).stdout


def problem(path: str, data: bytes) -> str | None:
    large_ok = path.startswith(LARGE_OK) and path.endswith(LARGE_OK_SUFFIXES)
    if len(data) > MAX_BYTES and not large_ok:
        return f"{len(data) / 1e6:.1f} MB (limit {MAX_BYTES / 1e6:.0f} MB)"
    kind = MAGICS.get(data[:4])
    if kind:
        return f"starts like a {kind}"
    if b"MOD0" in data[:0x100] and not path.endswith((".py", ".md", ".c", ".h", ".S", ".txt")):
        return "contains a Switch module header (MOD0)"
    return None


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--install", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    if args.install:
        hook = REPO / ".git" / "hooks" / "pre-commit"
        hook.write_text(HOOK, newline="\n")
        hook.chmod(0o755)
        print(f"installed {hook}")
        return 0
    bad = [(p, why) for p in staged_files() if (why := problem(p, staged_blob(p)))]
    for p, why in bad:
        print(f"refusing to commit {p}: {why}", file=sys.stderr)
    if bad:
        print("game data must never be committed (CLAUDE.md rule 1); "
              "if this is a false positive, check it and use --no-verify", file=sys.stderr)
    return 1 if bad else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

`tools/yw4/icon.py`:

```py
"""The game's icon from the user's own NSP or XCI, as <work_dir>/icon/icon.jpg for the launcher's Ready screen, and
on Windows as yw4.ico beside it for the exe (decision 0048).

    python -m tools.yw4.icon

The icon is game data (rule 1): it is never in the repo. It lives in the game's Control NCA (with control.nacp),
which an NSP or XCI holds but extracted ExeFS/RomFS folders don't; without one the exe simply has no icon.
tools.yw4.extract makes it too, from the NCAs it already unpacked.

- Only the small NCAs are unpacked (a Control NCA is under a megabyte; the program is gigabytes), then hactool
  says which is the Control one. The update's is preferred over the base game's: it carries the 4++ icon.
- The icon is a 256x256 JPEG (icon_AmericanEnglish.dat, else another language's). An .ico can't hold a JPEG, so
  Windows' own image library (System.Drawing, through PowerShell) draws it as PNGs at 256, 48, 32 and 16 pixels,
  and this script packs them into the .ico (PNG entries, Windows Vista and later). No Python image library needed.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import re
import shutil
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from . import config, extract, pfs0, xci

SMALL = 64 << 20  # NCAs larger than this are never a Control NCA
SIZES = (256, 48, 32, 16)
LANGS = ("AmericanEnglish", "BritishEnglish", "Japanese")


class IconError(Exception):
    pass


def unpack_small(path: Path, out_dir: Path, tag: str) -> tuple[list[Path], set[str]]:
    """The NCAs under SMALL bytes from an NSP or XCI, and its tickets' rights IDs."""
    ncas, rights_ids = [], set()
    with path.open("rb") as f:
        entries = xci.secure_entries(f) if xci.is_xci(f) else pfs0.read_entries(f)
        for e in entries:
            if e.name.endswith(".tik"):
                rights_ids.add(e.name[:-4].lower())
            elif e.name.endswith(".nca") and not e.name.endswith(".cnmt.nca") and e.size < SMALL:
                dest = out_dir / f"{tag}-{e.name}"
                if not (dest.is_file() and dest.stat().st_size == e.size):
                    pfs0.extract(f, e, dest)
                ncas.append(dest)
    return ncas, rights_ids


def icon_jpeg(hactool: Path, home: Path, ncas: list[Path], tmp: Path) -> Path:
    """The icon JPEG from the first Control NCA in `ncas` (put the preferred ones first)."""
    for n in ncas:
        if not re.search(r"Content Type:\s+Control", extract.run_hactool(hactool, home, ["-i", str(n)])):
            continue
        out = tmp / n.stem
        extract.run_hactool(hactool, home, [f"--romfsdir={out}", str(n)])
        for lang in LANGS:
            if (out / f"icon_{lang}.dat").is_file():
                return out / f"icon_{lang}.dat"
        found = sorted(out.glob("icon_*.dat"))
        if found:
            return found[0]
    raise IconError("no Control NCA with an icon")


def jpeg_to_ico(jpeg: Path, ico: Path, tmp: Path) -> None:
    if sys.platform != "win32":
        raise IconError("making the .ico needs Windows (System.Drawing)")
    script = ("Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Drawing; $src = [System.Drawing.Image]::FromFile($env:YW4_ICON_IN); "
              "foreach ($s in " + ",".join(map(str, SIZES)) + ") { "
              "$b = New-Object System.Drawing.Bitmap $s, $s; $g = [System.Drawing.Graphics]::FromImage($b); "
              "$g.InterpolationMode = 'HighQualityBicubic'; $g.DrawImage($src, 0, 0, $s, $s); "
              "$b.Save((Join-Path $env:YW4_ICON_OUT \"$s.png\"), [System.Drawing.Imaging.ImageFormat]::Png); "
              "$g.Dispose(); $b.Dispose() }; $src.Dispose()")
    env = dict(os.environ, YW4_ICON_IN=str(jpeg), YW4_ICON_OUT=str(tmp))
    r = subprocess.run(["powershell", "-NoProfile", "-NonInteractive", "-Command", script],
                       env=env, capture_output=True, text=True)
    pngs = [(s, tmp / f"{s}.png") for s in SIZES]
    if r.returncode or not all(p.is_file() for _, p in pngs):
        raise IconError(f"PowerShell could not convert the icon: {(r.stderr or r.stdout).strip()[-500:]}")
    data = [p.read_bytes() for _, p in pngs]
    head = struct.pack("<HHH", 0, 1, len(pngs))
    offset = len(head) + 16 * len(pngs)
    entries = b""
    for (s, _), d in zip(pngs, data):
        entries += struct.pack("<BBBBHHII", s % 256, s % 256, 0, 0, 1, 32, len(d), offset)
        offset += len(d)
    ico.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    ico.write_bytes(head + entries + b"".join(data))


def make(cfg: config.Config, home: Path, ncas: list[Path]) -> Path:
    """<work_dir>/icon/icon.jpg from these unpacked NCAs (preferred first; hactool's keys already in `home`): the
    launcher's Ready screen shows it, and its banner blurs it until there is a screenshot. On Windows also yw4.ico
    beside it, for the exe. The JPEG comes first: the .ico needs Windows, and when its error came first a Linux
    install had no picture at all (the launcher showed no icon and no banner)."""
    out = cfg.work_dir / "icon"
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as t:
        tmp = Path(t)
        jpeg = icon_jpeg(cfg.hactool_exe, home, ncas, tmp)
        out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.copyfile(jpeg, out / "icon.jpg")
        if sys.platform != "win32":
            return out / "icon.jpg"
        jpeg_to_ico(jpeg, out / "yw4.ico", tmp)
    return out / "yw4.ico"


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    try:
        cfg = config.load(require_exefs=False)
        files = [p for p in (cfg.update_nsp, cfg.base_nsp) if p is not None]  # the update's icon first
        if not files and cfg.dlc_dir and cfg.dlc_dir.is_dir():
            for p in sorted(cfg.dlc_dir.glob("*.nsp")):
                name = p.name.upper()
                if "010086C00AF7C800" in name or "[UPD]" in name:
                    files.insert(0, p)
                elif "010086C00AF7C000" in name or "[BASE]" in name:
                    files.append(p)
        if not files or cfg.hactool_exe is None or cfg.keys_dir is None:
            raise config.ConfigError("needs base_nsp (or update_nsp), hactool_exe and keys_dir: the icon is only "
                                     "in an NSP or XCI, not in extracted folders")
        nca_dir = cfg.work_dir / "icon" / "nca"
        nca_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        ncas, rids, tkeys = [], set(), {}
        for tag, p in zip(("upd", "base"), files):
            n, r = unpack_small(p, nca_dir, tag)
            ncas, rids = ncas + n, rids | r
            tkeys |= extract.ticket_keys_of(p)
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as t:
            home = Path(t)
            extract.write_temp_keys(cfg.keys_dir, rids, home, tkeys)
            ico = make(cfg, home, ncas)
        shutil.rmtree(nca_dir)
    except (config.ConfigError, IconError, extract.ExtractError, pfs0.Pfs0Error, xci.XciError) as e:
        print(f"icon: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print(f"wrote {ico}" + ("; the next python -m recomp.build puts it in yw4.exe" if ico.suffix == ".ico" else ""))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

`tools/yw4/ingest.py`:

```py
"""Input pipeline: ExeFS modules -> verified flat images in work_dir.

    python -m tools.yw4.ingest          verify main against target.toml, write outputs
    python -m tools.yw4.ingest --pin    record main's hash in target.toml (first run only)

Refuses to write anything if main does not match the pinned build.
Outputs (gitignored): <work_dir>/exefs/<module>.bin and modules.json.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import re
import sys
import tomllib
from pathlib import Path

from . import config, nso, progress

TARGET_PATH = config.REPO_ROOT / "target.toml"
MODULE_NAMES = ("rtld", "main", "sdk") + tuple(f"subsdk{i}" for i in range(10))


def load_target() -> dict[str, str]:
    with TARGET_PATH.open("rb") as f:
        return tomllib.load(f).get("main", {})


def pin_target(image_sha256: str, build_id: str) -> None:
    text = TARGET_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    # only the [main] entries, which come first; [sdk] is pinned separately (tools/yw4/sdkref.py)
    text = re.sub(r'(?m)^image_sha256 = ".*"$', f'image_sha256 = "{image_sha256}"', text, count=1)
    text = re.sub(r'(?m)^build_id = ".*"$', f'build_id = "{build_id}"', text, count=1)
    TARGET_PATH.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")


def process_module(path: Path) -> tuple[nso.Nso, bytes]:
    blob = path.read_bytes()
    header = nso.parse_header(blob)
    return header, nso.flat_image(blob, header)


def describe(name: str, header: nso.Nso, image: bytes) -> dict:
    return {
        "name": name,
        "build_id": nso.build_id_hex(header.build_id),
        "image_sha256": hashlib.sha256(image).hexdigest(),
        "image_size": len(image),
        "bss_size": header.bss_size,
        "segments": {
            s.name: {
                "mem_offset": s.mem_offset,
                "size": s.size,
                "file_size": s.file_size,
                "compressed": s.compressed,
            }
            for s in header.segments
        },
        "dynstr": list(header.dynstr),
        "dynsym": list(header.dynsym),
    }


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--pin", action="store_true",
                    help="record main's hash in target.toml (only when nothing is pinned yet)")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    try:
        cfg = config.load()
    except config.ConfigError as e:
        print(f"config error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    progress.report("ingest", 0, 1)
    # main first: nothing else runs until the build is verified.
    try:
        main_header, main_image = process_module(cfg.exefs_dir / "main")
    except nso.NsoError as e:
        from .extract import DAMAGED
        print(f"{DAMAGED}\n(main: {e})", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    got_hash = hashlib.sha256(main_image).hexdigest()
    got_id = nso.build_id_hex(main_header.build_id)

    target = load_target()
    want_hash = target.get("image_sha256", "")
    if not want_hash:
        if args.pin:
            pin_target(got_hash, got_id)
            print(f"pinned main image_sha256={got_hash} build_id={got_id} in {TARGET_PATH.name}")
            print("Commit target.toml, then run again without --pin.")
            return 0
        print(f"No build pinned in {TARGET_PATH.name}.\n"
              f"  main image_sha256 = {got_hash}\n"
              f"  main build_id     = {got_id}\n"
              "If this is the final 4++ update, run again with --pin.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    if args.pin:
        print(f"{TARGET_PATH.name} already pins a build; edit it by hand to change targets.",
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    if got_hash != want_hash:
        print("This is a different version of the game. Only the final 4++ update, 2.2.0, works: choose that update "
              "in the update box.\n"
              "Wrong game build: main does not match target.toml.\n"
              f"  expected image_sha256 {want_hash} (build_id {target.get('build_id', '?')})\n"
              f"  got      image_sha256 {got_hash} (build_id {got_id})\n"
              "This project supports exactly one version: the final 4++ update.",
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print(f"main OK  build_id={got_id}")

    out_dir = cfg.work_dir / "exefs"
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    modules = []
    for name in MODULE_NAMES:
        path = cfg.exefs_dir / name
        if not path.is_file():
            continue
        if name == "main":
            header, image = main_header, main_image
        else:
            try:
                header, image = process_module(path)
            except nso.NsoError as e:
                from .extract import DAMAGED
                print(f"{DAMAGED}\n({name}: {e})", file=sys.stderr)
                return 1
        (out_dir / f"{name}.bin").write_bytes(image)
        info = describe(name, header, image)
        modules.append(info)
        text = info["segments"]["text"]["size"]
        print(f"{name:9} image {len(image):>11,} bytes  .text {text:>11,}  -> {name}.bin")

    (out_dir / "modules.json").write_text(json.dumps(modules, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"wrote {out_dir}")
    progress.report("ingest", 1, 1)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

`tools/yw4/lz4_block.py`:

```py
"""LZ4 *block* format decoder (no frame header), as used by NSO segments.

Written by hand instead of depending on the `lz4` package: the format is
small, and owning it means we can explain every byte of the input pipeline.

A block is a list of sequences. Each sequence is:
    token        1 byte: high nibble = literal length, low nibble = match length - 4
    [lit ext]    if literal nibble == 15: extra bytes added until one is != 255
    literals     copied straight to the output
    offset       2 bytes little-endian: how far back in the output the match starts
    [match ext]  same extension scheme as literals
The last sequence stops after its literals (no offset, no match).
A match may overlap the bytes it is producing (offset < length); that is how
LZ4 encodes runs, e.g. offset 1 repeats the previous byte.
"""

from __future__ import annotations


def _read_length(src: bytes, i: int, base: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Apply the 255-continuation extension to a nibble value of 15."""
    length = base
    if base == 15:
        while True:
            b = src[i]
            i += 1
            length += b
            if b != 255:
                break
    return length, i


def decompress(src: bytes, out_size: int) -> bytes:
    dst = bytearray()
    i = 0
    n = len(src)
    try:
        while i < n:
            token = src[i]
            i += 1

            lit_len, i = _read_length(src, i, token >> 4)
            if i + lit_len > n:
                raise ValueError("literal run past end of input")
            dst += src[i:i + lit_len]
            i += lit_len
            if i == n:
                break  # last sequence: literals only

            offset = src[i] | (src[i + 1] << 8)
            i += 2
            if offset == 0 or offset > len(dst):
                raise ValueError(f"bad match offset {offset} at output {len(dst)}")

            match_len, i = _read_length(src, i, token & 0x0F)
            match_len += 4

            start = len(dst) - offset
            if offset >= match_len:
                dst += dst[start:start + match_len]
            else:
                # Overlapping copy: the match repeats the last `offset` bytes.
                pattern = bytes(dst[start:])
                reps, rem = divmod(match_len, offset)
                dst += pattern * reps + pattern[:rem]
    except IndexError:
        raise ValueError("truncated LZ4 block") from None

    if len(dst) != out_size:
        raise ValueError(f"decompressed to {len(dst)} bytes, expected {out_size}")
    return bytes(dst)

```

`tools/yw4/mainview.py`:

```py
"""Main-view map from one run's log: which engine function draws into which target.
    python -m tools.yw4.mainview <log with YW4_TRACE_DRAW_CALLERS=1 and YW4_GPU_TRACE=n>
Part 1: per distinct draw caller, the function that issued the draw (third stack frame,
named f_<start> from work/recomp/func_table.c), its shaders and target.
Part 2: the traced draws in order, grouped into passes (consecutive draws with the same colour and
depth target addresses), each with its draw count, target, shaders and the issuing functions."""
import bisect
import re
import sys
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]  # the repo
starts = sorted(int(m.group(1), 16) for m in re.finditer(r"\{\s*0x([0-9a-fA-F]+),",
                                                           (ROOT / "work/recomp/func_table.c").read_text())
                if int(m.group(1), 16) < 0x1100000)


def func_of(off):
    i = bisect.bisect_right(starts, off) - 1
    return f"f_{starts[i]:x}" if i >= 0 else f"?{off:x}"


log = Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text(errors="ignore").splitlines()

# part 1: callers
callers = {}  # (vs, fs, target) -> set of issuing functions
i = 0
while i < len(log):
    m = re.search(r"draw caller: vs (\w+) fs (\w+) target (\S+) \(([^)]*)\)", log[i])
    if m:
        frames = []
        j = i + 1
        while j < len(log) and log[j].startswith("       "):
            frames.append(log[j].strip())
            j += 1
        # the chain after the two NVN wrapper frames, up to the render-job dispatcher (main+0x979850)
        chain = []
        for f in frames[2:]:
            if not f.startswith("main+") or f == "main+0x979850":
                break
            chain.append(func_of(int(f[7:], 16) - 4))
        fn = " < ".join(chain[:5]) or "?"
        callers.setdefault((m.group(1), m.group(2), m.group(3)), set()).add(fn)
        i = j
    else:
        i += 1

# part 2: traced draws, grouped by target
draws = []
cur = None
for ln in log:
    m = re.search(r"gpu draw: vs (\w+) fs (\w+) prim \d+ count (\d+) target (\S+) \(([^)]*)\).*blend (\S+)", ln)
    if m:
        cur = {"vs": m.group(1), "fs": m.group(2), "count": int(m.group(3)), "dims": m.group(4), "desc": m.group(5),
               "blend": m.group(6), "colour": [], "depth": None}
        draws.append(cur)
        continue
    if cur is None:
        continue
    m = re.search(r"colour target (\d+) at (0x\w+).*format (0x\w+)", ln)
    if m:
        cur["colour"].append(f"{m.group(2)}:{m.group(3)}")
    m = re.search(r"depth target at (0x\w+).*format (0x\w+)", ln)
    if m:
        cur["depth"] = f"{m.group(1)}:{m.group(2)}"

passes = []
for d in draws:
    key = (tuple(d["colour"]), d["depth"], d["dims"])
    if not passes or passes[-1]["key"] != key:
        passes.append({"key": key, "draws": []})
    passes[-1]["draws"].append(d)

print(f"{len(callers)} distinct callers, {len(draws)} traced draws, {len(passes)} passes\n")
for n, p in enumerate(passes):
    ds = p["draws"]
    fns = Counter()
    for d in ds:
        for f in callers.get((d["vs"], d["fs"], d["dims"]), {"?"}):
            fns[f] += 1
    progs = Counter(f"{d['vs'][:6]}/{d['fs'][:6]}" for d in ds)
    col, dep, dims = p["key"]
    print(f"pass {n:3}: {len(ds):4} draws  {dims:10} {ds[0]['desc']:24} colour {' '.join(c.split(':')[1] for c in col) or '-':18}"
          f" depth {dep.split(':')[1] if dep else '-':5}  blend {Counter(d['blend'] for d in ds).most_common(1)[0][0]}")
    print(f"           by {', '.join(f'{f} x{c}' for f, c in fns.most_common(3))}")
    print(f"           programs {', '.join(f'{k} x{c}' for k, c in progs.most_common(4))}{' ...' if len(progs) > 4 else ''}")

```

`tools/yw4/nso.py`:

```py
"""Parse an NSO module and turn it into a flat memory image.

NSO is the Switch's executable format for ExeFS modules (rtld, main, sdk,
subsdk*). Layout of the 0x100-byte header (all little-endian u32 unless noted):

    0x00 magic "NSO0"           0x04 version        0x0C flags
    0x10 text  {file_off, mem_off, size}            0x1C module name offset
    0x20 ro    {file_off, mem_off, size}            0x2C module name size
    0x30 data  {file_off, mem_off, size}            0x3C bss size
    0x40 module_id (build ID, 0x20 bytes)
    0x60 text/ro/data size *in the file* (compressed size, 3 x u32)
    0x88 .api_info, 0x90 .dynstr, 0x98 .dynsym  {offset, size} relative to ro
    0xA0 SHA-256 of decompressed text, ro, data (3 x 0x20 bytes)

flags: bits 0-2 = text/ro/data is LZ4-compressed, bits 3-5 = check its hash.

The "flat image" is what the loader puts in memory: each segment at its
mem_off, gaps zero-filled, .bss not included. We hash that image to identify
the build, because it does not depend on how the NSO happened to be
compressed or which tool converted it.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import struct
from dataclasses import dataclass

from . import lz4_block

HEADER_SIZE = 0x100
SEGMENT_NAMES = ("text", "ro", "data")


class NsoError(Exception):
    pass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Segment:
    name: str
    file_offset: int
    mem_offset: int
    size: int            # decompressed size
    file_size: int       # size in the file (compressed size if compressed)
    compressed: bool
    check_hash: bool
    sha256: bytes        # expected hash of decompressed bytes, from the header


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Nso:
    version: int
    flags: int
    segments: tuple[Segment, Segment, Segment]
    bss_size: int
    build_id: bytes
    api_info: tuple[int, int]
    dynstr: tuple[int, int]
    dynsym: tuple[int, int]


def parse_header(blob: bytes) -> Nso:
    if len(blob) < HEADER_SIZE:
        raise NsoError("file is smaller than an NSO header")
    if blob[:4] != b"NSO0":
        raise NsoError(f"bad magic {blob[:4]!r}, expected b'NSO0'")

    version, _, flags = struct.unpack_from("<3I", blob, 0x04)
    file_sizes = struct.unpack_from("<3I", blob, 0x60)
    segments = []
    for idx, name in enumerate(SEGMENT_NAMES):
        file_off, mem_off, size = struct.unpack_from("<3I", blob, 0x10 + idx * 0x10)
        segments.append(Segment(
            name=name,
            file_offset=file_off,
            mem_offset=mem_off,
            size=size,
            file_size=file_sizes[idx],
            compressed=bool(flags & (1 << idx)),
            check_hash=bool(flags & (1 << (idx + 3))),
            sha256=blob[0xA0 + idx * 0x20:0xC0 + idx * 0x20],
        ))

    return Nso(
        version=version,
        flags=flags,
        segments=tuple(segments),
        bss_size=struct.unpack_from("<I", blob, 0x3C)[0],
        build_id=blob[0x40:0x60],
        api_info=struct.unpack_from("<2I", blob, 0x88),
        dynstr=struct.unpack_from("<2I", blob, 0x90),
        dynsym=struct.unpack_from("<2I", blob, 0x98),
    )


def decompress_segment(blob: bytes, seg: Segment) -> bytes:
    raw = blob[seg.file_offset:seg.file_offset + seg.file_size]
    if len(raw) != seg.file_size:
        raise NsoError(f".{seg.name} runs past end of file")
    try:
        data = lz4_block.decompress(raw, seg.size) if seg.compressed else raw
    except ValueError as e:
        raise NsoError(f".{seg.name}: {e}") from None
    if len(data) != seg.size:
        raise NsoError(f".{seg.name} is {len(data)} bytes, header says {seg.size}")
    if seg.check_hash and hashlib.sha256(data).digest() != seg.sha256:
        raise NsoError(f".{seg.name} SHA-256 does not match the NSO header (corrupt file?)")
    return data


def flat_image(blob: bytes, nso: Nso | None = None) -> bytes:
    """Decompress all segments and lay them out at their memory offsets."""
    nso = nso or parse_header(blob)
    end = max(s.mem_offset + s.size for s in nso.segments)
    image = bytearray(end)
    placed: list[tuple[int, int, str]] = []
    for seg in nso.segments:
        lo, hi = seg.mem_offset, seg.mem_offset + seg.size
        for plo, phi, pname in placed:
            if lo < phi and plo < hi:
                raise NsoError(f".{seg.name} overlaps .{pname} in memory")
        image[lo:hi] = decompress_segment(blob, seg)
        placed.append((lo, hi, seg.name))
    return bytes(image)


def build_id_hex(build_id: bytes) -> str:
    """Build ID as hex with trailing zero bytes trimmed (it is usually 0x14 bytes
    of GNU build-id padded to 0x20)."""
    return build_id.rstrip(b"\0").hex().upper()

```

`tools/yw4/nvn_report.py`:

```py
"""Summarize how main uses NVN, from the Ghidra NvnCallers trace.

    python -m tools.yw4.nvn_report

Needs a seeded Ghidra project (python -m tools.yw4.ghidra --seed). Runs
tools/ghidra/NvnCallers.java, then adds what Ghidra doesn't track:

- NVN entry points live in a table of pointers filled at startup. A function
  that reads a slot is that entry point's *wrapper*.
- Wrappers for draws are mostly not called directly: their addresses are built
  in code (ADRP+ADD) and stored, e.g. into render commands. Functions that take
  a wrapper's address are its *producers*, which is where the engine's render
  layer starts.
- Functions that sit in an RTTI vtable get their class name.

Writes <work_dir>/recon/nvn.md (and nvn.json).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import bisect
import collections
import json
import re
import struct
import sys

from . import config, ghidra, recon, reloc, symbols

DRAW_WORDS = ("Draw", "Dispatch", "QueueSubmit", "PresentTexture", "BindProgram")


def adrp_add_targets(words: tuple[int, ...]):
    """Yield (pc, target) for every ADRP Xd followed within 5 instructions by ADD Xd', Xd, #imm."""
    for i, w in enumerate(words):
        if w & 0x9F000000 != 0x90000000:
            continue
        rd = w & 31
        imm = (((w >> 5) & 0x7FFFF) << 2) | ((w >> 29) & 3)
        if imm & (1 << 20):
            imm -= 1 << 21
        page = ((i * 4) & ~0xFFF) + (imm << 12)
        for j in range(1, 6):
            if i + j >= len(words):
                break
            w2 = words[i + j]
            if w2 & 0xFFC00000 == 0x91000000 and (w2 >> 5) & 31 == rd:
                yield i * 4, page + ((w2 >> 10) & 0xFFF)
                break


def vtable_members(image: bytes, info: dict) -> dict[int, list[tuple[str, int]]]:
    """function entry -> [(demangled class, vtable index)] for primary RTTI vtables."""
    text = info["segments"]["text"]["size"]
    names = recon.dynsym_names(image, info)
    internal, external = reloc.pointer_map(reloc.read_relocs(image))
    typeinfo = {s: recon.c_string(image, internal[s + 8]) for s, (sym, _) in external.items()
                if names[sym] in recon.TYPEINFO_VTABLES and s + 8 in internal}
    dm = symbols.demangle(["_ZTS" + n for n in set(typeinfo.values())])
    members: dict[int, list[tuple[str, int]]] = collections.defaultdict(list)
    for slot, target in internal.items():
        if target not in typeinfo or struct.unpack_from("<q", image, slot - 8)[0] != 0:
            continue
        cls = dm["_ZTS" + typeinfo[target]].removeprefix("typeinfo name for ")
        pos, k = slot + 8, 0
        while pos in internal and internal[pos] < text:
            members[internal[pos]].append((cls, k))
            pos += 8
            k += 1
    return members


def main() -> int:
    try:
        cfg = config.load()
    except config.ConfigError as e:
        print(f"config error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    image, mods = recon.load_main(cfg)
    info = mods["main"]
    gdir = cfg.work_dir / "ghidra"

    names_file = gdir / "nvn_names.txt"
    names_file.write_text("".join(f"{m.start():#x} {m.group().decode()}\n" for m in
                                  re.finditer(rb"(?<=\0)nvn[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_]+(?=\0)", image)))
    trace_file = gdir / "nvn_callers.json"
    if ghidra.main(["--script", "NvnCallers.java", str(names_file), str(trace_file)]) != 0:
        return 1
    entries = json.loads(trace_file.read_text())["entries"]

    text = info["segments"]["text"]["size"]
    words = struct.unpack(f"<{text // 4}I", image[:text // 4 * 4])
    funcs = sorted((f["entry"], f["entry"] + f["size"])
                   for f in json.loads((gdir / "main.functions.json").read_text())["functions"])
    starts = [f[0] for f in funcs]

    def owner(addr: int) -> int | None:
        j = bisect.bisect_right(starts, addr) - 1
        return funcs[j][0] if j >= 0 and addr < funcs[j][1] else None

    wrappers: dict[int, set[str]] = collections.defaultdict(set)
    for e in entries:
        for entry, _ in e["callers"]:
            wrappers[entry].add(e["name"])
    producers: dict[int, set[str]] = collections.defaultdict(set)
    for pc, target in adrp_add_targets(words):
        if target in wrappers:
            o = owner(pc)
            if o is not None:
                producers[o] |= wrappers[target]
    members = vtable_members(image, info)

    def where(fn: int) -> str:
        return ", ".join(f"`{c}`[{k}]" for c, k in members.get(fn, [])[:2]) or "-"

    used = [e for e in entries if e["callers"]]
    by_object = collections.Counter(re.match(r"nvn([A-Z][a-z]+(?:Builder)?)", e["name"]).group(1) for e in used)
    lines = [
        f"- NVN names in main: {len(entries)}; table slots resolved: {sum(e['slot'] is not None for e in entries)}",
        f"- NVN functions actually read by code: **{len(used)}**",
        f"- Wrapper functions: {len(wrappers)}; functions that take a wrapper's address (producers): "
        f"**{len(producers)}**",
        "", "Used functions by object:", "", "| Object | Used |", "|---|---|",
    ]
    lines += [f"| {k} | {v} |" for k, v in by_object.most_common()]
    lines += ["", "Draw / dispatch / submit / present entry points:", "",
              "| NVN function | Wrapper | Wrapper's class | Producers |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
    for e in entries:
        if not any(k in e["name"] for k in DRAW_WORDS):
            continue
        for entry, _ in e["callers"]:
            n = sum(1 for p in producers.values() if e["name"] in p)
            lines.append(f"| `{e['name']}` | `{entry:#x}` | {where(entry)} | {n} |")
    lines += ["", "Largest producers:", "", "| Function | Class | NVN wrappers referenced |", "|---|---|---|"]
    for fn, ws in sorted(producers.items(), key=lambda kv: -len(kv[1]))[:25]:
        short = sorted(w.removeprefix("nvn") for w in ws)
        lines.append(f"| `{fn:#x}` | {where(fn)} | {len(ws)}: {', '.join(short[:5])}{' ...' if len(short) > 5 else ''} |")

    out = cfg.work_dir / "recon"
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (out / "nvn.md").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    (out / "nvn.json").write_text(json.dumps({
        "used": sorted(e["name"] for e in used),
        "wrappers": {hex(k): sorted(v) for k, v in wrappers.items()},
        "producers": {hex(k): sorted(v) for k, v in producers.items()},
    }, indent=1))
    print(f"used NVN functions: {len(used)}  wrappers: {len(wrappers)}  producers: {len(producers)}")
    print(f"wrote {out / 'nvn.md'}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

`tools/yw4/pfs0.py`:

```py
"""Read PFS0 archives (the container format of an NSP and of ExeFS).

Layout (little-endian):
    0x00 magic "PFS0"   0x04 u32 file count   0x08 u32 string table size   0x0C reserved
    then per file (0x18 bytes): u64 data offset, u64 size, u32 name offset, u32 reserved
    then the string table (NUL-terminated names)
    then the file data; data offsets are relative to the end of the string table.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import struct
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import BinaryIO


class Pfs0Error(Exception):
    pass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Entry:
    name: str
    offset: int  # absolute offset in the archive
    size: int


def read_entries(f: BinaryIO) -> list[Entry]:
    f.seek(0)
    head = f.read(0x10)
    if len(head) < 0x10 or head[:4] != b"PFS0":
        raise Pfs0Error("not a PFS0 archive")
    count, strtab_size = struct.unpack_from("<II", head, 4)
    raw_entries = f.read(count * 0x18)
    strtab = f.read(strtab_size)
    if len(raw_entries) != count * 0x18 or len(strtab) != strtab_size:
        raise Pfs0Error("truncated PFS0 header")
    data_start = 0x10 + count * 0x18 + strtab_size

    entries = []
    for i in range(count):
        offset, size, name_off, _ = struct.unpack_from("<QQII", raw_entries, i * 0x18)
        end = strtab.find(b"\0", name_off)
        name = strtab[name_off:end if end >= 0 else None].decode("utf-8")
        entries.append(Entry(name, data_start + offset, size))
    return entries


def extract(f: BinaryIO, entry: Entry, dest: Path, on_bytes=None) -> None:
    """Copy one entry to `dest`; `on_bytes(n)` after each chunk of n bytes, for progress."""
    f.seek(entry.offset)
    with dest.open("wb") as out:
        remaining = entry.size
        while remaining:
            chunk = f.read(min(remaining, 16 << 20))
            if not chunk:
                raise Pfs0Error(f"{entry.name} runs past end of archive")
            out.write(chunk)
            remaining -= len(chunk)
            if on_bytes:
                on_bytes(len(chunk))

```

`tools/yw4/pi/sdkrun.c`:

```c
/* Runs functions of the owner's sdk natively on the ARM64 reference machine (decision 0013).
 *
 *   sdkrun sdk.bin relocs.bin < cases > results
 *
 * sdk.bin is the sdk's flat image (from the owner's own dump, never committed). relocs.bin
 * lists the pointer slots to fill, prepared by tools/yw4/sdkref.py: little-endian records of
 * (u64 slot offset, u64 target offset, u64 kind), kind 0 = image base + target,
 * kind 1 = an import the sdk takes from another module: points at a stop function.
 *
 * Each input line is "<signature> <function offset hex> <argument bits hex>...", and each
 * output line holds the result bits in hex (plus the second result for frexp/modf/modff).
 * Only self-contained leaf-style functions make sense here: nothing that needs threads,
 * TLS or other modules.
 *
 * The Pi's FPCR is 0 at start-up, like every game thread on the Switch (decision 0008).
 */
#include <inttypes.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/mman.h>

static void unresolved_import(void) {
    fprintf(stderr, "sdkrun: the function called an import from another module\n");
    exit(2);
}

static uint8_t *load(const char *image_path, const char *reloc_path, size_t mem_size) {
    FILE *f = fopen(image_path, "rb");
    if (!f) return NULL;
    uint8_t *base = mmap(NULL, mem_size, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE | PROT_EXEC, MAP_PRIVATE | MAP_ANONYMOUS, -1, 0);
    if (base == MAP_FAILED) return NULL;
    size_t n = fread(base, 1, mem_size, f);
    fclose(f);
    if (!n) return NULL;
    FILE *r = fopen(reloc_path, "rb");
    if (!r) return NULL;
    uint64_t rec[3];
    while (fread(rec, 8, 3, r) == 3) {
        uint64_t v = rec[2] == 0 ? (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)base + rec[1] : (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)unresolved_import;
        memcpy(base + rec[0], &v, 8);
    }
    fclose(r);
    __builtin___clear_cache((char *)base, (char *)base + mem_size);
    return base;
}

static double d_of(uint64_t b) { double d; memcpy(&d, &b, 8); return d; }
static float f_of(uint64_t b) { float f; uint32_t u = (uint32_t)b; memcpy(&f, &u, 4); return f; }
static uint64_t bits_d(double d) { uint64_t b; memcpy(&b, &d, 8); return b; }
static uint64_t bits_f(float f) { uint32_t b; memcpy(&b, &f, 4); return b; }

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    if (argc != 4) {
        fprintf(stderr, "usage: sdkrun sdk.bin relocs.bin <memory size>\n");
        return 1;
    }
    uint8_t *base = load(argv[1], argv[2], strtoull(argv[3], NULL, 0));
    if (!base) {
        perror("sdkrun: load");
        return 1;
    }
    char sig[16];
    uint64_t off, a, b;
    char line[256];
    while (fgets(line, sizeof line, stdin)) {
        a = b = 0;
        if (sscanf(line, "%15s %" SCNx64 " %" SCNx64 " %" SCNx64, sig, &off, &a, &b) < 3) continue;
        void *fn = base + off;
        if (!strcmp(sig, "dd")) {
            printf("%016" PRIx64 "\n", bits_d(((double (*)(double))fn)(d_of(a))));
        } else if (!strcmp(sig, "ddd")) {
            printf("%016" PRIx64 "\n", bits_d(((double (*)(double, double))fn)(d_of(a), d_of(b))));
        } else if (!strcmp(sig, "ff")) {
            printf("%08" PRIx64 "\n", bits_f(((float (*)(float))fn)(f_of(a))));
        } else if (!strcmp(sig, "fff")) {
            printf("%08" PRIx64 "\n", bits_f(((float (*)(float, float))fn)(f_of(a), f_of(b))));
        } else if (!strcmp(sig, "frexp")) {
            int e = 0x7eadbeef;
            double r = ((double (*)(double, int *))fn)(d_of(a), &e);
            printf("%016" PRIx64 " %08x\n", bits_d(r), (unsigned)e);
        } else if (!strcmp(sig, "ldexp")) {
            printf("%016" PRIx64 "\n", bits_d(((double (*)(double, int))fn)(d_of(a), (int)(int32_t)b)));
        } else if (!strcmp(sig, "modf")) {
            double ip = 0;
            double r = ((double (*)(double, double *))fn)(d_of(a), &ip);
            printf("%016" PRIx64 " %016" PRIx64 "\n", bits_d(r), bits_d(ip));
        } else if (!strcmp(sig, "modff")) {
            float ip = 0;
            float r = ((float (*)(float, float *))fn)(f_of(a), &ip);
            printf("%08" PRIx64 " %08" PRIx64 "\n", bits_f(r), bits_f(ip));
        } else {
            fprintf(stderr, "sdkrun: unknown signature %s\n", sig);
            return 1;
        }
    }
    return 0;
}

```

`tools/yw4/profile.py`:

```py
"""Name the samples of a YW4_PROFILE=1 run (runtime/src/profile.c).

    python -m tools.yw4.profile [work/perf/profile_<time>.txt] [--top N]

Reads the newest profile by default, maps each yw4.exe offset to the function containing it
with llvm-nm (from the configured llvm-mingw), and prints the share of samples per group
(recompiled main / sdk code, runtime, outside = system DLLs and waits) and the top functions.
f_<hex> is main+<hex>, s_<hex> is sdk+<hex>.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import bisect
import collections
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from recomp import check

IMAGE_BASE = 0x140000000  # the executable's preferred base; profile offsets are relative to it


def symbols(exe: Path) -> tuple[list[int], list[str]]:
    nm = Path(check.host_cc()).with_name("llvm-nm.exe" if sys.platform == "win32" else "llvm-nm")
    out = subprocess.run([str(nm), "--defined-only", str(exe)], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
    syms = []
    for line in out.splitlines():
        parts = line.split()
        if len(parts) == 3 and parts[1] in "Tt":
            syms.append((int(parts[0], 16) - IMAGE_BASE, parts[2]))
    syms.sort()
    return [a for a, _ in syms], [n for _, n in syms]


def group(name: str) -> str:
    if name.startswith("f_"):
        return "game code (main)"
    if name.startswith("s_"):
        return "game code (sdk)"
    if name.startswith(("gpu_", "nvn", "tegra_", "vk", "image_of", "pixel")):
        return "runtime: graphics"
    if name.startswith(("hle_", "musl_")) or name in ("memcpy", "memset", "memmove"):
        return "runtime: C library / HLE"
    return "runtime: other"


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("profile", nargs="?")
    ap.add_argument("--top", type=int, default=40)
    ap.add_argument("--exe", default="work/build/yw4.exe")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    path = Path(args.profile) if args.profile else max(Path("work/perf").glob("profile_*.txt"), key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime)
    addrs, names = symbols(Path(args.exe))
    total = outside = 0
    per_fn: collections.Counter[str] = collections.Counter()
    per_via: collections.Counter[str] = collections.Counter()  # system DLL time, by the yw4.exe caller
    for line in path.read_text().splitlines():
        if line.startswith("#"):
            parts = line.split()
            total, outside = int(parts[2]), int(parts[4])
            continue
        off, n = line.split()
        key = int(off, 16)
        via = key >> 63  # the sample was in a system DLL called from here
        key &= (1 << 63) - 1
        i = bisect.bisect_right(addrs, key) - 1
        name = names[i] if i >= 0 else f"exe+{key:x}"
        if via:
            per_via[name] += int(n)
        else:
            per_fn[name] += int(n)
    print(f"{path}: {total} samples")
    groups: collections.Counter[str] = collections.Counter()
    for fn, n in per_fn.items():
        groups[group(fn)] += n
    groups["outside yw4.exe (system DLLs, waits)"] = outside
    for g, n in groups.most_common():
        print(f"  {100 * n / total:5.1f}%  {g}")
    print(f"top {args.top} functions:")
    for fn, n in per_fn.most_common(args.top):
        print(f"  {100 * n / total:5.1f}%  {fn}")
    print(f"time in system DLLs, by the yw4.exe function that called them (top {args.top}):")
    for fn, n in per_via.most_common(args.top):
        print(f"  {100 * n / total:5.1f}%  {fn}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

`tools/yw4/progress.py`:

```py
"""Progress lines for the launcher (decision 0050): with YW4_PROGRESS=1 the build steps print

    @progress <step> <done> <total> <what>

one per piece of work done, so the launcher can show a bar, the step and time left without parsing their normal
output (which stays the same). Steps: unpack, extract, icon, ingest, translate, shaders, compile, link. <done> and
<total> are counts of that step's own units (bytes, functions, shaders, files); a step with no count reports 0 1
at its start and 1 1 at its end. <what> is free text, possibly empty, on the rest of the line."""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys
import time

_on = os.environ.get("YW4_PROGRESS") == "1"
_last: dict[str, float] = {}


def report(step: str, done: int, total: int, what: str = "", every: float = 0.0) -> None:
    """One progress line (only with YW4_PROGRESS=1). `every`: at most one line per that many seconds for this
    step, except the last (done == total), for steps with very many small units."""
    if not _on:
        return
    now = time.monotonic()
    if every and done < total and now - _last.get(step, 0.0) < every:
        return
    _last[step] = now
    print(f"@progress {step} {done} {total} {what}".rstrip(), flush=True, file=sys.stdout)

```

`tools/yw4/recon.py`:

```py
"""Phase 0 recon: measure main and write tables for docs/recon.md.

    python -m tools.yw4.recon

Needs `python -m tools.yw4.ingest` first. Writes to <work_dir>/recon/:
    imports.json / imports.md   main's imports from sdk, grouped by library
    middleware.md               SDK MW+ tags and engine/middleware string hits
    rtti.json / rtti.md         C++ typeinfo + vtable survey, namespace counts
    code.md                     instruction counts (direct vs indirect branches), unwind-table functions
    render_classes.txt          RTTI class names that look renderer-related
    romfs.md                    RomFS layout and file types, including inside CPK archives

Outputs contain names and counts derived from the game, so they stay in
work/ (gitignored). docs/recon.md quotes the summaries.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import collections
import hashlib
import json
import re
import struct
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from . import config, cpk, ingest, reloc, symbols

TYPEINFO_VTABLES = {
    "_ZTVN10__cxxabiv117__class_type_infoE": "base",
    "_ZTVN10__cxxabiv120__si_class_type_infoE": "single",
    "_ZTVN10__cxxabiv121__vmi_class_type_infoE": "multiple",
}

MIDDLEWARE_KEYWORDS = {
    "CRI (ADX2 / Atom audio)": [b"CRIWARE", b"#CRIATOM", b"ADX2"],
    "CRI Sofdec / Mana (video)": [b"Sofdec", b"CriMana"],
    "CRI File System": [b"CRIFSMEM", b"CriFs"],
    "NVIDIA PhysX": [b"PhysX"],
    "Lua": [b"Lua 5.", b"lua_"],
    "zlib": [b"zlib"],
    "libcurl": [b"libcurl", b"curl_"],
    "Nintendo NEX": [b"nex::"],
    "Nintendo Pia": [b"pia::"],
    "NVN": [b"nvnDevice", b"nvnQueue"],
    "Havok": [b"Havok", b"hkBase"],
    "Wwise": [b"Wwise", b"AkSoundEngine"],
    "FMOD": [b"FMOD"],
    "Unity": [b"UnityEngine", b"il2cpp"],
    "Unreal": [b"UnrealEngine", b"UE4"],
    "Bink": [b"Bink"],
    "Effekseer": [b"Effekseer"],
    "FreeType": [b"FreeType"],
    "libpng": [b"libpng"],
}

RENDER_WORDS = re.compile(
    r"Render|Draw|Shader|Material|Mesh|Model|Camera|Texture|Light|Shadow|Post|Bloom|"
    r"Gfx|Graphic|Nvn|NVN|Frame|Sprite|Particle|Effect|Fog|Blur|Viewport|Scene|Layer|Gpu|GPU",
)


def load_main(cfg: config.Config) -> tuple[bytes, dict]:
    """main's flat image from work/exefs/ and the module info. Refuses (ConfigError) if the
    image doesn't match target.toml, so no tool can analyse a different build (rule 3)."""
    exefs = cfg.work_dir / "exefs"
    mods = {m["name"]: m for m in json.loads((exefs / "modules.json").read_text())}
    image = (exefs / "main.bin").read_bytes()
    want = ingest.load_target().get("image_sha256", "")
    if not want or hashlib.sha256(image).hexdigest() != want:
        raise config.ConfigError(f"{exefs / 'main.bin'} does not match target.toml; "
                                 "run python -m tools.yw4.ingest first")
    return image, mods


def dynsym_names(image: bytes, info: dict) -> list[str]:
    """Names in .dynsym index order (including the empty ones), for relocation lookups."""
    ro = info["segments"]["ro"]["mem_offset"]
    sym_off, sym_size = info["dynsym"]
    str_off, str_size = info["dynstr"]
    strtab = image[ro + str_off:ro + str_off + str_size]
    names = []
    for pos in range(ro + sym_off, ro + sym_off + sym_size, 24):
        n = struct.unpack_from("<I", image, pos)[0]
        names.append(strtab[n:strtab.find(b"\0", n)].decode("utf-8", "replace"))
    return names


def c_string(image: bytes, off: int, limit: int = 512) -> str:
    end = image.find(b"\0", off, off + limit)
    return image[off:end].decode("utf-8", "replace") if end >= 0 else ""


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- imports

def import_group(mangled: str, demangled: str) -> str:
    if mangled.startswith("nvn"):
        return "nvn (bootstrap)"
    if demangled.startswith("nv::"):
        return "nv (graphics init)"
    m = re.match(r"(nn::\w+)", demangled)
    if m:
        return m.group(1)
    for prefix, group in (("nnos", "nn::os"), ("nnsocket", "nn::socket"), ("nnssl", "nn::ssl"),
                          ("nnResult", "nn::result"), ("nndetailDiag", "nn::diag"),
                          ("__nnmusl", "libc (musl)")):
        if mangled.startswith(prefix):
            return group
    if demangled.startswith("std::") or "std::__1" in demangled:
        return "libc++"
    if mangled.startswith("_Z") or mangled.startswith(("__cxa", "__gxx", "__dynamic_cast", "_Unwind")):
        return "C++ runtime (new/delete, RTTI, exceptions)"
    if mangled.startswith("__rel_"):
        return "linker markers (not real imports)"
    return "libc (musl)"


def survey_imports(image: bytes, info: dict, sdk_exports: set[str]) -> dict:
    imps = [s for s in symbols.read_dynsym(image, info) if not s.defined]
    dm = symbols.demangle([s.name for s in imps])
    groups: dict[str, list[str]] = collections.defaultdict(list)
    for s in imps:
        groups[import_group(s.name, dm[s.name])].append(dm[s.name])
    unresolved = [s.name for s in imps if s.name not in sdk_exports and not s.name.startswith("__rel_")]
    return {
        "total": len(imps),
        "functions": sum(s.type == "func" for s in imps),
        "objects": sum(s.type == "object" for s in imps),
        "unresolved_by_sdk": unresolved,
        "groups": {k: sorted(v) for k, v in sorted(groups.items(), key=lambda kv: -len(kv[1]))},
    }


def imports_md(imp: dict) -> str:
    lines = [f"main imports {imp['total']} symbols ({imp['functions']} functions, {imp['objects']} data). "
             f"Not provided by sdk: {len(imp['unresolved_by_sdk'])}.", "",
             "| Group | Count |", "|---|---|"]
    lines += [f"| `{g}` | {len(v)} |" for g, v in imp["groups"].items()]
    lines.append("")
    for g, v in imp["groups"].items():
        lines.append(f"### {g} ({len(v)})")
        lines += [f"- `{n}`" for n in v]
        lines.append("")
    return "\n".join(lines)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- middleware

def survey_middleware(image: bytes) -> str:
    tags = sorted({m.decode() for m in re.findall(rb"SDK MW\+[\x20-\x7e]{3,80}", image)})
    lines = ["Middleware tags (`SDK MW+Vendor+Library-Version`):", ""]
    lines += [f"- `{t}`" for t in tags] + ["", "| Library | Hits | Found |", "|---|---|---|"]
    for name, kws in MIDDLEWARE_KEYWORDS.items():
        hits = sum(image.count(k) for k in kws)
        lines.append(f"| {name} | {hits} | {'yes' if hits else 'no'} |")
    m = re.search(rb"Lua 5\.\d(\.\d)?", image)
    if m:
        lines += ["", f"Lua version string: `{m.group().decode()}`"]
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- RTTI / vtables

def survey_rtti(image: bytes, info: dict) -> dict:
    names = dynsym_names(image, info)
    internal, external = reloc.pointer_map(reloc.read_relocs(image))
    text_end = info["segments"]["text"]["size"]

    # A typeinfo object starts with a pointer to (one of the __class_type_info vtables + 0x10),
    # followed by a pointer to its mangled name string.
    typeinfos: dict[int, tuple[str, str]] = {}
    for slot, (sym, _addend) in external.items():
        kind = TYPEINFO_VTABLES.get(names[sym])
        if kind and slot + 8 in internal:
            typeinfos[slot] = (kind, c_string(image, internal[slot + 8]))

    # Typeinfo objects also point at other typeinfos (their base classes). Mark every
    # byte range a typeinfo occupies so those links are not mistaken for vtables:
    #   base: vptr, name                          (0x10 bytes)
    #   single: vptr, name, base*                 (0x18)
    #   multiple: vptr, name, u32 flags, u32 n, n x {base*, offset_flags}  (0x18 + 0x10 n)
    inside_typeinfo: set[int] = set()
    for ti, (kind, _name) in typeinfos.items():
        size = {"base": 0x10, "single": 0x18}.get(kind)
        if size is None:
            size = 0x18 + 0x10 * struct.unpack_from("<I", image, ti + 0x14)[0]
        inside_typeinfo.update(range(ti, ti + size, 8))

    # A vtable is [offset_to_top][typeinfo*][fn0][fn1]...; find slots that point at a typeinfo.
    pure_virtual = {i for i, n in enumerate(names) if n == "__cxa_pure_virtual"}
    vtables = []
    for slot, target in internal.items():
        if target not in typeinfos or slot in inside_typeinfo:
            continue
        offset_to_top = struct.unpack_from("<q", image, slot - 8)[0]
        n = 0
        pos = slot + 8
        while True:
            if pos in internal and internal[pos] < text_end:
                n += 1
            elif pos in external and external[pos][0] in pure_virtual:
                n += 1
            else:
                break
            pos += 8
        vtables.append((slot - 8, typeinfos[target][1], offset_to_top, n))

    mangled = sorted({name for _, name in typeinfos.values() if name})
    dm = symbols.demangle(["_ZTS" + n for n in mangled])
    pretty = {n: dm["_ZTS" + n].removeprefix("typeinfo name for ") for n in mangled}

    ns = collections.Counter()
    for p in pretty.values():
        top = re.split(r"::|<", p, maxsplit=1)
        ns[top[0] if len(top) > 1 and "::" in p.split("<", 1)[0] else "(global)"] += 1

    primary = [v for v in vtables if v[2] == 0]
    return {
        "typeinfo_count": len(typeinfos),
        "typeinfo_by_kind": collections.Counter(k for k, _ in typeinfos.values()),
        "class_names": sorted(pretty.values()),
        "namespaces": ns.most_common(),
        "vtable_count": len(vtables),
        "primary_vtables": len(primary),
        "secondary_vtables": len(vtables) - len(primary),
        "vtable_slots_total": sum(v[3] for v in vtables),
        "vtable_slots_max": max((v[3] for v in vtables), default=0),
        "pure_virtual_slots": sum(1 for v in external.values() if v[0] in pure_virtual),
    }


def rtti_md(r: dict) -> str:
    kinds = r["typeinfo_by_kind"]
    lines = [
        f"- Classes with RTTI: **{r['typeinfo_count']}** "
        f"(base {kinds.get('base', 0)}, single inheritance {kinds.get('single', 0)}, "
        f"multiple inheritance {kinds.get('multiple', 0)})",
        f"- Vtables found: **{r['vtable_count']}** ({r['primary_vtables']} primary, "
        f"{r['secondary_vtables']} secondary from multiple inheritance)",
        f"- Virtual function slots: **{r['vtable_slots_total']}** total, largest vtable "
        f"{r['vtable_slots_max']} slots; {r['pure_virtual_slots']} pure-virtual slots",
        "", "| Top-level namespace | Classes |", "|---|---|",
    ]
    lines += [f"| `{n}` | {c} |" for n, c in r["namespaces"][:30]]
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- code

def eh_frame_function_starts(image: bytes) -> list[int]:
    """Function start offsets from .eh_frame_hdr's binary-search table.

    Header: u8 version (1), u8 eh_frame_ptr encoding, u8 count encoding,
    u8 table encoding, then the encoded eh_frame pointer and FDE count, then
    (initial_location, fde_address) pairs. We support what this toolchain emits:
    count as udata4 (0x03) and table entries as datarel sdata4 (0x3b), i.e.
    signed 32-bit offsets from the start of .eh_frame_hdr.
    """
    start = reloc.read_mod0(image).eh_frame_hdr[0]
    version, _ptr_enc, count_enc, table_enc = image[start:start + 4]
    if version != 1 or count_enc != 0x03 or table_enc != 0x3B:
        raise reloc.RelocError(f"unsupported .eh_frame_hdr encoding {image[start:start + 4].hex()}")
    count = struct.unpack_from("<I", image, start + 8)[0]
    return [start + struct.unpack_from("<i", image, start + 12 + 8 * i)[0] for i in range(count)]


def address_taken_functions(image: bytes, text_size: int) -> set[int]:
    """Targets of internal pointers into .text (vtables, callback tables, ...)."""
    internal, _ = reloc.pointer_map(reloc.read_relocs(image))
    return {t for t in internal.values() if t < text_size}


def survey_code(image: bytes, info: dict) -> dict:
    text = image[:info["segments"]["text"]["size"]]
    words = struct.unpack(f"<{len(text) // 4}I", text[:len(text) // 4 * 4])
    c = collections.Counter()
    for w in words:
        if w & 0xFC000000 == 0x94000000:
            c["bl"] += 1                      # direct call
        elif w & 0xFC000000 == 0x14000000:
            c["b"] += 1                       # direct jump / tail call
        elif w & 0xFFFFFC1F == 0xD63F0000:
            c["blr"] += 1                     # indirect call (virtual calls, function pointers)
        elif w & 0xFFFFFC1F == 0xD61F0000:
            c["br"] += 1                      # indirect jump (switch tables, indirect tail calls)
        elif w & 0xFFFFFC1F == 0xD65F0000:
            c["ret"] += 1
        elif w & 0xFFFFFC1F == 0xD4000001:
            c["svc"] += 1                     # syscall (should be ~0 in main; sdk does them)
        elif w & 0x9F000000 == 0x90000000:
            c["adrp"] += 1
        elif w & 0xFF000000 == 0x58000000:
            c["ldr_literal"] += 1
        elif w & 0x3F000000 == 0x08000000:   # load/store exclusive and ordered
            o2, load, o1 = (w >> 23) & 1, (w >> 22) & 1, (w >> 21) & 1
            if o2 == 0:
                c["ldxr" if load else "stxr"] += 1        # exclusive pair (v8.0 atomics)
            elif o1 == 0:
                c["ldar" if load else "stlr"] += 1        # acquire load / release store
            else:
                c["cas"] += 1                             # v8.1 CAS (Switch A57 lacks it)
        elif w & 0x3F200C00 == 0x38200000:
            c["lse"] += 1                                 # v8.1 LSE atomics (should be 0)
        elif w & 0xFFFFF0FF == 0xD50330BF:
            c["dmb"] += 1
        elif w & 0xFFFFFFE0 == 0xD53BD040:
            c["mrs_tpidr"] += 1                           # thread-local storage pointer read
        # FP/SIMD data-processing: bits 28-25 = x111
        if (w >> 25) & 0x7 == 0x7:
            c["fp_simd"] += 1
    mod0 = reloc.read_mod0(image)
    eh = set(eh_frame_function_starts(image))
    taken = address_taken_functions(image, len(text))
    return {"instructions": len(words), "counts": dict(c),
            "eh_frame_functions": len(eh),
            "address_taken": len(taken),
            "address_taken_with_unwind": len(taken & eh),
            "bss_size": mod0.bss_end - mod0.bss_start}


def code_md(code: dict) -> str:
    c = code["counts"]
    n = code["instructions"]
    lines = [
        f"- Instructions in .text: **{n:,}**",
        f"- Functions with unwind info (.eh_frame_hdr): **{code['eh_frame_functions']:,}**",
        f"- Address-taken functions (relocations into .text): **{code['address_taken']:,}**, "
        f"of which {code['address_taken_with_unwind']:,} are also unwind-table starts",
        f"- .bss size: {code['bss_size']:,} bytes",
        "", "| Kind | Count | Per 1000 instructions |", "|---|---|---|",
    ]
    for k in ("bl", "b", "blr", "br", "ret", "svc", "adrp", "ldr_literal", "fp_simd",
              "ldxr", "stxr", "ldar", "stlr", "cas", "lse", "dmb", "mrs_tpidr"):
        lines.append(f"| `{k}` | {c.get(k, 0):,} | {1000 * c.get(k, 0) / n:.1f} |")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- RomFS

def survey_romfs(romfs: Path) -> str:
    """File types on disk and inside every CPK archive (names and headers only)."""
    disk_n, disk_b = collections.Counter(), collections.Counter()
    inner_n, inner_b, inner_c = collections.Counter(), collections.Counter(), collections.Counter()
    top_b = collections.Counter()
    archives, errors = 0, []
    for p in romfs.rglob("*"):
        if not p.is_file():
            continue
        size = p.stat().st_size
        ext = p.suffix.lower() or "(none)"
        disk_n[ext] += 1
        disk_b[ext] += size
        rel = p.relative_to(romfs).parts
        top_b["/".join(rel[:2]) if len(rel) > 2 else rel[0]] += size
        if ext != ".cpk":
            continue
        archives += 1
        try:
            info = cpk.list_files(p)
        except cpk.CpkError as e:
            errors.append(f"{p.name}: {e}")
            continue
        for f in info.files:
            iext = Path(f.path).suffix.lower() or "(none)"
            inner_n[iext] += 1
            inner_b[iext] += f.extract_size
            inner_c[iext] += f.compressed

    mb = lambda b: f"{b / 2**20:,.1f}"
    lines = ["Top level:", "", "| Folder | MB |", "|---|---|"]
    lines += [f"| `{k}` | {mb(v)} |" for k, v in top_b.most_common()]
    lines += ["", "Files on disk:", "", "| Ext | Files | MB |", "|---|---|---|"]
    lines += [f"| `{e}` | {c} | {mb(disk_b[e])} |" for e, c in disk_n.most_common()]
    lines += ["", f"Inside {archives} CPK archives ({sum(inner_n.values()):,} files, "
              f"{len(errors)} unreadable):", "",
              "| Ext | Files | MB uncompressed | % compressed |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
    lines += [f"| `{e}` | {c} | {mb(inner_b[e])} | {100 * inner_c[e] // c}% |"
              for e, c in inner_n.most_common()]
    lines += [f"- {e}" for e in errors[:20]]
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- main

def main() -> int:
    try:
        cfg = config.load()
        image, mods = load_main(cfg)
    except config.ConfigError as e:
        print(f"config error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    sdk_image = (cfg.work_dir / "exefs" / "sdk.bin").read_bytes()
    sdk_exports = {s.name for s in symbols.read_dynsym(sdk_image, mods["sdk"]) if s.defined}

    out = cfg.work_dir / "recon"
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    imp = survey_imports(image, mods["main"], sdk_exports)
    (out / "imports.json").write_text(json.dumps(imp, indent=2))
    (out / "imports.md").write_text(imports_md(imp))

    (out / "middleware.md").write_text(survey_middleware(image))

    rtti = survey_rtti(image, mods["main"])
    (out / "rtti.json").write_text(json.dumps(rtti, indent=2))
    (out / "rtti.md").write_text(rtti_md(rtti))
    render = [n for n in rtti["class_names"] if RENDER_WORDS.search(n)]
    (out / "render_classes.txt").write_text("\n".join(render) + "\n")

    code = survey_code(image, mods["main"])
    (out / "code.md").write_text(code_md(code))

    (out / "romfs.md").write_text(survey_romfs(cfg.romfs_dir))

    print(f"imports: {imp['total']}  classes: {rtti['typeinfo_count']}  vtables: {rtti['vtable_count']}  "
          f"render-ish classes: {len(render)}  blr: {code['counts'].get('blr', 0):,}  "
          f"eh_frame functions: {code['eh_frame_functions']:,}")
    print(f"wrote {out}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

`tools/yw4/reloc.py`:

```py
"""Find and apply a module's dynamic relocations.

Switch modules are position-independent. In the flat image most pointers
(vtable entries, typeinfo links, function-pointer tables) are 0; the loader
writes them at boot from the relocation tables. To see what a pointer points
at, we have to replay those relocations ourselves.

How to find the tables:
    image[4:8]  u32 offset of the MOD0 header (from image start)
    MOD0        "MOD0", then i32 offsets relative to MOD0: dynamic, bss start,
                bss end, eh_frame_hdr start, eh_frame_hdr end, module object
    .dynamic    (tag u64, value u64) pairs; we need DT_RELA/DT_RELASZ (data
                relocations) and DT_JMPREL/DT_PLTRELSZ (PLT slots)
    Elf64_Rela  u64 offset, u64 info (symbol index << 32 | type), i64 addend

Relocation types that matter on AArch64:
    R_AARCH64_RELATIVE (1027)  *offset = module base + addend   (internal pointer)
    R_AARCH64_ABS64    (257)   *offset = symbol + addend
    R_AARCH64_GLOB_DAT (1025)  *offset = symbol                 (GOT entry)
    R_AARCH64_JUMP_SLOT(1026)  *offset = symbol                 (PLT slot)
We relocate as if the module were loaded at address 0, so a RELATIVE pointer's
value is simply its addend = an offset into the flat image.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import struct
from dataclasses import dataclass

R_AARCH64_ABS64 = 257
R_AARCH64_GLOB_DAT = 1025
R_AARCH64_JUMP_SLOT = 1026
R_AARCH64_RELATIVE = 1027

DT_NULL, DT_PLTRELSZ, DT_RELA, DT_RELASZ, DT_JMPREL = 0, 2, 7, 8, 23


class RelocError(Exception):
    pass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Mod0:
    offset: int
    dynamic: int
    bss_start: int
    bss_end: int
    eh_frame_hdr: tuple[int, int]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Reloc:
    offset: int
    type: int
    sym: int      # index into .dynsym (0 for RELATIVE)
    addend: int


def read_mod0(image: bytes) -> Mod0:
    base = struct.unpack_from("<I", image, 4)[0]
    if image[base:base + 4] != b"MOD0":
        raise RelocError(f"no MOD0 header at 0x{base:x}")
    dyn, bss_s, bss_e, eh_s, eh_e = struct.unpack_from("<5i", image, base + 4)
    return Mod0(base, base + dyn, base + bss_s, base + bss_e, (base + eh_s, base + eh_e))


def read_dynamic(image: bytes, mod0: Mod0) -> dict[int, int]:
    tags: dict[int, int] = {}
    pos = mod0.dynamic
    while pos + 16 <= len(image):
        tag, val = struct.unpack_from("<QQ", image, pos)
        if tag == DT_NULL:
            break
        tags.setdefault(tag, val)
        pos += 16
    return tags


def read_relocs(image: bytes) -> list[Reloc]:
    dyn = read_dynamic(image, read_mod0(image))
    relocs = []
    for start_tag, size_tag in ((DT_RELA, DT_RELASZ), (DT_JMPREL, DT_PLTRELSZ)):
        if start_tag not in dyn:
            continue
        start, size = dyn[start_tag], dyn[size_tag]
        for pos in range(start, start + size, 24):
            off, info, addend = struct.unpack_from("<QQq", image, pos)
            relocs.append(Reloc(off, info & 0xFFFFFFFF, info >> 32, addend))
    return relocs


def pointer_map(relocs: list[Reloc]) -> tuple[dict[int, int], dict[int, tuple[int, int]]]:
    """Return (internal, external).

    internal: slot offset -> target offset in this module (RELATIVE).
    external: slot offset -> (symbol index, addend) for slots filled from another module.
    """
    internal: dict[int, int] = {}
    external: dict[int, tuple[int, int]] = {}
    for r in relocs:
        if r.type == R_AARCH64_RELATIVE:
            internal[r.offset] = r.addend
        elif r.type in (R_AARCH64_ABS64, R_AARCH64_GLOB_DAT, R_AARCH64_JUMP_SLOT):
            external[r.offset] = (r.sym, r.addend)
    return internal, external

```

`tools/yw4/sdkref.py`:

